# Changelog

Every code change adds an entry here, in the same commit or PR as the code. This is step 7 of the
[development workflow](../CLAUDE.md#development-workflow) and is not optional.

## How to Add an Entry

- Read the first 40 lines of this file to place an entry, never the whole file. Add it at the
  **top** of the first group under `## Unreleased` that fits: `Added`, `Changed`, `Fixed`,
  `Removed`, or `Docs`. `grep -n '^### ' docs/CHANGELOG.md` lists the groups; create one, directly
  under `## Unreleased`, only when none of that name exists. One group per name, never a second.
- Write what changed for a reader who was not in the conversation, and link the main file. Open
  with one bold sentence: the app's Release Information dialog shows those sentences from the top
  section as the release notes. Say the
  effect, not the internal detail: "Image Selection screens fill the app shell", not "swapped a
  min-height".
- When `develop` is promoted to `main`, rename `Unreleased` to `## <version> — <date>` —
  `## 1.2.41 — 2026-08-27` — and start a fresh `Unreleased` above it. Run
  `scripts/app-version.sh --next` on `develop` for the version that promotion ships under: the
  build number is counted from the promotions to `main`, not chosen. See
  [Versioning](project-state/DEPLOYMENT-WORKFLOW.md#versioning). In the same commit, move the
  release that was below `Unreleased` to `docs/changelog/<version>.md` with its links rewritten
  one level deeper: this file keeps `Unreleased` and the release being shipped, nothing older.

---

## Unreleased

### Added
- **A client's own site can now read the subscription BeamCraft set up for it.** Client Details → ⋮ →
  **Site key** on a set-up client makes a new key (replacing the old at once), keeps only its SHA-256
  hash, and shows it once as the `.env` lines for the client's server. That server calls the public,
  rate-limited `GET /api/client-site/subscription` (`Authorization: Bearer <key>`, `X-Site: <subdomain>`)
  and gets the live fields only — never a change waiting for Update site — including `passwordSetAt`
  from the new `admin_password_set_at` column, set at the first setup and at every Reset password.
  [siteApi.js](../backend/src/modules/subscribe/client-onboarding/siteApi.js); migration
  `20261104200000_client_site_key`. Same roles as before: SUBSCRIBE / Client Onboarding at READ_WRITE
  makes a key; no new permission.

### Removed

  and `deploy.yml` checked DBS's `develop` and deployed `main` to the DBS VPS; nothing in this repository
  runs automatically now. The `ci.yml` / `deploy.yml` sections of
  [DEPLOYMENT-WORKFLOW.md](project-state/DEPLOYMENT-WORKFLOW.md) describe DBS and no longer apply here.

### Fixed
- **The Interview register accepted the same candidate over and over — three of the four ways in
  never asked.** Only the Google Sheet importer checked; **Add Application**, **Bulk Entry** and the
  **CSV import** wrote whatever they were handed. So a candidate who applied twice, a file imported
  twice, or a name typed in by two people became two records — two stages, two sets of remarks, and
  an interview booked against the copy nobody is reading. All four now hold to **one person, one
  row**, matched on **phone or email** using the sheet importer's own normalised keys, so
  `98765 43210`, `+91 9876543210` and `9876543210` are one person and not three, and an address
  matches whatever it was capitalised as. Names are deliberately not matched: two Priya Sharmas are
  two people. A refusal **names the candidate and their ID**, so the studio can go and open the
  record rather than hunt a register of thousands for it. **Bulk Entry** follows the CRM board
  exactly: the whole batch is answered **before any of it is written**, every clashing row is
  reported rather than the first, the grid marks those rows in place, and two rows of one paste
  carrying the same number catch each other — the case no per-row check can ever see. **Editing** is
  guarded too, but only where the write actually *changes* the number or address: the register
  already holds duplicates from before the rule existed, and refusing an unchanged value would make
  exactly those rows uneditable, so nobody could open one and correct it. A candidate with neither a
  phone nor an email — a referral that arrives as a name — is still accepted, because there is
  nothing to match on and nothing to refuse.
- **Add Application now says "already on the register" while the number is still being typed.** The
  rule above is enforced on the save, and a refusal that arrives after somebody has filled in a
  whole application arrives too late. So both forms that take a contact number — **Add Application**
  and the candidate record's own form — ask the register as it is typed and answer **under the
  field**, naming the candidate and their ID so it can be gone and looked at. It is **amber, not
  red**: a number the register already holds is worth stopping for and is not an error, and the form
  is perfectly valid. Asked only once the number is whole, so nothing appears against the first four
  digits of one; debounced; and every answer is held against the field as it stands, so a reply
  landing after an edit warns about nothing rather than about a number nobody is looking at. A check
  that cannot be made is not a clash — the form stays usable and Confirm is never held up by a
  network having a moment, because the save is refused by the server regardless. The warning and the
  refusal share one definition of "the same person", or a form would warn about what it then accepts.
  Bulk Entry is deliberately unchanged: it marks its rows when the register refuses the batch, which
  is what the CRM's own Bulk Entry does.
- **The Status filter on the Interview register offered an empty menu.** Every other column's menu
  listed its values; Status listed nothing, so the one column whose values a reader already knows by
  heart was the one they could not pick from. The menu query asked for rows where the column "is not
  null", which Prisma refuses outright against a column that is **required** — and Status is the only
  filterable column on the register that cannot be null, which is exactly why it was the only one
  that broke. The read threw, the page turned a failed read into an empty list, and the menu drew
  itself blank with nothing anywhere saying why. Blanks are now dropped after the read instead
  ([service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/interview/service.js)), where a null and the empty string
  a spreadsheet import leaves behind are the same thing and both have to go. Two tests hold the
  shape: every column offered as a filter is a real column, and the register never offers a menu the
  server will not answer for — both routes to the same blank menu.
- **Filtering the Interview register now filters the register, not the hundred rows you have
  scrolled to.** The register is read a page at a time, but its filter row was matched in the
  browser — so a filter only ever saw the rows already fetched. Picking a value the menu plainly
  listed answered **"no records found"** over a stage holding hundreds of them, and the menu itself
  grew as you scrolled because it was built from the rows in hand. Both now go to the server
  ([service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/interview/service.js)): a filter is part of the query, a
  menu asks the column what it holds, and **Select all** resolves to the filtered set rather than
  the whole stage — so a bulk action can no longer reach rows the reader had filtered away. The
  menus also **cascade**, the way Leads and Follow-ups do: opened with a Source filter on, the
  Position menu offers the positions that Source actually holds, so the values on offer are values
  that would find rows. Two things keep that from turning on the reader. A column's own filter is
  left out of the query behind its own menu, or ticking one value would narrow that menu to the one
  value ticked and a filter could never be widened again. And a menu already open **does not
  re-narrow under the hand using it** — these are multi-selects, so the reader is still in the list
  when the filter changes; it settles on the next open instead. The CRM board reached the same two
  conclusions. Typing into a text filter is debounced, and switching stage tab clears the filter
  row along with the selection — a stage is its own set of values, and a filter carried across is an
  empty table over a stage that has rows. Only listed columns can be filtered; anything else in the
  parameter is ignored rather than handed to a query.
- **A candidate added by hand had no Source, so the column was blank for exactly the rows a person
  was responsible for.** The sheet importer stamped "Google sheet integration" and the public
  application form stamped "Application Form", but a candidate typed into **Add Application** or
  **Bulk Entry**, or brought in by **CSV import**, was left with nothing — so the column answered
  "where did this come from?" for everything an importer brought and for nothing anybody entered.
  Those three now stamp **"Manual entry"** and **"CSV import"**, so all four ways into the register
  say which way it was. It is a **fallback, never an override**: a Source somebody names — Naukri, a
  referral, a walk-in — is kept exactly as they named it, which is the same rule the sheet importer
  has always followed for a row carrying its own Source column. Stamped at the way in rather than in
  the service, because the service cannot tell them apart: a CSV row and a typed one are the same
  `createCandidate` call, and only the route knows which it was.
- **Add Lead cannot make two leads out of one double-click any more.** Its Confirm button had no
  in-flight guard at all — a plain button with nothing disabling it — and the enquiry id is minted on
  the **server**, so a second press was not a duplicate anything could refuse: it was a second, real
  lead with its own id for somebody to find and delete. On a slow connection the window was seconds
  wide, which is exactly when people press again. Confirm now stands down and reads **Adding…**
  while the lead is being written, and so does Cancel. The "go on with it anyway" path out of the
  duplicate-phone warning reaches the same save by a second route, so it carries the same guard.
  The **lead popup's** three save buttons got it too, for a different reason: writing the same values
  twice leaves the lead as it was, but **Update and Proceed Next** advances the board, so a
  double-click saved one lead and stepped past two — and the one it skipped is the one nobody then
  works. **Bulk Entry** already disabled its button while saving and was never the one producing
  duplicates; it gained the missing half below.
  The guard itself is [`useSubmitOnce`](../frontend/src/components/shared/useSubmitOnce.js), and it
  is a **ref** as well as a state flag. `disabled={busy}` is the half everyone writes and it is not
  enough on its own: React applies state on the next render, so two clicks in the same tick — which
  is what a double-click *is* — both read the old value and both fire. The ref is written before
  anything awaits. It is released in a `finally`, so a save that failed leaves the form usable
  rather than locking somebody out of what they typed. A **delay** on the button is deliberately not
  the answer: whatever delay is chosen, a save slower than it is still double-postable, and every
  ordinary save is made to feel sluggish to pay for it.
- **Every button that writes now says the same thing while it is working.** The application had
  three different answers to "this is in flight": some buttons greyed *and* said **Saving...**, some
  only greyed, and a few did neither. Those read as three different things to somebody waiting — and
  a greyed button with no word reads as *refused* rather than *working*, which is precisely the
  reading that makes people press again. It is now one prop on the shared `Button`: **`busy`**
  disables it, flips its label, and tells a screen reader (`aria-busy`) the same thing the colour is
  saying. The verb follows the button rather than being written twice — **Add Lead** → *Adding...*,
  **Send Screening Form** → *Sending...*, **Update and Close** → *Updating...*, **Save Changes** →
  *Saving...* — with `busyLabel` for the cases where the obvious word is not the honest one, and
  *Saving...* as the fallback for a label it cannot read. Three dots, matching the 183 places that
  already wrote it that way rather than the 26 that did not. A **Cancel** beside a running save is
  deliberately left grey and silent: it is disabled because the form cannot be dismissed mid-save,
  not because it is doing something ([Button.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/Button.js)).

### Changed
- **One linked Google account now schedules for the whole studio.** Booking an interview used to
  demand a connection from whoever pressed the button, so every recruiter had to link their own
  Google account before they could schedule anything — and a studio that had already connected one
  still had to do it again, person by person. Once **any** account is linked under Settings →
  Integrations → Interview, everybody schedules through it.
  Your own still wins where you have one: the interview lands in your own diary and the invite goes
  out in your name. The studio's account is the fallback, not the rule, and it is the **earliest**
  linked account carrying the Calendar consent — earliest so the organiser does not change as other
  people connect their own. A connection Google has since rejected is skipped rather than refusing
  the studio. When the fallback is used the confirmation says so — *"It is on the studio's calendar
  (address), not yours"* — because the first thing that otherwise happens is somebody opening their
  own calendar, not finding the interview, and booking it twice. Cancelling runs as the account that
  **owns** the event, since an interview on the studio's calendar cannot be deleted with a
  recruiter's own token. This is the reading the linked Google Sheets have always used, where the
  connection stored on the *link* does the reading rather than whoever triggered the sync
  ([meetings.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/interview/meetings.js)).

### Fixed
- **The Interview table's column filters offered only the values on the page you had scrolled to.**
  The register is read a page at a time, and the filter menus were built from the rows the browser
  held — so Position offered a handful of the 34 the column actually has, and the list *grew* as you
  scrolled. A filter that hides the rows it was opened to find is the one thing a filter must not
  do. Each menu now asks the column: a new `GET /api/hrm/interview/candidates/column-values`, called
  when the menu opens (one per column, and most are never opened), narrowed by the stage being read
  so the list describes the tab in front of you. An answer arriving after you have changed tab
  belongs to the tab you left and is discarded; a column already answered is not asked twice. The
  column is checked against an allowlist on both sides rather than trusted, and a test asserts the
  two lists name the same set. Tables that hold all their rows are untouched — deriving the values
  from the data is the whole answer there, and `DataTable` still does exactly that unless a page
  supplies `filterValues`.

### Reverted
- **Position Applied For reads the designation list again.** It was changed to offer the positions
  the register holds, on the theory that a picker missing 34 of them was why they were not showing.
  It was not: the picker is what somebody **chooses from** when writing an application down, and the
  filter that was actually hiding them is fixed above. Offering the sheet's own ad labels
  ("CRM Static Erode") as positions to assign would have put them on new candidates — the same fault
  the CRM's assignee picker was fixed for. The two questions stay apart: the picker is the studio's
  maintained roles, the filter is what the column holds.
- **"Select all" on the Interview register selected the first 100, not every candidate.** The
  register is read a page at a time, and the header checkbox ticked `table.getRowModel().rows` — the
  rows loaded so far. So it selected 100 of 5,769, and worse, the same gesture meant a different
  number depending on how far somebody had scrolled. It now uses the **same selection model the
  Leads board already had** (`lib/leadSelection`): `allMatching` plus the exceptions somebody
  un-ticked, which is one boolean for a stage of five thousand rather than five thousand strings,
  and lets a row fetched later arrive already ticked. The count reads against the stage's own total,
  so the bar says 5,769 and means it. The ids are resolved when an action runs, from a new
  `GET /api/hrm/interview/candidates/ids` behind the module's existing guard, with the reader's
  exceptions removed — and a stage larger than 20,000 is refused outright rather than silently acted
  on in part. `DataTable`'s selection now takes an optional `model` for a paged table; the sixteen
  client-side tables keep the plain set of ids, which is correct for them because they hold every
  row. Checked all 18 tables with selection: Interview was the only one affected — Leads already
  handled it, and the rest load their rows whole.
- **Position Applied For offered the wrong list, so 34 of the register's positions were unpickable.**
  The picker was built from the studio's **designation** list, on the argument that most applications
  are for a role the studio actually has. That is a different question: a designation is what
  somebody is *employed* as, a position applied for is what an advert asked for, and nobody keeps the
  two in step. The register held **36** positions against a picker offering **32** designations, with
  **34 of the 36 missing** — every one written by the linked Google Sheet, which is where 5,752 of
  the 5,757 candidates with a position came from. The sheet writes the candidate's `position` and
  nothing in the sync path touches the option lists, so the gap only appeared once a sheet was
  linked: with hand-typed candidates the two agreed by construction, because every position on a row
  got there by being picked. The picker now offers the studio's own **Interview → Positions** list
  first, then every position the register already holds (a capped `DISTINCT` over the column). The
  `designation` table is no longer read by this endpoint and is still never written to it.

### Changed
- **A role's branches now apply to the permissions that role grants, and to nothing else.** Somebody
  holding **CRM Leads across all six branches** through one role and **Asset Management in
  Coimbatore** through another reaches six branches *for leads* and one *for assets* — the branch
  picker on each screen offers accordingly, and each screen's save is checked against its own answer.
  Until now there was one answer per person, the union of every branch every role they held happened
  to name, so **the widest role somebody held silently widened all the others**: that person got
  every branch's assets too. Every call into the branch API now names the `module / feature` it is
  asking about, and `checkBranchAccess` refuses to be built without one rather than falling back to
  the union — which would fail open, on a write.
  Two consequences worth knowing before you deploy. **A role that names no branches contributes
  none** — it is not read as "all of them"; Role Management already refuses to save a role without a
  branch, so this only affects roles that predate that rule (`EMPLOYEE`, `TEAM_LEAD`,
  `BRANCH_MANAGER` and two demo roles currently have none). And **a person's own branch is no longer
  added automatically**: it used to be, which is what made a restriction unenforceable — a role
  saying "Coimbatore only" still showed an Erode-based person the whole of Erode. Being narrowed to
  no branch is not being shown nothing: everybody still sees the work their own name is on and their
  team's. Where a screen asks both questions, they take two permissions — *where may you use this
  screen* is the screen's own, *whose work may you see that is not your own* is
  `ADMIN / Branch Administration` ([iam.service.js](../backend/src/services/iam.service.js),
  [dataScope.service.js](../backend/src/services/dataScope.service.js),
  [IAM.md](project-state/IAM.md#branch-reach-belongs-to-the-permission-not-to-the-person)).

### Added
- **Approvers now say how much a worked day earned, and half days pair up into whole days off.**
  Approving a Comp-Off Credit used to be yes or no, and a day worked meant a whole day off. The
  approver's dialog now asks "How many days does this earn?" - nothing, half a day, a day, and up in
  half steps to the days worked, so a short day on a weekly off can be worth half a day and a
  Saturday, Sunday and holiday worked back to back are one question answered once. Every approver
  still has to approve, and the amount granted is the lowest any of them chose, so an approver who
  thinks a run was worth less says so with a number instead of refusing it outright. `0` is a
  refusal with a number on it, and it reads as "granted nothing" rather than as a rejection nobody
  can tell from a disagreement about the amount.

  Because there is no half day off to take, **a day off costs one whole day of credit**: one worked
  day granted a whole day, or two half days claimed together. Raise Request now offers days off
  rather than worked days - a pair appears as one choice, headed "Half a day each", with both days
  and their hours under it - and "Comp-offs to claim" counts days off you can actually take. A lone
  half day is listed as waiting for another half rather than left out, so half a day granted never
  looks like nothing granted. A day off has to fall after the later of the two days worked and
  expires on the clock of the earlier, which is the credit that runs out first; where a credit covers
  a run, the grant is shared out in half days from the earliest day, so no amount is ever a quarter
  that nothing could spend.

  **This fixes a real miscount:** two days granted half a day each were still being offered as two
  whole days off, because nothing read the amount the approvers had granted. Claiming one half on its
  own is now refused, saying so in the form, and both days a claim spends are marked as spent.
  Nothing anyone was already shown changes: a credit approved before amounts existed is still a whole
  day, as it was earned.
  [backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/compOffCredits.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/compOffCredits.js)

- **Every message on Settings → Templates now has its own on/off switch.** Above its wording, so a
  studio can stop one message without touching the rest: "shoot completed" on and "started from
  studio" off, where before the only switch covered a whole feature and the production step messages
  had none at all. Everything stays on until you turn something off, the wording is kept when you do,
  and a message skipped while it was off is still owed when you switch it back on - it is not quietly
  spent. A switched-off step shows no "Not sent · Retry" either, because nothing was attempted.
  It works on a message nobody has written yet, which matters: those are the ones sending the app's
  built-in wording, so they are exactly the ones somebody wants stopped.
  [frontend/src/components/settings/MessageTemplatePanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/MessageTemplatePanel.js)

- **Leave cannot be applied for on a day you are on a shoot.** The request is refused as it is made,
  and the refusal names the shoot - its id and name, the day, where it is, and what you are on it for
  - then says to ask that project's Production Manager, by name, to take you off it before applying
  again. Approved leave on a shoot day was how a crew turned up one short with nobody having decided
  that: the leave was answered by an approver who could not see the plan, and the plan was made by a
  manager who could not see the leave. It counts all three ways of being on a shoot - given a service,
  on the production team, or as its Production Coordinator - and covers leave spanning several days,
  listing every shoot in the range. **Permission is not affected**: an hour or two inside a day is
  often exactly what somebody on a shoot asks for. It names the manager rather than freeing the person
  itself, because taking somebody off a shoot is re-planning it.
  [backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/controller.js)

- **The User Activity Logs now say what a write changed, not just that somebody saved.** A **What
  changed** column reads "Main Event Date: 20 Nov 2026 → 22 Nov 2026 · Production Manager: — →
  Karthik", so "he says he updated it and it is not reflecting" can be answered from the log instead
  of taken on trust. Searchable by word, so "event date" finds every line that moved one, whoever
  moved it. Live on **Start / Edit Project** and **Edit Sale Details** first - the two saves that
  raised this - and each project's own Activity tab now says the same thing rather than "Project
  details saved".

  **It covers every screen, not the ones somebody remembered.** The detail comes from the writes
  themselves rather than from each handler being wired up: a project, a shoot, an employee record or
  a payment request now describes what changed whenever it is saved, from any screen, including ones
  built later. That matters because the first version was wired by hand and missed the save the
  studio was actually pressing - it had been used 131 times in three days while the two wired saves
  had run four times in a week. Money and approvals still get their own wording where it reads better
  than a list of columns.

  **It records nothing it should not.** Relations, the columns every save touches (Updated At, Sort
  Order, the text the app keeps beside each id) and anything whose name looks like a secret are all
  dropped, so the lines stay readable. A refused save records nothing, because nothing changed. Each
  watched save costs about 6 ms. Two things to know: it only records from the day it ships, so it
  cannot say what anybody did last week; and a log line is deleted with the rest - automatically after
  `ACTIVITY_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 186, about six months) and whenever somebody runs Settings →
  Activity Log Purge - so a record whose history must outlive that is better read from its own
  Activity tab, which neither of those touches.
  [backend/src/services/recordChanges.js](../backend/src/services/recordChanges.js)

- **An expense line's date now fills itself in from the shoot you picked.** On a **vendor payment**
  and on an expense submission that is a **reimbursement**, choosing the Shoot ID puts that shoot's
  own day into Expense Date - the two sat next to each other on the line and were being typed one
  after the other off the same row. It stays editable: change it whenever the bill is dated
  differently, and **a date you typed is never overwritten**, even if you then change the shoot. The
  box says where its answer came from while it is still the shoot's. Not on an advance against
  expenses, which is dated when the money is *needed* rather than when anything happened, nor on an
  expense excess, which is unspent advance money coming back and has nothing it was spent on.
  [frontend/src/components/hrm/PaymentRequestExpenseLines.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PaymentRequestExpenseLines.js)

- **The project Boards show each column's money, as a project's Payments tab shows it.** On
  Projects, Bookings, Pre Production, Production and Post Production:
  - Under each column: **"Client paid ₹2,81,500 · Balance due ₹833"**: what the clients have paid so far and what they still owe, for the projects in that column,
    each counted once.
  - On a card whose client still owes money: a **"Balance due ₹833"** tag.
  - **Who sees it:** only somebody who may see a project's Payments tab, which means
    `ACCOUNTS / Cash Management` Read plus a project board's Read. Everybody else keeps the column's
    previous figure (converted value, or shoots) and makes no request for the money.
  - **Backend:** `GET /api/sales/projects/payments-summary?ids=…`
    ([payments-summary.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/payments-summary.js),
    [projectMoney.js](../backend/src/services/projectMoney.js)), under the same guards as
    `/projects/:id/payments`. Each project goes through the reader's reach, and the totals are
    tested against the Payments tab's own calculation.
  - No new permission or migration.
- **The money boards show a ₹ total under each column**, the way CRM shows "Est." and Bookings
  "Converted". Each total adds up the cards the column is showing, so it follows the column's period
  and search the way its count does.

  | Board | What each column shows |
  | --- | --- |
  | Employee Referral | **Owed** (Outstanding, Overdue), **Paid** (Paid), **Cancelled** (cancelled or stopped instalments) |
  | Payment Requests | **Requested**, **Approved**, **Rejected** |
  | Accounts Manager, scheduled payments | **Pending** |
  | Accounts Manager, cash entries | **Received** / **Spent** / **Transfer**, or **Total** by category |
  | Payroll Advance | **Owed** (Pending, Skipped), **Deducted** |
  | Payroll Recovery and Policy Breach | **Total** (an LOP breach is days, so it adds nothing) |
  | Payroll Main Page | **Net pay** |
  | Quotations | **Quoted** |
  | Assets | **Value**, from the purchase price |

  - **Pre Production and Production** show, under each column, how many shoots it holds and the
    nearest one still to come, as a phrase: "6 shoots, next on 14 Nov" (or "1 shoot" when none is still to come; nothing for an empty column). A shoot with no date of its own counts at
    its project's main event (`columnShoots`; `ColumnAmount` now also takes `text`).
  - **The boards that are not about money show the number that matters there**, under the open
    columns only (none under Completed, Cancelled, Submitted and the like):

    | Board | Under each column |
    | --- | --- |
    | Tasks | **Overdue N** (same rule as the Overdue tab) |
    | Attendance Requests | **Permission 12 h** (permission hours; leaves have no hours) |
    | Interviews | Yet to Connect to Form Submitted **Not updated 7+ days N** · Interview Scheduled **Date passed N**, else **Next interview 6 Nov** · decided columns none |
    | CRD Documents, Client Gifts, Feedback, Speak Up review | **Waiting 7+ days N** |
    | Client Storage | **Size 2.4 TB**, read from the footage size typed in |
    | Onboarding and resignation-form invites | **Expiring soon N** (within 2 days) |
    | Meetings | **Next 6 Nov** |

    - CRD Documents records no link-sent date, so "waiting" there counts from when the document was
      raised.
    - Helpers: `columnCount`, `columnNext`, `columnSumText`, `daysSince` and `expiresSoon` in
      [kanbanSummary.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/kanbanSummary.mjs).
  - **Every other board now shows a figure too**, worked out from rows it already shows (no pay
    or spend a viewer could not already see):

    | Board | Under each column |
    | --- | --- |
    | User Management | Employee Submission Pending **2 links expire in 2 days**, else **Oldest invite sent 12 days ago** · HR Onboarding Pending **Oldest waiting 9 days** · Active **3 reviews due this month** (Next Review Date; cards tagged "Review due 12 Nov") · Serving Notice **Next to leave: bc dc on 2 Dec** |
    | Attendance Requests | Pending **Waiting 2+ days N** · Approved **Permission N h** (it showed "0 h" on every column before) |
    | Attendance Register | Present **Late N** · Leave **Irregular N** |
    | Admin attendance | **Late days N** per branch |
    | My Attendance | **Worked N h** · breaks **Break N h** |
    | My Payslips | **Paid ₹…** · **Due ₹…** |
    | My Speak Up | Pending **Waiting 7+ days N** |
    | Users | **Not linked N** (logins with no employee record) |
    | Roles | **Users N** |
    | Vendors | Active **Crew-ready N** |
    | Contacts | **New 30 days N** |
    | Project Settings, Services | **No deliverable N** |
    | User Activity Logs | **Failed N** (response status 400+) |
    | WhatsApp Activity Log | Failed **Resendable N** · Queued/Processing **Waiting 1+ days N** |
    | Interview form invites | **Expiring soon N** |
    | CRM Reports | **Connected N**, **Talk 3 h 20 m**, **Worked N h**, **Attempts N**, **Calls N** by report |

    Excluded Numbers and the Project Settings deliverables board have nothing worth adding up, so
    they keep their counts alone.
  - **Figures read as plain sentences, and say nothing when there is nothing.** A count reads
    number first ("3 overdue", "2 waiting 7+ days"); a count of 0 or a date with nothing still to
    come is not shown at all, rather than "Expiring soon 0" or "Next none". `columnOldest` and
    `columnNextWho` give "Oldest invite sent 12 days ago" and "Next to leave: bc dc on 2 Dec".
  - **A count under a column names its cards.** Wherever a column shows a count, such as "Not
    updated 7+ days 4", "Overdue 3", "Expiring soon 1", "Late 2" or "Failed 6", each card it counts
    carries an amber tag saying why: "Not updated 15 days", "Overdue 3 days", "Expires 6 Nov",
    "Late", "Failed (500)". The count and the tag come from the same rule, so they always agree.
    `KanbanBoard` takes `cardFlag(row, column)`.
  - An Employee Referral card now reads "₹6,000.00 · 1/3 Paid" instead of the cut-off
    "₹0.00 outstanding of ₹6,00…".
  - User Management is left out on purpose: a salary total would show pay to anyone who can open the
    board.
  - Shared helper: `columnTotal` in [kanbanSummary.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/kanbanSummary.mjs). No
    permission changes; each board adds up only the rows it already shows.
- **Every Board card now has its own ⋮ (More), with the same options as its row's ⋮ in Table
  view.** Before, a card could only be opened or dragged; anything else meant switching back to
  Table. Now, for example, a Payment Request card offers View, Edit, Approve, Reject and Withdraw.
  - **Same options, same permissions.** The card's ⋮ and the row's ⋮ are built by the same
    function, so a person never sees an option on a card that their row would not offer. A card with
    nothing to offer has no ⋮.
  - **A smaller menu.** The card's ⋮ opens a compact menu: tighter rows, smaller type, as wide as
    its longest option. It opens with a short grow-and-fade from the ⋮, which is turned off when the
    device asks for reduced motion. On a phone its rows keep a finger's height. Shared as
    `OptionsMenu`'s `compact` prop.
  - **Boards inside a panel or dialog** (Onboarding and Offboarding invites, Project Settings,
    Excluded Numbers) open the menu above it, as their rows do.
  - **Shared Board.** [KanbanBoard.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/KanbanBoard.js) takes
    `cardActions(row)` and `cardMenuProps`; the CRM leads board has the same card ⋮.
  - **Wired on:** Payment Requests, Accounts Manager (payments and cash entries), Users, Roles,
    Assets, Vendors, Client Storage, Contacts, User Management, Onboarding and Offboarding invites,
    Attendance Requests, Interviews, Employee Referral, Payroll Advance and Recovery, Speak Up
    review, Tasks, Projects, Bookings, Pre Production, Production, Post Production, Client Gifts,
    Feedback, Project Settings, CRD Documents, Quotations, Meetings, CRM leads and Excluded Numbers.
  - **Left as they were:** boards whose table rows have no ⋮ — logs, registers and reports: User
    Activity Logs, WhatsApp Activity Log, Attendance Register, admin attendance, Employee Attendance,
    My Payslips, Payroll Main Page, Speak Up (mine), CRM Reports and the interview form invites.
  - No permission changes.
- **Employee Referral: Delete on each row's ⋮, and for ticked rows.** A referral and its
  instalments can be deleted, and payroll then has nothing of it to pay. The employee's Referred By
  reads empty afterwards.
  - **Never once something on it was paid**, through payroll or by hand. A paid instalment is a
    record of money that left the studio. Such a row offers no Delete, the server refuses it (409),
    and a bulk Delete leaves it alone and counts it as not deleted. This is the same rule the
    employee form already keeps when Referred By is cleared.
  - **Access:** `HRM / Employee Referral` Read / Write; the bulk Delete also needs
    `ADMIN / Table Select All`. The server only deletes a referral the person can see (404 otherwise).
  - No new permission or migration. Back end: `deleteReferral` in
    [referrals/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/referrals/service.js), `DELETE
    /api/hrm/referrals/:id` and `/bulk`. Screen:
    [EmployeeReferralsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeReferralsPage.js).
- **Employee Referral: an Instalments column ("1/3 Paid"), and a column for every instalment
  month, including the 9th.** The table had fixed 3rd Month and 6th Month columns. A referral
  recorded over three instalments (3rd, 6th and 9th month) had its 9th month left off the table,
  even though the ⋮ offered "Mark 9th month paid".
  - The table now shows one column for each month any referral on it is paid in.
  - **Instalments** counts how many are paid out of how many, read like Shoots Done / Progress:
    "0/2 Paid", "1/3 Paid", "2/2 Paid".
  - Paid by payroll or by hand both count. A stopped instalment still counts toward the total.
  - [EmployeeReferralsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeReferralsPage.js),
    `instalmentProgress` and `instalmentMonthsOf` in
    [referralPayouts.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/referralPayouts.js). No permission changes.
- **Employee Referral: "Mark 3rd month paid" / "Mark 6th month paid" are back on each row's ⋮.**
  The studio settles some referral instalments by hand (cash, a bank transfer). This option was
  removed by mistake on 25 Oct 2026, and is now restored the way it worked before: pick the
  instalment, confirm, and the referral moves to Settled once nothing is left to pay.
  - **Payroll cannot pay it twice.** Payroll adds only instalments that are still unpaid to the
    referrer's Referral Bonus. So one marked paid by hand is left out of the month it falls due in.
  - If that month's payroll was already worked out with the bonus in it, paying the month asks for
    a Refresh first, which drops the bonus.
  - If an instalment is marked paid at the very moment its payroll month is being paid, payroll now
    refuses ("Refresh the month, then pay it") instead of paying the bonus again.
    [payroll-register/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/service.js)
  - An instalment already paid through payroll, or stopped because the referrer or the employee
    has left, cannot be marked paid.
  - **Access:** `HRM / Employee Referral` Read / Write. Without it the ⋮ is not shown, and the server
    refuses a referral outside the person's reach.
  - **No new permission or migration.** Back end:
    [referrals/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/referrals/service.js) `updatePayout` and
    `PATCH /api/hrm/referrals/payouts/:payoutId`. Screen:
    [EmployeeReferralsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeReferralsPage.js).
  - **Payroll checked against the local data.** Revathi Krishnan's referral of Keerthana Raj carries
    ₹3,000 into December 2026 and ₹3,000 into March 2027. DBS-REF-000005 is ₹0 because Settings →
    Employee Referral's amount is ₹0; a referral keeps the amount it was recorded with.
- **Every project board now shows converted values: Bookings, Projects and Post Production.** Each
  card shows its Initial Converted Value (e.g. `₹1,20,000`) after its event date. Each column shows
  "Converted ₹…" under its heading: the total of the cards it is showing, so it follows the column's
  period and search the same way its count does. This lives once in the shared project card
  (`PROJECT_BOARD_CARD` and `projectColumnAmount` in `lib/projectStatuses.mjs`), and the CRM board's
  "Est." / "Converted" figure is drawn by the same shared `ColumnAmount` (`KanbanSummary.js`). No new
  permission is needed: these tables already show the Initial Converted Value column.
- **Every board's column period list is now All / Today / This week / This month / Last month.**
  "2 months" is gone. "Last month" is the 30 days before "This month" (which is the last 30 days),
  so the two never overlap, and its trend compares it with the 30 days before that. The CRM board
  asks the server for the same days. A column that was set to "2 months" goes back to All.
- **Edit Sale Details' Extra section lists what approved Extra Quotations added.** The shoots,
  services and deliverables an approved raised request put on the project now appear under **Added**, in
  their shoot, marked "Extra quotation EXT-… · already counted in Payments" - the amount shown, nothing to
  type, never counted twice. **Updated Total** now includes the approved extra quotations ("incl. ₹… extra
  quotations"), so it matches Payments. Such an item can be removed from its ⋮ like any other: its Removed
  line says "From extra quotation EXT-…" and starts at the amount approved for it, so publishing it takes
  that amount off; ⋮ Add back puts it back as it was. The client's quotation link (and its PDF) shows them
  too: what approved extra quotations added - and any extra quotation raised by hand, by its name - is
  listed under **Added Items** with no prices, and its **Updated Total Amount** counts the approved extra
  quotations, the same figure as Payments; the section now appears as soon as one is approved, published
  revision or not.
  [SaleExtrasSection.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SaleExtrasSection.js),
  [sale-extras/service.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/sale-extras/service.js)
- **Services and deliverables can be removed and added back from Edit Sale Details' Extra section, as
  often as needed.** The newest line about each item has a ⋮: **Remove** while it is on its shoot (an
  Added line), **Add back** while it is off (a Removed line); older lines about the same item have none.
  Each Removed line says where the item came from and starts at the value it stood at - **From the
  quotation** at its quotation line price (unit price x quantity, ₹0 if complimentary), or **Added as an
  extra** at the amount it was published at - still editable before publishing. Add back returns the same
  line to Service Creation (a quoted service with its post-production work and the deliverables it
  brings): while the removal is unpublished nothing is left behind - a quoted item is back as quoted, an
  extra at the amount it was added at; after a published removal it comes back as an addition starting at
  what the removal took off. Remove takes an item off exactly as Service Creation does; an addition never
  published simply goes. Picking a removed quoted item again in Service Creation also counts as putting it
  back, however much later - it used to count only within a minute. Remove and Add back ask for what
  Service Creation's own changes ask: PROJECT / Projects (or Show All Projects) Read / Write.
  [SaleExtrasItemsTable.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SaleExtrasItemsTable.js),
  [sale-extras/service.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/sale-extras/service.js)
- **Client Requests can raise and decide project change requests.** A new **Raised Requests** view
  (switch in the header, beside **From Client App**, which is unchanged) and **Raise Request** let the
  studio ask, for a booked project, for a **new shoot** with its services and deliverables, **services**
  or **deliverables** for one of its shoots, or a **correction** - with Create Project's own shoot and
  line pickers, and no prices. Whoever holds the new **CLIENT / Request Approval** permission prices and
  approves or rejects each item (₹0 for complimentary, a reason for each rejection), can save progress or
  ask the requester for more, and submits the decision: only the approved items are added to the project,
  their total is recorded as one approved Extra Quotation so it counts on Payments once (Sale Extras does
  not price them again, and the payment schedule is not rewritten), and an approved correction becomes an
  HRM task for the project's Project Manager. Requests are Waiting, In progress, Accepted, Partially
  accepted or Declined, each decided once (a second or stale decision is refused), with every step in
  their Activity. Migration `20261104150000_project_change_requests` adds three tables and the permission,
  granted to **Super Admin only** - tick it in Role Management for the Project Managers and Admins who
  should approve; raising stays on CLIENT / Client Requests (Read / Write).
  [RaiseRequestDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/client-management/RaiseRequestDialog.js),
  [RaisedRequestPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/client-management/RaisedRequestPanel.js),
  [change-requests/service.js](../backend/src/modules/client/change-requests/service.js)
- **Shedule Payment shows what the project has received and still owes.** In Edit Sale Details and
  Projects → Start / Edit Project the summary above the table now lists **Received**, **Balance
  Amount** and, when there are any, **Refunded** and **Overpaid** (the table itself has no balance
  column). The balance starts at the Updated Total Amount - Signed
  Quotation plus Net Extra (the published Sale Extras, now shown on Start / Edit Project too, read
  from the server there) plus any approved **Extra Quotation** (now shown as its own line) - and
  only money actually received comes off it: a payment that is Due, Overdue, On Hold or still to come
  takes nothing off, a part payment takes off only what was paid, a Client Refund is added back, and
  a withdrawn or corrected receipt moves it the next time the schedule is opened. The figures are
  read by the server from Accounts' cash entries every time
  ([service.js](../backend/src/modules/accounts/scheduled-payments/service.js) `projectLedger`,
  returned by `GET /api/sales/projects/:id/payment-schedule`) and nothing new is stored, so no
  migration. Money paid past the total shows as Overpaid instead of a negative balance; money
  received on no payment counts in the Balance Amount and is noted under it. Same permissions as
  the schedule itself; Create Project is unchanged. Typing "done" in a payment's remarks records no
  money, so each saved payment not yet received in full now has **Receive** under its Amount, for
  somebody with ACCOUNTS / Cash Management write: it opens Accounts' own scheduled
  payment panel (Clear or Partially paid, then Cash Received - mode, transaction ID, proof), and
  once recorded the schedule, Received and the Balance Amount are read again. With unsaved changes
  to the schedule it asks for Update Project first, so nothing typed is lost
  ([useScheduleReceiver.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/useScheduleReceiver.js)).
- **Every WhatsApp message under Settings → Templates can be switched ON or OFF, and Send WhatsApp
  shows only when it can be used.** Each message sent over WhatsApp has a **Send this message**
  switch above its wording - Cash Received, Employee Invite, Login Credentials, Client Login
  Credentials, CRD Document Link, Payment Reminder, Shoot Crew Notice and Shoot Crew Removed, the
  three Production messages, and each tab of the Wishes Scheduler (Birthday, Anniversary, Work
  Anniversary) - plus a new **Interview Application Invite** entry for the invite's WhatsApp wording
  and switch. OFF means the message is not sent at all: its **Send WhatsApp** button is hidden (and
  refused by the server, `409`), and its automatic sends stop - a Shoot Crew change while it is OFF
  is settled without a message, so switching it back on sends no backlog; a Production step completes
  with no message. Every message is ON until somebody switches it; nothing changes for existing
  messages. Attendance WhatsApp Report, Photo Selection Submitted, New Lead Welcome and Interview
  Welcome keep the switches they already had. **The offboarding and feedback messages can now be sent
  on WhatsApp too, each with its switch** (they were copy-only): the **Offboarding Form** from the
  form's sent screen; from a form's row menu, **Send reminder on WhatsApp** while it is open and in
  date (the Offboarding Reminder wording, unused until now), **Send confirmation on WhatsApp** once
  approved and **Send the refusal on WhatsApp** once rejected - each opening the message with its Copy
  and Send WhatsApp - all to the employee's own number on their record; and **Feedback Thank You /
  Feedback Issues** from the dialog after Save Feedback, to the client main number on the project.
  Sent only when somebody presses the button - nothing is sent automatically, and the Copy options
  stay. The server refuses a message in the wrong state (a confirmation for a form not approved, a
  reminder past the link's last day). **Send WhatsApp** also stays hidden while your own WhatsApp is not
  linked - now including Image Selection's and Signature Album's **Send to Group** (Send to Client,
  which only opens WhatsApp, is unchanged; Link a group still pairs WhatsApp and brings the button
  back). A switch answers to the permission that rewords the message (`SETTINGS / Message Template`,
  or `SETTINGS / Wishes`). Migration `20261103160000_message_template_switches` adds the empty
  `message_template_switch` table; no existing row changes. No new permission
  ([messageTemplateSwitches.js](../backend/src/services/messageTemplateSwitches.js),
  [MessageSwitch.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/MessageSwitch.js)).
- **A vendor confirmed on a shoot is now told about it on WhatsApp, from the project's Production
  Manager.** Half an hour after the production manager sets a vendor to Confirmed, that vendor is sent
  what the shoot is, when and where it is, and the service they are on; they are reminded two days
  before it; they are told whenever the day, the place or their own service changes; and they are told
  not to travel if they come off it - the seat taken from them, put back to Waiting, the plan withdrawn
  or the shoot deleted. A vendor with no number saved waits in Settings rather than being lost, and
  gets their message the moment somebody saves one. Until now the app told a vendor nothing at all, so somebody rang them by hand
  and a vendor whose shoot had moved sometimes drove to the old venue. Switched on separately from the
  crew notice in Settings → Project Management → **Shoot crew notice**, and **switching it on messages
  nobody who is already confirmed** - every vendor standing is recorded as told, because telling the
  studio's whole vendor book at once from personal numbers is what gets a WhatsApp number banned.
  Six wordings under Settings → Templates, one per situation, so a reminder does not read like a first
  contact. Five messages a minute at most, no more than three from any one manager's phone, and no
  more than 30 an hour from one number counting the crew messages too - the same limit the New Lead
  Welcome already holds to, because a steady stream of automated messages from a personal number is
  what gets it banned. Off with `VENDOR_SHOOT_NOTICE_AUTOSEND=false`.
  [backend/src/modules/settings/shoot-crew-notice/vendorSender.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/shoot-crew-notice/vendorSender.js)

- **Onboarding puts a new employee into their departments' WhatsApp groups, and being relieved takes
  them out of every group.** A WhatsApp group in Settings now says which departments it serves (see
  below), and those two ends follow from it. **Joining:** creating an employee queues them into every
  group their departments claim - somebody in two departments gets the groups of both, and a group
  under no department is never one the app adds anybody to. **Leaving:** when a separation's last
  working day passes and the relieving closes their login, they are queued **out of every group the
  app has them in**, not only their departments' - a group somebody was put in by hand is one they can
  still read tomorrow. Removal is new: WhatsApp has no "ask them to leave", so it is Baileys' own
  remove, and it needs a linked WhatsApp that is an **admin** of the group, exactly as adding does.
  Both ride the queue that already existed for adding somebody by hand, so the statuses read on each
  employee's Employee Preference as before, with four more for leaving (queued, removed, was not in
  it, failed). **Removals wait 30 seconds apart** - far longer than the 5 between adds - because
  taking one leaver out of a dozen groups is the burst of group administration WhatsApp reads as
  automation, and nobody is waiting on it; adds are served first, since somebody is. Neither can
  break what it follows: both are queued **after** the transaction and never throw, so an employee is
  still created and a login still closes on the right day if WhatsApp is unreachable, and the queue
  is retried from the employee's own screen. Carries a **migration** adding one nullable column
  ([service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/whatsapp-groups/service.js),
  [sessionManager.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/whatsapp-chat/sessionManager.js)).
- **A WhatsApp group in Settings can now say which departments it is for.** Settings → Employee →
  **WhatsApp Groups** is now a **table of departments**: one row per department with its groups in a
  single comma-separated cell, and the row's ⋮ → **Edit** is where they are added and taken away. That
  is the question somebody actually asks - "which groups does Production have" - and the end the work
  happens from. Every active department is a row, including those with no groups, since a department
  missing from the table is one nobody would think to give groups to. Adding a group that the studio
  already uses puts it under this department **too**, rather than refusing a name that is taken: a
  group's name is unique because it is one group on WhatsApp. Removing takes the group out from under
  that department and **keeps the group**, which may serve others. **An employee's own WhatsApp
  Groups box now follows it**: it offers the groups of their departments rather than every group in
  the studio, with all of them **ticked for them** - taking one off is the decision, and the common
  case needs no clicks. A group they are already in that their departments no longer claim is still
  listed, marked "not in their department", because a membership that exists has to stay visible. The
  departments themselves stay where they are set, under **Employment Details** - this tab reads them
  and does not offer a second place to change them - but **Department now saves the moment it
  changes** on an employee who already exists, because it is the one field another screen reads
  before Save: picked and left unsaved, the WhatsApp Groups box sat empty while somebody had visibly
  chosen departments a moment earlier, and nothing on either screen said why. Only that field, only
  on an edit (a new employee's departments go in with the rest on Save), and a failure stays quiet
  since the form's own Save writes it again. The credentials page is told as well - it holds the
  employee as it was when the panel opened, so without that the groups box had already fetched and
  had no reason to ask again, and still sat empty right after somebody had chosen departments. An empty box says **which departments it looked
  at**, since "none saved yet" and "their departments have no groups" need opposite fixes: the first
  is a save on Employment Details, the second a change in Settings. A group may be for
  **several** departments - an "All Managers" group covers Sales and Production alike, and it is still
  one group on WhatsApp - so the departments are rows against the group rather than a single column,
  and the same group is simply added under each department that wants it.
  The list offered is the department register's own, so every department the studio has is there and a
  new one needs no change here; a renamed department reads as its new name without anything being
  rewritten. **Every group that exists today starts under no department**, which is the honest answer
  since nobody has said which department any of them is for - nothing was guessed or backfilled - and
  a group under no department is listed only when the dropdown shows all of them. This is the
  groundwork for onboarding adding a new employee to their departments' groups; **nothing adds or
  removes anybody yet**. Needs `HRM / Employee Management` Read to see and Read / Write to change, the
  permission the screen already uses, so no new permission - but it does carry a **migration** that
  creates one empty table
  ([service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/whatsapp-groups/service.js),
  [EmployeeWhatsAppGroupsPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/EmployeeWhatsAppGroupsPanel.js)).
- **The WhatsApp Activity Log now says which messages are waiting on a group.** A WhatsApp group is
  addressed either by its id or by its name, and the ones addressed by name - the attendance report,
  the wishes, the photo selection group - are looked up when the message is sent. Rename the group on
  WhatsApp and the lookup finds nothing, so the message silently never goes; a project whose group was
  never linked fails the same way. Nothing announced either, and the studio found out when somebody
  noticed a message had not arrived. A bar now sits **under the top bar on every page** listing them,
  grouped by the thing that fixes them rather than by the message - one project with six shoots is
  six messages waiting and one job, which is to link its group. It is on every page rather than on a
  settings screen because a studio that has not sent a client their shoot message does not find that
  out by opening a panel. There is no close button on purpose, so it holds only this one failure and
  nothing else: a send that failed because WhatsApp was down would never clear. The list is an
  accordion, so it folds away if it is in the way - which is not the same as closing, since the line
  saying how many are waiting stays on every page whatever the fold is doing. **Link group & retry** does the two halves of the job
  in order. A project's messages are addressed by the group's **id**, stored when somebody links the
  group in the app, so renaming a group on WhatsApp - or creating one with the right name - clears
  nothing by itself; only linking it does. So the button links the group from the presser's own
  WhatsApp first and then sends, through the module that owns the message, which already claims it so
  two people pressing at once cannot send it twice - the second is told it has already gone - and a
  successful retry clears the row for everybody, while one that fails again leaves it there for
  everybody. The row says what linking costs before anybody presses it: **whoever links becomes the
  project's sender**, and its production messages go out from their WhatsApp from then on. When the
  group cannot be linked, **nothing is sent at all** and the reason says why - no group of yours has
  that name, more than one does, your WhatsApp is not connected - instead of seven sends that are
  each certain to fail. A failure that renaming or relinking will never clear says where it is
  actually fixed: chat switched off for the studio points at Settings → WhatsApp Chat, and a group
  that is linked but whose linker no longer has a login asks for it to be linked again. A job of several messages is sent **one at a time,
  30 seconds apart**, never all at once, because a burst to one group is what risks the studio's
  paired number being flagged. That makes seven messages a three-minute job, so the button says where
  it has got to - "2 of 7 sent — next in 30s" - instead of going quiet. If the first message still cannot find the group, the
  job **stops there** rather than working through the rest - they all go to the same group, so there
  is nothing to learn from trying six more - and says so. If a retry is refused for going too
  quickly, it says how many were **not tried yet** and to press again shortly, rather than reporting
  them as still waiting on the group. The button appears only for somebody who holds both
  `PROJECT / Production` and `PROJECT / Pre Production` at **Read / Write**, since it sends a
  project's message and links its group - holding only the first gets a row naming who can link it
  rather than a button certain to be refused; a scheduled
  message is listed with no button, because its own scheduler sends it once the name matches. Seeing
  the bar needs **no permission at all**, deliberately. It had one of its own for a while and that was
  the wrong shape for the question: a permission answers *may you open this screen*, and this is not a
  screen anybody opens - it is a strip about your **own** work, and whose rows you get is a question
  the app answers one way for everybody with no setting per role. A tickable gate in front of that
  could only ever hide a project manager's own row from them, and that is exactly what it did: a new
  permission is granted to `SUPER_ADMIN` alone, as every new permission must be, so the manager of a
  project whose client never got their message was shown nothing until somebody ticked a box nobody
  knew existed. **What it lists depends on the viewer** instead, and that narrowing is the access
  control rather than a filter applied after one: somebody who may see every project
  (`PROJECT / Show All Projects` - Super Admin, administrators) gets all of them and the ownerless
  Settings groups too, and everybody else is shown only the projects they are the **project manager**
  of, matched on the employee their login is linked to. An employee on no such project gets an empty
  list and so no bar, and there is no call here that can answer with somebody else's row - which is
  why the route carries authentication and no permission guard, a considered exception to the rule
  that every route mounts one
  ([groupFailures.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/whatsapp-activity/groupFailures.js),
  [WhatsAppGroupFailuresBanner.js](../frontend/src/components/app-shell/WhatsAppGroupFailuresBanner.js),
  [whatsappGroupRetry.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/whatsappGroupRetry.mjs)).
- **Edit Project now has Linked Modules, so a Visual Curation project can be unlinked and linked
  again - unlink only, never a delete.** In AI Culling, AI Editing, Photo Selection and Signature
  Album, Edit Project shows the same boxes as Create Project, ticked where this project is linked;
  only modules the viewer may open are listed, never the project's own, and one the viewer may only
  read is greyed. Links are **per pair**: unticking AI Editing on an AI Culling project unlinks only
  those two - the AI Editing project keeps its ID, name, client, photos, edits and history in its
  own module, and stays linked to the others. Ticking it again reconnects **the same project** (no
  second one is made); ticking a module that has no project creates one, linked to this project.
  Sends follow the links on the server and on screen: AI Culling → AI Editing / Photo Selection /
  Signature Album and AI Editing → Signature Album are refused between unlinked projects
  (`409 MODULE_NOT_LINKED`), and the automatic edit-to-album sync waits until AI Editing and the
  album are linked again. The projects still share one set of photos - unlinking stops sending,
  nothing else. An unlink waits while the client still holds the other project's link (a published
  Photo Selection gallery, a published, unexpired Signature Album): the save is refused, says so,
  and offers that module's project to unpublish it in - nothing is unpublished for you. Every change
  needs Read / Write on that module, checked on the server, and is saved in one transaction with the
  name and client, so a refusal saves nothing. On the web and the desktop app. Migration
  `20261103150000_visual_curation_module_links` adds the empty `visual_curation_module_link` table;
  no existing row changes. No new permission
  ([moduleLinks.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/projects/moduleLinks.js),
  [CreateImageSelectionProject.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/CreateImageSelectionProject.js)).
- **Photo Selection → Expand now opens with Enabled and Disabled cards.** They lead its card grid -
  now two rows of six on a desktop screen (Enabled, Disabled and the ten summary cards; three rows of
  four on a tablet, two to a row on a phone) - and count every project by its Enabled switch as it
  stands now. Like every other card they carry the range's arrow and "vs Last Month" (or week,
  quarter...): how many were enabled and disabled at the start of the range, from when each project
  was created and switched off; Lifetime shows no arrow. A project switched off and back on inside
  the range leaves no record, so it counts as enabled at both ends. Each narrows the
  projects table to those projects when pressed - with its own "Enabled projects" / "Disabled
  projects" chip and × to let go - the only way to see the disabled ones, since the summary cards
  count enabled projects alone. Pressing either kind of card lets go of the other. On the web and
  the desktop app; the switch, the counts and the table are otherwise unchanged
  ([ExpandDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/dashboard/ExpandDialog.js),
  [imageSelectionDashboard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/imageSelectionDashboard.mjs)).
- **AI Culling, AI Editing and Signature Album are now Visual Curation modules of their own,
  each with a Dashboard and a Projects page like Photo Selection's - on the web and the desktop app -
  and no longer tabs inside a Photo Selection project.** The sidebar lists seven entries side by
  side: AI Feature, Photo Selling, Photo Selection, AI Culling, AI Editing, Signature Album, Album
  Proofing. Each module's Projects page lists the projects it belongs to, with the same search,
  collapse and status filter as Photo Selection's (its own statuses: a culling run's, the editing
  bay's, the album's), and opens a project straight on that module's workspace; Photo Selection's
  project now shows Photo Selection alone. Each Dashboard shows the module across every project,
  from one read-only request (`GET /api/image-selection/stage-dashboards/<module>`). Nothing about
  the work changed: the same projects, culling runs, edits, albums, client links and statuses, and
  every send (kept photos to AI Editing, to Photo Selection, to the Signature Album) works as
  before - "Open AI Editing" after a send now opens that module on the same project. **Each module
  owns its projects:** AI Culling, AI Editing and Signature Album projects are records of their own
  (`visual_curation_module_project`), each with its own ID - DBS-VCAC-, DBS-VCAE-, DBS-VCSA- -
  its own name and client, listed, edited and deleted only in its own module. **One Create Project,
  every module:** every module's New Project (Photo Selection's too) has a **Linked Modules** field
  in place of the old Selection Fields - the other modules the person may create projects in (Read /
  Write on each), never the form's own - and one submission creates a project in each, in one
  transaction, linked by being created together and nothing else (never a matching name), then says
  which IDs it made (`POST /api/image-selection/module-projects`). Edit changes that module's project
  and lists the projects it is linked with; its Linked Modules link and unlink them afterwards (the
  entry above). Delete removes
  that module's project and keeps the photos for the others, deleting the photos only with the last -
  Photo Selection's Delete included. Photos go on from one module to another only into a linked
  project: the server refuses any other send (`409 MODULE_NOT_LINKED`), and the AI Culling screen says
  "No linked AI Editing project" instead of offering anything else. **Each module answers to its own
  permission alone:** AI Culling's runs, folders, uploads and previews now open on AI Culling's
  permission, AI Editing's on AI Editing's, the album's on Signature Album's - a person with AI
  Culling and AI Editing but no Photo Selection sees exactly those two modules and can do all of
  their work - while Photo Selection's own client gallery, selections and publishing keep Project
  Management alone. Migration `20261103140000_visual_curation_module_projects` adds the table and
  gives every existing manual project its module records (new IDs, name and client copied); nothing
  existing changes. Projects from Project Management keep taking their modules from their allocation
  ([moduleProjects.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/projects/moduleProjects.js),
  [modules.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/projects/modules.js),
  [stage-dashboards/](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/stage-dashboards/),
  [CreateImageSelectionProject.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/CreateImageSelectionProject.js),
  [StageProjectsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/stage-dashboard/StageProjectsPage.js),
  [ImageSelectionProjectWorkspace.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/ImageSelectionProjectWorkspace.js)).
  **New permission `IMAGE_SELECTION / AI Culling`** opens the AI Culling module and everything in it:
  migration `20261103120000_ai_culling_dashboard_permission` writes
  it for Super Admin and `20261103130000_ai_culling_grants_follow_project_management` gives it to
  every role holding Project Management at the same level, as the studio asked, so everyone who
  culled from the old tab still can. AI Editing and Signature Album open on the permissions they
  already had. The desktop's sidebar heading now reads "Visual Curation", and both apps' Photo
  Selection header says "Photo Selection", as the sidebar does.
- **Work Anniversary wishes, under Settings → Templates → Wishes Scheduler.** A new **Work Anniversary
  Wishes** tab sits after Birthday Wishes and Anniversary Wishes, with ten editable wishes and the same
  live preview.
  Each year an employee completes with the studio, counted from their Date Of Joining, one is picked
  at random and sent to the Wishes Scheduler's WhatsApp group at its time, by its Sender or Rotation.
  It starts from the 1st anniversary; the joining day itself is never a work anniversary. A wish can
  use `{employee name}` and `{years}` ("3 years"). Someone who joined on 29 February is wished on the
  28th in a year without one. Only active employees are wished. The WhatsApp Activity Log shows each
  one as "Work anniversary wish". Migration `20261103120000_work_anniversary_wishes` adds the ten
  wishes (`INSERT IGNORE`, insert-only). No new permission: the page answers to `SETTINGS / Wishes`.
  (`backend/src/modules/settings/wishes/`, `backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js`,
  `frontend/src/components/settings/WishesPanel.js`, `SettingsOverlay.js`)
- **Add Request on Asset Management → Vendors raises a vendor's bill without leaving the page.** It
  opens the Payment Requests screen's own form on the **Vendor Payment** kind, with the row of kinds
  not drawn at all - this page is about vendors, and offering a salary advance here would be a
  question with one sensible answer and three wrong ones. What it raises is an ordinary payment
  request from the moment it is saved: it lands in Payment Requests, it is decided there, and it
  appears on this page's Vendor Payments view, which re-reads itself when one is raised. The button
  is drawn only for `ACCOUNTS / Payment Request Approval` **Read / Write** - the permission the POST
  behind it is guarded by - and is absent, not refused, without it
  ([VendorPaymentRequestButton.js](../frontend/src/components/assets/VendorPaymentRequestButton.js)).
- **Asset Management → Vendors now shows what the studio owes each vendor.** A picker beside the
  heading switches the screen between **Vendors** (the register, unchanged) and **Vendor Payments**:
  one row per Vendor Payment bill, with the vendor, the bill date, the amount, where it got to, and
  what has actually left the account against it - the cash entries the approval wrote, summed by the
  server rather than added up on screen. Tabs for Pending, Approved and Rejected, and the three
  figures at the foot: billed, paid, still owed. One vendor's ledger is read through the table's own
  Vendor column filter, so there is no second picker above it asking the same question. Counted and
  totalled over everything the reader may see rather than over the tab in front of them, so switching
  tabs never changes what the studio owes.
  **Read-only on purpose:** raising a bill stays in HRM → Payment Request and deciding one stays in
  Payment Requests, where the approval form is what says how the money actually moves. A second place
  to approve money is a second answer to "has this been paid".
  It answers for **`ACCOUNTS / Payment Request Approval`**, not for Vendor Management - who may read
  what the studio is paying is that permission's answer - so a reader holding only Vendor Management
  is never offered the view, and the endpoint behind it refuses them in any case. The server's own
  visibility rule applies underneath: somebody who may not decide requests sees the bills they raised
  themselves. No permission was added and nothing changed in Role Management
  ([VendorPaymentsView.js](../frontend/src/components/assets/VendorPaymentsView.js),
  [payment-requests/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payment-requests/controller.js)).
- **A vendor payment now names its vendor by id.** The form has always picked the vendor from the
  register, but only `vendor_name` and `vendor_phone` were stored - so "this vendor's bills" could be
  matched by name alone, which a rename or two vendors called the same thing answers wrongly. The
  link (`payment_request.vendor_id`, indexed, with the vendor's own `paymentRequests`) is what the
  ledger reads by; the text columns stay as the copies the request was raised with, so a decided
  request still reads as it was approved and a vendor since removed from the register still says who
  was paid. Migration `20261102150000_payment_request_vendor_link` adds the column and backfills it
  only where the stored name belongs to exactly one live vendor - two vendors sharing a name is the
  one case a name cannot answer, so those rows are left for somebody to set rather than guessed at.

### Fixed
- **A leaver is now taken out of the studio's WhatsApp groups when the exit is recorded, not only
  weeks later.** The removal was wired to one place - the scheduled job that relieves somebody at the
  end of their notice - which left two kinds of people in every group they had ever been added to.
  An exit whose **last working day is already past** is relieved by the save itself, and that job only
  looks for exits not yet relieved, so it never saw them: HR recorded the exit, the login closed, and
  the groups were never touched. And anybody marked inactive by a **status change** has no exit at all
  for a job to find. Recording the exit now queues the removals itself, whatever the last working day,
  and **Employee → WhatsApp Groups has a "Remove from all groups" action** for the people already in
  that state - recording an exit retroactively would have closed their login and moved their reports,
  which is a lot to do to fix a WhatsApp group. The removals still go one at a time, about half a
  minute apart, from the studio's own number. Note that somebody serving notice is now removed when
  the exit is recorded rather than on their last day - they are still coming in, and they lose their
  work groups that day.

  **And marking somebody active again puts them back.** Their departments' groups are queued once
  more, which previously nothing did: the automatic add runs at creation only, and its rule is to
  leave alone any group somebody has acted on - so a returning employee's groups, all of them marked
  removed by the leaving, were skipped for exactly that reason. Only their **departments'** groups come
  back. A group somebody was added to by hand was a decision, and making it again is a person's to
  make.
  [backend/src/modules/hrm/separations/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/separations/controller.js)

- **Approving a payment request now shows what you are approving.** The Approve dialog asked for a
  remark and showed nothing else: the request code in the title, and no sign of which shoots the
  money was spread across, what each line was for, or what the line actually said. The breakdown was
  only on the record view, opened separately - so the honest answer to "how can I approve without
  seeing it" was that you could not. The same table the payment panel already draws now sits in the
  Approve dialog, and in the Reject dialog too, since a rejection is written *about* those lines.
  The side panel's short list also says each line's description, which it used to leave out - a line
  whose description was the whole point of it read as a bare figure against a shoot code. Nothing
  was missing from the data: the server always sent it.
  [frontend/src/components/accounts/usePaymentRequestActions.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/usePaymentRequestActions.js)

- **Every long dropdown in the app now searches the whole list instead of the most recent 200.** A
  picker like Shoot ID, Project or Vendor was handed a list when the form opened - capped so the
  payload stayed sane - and filtered that list in the browser as you typed. The cap reads like a page
  but nothing fetched the next one, so it was the limit of **what could be chosen at all**, and
  because the lists were ordered newest-first what fell off the end was the oldest: a studio that
  brought its past projects in through the Pre-Production import could not file a payment request, a
  cash entry or an extra quotation against any of them. Typing the id showed "No options available",
  which reads as the record not existing. On the development database that was 200 of 986 shoots and
  200 of 640 projects reachable. Typing now goes to the server - every word you type, in any order,
  against the id, the name and the code of whatever it belongs to - over every row, the way the
  Enquiry ID picker on Create Project already worked. Fixed in **Payment Requests** (Shoot ID,
  Vendor), **Accounts cash entries** (Project, Shoot ID) and **Extra Quotations** (Project, Shoot
  ID). The menu says "Showing 50 of 312" where more matched, so a list that stops no longer reads as
  one that has lost entries; the row already chosen keeps its name when you search for something
  else; and a picker is no longer disabled just because its first page came back empty, since typing
  is how the rest is reached.
  [backend/src/services/pickerSearch.js](../backend/src/services/pickerSearch.js)

- **Board columns and cards no longer cut words off.** A column's figure of one sentence ("Oldest
  invite sent 19 days ago", "Next to leave: Keerthana Raj on 2 Dec") was held on one line and clipped;
  it now wraps between its words, while a two-part money figure still keeps "Client paid ₹…" and
  "Balance due ₹…" whole. Column names ("Employee Submission Pending") and every card line - name,
  subtitle, status chip, amber tag - wrap too instead of ending in "…", on every Board through
  [KanbanBoard.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/KanbanBoard.js) and
