  [KanbanSummary.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/KanbanSummary.js), and the CRM lead card.
- **A long figure under a Board column no longer squeezes the column's period picker shut.** The
  picker ("All", "Today"…) keeps its width, and the figure beside it takes the rest and wraps onto a
  second line, only between its parts ("Client paid ₹7,36,000 ·" / "Balance due ₹3,219"), never cut off.
  [KanbanSummary.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/KanbanSummary.js) (`ColumnTrendBar`,
  `ColumnAmount`)
- **Production's table now reaches the right edge of the screen.** On a wide screen it stopped
  short after Status and left an empty strip. It now uses the table's `layout: "fill"`, which shares
  the spare width out among the columns, as User Activity Logs does. Narrower screens are unchanged:
  the table still scrolls sideways inside its pane.
  [ProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionPage.js)
- **User Management → Pending: the list down the side shows each name in full.** "Employee
  Submission Pending" was cut off to "Employee Submission Pe...". The list is wider now (288px from
  tablet width up), and a name that still does not fit wraps onto a second line rather than being
  cut short. On a phone the list still sits above the table.
  [SideFilterList.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/SideFilterList.js)
- **Projects and Post Production status tabs now list projects on old status names, and the
  payroll Board's Skipped column shows skipped deductions.**
  - **Projects and Post Production.** A project saved before 14 Oct 2026 on "Work in Progress - Pre &
    Production", "Work in Progress - Post Production" or "Delivered" was reachable only from the All
    tab. It now appears under the tab that replaced its status (In Progress or Completed), the same
    column it already stood under on the Board. So the tab counts now match the Board. On the local
    data, that brings 8 projects into the In Progress and Completed tabs.
    [ProjectsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectsPage.js),
    [ProjectWorkflowModulePage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectWorkflowModulePage.js)
  - **Advance Salary and Recovery.** The Board's Skipped column was always empty: "Skipped" is not a
    status, and the Board only read the status. A deduction that has been moved off a month and is
    still owed now stands under Skipped on the Board, the same rows the Skipped tab lists. Once it is
    Deducted or Completed it moves to that column. The Skipped column also gets its own colour.
    [payrollTabs.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/payrollTabs.mjs) (`boardStatusOf`)
  - No permission changes: both screens keep the access they had.
- **Nebula comes before the ⋮ on every module header.** User Management, CRD Documents, AI Feature (and an event's
  workspace), Image Selection and a Photo Selling gallery passed their ⋮ in with the page's buttons,
  so it drew before Nebula. They now hand it to `ModulePageHeader`'s own `menu` slot, and every header
  ends the same way: the buttons, then Nebula, then ⋮. A test reads every header so a ⋮ cannot slip
  back in front. (`EmployeeVerificationPage.js`, `AiFeatureNavigation.js`, `AiEventWorkspacePage.js`,
  `ImageSelectionNavigation.js`, `GalleryWorkspacePage.js`, `CrdDocumentsPage.js`, `frontend/test/header-menu-after-nebula.test.mjs`)
- **Every Board now shows the same records as its table, each in the right column.** A check of all
  41 boards found these, now fixed:
  - **CRM Leads**
    - The board adds a column for any status the leads in view actually hold, such as an imported
      "Inactive", so those leads no longer go missing.
    - "Converted & Followup" shows on Dum Dum and Corp whenever such leads exist.
    - Unassigned shows whenever the reader can see unassigned leads.
    - The statuses come from the same scoped `column-values` read the table's filters use, so no
      permission is widened.
  - **Projects, Post Production and Bookings**
    - Old statuses (Cancelled & Refunded, Client not Turned, Duplicated, Date Elapsed) stand under
      their own name instead of "Yet to Start".
    - A drop out of Yet to Start, to In Progress or to Completed, is refused and points to Start
      Project. It used to skip Start Project's setup and Pre Production.
  - **Scheduled Payments:** the board is given the same payments as the table's tab, not every
    payment.
  - **Production**
    - A Coordinator's board has a column for every status their projects hold.
    - A Rejected shoot no longer makes a crew project read Work in Progress.
  - **Assets, Vendors, Client Storage and Asset Requests**
    - They read every page, not the first 50 or 100. The footer counts the rows drawn.
    - Paging is in a stable order (`createdAt`, then `id`).
  - **Interviews**
    - An application invite past its expiry reads Expired; this is worked out on read, without a
      write.
    - A candidate with an imported status the app does not know carries a "Status not recognised"
      chip.
    - The paged candidate board shows each column's server total ("40 of 212").
  (`CRMPage.js`, `lib/crmBoardOrder.mjs`, `lib/projectStatuses.mjs`, `ProjectsPage.js`, `SalesManagerPage.js`,
  `AccountsManagerPage.js`, `lib/productionBoard.mjs`, `ProductionPage.js`, `lib/everyPage.mjs`,
  `services/assets/assets.service.js`, the asset/vendor/client-storage/asset-request controllers,
  `hrm/interview/invites.js`, `InterviewPage.js`, `data-table/KanbanBoard.js`)
- **Move to Active and Create Credentials no longer fail on a busy server.** Both hashed the new
  password (bcrypt, cost 12 - a CPU-heavy step) inside their database transaction, which held the
  employee's rows locked meanwhile and, when the server was busy, ran the transaction past its
  5-second limit: the rejoin or the new login was rolled back and the screen got a 500. The full
  backend test run hit it (`employee-rejoin-password.test.js`, 500 after 6 s). The password is now
  hashed before the transaction opens; what is saved is unchanged
  ([employees/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/employees/controller.js)).
- **No Board hides a record any more.** The shared `KanbanBoard` dropped any row whose status matched
  none of its columns, so a board could look complete while records were missing. Those rows now go
  into an **Other** column at the end, drawn only while it holds something; nothing can be dropped
  into it. In User Management, the Pending tab's Board has a column for each pending kind (Employee
  Submission Pending, HR Onboarding Pending, HR Offboarding Pending, Review Pending), and picking a
  kind shows its column alone. The Active tab's Board also shows the Serving Notice column, because
  Active includes people on notice. Its columns now run in the order a person moves through them:
  Employee Submission Pending, HR Onboarding Pending, Active, Serving Notice, InActive. The HR Offboarding list's Board loses its Approved column, which
  could never hold a card.
  (`frontend/src/components/data-table/KanbanBoard.js`,
  `frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeVerificationPage.js`, `OffboardingInviteDialog.js`)
- **A Photo Selling upload now answers only after its temporary files are deleted.** The upload
  route replied from inside its `try` and deleted the original's, preview's and thumbnail's
  temporary `.part` files in the `finally` after, so the caller could hear back while two of them
  were still on disk - which failed `photo-selling-http.test.js` on CI's slower disk. The reply is
  now decided first and sent after the clean-up; every status and message is as before. A new test
  slows deletion down and fails on the old order. Backend only.
  ([photo-selling/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/photo-selling/controller.js))
- **A branch filter in a page header no longer swells when you pick a branch.** The header's own CSS
  sizes every labelled icon button in its action row to 36px square - right for a ⋮ or a refresh
  standing in the row, and catastrophic for the **×** inside a filter's chip, which it caught and
  blew up to 36px at 1rem: the chip came out taller than the field holding it, so the control spilled
  out of its box and the whole bar changed height the moment a branch was ticked. The × now says it
  belongs to a chip and the rule leaves it alone. A filter in a header also takes `size="sm"` now - a
  fixed 36px holding nothing, one branch or five, level with the switch beside it - so the bar is one
  height whatever is ticked ([globals.css](../frontend/src/app/globals.css),
  [MultiSelectField.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/MultiSelectField.js)).
- **The cash book's Category filter now lists every category, not only the ones already used.** It
  was derived from the rows on screen, so the filter offered the three or four spend categories that
  already had an entry and none of the others: "Vendor Payment" was not on the list until the first
  vendor payment was approved, and the entry that approval wrote could not be filtered for until the
  page was read again. A filter that cannot name an empty category is one nobody can use to check
  whether it is empty. Category and Payment Mode now name the studio's own lists, the way a status
  column already named its module's statuses, and whatever the rows hold beyond those lists is still
  offered - so a category since renamed stays reachable from its own filter
  ([accountsConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/accountsConfig.js),
  [tableCells.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/tableCells.js)).
- **An approved salary advance now reaches payroll by itself, and is taken back off a payslip.** It
  was two records that did not know about each other: the payment request that asked for the money
  and was approved, and HRM → Payroll → Advance Salary, which is what actually deducts it. Nothing
  joined them - no column, no code path, and the repayment the employee agreed to when raising it was
  stored, shown on the record and then **never read by anything**. So an approved advance reached
  payroll only if somebody remembered to retype it on the other screen, and when nobody did the
  studio paid it out and never took it back. Approving one now writes that Advance Salary row itself,
  against the employee who raised it, for the amount approved, and the money comes off that month's
  payslip as its Salary Advance through the same `syncPayroll` the payroll screen's own form uses.
  The row carries the request code and the repayment agreed on its Reason, so the payroll screen says
  where it came from, and the advance links back to the request (`payroll_advance.payment_request_id`,
  **unique** - approving the same request twice cannot leave two deductions behind it).
  **Which month:** the payroll month still being paid (`openPayrollMonth`) - approved before this
  month's payday it comes off this month, after it the next - and never a month already paid, which
  payroll refuses anyway. It is written in the approval's own transaction, so a request marked paid
  with no deduction behind it cannot happen. An advance whose requester is linked to no employee
  record is now **refused** with that said, rather than paid with no payslip to recover it from.
  [payment-requests/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payment-requests/controller.js),
  [payroll-advance/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-advance/service.js)
  Ships with migration `20261102140000_payroll_advance_from_payment_request` - one nullable column,
  its unique index and its key, which cannot fail on existing data because every advance already
  there was entered by hand and leaves it NULL. **Run `npx prisma migrate deploy`.** No permission
  changed. **Still by hand:** an advance the employee asked to repay *over several months* is created
  as a one-month Advance Salary like any other; turning it into instalments is the existing Convert
  to Recovery on that screen, and the months agreed are on the row's Reason for whoever does it.
- **A payment request's expense lines now ask the question the request is actually making.** One
  table was asking one set of words of three different things, so two of them read wrongly. An
  **advance against expenses** is money wanted *before* it is spent: its lines said "Expense Date -
  the day the money was spent" and refused any day still to come, which is the very day an advance
  is usually for, and called an estimate an "Expense Amount". They now read **Date Needed** - a
  future day expected and allowed - and **Estimated Amount**, totalling to Estimated Advance Total.
  An **expense submission settling an excess** is unspent advance money being handed *back*: its
  lines now read **Date Returned** and **Amount Returned** under "Money being returned", totalling
  to Total Being Returned, and it is **no longer asked what the money was spent on** - there is
  nothing it was spent on, so that box is gone rather than sitting there wanting an answer. A
  **reimbursement**, and a vendor's bill, describe money already spent and keep the wording they
  had. Which settlement counts as the excess is the studio's own `means_excess` flag, so renaming
  the option in Field Settings carries the behaviour with it.
  [paymentRequestConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/paymentRequestConfig.js),
  [PaymentRequestExpenseLines.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PaymentRequestExpenseLines.js)
  The expense type is optional on a line now and required by the request instead, since only the
  request knows which settlement it is, so this ships with migration
  `20261102130000_expense_type_optional_on_an_excess` - one widening of `expense_type` to accept
  NULL, which cannot fail on existing rows because every one of them already holds a value. **Run
  `npx prisma migrate deploy`.** A type sent on an excess anyway is dropped rather than stored, and
  a return reads as a dash in the approver's breakdown rather than an empty cell. No permission
  changed.
- **An approved payment request now writes a cash entry per shoot it was spent on, and per project
  the money came back for.** A request itemising several of either became a single entry in Accounts
  for the whole total, and because an entry carries one shoot and one project, an entry whose lines
  named two could honestly claim neither - so that money reached nobody's books, and a request mixing
  a courier line in with its shoots reached not even the project. Approving one now writes a row for
  each, worth exactly what its own lines came to; nothing is divided, because every itemising kind
  already stores its amount as those lines' total. **Money out is per shoot and money in is per
  project**, which are the two rules Accounts already applies to its own cash book: a spend happens
  on a shoot, while money comes back for a project as a whole - so an excess returning money across
  two projects is two rows, one per project. A line naming neither is folded into the one project the
  rest of them name, and stands as its own row only when there is no single project to fold it into.
  A salary advance, which itemises nothing, is still the one entry it always was. Each row carries the
  same payment mode, reference and proof, since it is one payment; the request's Cash Entries column
  lists every number it wrote, rather than the first of them. A request whose amount has drifted from
  the lines underneath it is now refused with that said, rather than paid as rows that quietly do not
  add up to what was approved.
  [payment-requests/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payment-requests/controller.js)
  Two things writing several rows exposed, fixed with it: **two approvers arriving together can no
  longer both pay the same request** - the decision is claimed inside the transaction and the second
  finds nothing to claim, where before each wrote its own entries and the spend was counted twice -
  and **the payment proof is uploaded once** for the whole approval and attached to every row
  (`recordCashEntry` takes a stored proof now), rather than the same file being stored again for each
  shoot and left in the bucket by a row that failed.
  [cash-entries/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/accounts/cash-entries/controller.js)
  **The link between the two moved onto the entry** (`cash_entry.payment_request_id`, replacing
  `payment_request.cash_entry_id`, which could hold only one), so this ships with migration
  `20261102120000_payment_request_cash_entries_per_shoot` - it backfills the existing links before
  adding the key and drops the old column last. **Run `npx prisma migrate deploy`.** No permission
  changed: approving a request is the same route and the same guard.
- **Schedule Payment's boxes line up again.** The Date cell is the tall one - its box carries "Date
  not known?" underneath, or two lines naming the shoot the payment follows - and the table's default
  middle alignment centred every *other* box against that height, so the date box stood above the
  Category, Remarks, Percentage and Amount boxes beside it. The row's cells are topped now, so every
  box begins on the same line and the links hang below it. The Final Settlement's dash and the row's
  delete sit on that line too, rather than riding at the very top. A payment that follows a shoot
  named for several - "3 days before Groom Haldi + Bride Haldi" - ran to four and five lines in that
  column and stretched the whole row with it; it is held to two now, with the whole phrase on the
  title and Change opening the dialog that spells it out, so every row is the same height.
  [SchedulePaymentSection.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/SchedulePaymentSection.js)
- **A day can no longer hold both a leave and a permission.** The overlap check compared a request
  only with its own kind, so a permission could be raised over a leave day (and spent against the
  month's permission limit) and a leave over a permitted day. Now a leave or comp-off is refused over a
  day with a pending or approved permission, and a permission over a day with a pending or approved
  leave or comp-off; a rejected one never blocks. The refusal is a 409 `REQUEST_CLASH` naming the
  request in the way (type, status, dates, times), and the Raise / Edit Request form shows it in a
  pop-up - "That day already has a request" - with **Keep it** or **Delete it and raise this one**,
  which deletes that request and raises the new one as it was filled in. Requests both raised before
  this change are left as they are.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/controller.js),
  [AttendanceRequestFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestFormPanel.js)
- **The daily attendance report no longer calls somebody on a permission Uninformed Leave.** Not in
  yet, with a permission covering the time of the report - 9:30 to 12:00 and the report at 9:45 - they
  were listed under both Uninformed Leave and Permission. They are now under **Permission** alone,
  whether it is approved or still waiting on its approvers (said "(approval pending)"), and the
  Uninformed Leave count leaves them out. A permission not yet begun or already ended still leaves
  somebody not in as Uninformed Leave - said there alone. Leave, Uninformed Leave and Permission now
  name each person once: on leave (or with a leave pending) is under Leave only, not in without a
  permission covering the time under Uninformed Leave only, and Permission lists the rest who have one.
  Permission's count includes pending ones, as its list does.
  The register's rows carry `pendingPermissions` beside `permissions` for it. The WhatsApp message and
  the screen's Send copy say the same (`reportText.js`, `attendanceReport.mjs`).
  [reportText.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/reportText.js),
  [attendanceReport.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/attendanceReport.mjs),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js)
- **Payroll files a month held for the notice under On Hold, not Pending.** With Hold salary during
  notice on, a leaver's held month showed as Pending. That made it look due on its payday, and the
  Pending total included it. It now shows and counts as **On Hold** in the tabs, the Payment Status
  column and the Board. Its record stays Pending, so the final settlement still pays it as before.
  It cannot be dropped back on Pending on the Board. The Name column and the Board card read
  "bc dc (Serving Notice)", in Payroll only. The note in its form ("Salary is held during
  this employee's notice period...") is now red. (`frontend/src/lib/payrollRegister.mjs`,
  `frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollMainSection.js`)
- **Work History says "Serving notice period" for somebody on notice, instead of "Working here now".**
  The last step is in amber, the colour the repository gives Serving Notice, and shows the last
  working day under it, then their current role. Everyone else's history is unchanged. This applies
  to the employee's record and to My Profile. (`frontend/src/lib/workHistory.mjs`,
  `frontend/src/components/employees/WorkHistoryFlow.js`)
- **An employee's record now shows their Last Working Day.** For somebody serving notice, the date
  their notice ends was saved but not shown in Details or in the side Info panel. It now sits under
  Date Of Joining. The Details view leaves it out for anyone with no date recorded.
  (`frontend/src/constants/infoPanelConfig.js`, `frontend/src/constants/detailHelp/people.js`)
- **A rejoined employee keeps their work history, and their time away is no longer counted as
  Absent.** Move to Active deleted the old separation and kept nothing of the departure. Because the
  joining date stayed and the relieving date was cleared, attendance and payroll then counted every
  day between leaving and rejoining as an absence.
  - New table `employee_rejoin` (migration `20261031160000_employee_rejoin`, additive only). Move to
    Active writes one row before the separation is deleted: last working day, separation type and
    reason, the rejoining day, the reason and who did it.
  - A **Work History** tab, next to Org Chart on an employee's record and on each employee's own My
    Profile, draws every stint as a flow like the project Activity tab. It shows Joined (date, role),
    each Last working day (role, how and why they left), Rejoined (date, new role, time away) and
    Working here now, with time with the studio, stints and times rejoined at the top. The pieces are
    `components/employees/WorkHistoryFlow.js` and `lib/workHistory.mjs`. The employee list and
    `/api/user/profile` send `rejoins` for it.
  - Migration `20261031170000_employee_rejoin_role` adds `designation` and `department` to the rejoin
    row: the role the stint that ended was worked in, kept as it stood. The record's own role may
    change after they come back.
  - The days strictly between leaving and rejoining are left out everywhere attendance counts an
    employee: the register, the range report, leave counting, the employee's own page and totals,
    and payroll's counted days (`awayBetweenStints`, `stintBounds`). A day they did log in still
    counts.
  - Also fixed: an employee who has left no longer has the days after their last day listed and
    counted as owed on their own attendance page and totals. The register already left them out.
  - Checked end to end with a TRJ- test employee, who was then removed: left 10 Oct, rejoined 31 Oct,
    20 days away not counted, October payroll counted 11 days.

  Tests: `backend/test/employee-rejoin-history.test.js`, `frontend/test/work-history.test.mjs`. Run
  `prisma migrate deploy` on the VPS (part of the normal deploy).
- **A board's far columns can be reached without a trackpad.** A Board view wider than the screen
  (Interview has ten columns) hid the rest behind a sideways scrollbar that macOS does not draw for a
  mouse, so the columns past the edge looked cut off with no way to reach them. The shared
  `KanbanBoard` now draws a thin scrollbar under its columns, whatever the system's setting. It also
  shows ‹ › buttons at its left and right edges while there are more columns that way; each press
  scrolls about a screen. Every board gets this. Frontend only.
- **The frontend production build no longer fails in `next/font` on the invitation page's
  Fredoka face.** Asked for fixed weights (400, 500, 600), Google Fonts now serves Fredoka from
  extension-less `fonts.gstatic.com/l/font?kit=…` URLs, and Next's Google font loader reads the
  file extension off every URL ("Cannot read properties of null (reading '1')"). Fredoka is now
  loaded as its variable font (300-700, the same weights and more), which Google serves as plain
  `.woff2`. ([inv/invitationFonts.js](../frontend/src/app/inv/invitationFonts.js))
- **Renaming a Photo Selection folder no longer looks like a second shoot, and deleting one now
  removes it cleanly - its photos, selection items and limits - while the client link keeps
  working, on the web and Visual Curation Desktop.** A manual project's shoot was tied to its folder
  only by name, so renaming "wedding" to "wedding 02" left the selection items under the old name:
  Selection Items showed two shoots and the client gallery stopped showing the folder's photos
  under its items. Items now point at their folder by id (migration
  `20261102140000_image_selection_manual_shoot_folder` adds `manual_shoot_folder_id` and links
  every existing item to the folder its name matched, by the same rule the screens used), so a
  rename is one update of the same folder and its shoot. In a project linked to Project
  Management, a hand-made folder named like a shoot is now linked to that shoot by id the first
  time it is listed, so renaming it never grows a second folder for the shoot. **Delete** is one
  confirmation - "Are you sure you want to permanently delete this folder? ..." with Cancel and
  Delete Permanently - and now also deletes the selection items and limits filed under the folder,
  so no shoot is left behind without its folder; R2 previews and thumbnails are purged except any
  another photo still uses; originals on the studio's storage are never touched; the client link,
  PIN and short code are unchanged, so every other folder stays available to the client. Every
  folder row now shows its ⋮ (Rename, Delete) without hovering. A rename now shows everywhere the
  moment the server confirms it, with no page reload: the tree, the open folder (the desktop kept a
  stale copy of it, so its upload line still named the old folder) and the shoot groups in
  Selection Items (loaded once with the rail, now headed by the folder's live name); the folder
  stays selected, a double Enter sends one request, an older listing still in flight can no longer
  put the old name back, and a failed rename keeps the old name with the reason. No selection item
  can outlive its folder any more: migration
  `20261103100000_image_selection_manual_item_folder_cascade` makes the item→folder key
  `ON DELETE CASCADE` (it was `SET NULL`, which turned an item into a shoot with no folder) and
  removes the items written before the id link whose folder had already been renamed or deleted -
  only those no folder matches and the client never picked against; one with picks is kept. Adding
  an item under a shoot name no folder has is refused rather than saved unlinked. Delete sends one
  request however fast it is clicked, a folder already deleted elsewhere just leaves the tree, and
  the deleted folder's selection items and limits leave the Selection Items rail at once - they
  used to stay on screen until the page was reloaded.
  Project Management shoot folders are still renamed and deleted only in Project Management. No
  new permission.
  ([folders/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/folders/service.js),
  [DeleteFolderDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/DeleteFolderDialog.js))
- **A guest's WhatsApp photo-match message now records whether Meta delivered it, and one Meta
  could not deliver no longer hides the guest's photos for good.** Meta's delivery webhook used to
  update only the Image Selection activity log, so an AI Feature summary or a Photo Selling
  photo-match message stayed "sent" even when Meta later reported it failed (a number not on
  WhatsApp, a rate limit), and the matches it carried were never reported again. The webhook now
  also moves those messages forward by Meta's message id - delivered, read, or failed - never back,
  so duplicate and out-of-order reports change nothing. A failure only releases the photos for the
  next message when Meta's code is a passing one (rate limits other than the number's own spam limit, Meta's own errors), at most three
  times per guest; an undeliverable number or template problem keeps them claimed rather than being
  retried. Delivered or read messages, and sends whose outcome was unknown, are never resent.
  A report Meta sends before the app has stored the message's id - for these messages and the
  Image Selection activity log alike - or that failed to apply, is no longer dropped: it is kept
  (signed webhooks only, once however often Meta repeats it), applied in Meta's order the moment the
  send stores the id, picked up by a sweep at start-up and every 5 minutes if that was missed, and
  deleted after 7 days; one that could be neither applied nor kept is answered 500 so Meta resends
  the report. On the VPS, check that `TRUST_PROXY_HEADER` is set, so the webhook's rate limit counts
  each caller rather than the proxy. Both migrations must be applied before the new code starts (the
  deploy pipeline runs `prisma migrate deploy` ahead of the restart): the new code reads the new
  columns on every AI Feature and Photo Selling message.
  Migrations `20261031120000_whatsapp_notification_delivery_status` (`delivered_at` / `read_at` on
  both message tables, an index on Photo Selling's message id) and
  `20261031130000_whatsapp_pending_status` (a new, empty table) - additive only. Takes effect where
  `META_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN` and `META_WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET` are set.
  [whatsappNotificationDelivery.js](../backend/src/services/whatsappNotificationDelivery.js),
  [whatsappPendingStatus.js](../backend/src/services/whatsappPendingStatus.js),
  [metaWebhook.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/whatsapp-activity/metaWebhook.js)
- **An employee who allows anyone to add them is no longer told their privacy is at fault.** WhatsApp
  refuses an add in two different ways and the app reported both as the first: **403**, their privacy
  keeps a non-contact from adding them, and **408**, which is what WhatsApp answers for somebody who
  **left that group recently** - it holds them out for a while however their privacy is set. Both get
  the invite link, as before; the row now says which refusal it was, so somebody with "anyone can add
  me" switched on is not sent looking at a setting that was already right. Any other code is reported
  as itself rather than guessed at.
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/whatsapp-groups/service.js)
- **A production team member's calendar shows their shoots.** Somebody holding `PROJECT / Production`
  without Projects, Pre Production or Sales Manager was offered **My Attendance** as their only calendar
  source - shoots came under Projects, which needs one of those - so the switch hid itself, the page sat
  on attendance, and every shoot the server sent them was filtered out: the calendar showed Absent and
  On leave and nothing else. They now have **My Shoots** (offered only to them; somebody sent every
  shoot keeps Projects), so the switch opens on **All**: their shoots and their attendance together,
  and in the List view their shoots as rows (the shoot, its project and Event ID).
  [meetingSources.js](../frontend/src/lib/meetingSources.js),
  [MeetingsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/MeetingsPage.js)
- **Invitation cards open at `/inv/<token>`; `/i/<token>` stays the client's invoice.** develop made
  `/i/<token>` the public invoice page that receipt messages link to, and the invitation cards had
  taken the same address. The invitation page moved to `frontend/src/app/inv/[token]`, and the
  backend builds `/inv/` links (`client/invitations/service.js`, `card.js`, `video.js`). No
  invitation link had gone out yet, since the cards were not on develop or live, so nothing sent
  breaks.
- **Every module with more than one screen reopens the page you left.** Each of these opens a family
  of screens switched from a control on the page:
  - User Management: Administration, Employee Referral, User Activity Logs, Users and Roles.
  - Pre Production: All, Dum Dum, Qua Qua and Corp.
  - Production: Table and Schedule.
  - AI Feature: Dashboard and Events.
  - Image Selection: Dashboard and Projects.
  - Album Proofing: Dashboard and Projects.

  Leaving for another module and coming back through the sidebar always landed on the first screen,
  so somebody working in Employee Referral or Corp was sent back to Administration or All. The
  sidebar row now opens the screen that login last left.
  - The page is saved to the login (`tab:page.<row id>`, a namespace the server already accepts), so
    it survives a reload and follows the person to another device.
  - `useRememberLastPage`, in the app shell, records it. `useSidebarLayout` points the row at it
    through the pure `lib/lastPage.mjs`. `PAGE_FAMILIES` there lists the families, so a new one is
    one line. `usePreferenceValues` (in `PreferencesProvider`) reads every family's key at once.
  - A stored page is used only if it is one of that family's screens and the reader may still open
    it. Otherwise the row opens the first screen they may open, as before.

  No backend or permission change. Test: `frontend/test/last-page.test.mjs`, which also checks that
  every family is a real sidebar row and every screen of it a page that exists.
- **The CRM's Google Sheets auto-sync stops re-importing a sheet that has not changed.** Every 2
  minutes, on the same thread that answers every screen, each linked sheet was matched against every
  live lead, every deleted lead and every enquiry id read out of the database. That work grows with
  the CRM, and on live it is a regular stall for everybody. The poller still reads the sheet, which
  is two Google calls and the only way to see a change. When the sheet hashes the same as at the
  last pass that finished cleanly, the import is skipped and only `last_synced_at` moves.
  - A pass with a failed row is not remembered, so it runs in full again next time.
  - Every sheet still gets a full pass at least every 30 minutes.
  - After a restart, everything runs once as before.

  The manual Sync button always does a full pass, and imported leads are unchanged. Test:
  `backend/test/crm-auto-sync-unchanged.test.js`.
- **Less background load on every page, so the live server answers faster for everyone.**
  - **The WhatsApp gate read the session every 5 seconds, in every tab, for every user.** That
    included administrators and people already linked, who are never held. It now reads every
    5 seconds only while the gate is holding somebody, and once a minute otherwise. That removes
    11 of every 12 of those requests.
  - **Each permission check re-read the user, their roles and every grant: 8–10 queries, every
    time.** One click passes several checks (the bell alone asks 6). New
    `backend/src/services/requestCache.js` keeps those reads for the length of one request
    (AsyncLocalStorage, mounted in `server.js`). `iam.service.js` `getUserWithPermissions` and
    `getUserPermissions` go through it. Nothing outlives the request, so a role or grant edited in
    Role Management applies on the next request exactly as before. `createUser`/`updateUser` clear
    it.
  - **The bell's derived-notices cache expired just before each poll.** The TTL is now 90s (was
    60s, the same as the poll), so a poll reuses the last answer instead of recomputing every
    source.

  No permission change. Tests: `backend/test/request-cache.test.js`,
  `frontend/test/whatsapp-gate-pacing.test.mjs`.
- **Every click is cheaper: permissions are read once per request, and the WhatsApp check stops polling
  every 5 seconds.**
  - Each permission guard and scope check re-read the user, their roles and every grant: 8-10
    queries a check, and the notification bell alone runs six checks. `services/requestCache.js`
    (AsyncLocalStorage, mounted in `server.js`) now holds `getUserWithPermissions` and
    `getUserPermissions` for the length of one request. Measured: six checks dropped from 110 ms to
    13 ms per request.
  - Nothing outlives the request. A role edited in Role Management takes effect on the very next
    request, exactly as before, and `createUser` / `updateUser` clear what the request had read.
  - The WhatsApp-required gate is mounted on every page and read `/my-session` every 5 seconds for
    everyone, forever: 12 requests a minute per tab that changed nothing. It now reads every 5
    seconds only while it is actually holding somebody to scan a code, and once a minute otherwise.

  No permission change. Tests: `backend/test/request-cache.test.js`,
  `frontend/test/whatsapp-gate-pacing.test.mjs`.
- **Lighter on every page: permissions are read once per request, and the WhatsApp gate stops polling
  every 5 seconds.**
  - Every permission guard and scope check read the user, their roles and every grant again, about
    8-10 queries a check. The notification bell alone asks six checks. They now share one read for
    the length of the request (`services/requestCache.js`, an `AsyncLocalStorage` store mounted in
    `server.js`). Nothing outlives the request: a role edited in Role Management applies on the very
    next request, as before. Every user, role and grant write clears it once the write has
    landed: the `iam.service` writers through one wrapper, and the direct writes in
    `admin/routes.js`, the role matrix included, after their transaction.
  - `WhatsappRequiredGate` is mounted on every page of every tab. It read the session every 5
    seconds for everybody, about 12 requests a minute a tab. It now reads every 5 seconds only while
    it is holding somebody to pair, and once a minute otherwise.

  No permission change. Tests: `backend/test/request-cache.test.js`,
  `frontend/test/whatsapp-gate-pacing.test.mjs`.
- **Projects no longer downloads the whole register after every edit, and Contacts opens a project
  without it.** `GET /api/sales/projects` sends every project with all its shoots, deliverables and
  attachments, about 10 KB a project, so megabytes on live. Three places downloaded all of it to
  show one project:
  - Edit Project's autosave downloaded it after **every field changed**.
  - Sale edits, Start Project, Send Back, Delete and a single row's status change did the same.
  - Contacts downloaded it to open one project.

  New `GET /api/sales/projects/:id` (an id over 64 characters is refused) returns one project, by id or Event ID, in exactly the register's
  shape (`PROJECT_REGISTER_INCLUDE` + `registerRows`, shared with the list). It has the same guard
  (`readsTheRegister`) and the same reach (`projectAccessWhere`); a project outside reach is 404.
  Projects now replaces just that row, and drops it when it was sent back, deleted or left the
  reader's reach. Bulk changes and imports still read the register. No permission change. Tests:
  `backend/test/project-single-read.test.js`, `frontend/test/project-send-back.test.mjs`.

  The register also stops sending each project's attachments, which no screen reads from it. Sales
  Manager, Meetings and Album Proofing now ask for `?view=summary`, which leaves out each shoot's
  deliverables and services; those three screens show neither. Measured locally the summary is
  52 KB against 116 KB, less than half. Projects and Post Production show services and deliverables
  in their columns, so they still read the full shape.
- **The notification bell asks the server once per page, not three times.** Its stored notices and its
  derived ones each fetched `/api/notifications` on their own, on every page load and every poll.
  `getNotifications` now shares the request already in flight. Measured on Payroll: 3 calls became
  1. On the server, the derived notices it computes are now cached for 90 seconds
  (`DERIVED_TTL_MS`, was 60). At exactly the one-minute poll interval the entry had nearly always
  expired by the next poll, so every poll ran the heavy queries again.
- **Resizing a table column follows the mouse smoothly, in every table.** Dragging a column's edge
  lagged, jumped or stopped working. There were six causes, all in the shared `DataTable`:
  - The grab area was 4px wide. It is 12px now, with a thin line on hover and while dragging.
  - A press on the edge could start the header's own drag, the one that moves the column. That
    drag swallowed the mouse moves. A press on the edge now only resizes.
  - The first drag on a table snapped the column to about 150px. TanStack counts an unsized column
    as 150, so the drag now starts from the width actually on screen.
  - Every pixel dragged saved the table layout, a preference every screen re-renders on. Now the
    layout is saved once, on release.
  - Every frame of the drag redrew every visible row. On the 33-column CRM board that stuttered.
    While dragging, React now draws nothing. The new width is written straight onto the column's
    `<col>`, its header cell and the table width, and a fixed layout moves the rows from those
    alone. React redraws once, on release. Dragging a frozen column moves the frozen columns
    after it the same way, by shifting their cells' `left`. The frozen widths are not re-measured
    mid-drag; that measuring alone was redrawing the table on every frame.
  - The drag also starts from the width on screen rather than the stored one. A column whose stored
    width is under its `minSize` is drawn at the minimum, and the edge used to trail the pointer by
    the difference. The drag is held between the column's `minSize` and `maxSize`.

  The Production Schedule sheet's own grip gets the same 12px edge. No permission or backend
  change. Tests: `test/table-column-resize.test.mjs`.
- **Save closes the window, everywhere.** Every popup and side panel was checked. Three stayed open
  after a successful save:
  - Pre Production's General panel.
  - A Production shoot's plan (Submit plan, Save changes, Mark as pending) when opened from a board
    row, Production Schedule, Meetings or the Shoot Board. Saving it now closes it wherever it was
    opened from. The `closeOnSave` prop is gone.
  - Booking a project from a Meetings day closed the panel too soon, before the client's login could
    be shown. It now shows the login, then closes.

  A failed save still keeps the window open with what was typed. These stay open on purpose:
  - Buttons that move on: Update and Proceed Next, Save & Next, Save Draft.
  - Screens that show a result: a created invite or link, an import summary, a WhatsApp resend, a
    lead's Meetings list.
  - Full Settings screens.

  Frontend only; no permission change. Test: `test/close-on-save.test.mjs`.
- **CRM lead popup: Event Details can be scrolled to, and the footer buttons clear the Nebula AI
  button.** On a laptop screen the left column was held to the screen height, so Client Details
  squeezed Event Details to a thin strip and its shoot rows could not be reached. The left column now
  scrolls on its own, and Event Details always keeps room for its rows. The footer also leaves space
  on the right, so **Update and Proceed Next** is no longer hidden behind the floating Nebula AI
  button.

- **A shoot edited to "Shoot Date Known: No" loses its date.** The dialog sent no date, but Edit
  Project (`useProjectPlan` `saveShootEdit`) and a new project's shoot list
  (`CreateProjectFormPanel` `savePendingShootEdit`) fell back to the shoot's saved date, so the old
  day stayed. Both now take the dialog's date as given. Frontend only.
  [useProjectPlan.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/useProjectPlan.js),
  [CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js)
- **The Schedule's person picker no longer offers somebody busy on another shoot at that time.** It
  listed them, and choosing one was then refused ("… is on another shoot at that time"). It now leaves
  them out as the plan form does: opening a picker asks that shoot's busy list (its own read,
  `busyCrewEmployeeIds`) once, kept until the schedule reloads; the person already on the seat stays. Frontend only.
  [ProductionSchedulePage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionSchedulePage.js),
  [ProductionScheduleView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionScheduleView.js)
- **A deploy no longer dies at 10 minutes on the slow VPS, and a half-finished one is finished by
  running the pipeline again.** On 29 Oct two deploys in a row were killed by the SSH step's default
  10-minute limit - one inside the backend's `npm ci` alone - leaving the server on the new commit
  with nothing built or restarted, and every re-run then stopped as "nothing new to deploy" because
  it compared `git HEAD`. Now: the Deploy step may run 40 minutes (the job 55); `npm ci` runs only
  when that side's `package-lock.json` changed since the last install that finished (a hash stamped
  in `node_modules`); and `RELEASE` is written after the migrations and the build, just before the
  restart, with the "nothing new" test reading the commit from `RELEASE` instead of `HEAD`. The fix
  takes effect from the first run of a `main` commit that contains it - re-running an older run uses
  that run's own copy of the workflow.
  [deploy.yml](../.github/workflows/deploy.yml),
  [DEPLOYMENT-WORKFLOW.md](project-state/DEPLOYMENT-WORKFLOW.md)

- **The project-scope and client-reviews tests no longer fail in a full run on a deadlock.** The
  suite runs its files side by side against one database, and their fixture inserts
  (`sales_project`, `image_selection_project`, leads) could be picked by MySQL as a deadlock victim
  (P2034), failing every test in the file before it ran. Each fixture write now retries on its own,
  through one shared helper, [test/helpers/retrying.js](../backend/test/helpers/retrying.js), which
  `data-scope-lead-children.test.js` already used as its own copy. Tests only.
- **A client no longer meets "Too many requests" while using their app.** The client portal allowed
  60 requests a minute per account, across all their devices, and a client switching between screens
  quickly - or using the app and the website at once - went over it. Now 180, which a looping script
  still cannot get past. ([portal/routes.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/routes.js))

### Docs
- **The Meta WhatsApp webhook's two settings are now listed in the example env file.**
  `META_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN` and `META_WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET` were read by the existing
  delivery-status webhook but missing from `.env.example`, so nothing said the route stays unmounted
  (404 to Meta's verify call) until both are set. No code changed.
  [.env.example](../backend/.env.example),
  [metaWebhook.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/whatsapp-activity/metaWebhook.js)

### Changed
- **A project's shoot messages now come from its Pre-Production Coordinator.** Started from studio,
  reached the shoot place and shoot completed used to go from whoever **linked** the project's
  WhatsApp group - which made the sender an accident of who happened to press Link, and stopped a
  project's messages dead when that person left the studio ("Whoever linked the WhatsApp group no
  longer has a login"). They now come from the same person the crew notice comes from, so one number
  carries everything a project's people hear.

  **One thing to know before relying on it:** WhatsApp only accepts a group message from somebody who
  is **in that group**. The linker always was, by definition; a Pre-Production Coordinator who is not
  a participant cannot send, and the step will read as not sent. Add each coordinator to the groups of
  the projects they run.
  [backend/src/modules/project-management/production/messages.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/messages.js)

- **Approving a payment request is now its own permission, so nobody approves their own.** One
  permission did both jobs: `ACCOUNTS / Payment Request Approval` at Read / Write let somebody raise
  a request **and** approve it, so a holder could ask the studio for money and allow it in two
  clicks - and the record then named the same person as who requested it and who decided it, with
  nothing marking that as unusual. It is now split: the person who **raised** a request may view it
  and **withdraw** it, and nobody else may; the new **`ACCOUNTS / Payment Request Approver`** may
  view the whole queue, **correct** a request and approve or reject it, and may **not** withdraw -
  an approver who disagrees rejects, which records who decided and why, where withdrawing deletes
  the row and leaves nothing. Correcting moved to the approver so the figure they are reading cannot
  change under them between reading it and deciding it; a requester who got their own ask wrong
  withdraws it and raises the one they meant.

  **The old permission is also renamed** to `ACCOUNTS / Payment Request`, displayed as "Payment
  Requests", because it no longer approves anything: it is the screen, raising a request and
  withdrawing your own. Role Management was showing "Payment Requests" over a key reading "Approval".
  Nobody's access changes - grants point at the permission row, not at its name, so every role keeps
  exactly what it had. The rename went to **this** permission rather than the other on purpose:
  keeping "Approval" for approving would have handed the approval power to everybody who holds it
  today to raise requests, which is the hole being closed.

  **Two things to do after this ships.** The new permission is granted to **Super Admin only**, so
  until you tick it in Admin → Role Management for your finance roles, nobody else can approve or
  reject and the queue will not move. And an approver needs **`Payment Request` at Read** as well, to
  open the screen at all - a route names one permission, and that screen is the older one's.
  [backend/prisma/migrations/20261104100000_payment_request_approver_permission/migration.sql](../backend/prisma/migrations/20261104100000_payment_request_approver_permission/migration.sql)

- **A project's production messages waiting on an unlinked WhatsApp group are back in the top bar,
  as one job per project.** They were taken out because the bar filled with rows - started to shoot,
  reached venue, shoot completed, once per shoot - whose answer was always the same single job, and
  because it offered a Retry most readers could not use: the button was drawn from `PROJECT /
  Production` at Read / Write while the endpoint allows only that project's own Production Manager,
  so anybody else pressed it and was told it was not theirs. Both are answered rather than avoided:
  the rows gather under their project, so six shoots waiting on one group read as the one job they
  are with a count beside it, and the Retry is now offered only to somebody the endpoint will accept
  - everybody else sees what the job is and who finishes it. The bar also now shows a project's rows
  to its **Production Manager**, who could always act on them and was the one person not being shown
  them. [whatsapp-activity/groupFailures.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/whatsapp-activity/groupFailures.js)
- **Switching a notification back on now starts it fresh: it reports what goes wrong from then on,
  never what went wrong before it was switched off.** The banner across the top of the app lists the
  WhatsApp messages waiting for somebody to find their group, and it cannot be dismissed - right for
  real work, wrong for a message the studio has stopped sending. Switching the attendance report off
  left its old failure sitting there for good, and switching it back on brought every failure from
  before it straight back. The notice now leaves out a failure whose message is switched off, **and**
  one that failed before the last time it was switched off, so a message switched on again has a
  clean slate. The activity log itself is untouched - that is the record of what happened, and it is
  never rewritten; what is recorded instead is the moment the studio answered it by pressing the
  switch. A notification already switched off is stamped by a migration, so this holds for the ones
  switched off before it shipped. **The rule is now written once** for every switchable notification -
  the attendance report, Photo Selection Submitted, New Lead Welcome, Interview Welcome and both arms
  of the shoot crew notice - instead of six modules each keeping their own copy of it, one of which
  was missing. [notificationSwitches.js](../backend/src/services/notificationSwitches.js)
- **The Attendance WhatsApp Report, Photo Selection Submitted and New Lead Welcome no longer show
  two switches for one message.** Each of those settings sections has a notification panel with its
  own on/off - the one that also holds the send time, the group and the senders - and the wording
  below it had grown a second "This message is sent" switch of its own. Two switches for one message
  is one too many, and nothing on the screen said which of them decided: in fact the template's
  switch did nothing at all for these three, because their senders never ask whether the message is
  switched off. The wording panel now shows the switch only where it is the message's only one
  (Cash Received, the onboarding invite, the production step messages and the rest, which do ask).
  For these three the panel above is the switch and the panel below is the wording.
  [MessageTemplatePanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/MessageTemplatePanel.js)
- **Switching any notification off now clears the error it was showing, and switching it back on
  starts that module fresh.** Every automatic message keeps the reason its last send failed and shows
  it in red on its panel, because somebody is meant to fix it. Switching the message off *is* the
  answer to it - nothing is being sent any more - but the reason stayed in its column until the next
  successful send, so the panel went on showing a failure for a notification that was off, and
  switching it back on months later put that old failure straight back on the screen. Now the switch
  clears it, every time, and only the module's own next try can put anything there again. **The daily
  attendance WhatsApp report** was the one switch that did not do this; Photo Selection Submitted, New
  Lead Welcome, Interview Welcome and both arms of the shoot crew notice already did, and are now held
  to it by a test that covers every switch at once. Nothing else is touched - send times, chosen
  senders and group names all stand, so switching a notification back on resumes exactly as before.
  [attendance/reportGroup.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/reportGroup.js)
- **Switching a message off on Settings → Templates now clears the failed sends of it that were
  waiting, instead of leaving them on the step.** A production step message that did not reach the
  project's WhatsApp group sits on its step in red with a Retry beside it, because somebody has to
  decide what to do about it. Switching that message off is the decision - it is never going to be
  sent - but the step went on showing the failure and offering a Retry that could not send anything,
  and pressing it left the message stuck on "still sending" for good. Now the switch closes those
  sends as it is pressed: the step shows nothing, the Retry refuses while the message is off, and
  **switching the message back on later does not bring the old failures back** - they were answered,
  not hidden. A step whose message is switched off also stops saying it will post to WhatsApp and
  stops asking to be confirmed. Nothing is deleted: each row keeps what went wrong, and the shoot's
  Activity tab keeps its "WhatsApp not sent" entry. Messages switched off before this are closed by
  a migration. [production/messages.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/messages.js)
- **File in's Footage URL is now Footage Location and takes plain text, so footage kept on a hard
  disk can be recorded.** It
  only accepted an http(s) link - a link pasted without `https://` had it added, and anything else
  was refused with "Enter the footage link as an http(s) URL." That is right while every backup goes
  to Drive or the NAS, and wrong the moment a shoot's footage goes onto a disk that lives on a shelf:
  there was no way to write "Seagate 3, Reception shelf", so the step could not be completed
  honestly. The box now takes whatever says where the footage is - a link, a path, a disk and its
  place - and still has to be filled in to complete the step, so it is renamed **Footage Location**
  on the step and on the import sheet. A spreadsheet still headed Footage URL imports exactly as it
  did, by that old heading. Nothing already saved changes, and a link is stored exactly as it was
  typed rather than having a scheme added to it. [production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/controller.js)
- **A shoot's day is now seven steps, Happy clients ends it, and a shoot that stops is paused rather
  than put through a status step.** The Shoot status step - where the coordinator chose Paused, On
  hold, Rejected or Completed, with a resume loop back to Happening now - and the trip back, Started
  from venue and Reached studio, are no longer worked: the studio's day ends when the client is happy
  and the footage is in, and saying "the client is happy" and then "the shoot is Completed" was the
  same fact twice. **Happy clients now completes the shoot itself**, marking it Completed and sending
  the Shoot completed message, with File in the one thing after it. Two steps are renamed to what the
  crew calls them - Started from studio is **Started to shoot** and Reached shoot place is **Reached
  venue** - and an indoor shoot's first step reads **Ready**, since nothing has gone anywhere. An
  indoor shoot now has four steps and an outdoor one seven.
  **Pausing stayed, as a control rather than a step:** Pause the shoot / Start the shoot sits in the
  step's own title bar from Shoot started being done until Happy clients ends the shoot, asks why
  both ways round, and a paused shoot shows **Paused** with its reason on the Execution tab, the
  board and the Production Schedule and completes no step until it starts again. The shoot's status
  through its day now reads Travelling → Setting up → Shoot in progress ⇄ Paused → File in pending →
  Shoot completed, where it used to jump from Work in Progress to Shoot started.
  Nothing already recorded is rewritten: a shoot left standing on one of the retired steps reads as
  being on File in - the shooting is over, the footage is what is left - the retired steps' own times,
  photos and remarks are kept, and the old spreadsheet still imports, its old step names and its old
  Shoot Status column read as before. The client portal no longer shows a halted shoot, since nothing
  can halt one any more. [production/steps.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/steps.js),
  [ProductionPauseControl.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionPauseControl.js)
- **Accounts Manager now lets you choose whether entries are grouped by project, and lists them one
  by one by default.** The All, Received and Spent tabs always grouped: a project with several cash
  entries read as one row with its total, and its entries opened underneath. That is the right view
  for "what has this wedding taken and spent" and the wrong one for the question the page is usually
  opened with - "what came in today" - because a project row sits where its *first* entry would, so
  this morning's receipt was down the page under a wedding from August. A **Grouped / Ungrouped**
  switch now sits beside Table / Board, it opens on **Ungrouped** (every entry on its own line,
  latest first), and it remembers what you picked. Nothing about the grouped view changed. The switch
  is absent on Transfers, which are the studio's own money moving between branches and carry no
  project to group by, and on the Board, which groups by category of its own.
  [frontend/src/components/accounts/CashEntryGroupingSwitch.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/CashEntryGroupingSwitch.js)

- **The bar at the top of the page no longer lists a project's production messages.** It was
  carrying every shoot step message a project had waiting - started from studio, reached the shoot
  place, shoot completed - so a project with several shoots filled the bar with rows whose answer was
  always the same single job, linking its WhatsApp group. It was also offering a Retry that most
  readers could not use: the button appeared for anyone holding Production and Pre Production at
  Read / Write, while the server allows a retry only to that project's own Production Manager, so
  everybody else pressed it and got "Only this project's Production Manager can retry its messages".
  Messages addressed by group **name** - the attendance report, the wishes, the photo-selection group
  - are unaffected and still listed, because the bar is the only place a renamed group announces
  itself. Switched off rather than deleted: `SHOWS_PRODUCTION_STEPS` puts them back, and the tests
  still cover that arm.
  [backend/src/modules/settings/whatsapp-activity/groupFailures.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/whatsapp-activity/groupFailures.js)

- **Payment Requests no longer has the Extra Quotation button or the Extra Quotations tab.** Extra
  quotations are raised, approved and rejected on the project's own **Payments** view, which is
  unchanged. Nothing is deleted and the server is untouched; a remembered Extra Quotations tab opens
  on All. [PaymentRequestsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/PaymentRequestsPage.js)
- **User Management: somebody serving notice now reads "Active (Serving Notice)".** Their
  Employment Status used to read just "Active" (or "in Training", or "PIP"), the same as everyone
  still working. It now says they are on notice, e.g. "in Training (Serving Notice)". This shows in
  the table and its CSV export, on the Board card, in the Info panel and in the record view.
  - Nothing stored changes. The dot keeps the status's colour, and the Employment Status filter
    still finds them under Active.
  - Shared helper: `employmentStatusLabel` in [employmentStatus.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/employmentStatus.mjs).
    `TableCellValue` takes a new `statusLabel` prop.
  - No permission changes.
- **Raised Requests has no Action column.** A request is opened from its row's ⋮ - **Review** for whoever
  may decide it while it is open, **View** otherwise - or by double-clicking the row, as before.
  [RaisedRequestsTable.js](../frontend/src/components/client-management/RaisedRequestsTable.js)
- **An item taken off and put back shows once, where it stands now.** In Edit Sale Details' Extra
  section and on the client's quotation link (and its PDF), a shoot, service or deliverable removed and
  added back - however many times - is listed once: under Added while it is on the project, under Removed
  while it is off, at its latest change. It used to show a line for every change, the same item under
  both. Every change is still recorded and counted in the totals exactly as before; unpublished changes
  always show, each needing its amount. An item added back is now dated when it was added back.
  [saleExtras.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/saleExtras.mjs), [totals.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/sale-extras/totals.js)
- **Create Project fills the Vertical from the chosen quotation.** Picking a finalized quotation now
  selects the vertical it was made under - Dum Dum, Qua Qua or Corp - beside the number and branch it
  already filled. It stays changeable. Where a saved WhatsApp group name is attached, that name still
  decides the vertical. [SaleDetailsSection.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SaleDetailsSection.js)
- **Edit Sale Details' Extra lists Added and Removed as two headings, shoot by shoot under each.**
  Instead of one card per shoot holding both lists, the section now reads **Added (n)** - a card for
  every shoot something was added to, with a table of what was added - then **Removed (n)**, the same
  for what was taken off. Amounts, remarks, the required check and Publish Updated Quotation work as
  before. [SaleExtrasSection.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SaleExtrasSection.js)
- **Payment Requests no longer has an Extra Quotations tab.** The page lists payment requests only
  (All, Pending, Approved, Rejected, as table or board); extra quotations are read, and a pending one
  approved or rejected, on its project's Payments tab. Somebody who last left the page on that tab
  opens on All. No server route changed.
  [PaymentRequestsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/PaymentRequestsPage.js)
- **Edit Project's Payments tab names who added each extra and no longer raises one.** Every row under
  **Extras** now reads **Added by** and the employee it is credited to, and the Extras column's add (+)
  button is gone from Edit Project. The Pre Production and Production panels keep the button; extras
  still waiting keep their Edit and approval everywhere.
  [ProjectPaymentsView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectPaymentsView.js)
- **Raise an Extra Quotation offers deliverables as well as services.** The **Service** field is now
  **Service / Deliverable**: its list shows every active service, then every active deliverable from
  Project Settings, each under its own heading, with **Others** last for anything not on either list.
  An extra is stored by name as before, so existing extras read unchanged, and editing one whose name
  is now on the deliverables list opens it selected rather than as Others. No permission change, no
  migration ([extraQuotationOptions.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/extraQuotationOptions.mjs),
  [ExtraQuotationFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ExtraQuotationFormPanel.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/extra-quotations/controller.js) `options`).
- **Edit Sale Details → Extra lists its items in normal weight.** An item's name ("360 Video Booth
  | 8-9 Hours (Full Session) | Outdoor / On-Location") was bold, heavier than the Category and
  Created beside it; it now reads in the same normal font as the rest of the row. Wording and
  layout unchanged ([SaleExtrasItemsTable.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SaleExtrasItemsTable.js)).
- **A shoot added after booking is now badged "Extra Shoot".** In Edit Sale Details → Extra, the
  card of a shoot added since the sale read "Added shoot"; it now reads **Extra Shoot**, matching
  the section and the Net Extra it adds to. Wording only - nothing else changed
  ([SaleExtrasShootCard.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SaleExtrasShootCard.js)).
- **Edit Sale Details → Shedule Payment opens ready to edit.** For somebody who may change the
  schedule (SALES / Booking Edit, or PROJECT / Projects on that project, as before) **every** payment
  is a form as soon as the panel opens - completed and upcoming alike - with a blank row under the
  last to schedule the next one; there is no Edit button to press first. Everybody else still sees
  it read-only. Payments Accounts has already
  worked (Cleared, part-paid, On Hold, "Pending from …") can now be changed and removed here and on
  Projects → Start / Edit Project, which used to show them read-only and keep them whatever was
  sent; their status is written under their remarks while they are edited. Removing a paid payment
  never removes money: its receipts stay on the project's books, unlinked from it, so they still
  count in the Balance Amount (noted as received on no payment) and can be edited in Accounts. A
  payment fixed at an amount by a part payment stays fixed unless its amount is changed. A change to
  the schedule alone is now saved by Update Project (it used to close without saving when nothing
  else changed), without sending the sale again; a sent-back project's Update to Project still
  returns it to Projects. No permission change
  ([SchedulePaymentSection.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/SchedulePaymentSection.js),
  [CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/accounts/scheduled-payments/service.js) `saveProjectSchedule`).
- **Payment Requests no longer has an Extra Quotation button.** The button beside Add Request is
  gone. An extra quotation is still raised from its project's own Payments, and the **Extra
  Quotations** tab still lists, approves and rejects them, exactly as before. Nothing else changed
  ([PaymentRequestsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/PaymentRequestsPage.js)).
- **Both shoot notices now come from the project's own people instead of one phone chosen in
  Settings.** A shoot's crew hears from that project's **Pre-Production Coordinator** and a vendor from
  its **Production Manager**, from their own WhatsApp - so the number changes with the project, and a
  vendor who replies "can we shift by an hour?" is replying to somebody who can answer rather than to
  whoever the studio nominated once. There is **no fallback**: where that person is not named on the
  project, has no login, has not had Allow WhatsApp ticked, has their chat switched off or has not
  connected their WhatsApp, that project's messages **wait** and go the moment it is sorted; they never
  go from anybody else's number. Because a waiting message fails silently, the card that used to hold
  the sender picker now lists what is waiting, naming the reason and who fixes it - and lists only
  what is genuinely owed, not every project whose sender happens to be unreachable. **Both arms also
  stop losing every second sweep under load**: writing down a sweep's trouble used to stamp its own
  claim again, so a sweep that took more than ten seconds blocked the next minute's. **This means a
  project with no Pre-Production Coordinator named stops sending crew messages**, where before they
  went from the studio's chosen phone - so check that every project names one, and that each
  coordinator and manager has a login with Allow WhatsApp ticked and their WhatsApp connected. The
  Sender and Rotation this message used to answer to are removed rather than left deciding nothing -
  the migration deletes that one row from `whatsapp_sender_policy`, which cannot be undone.
  [backend/src/modules/settings/shoot-crew-notice/projectSender.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/shoot-crew-notice/projectSender.js)

- **Approving a payment request and paying it are now two steps.** Approving a request used to pay
  it: the approval form asked how the money moved, wrote the cash entries and - for a salary advance
  - the payroll row that recovers it, all in the act of saying yes. One person therefore had to do
  both, and a request only reached the cash book once it was too late to question. Now **Payment
  Requests** is where a request is approved or rejected, and approving asks for an optional remark
  and records the decision, nothing more. The request then appears under **Accounts Manager →
  Pending**, where ⋮ → **Record Payment** opens the form that was the approval's and releases the
  money. A salary advance becomes its Advance Salary row at that point rather than at approval,
  since nothing is owed back until the money has been handed over; every other kind of request ends
  at the cash entries. Paid is not a new status - it is whether the request has cash entries, shown
  as a **Payment** column ("Awaiting Payment" / "Paid", and blank on a request nobody has approved)
  on the Payment Requests table - and a request already paid cannot be paid twice, including when two
  people try at the same moment. **Releasing the money needs `ACCOUNTS / Cash Management` Read /
  Write**, with only **Read** on `Payment Request Approval` beside it, so the separation works both
  ways: an approver who does not keep the cash book can say yes and no more, and somebody who keeps
  the cash book can pay without being able to approve. The studio may want to review who holds Cash
  Management write now that it is what releases a payment request. No new permission and no
  migration: both permissions already exist, and every request approved before this reads as Paid
  because its entries are already there
  ([controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payment-requests/controller.js),
  [usePaymentRequestActions.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/usePaymentRequestActions.js)).
- **A shoot's services are listed in the order the studio crews them, on the Production Schedule and
  on the plan.** Both screens listed a shoot's services in the order somebody happened to book them,
  so the same two sheets read differently from one project to the next and the person assigning
  employees had to find each service before filling it. They now read one order: Traditional Photo,
  Traditional Video, Semi Candid Photo (and `+ reel`), Candid Photo (and `+ Reels`), Semi Candid
  Video, Candid Video, Drone, Complementary Drone, then every other service alphabetically - with
  the shoot's **Assist** last, where it already sat. The order is the service's own `sortOrder` in
  Settings → Project → Services, not a list of names in the code, so renaming a service keeps its
  place and the studio can reorder its services without a release; a service no longer in Settings
  sorts last rather than first, where it reads as the one nobody can be assigned to. The same order
  now also reaches the plan's own "still to fill" checklist, the Settings services list, client
  service requests and extra quotations, which all read that field. One caveat for the studio: the
  migration behind it re-ranks every **other** service alphabetically after those ten, so if any of
  them had been dragged into an order of its own in Settings, that order is replaced and can simply
  be dragged again
  ([serviceOrder.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/serviceOrder.js)).
- **The hamburger now opens the menu with the cursor in Search.** Type a screen's name straight
  away. On a computer (mouse or trackpad) only: on a phone or tablet the menu opens as before, so the
  on-screen keyboard does not cover it. Closing the menu - the hamburger included, which used to keep
  the last search - now always empties Search, so it reopens on the whole menu
  ([AppSidebar.js](../frontend/src/components/app-shell/AppSidebar.js)).
- **A sent-back project's Edit Sale Details now ends in Discard, Save Draft and Update to
  Project.** In Bookings & Converted, editing a project Projects sent back offers three buttons
  instead of Discard Changes / Update Project. **Discard** throws away what was typed on the form
  and closes - asking first when anything was changed; shoots, services and payments saved through
  their own dialogs stay saved, as before. **Save Draft** saves the sale details with the same checks
  as an update and leaves the project under **Sent Back**, still editable there
  (`PATCH /api/sales/projects/:id?draft=true`; refused 409 on a project that is not sent back).
  **Update to Project** saves them and, in the same write, returns the project to Projects and sets
  its status to **Yet to Start** - whatever status it had - so Projects starts it again; its shoots,
  payments and history are kept. With nothing changed on the form it only returns it (new
  `POST /api/sales/projects/:id/return-to-projects`, guarded as the edit is, refused 409 when it is
  no longer sent back). Both are in the project's Activity. Editing any other project is unchanged.
  No new permission, no migration
  ([CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js),
  [SalesManagerPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SalesManagerPage.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js)).
- **The project list's filter in every Visual Curation module now reads Expand and Sort.** Sort
  opens in place onto All, Yet to Start, In Progress, Partially Completed and Completed, and names the
  one chosen beside it; Expand (Photo Selection) and Show archived (desktop) are unchanged. AI
  Culling, AI Editing and Signature Album now sort by the same four as Photo Selection - a culling
  run ready for review or failed, some photos edited or a render failed, an album ready to publish
  or expired all sit under Partially Completed - and each project's dot still names the module's own
  status on hover. Web and desktop
  ([ProjectSidebar.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/ProjectSidebar.js),
  [stageDashboards.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/stageDashboards.mjs)).
- **A project's header is one row in every Visual Curation module.** Photo Selection, AI Culling,
  AI Editing and Signature Album show the project's name and created date on the left and, on the
  same line, its last update and status - Photo Selection's publish badge or Download Selected, the
  album's status - on the right, instead of a second row below; on a phone the right-hand side
  wraps under the name. Web and desktop
  ([ImageSelectionProjectWorkspace.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/ImageSelectionProjectWorkspace.js)).
- **Wishes Scheduler has moved from Settings → Employee to Settings → Templates, with the wishes inside
  it.** One screen holds the sending settings (time, Sender or Rotation, WhatsApp group), and under them
  three tabs: **Birthday Wishes · Anniversary Wishes · Work Anniversary Wishes**. These replace their
  three separate Settings entries. Switching tabs with unsaved wording asks first. Nothing about how the
  wishes are sent changed; it still needs `SETTINGS / Wishes` at Read, and Read / Write to reword.
  (`frontend/src/components/settings/WishesSchedulerPanel.js`, `SettingsOverlay.js`)
- **Every Board's columns run in the order its records move through them.** The tabs keep their
  order; only the Board columns change.
  - Tasks: Pending, In Progress, Finish & Send Back, Completed, then Reassigned and Cancelled.
  - Pre Production: Yet to Start, Work in Progress, Planned, then Hold and Rejected.
  - Production: Yet to Start, Work in Progress, Planned, Execution, Completed, then Hold and Rejected.
  - CRD Documents: Link Not sent, Yet To Receive, Submitted. They used to run backwards.
  - Attendance login and break summaries: a good day first, then late or short days, days away, and
    days gone wrong; On break before Completed. They used to be A-Z.
  - CRM Reports: lead reports follow the Leads board's pipeline, through a shared list in
    `lib/crmBoardOrder.mjs`. Summary's months and Work Hours' days run in time, so "10 Oct" comes
    before "1 Nov".
  - Calendar list: project statuses follow the project's flow instead of A-Z.
  (`TasksPage.js`, `PreProductionPage.js`, `ProductionPage.js`, `CrdDocumentsPage.js`,
  `EmployeeAttendancePage.js`, `CrmReportsPage.js`, `CRMPage.js`, `MeetingsPage.js`)
- **A resignation waiting for approval is in Pending, and only an approved one is Serving Notice.**
