  User Management's Serving Notice tab listed people whose resignation form was only Submitted
  (Keerthana Raj, still waiting for HR). It now lists only those HR has approved, now serving their
  notice. Someone waiting is under **Pending → HR Offboarding Pending** until HR decides. Their row ⋮
  **Review Resignation** now opens that form's Review directly, instead of the whole forms list.
  Approve moves them to Serving Notice; Reject or Send back keeps them working. Review is no longer
  in the HR Offboarding list's ⋮, and a Board drop no longer opens it, so a resignation is decided in
  one place. `isLeaving` is removed. (`frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeVerificationPage.js`,
  `OffboardingInviteDialog.js`, `frontend/src/lib/employmentStatus.mjs`)
- **User Management's pending kinds are reached only inside Pending.** Employee Submission Pending
  and HR Onboarding Pending are no longer tabs in the top bar. They are listed down the side of the
  Pending tab, with a new **HR Offboarding Pending** and Review Pending. HR Offboarding Pending lists
  everyone whose resignation form is Submitted and waiting for HR to approve or reject it; a form
  still Sent or Verified is waiting on the employee and is not counted. The bar reads All, Pending, Active, Serving Notice, Incomplete
  Profiles, InActive. Incomplete Profiles is no longer a kind inside Pending, and is no longer counted
  in Pending's total; it stays a tab of its own. (`frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeVerificationPage.js`)
- **Every message under Settings → Templates now shows a "Preview with sample details" under its
  wording, updating as it is typed.** Only Interview Welcome, New Lead Welcome, Photo Selection
  Submitted, Payment Reminder and Attendance WhatsApp Report had one; Cash Received, Employee Invite,
  the four Offboarding messages, Login Credentials, Client Login Credentials, CRD Document Link,
  Feedback Thank You and Issues, Shoot Crew Notice and Removed, and the three Production messages
  now do too, each with sample details for every placeholder its sender fills (Shoot Crew Removed's
  `{service}` empty, as sent). Cash Received's preview adds the invoice link at the end where the
  wording leaves `{invoice link}` out, as the receipt sender does. Birthday and Anniversary Wishes
  show a preview under each of their ten wishes. One shared `MessagePreview` draws them all; nothing
  is sent or saved by a preview, and no wording, placeholder or sending changed.
  ([MessageTemplatePanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/MessageTemplatePanel.js),
  [MessagePreview.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/MessagePreview.js))
- **The Automatic WhatsApp Message group is gone from Settings: each automatic message is one entry
  under Settings → Templates, laid out as Interview Welcome - its notification above its wording.**
  Attendance WhatsApp Report (on / off, daily time, Sender or Rotation with the fallback order, the
  group), Photo Selection Submitted (on / off, senders, group) and New Lead Welcome (on / off, then
  the per-vertical Office time / After hours wording) each show their Notification card, then the
  message with its placeholders and a live preview; the attendance report's preview is new (sample
  details for every placeholder it fills). Each half keeps its own permission and endpoint - the card
  on the notification's (`SETTINGS / Automatic WhatsApp Message`, or the attendance report's
  administrator / `HRM / Attendance WhatsApp Report` / chosen sender), the wording on
  `SETTINGS / Message Template` - and the entry is offered to whoever can open either. Nothing is
  stored, sent, scheduled or rotated differently, and no data moved; links to the old screens
  (`?settings=attendance-whatsapp-report`, `photo-selection-submitted`, `new-lead-welcome`) open the
  new entries. Birthday Wishes and Anniversary Wishes moved to Templates from Employee → Wishes too;
  Employee keeps Wishes Scheduler. Interview Welcome is unchanged; Payment Reminder and Shoot Crew
  Notice keep their notifications under Project Management, their wording already in Templates.
  ([SettingsOverlay.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/SettingsOverlay.js),
  [NotificationTemplatePanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/NotificationTemplatePanel.js))
- **Who may be put on a shoot is the Technical department, not a list of shooting skills.** The
  Person and Assist pickers on a production plan, the Shoot Board's free shooters and the rule
  behind them all asked whether an employee held one of nine skills - Candid Photographer, Drone,
  Outdoor Shoot and six more - matched against Settings → Skills. So somebody the studio sends on
  shoots could not be put on one until a skill was ticked on their profile, and the nine names had
  to be kept in step with the services the studio sells. They now ask the employee's **department**:
  anybody in **Technical** can work a service, and nobody else. Read through the department link on
  the employee record rather than the text beside it, so a rename in Settings is still the same
  department, and matched exactly - "Non Technical" is a department of its own and is not this one.
  **Worth knowing before it is deployed:** nobody is in Technical on this database, so the pickers
  will offer vendors only until the people who shoot are put in that department
  ([crew.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/crew.js)).
- **A day's Team Attendance on the calendar is one chip, read in its pop-up.** A day with two
  absences and three on leave drew two chips, and in a busy month they stacked under the shoots and
  the meetings until the cell was a column of counts nobody could take in. The day now carries one
  - "Attendance · 5" - and the pop-up behind it says which five: the count per status under the
  date, then the names under their own heading, Absent first and then On leave. A day of one status
  keeps that status's colour; one holding both takes a neutral grey, since red over a day that is
  half leave would read as five absences. The branch filter rebuilds the counts from whoever is
  left, so the chip never says five over a pop-up listing two, and the table still reads one row
  per person per day ([calendar/service.js](../backend/src/modules/schedule/calendar/service.js),
  [TeamAttendancePeople.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/TeamAttendancePeople.js)).
- **The calendar's attendance list is one Attendance column, with the day's times in the popup.** A
  day was spread over Status, Login, Logout and Worked - four columns, three of them blank on
  exactly the days this list is read for, since an absence and a day's leave have no times at all.
  What the day **was** is the answer; the register's own login, logout and hours are the detail
  behind it, and they are in the entry's popup, which already drew them and now names the status
  beside them. The column still filters by the six statuses the calendar shows and the board still
  groups by it ([meetingSources.js](../frontend/src/lib/meetingSources.js),
  [MeetingsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/MeetingsPage.js)).
- **The Production Schedule's Assist shows everybody on it, by name.** Two things were squeezed into
  the 176px a column is: the list of employees, which cut every name in half, and the names already
  chosen, which read as "Asha, Ravi, Div...". The Assist block now **grows sideways** to whatever its
  names need, all the time rather than only while somebody is filling it: every assistant is a chip,
  each name whole, and the block is as wide as its answer - so the sheet says at a glance which
  shoots are carrying a crew. It can grow because it is the last block in a row, with nothing to its
  right to push; a service block stays one name wide, columns being easier to read down when they
  line up, and the growth stops at 32rem, past which the row scrolls as it always has. The **menu** is pinned to one width whatever the box
  does, so the list stays readable without becoming five names across an empty half-metre.
  A chip also **says who somebody is** now. The picker lists who may be put on a shoot today, so
  anybody already on one who has since left - or whose department has changed - was not in it and
  their chip read `emp:27068`, which names nobody. The name is sent beside the id and the chip reads
  it, so they are named and can still be taken off
  ([ProductionScheduleView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionScheduleView.js),
  [MultiSelectField.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/MultiSelectField.js),
  [read.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/read.js)).
- **Nebula now sits at the end of every module header, just before the ⋮.** It used to open the
  action row. That read well on a page whose actions are buttons and badly on one ending in a ⋮ -
  two quiet icons with the primary button stranded between them. The row now runs: what scopes the
  page, then its buttons, then Nebula, then the ⋮. The ⋮ has a slot of its own on the header
  (`menu`) so the order is fixed in one place rather than page by page, and the ten screens that
  have one pass it there - Assets, Vendors, Client Storage, Projects, Pre Production, Production,
  Bookings, CRM, Interview and Accounts Manager. Nothing moved on a page without a ⋮ except Nebula
  itself, which is now last ([ModulePageHeader.js](../frontend/src/components/layout/ModulePageHeader.js)).
- **The calendar's branch filter takes several branches, and sits with the page's controls.** It was
  one branch at a time, beside the heading; it is now the same multi-select the Assets register uses,
  in the row of controls at the right, kept between the calendar and the list - nothing ticked is
  every branch. Holidays and your own attendance belong to no branch and stay whichever branches are
  picked, as they always did ([MeetingsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/MeetingsPage.js)).
- **Asset Management is filtered by branch instead of by category, and by several branches at once.**
  The main-category picker beside the heading is gone; a **Branch** picker sits with the header's
  controls, taking as many branches as you tick - the shape the Shoot Board's own branch filter
  already uses, since a studio comparing two branches should not have to look at each in turn.
  Nothing ticked is every branch, which is also the way back. The table, the status tabs and their
  counts all narrow with it, and the ticks are kept in the URL (`?branch=3,7`) like the status tab,
  so a link holds what it was shared on. The branches offered are only the ones the viewer's roles
  reach for `ASSET / Asset Management`, answered by `/api/assets` rather than read from the branch
  register, so the picker cannot offer a branch whose assets the data scope would hide and leave an
  empty table reading as a fault. Branches named in a link that the viewer does not reach - a link
  shared by somebody who does - are said and left out rather than left showing an empty table, and
  an empty table names what it was narrowed by. It is not drawn on the **Asset Requests** tab, where
  a branch narrows nothing, though the ticks are kept so coming back to the register restores them.
  `/api/assets` takes the list as `?branchIds=3,7`; the single `?branchId=` still answers beside it,
  and `categoryId` and `includeChildren` are still accepted though no screen sends them any more
  ([AssetManagementPage.js](../frontend/src/components/assets/AssetManagementPage.js),
  [assets.controller.js](../backend/src/modules/assets/assets.controller.js)).
- **Changing a password now signs the account out of every device.** It did not: a request is
  authenticated by a stateless token that carries the account's id and role but **not** its password,
  and is good for seven days - so somebody who changed their password because it had been found out
  went on being followed by whoever had it, for up to a week, and longer where that device kept
  refreshing itself. Nothing but deactivating the account or pressing Logout on that very device
  ended a session.

  The moment of the change is now stamped on the account (`password_changed_at`) and every token
  minted before it is refused, so the next thing each signed-in device asks for comes back refused
  and the app asks for the new password. The refresh sessions are revoked with it, or a device would
  simply mint itself a fresh token. It applies to all three ways a live account's password is
  replaced: **Profile → Change Password**, the **forgot-password reset** - the sharper case, since a
  reset is what somebody does when the old password is in the wrong hands - and **HR reopening a
  login**. The device doing the changing is signed out too and goes straight to the sign-in, rather
  than meeting a refusal mid-screen a moment later.

  A refusal says which it is: a password changed, a closed account (HR's to undo), or a sign-in that
  was never valid. **Migration** `20261102100000_password_changed_at` adds the column as NULL, which
  reads as "never changed", so nobody signed in today is thrown out by the deploy itself.
  [passwordSessions.js](../backend/src/services/passwordSessions.js),
  [authMiddleware.js](../backend/src/middleware/authMiddleware.js)
- **Add and Edit Shoot both pick shoots the same way.** Editing a shoot offered a single picker, so a
  shoot named for several - "Haldi + Mehandi" - could not be re-named without typing the joined name
  by hand, and its Additional Text had nowhere per name to sit. Editing now opens the same tick-list
  Add Shoot has, with the shoot's own names already ticked: untick one and the shoot is renamed for
  what is left, tick another and it joins them. It is still **one** shoot either way - adding builds a
  row per batch, editing rewrites the one being edited - and the saved row is built the same way for
  both (`formRows`), so the joined name's length is checked and each name's Additional Text is carried
  across. The place-per-name choice under Location works on an edit as it does on an add.
  [AddShootDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/AddShootDialog.js)
- **Pre Production and Production: a project stands under every status its shoots are at.** It was
  listed under one status rolled up from all its shoots; now a project with a shoot Planned and another
  in Work in Progress is under both tabs, opened there to only the shoots at that status, and has a card
  in each Board column. A shoot's own Hold or Rejected puts it there; in Production a shoot whose day has
  begun is under Execution; WCR leaves a shoot where its details put it (Follow-up still lists it by
  date). A status set by hand on the whole project keeps it in that one place. Tab counts now count a
  project once per status, so they can add up to more than All. The project's own status column and
  label are unchanged. Frontend only.
  [preProductionProgress.js](../frontend/src/lib/preProductionProgress.js),
  [productionBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionBoard.mjs)
- **Production's shoot tiles say what is pending as Pre Production's do.** Until a shoot is Planned its
  tile read "Plan: 3 of 6 filled"; it now reads "3 details pending" (or "1 detail pending"), the
  wording Pre Production's tiles use, from one shared `pendingDetailsText`. A complete plan not yet
  submitted still reads "Plan filled - submit it", and a Planned shoot its next step. Frontend only.
  [pendingDetails.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/pendingDetails.mjs),
  [productionBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionBoard.mjs)
- **Pre Production and Production: each counted question says Pending until it is answered.** The
  answers a shoot is counted on for **Planned** - the asterisked ones: in Pre Production the Shoot
  Date, the event's start and end, the reporting time and each venue's address (or the branch for an
  indoor shoot); in Production the coordinator, Travel Mode, the Studio Start Date and Time, each
  service's person and a vendor still Waiting - carry a small amber **Pending** tag at the end of their
  label line, gone the moment they are filled. One shared `PendingField` (on `ProgressChip`), switched on
  by `context.pendingTags` in the schema form. Frontend only.
  [PendingField.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/PendingField.js),
  [SchemaFormFields.js](../frontend/src/components/schema-form/SchemaFormFields.js),
  [ProductionServiceCrew.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionServiceCrew.js)
- **Accounts Manager → All, Received and Spent: one row per project, money in and out together.** A
  project with several cash entries on the tab - grouped by its Event ID - is one row, led by the Event
  ID and the count ("DBS-EVT-0001 · 3 entries"), the types it holds (Received /
  Spent), its latest date and the amount (the total, or the net received less spent where they mix) -
  opened with its chevron to show each entry with its own ⋮ (View, invoice, Edit, Delete) and tick box.
  An entry on no project, or alone on its project, stays a plain row. The project row has no ⋮ and opens
  no info panel; its tick box selects or clears every entry under it (part-ticked when some are), and
  "select all" takes in the entries inside projects too - through a new opt-in DataTable
  `selection.subRows`, so other expandable tables (a project's shoots) are unchanged. The CSV lists the
  entries, one line each. Transfers is unchanged. Frontend
  only.
  [AccountsTable.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/AccountsTable.js),
  [cashEntryGroups.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/cashEntryGroups.mjs)
- **Production → Schedule: the Assist is always shown, and picked from a multi-select.** Every shoot
  ends with its Assist block, "Not assigned" when nobody is on it. Whoever may change the plan clicks it
  to open a multi-select of the shooters and vendors (less any employee on another shoot at that time),
  and what was ticked is saved once as the picker closes - the plan's own `team` save, so the
  Production Manager check, active people and the busy-elsewhere refusal all hold. The Assist is not
  dragged. Board rows now also carry `assistPeople` (`emp:<id>` / `ven:<id>`). `MultiSelectField` gains
  `defaultOpen` and `onClose`. No migration.
  [ProductionScheduleView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionScheduleView.js),
  [ProductionSchedulePage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionSchedulePage.js),
  [MultiSelectField.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/MultiSelectField.js),
  [read.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/read.js)
- **Tasks → Dashboard's Recent Tasks has a Task ID column.** The ID (DBS-TK-00166) used to be a small
  grey line under the task's name. It is now the first column, so it can be read, sorted and filtered
  like the others. Its "Side" column is now called **Who Given** (My Task, Given or Studio).
  (`frontend/src/components/hrm/TaskDashboard.js`)
- **A Board column's trend is an arrow before its count, in the header's corner.** The count is the
  same size as the column's name. The +1 / −3
  number no longer shows on its own: it appears beside the arrow on hover, keyboard focus or a tap,
  with no popup. The period picker below reads **All, Today, This week, This month, 2 months**. This
  week and This month are still the last 7 and 30 days. A board whose cards carry no date has no
  trend, so it shows only the count. The small line under the heading is gone, because the arrow
  already says which way the column is going. This applies to every Board, CRM Leads included.
  (`frontend/src/components/data-table/KanbanBoard.js`, `KanbanSummary.js`,
  `frontend/src/components/sales/CrmKanbanBoard.js`, `frontend/src/lib/kanbanSummary.mjs`,
  `frontend/src/components/shared/SummaryCard.js`)
- **User Management's resignation entry points are one, and are called HR Offboarding.** The
  header ⋮ no longer has Resignation Request. Use HR Offboarding → Raise a form, which opens the
  same form with the employee picker. Offboarding Forms is now **HR Offboarding**, in the menu and
  as the title of the list it opens. A row's
  Offboarding Form is now **Resignation Form**, and the dialog, its list and its messages say
  "resignation form". The employee's public link page, the server's own messages and the Settings
  message template keep their names. (`frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeVerificationPage.js`,
  `EmployeeTable.js`, `OffboardingInviteDialog.js`, `docs/project-state/PROJECT-STATE.md`)
- **User Management's Pending tab now sits second, right after All.** It used to be the last tab, after
  InActive. The other tabs keep their order. (`frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeVerificationPage.js`)
- **Somebody serving their notice is listed under Active again, as well as under Serving Notice.**
  They are still working until their last day, so the Active tab and its count left them out wrongly.
  Serving Notice still lists them on its own. The Board keeps them in their own Serving Notice
  column. (`frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeVerificationPage.js`)
- **Review Pending is no longer a tab of its own in User Management.** It is still listed down the
  side of the Pending tab, with its count, so the bar no longer repeats it. Start Review stays in the
  ⋮ menu of any row whose review is overdue. If the page last showed Review Pending, it now opens on All.
  (`frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeVerificationPage.js`)
- **Offboarding starts a notice period again, instead of relieving at once.** When the last working
  day is today or later, the employee stays in Serving Notice with their status and login, and is
  relieved the day after their last working day (`servesNotice` in
  [separations/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/separations/controller.js)). This reverses
  the 27 Oct 2026 relieve-at-once rule. A last working day already past still relieves at once.
- **The frozen-column divider and the column resize line are quieter.** The line where frozen columns
  end was 2px over a dark blurred shadow, and it read as a thick blue bar down every table. It is
  now a 1px hairline (`--employee-table-divider` #e2e8f0) with a faint shade. A column's resize line
  was bright blue on hover and while dragging; it is now a 1px slate line that fades in, in the
  shared table and on the Production Schedule. Frontend only.
- **A board column's small dashboard takes less room.** On every Board view, each column's header,
  period picker, trend, trend line and search box are smaller, so the cards start higher:
  - The count is a size down.
  - The share ring went from 22 to 18 px.
  - The period picker, trend and column search use new `compact` options on the shared
    `Dropdown` (switch mode), `TrendBadge` and `SearchField`.
  - The trend line went from 56×20 to 44×16.

  Everywhere else those components keep their full size. Frontend only.
- **Any Photo Selling gallery can now be deleted from its card's ⋮ menu - live and sold ones too.**
  Delete used to appear only on an unpublished gallery with no paid orders
  ([GalleriesPage.js](../frontend/src/components/photo-selling/galleries/GalleriesPage.js)). A live
  gallery stops selling as it is deleted. A gallery with no orders is removed entirely, as before. One
  with orders loses its photos, files and guests' details and selfies, but its orders and payments
  stay in Orders for the studio's records, marked "(deleted)"; buyers can no longer download what they
  bought, which the confirmation says, pointing to Archive for keeping their downloads
  ([galleries/service.js](../backend/src/modules/photo-selling/galleries/service.js)). Needs migration
  `20261031140000_photo_sale_gallery_deleted_at` (one new nullable column, no existing row changed).
- **A Photo Selling share link or QR code now opens on a Login page - the same one AI Feature
  guests see - and the selfie page comes after it.** The store's first screen
  ([StoreLanding.js](../frontend/src/components/photo-selling/store/StoreLanding.js)) is now the AI
  Feature's guest login (its cover, studio mark and glass join card, reused through new optional
  copy props on `GuestLanding` / `GuestJoinCard`; the AI Feature's own page is unchanged): name,
  WhatsApp number with a country picker, and the PIN where set. After logging in the guest lands on
  the selfie page, where an uploaded photo is now previewed first with **Find my photos** and
  **Choose another**, as on the AI Feature. Everything behind the login now looks like the AI
  Feature's guest gallery too: its header (studio logo, gallery name, "Hi" and the guest's name,
  with the store's Cart and My orders beside it), the cover strip on a phone, its Find your photos
  card, a "Your Moments" summary above the matched photos, and its footer. The cover the studio
  picks (Photos step → **Use as cover**) fills the login's background **without the watermark** - its
  web-size preview, never the original, and only while that photo is on sale
  ([public/service.js](../backend/src/modules/photo-selling/public/service.js)); every other photo a
  guest sees is still watermarked. With no cover chosen the login stays a plain dark background. A session kept on the device is checked with the server
  before anything behind the login is shown, so a refresh stays logged in and an expired or invalid
  session returns to the Login with a notice. Same store session, no new sign-in method and no OTP;
  existing links, QR codes, selfie matching, cart, Cashfree payments, orders and WhatsApp messages
  are untouched.
- **Create Project books only at a finalized quotation.** Select Quotation now lists every version
  of the chosen enquiry's quotations, drafts included, grouped under each quotation number (V1 first),
  each with its status as a pill: **Finalized** (green) or **Unfinalized** (grey - a saved draft
  included). Only a Finalized version can be chosen - the others are shown dimmed
  and ignore a click, Enter and the arrow keys - read from the version's own state rather than its
  name or number. With nothing finalized it says "No finalized quotations available for this
  enquiry. Please finalize a quotation before creating a project."; a failed load offers Try again;
  the list is re-read when the tab comes back to the front, and a picked version unfinalized
  meanwhile is taken off the form with a note. `GET /api/sales/quotations?enquiryId=…&withDrafts=1`
  lists the enquiry's drafts too (without the flag nothing changes), and a Dropdown option may carry
  a `status: { label, tone }` pill. The register's **Create Project** is offered only on a finalized
  version. The server checks on save, whatever the form sent: a draft, a version never finalized or
  since unfinalized (409), another enquiry's version or one that does not exist (400) is refused and
  nothing is written; the row is locked while the project is saved. Existing projects are untouched:
  editing one keeps the version it is booked at even if it has since been unfinalized, and only
  moving it to another version is checked. No migration and no new permission - the project still
  stores the exact version id in `sales_project.quotation_id`.
  [SaleDetailsSection.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SaleDetailsSection.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js),
  [sales-project-finalized-quotation.test.js](../backend/test/sales-project-finalized-quotation.test.js)
- **Accounts Manager → Due and Overdue: one row per project, its payments under it.** A project
  owing several payments on the tab is one row - "N payments", the earliest due date, the amount and
  pending summed - opened with its chevron to show each payment, each with its own ⋮ View / Record. A
  project with one payment stays a plain row. The project row has no ⋮ and a double click on it does
  nothing. A filter searches the payments under it, and the CSV still lists one line per payment. On
  Hold is unchanged. Frontend only.
  [ScheduledPaymentsTable.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/ScheduledPaymentsTable.js),
  [scheduledPayments.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/scheduledPayments.mjs)
- **Production → Schedule: an EXT vendor's service shows Waiting in amber and Confirmed in green.**
  The whole service block takes the Shoot Board's amber or emerald tint (with its dark-theme pair): the
  service's name line in the stronger shade, the vendor's box, the Waiting / Confirmed word and the
  block's border. An employee's service and an empty seat stay plain.
  Frontend only.
  [ProductionScheduleView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionScheduleView.js)
- **File in asks a copy only for the services that hand files over.** A shoot's File in asked for a
  footage URL, who backed it up, a file count, a size and a first and last file name against **every**
  service booked on it - an LED wall and a hired light included, which bring nothing back to copy, so
  somebody had to put something in five boxes per service to finish the step. It now asks only for
  services whose Settings → Project → Services row has **Deliverable added = Yes**. A shoot whose
  services all deliver nothing says so and the step is finished by pressing it; a shoot with **no**
  services booked still answers once for the whole shoot, as before. The server decides the list
  (`photoCopyKeys`) and refuses an answer for a service that delivers nothing, so the screen is not
  the only thing enforcing it.

  **Only an explicit Yes counts**, which is how the quotation generator and the Settings table already
  read the flag - a service nobody has answered it for is a No. **A studio that has not set it on any
  service is therefore asked for nothing**, so tick it on the services that deliver files before
  relying on this. Footage already recorded against a service that no longer qualifies is left alone.
  [execution.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/execution.js),
  [ProductionStepForm.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionStepForm.js)
- **The calendar shows a production team member only their own shoots.** Somebody holding
  `PROJECT / Production` and none of Projects, Pre Production or Sales Manager was shown every shoot
  the Shoot Board lists for them - every shoot of a project they hold any role on (a Creative Manager,
  a Post Production Coordinator) and every shoot of the people reporting to them. Now the calendar is
  their own diary: the shoots they are on themselves - Production Coordinator, Production Team or a
  service's crew - and those of a project they are Production Manager or Project Manager of
  (`ownShootsWhere`). A Super Admin and Show All Projects still see every shoot, and so does anybody
  holding Projects, Pre Production or Sales Manager. The Shoot Board is unchanged.
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/schedule/calendar/service.js)
- **A shoot's steps can be run with Production Execution alone.** Completing a shoot's steps - Started
  from studio through File in, its status, its photos - took **both** `PROJECT / Production` at
  Read / Write and `PROJECT / Production Execution` at Read / Write, because the routes sat behind
  Production's own guard; a crew member named on the shoot with Execution, and Production only at Read,
  saw "Only the people named on this shoot, with Production Execution access, complete its steps".
  Now either permission is enough: **Production at Read / Write includes the execution, and Production
  Execution at Read / Write is the execution alone**. Being named on the shoot (coordinator, a service's
  crew or the Production Team) is still required. Those five routes sit above the router's guard behind
  `checkAnyPermission` of the two; the plan and everything else is unchanged and still Production's -
  a ticket upload, which is the plan's, asks Production at Read / Write in `execution.js`. The screen
  goes by the server's answer, and the message names both permissions. No new permission.
  [routes.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/routes.js),
  [access.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/access.js),
  [ProductionShootPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionShootPanel.js)
- **Crew see a shoot on Production once that shoot is planned.** A project's shoots are planned one by
  one, often weeks apart, but somebody only on a shoot's crew - a service's person or the Production
  Team - saw nothing until **every** shoot of the project was planned. Now a crew member is shown the
  project as soon as a shoot they are on is planned (or past it), with those shoots of theirs and no
  others, its status read from those shoots - so it stands under **Planned**, not only All; once the whole project is
  Planned they see it as before. The board's rows now say whether the viewer is on each shoot
  (`viewerOnShoot`); the Production Schedule follows the same rule. Nothing visible before is hidden.
  [read.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/read.js),
  [productionBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionBoard.mjs)
- **Production's full status bar is for the project's leads only.** Every status tab - Yet to Start,
  Work in Progress, Follow-up and the rest - is now offered only to somebody who **leads** a project:
  its Production Manager or Project Manager, a Super Admin, an administrator, or Show All Projects at
  Read / Write (`viewerLeads`). A shoot's **Production Coordinator** used to get it too, from a single
  shoot coordinated; they are now offered the crew's tabs (All, Planned, Execution, Hold, Rejected,
  Completed). Their own project still lists at every status under **All**, since they plan its shoots
  before it is Planned. What anybody can see or change is unchanged.
  [read.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/read.js),
  [productionBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionBoard.mjs)
- **A client's invoice link opens the invoice itself.** `/i/<token>` used to show a summary card and
  a View invoice button; a person opening it is now redirected straight to the PDF before any page is
  drawn (the app's first `src/proxy.js`, matching `/i/:token` only), where the phone's viewer offers
  the download. Link-preview bots (WhatsApp and the like) still get the page with the studio's name
  and logo, and a dead link is sent back by the PDF route to the "not available" page
  (`?unavailable=1`).
  [proxy.js](../frontend/src/proxy.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/accounts/cash-entries/controller.js)
- **Production → Schedule: more columns and Freeze Columns in its ⋮.** Manage Columns now offers
  Shoot Place, District, State, Shoot Type, Production Manager and Production Coordinator. They start
  hidden, and each has its own filter box once shown. The ⋮ also has **Freeze Columns** (None / First
  1-5): the first shown columns, counting the Shoot after them, stay at the left while the plan scrolls
  sideways. Column choices, freeze and widths are now kept as one `table:production-schedule` layout,
  which the server accepts. The old `production-schedule:*` keys were refused by the server (400),
  so they only ever lived in one browser, and anybody who had hidden or resized columns there sees the
  default layout once. The board rows now also carry `district`, `state` and `shootType`. No
  migration.
  [ProductionScheduleView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionScheduleView.js),
  [ProductionSchedulePage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionSchedulePage.js),
  [read.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/read.js)
- **Tasks has an Overdue tab, and a late due date reads in red.** Task Management gets an **Overdue**
  tab after All, counted like the others.
  - It lists tasks whose due day has passed while they are still owed: Pending, In Progress, or
    Finish & Send Back waiting for approval. A passed-on task does not count for the person who
    passed it on, and in My Tasks work you sent back does not count either.
  - It is an overlay, not a status: an overdue task stays under its own status tab too. The board
    has no Overdue column.
  - In every tab the Due cell of such a task reads e.g. "28/10/2026 · 3 days late" in red.
  - The rule (`taskIsOverdue` / `daysOverdue` in `constants/taskConfig.js`) is the Task
    Dashboard's Overdue card rule, so the two always agree.
  - The whole task workflow was checked end to end against the real API, as the giver, the holder,
    a third person, someone not on the task and a Super Admin. 29 checks all pass: create, start,
    finish and send back, approve, revoke, reassign, cancel, edit, overdue, delete, and who may and
    may not do each. No workflow bug was found.

  Frontend only. Tests: `frontend/test/task-overdue.test.mjs`.
- **Recycling Bin is now called Project Vault.** Resource Management → Recycling Bin is renamed
  Project Vault everywhere it is shown: the sidebar, the page title and table, its empty and
  loading messages, the Delete confirmations on Projects and Bookings & Converted, and the server's
  messages ("Project moved to the Project Vault.").
  - The permission's display name in Role Management changes too, through migration
    `20261031140000_project_vault_label` and the catalogue.
  - Its key stays `ASSET / Recycling Bin`, since every grant and route guard names it, and so does
    the URL `/asset-management/recycling-bin`. No role gains or loses anything, and nobody needs to
    be granted it again.
  - Run `prisma migrate deploy` (part of the normal deploy) to rename it in Role Management.
- **A resignation shows under Serving Notice as soon as the employee sends their offboarding form.**
  Before, a submitted form was invisible on the repository until HR opened Offboarding Forms and
  approved it.
  - The employee list now carries `resignationPending` (`{ submittedAt, proposedLastWorkingDate }`)
    for anyone whose form is Submitted. `isResignationPending` and `isLeaving` in
    `lib/employmentStatus.mjs` read it.
  - Those employees leave Active and appear under Serving Notice, in both the table and the board.
    Their board card says "Resignation awaiting HR".
  - Their row ⋮ offers **Review Resignation**, which opens Offboarding Forms where HR approves or
    rejects it. It replaces Offboarding Form on that row.
  - Nothing about the employee is written on submit. HR's approval is still what records the
    separation, sets the last working day, hands the work on and closes the login on the right day.
    A rejected form returns them to Active.

  No permission change. Tests: `backend/test/offboarding-invites.test.js`,
  `frontend/test/resignation-pending.test.mjs`.
- **An employee's offboarding form can be sent from their own row.** User Management → Administration
  → an employee's ⋮ now has **Offboarding Form**. It opens the same Resignation request form
  as the header's ⋮ → Resignation Request, with that employee already chosen, instead of picking
  them from a list.
  - It is offered only to readers who may change the repository, and only on someone working who is
    not onboarding, serving notice or already gone.
  - Someone with a form already open is told so, and the dialog shows the Offboarding Forms list,
    where their form is.
  - Opened from a row, the form is titled **Offboarding Form** and shows the employee's name as a
    read-only field, not a picker. It has no back arrow, since there is no list behind it.
  - The form no longer shows the line under the notice period ("They will be asked when their
    notice starts…") or the paragraph under the title ("Pick the employee…"). The ⓘ beside each
    field still explains it.
  - HR's form now asks the **Resignation date** (today by default) below the notice period. It shows
    the **Proposed last working day** beside it, the same two fields the employee's form has.
  - The server stores the date and works out the last day from it (`lastWorkingDateFrom`); a last
    day is never taken from the request. The employee's form opens on that date (`answers` on
    verify), and they can still change it before sending.
  - **The dates are HR's.** When HR set the resignation date, the employee's form shows it and the
    last working day read-only. The employee fills in only the reason, comments and letter.
    `hrSetResignationDate` (a date on a form never yet submitted) decides this, and verify sends it
    as `resignationDateFixed`.
  - On submit the server keeps HR's date, whatever the request says. When HR edits the notice
    period, the last working day is recounted from that date.
  - A form sent back after a submission carries the employee's own date, which stays theirs to
    correct.
  - `dayFromToday` moved into `lib/offboardingNotice.mjs` so both forms share it.
  - **Start Offboarding opens filled in from the employee's form.** When nothing is recorded yet and
    the employee has an offboarding form, the panel starts on it: Separation Type Resignation, the
    reason and comments they gave, the resignation date, their letter, the last working day, HR's
    notice days and HR's note as HR Remarks. The answered (Submitted) form is used first. A separation
    already on file always wins.
  - Completing a resignation from that panel approves the employee's Submitted form and links it to
    the separation (`createSeparation`), the same as approving it from Offboarding Forms would. The
    form is no longer left waiting in HR's queue. This is logged, never thrown, since the separation
    is already recorded.
  - The header's Resignation Request and Offboarding Forms are otherwise unchanged.

  Frontend only; the server's checks are unchanged and no permission changes. Test:
  `frontend/test/offboarding-from-row.test.mjs`.
- **A vendor is named the same way everywhere: `EXT-Sudeep (DBS, Erode)`.** That is the source type
  and vendor name, then the business registration name and city in brackets. A part the vendor has
  not filled in is left out, e.g. `EXT-Sudeep (Erode)`, and there is never an empty bracket. Before,
  each screen did its own thing: "EXT - name" in Production, "name · ID" in Payment Requests, the
  bare name elsewhere. It now applies to:
  - Production's service crew and Assist pickers, the schedule, and the Shoot Board and calendar
    team lists.
  - The crew swap log line and plan refusals.
  - The Asset status vendor picker and the Payment Request vendor picker.
  - The Vendors board card and the vendor's own panel title.

  The table keeps its separate Vendor Name and City columns. Nothing stored changes: the vendor's
  name is still saved as typed. The format is written once on each side,
  `backend/src/services/vendorLabel.js` and `frontend/src/lib/vendorLabel.mjs`, and
  `test/vendor-label.test.mjs` holds the two to the same answer. No permission change.
- **Automatic WhatsApp Message cards renamed: Sender and WhatsApp Group.** On Attendance WhatsApp
  Report and Photo Selection Submitted, the card "Who sends it" is now **Sender** and "Where it goes"
  is now **WhatsApp Group**. Both screens draw these cards from the same panel. Only the words
  changed.
- **A project's Activity tab now reads as a flow chart, with avatars.** Above the timeline, a
  journey strip shows every stage from Enquiry to Client Gifts, joined by arrows. Stages the project
  has reached are coloured and show how many steps each holds; stages still ahead are grey and
  dashed. Pressing a reached stage filters the timeline to it, the same as the Stage filter. The
  timeline is one thick line down the middle, oldest at the top. Each step is a ringed node in its
  stage colour, and the line down to the next step is that colour too. What happened (stage, title,
  detail) sits left of the line. On the right are an icon where a new stage begins (headset for
  Enquiry, camera for Production, gift for Client Gifts and so on), then the initials avatar and name
  of the person who did the step ("System" when nobody did), and the date and time. On a phone the
  line moves to the left edge and everything reads beside it. The layout follows the width of the
  pane the tab is shown in, not the window: beside the Pre Production follow-ups it switches to the
  one-sided layout sooner. The Activity tab also fills its pane now. In Pre Production, Production
  and Start Project it was boxed at 860px, leaving empty space to its right. The journey strip wraps
  onto a second line instead of scrolling sideways, so no stage is cut off at either end. A grey,
  dashed stage can be pressed too. A note under the strip then says nothing is recorded there yet
  and what will fill it, e.g. "It fills in when the team plans a shoot in Pre Production". It also
  says a stage the viewer's role cannot open stays grey. Pressing it again, or ×, hides the note. A ring on the line,
  or a stage's picture beside it, can be pressed as well: it shows only that stage's steps, and
  pressing it again shows every stage. Search and the Stage and Person filters work
  as before. The journey strip is a new shared component, `components/shared/JourneyStrip.js`, so
  another process can be drawn the same way. Only the look changed: there is no new permission and
  no backend change.
- **Every Board has a new look: glass lanes with avatars.** A column no longer wears a solid coloured
  header bar: its status colour is a thin line along the top and a light wash over the lane, beside
  a large count and a small ring showing the column's share of every card on the board (the Leads
  board, which pages its leads, shows the count without the ring). Cards carry an initials avatar and
  a left edge in the column's colour, and their details as small chips. The colour is read from the
  class each screen already gives its columns (`lib/boardTone.mjs`), pale colours write their
  letters in slate so they stay readable, and the lane keeps its themed fill so dark mode still has
  edges. Every board - and Leads & Followups - changes at once; drag and drop, trends, periods and
  search behave as before.
  [KanbanBoard.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/KanbanBoard.js),
  [boardTone.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/boardTone.mjs)
- **Production: Table, Board and Schedule are one dropdown at the right end of the header.** The
  Table / Schedule switch sat beside the title and the Table / Board switch at the right; both
  Production pages now carry one `ProductionViewSwitch` in their actions. Board still uses the
  remembered layout, so picking Table or Board from the Schedule sets it and returns to the
  table page. Production only - every other screen keeps its own Table / Board switch.
  [ProductionViewSwitch.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionViewSwitch.js)
- **Studio Start Date and Time move from Pre Production to Production.** When the crew leaves the
  studio is the Production Manager's to plan, so it is now asked on the plan's Travel section
  (outdoor shoots only, mandatory like Travel Mode - counted in the plan's progress and needed to
  submit it) and no longer on Pre Production's form, info panel or progress
  count - an outdoor shoot is Planned on five mandatory answers, not seven - nor on the client
  portal. Migration `20261030120000_production_studio_start` adds `project_production.studio_start_date`
  / `studio_start_time` and copies every raised production's answer over from pre production; the
  old columns stay (deprecated) and are carried once onto a production raised later. The Pre
  Production import still reads the two columns and writes them to the production row. Run
  `npx prisma migrate deploy`; no seed and no permission - it rides on `PROJECT / Production`.
  [productionFormConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/productionFormConfig.js),
  [plan.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/plan.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/service.js),
  [formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js)
- **Calendar: a shoot opens on Projects, and its ⋮ opens every board on that shoot.** A shoot in the
  shoot window opened the Production panel, and one in a day's **Shoots · N** pop-up opened its Pre
  Production or Production form depending on its stage. Pressing a shoot now opens the **Projects**
  board on **All**, filtered to its Shoot ID, so the project opens on that shoot's row. The ⋮'s
  **Navigate to**, which only filtered each board to the project, now lands on the shoot itself
  (`boardJumps.mjs` `shootBoardHref`): Projects as above, **Pre Production** and **Production** on the
  shoot's own form (`?project=…&shoot=…`), Bookings & Converted and Post Production - no shoot rows -
  on the project. Update is unchanged. Pressing needs `PROJECT / Projects` Read: without it the
  window's card is not a button and the pop-up's opens the shoot window. The calendar no longer opens
  the Production panel itself. Frontend only, no new permission.
  [MeetingsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/MeetingsPage.js),
  [boardJumps.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/boardJumps.mjs)
- **Production → Schedule's Date column shows the shoot's time.** Under each date, its start and end
  ("6:30 pm – 10:00 pm", "(next day)" where it ends after midnight), the start alone where only that is
  set, and **No time** where neither is. Read from the shoot's own times on the rows the screen
  already loads (`scheduleTimeLabel`, using the board's `shootTimeLabel`); the column is a little wider
  for it. Frontend only, same guard.
  [ProductionScheduleView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionScheduleView.js),
  [productionSchedule.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionSchedule.mjs)
- **A drone service may be flown by somebody already on another service of the shoot.** Any service
  with "drone" in its name is left out of "one employee, one service of a shoot": the same employee may
  work, say, Traditional Video and Complementary Drone, or another of the team may fly it. Its picker
  (on the Schedule and in the plan form) leaves nobody out, flying it takes nobody off another
  service's list, and a drag onto it - or of its pilot onto another service - is not refused for it. Every
  other service still takes one employee only, and the time clash across shoots still applies.
  `crew.isDrone` / `doubledPerson(crew, held, services)`, `swap.js` `refuseDoubled`, `isDroneService`.
  [crew.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/crew.js),
  [swap.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/swap.js),
  [productionSchedule.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionSchedule.mjs),
  [ProductionServiceCrew.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionServiceCrew.js)
- **A submitted plan may have a service emptied; it then reads Work in Progress.** The Schedule's
  person picker always offers **Not assigned** (it used to be hidden on a submitted plan), a person
  dragged onto an empty service may leave their own empty on a submitted plan, and filling one of
  several empty services on a submitted plan now saves. Such a plan stays submitted and reads **Work in
  Progress** until every service has its person - the status already counted an empty service as
  missing. Submitting still needs a person on every service; the plan panel's Save changes on a
  submitted plan no longer demands one. `plan.js` refuses an empty service only when submitting;
  `swap.js` no longer refuses. Same guard, no new permission.
  [plan.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/plan.js),
  [swap.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/swap.js),
  [ProductionScheduleView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionScheduleView.js),
  [ProductionShootPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionShootPanel.js)
- **"Use the same team as above" on a Schedule shoot's ⋮.** Where the shoot of the same project just
  above shares a service with this one, the ⋮ offers it: each shared service takes that shoot's person,
  and this shoot's other services stay as they are. Shown only when it would change something and only
  to whoever may change this shoot's plan. Saved by a new `POST
  /api/project-management/production/shoots/:shootId/copy-team` (`plan.js` `copyTeam`), through the
  plan save and all its rules; a refusal is said in the "This action is not possible" dialog. Same
  router guard (`PROJECT / Production`), no new permission.
  [plan.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/plan.js),
  [ProductionSchedulePage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionSchedulePage.js),
  [productionSchedule.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionSchedule.mjs)
- **A vendor's Waiting / Confirmed is changed on the Schedule right under the vendor, without a pop-up.**
  The status line under a vendor's box is now the control: click **Waiting** (or **Confirmed**) and pick
  the other from a small menu; it saves at once through the same seat save. The service line's **⋮ →
  Change status** and its **Vendor status** box are gone (`VendorStatusDialog.js` deleted). Same guard,
  no new permission.
  [ProductionScheduleView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionScheduleView.js),
  [ProductionSchedulePage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionSchedulePage.js)
- **Production → Schedule shows each person in a picker's box again, with their face, and no colour.**
  The person under a service reads as the dropdown it opens - avatar, name, arrow - instead of plain
  text, and the red / amber / green fills are gone: "Not assigned" is grey, a vendor still reads
  "EXT - name" with "Waiting" under it while waiting. The real picker is still mounted only when a box is
  clicked, so the sheet scrolls as fast as before. Frontend only.
  [ProductionScheduleView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionScheduleView.js),
  [ProductionSchedulePage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionSchedulePage.js)
- **AI Feature has one notification setting: New match notification**, on web and desktop (Event
  Default Settings and each event). New photo notification, Processing completed and the old studio
  New match switch are gone - none of them ever sent anything. The remaining switch is the guest's
  WhatsApp message when photos uploaded later are matched to them (stored as before,
  `notifications.guestWhatsAppSummary`, off by default - so no event starts messaging on its own).
  Sending, deduplication, the `photos_ready` template and `AI_FEATURE_WHATSAPP_ENABLED` are
  unchanged; the retired keys stay stored, unread.
  [SettingsGroupForm.js](../frontend/src/components/ai-feature/shared/SettingsGroupForm.js)
- **Photo Selling's Orders now use the application's standard table**, as Projects and the Image
  Selection dashboard do: the same headings and rows, a filter box under each heading, sorting, Table
  Options (columns, compact view, CSV), and the usual loading and empty states. The status is now
  tabs, each with its count for the range picked - All orders (2) / Paid (1) / Awaiting payment (0) /
  Payment failed (1), counted by the server (`counts` on the orders list) - and the search box is
  gone; beside the tabs, a range -
  Lifetime, This week, This month, 3 months, 6 months (rolling: the last 7 or 30 days, 3 or 6 months;
  `GET /api/photo-selling/orders?range=7d|30d|3m|6m`). Status, range and the 50-a-page paging are the
  server's, so counts are right; a row still opens the
  order. Same table on a gallery's own Orders tab.
  [OrdersTable.js](../frontend/src/components/photo-selling/orders/OrdersTable.js)
- **Photo Selling's Dashboard no longer shows the server's setup status** (Payments, Originals
  storage, Selfie search) on web and desktop - only the sales figures. The same status is still in
  Photo Selling → Settings, and on desktop in a project's Details and Preview steps.
  [PhotoSellingOverviewPage.js](../frontend/src/components/photo-selling/overview/PhotoSellingOverviewPage.js)
- **Photo Selling's section menu reads Dashboard / Projects / Orders, on web and desktop.** Overview is
  now labelled Dashboard and Galleries Projects - names only: the same pages at the same addresses,
  with the same permissions, data and actions; the Projects page's words ("Projects appear here",
  "Back to projects") follow.
  [PhotoSellingNavigation.js](../frontend/src/components/photo-selling/PhotoSellingNavigation.js)
- **The desktop app's searches now find words in any order, like the web (Word Chunk Search).**
  Typing "we ot", "ot 689" or "366895 we" finds "WED other 366895" in the desktop's Image Selection
  sidebar, every dashboard table's filter boxes, the projects hub, the WhatsApp group picker, Album
  Proofing's group names and AI Feature's person search: every word typed must be found somewhere,
  inside a word or number too, ignoring case and extra spaces. Before, the desktop matched the typed
  text as one piece, so "we ot" found nothing there while the web found it. Each table filter box
  still searches only its own column; the projects hub and person search let each word be found in
  either of their two fields. The rule is the web's own `lib/wordChunks.mjs`, copied word for word
  into the desktop's `src/lib/wordChunks.js` (a test holds the two identical). Web and server
  searches already worked this way and are unchanged; the date and day columns still read "12 Oct"
  as one phrase. No migration.
- **Money received now settles the project's scheduled payment it is for, wherever it is recorded.**
  A payment taken at booking, or added on Add Entry or a project's Payments tab, was filed against
  the project but not against its Schedule Payment, so the Advance it paid still read unpaid and
  turned Overdue - and pressing Clear on it then recorded the money a second time. Now choosing the
  project shows **Settles Payment** (its payments still open, oldest first, None by default) and, once
  one is chosen, **Full payment** (the amount is filled in with what is pending; the payment clears)
  or **Partial payment** (two boxes, **Amount Paid Now** and **Amount to Pay Later**, which always add
  up to what is pending - typing either fills the other - and a **Balance Due Date**; the rest becomes
  a payment of its own). The receipt that opens after Save & Next now shows over the cash form rather
  than behind it, on Accounts Manager and on a project's Payments tab.
  The booking form (Bookings and Converted) offers the schedule being booked the same way, with its
  first payment (the Advance) already chosen unless changed to None, and now saves the schedule
  before the advance; Import from PDF gets it through the same form; the CSV import takes two optional
  columns, **Scheduled Payment** and **Balance Due Date**. Every path, Clear and Partially paid
  included, goes through one rule, `settleInTx` in
  [scheduled-payments/service.js](../backend/src/modules/accounts/scheduled-payments/service.js),
  in the entry's own transaction, and only for a project the person may work (Cash Management's
  reach, or the project on their board). A receipt that settled a payment keeps its amount and
  project on edit. Entries recorded before this are not tied automatically. `GET
  /api/accounts/scheduled-payments/project/:projectId/open` is new, under the same guard. No schema
  change, no new permission.
- **Running a shoot's execution steps needs the new `PROJECT / Production Execution` permission.**
  Being named on the shoot (its Production Coordinator, the project's Production Manager, its
  Production Team or a service's crew) still decides *which* shoots a person runs; the permission,
  at Read / Write, now decides *whether* they run steps at all - completing a step, File in, the
  step photos, the shoot status. Named without it, they read the Execution tab ("Only the people
  named on this shoot, with Production Execution access, complete its steps.") and the server
  refuses with 403. The Plan is unchanged, and a Super Admin and `PROJECT / Show All Projects` Read
  / Write still run every shoot. Migration `20261030090000_production_execution_permission` adds the
  permission and grants it to `SUPER_ADMIN` only, so **until roles are ticked, only those two run
  steps** - the studio may want to grant it to the roles its Production Coordinators, Production
  Managers and shooting crew hold, in Role Management. Rule in `accessFor`
  ([production/access.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/access.js)).
- **Whoever holds Cash Management can work every payment on a project they can see.** On a project's
  Payments tab, View, Download invoice, Edit and Share used to answer "Cash entry not found" for a
  payment somebody else recorded on a branch outside the viewer's own Cash Management scope, even
  though the tab listed it. Now any payment filed against a project the viewer sees on their board
  opens, downloads, edits and shares, whoever recorded it and whatever its branch; an edit that keeps
  it on that project and in its branch is not refused for the branch. Delete, the bulk delete and the
  Accounts Manager list keep to the Cash Management scope as before, and so does moving a payment to
  another project or another branch.
  `scopedEntry(…, { throughProject: true })` and `onVisibleProject` in
  [cash-entries/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/accounts/cash-entries/controller.js), read
  through `readableProject`. Same guard (`ACCOUNTS / Cash Management`), no new permission.
- **A shoot's row under its project has Edit, opening the project's form on that shoot.** On Projects
  and Bookings & Converted, a project's shoots (▸) offered only "Open project" in their ⋮. They now also
  offer **Edit** wherever the project's own Edit is offered to that person: it opens the same form the
  project's Edit does - Start / Edit Project for whoever may plan it, Edit Sale Details for whoever may
  change the booking - with that shoot's edit box open once the form has loaded. A shoot of a project
  the person may not edit offers Open project alone. Pre Production and Production already offered
  Edit (or View) on a shoot's row, opening its form, and are unchanged. Permission-led as before; no
  server change.
  [ProjectDataTable.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/ProjectDataTable.js),
  [useProjectPlan.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/useProjectPlan.js)
- **A project's shoots are listed by date everywhere, earliest first, with undated shoots last.** The
  server already sorted them by date, but MySQL puts an empty date first, so every list of a project's
  shoots opened on the shoots nobody had dated - before the ones actually coming up. Now the dated ones
  come first, in date order, and the undated after them: Pre Production's shoot tiles and table rows,
  Projects, Bookings & Converted and their shoot rows and columns, the project form and its services,
  the project stage view, the calendar, the Shoot Board, CRD events and the client app. The project
  form and Create Project keep that order while shoots are added or re-dated, rather than putting a new
  one at the end. The Quotation Generator keeps the order its shoots are dragged into. One rule on each
  side: `services/shootOrder.js` (`SHOOT_DATE_ASC`) and `lib/shootOrder.mjs` (`shootsByDate`).
  [shootOrder.js](../backend/src/services/shootOrder.js),
  [shootOrder.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/shootOrder.mjs)
- **Production → Schedule stays fast with thousands of shoots.** On production, with 5,000+ shoots, it
  loaded every shoot ever booked and drew a person picker on every service of every one at once. Now:
  it asks the server for only the days chosen (`GET /api/project-management/production/shoots?from=&to=`
  or `?undated=1` - the Production table still reads every shoot, asking for none) and **opens on
  Upcoming**, with All dates one choice away; it draws 60 shoots and another 60 as you scroll to the end
  ("Showing 60 of 412 shoots - scroll for more"), "Today" drawing down to its shoot first; and each
  service shows its person as text, the picker appearing - already open - only when it is clicked. A
  newer load never draws over an older one still arriving. The shared `Dropdown` gains `defaultOpen`.
  [ProductionSchedulePage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionSchedulePage.js),
  [ProductionScheduleView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionScheduleView.js),
  [read.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/read.js)
- **Production → Schedule can show the shoots with no date yet.** Its date choices - All dates,
  Upcoming, Next 30 days, Custom - now include **Unknown date**, which lists only the shoots nobody has
  dated, with the Projects filter and everything else on the sheet working as before. The count beside
  it reads "Unknown date". All dates still shows every shoot, dated or not; a span of days shows none of
  the undated ones.
  [ProductionSchedulePage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionSchedulePage.js),
  [ShootDateRangeFilter.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/shoot-board/ShootDateRangeFilter.js),
  [productionSchedule.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionSchedule.mjs)
- **Production → Schedule's Dates filter is down to three choices: All dates (still the default),
  Upcoming - every shoot from today on, with no last day - and Next 30 days.** This week, This month,
  Next month, Next 3 months and Custom dates are gone from it; the Shoot Board keeps its own list
  unchanged. The shared Dates filter takes a choice with its own range for Upcoming. Frontend only.
  [ProductionSchedulePage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionSchedulePage.js),
  [ShootDateRangeFilter.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/shoot-board/ShootDateRangeFilter.js)
- **Production → Schedule groups a project's shoots on continuous days, not the whole project.** A
  project's shoots sit together only while each is on the same day as the one before it or the next;
  a gap of a day or more starts a new group, placed by its own date. So shoots on the 11th, 11th, 15th,
  16th and 19th show as three groups - 11 + 11, 15 + 16, 19 alone - with other projects' shoots between
  them where their dates fall. Event ID and Event are written on each group's first row, and the
  colours start again from the first one in every group. Frontend only, no permission change.
  [productionSchedule.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionSchedule.mjs),
  [ProductionScheduleView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionScheduleView.js)
- **A vendor (EXT) may now work several services of one shoot, and shoots at the same time.** The
  "one person works one service of a shoot" rule and the time-clash rule are now for employees only.
  The plan's Services pickers and the Production Schedule's pickers keep offering a vendor already on
  another service of the shoot, a drag that puts a vendor on a second service is no longer refused, and
  the plan save, the seat save and the seat swap accept it (`crew.doubledPerson` counts employees only;
  `swap.js` `refuseDoubled` skips vendors). The time clash already left vendors out. No new permission.
  [crew.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/crew.js),
  [swap.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/swap.js),
  [productionSchedule.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionSchedule.mjs),
  [ProductionServiceCrew.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionServiceCrew.js)
- **A vendor's status is changed from Production → Schedule itself.** A vendor's service box has its
  own **⋮** on the grey line, for whoever may change that shoot's plan: **Change status** opens a small
  **Vendor status** box - Waiting or Confirmed - and Save stores it on that seat, the box turning green
  ("EXT - name") when Confirmed. No need to open the production plan. The seat save (`PATCH
  /api/project-management/production/shoots/:shootId/seat`) takes an optional `vendorStatus` (Waiting /
  Confirmed) for the vendor already on the seat; a vendor new to a seat still starts on Waiting whatever
  is sent. Same guard as before, no new permission.
  [ProductionScheduleView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionScheduleView.js),
  [VendorStatusDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/VendorStatusDialog.js),
  [plan.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/plan.js)
- **Production → Schedule has Table Options and resizable columns.** The ⋮ is the same menu every
  table has. **Manage Columns** shows or hides the shoot's own columns - Event
  ID, Event, Shoot ID and Date - remembered for each person; the Shoot and its production plan always
  show. **Compact view**, the application's one density setting, draws the sheet a size smaller on top
  of its Zoom, which stays as it was. Each column - the shoot's four and the Shoot - is **resized** by
  dragging its header's right edge, as on the tables, and keeps that width for that person at any zoom;
  **Reset Table Layout** brings back the defaults once something is hidden or resized. The ⋮ sits at
  the end of the sheet's header row, held in view while it scrolls sideways (in the top bar on a phone). Each
  shoot has its own **⋮** at the end of its row with **Navigate to** Projects, Pre Production or
  Production for its project - the row menu's own entry, so a board is offered only where the project
  is on it and the viewer holds that board's permission; Production opens the Production table
  filtered to the project.
  [ProductionSchedulePage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionSchedulePage.js),
  [ProductionScheduleView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionScheduleView.js)
- **On the Projects screen, PROJECT / Projects Read / Write is enough to edit both a project's plan
  and its sale details.** Whoever holds it now sees both **Start / Edit** (the project form) and **Edit
  Sale Details** (the booking form) in a project's row menu, started or not. Before, a started project's
  plan was its Project Manager's, a branch administrator's or a Show All Projects holder's only, so a
  Projects Read / Write holder saw a single "Edit" that opened the sale form instead of the project.
  The server allows the same: changing a started project's plan, its shoots and allocations
  (`mayEditStartedProject`), and saving its sale details (`mayEditProject`). Bookings & Converted is
  unchanged: the CRM side still edits there only after Send Back.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js),
  [ProjectsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectsPage.js)
- **The project boards' row ⋮ says "Navigate to" in place of "Jump to".** On Projects, Pre
  Production, Production and Post Production, the menu line that opens the same project on another
  board is now **Navigate to**, with the boards inside it as before. Only the wording changed.
  [boardJumps.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/boardJumps.mjs)
- **The Attendance Register has an Irregularities card among its status cards.** Beside Present,
  Available, Leave, Permissions and Break, **Irregularities** counts the fixed-shift people Absent
  that day - away with no approved leave, comp-off or permission - and pressing it narrows Today's
  Attendance to them, as the other cards do. They are the same people as the Irregularities card's
  Today tab below; a flexible shift's absence is judged the day after and stays on that card's
  Yesterday tab. Six cards in a row from a laptop up; on a phone it takes a row of its own.
  [AttendanceRegisterPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRegisterPage.js)
- **The daily attendance report lists a leave not yet approved under Leave, "(approval pending)".**
  Somebody not in whose leave or comp-off for the day is still waiting on its approvers used to be
  listed under Uninformed Leave - or under nothing at all on a Flexible Shift, still "Yet to log
  in". The WhatsApp group message and the report copied from the Attendance Register now put them on
  the Leave list as "Name (ID) (approval pending)" ("- Comp-off (approval pending)" for a comp-off),
  counted in Leave and not in Uninformed Leave. The day itself is unchanged: it reads On leave only
  once the request is approved. The register sends `leavePending` on each row for this.
  [reportText.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/reportText.js),
  [attendanceReport.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/attendanceReport.mjs),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js)
- **Requests are answered in bulk with one Update, for "Select Table Rows in Bulk", on any tab.**
  On HRM → Request (and Employee Attendance → Request), the tick boxes and their **Update** button
  are for a role holding `ADMIN / Table Select All` - a Super Admin always does - and appear on every
  tab, not only Waiting for me. Update asks **Approve**, **Reject** or **Send back** from a Decision
  drop-down; Reject and Send back also ask the reason, given to every request answered. Send back
  reaches the requests the row's own menu would send back - never a comp-off credit attendance raised -
  and clears their approvals, as one at a time. It replaces the separate Approve and Reject buttons. Only the requests waiting on that person are answered: one they are
  not a named approver on, their own, or one already answered is skipped, and the message says how
  many ("12 requests approved. 3 requests skipped - not waiting for your answer"). An approver
  without the permission answers requests one at a time from each row's menu, and loses the tick
  boxes they had before. Each answer is still the single approve / reject call, checked by the
  server per request. No new permission: the studio grants `ADMIN / Table Select All` in Role
  Management to the admin roles it wants to have this.
  [AttendanceRequestsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestsPage.js)
- **Branch, Department, Vertical and Status columns always filter by a dropdown.** A table's filter
  row used to guess, from the rows on screen, whether a column was a list or a text box - so a
  Branch or Status column showed an empty text box to type into on an empty or nearly empty table,
  on a big one (more than 40 different values) and wherever a few rows each had a different branch.
  These are columns whose answers the studio already knows, so they no longer guess: every Status
  column lists its module's statuses, and every Branch, Department and Vertical column lists the
  studio's branches, departments and verticals from master data - all of them, even ones no row uses
  yet - plus any value a row holds beyond the list. Tick to filter, as before. **A cell naming
  several answers is split**: an employee in "Management, Sales" no longer makes "Management, Sales"
  an option of its own - the list shows Management and Sales once each, and ticking Management finds
  everybody in Management, alone or beside another department (it used to find only those in
  Management alone). The same holds for any column listing several values. ID, name, phone, email,
  amount and date columns keep their text or date boxes. Applies to every table at once; tables that
  filter at the server (CRM Leads, Activity Logs, WhatsApp log) keep their own lists. No backend
  change.
  [tableCells.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/tableCells.js),
  [useKnownFilterLists.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/useKnownFilterLists.js)
- **An Image Selection gallery with no photos left goes offline by itself, and comes back with the
  same link and PIN.** A gallery is now published only while the client has a photo to see anywhere
  in the project, in any folder or subfolder. Deleting one folder while photos remain elsewhere
  changes nothing. With none left, Publish Status turns off on its own, and the client's link says
  "Your photos are not available yet".

  When a photo is back, the gallery is published again with the same URL, PIN and expiry, and
  clients who already have the link need nothing new. A photo is back when an upload finishes, AI
  Culling is finalized or reopened, or photos are sent on from AI Editing.

  Photos still processing, rejected by a cull, waiting in AI Culling or AI Editing, or in a shoot
  whose date has not come do not count. A gallery the studio unpublished by hand, one that expired,
  and one unpublished before this change are never republished automatically.

  **Migration** `20261029130000_gallery_publication_revoked_reason` adds the nullable
  `revoked_reason` column (MANUAL / EXPIRED / EMPTY) to `image_selection_gallery_publication`. No
  existing value changes; run `prisma migrate deploy`. The first time each studio panel is opened,
  or each client link is used, after deploying, a published gallery that already has no visible
  photo is taken offline this way.
  [publication/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/publication/service.js),
  [publication/repository.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/publication/repository.js)
- **A shoot with no Photo Selection deliverable is now on none of Image Selection's tabs.** Before,
  a shoot added with no deliverables (a Haldi on an existing booking) was hidden from Photo
  Selection but still listed under AI Culling and AI Editing. When those two tabs have no allocation
  of their own, they now show the same shoots as Photo Selection. Allocating Photo Selection to the
  shoot in Project Management puts it on all three. Nothing is deleted or moved, and a project with
  no Photo Selection allocated anywhere still shows every shoot on every tab.
  [imageSelectionTabs.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/imageSelectionTabs.mjs)
- **Every started project gets its Image Selection project, under its current name.** Before, only In
  Progress projects were linked, so a booking moved to Completed or On Hold before anybody opened
  Image Selection never got one. Now every project except Yet to Start is linked, by its Sales
  project id and only once. A status change never makes a second one, and Production and Pre
  Production play no part. It still appears in the sidebar only from its first shoot's date.

  A linked project's name now follows the WhatsApp group name: a group renamed in Project Management
  used to leave Image Selection showing the old name. Each list load brings the name back in step.
  Only the name changes; the links, folders, photos and picks stay as they are. A rename that would
  give two projects one name, or a project left unlinked because its name is taken, is now logged
  instead of skipped silently. Album Proofing's own rows are not renamed.

  The `client-push` test suite's leftover projects (`TCPU-…`) are now cleared by the test fixture
  sweep before each `npm test` run. No migration and no data change.
  [projects/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/projects/service.js),
  [projects/repository.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/projects/repository.js),
  [clear-test-fixtures.js](../backend/scripts/clear-test-fixtures.js)
- **Image Selection opens each shoot on its own date, India time, and a re-dated shoot keeps the
  client's work.** A Wedding on 28 Oct and a Reception on 29 Oct now appear in Image Selection - the
