  shoot's folder, its photos and its selection items - from 00:00 IST on their own dates, one at a
  time. This used to be the day after, counted from midnight UTC (05:30 in India). An undated shoot
  stays hidden until it has a date. Production and Pre Production statuses play no part. A shoot
  moved to a later date is only hidden, in the studio's tree and in the client gallery and portal
  alike. Its photos, picks, submissions and published gallery are kept, and come back as they were
  on the new date. Its selection items are no longer marked inactive; only a deliverable taken off
  the project is. Linking is unchanged: each Image Selection project belongs to its Sales project by
  id. No migration and no data change.
  [shoot-visibility.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/shoot-visibility.js),
  [deliverables/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/deliverables/service.js),
  [gallery/repository.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/gallery/repository.js)
- **A half day now counts as 0.5 present and 0.5 absent.** On the employee's own Attendance →
  Dashboard ("Your attendance") and on the administrator's Attendance Dashboard (the cards, the
  day-by-day table and the per-employee table), a Half day used to add a whole day to Present and
  nothing to Absent. It now adds half to each, so twenty owed days with two half days read 19
  present and 1 absent. The Half day figure is still the number of half days, and the day itself
  still reads "Half day" on the calendar, the register and the day rows. The rule is `dayShares` in
  [attendanceRules.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/attendanceRules.js), read by
  `attendanceSummary`, `attendanceTotals` and the Dashboard's `tallyRange` in
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js). Unchanged: the register's
  Today's Attendance cards, which count people at that moment, and payroll, which already counted a
  half day as 0.5 of lost pay. No permission changed.
- **The Attendance Register's Irregularities card has Today and Yesterday tabs.** **Today** lists
  the fixed-shift staff absent today with no approved leave or permission. **Yesterday** lists the
  flexible-shift staff absent yesterday: their day is only judged once it is over, so they were
  never listed for today and were mixed into the same list before. Each tab shows its count, and the
  card title still shows the total. The split is `irregularityTabs` in
  [attendanceRegisterCards.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/attendanceRegisterCards.mjs), drawn with the
  shared `Tabs` in [RegisterAttentionCards.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/RegisterAttentionCards.js).
  Frontend only: the server's list and who may read it are unchanged.
- **Every payment in Shedule Payment now needs a date.** On Create / Edit Project and Start / Edit
  Project the Date column is marked required. A save with a payment that has a category and a
  percentage but no date is refused with "Choose a date for every payment under Shedule Payment."
  and the empty dates are outlined in red. The new blank row added below the last payment is not
  counted until something is typed in it. Two rows are exempt: the row settling the balance (the
  category flagged so in Settings → Field Settings, Final Settlement by default), which takes no
  date, and a payment Accounts has already worked, which is kept as it is. The rule is
  `undatedPayments` in [paymentSchedule.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/paymentSchedule.mjs), and
  `saveProjectSchedule` in
  [scheduled-payments/service.js](../backend/src/modules/accounts/scheduled-payments/service.js)
  refuses the same rows with a 400 before writing anything, so the API cannot skip it. A project
  saved earlier with an undated payment needs that date filled in the next time its schedule is
  saved. `SchedulePaymentSection` now takes its categories from the form (`usePaymentCategories`),
  so the form's check and the red cells read one list. No permission changed.
- **A "Jump to" between project boards always lands on the All tab.** Each board remembers the tab
  it was last left on. A jump used to come to All only when the project was not on that tab, so a
  project on the remembered tab (In Progress, Hold, …) opened there, and clearing the project
  filter afterwards showed that one status rather than the whole board. Now Projects, Pre
  Production, Production and Post Production all switch to All whenever a jump arrives, then
  filter to the project as before. The board then stays on All next time, like any tab the reader
  picks. The rule is in
  [useLinkedProject.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/useLinkedProject.js); the callers no
  longer pass the rows it used to check. No permission changed.
- **Attendance requests: bulk Approve and Reject.** On Waiting for me (and an administrator's All),
  an approver ticks the requests still waiting for their answer and presses **Approve (n)** - done at
  once - or **Reject (n)**, which asks one reason for all of them. Each button counts as it goes
  ("Approving 3 of 10…") and a notice says how many were approved or rejected; any the server refused
  stay ticked with its reason. Each request is sent through the same approve / reject call as its own
  ⋮, so the server decides every one again and nothing about who may decide changed. An approver
  without `ADMIN / Table Select All` gets tick boxes on the rows they can answer only; with it, the
  table's usual selection carries the two buttons beside Export / Delete. Reject skips a request the
  approver already rejected (they may still approve it). No backend change, no new permission.
- **User Management and Role Management list only the studio's own people, not client logins.** A
  client's sign-in (Create Project → Client Credentials, named after the project's WhatsApp group) no
  longer appears in the Users table, in a role's Manage Users picker or among a role's holders
  (`GET /api/admin/users`, `GET /api/admin/roles/:roleId/users` now leave out `role` CLIENT), and
  `POST /api/admin/users/:userId/roles` refuses to give one a role (400). Client logins are unchanged
  and still sign in to the client portal. Same guards as before, no new permission.
- **Production → Plan → People: assistants are chosen once for the whole shoot, under Assist.** Service
  cards no longer offer assistant seats; each service takes its own person and cameras only. One
  searchable multi-select **Assist** field sits below the last service card (removable chips), listing
  shooters and active vendors who are not on an overlapping shoot. It is kept as the shoot's Production
  Team (`ProjectProductionTeamMember`), so there is **no schema change or migration**: the board, access,
  feedback, handover and sheet import already read it. The plan save (`team` in the plan body) checks
  each entry is one employee or one vendor, appears once, is active, and an employee newly added holds
  a shooting skill and is free at that time. Assist members now also count as busy for other shoots.
  Assistants given to a service before are shown under Assist and move there on the next save; a save
  sending no `team` (an older client) keeps them. Same guard as the plan (`PROJECT / Production`), no
  new permission.
- **Production's status tabs now follow the viewer's part in each project.** Whoever runs a project -
  its Production Manager, Project Manager or the shoot's Coordinator, or an administrator, a Super
  Admin or Show All Projects (Read / Write) - sees it at every status, with every tab. Somebody who is
  only on its crew (Production Team, a service's crew) sees it only from **Planned** on: Planned,
  Execution, Hold, Rejected, Completed; and somebody who runs no project at all is offered only
  those tabs (and All, which then lists only those). The server says per row whether the viewer runs
  the project (`viewerManages`). No permission or data changed.
  [productionBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionBoard.mjs),
  [ProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionPage.js),
  [read.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/read.js)
- **A weekly off or holiday worked now earns a comp-off only once the approvers approve it, and
  Comp-Off is raised as a Leave Type.** Raise Request no longer has Comp-off as a Request Type; it is
  **Leave → Leave Type: Comp-Off**, beside Casual Leave and Loss of Pay, showing the approved days
  available to use and how many. A full day logged on a weekly off or holiday now raises a **Comp-Off
  Credit** request by itself, to every Leave Approver - all must approve, one rejection settles it -
  listed with the comp-offs on HRM → Request with the day, login, logout, hours worked, approvers and
  whether its comp-off is Available, Claimed, Used or Expired. Pending or rejected, it is not a
  comp-off: the balance, the picker and the server all refuse it; approved, it is exactly one. Nobody
  can raise, edit, revert, delete or send back a credit. Every other leave, permission and
  regularization works as before, and so does every comp-off already raised (still stored as
  `COMP_OFF`). **Comp-offs earned before the change keep working:** migration
  `20261029110000_comp_off_credit_approval` sets `attendance_settings.comp_off_approval_from` to the
  day it runs, and only days worked from then on need approval; it also adds `attendance_request.credit_key`
  (unique, one credit per employee and day). No new permission: credits are decided by the Leave
  Approvers through the existing request routes.
  [compOffCredits.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/compOffCredits.js),
  [attendanceRequestConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/attendanceRequestConfig.js),
  [attendanceRequests.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/attendanceRequests.js)
- **The client gallery's People and Scene filters are ready sooner.** Face recognition for a gallery
  now asks the face engine for faces only and skips the expression and face-sharpness readings that
  only AI Culling uses - measured on real previews, about 1.56x faster per photo (1.24 s to 0.80 s),
  with exactly the same faces, groupings and cover photos (box, embedding and quality are identical;
  the landmark model still runs because the quality score reads its head pose). AI Culling, AI
  Feature and every other caller still get every signal. Scenes now start being read the moment a
  gallery is published, instead of on the client's first look at People, so "Organizing scenes..."
  is usually already done when they arrive. No setting, data or screen changed.
  [faces/engine.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/faces/engine.js),
  [face_engine.py](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/face-engine/face_engine.py),
  [publication/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/publication/service.js)
- **Table filter boxes use Word Chunk Search: every chunk typed, each found anywhere.** Typing "we ot"
  in a column's filter box keeps only rows holding both "we" and "ot" - inside a word too, in any
  order and ignoring case - so it finds "WED other 366895" and not "WED second" or "WED first"; "we
  se" finds "WED second". The Search inside a column's pick-list narrows its options the same way. A
  single word searches exactly as before, extra spaces are ignored, and date and day columns still
  read what is typed as one phrase, so "12 Oct" means that date. Every table's filter, in the browser
  and on the server, now follows the one rule the dropdowns and sidebar already did,
  [wordChunks.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/wordChunks.mjs), used by
  [DataTable.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/DataTable.js),
  [tableCells.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/tableCells.js) and
  [FilterMultiSelect.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/FilterMultiSelect.js); the tables'
  separate any-word `wordChunkSearch.mjs` is gone.
- **The calendar now shows each person the shoots their permissions reach.** It showed every shoot to
  every signed-in employee. Three readings now: **Projects, Pre Production or Bookings & Converted** -
  the permissions about the studio's work as a whole - see every shoot; **Production alone** sees the
  shoots that person is **named on**, which is their own roster; and somebody holding none of those
  sees no shoots at all, their calendar still carrying the studio's holidays, their attendance and
  their meetings. "Named on" is the Shoot Board's own rule (`boardWhere` - the project's roles, the
  production coordinator, the team and a service's crew, for them and their reports), so the two
  cannot disagree about whose shoot it is. Opening one is unchanged and still answers to the owning
  module's permission.
  [calendar/service.js](../backend/src/modules/schedule/calendar/service.js)
- **Picking projects or branches on the Shoot Board now fits the selection's shoots on one screen, and
  only gives up dates when it has to.** A project's first and last shoot can be six weeks apart, and on a timeline
  that gives every date the same width they could not both be in view - the answer to "show me this
  project" was a scroll through empty days. Now the **dates** give way instead of the shoots, as far
  **by zooming out first, and only when it has to.** Picking a project - or a **branch**, which
  narrows the board the same way and asks the same question of it - scrolls to the first shoot of
  what was picked, and touches the zoom for one reason: its first shoot and its last are
  further apart than the screen. Shoots in the same week change nothing - they are already on screen
  - and shoots a month apart draw the days narrower until both are. **Clearing the filter gives the
  zoom back**: the board remembers the one the reader had before it meddled, so a board that zoomed
  out to show a distant shoot is not left zoomed out over everything once that project is
  deselected, and pressing − or + makes the zoom theirs again. Only where no zoom level is
  enough - a quarter, a long custom range - do the **dates** give way: each shoot keeps its
  own dates around it, grown outwards until the next would not fit, and the empty stretches between
  those islands become narrow dotted marks saying how many days they stand for. Every bar is still a
  bar, in its own row, on its own date, and with no project picked the board is exactly as it was.
  [shootBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/shootBoard.mjs),
  [ShootTimeline.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/shoot-board/ShootTimeline.js)
- **The calendar shows every shoot to everybody.** A shoot appeared on the calendar only for
  somebody holding `PROJECT / Projects`, `Pre Production` or `Production`, and then only for the
  projects they were named on - so a driver, an editor or somebody in accounts could not see that a
  team was out on Saturday, which is the thing an employee planning their week most often needs from
  a calendar. Where the studio is shooting is now a fact every signed-in employee can read, the same
  way the studio's declared holidays already are: a shoot opens its window with the project, the
  Event ID, the place, the timings and who is going.
  **Opening one is still a permission, and nothing is offered that would be refused.** A card inside
  that window opens the shoot's **Production panel** for somebody holding `PROJECT / Production` -
  read-only without Read / Write - or the **Projects board** for somebody holding `PROJECT /
  Projects`. For anybody holding neither, the card is not a button: no error, no message, pressing
  it does nothing, which is the rule the Shoot Board's own cards already follow. Deleted shoots, and
  shoots of deleted projects, stay out as before.
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/schedule/calendar/service.js),
  [MeetingsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/MeetingsPage.js). No migration and no new
  permission - and note that a shoot's details are readable studio-wide now, which is the point of
  the change rather than a side effect of it.
- **A quotation's Shoot List now names a shoot the way the rest of the quotation does.** The table
  under Shoot List - and the cards it becomes on a phone - printed the bare shoot while the card it
  opens, the Add Shoot list and the client's own quotation all read **"Rituals (Bride Varatham)"**:
  one shoot with two names on one screen. All of them go through `shootDisplayName` now. **Booking &
  Converted and the project screens are unchanged**, and need no switch to stay that way: Additional
  Text is the Quotation Generator's own field, kept in the quotation's payload, and a quotation
  becoming a project leaves it behind - the plan hand-off does not carry it and `project_shoot` has
  no column for it - so a project shoot has nothing to show and reads exactly as it did.
  [ProjectShootList.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectShootList.js)
- **Your attendance dashboard now counts by the pay cycle, not the calendar month.** HRM → Employee
  Attendance → Self Dashboard opened on **This month** - the 1st to today - while payroll counts from
  the pay cycle day set in Settings (the 25th unless the studio changed it). The same working days,
  absences, late days and hours over two different windows never agreed with the payslip. It now
  opens on **Pay cycle**, so today's figures cover 25 Sep – 24 Oct and match what payroll is
  counting. The totals strip, the calendar and the Login Summary all read that one range, so none of
  them can disagree with another. **This month is still in the list** for anyone who wants the
  calendar month, along with This week, Last 6 months, This Year and Lifetime, all unchanged. A
  cycle still running is counted **up to today**, never to its closing date - a working day that has
  not happened yet would otherwise read as Absent. The cycle day travels with the attendance
  settings the page already fetches, so changing it in Settings moves the dashboard with payroll.
  [EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js),
  [attendanceTime.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/attendanceTime.mjs). No migration, no new permission.
- **A holiday or a weekly off can now be regularized.** The studio shoots on Sundays and festival
  days, and somebody who worked one and marked nothing had no way to say so: the day read "Weekly
  off", and the Attendance Regularization form refused with "there is no attendance to correct" -
  true of the record and false of the day. Both are their own **Current Status** now, so the day can
  be asked to read as Present, Half day or whatever it actually was, and the form says beside the
  choice to raise it only if the day was really worked and that the approver will see the day was
  off. Neither is offered as a status to change a day **into**: which days are off is the calendar's
  to say (Settings → Holidays, the attendance rules' week-offs), not one request's. A day still
  logged in, and a day attendance is not owed for, are refused exactly as before.
  [attendanceRules.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/attendanceRules.js),
  [attendance/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/controller.js)
- **The Accounts Manager CSV import now files each payment against its project, and reads dates
  the Indian way.** The Client Name column is matched to the project's WhatsApp group name (case and
  spacing ignored), and a new optional **Event ID** column picks the project when two share a group
  name - 23 of the current 637 do. A received payment matching no project or several is refused with
  the Event IDs to choose from, rather than saved against none; the project's branch and client are
  used, so Branch is now needed only for money out against no project. Entry Date was read the
  American way - 05/10/2026 saved as 9 May, 26/10/2026 refused, 5 Oct landing on the 4th - and is now
  read day first. Transaction ID, Received / Paid From Account and Remarks may be left empty in an
  imported row, and so may an expense's Paid To and Handled By (the form still asks for all of them);
  an expense naming no handler stores none, where the lookup would otherwise have matched the first
  employee in the table. And the import no longer refuses every row not paid
  by "Other": Handled By was checked before its name was turned into the employee, so a filled-in
  Handled By read as no handler. [cash-entries/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/accounts/cash-entries/controller.js),
  [importColumns.js](../frontend/src/constants/importColumns.js)
- **Services and Deliverables in Settings → Project can be put in order by dragging their rows.**
  A grip in front of each row moves it up or down. Focus it and use the arrow keys, or on a phone
  use Move up / Move down. The column headers stay as they are, and the order is saved the moment a
  row is dropped. It is the order everything else lists them in: the quotation generator, the
  quotation calculator, Create Project, Extra Quotation and the service and deliverable pickers.
  These used to be alphabetical everywhere.
  - A new service or deliverable joins at the end, and so does one restored after removal.
  - A deliverable's companies and variants keep the order set in its own dialog.
  - While a column is sorted by its header the grip is paused, and its tooltip says to clear the
    sort.
  - If the server refuses the order, the panel says so and shows the order that is saved.
  - Migration `20261026130000_project_definition_order_from_names` numbers both lists by name once,
    a data-only change, so nothing moves on deploy until somebody drags a row.
  - Access is unchanged: the order is written behind `PROJECT / Projects` Read / Write, the same as
    Add, Edit and Remove.

  [ProjectSettingsPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectSettingsPanel.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js)
- **Every form panel's footer buttons now sit together at the bottom right.** They did not: the
  panel's footer row flowed from the left and each screen pushed its primary button over with
  `ml-auto`, so Cancel sat at the far left and Save at the far right - a row that reads as two
  unrelated controls - while a three-button footer read as two groups with a hole in the middle, and
  the dialogs beside them had always grouped theirs. Which side a button landed on depended on which
  panel you had opened. The row is right-aligned once, in `SchemaFormPanel`, and the auto margins are
  gone from all of it: Start / Edit Project, Create Project, the quotation generator, the production
  shoot and project panels, Pre Production's project panel and General, the employee form, cash
  entries, payment requests, assets, master data, settings, record views and the rest. Nothing moves
  on a phone, where the buttons fill the row as before. One test reads every screen that draws a
  panel and fails on an auto margin in a footer, so a new form cannot drift back out of line.
  **The dialogs and the popups follow the same rule**, since they had the same split: the candidate
  popup's Discard, Manage Columns' Reset to Default, Settings → Holidays' Remove, the quotation
  settings dialog, the project and department status dialogs, the shoot run, free-shooters and
  calendar shoot windows. A footer may still carry a line of **text** at the left - "Unsaved
  changes", a warning, a count - and several do; it is buttons that now always sit together.
  **The lead popup's own footer is in line too**: its **Back** sat alone at the far left under a
  `justify-between`, with a hole across the middle of the row, and it was written as a bordered
  `<div>` rather than a `<footer>` - which is how it escaped the first pass. It is a `<footer>` now,
  and the test reads every footer under `src/components` (the `footer` prop, anything named footer,
  and `<footer>` itself) and fails on a button with an auto margin **or** a `justify-between` in one.
  [SchemaFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/schema-form/SchemaFormPanel.js)

- **Overall Status updates from the Pre Production and Production panels, by each stage's own
  permission.** The tab was read-only on both boards, so somebody holding Pre Production at Read &
  Write had to leave the panel and find the shoot again to do what the tab was already showing them.
  A stage the viewer may change now carries **Update** there, exactly as it does on Projects - and it
  is the stage's own permission that decides, not the tab: Pre Production at Read & Write shows Pre
  Production's Update, Production at Read & Write shows Production's (per shoot, where the shoot has a
  production record), and one without the other shows one button and not the other. The editor it
  opens is still handed the permission, so a production plan is editable only for whoever may edit
  *that* shoot's plan. **Project Initiation carries an Update as well**, offered to whoever may
  actually change the project: the server answers both halves of the rule its save answers to - the
  permission that opens the project's form (`PROJECT / Projects`, or `Show All Projects`, at Read &
  Write) and, on a started project, being its Project Manager, a branch administrator, or whoever
  works every project - so a Project Manager, a branch admin and a Super Admin each get it, and
  somebody the save would refuse does not see it. Its editor is the project's own form, which Projects
  owns, so the Update hands the project over to that page with its Event ID in the address and it
  opens there through the same `openPlan` the row's ⋮ uses - which decides again and says so if it
  refuses, because a link is not a permission. The double-click **record** panel on Projects and
  Bookings & Converted stays read-only throughout.
  Post Production and Delivered still carry no Update: the first has no editor wired yet, and the
  second is the end state.
  [PreProductionProjectPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionProjectPanel.js),
  [ProductionProjectPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionProjectPanel.js)

- **The employee's Attendance Dashboard opens on "Your attendance", not "How the range went".** The
  old title named nothing in the card - every card on that screen is about the range - and read as a
  verdict on the range rather than as the reader's own record of it. The note beside it says what both
  figures are as well: **"157h 17m worked of 127h 30m expected"**, where "Worked 157h 17m of 127h 30m"
  left the second to be guessed at, and a first figure larger than the second read as a mistake until
  you knew it was what the range expected. The figures themselves are unchanged.
  [EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js)

- **The Production Manager is named on the project, with the other four seats, instead of on Pre
  Production → General.** Start Project and Edit Project → **Project Setup** now asks for Project
  Manager, Pre Production Coordinator, **Production Manager**, Creative Manager and Post Production
  Coordinator together, so a project is staffed in one place; the picker is gone from Pre
  Production's General panel and from the bar above the shoot cards. Nothing else about the seat
  changed: naming somebody still raises that project's production rows there and then, the pre
  production board still carries the **Production Manager** column and the record panel still lists
  it, and being the Production Manager still grants no editing of the project. What **did** change is
  who may set it: Edit Project's own rule, which is `PROJECT / Projects` (or `PROJECT / Show All
  Projects`) at Read & Write **and**, on a project that has started, being its Project Manager, a
  branch administrator or a holder of Show All Projects at Read & Write. `PROJECT / Pre Production`
  at Read & Write no longer carries it - the pre production route refuses the field outright - so a
  Pre Production Coordinator who used to fill this seat now asks the Project Manager for it. The
  studio may want to grant Projects at Read & Write, or Show All Projects, to whoever was doing it.
  [StartProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/StartProjectFormPanel.js),
  [PreProductionGeneral.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionGeneral.js),
  [projects/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js)

### Added
- **User Management has an HR Offboarding List tab.** It sits after Serving Notice and shows every
  resignation form, newest first, on the page itself: the same list, Table / Board switch, Raise a
  form and row actions as the header's ⋮ → HR Offboarding, which still opens it as a popup. Raise a
  form, Review, View and Edit open over the list and close back to it. Its count is the number of
  forms, shown once the tab has been opened. Its **Status** says where each leaver stands, not only
  that the form was approved. An approved form reads **Serving Notice** while they are still working,
- **The HR Offboarding list (User Management ⋮ → HR Offboarding) says where each leaver stands.** Its
  **Status** is no longer just "Approved" once a form is approved. An approved form reads **Serving Notice** while they are still working,
  **Relieved** (or Absconded / Fired) once they have left, and **Withdrawn** if the offboarding was
  removed afterwards. The other forms keep their own status: Sent, Verified, Submitted, Sent Back,
  Rejected, Cancelled, Expired. The status filter and the Board use the same words. Resignation date
  and Proposed last day now read as dates ("03/11/2026") instead of raw timestamps, and sort as dates.
  The server works the stage out (`offboardingStage`, `stage` on each form); the form's own status
  is unchanged, so its actions are too. Rows can be ticked, with a Select All box in the header, to
  **Export** or **Delete** the forms picked. This is for roles with `ADMIN / Table Select All`, like
  every table, and Delete also needs `HRM / Employee Management` Read / Write. Each row's ⋮ also has
  **Delete**, which asks first. Deleting removes the form and its uploaded letter at any status. It
  never changes the employee: a notice or relieving already recorded from the form stays. New routes
  `DELETE /api/hrm/offboarding-invites/:id` and `/bulk` share one delete (`deleteInviteRecord`).
  (`frontend/src/components/employees/OffboardingInviteDialog.js`,
  `backend/src/modules/hrm/offboarding-invites/controller.js`)
- **Payroll's three deduction screens have a Skipped tab.** Which advances, recoveries and policy
  breaches somebody has moved off a month on the Main Page was answerable only by filtering the
  Skipped Months column by hand, which is not how anybody reads a list. Advance Salary now reads
  All / Pending / Deducted / **Skipped**, and Recovery and Policy Breach All / Active / Completed /
  **Skipped**, each with its count. Skipped means **deferred and still owed**: a skip is kept on the
  row for good, so one moved in November and then taken in December would otherwise sit there for
  ever beside the ones genuinely being pushed month after month - once the money is back the row
  reads under Deducted, or Completed, where it belongs. Until then it keeps its live status, so a
  deferred advance is on both Pending and Skipped: the tabs are questions asked of the same rows,
  not buckets, and their counts are not meant to add up to All. Written once in
  [payrollTabs.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/payrollTabs.mjs) so Skipped means the same thing on all
  three, in place of the status filter each screen had written out for itself.
  [PayrollAdvanceSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollAdvanceSection.js),
  [PayrollRecoverySection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollRecoverySection.js)
- **Accounts Manager has a Pending tab: the payment requests waiting for a decision.** Money the
  studio has been asked to pay, read beside the cash book that records what it has already paid -
  without leaving the screen for the Payment Requests one, which keeps its own Pending tab unchanged.
  The tab appears only for a reader who may see payment requests at all (`ACCOUNTS / Payment Request
  Approval`): it lists that screen's rows, so somebody holding the cash book alone does not get a tab
  that then refuses to load. It sits last, after the scheduled payments.
  **A request is decided from here too**: the row's ⋮ carries View, Approve, Reject, Edit and
  Withdraw, the same five the Payment Requests screen offers, so nobody has to change screens to pay
  what they are looking at. Approving and rejecting need Read / Write on that same permission and
  the right to decide, exactly as they do there; a reader who may only look gets View alone. Status,
  Decided On and Cash Entries are left out of the table, since every row is pending, decided by
  nobody and has written no entry. No new permission, and no backend change: the request list already
  answers `?status=PENDING` behind that guard.
  [PendingRequestsTable.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/PendingRequestsTable.js),
  [AccountsManagerPage.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/AccountsManagerPage.js)
  Those five actions, the approval panel, the rejection's required reason and the withdraw confirm
  now live in one place (`usePaymentRequestActions`) that **both** screens mount, rather than being
  copied into the second one - deciding money is not a thing to keep two copies of, and the copy that
  drifted would be the one nobody tested. The Payment Requests screen keeps its own table, board,
  tabs, Raise Request and detail panel; what moved out of it is only the row's actions and their
  panels, and its board still decides a request by dragging it, through the same two openers.
  [usePaymentRequestActions.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/usePaymentRequestActions.js)
- **Every WhatsApp group add says what happened to it, in the row itself.** Employee → Edit →
  WhatsApp Groups showed a pill per group - Added, Invite link sent, Not added - and a reason only
  sometimes. Each group now carries a line under it in its own colour: **Added** needs no explaining
  and gets none; **Already in group** says nothing was sent; **Invite link sent** says WhatsApp would
  not let them be added and they join by tapping the link; **Not added** says so and keeps its Retry
  beside the words. WhatsApp's own reason is shown where it gave one - which is what tells a privacy
  setting apart from somebody who left the group recently - and the status's own words where it did
  not. A new employee, who has no record to add to yet, is told to save first rather than offered an
  Add that would fail. [EmployeeWhatsAppGroups.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeWhatsAppGroups.js)
- **A shared `InlineAlert` for messages that sit beside what they are about.** The same three lines of
  Tailwind were hand-typed in more than fifty files, each with its own tint, padding and text size, so
  a reader met a slightly different-looking message every time. One component now holds the four tones
  (error, warning, success, info) with their icons, how each announces itself to a screen reader, a
  small size for a line inside a row and a slot for an action such as Retry. It is not FloatingNotice:
  that floats over the screen and is dismissed, this stays while the state it describes is true. Only
  the WhatsApp group rows use it so far; the other fifty are left where they are until they are next
  touched. [InlineAlert.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/InlineAlert.js)
- **The CRM board shows what each column's leads are worth.** On the line under each column's
  heading, beside the period picker, every column shows the total Estimated Value of its leads
  ("Est. ₹23,50,000"). The Converted column shows
  instead the value its leads were last converted at: each lead's newest project, so a lead booked
  twice counts once ("Converted ₹6,59,200"). Both follow the column's period and search. An Estimated
  Value that is not a number, such as "TBD", adds nothing. (`backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/leadQueryService.js`,
  `controller.js`, `frontend/src/components/sales/CrmKanbanBoard.js`, `CRMPage.js`)
- **Payroll can hold a leaver's salary through their notice and pay it all as the full and final
  settlement.** A new switch, Settings → Payroll rules → **Hold salary during notice**, is off by
  default.
  - **Who it applies to.** It only affects resignations recorded while it is on: a Resignation or
    Mutual Separation with a notice to serve is marked `salary_held` from its resignation date.
  - **Which months are held.** Every unpaid month payable on or after the resignation date, up to
    the last working day, including a month already worked.
  - **When they are paid.** All together, with the month whose pay cycle holds the last working day,
    on that month's payday.
  - **The Main Page.** A new **Final Settlement** column marks rows *Held for notice*, *Final
    settlement* or *Settled*. A held month cannot be ticked or marked Paid on its own, and the
    server refuses it with the month that will pay it. Paying the settlement shows and pays the full
    and final total: its own salary plus each held month's, each under its own month's rules. The
    held months are marked Paid with it, in one transaction. Setting the settlement back to Pending
    reopens them. The settlement cannot be removed while it pays held months, and once it is paid a
    month found later is paid normally, so no salary is left stuck as held.
  - **What is never touched.** A month already paid, and everybody else's payroll. Withdrawing the
    notice or rejoining releases the hold at once, because it is worked out on read
    ([noticeHold.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/noticeHold.js)).
  - **Payslips.** A held month's payslip says it is held. The settlement payslip lists "Held salary -
    <month>" lines and pays the total.
  - **The Offboarding Confirmed message.** It now has `{final settlement date}` and `{salary hold}`.
    The shipped wording is updated to use them; wording the studio has changed is left alone.
  - **Database.** Migrations `20261101100000_payroll_notice_hold` (additive only: the switch, the
    mark on the separation, and `payroll_entry.settled_in_entry_id`) and
    `20261101110000_offboarding_approved_settlement_date`. No new permission: it sits under
    `HRM / Payroll Register`, and a branch-limited user cannot change it.
  - **Known limit.** A relieved leaver's login is closed, so they cannot open their settlement
    payslip themselves. HR shares it.
- **User Management has a Pending tab.** A new **Pending** tab after InActive gathers everyone waiting
  on somebody: Employee Submission Pending, HR Onboarding Pending, Incomplete Profiles and Review
  Pending. Its count counts a person once, even when they are pending in two ways.
  - Inside it, each kind is listed down the left with its count, with **All Pending** at the top.
    Clicking one shows those employees in the table beside it, with the usual columns, menus and
    info panel. The last kind chosen is remembered.
  - On a phone the list wraps above the table.
  - The Board offers every tab too: Active, Serving Notice, Employee Submission Pending, HR
    Onboarding Pending, InActive and Pending. Before, it offered only All, Incomplete Profiles and
    Review Pending. A status tab shows that column alone; Incomplete Profiles, Review Pending and
    Pending narrow the cards in every column, and Pending keeps its side list.
  - The existing tabs are unchanged.
  - The list is a new shared component, `components/shared/SideFilterList.js` (a vertical tab list
    with counts; Up and Down move through it), for any tab that holds several views.

  Frontend only, no permission change. Test: `frontend/test/employee-pending-tab.test.mjs`.
- **Every automatic WhatsApp message now chooses Sender - one person, every time, with a fallback
  order you drag - or Rotation - every employee with Allow WhatsApp ticked taking turns in an order
  you drag.** The attendance report, the wishes, Photo Selection Submitted, the shoot crew notice,
  the payment reminder (and with it the money-received message) and Interview Welcome each have the
  choice. In **Sender** mode, where the Sender cannot send, every other Allow-WhatsApp employee is
  tried in the fallback order dragged under them - until now that fallback was name order and could
  not be changed. In **Rotation** each message goes from the next person in its own dragged order,
  one who cannot send passed over for the next. Anybody given Allow WhatsApp later joins the end of
  both orders. Each mode keeps its own setting and its own order, so switching between them loses
  neither. Where nobody can send, Settings - and the WhatsApp Activity Log - say why. A
  message that may already have gone still stops there rather than risk sending it twice. New Lead Welcome is unchanged (it goes from the
  lead's owner), and manual sends still go from whoever presses Send. One shared field,
  [SenderOrderField](../frontend/src/components/settings/SenderOrderField.js), replaces the Priority 1
  dropdown and the fallback list; the rule is [senderPolicy.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/automatic-whatsapp/senderPolicy.js).
  Migration `20261102120000_whatsapp_sender_policy` adds `whatsapp_sender_policy` and
  `whatsapp_sender_policy_member`, carries every sender already chosen over as that message's Sender
  (Sender mode) and as the start of its Rotation order; the shoot crew notice's Priority 2 heads its
  fallback order. It drops the old single-sender columns. **After deploying, check each message's
  fallback order** - it starts in name order, as before, until somebody drags it. No new permission - each list is saved under the guard its
  message's sender setting already had.
- **Edit Sale Details now records every shoot, service and deliverable added, removed or changed after
  booking as an Extra, priced by hand and published onto the client's existing quotation link.** A new
  section, **EXTRA – ADDITIONAL & REMOVED ITEMS**, sits above Shedule Payment
  ([SaleExtrasSection.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SaleExtrasSection.js)). Changes made on any
  screen are picked up, and every shoot, service and deliverable is a line of its own with its own
  amount - a new shoot's services and deliverables too, and what was removed with a shoot; scope edits
  (quantity, duration, size, variant, number of photos) are recorded as Changed. The section is a card
  per shoot that changed, drawn like Service Creation's (blue border, the shoot name, then "Shoot ID |
  date | place"; a new or removed shoot says so), listing only what changed from the quotation:
  **Added** (additions, and changed quantities as "Changed: Quantity 1 → 2") and **Removed** - each
  line with its category, date, amount and remarks. The totals (original, unpublished, published, updated)
  sit at the top, held under the section title while its cards scroll, and scroll away with the section.
  Every line - published or not - has an **Amount** box (required; before GST, no discount; ₹0
  allowed) and a **Remarks** box. There is no Save Changes: **Publish Updated Quotation** is open
  whenever something changed, refuses while any amount is empty, and sends what is in the boxes in one
  all-or-nothing transaction; leaving with typed amounts asks first. While Publish is open, Edit Sale
  Details' **Update Project** is held ("Publish the Extra changes first."), and Enter in the form does not
  save the sale either. Changing a published amount adds a
  correction for the difference in that publish - the published line itself never changes. Publish
  reviews the added, removed and changed items and corrected amounts with their remarks, the net and
  the updated total, and freezes a revision - the client's same link and PDF then show, after
  the quotation's own pricing card (unchanged), an **Extra** section listing **Added Items** and
  **Removed Items** (item, category, related shoot, date; a changed quantity reads "Quantity 1 → 2"
  under Added) with no prices, then an **Updated Total Amount** card with only the total, the GST
  line where General Settings shows it, and "Updated <date>" - no revision number, no net. The Event
  cards stay exactly as quoted, and drafts never show. Published extras count once toward the outstanding
  balance, receipts and Total Signed; the payment schedule, receipts and the original quotation are never
  changed, and nothing is sent to the client. Projects without a finalized quotation are not tracked;
  Extra Quotations (EXT-) are unchanged.
  - **Migration `20261101160000_sale_extras`** (run with `prisma migrate deploy`): adds `sale_baseline` to
    the shoot, service and deliverable tables - filled for every existing row, so every project's plan as
    it stands today is its baseline and no old project shows extras - and the `project_sale_extra` and
    `project_sale_extra_revision` tables. Nothing else is written; rehearsed on a copy of the database.
  - **Migration `20261101180000_sale_extras_deleted_rows`** (runs right after the first): rows that were
    already deleted before Sale Extras was installed get no baseline, so an old deletion never shows as a
    Removed extra; the draft lines it had caused are cancelled.
  - **Shedule Payment** shows **Net Extra** (all published extras together) and **Updated Total Amount**
    (Signed Quotation + Net Extra) under the Signed Quotation once anything is published; its payment rows,
    dates, percentages and receipts are not changed. The section lists no revisions; each published row
    keeps its revision number in its status.
  - **Corrections:** a published line is final; editing its amount publishes a correction line for
    the difference (migration `20261101170000_sale_extra_corrections`, one nullable column, no row
    written).
  - **No new permission:** pricing and publishing use the guards that save Edit Sale Details. A quotation
    carrying published extras cannot be unfinalized or swapped on its project.
  - Not deployed.
- **A quotation version can be finalized, and unfinalized - one finalized version per quotation.**
  Every version now has one of two statuses, each version on its own: **Finalized** or
  **Unfinalized** (every version starts unfinalized). The Quotation Generator's footer ends with a
  green **Finalize Quotation** after Save as new version; confirmed first, it finalizes the version
  that is open - newest or older - without raising a version. A finalized version is kept exactly as
  it is, its client link never expires, and it is read-only: Save as new version is shown disabled
  ("This version is finalized. Unfinalize it before editing it or creating a new version from it."),
  it cannot be deleted, and the server refuses all of that too. **At most one version of a quotation
  is finalized**: finalizing another is refused with "Another quotation version is already
  finalized. Please unfinalize that version before finalizing this one." (the generator shows
  Finalize disabled, naming that version), and nothing ever unfinalizes a version by itself.
  **Unfinalize** (confirmed) changes only that version: kept exactly as it was, editable again, its
  link on a five-day clock. Any unfinalized version can be edited and saved as the next version,
  which starts unfinalized; no other version's status moves. Finalize is also refused while there
  are unsaved changes on screen, on a saved draft, and on a version whose link has lapsed
  (re-enable it first). Finalize and Save as New Version lock the quotation's versions while they
  write, so two finalizes at once let one through, the same document saved twice raises one
  version, and a failed save writes nothing; MySQL holds the one-finalized rule too (a unique
  `finalized_chain_key` it computes itself). The version history and the version picker show each
  version's status, with when it was finalized and by whom. Quotation links are unchanged: their
  random token and rate limit, and an unfinalized lapsed link stays lapsed. Same
  `SALES / Quotation Management` permission as Edit - no new permission. **Production needs two
  migrations** (`prisma migrate deploy`): `20261030140000_sales_quotation_finalization` (four
  nullable columns on `sales_quotation`) and `20261031100000_sales_quotation_one_finalized_version`
  (a generated column and its unique index; no stored data is rewritten). Then `npm run
  prisma:generate` and a backend restart.
  [QuotationGeneratorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationGeneratorPanel.js),
  [QuotationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationPage.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js),
  [sales-quotation-finalize.test.js](../backend/test/sales-quotation-finalize.test.js)
- **A logout past 18 hours is taken, and sends itself for approval.** A login stops being one after
  18 hours, and the logout was refused outright: the day read **Absent** and the hours worked past
  them were nobody's - the person was told to go and raise a regularization about their own day. The
  **logout is now taken**, exactly as any other - the selfie, the position and the CHECK_OUT capture -
  and it sends the extra time for approval by itself.

  The Logout box asks why before it goes (required: the approver reads it before deciding) and says
  what will happen - the day is logged out, the extra time goes to **their Permission Approver by
  name**, the day **stays Absent until it is approved** and **reads Present** once it is. **Today's** day has the same thing on the
  attendance banner as **Log out late**, which writes the same logout with no selfie it never took.
  A day that has already rolled over is not one anybody is still working, so it keeps the attendance
  regularization alone, as it always had; the banner now also names today as "Today's attendance"
  rather than by its date.

  So the day reads as what it was - logged in at 00:30, logged out at 20:31 - rather than going on
  saying nobody logged out. Because a written logout would otherwise finish the day as Present on its
  own, the day is pinned to **Absent** by a status override until the request is answered; approving
  it replaces that override with **Present**, the same write an approved regularization makes.

  It is its own kind of request - **Extra Time**, not a regularization - carrying the clock time the
  logout was pressed and the employee's own words. Somebody with no Permission Approver is still
  logged out and told to ask HR, rather than the logout failing over a request nobody could answer.
  A day already asked about cannot be sent twice, and the row is locked so two taps raise one request.
  Nobody can raise, edit or revert one by hand - only the logout creates it. Raising a regularization
  stays beside it, for a day whose right answer is not "I worked on". No new permission.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/controller.js),
  [ExtraTimeDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/ExtraTimeDialog.js)
- **A vendor's phone number on the shoot's plan.** A service worked by a vendor now shows who to ask
  for and their number under the person and status fields, and the number **dials** - the coordinator
  rings a vendor more often than they do anything else on this form, and the number was only on the
  vendor's own record in Asset Management. The mobile is shown, falling back to the WhatsApp number;
  nothing is drawn for an employee, for a vendor with no number recorded, or for one since retired.
  It rides on the plan's own vendor list, so the form asks the server for nothing extra, and it shows
  wherever the plan is read, including read-only. No new permission - whoever may read the plan sees it.
  [ProductionServiceCrew.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionServiceCrew.js),
  [read.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/read.js)
- **A shoot's crew is told about it on WhatsApp, two days before.** Settings → Project Management →
  **Shoot crew notice**: everybody given a service on a shoot is sent what the shoot is, its date and
  day, when it runs, where it is and its district - every place of a multi-location shoot - and the
  service they are on. Then:
  - **a plan changed after that tells only the people whose own part changed** - a seat handed to
    somebody else tells those two and nobody else, and the rest of the crew hear nothing;
  - **somebody taken off the shoot is told that instead**, so they do not travel for it;
  - **the shoot itself moving** - its day, its times, its venue - is everybody's change, so everybody
    on it is told again;
  - **nothing goes until the plan has been still for thirty minutes**, so a plan worked in passes
    sends one message rather than one a keystroke. That same rule sends a plan settled late - inside
    the two days, or on the day - half an hour after it is planned.

  Only a settled plan is sent: submitted, and not on Hold, Rejected or waiting on the client. A
  vendor's seat and a service nobody is on carry nobody to tell, and a person holding two services on
  one shoot gets one message naming both. Two senders are chosen in Settings - **Priority 1 and
  Priority 2** - and behind them **every other employee with Allow WhatsApp ticked**, in name order,
  the same fallback the daily attendance report uses; the first who can send does, each from their own
  WhatsApp, and where nobody can, nothing goes out and the panel says why. At most five a sweep, a few seconds apart, and every
  message is in the WhatsApp Activity Log. The two wordings are message templates (**Shoot Crew
  Notice** and **Shoot Crew Removed**) with twelve placeholders. **Off by default.**

  Each message is claimed before it is sent, so two API processes cannot both tell somebody, and the
  log's key is the **change** rather than where it landed - told A, then B, then A again is a third
  message, not one the log mistakes for the first. Every attempt is paced and counted, not only the
  ones that go, so a run of unreachable numbers is not a burst from the studio's number.

  **New permission** `SETTINGS / Shoot Crew Notice`, granted to **Super Admin only**; every other role
  starts at DISABLED, and the studio grants it in Role Management - the studio might want it for
  whoever runs production scheduling. **Migrations** `20261031160000_shoot_crew_notice` adds
  `shoot_crew_notice_settings` and `project_shoot_crew_notice`, the permission and the two wordings;
  `20261031170000_shoot_date_index` indexes `project_shoot.date_created`, which the sweep reads every
  minute. `SHOOT_CREW_NOTICE_AUTOSEND=false` turns the sweep off.
  [due.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/shoot-crew-notice/due.js),
  [sender.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/shoot-crew-notice/sender.js),
  [ShootCrewNoticePanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/ShootCrewNoticePanel.js)
- **A scheduled payment can follow a shoot when its date is not known.** Under Schedule Payment, each
  row's Date has a "Date not known?" link: answer No and pick the shoot (the main event unless
  another is chosen) and Before, On or After it, with how many days. The due date is worked out
  from the shoot and moves whenever the shoot's date changes - from Create / Edit Project, Pre
  Production, the client's own form or the sheet import. Until the shoot has a date the payment
  reads "Waiting for shoot date" in Accounts and on the Payments tab, and is neither Due nor
  reminded; a payment whose shoot is removed waits for a shoot to be picked again. A payment Accounts
  has worked keeps its date. Run `prisma migrate deploy` (`20261031140000_payment_due_on_shoot`).
  [shootLinkedDueDates.js](../backend/src/services/shootLinkedDueDates.js),
  [PaymentDueDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PaymentDueDialog.js)
- **Payment reminders and the money-received message now go to the project's WhatsApp group on
  their own.** Two days before a scheduled payment is due, a reminder is posted into the project's
  group, and the Cash Received message (with the invoice link) is posted the moment money received
  is recorded - from Add Entry, or a scheduled payment's Clear or Part payment - both from the one person chosen in the new Settings → Project Management → Payment
  reminder, at the time set there (10:00 am unless set). Only payments still to be received are
  reminded, once per due date; nobody else is tried when the sender cannot send, and the reason shows
  in that section and in WhatsApp Activity Log. The receipt popup no longer opens on save (Share
  invoice still opens it). The wording is Settings → Message Templates → Payment Reminder. New
  permission `SETTINGS / Payment Reminder`, granted to SUPER_ADMIN only by migration
  `20261031120000_payment_due_reminder` - the studio may want to grant it to the Accounts or Project
  Manager roles in Role Management. Run `prisma migrate deploy`; no seed. `PAYMENT_REMINDER_AUTOSEND=false`
  turns the reminder off on a server. Money-received messages go one at a time, a few seconds apart,
  at most 30 a day, and only for entries typed in (not a PDF or CSV import).

  [receivedMessage.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/payment-reminder/receivedMessage.js),

- **Quick filters on Production → Schedule, and a people filter that includes the Assist.** A box
  under each column, as the app's tables have: Event ID, Event, Shoot ID and Shoot pick from the values
  the shoots hold, Date takes a typed or picked day (or "2026-11" for the month), and the Production plan
  column's one box picks people - a shoot is kept where any of them works one of its services **or is on
  its Assist**, so it lists every project somebody is on. On a phone the boxes are a labelled strip above
  the cards. Clear empties them; a hidden column's box filters nothing. Frontend only, reusing
  `FilterMultiSelect` and `FilterDateInput`.

- **Guests keep up to 10 selfies, in the AI Feature and in Photo Selling.** A "Your Selfies" section on
  the guest page (My Photos; the store's results and waiting screens) shows them as small private
  thumbnails with a remove button, the count ("3/10 selfies") and Add Selfie - disabled at ten with
  "Remove one to add another". Every selfie is searched with and matched against photos uploaded
  later; a photo shows once whichever selfie matched it. Removing one deletes its face data and files
  and drops only the photos no other selfie of the guest still matches. The limit is the server's (one
  conditional update; an eleventh, even sent at once, is refused) and every list, picture and removal
  is the guest's own session's. WhatsApp photo-match messages are unchanged: still once per photo,
  only for later uploads, only to guests who asked.
  - **AI Feature:** no database change - selfies already had a row each; a new selfie is now added
    beside the others instead of replacing them, and the limit counts active selfies (a count from
    before is brought down to what is kept). New guest routes `GET :code/selfies`,
    `GET :code/selfies/:id/thumbnail`, `DELETE :code/selfies/:id`. A face in a new upload now counts
    each guest's best selfie once, so one guest's selfies never crowd another out of the top three.
  - **Photo Selling:** migration `20261030130000_photo_selling_guest_selfies` (owner-approved): table
    `photo_sale_guest_selfie` and `photo_sale_guest.selfie_count`; a consenting guest's one kept face is
    copied in as their first selfie. Every registered guest's selfies are now kept (face and a private
    thumbnail, never the selfie) until they remove them - the store says so. Routes
    `GET :code/guest/selfies`, `GET :code/guest/selfies/:id/thumbnail`, `DELETE :code/guest/selfies/:id`.
    Run `prisma migrate deploy`.
  [GuestSelfies.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/GuestSelfies.js),
  [guests/service.js](../backend/src/modules/photo-selling/guests/service.js),
  [matching.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/matches/matching.js)
- **Guests can leave their WhatsApp number and be told when new photos of them are found - no login
  code - in the AI Feature and in Photo Selling.** Both are off until the server's own switch and the
  event's or gallery's switch are on; no message is sent from this change alone.
  - **AI Feature:** the join card's "Send me a WhatsApp when my photos are found" box, or Turn on in
    My Photos, is now the consent by itself - the SMS code step is gone from this path (a guest with
    photos who rejoins on another device still gets the login code, so nobody else can open them).
    The message goes to the number the guest joined with; staff changing it withdraws the consent. It
    now uses the approved `photos_ready` template (body: name, new photos, event; button: `e/<code>`).
    With no match yet, a guest who asked sees "Your photos haven't been found yet. We'll notify you on
    WhatsApp when your photos are available."
  - **Photo Selling:** new **Guest selfie search & WhatsApp notifications** settings on the studio
    defaults and each gallery (web and desktop): **Enable guest selfie search** (default on - the
    store as before) and **Enable WhatsApp photo-match notifications** (default off), with what the
    server has in place and whether Meta approved the template. With it on, a guest leaves their name
    and WhatsApp number before the selfie, with an unticked box to be told; only with that tick is
    their selfie's face kept, so photos uploaded later are matched to them as they finish indexing and
    one message per guest goes once the batch settles (template `photos_ready`, button `s/<code>`).
    Their later matches appear when they come back and can be bought as before; "Stop WhatsApp
    messages" clears the kept face at once. Every Photo Selling guest now gives their name and
    WhatsApp number on the store's first screen - with the PIN on the same screen where the gallery
    has one, and no code - as on the AI Feature's join card; the WhatsApp tick shows only where the
    gallery's messages are on and set up. Links, QR codes, PINs and payments are unchanged. Each match is reported once; a send Meta may have taken is
    never repeated.
  - **Migration** `20261030120000_photo_selling_guest_notifications` (owner-approved): three new
    empty tables (`photo_sale_guest`, `photo_sale_guest_match`, `photo_sale_notification`) and two
    switches on `photo_sale_gallery` and `photo_sale_setting` defaulting to today's behaviour. Run
    `prisma migrate deploy`. New server settings (see `backend/.env.example`):
    `PHOTO_SELLING_WHATSAPP_ENABLED`, `PHOTO_SELLING_WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_NAME` / `_LANGUAGE`,
    `PHOTO_SELLING_WHATSAPP_DIAL_CODES`, `PHOTO_SELLING_NOTIFY_QUIET_MS`, and the read-only
    `META_WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_ACCOUNT_ID`. The Meta template's button URL must be fixed and approved
    before any message can be sent.
  [guests/service.js](../backend/src/modules/photo-selling/guests/service.js),
  [notifications/service.js](../backend/src/modules/photo-selling/notifications/service.js),

- **Photo Selling: the studio's own photo galleries, sold to guests, on the web and the desktop app.**
  Visual Curation now lists **Photo Selling** as an entry of its own, beside **AI Feature** (the event
  workflow, unchanged), and looks and works like it: a gallery's header **Share** button opens the
  same **Share with guests** dialog an AI Feature event has (the gallery's own link, PIN, QR, short
  code, closing date and message) with its **QR Template** (the same ten poster designs, live preview
  and A1 PDF / PNG downloads of the gallery's own link), each gallery card has the AI Feature's ⋮ (Open,
  Edit, Duplicate - a new draft with the same sales set-up, without photos, orders or the original
  event's client, date and venue - Archive / Restore,
  Delete), and its cards, status pills and dashboard range bar are the AI
  Feature's. A gallery is made with nothing but a name and set up in three steps - Details,
  Photos (uploaded straight into the gallery, with progress, pause and retry), Prices (one price per
  photo, per-photo prices, tax, packages such as "any 3 photos for ₹300") - then published from the header once nothing blocks it,
  saving as it goes, so a draft can be finished later. No AI Feature event is needed or created.
  **What is sold is each photo's original.** It is uploaded byte for byte from the web or the
  desktop app (checked by its content and its SHA-256), stored in a **private** R2 bucket under
  `photo-selling/gallery-<id>/originals/`, and never given a link: a buyer downloads it only after
  the server has verified their payment with Cashfree, through a ten-minute ticket that works once,
  streamed by the server. Each bought photo can be downloaded 20 times within 365 days of payment
  (`PHOTO_SELLING_DOWNLOAD_LIMIT` / `_DAYS`). Web-size previews made on the uploader's computer go to
  the public bucket for showing, watermarked; a re-sent photo is recognised and never stored twice.
  Guests open `/s/<code>`, enter the PIN if set, and find their photos **by a selfie only**: the
  gallery is never shown whole and there is no route that lists it; only photos with a confident
  face match (the AI Feature's own InsightFace engine and high-confidence threshold) are shown, priced
  or sold, and opening the store is not a match - a device with no matching search can buy nothing.
  No match says "No matching photos found" with tips, never falling back to other photos (consent
  first; the selfie and its face data are never stored; a search keeps only which photos matched, for
  24 hours). A gallery cannot be published until its photos' faces are found **and the face engine
  is actually running**: readiness reads the AI Feature engine's own health (Not set up / Model
  missing / Offline / Starting / Ready, with the reason), not its settings. Matching is the AI
  Feature's own engine, model, similarity and 0.62 threshold, on wherever that engine is
  (`AI_FACE_ENGINE_ENABLED`) - Photo Selling has no face setting of its own, no AWS Rekognition and no
  licence switch (the studio governs the shared `buffalo_l` weights for both modules alike).
  Payments are ready only once **Cashfree accepts the server's keys** (checked against Cashfree, not
  from their presence: "Keys refused" says which environment's keys are wanted), and the worker settles
  payments still open after two minutes every ten, so a buyer who closed the tab is unlocked without
  a webhook. Photo Selling has its **own Settings** (Galleries → ⋮ beside New Gallery → Settings, a
  dialog over the page - not a section of its own; the old Settings address opens it there; table
  `photo_sale_setting`): new-gallery defaults (price, tax, PIN, match strictness,
  watermark, colour), the buyers' download policy and the QR poster defaults - new galleries copy
  them, and nothing reads the AI Feature's settings in their place. Each gallery has a **QR poster**
  step: the shared poster designs with Photo Selling's own words, saved per gallery, encoding the
  gallery's own store link. Creating a gallery asks for the client's name and phone. **Deleting a
  draft removes its files from R2 durably**: every file it owned is recorded in the same transaction
  that deletes it (`photo_sale_storage_cleanup`) and retried by the worker until gone, only inside
  that gallery's own folder. Guests add photos to a cart the server prices, pay through Cashfree and download the
  originals from their order page. An order is paid only when the server has asked Cashfree;
  webhooks are signature-checked and applied once; retries never double-charge; a mismatched amount
  unlocks nothing. New permission `IMAGE_SELECTION / Photo Selling`, granted to SUPER_ADMIN only by
  migration `20261023130000_photo_selling` (new `photo_sale_*` tables, nothing existing altered);
  `20261026120000_photo_selling_originals` adds the originals' keys, one price per photo and
  single-use download records to those same tables, and `20261027120000_photo_selling_settings_qr_cleanup`
  the settings and cleanup tables and the gallery's client, access and QR columns. The studio may want to grant the permission in
  Role Management to the roles that run event sales or accounts, but not to a branch-scoped role
  yet, since galleries and orders are studio-wide. Originals are stored in the studio's existing
  R2 bucket in Photo Selling's own folder (`photo-selling/gallery-<id>/originals/<random id>/`) - no
  new bucket - protected by an unguessable key that never leaves the server; setting
  `R2_PRIVATE_BUCKET_NAME` (or `PHOTO_SELLING_ORIGINALS_BUCKET`) to a bucket with public access off
  moves them there instead. Before deploying: check in the Cloudflare dashboard that no lifecycle
  (expiry) rule covers `photo-selling/`; allow `PHOTO_SELLING_MAX_ORIGINAL_MB` (default 200) in
  Nginx's `client_max_body_size` for the upload route; set `CASHFREE_CLIENT_ID` /
  `CASHFREE_CLIENT_SECRET` (sandbox by default; production also needs
  `PHOTO_SELLING_PRODUCTION_PAYMENTS=true`) and `PHOTO_SELLING_NOTIFY_URL`, and add the webhook
  `/api/public/photo-selling/webhooks/cashfree` in the Cashfree dashboard. Selfie search needs only
  the AI Feature's face engine on (`AI_FACE_ENGINE_ENABLED=true`).
  [PHOTO-SELLING.md](project-state/PHOTO-SELLING.md),
  [photo-selling/](../backend/src/modules/photo-selling/),
  [components/photo-selling/](../frontend/src/components/photo-selling/)

- **Settings has a search at the top of its sidebar, as Role Management does.** "Search settings..."
  finds a screen by its name, the group it sits in (User Settings → WhatsApp), its help text, or a
  setting on it ("messages a day", "instalments") - every word typed, in any order, ignoring case and
  spaces, the same word search Role Management uses. Each result shows where it sits; opening one
  goes there like a sidebar click (an unsaved edit still asks first), opens the group holding it, and
  points out the setting it named for a moment. Clearing the search brings the sidebar back exactly
  as it was left; nothing matching says "No settings found". Only the screens the reader may open are
  searched, nothing is asked of the server while typing, and no setting, API or permission changed.
  The rail's search is an optional prop of the shared `SchemaFormSidebar` - every other form is as it
  was.

- **A project's Shoot List can be dragged into the order you want.** On Bookings & Converted (Edit),
  Create Project, Edit Project and Start Project, each shoot row has a grip to drag it up or down,
  and on a phone its ⋮ has Move up / Move down - the same as the Quotation Generator's shoots. The
  order is saved for the project at once and kept the next time it is opened; a project created
  after dragging keeps that order. Only the list's order changes: no date, Shoot ID, service or
  deliverable is touched, and Pre Production, Production, the calendar and Image Selection still list
  shoots by date. A list nobody has dragged stays in date order (undated last, as the server lists
  it), and a shoot added or re-dated later follows the arranged ones - the Shoot List shows the date
  order with the dragged positions on top (`shootListOrder`). Shoots brought in from a quotation stay
  as quoted, without the grip. Saving the
  order uses the same permissions as adding or editing a shoot (`PUT /api/sales/projects/:id/shoots/order`).
  **Migration** `20261030100000_project_shoot_sort_order` adds the nullable `project_shoot.sort_order`;

- **A payment's invoice link, and its receipt message shared from three places.** Every payment
  received now has a client **invoice link** (`/i/<token>`) that opens its invoice with no sign-in -
  the invoice number, date, amount and who it was from, and **View invoice** for the PDF. The receipt
  message (Settings → Message Templates → Cash Received) carries it through a new `{invoice link}`
  placeholder, or as a line of its own at the end where the wording leaves it out, so no template has
  to change. The message is offered **right after a payment is recorded** (Accounts Manager, and now a

  ⋮ and a share icon on the Payments tab. The dialog has Copy, and **Send to "<group>"** where the
  sender's WhatsApp is linked: one message, into the project's own WhatsApp group (found as CRD Link
  Ready finds it), sent because a person pressed it, and logged in the WhatsApp Activity Log as
  *Payment receipt and invoice*. Sharing takes `ACCOUNTS / Cash Management` Read / Write; reading and
  downloading the invoice stay at Read. The link is made the first time the receipt is shared and kept,
  96 random bits, behind a rate limit that counts misses; deleting the entry takes the invoice down.
  **Migration** `20261029170000_cash_entry_invoice_token` adds `cash_entry.invoice_token` (NULL until
  shared). No new permission.

- **A project's Payments tab lists its dues, and a payment is recorded from there.** The Payments tab

  still to bring money in under **Still to Receive** - each part with its due date, what is left of it
  and its status (Overdue, Due, On Hold, and a part not near its date yet) - below the Project Summary.
  A part received in full is left out: it is already on the same tab under Cash Received, as the money
  that actually arrived. **Record payment** on a due opens Accounts' own scheduled

  Read, as the tab already does; Record payment is offered only with its Read / Write. The scheduled
  payments list takes `?projectId=` for this, still inside the caller's reach. No new permission.

- **Interview Welcome has an office-time and an after-hours message, as New Lead Welcome does.**
  Settings → Templates → Interview Welcome now has **Office time** and **After hours** tabs above the
  wording. A candidate a linked interview sheet brings in inside the attendance shift on a working day
  is sent the office-time message (Interview Welcome itself); one arriving at any other time - a weekly
  off or a holiday, the studio's or the candidate's branch's, included - is sent the after-hours message.

- **Deleting a project now moves it to a new Resource Management → Recycling Bin, where it can be
  restored or deleted permanently.** The ⋮ menu's Delete and ticked rows → Delete on Projects and
  Bookings & Converted no longer erase anything - not even Image Selection photos (the single Delete
  used to purge them, and the tick-box delete used to erase the whole project for good). The bin
  lists every deleted project (Event ID, WhatsApp group name, vertical, client main number, deleted
  by, deleted on). **Restore** brings back exactly what the delete took - the project, its galleries,
  its client's app login (only if the delete switched it off) and its client storage records (only
  those removed with the project) - and refuses with a clear message if a live project now holds its
  Event ID. A client login an admin had switched off stays off. **Delete permanently** must name the
  project's Event ID (`confirmEventId`), claims the project first so a Restore or a double-click
  meanwhile is refused, purges its photos and erases the project as the old hard delete did; an
  Album Proofing gallery is unlinked from the project, never purged. A failed photo purge leaves the
  project in the bin to try again. Nothing empties the bin automatically. New permission
  **`ASSET / Recycling Bin`** (`RECYCLING_BIN_MANAGE`; Read to see the bin, Read / Write to restore
  and delete permanently) - its holder may restore or permanently delete **any** binned project in
  their branch reach, whether or not they could have deleted it. Granted to Super Admin only by
  migration `20261029170000_project_recycling_bin` (also `sales_project.deleted_by_user_id`);
  `20261029180000_project_recycling_bin_claims` adds `sales_project.purging_at` and
  `user.deactivated_with_project_at`. The studio may want to grant it in Role Management to Branch
  Admin or whoever it trusts to erase bookings for good. A project deleted before
  this change shows with no "Deleted by" and restores without its client login; its photos were
  already purged. **A project in the bin shows nowhere else**: its cash entries (still counted as
  "already recorded" by the bank statement import, but not listed or named), payment requests with a
  line on it, extra quotations, feedback tasks, client chats, album proofs, client pre production form
  and shoots in every picker are hidden until it is restored (`liveProjectWhere` in
  `services/projectScope.js`). Its CRM lead **reads "Project deleted"** - in the Status column, the
  board's last column, the status filter and counts, and out of the Converted and Rejected tabs -
  while every project of the enquiry is in the bin; the stored status is untouched and comes back on
  Restore, and nobody can choose it as a status. Deleting that lead is still refused, saying its
  project is in the Recycling Bin. Clicking a row in the bin opens a read-only view of the project
  (`GET /api/recycling-bin/projects/:id`). Bell notices about a binned project's tasks or chats stay in
  the bell and open onto "not found"; the WhatsApp activity log keeps its lines, being a log of what
  was sent. Tables gain a column `meta.help` ⓘ.
