  project Payments, Overall Status and Activity tabs, the CRM lead Info tab and Meetings panels).
  `test/detail-help.test.mjs` fails on a details field added without help. Settings shows no explanatory
  paragraphs any more: a page's, card's, dialog's or field's explanation is its ⓘ (`SchemaFormSection`,
  `DashboardCard noteAsTip`, `Dialog`/`SchemaFormPanel descriptionAsTip`); errors, warnings, empty
  states and live values stay on screen. On any Board
  view a card can now be carried to any column. Where the move is a real action it runs as before -
  and four boards gained one: **Bookings & Converted** opens Update status with the column chosen
  (Projects or Show All Projects at Read / Write, the same `/projects/bulk-status` write), **User
  Management** moves a login's home branch after a confirmation (User Management at Read / Write,
  the existing `PATCH /admin/users/:id`), the **WhatsApp Activity Log** opens a Failed message's
  detail for Resend when it is dropped on Queued, and **Project Settings** opens a service's or
  deliverable's Edit with Charged / Complimentary or Image / Video already chosen. Anywhere else the
  card goes back with a short note saying why and where it is changed - a log, a report, payroll's
  own statuses - instead of snapping back in silence. Every Settings screen now carries a helper line
  under its title ([settingsHelp.js](../frontend/src/constants/settingsHelp.js)) and a grey helper
  note on each of its fields - what to enter and what it changes - kept out of the way: a small ⓘ
  beside the label opens it as a tooltip on hover, keyboard focus or a tap
  ([HelpTip.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/HelpTip.js), drawn by every shared input that takes
  `helperText`), so a page full of fields stays one label and one box each; the message
  templates no longer all say "The wording sent to the client", which was wrong for the employee,
  attendance and production messages. No new permission and no backend change.
  [KanbanBoard.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/KanbanBoard.js),
  [SchemaFormSection.js](../frontend/src/components/schema-form/SchemaFormSection.js)
- **New interview candidates from a Google Sheet can be messaged on WhatsApp automatically, from
  one HR number.** Settings → Templates → **Interview Welcome** has the wording - seeded with the
  studio's screening questions (position, software, joining date, expected and least expected salary,
  experience, current company and salary, where from, reason for leaving, native place) - and above
  it a switch, **off by default**, and **Send from**: one HR person, chosen from the active employees
  with Allow WhatsApp ticked. When on, each candidate a linked interview sheet brings into the
  Interview register gets the message from that person's WhatsApp, so the replies land in their chat.
  Add Application, the public form and CSV import never send it. As New Lead Welcome: at most 20 per
  sync and 30 an hour from the sender (the rest logged as Failed, to message by hand), retried three
  times within two hours when the sender's WhatsApp is not linked, each one a `INTERVIEW_WELCOME` row
  in the WhatsApp Activity Log where it can be resent. The wording can use {candidate name}, {sender
  name}, {greeting}, {date}, {day} and {time} the candidate came in (studio clock), and their
  {position}, {department}, {branch}, {city} and {candidate id}. Migration `20261029150000_interview_welcome_message` adds
  `hrm_settings.interview_welcome_enabled` (default off), `interview_welcome_sender_user_id` (a key
  to `user`) and `interview_welcome_last_error`, and the template row (`WHERE NOT EXISTS`). The switch
  and the sender use the existing `SETTINGS / Automatic WhatsApp Message` (Read to see, Read / Write to
  change) and the wording `SETTINGS / Message Template`, so no permission is new.
  `INTERVIEW_WELCOME_AUTOSEND=false` stops the sender entirely.
  [interviewWelcome.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/automatic-whatsapp/interviewWelcome.js),
  [sheetSyncService.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/interview/sheetSyncService.js),
  [InterviewWelcomePanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/InterviewWelcomePanel.js)
- **New Lead Welcome is worded per vertical, with an office-time and an after-hours message.**
  Settings → Templates → **New Lead Welcome by Vertical**: choose a vertical, then **Office time** or
  **After hours**, and write that message. It replaces the single New Lead Welcome template, which is
  no longer in Templates. General and Team 33 are not offered. The wording can say {greeting} (Good
  morning / afternoon / evening), {date}, {day} and {time} the lead came in, on the studio's clock,
  and the lead's {vertical}, {branch} and {enquiry id}, beside {client name} and {sender name}. When a
  linked Google Sheet brings in a new lead, it is sent its vertical's office-time message if it
  arrives inside the attendance shift (Attendance Rules' start and end) on a working day, and its
  after-hours message otherwise - a weekly off or a studio-wide holiday is after hours all day. A
  lead with no wording for that moment - General, Team 33, no vertical, a vertical nobody has worded,
  or a vertical's wording taken away before it went - is **not messaged**: it shows as Failed in the
  WhatsApp Activity Log, saying why, to message by hand (there is no built-in fallback wording any
  more). The vertical picker and the two tabs say which are not written yet, and the screen shows the
  shift hours office time means. A holiday of the lead's own branch counts too. The choice is made when the lead arrives and kept on its row in the
  WhatsApp Activity Log, so a retry sends the same wording. Everything else about the automatic
  welcome - the switch, the sender, the limits - is unchanged. The messages are ordinary templates
  keyed by the vertical's id (`CRM_LEAD_WELCOME_V<id>_OFFICE` / `_AFTER_HOURS`). Migration
  `20261029140000_lead_welcome_vertical_templates` adds a formal office-time and after-hours wording
  for each of Dum Dum (weddings), Qua Qua (children's shoots) and Corp (corporate work), each asking
  that vertical's own details and quoting the enquiry's date, time and reference (found by vertical
  code; a wording already written is left alone);
  the verticals list for the editor is `GET /api/settings/message-templates/lead-welcome/verticals`,
  behind the existing `SETTINGS / Message Template` Read. No new permission.
  [newLeadWelcome.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/automatic-whatsapp/newLeadWelcome.js),
  [LeadWelcomeVerticalTemplates.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/LeadWelcomeVerticalTemplates.js)
- **Production has a Schedule view beside its Table - the production schedule sheet in the app, its people assigned in place.**
  Switched by the dropdown beside the Production title (Table / Schedule), as the CRM switches its
  boards; it opens on All dates, every project's shoots by date, scrolled to today's shoot - or the
  nearest one when nothing is on today - with a Today button to return to it: one row per shoot, a project's shoots
  together under the row that names it - Event ID and event once per project, then Shoot ID, date and
  shoot, read-only - then a block per booked service with who works it,
  and the shoot's Assist; nobody on a service is red, a vendor still Waiting amber, a confirmed vendor
  green. Each shoot is tinted by its place in its project - every first shoot one colour, every
  second shoot the next, the same across projects - and keeps to one line, cut with "…". The person
  under a service is a picker for whoever may change that shoot's plan (its
  Production Manager, or someone who works every project, with Production at Read / Write), saved at
  once; the rest of the plan is kept as it is. **A person is dragged onto another service** - on the
  same shoot or another the viewer may change - and the two swap; somebody who already has a shoot at
  that time is refused with a "This action is not possible" dialog naming that shoot, its project and the service (only where the
  viewer may change that shoot too), so it is changed first. **One person works one service of a
  shoot**: every crew save - here, the shoot's own plan form and the swap - refuses putting somebody
  on a second service of the same shoot, and the pickers leave them out (a shoot that already had
  somebody on two still saves). Filters by dates and projects, zooms out
  and in. Guarded by the existing `PROJECT / Production` permission (it reads and writes the
  Production board's own endpoints), so whoever opens Production opens this; no new permission. New
  `PATCH /api/project-management/production/shoots/:shootId/seat` and `POST
  /api/project-management/production/seat-swap`; the board rows now carry each
  service's person, the shoot's Assist and `canEditPlan`. The Shoot Board's Dates filter is now one
  component both pages share.
  [ProductionSchedulePage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionSchedulePage.js),
  [ProductionScheduleView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionScheduleView.js),
  [productionSchedule.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionSchedule.mjs),
  [ShootDateRangeFilter.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/shoot-board/ShootDateRangeFilter.js),
  [plan.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/plan.js),
  [swap.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/swap.js),
  [read.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/read.js)
- **A shoot held at several places is asked a venue for each place in Pre Production, and the
  production plan shows them.** When a combined shoot ("Haldi + Mehandi") is set to Location:
  Multiple on Add / Edit Shoot, its pre production form asks a **Location Link** and then a **Location
  Address** under each shoot's name ("Haldi - Location Link") in place of the one pair. The link
  sent to the client and the Download PDF ask and show the same, and a shoot counts as Planned only
  once every shoot's address is in. The Plan tab of Production shows the addresses and links
  read-only in a new **Location** box, one per shoot, as Pre Production saved them (a shoot at one
  place shows its one address and link there too). A shoot already given one address starts each
  shoot on it; the crew's WhatsApp message and the export read the addresses labelled, one per line.
  [formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js),
  [ProductionContextSummary.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionContextSummary.js),
  [shootLocations.js](../backend/src/services/shootLocations.js),
  [preProduction.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/preProduction.js). Migration
  `20261029130000_pre_production_locations` adds the nullable `project_pre_production.locations`
  (JSON; every existing shoot stays at one address). No new permission: it uses the existing pre
  production and production endpoints and their guards.
- **Employees can be added to the studio's WhatsApp groups from the app.** In **Settings -> Employee ->
  WhatsApp Groups**, type a WhatsApp group's name exactly and press **Add**; the groups added are listed
  under it, with Remove. In an employee's **Edit -> Employee Preference**, a new **WhatsApp Groups**
  section (between Flexible Shift and Alternative) is a multi-select of those groups with an **Add**
  button: tick the groups, press Add, and the employee's mobile number is added to each - one group
  every few seconds in the background, so the number is not restricted for bulk adding. WhatsApp only
  lets a group's admin add people, so each add finds the group with that name among a WhatsApp linked
  to the app where it is an admin - the person pressing Add's first, then any other linked one. Under it
  each group says how it went: **Added**, **Already in group**, **Invite link sent** (their privacy does
  not allow being added, so the group's link was sent to them on WhatsApp) or **Not added** with the
  reason - such as no linked WhatsApp being an admin of a group with that name - and a **Retry**.
  Groups they are already in are not offered again, and nobody is taken out of a group from here.
  Behind `HRM / Employee Management` - Read sees, Read / Write changes; no new permission. Migration
  `20261028170000_employee_whatsapp_groups` adds the `employee_whatsapp_group` (name) and
  `employee_whatsapp_group_member` tables (new tables only).
  [whatsapp-groups/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/whatsapp-groups/service.js),
  [EmployeeWhatsAppGroupsPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/EmployeeWhatsAppGroupsPanel.js),

- **Every picture in the application opens in one full-screen image viewer.** Pressing an image -
  a bill or QR code on a payment request, an employee's photo or Aadhar, a table thumbnail, the
  preview in any image upload field, a CRD response's photos, a task's attached picture, an
  inspection or attendance capture - opens it full screen over whatever it was opened from, Google
  Photos style: the picture at its own size, previous / next through the other images in the same
  place with "2 of 5", Escape to close, and the original in a new tab. CRD responses used to open the
  raw file in a new browser tab, and a task's photo used to download when pressed; Download is still
  in its ⋮. The Events gallery's photo, a WhatsApp chat photo and the attendance check-in selfies on
  Today's Attendance open in the same viewer (a WhatsApp video or PDF keeps its own player). A new
  picture added through any upload field opens there too. The viewer is titled with what the picture
  is ("Profile Photo", "Bills 2"). **Image Selection's Photo Selection gallery** opens each photo
  there too (its larger preview, previous / next through the gallery) - it had plain tiles only. Where
  pressing a photo picks it - the Signature Album's delete selection, the album's Add Photos and cover
  pickers - a small zoom button on the tile views it instead. Kept on their own viewers, by design:
  AI Culling's preview and AI Editing's editor (they carry pick and edit controls), the profile photo
  editor, QR codes, and public client pages.
  [ImageViewer.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/ImageViewer.js),
  [RecordDetails.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/RecordDetails.js)
- **Every table now has a Board (Kanban) view beside it.** A **Table / Board** switch sits in the
  header of every register in the application - 33 screens across HRM, Payroll, Accounts, Projects,
  Sales, Assets, Admin and Settings - and is remembered per screen. The Board stands the same rows
  in a column per status (Pending | In Progress | Completed ...), in the screen's own order and
  colours, with each column's count; a screen with no status is grouped by the category it carries
  instead - Contacts by vertical, User Management by branch, Role Management by type, Activity
  Logs by module, Excluded Numbers by first letter. A card opens the record as a double-click does.
  **Dragging a card runs that record's own action and only where it already has one**: Tasks Start /
  Finish & Send Back / Mark as Completed, Payment Requests Approve / Reject, Projects and Pre
  Production / Production status (their status dialog opens with the target already chosen), Assets
  and Client Storage moves, Employees Move to Active / Offboarding, Leave requests decisions,
  Interview stage moves and so on - any remark, reason or confirmation is still asked. Boards with
  no such action are view-only. Built once as the shared `KanbanBoard` and `TableBoardSwitch`; the
  CRM keeps its own board. Not boarded, by design: the day-by-day attendance calendar, the services
  grids inside the project form, and the shoot list inside forms. No backend change, no migration,
  no new permission.
  [KanbanBoard.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/KanbanBoard.js),
  [TableBoardSwitch.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/TableBoardSwitch.js)
- **Tasks has a Dashboard, the way Image Selection does.** It is the first entry in the Tasks
  dropdown - Dashboard · All Tasks · My Tasks · Tasks Given for whoever holds All Tasks, Dashboard ·
  My Tasks · Tasks Given for everybody else (the dropdown keeps that order rather than sorting) - and
  where the screen now opens, for everybody with Tasks. A reader of **All Tasks** gets a first row
  of five over every task that list reaches (All Tasks, All Pending, All In Progress, All Overdue, All
  Completed), under the same data scope. Then ten cards over **your own** tasks: **My Tasks, Pending, In Progress, Overdue, Completed**
  for the work assigned to you, and **Tasks Given, Not Started, Given In Progress, Finish & Send
  Back, Given Completed** for the work you assigned. Each card shows its change against the start of
  the range picked (This Week, This Month, 3 or 6 Months, Lifetime), worked out from each task's
  activity log, so nothing new is stored. Pressing a card narrows the **Recent Tasks** table under
  it to the tasks behind the number; double-clicking a row opens that task. Built from the same
  shared dashboard parts as Image Selection, and usable at 360px. No migration and no new
  permission - `GET /api/hrm/tasks/dashboard` sits behind `HRM / Task Management` Read.
  [dashboard.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/tasks/dashboard.js),
  [TaskDashboard.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/TaskDashboard.js),
  [taskDashboard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/taskDashboard.mjs)
- **Tasks: Finish & Send Back, Mark as Completed and Revoke.** Whoever a task is assigned to now
  presses **Finish & Send Back** (in the ⋮ menu and the task panel) instead of Mark Complete once
  they have started it. Whoever assigned it is told, and it moves to a new **Finish & Send Back** tab,
  after Cancelled, in their **Tasks Given**. My Tasks has no such tab: there, work you sent back
  counts as Completed, and a task you passed on reads Reassigned, so every row says the tab it is
  under. Only the person who **assigned** the task (Assigned By)
  can then **Mark as Completed**, and only after it is sent back. They can also **Revoke Task** at any
  point while it is open: it is taken back from the assignee, and in the same dialog they can
  **reassign it to anyone**, who follows the same flow from the start. Edit and Delete stay theirs.
  Each step writes its own Activity line ("Finished by … and sent back to …", "Revoked from … by …
  and reassigned to …", "Marked as completed by …"). No migration (`SUBMITTED` fits the existing
  status column) and no new permission - the new routes sit behind `HRM / Task Management`
  Read/Write.
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/tasks/service.js),
  [TaskDetailPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/TaskDetailPanel.js),
  [taskConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/taskConfig.js)
- **Image Selection has Expand: a dashboard of every project, opened from the Projects sidebar,
  where a project can be disabled - which holds it back from the client until it is enabled.** The
  sidebar's filter menu now starts with **Expand**, above a rule and the status filters, which are
  unchanged. It opens the dashboard's ten cards and its projects table in a popup over the Projects
  page, with the period selector in its header; the cards count the enabled projects, and the table
  adds an **Activity** column (Enabled / Disabled) and, in every row's ⋮, an **Enabled** switch. The
  header ⋮ is the Table Options every table carries, opening above the popup; the desktop app gains
  the same menu on this table, its layout saved per login under the web's own key (a CSV saves to a
  folder you pick; the desktop's file-save command now also takes a `.csv`). Disabling is one state
  for everyone: the project is marked **Disabled** in the sidebar and stays searchable; uploading,
  publishing, a new PIN and sending the client link are refused - on screen with "This project is
  disabled. Enable it from Expand to upload photos or send the client link." and by the server for
  any direct call - and the client's published link shows "temporarily unavailable" until it is
  enabled, with its URL, PIN, expiry, photos and selections all kept. Enabling restores everything
  and sends nothing by itself. Switching needs IMAGE_SELECTION / Project Management `READ_WRITE`.
  **Migration** `20261029140000_image_selection_project_disabled` adds two nullable columns to
  `image_selection_project` (`disabled_at`, `disabled_by_user_id` with its key and index); every
  existing project stays enabled; run `npx prisma migrate deploy`. No permission was added.
  [ExpandDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/dashboard/ExpandDialog.js),
  [projectEnabled.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/projectEnabled.js),
  [expand.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/dashboard/expand.js)
- **Accounts → Add Entry now records a Branch Transfer.** Beside Cash Received and Cash Spent, the
  first step offers Branch Transfer: money moving from one branch's account to another's, saved as
  one entry with the From Branch and the account it left, the To Branch and the account it reached
  (each account picked from its own branch), the amount, date, mode, reference, who made it and
  proof. It is filed in the From Branch's books under its own number run (`…-MT-…`), listed under a
  new **Transfers** tab with a **To Branch** column, and counted as neither income nor spend - no
  client, project or category. Recording or editing one needs `ACCOUNTS / Cash Management` Read /
  Write on **both** branches; no new permission. Migration
  `20261029100000_cash_entry_branch_transfer` adds `cash_entry.to_branch_id` and lets `client_name`
  be empty (additive, nothing rewritten).
  **Import from PDF → Record** opens the same form with the kind still choosable, pre-selected from
  the statement's credit or debit, so each payment is marked Cash Received, Cash Spent or Branch
  Transfer as it is recorded.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/accounts/cash-entries/controller.js),
  [accountsConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/accountsConfig.js),
  [CashEntryFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/CashEntryFormPanel.js),
  [StatementImportDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/StatementImportDialog.js)
- **A combined shoot can now be held at a different place for each of its shoots.** On Add Shoot and
  Edit Shoot, once two or more shoots are chosen (they are saved together as one shoot, "Haldi +
  Mehandi"), a new **Location** choice appears. **Single** works as before: one Shoot Place,
  District and State for all of them. **Multiple** asks for a Shoot Place, District and State under
  each shoot's name. It is still one shoot, with one Shoot ID, one pre production and one production
  plan, but it keeps each shoot's own place, and its Shoot Place reads "Chennai + Madurai" in the
  same order as the name on every screen that shows it. A saved shoot reopens on Multiple with its
  places. The Quotation Generator, Create Project and a project's plan all use the same dialog, and
  a quotation's places carry into the project.

  [shootLocations.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/shootLocations.mjs),
  [shootLocations.js](../backend/src/services/shootLocations.js). Migration
  `20261028120000_project_shoot_locations` adds the nullable `project_shoot.shoot_locations` (JSON;
  every existing shoot stays at one place). No new permission: it uses the existing shoot endpoints
  and their guards.
- **New leads from a Google Sheet can be welcomed on WhatsApp automatically, from their owner's
  number.** Settings → User Settings → Automatic WhatsApp Message → **New Lead Welcome** is one
  switch, **off by default**. When on, every lead the Google Sheet sync creates gets one message,
  after it is on the CRM Leads board, sent through `sendMessageToLead` from the linked WhatsApp of
  whoever the lead is assigned to, so the reply lands in that person's chat in the lead's thread.
  A lead who replies is a real one. A sheet link's first import is welcomed too. Nothing is sent for
  Add Lead, Bulk Entry, CSV import, the refill rebuild, a number that is not 10–15 digits, or a row
  whose enquiry date is before yesterday (which is what keeps a newly linked sheet's history from
  being messaged). To protect personal numbers from a ban, a
  sync welcomes at most 20 leads (the rest are logged as Failed, to message by hand) and one owner's
  WhatsApp sends at most 30 welcomes an hour (the rest wait for a later retry). The lead's name from
  the sheet is reduced to one short line with no links or formatting before it goes into the message,
  and only the app's own error sentences are logged or stored, never a library's text. Each message
  is a `CRM_LEAD_WELCOME` row in the WhatsApp Activity Log. If the owner's WhatsApp is not linked,
  nobody is assigned, or chat is switched off, it is retried three times, five minutes apart, within
  two hours, then shown **Failed** with the reason and can be resent from the log. The wording is a
  new template under Settings → Templates → New Lead Welcome ({client name}, {sender name}), seeded
  with a message that asks for the event date, location and type. Code:
  [newLeadWelcome.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/automatic-whatsapp/newLeadWelcome.js), hooked
  into `runGoogleSheetLinkSync` in
  [googleSheetsService.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/googleSheetsService.js), and
  [NewLeadWelcomePanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/NewLeadWelcomePanel.js). Migration
  `20261028110000_crm_lead_welcome_message` adds `hrm_settings.lead_welcome_enabled` (default off)
  and `lead_welcome_last_error`, and the template row (`WHERE NOT EXISTS`). Access uses the
  existing `SETTINGS / Automatic WhatsApp Message` permission (Read to view, Read / Write to switch),
  and editing the wording uses `SETTINGS / Message Template`, so no permission is new and no role
  needs re-saving. `LEAD_WELCOME_AUTOSEND=false` stops the sender entirely.
- **Send Back: Projects can return a project to Bookings & Converted to be corrected.** Projects'
  row menu has **Send Back** (whoever may write PROJECT / Projects; confirmed first, no reason asked).
  The project itself is marked - never copied: its id, shoots, quotation, payments, status and
  history stay as they are - and it leaves the Projects page and appears under a new **Sent Back** tab
  in Bookings & Converted (beside **All**, which still lists it), with counts. **Bookings & Converted
  now offers Edit only on a sent-back project** - the existing sale-details form; once a change is
  **saved**, the same save takes it out of Sent Back, puts it back on Projects, and locks it from
  editing in Bookings & Converted again until it is sent back once more (an edit that changes nothing
  closes without saving, as before, and leaves it Sent Back). The server enforces it: a booking-side
  editor (Sales Manager / Booking Edit) is refused (403) on a project that is not sent back, while
  whoever plans projects (PROJECT / Projects or Show All Projects write) still edits sale details
  from the Projects page as before. A second Send Back is refused (409). Both steps are in the project's Activity. Production,
  Pre Production and every other board are unchanged. Migration `20261029120000_project_send_back`
  adds `sales_project.sent_back_at` and `sent_back_by_user_id` (a key to `user`), both NULL on every
  existing project. No new permission.
  [ProjectsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectsPage.js),
  [SalesManagerPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SalesManagerPage.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js)
- **Production and Pre Production project panels have a Payments tab.** It is the same Payments
  section as Edit Project - Accounts Status, Signed Quotation, Extras, Cash Received, Cash Spent and
  the Project Summary - on the same project, so the figures match wherever it is opened. Access uses
  the existing permissions, nothing new to grant: the tab is shown only with **ACCOUNTS / Cash
  Management** Read (without it the tab is not there); **Record cash** (received and spent) needs
  Cash Management Read / Write and still saves through Accounts' own routes; **Add / Edit an extra**
  needs **PROJECT / Projects** Read / Write (Edit Project used to offer it without checking; the
  server always refused it); approving or rejecting an extra stays with the project's manager or a
  Super Admin, and is now offered only with PROJECT / Projects Read / Write too, as its route requires.
  The server's `GET /api/sales/projects/:id/payments` now accepts **PROJECT / Production** or **Pre
  Production** Read in place of Projects - always together with Cash Management Read, and only for a
  project in the reader's reach. A studio wanting a Production user to see project money ticks Cash
  Management (Read) on that user's role in Role Management.
  [PreProductionProjectPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionProjectPanel.js),
  [ProductionProjectPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionProjectPanel.js),
  [routes.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/routes.js)
- **A policy breach can be taken as loss-of-pay days instead of an amount.** Create Policy Breach
  has **Deduct by: Amount / LOP** under Employee Name. Amount works exactly as before; LOP turns Total
  Amount into **Total Days**, spread over the chosen months in half days (10 days over 3 months is
  3.5, 3.5 and 3 - the extra half days go to the earliest months). Each month's share shows on the
  Main Page in a new **Policy Breach LOP Days** column, beside the typed Policy Breach Leaves, and is
  added to Total Leaves - so it is cut at that month's day rate in the LOP Deduction and on the
  payslip. Skip on the Main Page moves its days along the run as it does an amount. The list,
  details and Payment History of an LOP breach read in days. New migration
  `20261029100000_policy_breach_lop` adds `deduct_by` (default AMOUNT) and `total_days` to
  `payroll_policy_breach`, and `policy_breach_lop_days` (default 0) to `payroll_entry` - every
  existing breach and payroll row is unchanged. Same routes and permission (`HRM / Payroll Policy
  Breach`); no new permission.
  [PayrollRecoverySection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollRecoverySection.js),
  [payroll-policy-breach/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-policy-breach/service.js),
  [payroll-register/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/service.js)
- **A quotation's version history has an Open link button again.** Next to Download and Copy link
  on every live version, it opens the client's public quotation page in a new tab, so the studio can
  see exactly what the client will get before sending it; the history stays open behind it. Like the
  other two it is shown only while the link is live.
  [QuotationVersionsDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationVersionsDialog.js)
- **Services and deliverables can be dragged into order on Bookings & Converted, Create Project,
  Edit Sale Details and Start / Edit Project, as they already could on the Quotation Generator.**
  Each shoot's Services table and Deliverables table now has the same grip at the front of every row
  (Move up / Move down on a touch screen); nothing is repriced. On a saved project the order is kept
  the moment a row is dropped; on a new project it is kept when the project is created. Lines brought
  in from a quotation stay read-only on Create Project and keep the quotation's order, which is set by
  dragging in the Quotation Generator. Existing projects show their lines exactly as before until
  someone drags one, and a line added after a drag lands at the end. New migration
  `20261029090000_project_line_sort_order` adds a nullable `sort_order` to
  `project_post_production_allocation` and `project_shoot_deliverable` (no value changed). The two
  new routes, `PUT /api/sales/projects/:id/shoots/:shootId/{service,deliverable}-allocations/order`,
  take the same guards as editing a line - no new permission.
  [useProjectPlan.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/useProjectPlan.js),
  [CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js)
- **Spot Review and Cyclic Review.** Add Review now asks which kind it is, and opens on Spot Review
  (Start Review, for a review that is due, opens on Cyclic with its due date). A **Cyclic Review** is
  the regular one: all the fields, with the Review Date filled in by itself - the date the review
  was due, else the employee's Next Review Date, else today - and the next review six months on. A
  **Spot Review** asks only the Review Outcome (required) and Remarks, is dated today, and changes
  neither the review schedule nor the salary totals; it shows a "Spot" tag on the Salary Timeline.
  **Migration** `20261027180000_employee_review_type` adds `employee_review.review_type`
  (`CYCLIC` / `SPOT`, default `CYCLIC`) - additive, every existing review reads as Cyclic. No
  permission change.
  [AddReviewDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/AddReviewDialog.js),
  [employees/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/employees/controller.js)
- **Add Review on the employee row menu.** User Management's ⋮ menu now offers Add Review, just
  under Start Offboarding, on every employee row that is past onboarding. It opens the employee's
  Edit panel on Reviews with the Add Review dialog already open - prefilled with the due date when a
  review is due - and is saved with the employee as before. Start Review on an overdue row is
  unchanged. Same permission as Edit (HRM / Employee Management, Read / Write).
  [EmployeeTable.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeTable.js)
- **A rejoining employee gets a new auto-generated password.** Move to Active on somebody in the
  InActive tab brings back the same record, username, roles and branch, but their login now reopens
  on a freshly generated password instead of the one they left with: the old password stops working,
  any saved desktop session is revoked, and they are asked to choose their own at first sign-in. The
  new password is emailed to the employee, and shown in the Login credentials dialog (copy, or Send
  WhatsApp) to whoever also holds User Management Read / Write; if the email is refused the rejoin
  still happens and the screen says why. Withdraw Notice is unchanged. No migration, no permission
  change. [employees/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/employees/controller.js),
  [loginCredentials.js](../backend/src/services/loginCredentials.js)
- **A client's sign-in needs a code sent by SMS (Beam Craft app).** For a client login a right
  password no longer returns a token: `POST /api/auth/login` answers `{ otpRequired, challenge, mobile
  (last four digits), expiresInSeconds }` and sends a six-digit code to the project's Client Main
  Number through the existing SMS gateway (`smsSender`). `POST /api/auth/client-otp/verify` takes the
  challenge and code and answers as login always has; `POST /api/auth/client-otp/resend` sends a new
  one for the same sign-in. Five minutes, single use, five wrong guesses spend it, only the hash is
  kept (new table `client_login_otp`, migration `20261026120000_client_login_otp`). Staff sign-in is
  unchanged. **Off until `CLIENT_LOGIN_OTP="on"`** - the default signs clients in with the password
  alone, as before; turn it on once `SMS_PROVIDER` and its keys (an approved DLT template for MSG91)
  are set. Turned on with no gateway, clients still sign in as before (logged), so it cannot shut them out. Locally (`NODE_ENV=development`) the code is echoed to the server console.
  [authController.js](../backend/src/controllers/authController.js)
- **A client sets their own password in the Beam Craft app.** Client logins are now made with
  `mustChangePassword`, and the app asks for a new password on sign-in while it is set (and from
  Profile any time), through `POST /api/user/change-password` - now open to client tokens - with the
  current password, the studio's password rules and history. It clears the flag and pushes "Your
  password was changed" to the client's phones. Client Credentials shows **Password: Set by the
  client** or **Studio's password - not changed yet**. Migration `20261026100000_client_must_change_password`
  sets the flag on every existing client login (staff untouched), so each is asked once.
  [routes.js](../backend/src/modules/user/routes.js)
- **A shoot's pre production details, filled in by the client in the app.** Pre Production -> a
  shoot -> **Client** -> **Send to client** asks the project's client (push, bell, Action Needed) to
  fill in **every pre production field still empty**, in the team form's order and words: concepts,
  the Dum Dum / Qua Qua checklist, travel and stay, location and event timing; whatever the team
  filled is shown, not asked. **Get Invitation Soft Copy, Getting Dresses Images and Getting Decor
  Images are uploads** - several files each, photos (compressed) or documents (PDF, Word, Excel,
  CSV, text; 5 MB each) - and tick those checklist answers. The client submits a few answers at a
  time; each locks once submitted, and lands in the shoot's own fields at once. The Client section
  lists what is still owed and every uploaded file with **Download** (under the client's file name).
  `GET`/`PATCH /api/client/pre-production`, `POST .../pre-production/:shootId/send-to-client`,
  `GET .../:shootId/client-form`, `GET .../:shootId/client-files/:fileId`; migrations
  `20261026160000_client_pre_production`, `20261026170000_client_pre_production_files`.
- **The CRD document in the client's app.** CRD Documents -> **Send Link** now also pushes "Please
  fill in your CRD document" to the project's client (kept for the app's bell, once within ten
  minutes, never for a submitted document), and `GET /api/client/crd?event=` gives the app the
  event's document once its link is sent - the link to the same `/crd/<token>` form, its status and
  submission time. The client fills and submits it in the app; the studio reads it under View as before.
- **More client pushes from Image Selection.** Photo Selection's **Send to Client** and **Send to
  Group** now also push "New photos are ready for you" to the booking's client (photos added to a
  gallery already published are announced this way), and publishing a **Signature Album** pushes
  "Your album is ready to view". After the send succeeds, never holding it up; the same message for
  the same gallery within ten minutes goes once. `clientPush.notifyGallery`.
- **Push notifications to clients' phones (Beam Craft app).** New table `client_push_token`
  (migration `20261024190000_client_push_token`) holds each phone's Expo push token against the client
  login; the app adds it with `POST /api/client/push-token` and removes it on sign-out (`DELETE`).
  DBS then sends through Expo, after its own save commits and never holding it up: a payment
  Received (cash book, project advance, scheduled payments), the gallery published, the crew on the
  way / at the venue / shoot started / completed, and the studio receiving the selection. A client
  reaches a project through its login or its Client Main Number. Tokens Expo reports gone are
  removed. [clientPush.js](../backend/src/services/clientPush.js)
- **A client can open their WhatsApp group from the app.** When the team pastes the group's invite
  link (https://chat.whatsapp.com/…) into a project's WhatsApp Group Name, `GET /api/client/project`
  sends that link as `whatsappGroupLink` - only the link, never the rest of the name. Null otherwise.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/controller.js)
- **One client, several events, one login.** A client login now reads every live project saved with
  the same Client Main Number (its last ten digits, the login's username) - a client who comes back
  for another event keeps one login. `GET /api/client/projects` lists the Event IDs, oldest first;
  every client route takes `?event=<Event ID>`, held to the client's own; without it the login's own
  project answers, as before. [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/controller.js)
  Create Project no longer refuses a returning client's number ("already used as a login
  username"): Client Credentials shows the login they already have (`GET /api/sales/client-logins/by-number`)
  and makes none; Edit Sale Details shows it too. A staff username with the same digits is still
  refused. [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js),
  [ExistingClientLogin.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/ExistingClientLogin.js)
- **A client can call or WhatsApp their project team.** `GET /api/client/project` adds `team`: each
  role's person with a number - the company-given phone, else the person's own contact number (a
  name typed by hand has none). The personal number is never sent when a company phone exists.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/controller.js)
- **The client app shows the studio's cover photo for each shoot.** `GET /api/client/project` adds
  `coverUrl` to each shoot: the cover uploaded in Settings -> Quotation Settings -> PDF Content,
  picked for the shoot the way a quotation picks its set, from the signed quotation's brand (else the
  project's vertical), read live so a changed cover reaches the app at once. Null when none is set.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/controller.js)
- **A client sees their shoot's place, session and crew size.** `GET /api/client/project` adds to
  each shoot its code (`DBS-SID-…`), place, session ("Full Session", duration) and how many crew are
  on it - for the client app's Live now card. Never the crew's names or numbers.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/controller.js)
- **Clients can follow their photo selection from start to finish.** `GET /api/client/reviews` now
  keeps a gallery listed after the client submits (`state: "submitted"`) and adds `progress` - shared,
  first opened, last activity, submitted, and when the studio downloaded the selection - plus each
  item's chosen count, limit and when it was sent. Read-only, the client's own project only.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/controller.js)
- **The client portal names the client by their own name, not the studio's group name.**
  `GET /api/client/project` now sends `clientName` - "Vikram and Harini", worked out as the client's
  invoice names them - instead of `projectName`, the WhatsApp group name ("WED 4t4 Erode TN … | NSM |
  …"), which is the studio's internal code and no longer leaves the API for a client.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/controller.js)
- **Clients can always download their own signed quotation from the app.** `GET /api/client/quotation/pdf`
  no longer refuses a quotation whose public link has lapsed or whose brand keeps client downloads off:
  a signed-in client's own signed quotation is theirs to keep. A lapsed one is printed with a one-time,
  two-minute pass for that quotation only, so its public link stays lapsed for everyone else and nothing
  is renewed; the brand setting still governs the public link.
  [quotationPrintPass.js](../backend/src/services/quotationPrintPass.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/controller.js)
- **Client accounts can see what is waiting for their review.** `GET /api/client/reviews` lists a
  published Image Selection gallery the client has not submitted yet (with the items still to choose
  for) and every Album Proofing album Ready for Your Review, each with the link and PIN the studio
  already sends on WhatsApp, for the Beam Craft client app's "Needs your review". Only the client's own
  project; read-only; the review itself still happens on the existing gallery and album pages.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/controller.js)
- **Client accounts can read their own payments and download their quotation and receipts.** Three
  routes join the client portal for the Beam Craft client mobile app: `GET /api/client/payments`
  (what the project is signed for - Initial Converted Value plus approved extras - and every payment
  received, added up exactly as Edit Project → Payments does), `GET /api/client/quotation/pdf` (the
  signed quotation's PDF, under the same lapsed-link and Allow Client Download rules as the client's
  quotation link) and `GET /api/client/receipt?entry=<receipt no.>` (one payment's invoice, only for
  money received on the client's own project - the studio's own invoice, unchanged). Never in the
  payments data: money spent, entry descriptions, remarks, who took the money, or extras still waiting. The project is read from the client's account, never
  from an id in the request; the two PDFs share a per-account download limit. API only - the web
  client portal is unchanged. No permission or migration: the portal belongs to the CLIENT role.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/controller.js),
  [routes.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/routes.js),
  [authMiddleware.js](../backend/src/middleware/authMiddleware.js)
- **Every cash entry now says where it came from.** A **Source** column in the Accounts Manager
  table, its filter and the entry's details reads **Manual** (Add Entry, a project's Payments tab,
  Create Project's advance, a scheduled payment cleared, an approved payment request), **CSV
  Import** or **PDF Import**. Entries recorded before this read "—": where they came from was never
  kept, so none is guessed. Migration `20261028100000_cash_entry_source` adds the nullable
  `cash_entry.source` column. The value is set by the code that writes the entry, never taken from
  the request, except that the cash entry form may say PDF Import.
  [cash-entries/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/accounts/cash-entries/controller.js),
  [accountsConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/accountsConfig.js)
- **Accounts Manager can now read payments - received and spent - straight from bank statements and receipts.** ⋮ →
  **Import from PDF** takes several PDFs at once, each with its own password (used to open the file,
  never stored), and lists every payment received in one table - **New**, **Duplicate** when a payment
  with the same transaction ID / UTR, date, amount and details is already in the cash book or earlier in the
  batch, **Recorded**, and a row
  for a file with **No transactions** or that **Failed** (wrong password, a scanned image). A PDF
  uploaded before is recognised by its contents even under a new name. **Record** opens the usual
  Record Cash Received form filled in from the PDF, where the project, the category (advance, extras,
  final settlement...) and the rest are chosen before anything is saved. Statements are read by their
  column headings, by the running balance where a bank draws its headings as pictures (SBI), or by
  each row's Credit / Debit or +/- on a payment-app statement, and what is found is checked
  against the statement's own printed Total Credits and Total Debits - a difference is a red warning.
  Withdrawals are listed as Cash Spent beside the money received, under All / Received / Spent tabs,
  and a status bar shows each side's total and how many are found, recorded, duplicate and left to
  record; Record opens Record Cash Spent for a withdrawal. Each file is
  read on its own, so one failure does not stop the batch. Uses the existing `ACCOUNTS / Cash Management`
  permission - no new one, no role changed. New dependency `pdfjs-dist` 4.10.38; migration
  `20261028090000_cash_statement_import` adds the `cash_statement_import` table (file hashes only)
  and an index on `cash_entry.transaction_id`.
  [StatementImportDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/StatementImportDialog.js),
  [statement-import/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/accounts/statement-import/controller.js),
  [parser.js](../backend/src/modules/accounts/statement-import/parser.js)
- **Somebody resigning now fills in their own notice dates, and HR's approval is what starts the
  notice period.** HR raises a **resignation request** from the Employee Repository's options menu -
  the employee is picked from a dropdown of anybody working here who is not already serving notice
  and has no form open - and says how many days of notice is to be served. That sends them a
  tokenised link: they confirm the email or phone on their record, say **from when** they are serving
  notice, and the form shows them the **expected last working day** it produces, counting the first
  day of notice as served. They may attach a resignation letter and write anything HR should know.
  Nothing about their employment changes when they send it: it reaches HR as **Submitted**, and only
  **Approve** writes the separation - through the same `recordSeparation` the separations form uses,
  so Serving Notice, the login closing on the right day and the roll-up that relieves them the
  morning after are the one path they always were. **Nothing is taken off them while they serve
  notice**: their team and their own work stay with them, the reporting line moves itself when they
  are relieved, and their pending work is handed over by HR from the InActive row's new **Hand Over
  Pending Work** - so approving a resignation no longer asks who takes over a day that has not come,
  or refuses outright because nobody above them is free to take their reports. A separation with no
  notice to serve still does both at once, since it makes them InActive immediately. A
  rejection has to say why and leaves the employment untouched, and a form that is only **nearly**
  right goes back rather than being refused: **Send back** reopens it on the same link with
  everything they filled in still on it and HR's remark saying what to change - the onboarding
  invite's own Send Back, at the other end of the employment - and the register marks those forms
  **Sent Back**. Approving, rejecting, sending back and cancelling each confirm first, and the review
  shows the letter it is deciding on. Every one of a row's actions is on its own **⋮** in the
  register, the way the onboarding invites' are: **View** on any row (a decided form is history and
  still worth reading), **Review** on a submitted one, **Edit form** while it is still open - the
  notice period or the note, never who it is for, and the link never changes - **Copy link**, the
  confirmation or refusal message once it is decided, and **Cancel form**. The studio hands the form
  over itself, so no screen emails it: the message from Settings and the link beside it are the way,
  and the only automatic email is the one that reopens a form sent back.
  The form asks what the studio's own resignation form asks: the record read back (employee ID, name,
  designation, team, reporting manager, joining date, official email), then the **resignation date**
  (today by default), the **reason** picked from the same list HR's separation form offers, anything
  more they want to say, and the **proposed last working day**, which is shown rather than asked:
  it is the notice period counted from the resignation date, worked out and stored by the server and
  never sent by the browser, so nobody agrees to a date they cannot see and nobody can shorten one.
  Leaving earlier than the notice allows stays HR's to set on the separation itself.
  The form's register sits beside the onboarding invites, under **Offboarding Forms** in the same
  menu, and both menu entries are drawn only for a writer.
  Both sides are guarded by `HRM / Employee Management` (Read to look, Read / Write to raise, send,
  cancel or decide), narrowed by the Employee Repository's own `employeeVisibility` - so a
  branch-scoped HR user neither sees nor acts on a form about somebody out of their reach. The
  employee's own three routes are public and authenticate by token, rate limited, never cached, with
  the contact masked to its domain and last two digits and five wrong answers closing the link for
  half an hour (HR emailing it again hands the tries back); an attached letter must be a PDF or an
  image whose first bytes carry the type it claims, and is stored before the form is marked sent, so
  a file the studio's storage refuses leaves the form open to try again.
  **The four messages the flow sends are the studio's own words**, in Settings → Message Template:
  **Offboarding Form** (the sent screen is now that message with its own Copy and nothing
  beside it - the onboarding invite's own screen - rather than a bare link in a read-only box;
  emailing the form and copying the bare link are on the register's row menu, for every form), **Offboarding Reminder**, **Offboarding Confirmed** - the dates
  a leaver keeps - and **Offboarding Not Accepted**, which carries HR's remark. The last three are
  offered from the form's own row in the register, so approving and telling somebody stay two acts.
  A studio that has not reworded one gets the wording the screens shipped with.
  **Needs `npx prisma migrate deploy`** for `20261026090000_employee_offboarding_invite`,
  `20261027090000_offboarding_form_message_template`, `20261027110000_offboarding_resignation_dates`
  and `20261027120000_offboarding_send_back`; no new permission, so nothing has to be granted
  in Role Management.
  [offboarding-invites](../backend/src/modules/hrm/offboarding-invites/controller.js),
  [OffboardingInviteDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/OffboardingInviteDialog.js),
  [PublicOffboardingForm.js](../frontend/src/components/offboarding/PublicOffboardingForm.js)
- **HRM → Events has a Download on each event, granted on its own in Role Management.** Download,
  beside View on the card and in the photo viewer, saves the event's photos: one photo as that
  picture, several as a ZIP named for the event, in posting order. It answers to a new permission,
  `HRM / Event Download` (Read is enough). It sits beside `HRM / Events`, which is still needed to
  see the wall. Without it the button is absent and `GET /api/hrm/events/:id/download` refuses
  with 403, so seeing an event and taking its photos away are now separate grants.
  - Photos are read only from the studio's own storage, by key or inline data. An outside link
    stored on an old event is never fetched, and is listed in a `NOT-INCLUDED.txt` instead.
  - The button reads *Downloading...* while it works, every other Download waits, and success or
    failure is shown in the page notice.
  - Migration `20261026120000_hrm_event_download_permission` adds the row and grants it to
    `SUPER_ADMIN` only. Every other role starts without it: tick **Download Events** in Role
    Management for the roles that should have it, for example HR or the studio's administrators,
    and re-save them.

  [download.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/events/download.js),
  [routes.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/events/routes.js),
  [EventsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EventsPage.js)
- **The Shoot Board filters branch wise, several branches at once.** A **Branches** multi-select sits
  beside Projects, over the branch each shoot's *project* belongs to - a shoot holds no branch of its
  own, and the booking's is what branch-wise means on every other board. It offers the branches the
  loaded range actually holds; a branch picked earlier that this range has no shoot for is set aside
  rather than emptying the board, and comes back with a range that has it - the rule the Projects
  filter already followed. Projects and Branches narrow together, Clear returns all three to their
  defaults, and a shoot whose project has no branch linked is offered under **No branch** rather than
  being unfilterable. The board now sends each shoot its project's `branchId` with the name read
  through the relation, so two branches once typed the same way are still two branches.
  **And picking a project or a branch now takes the board to it.** The board scrolls sideways through
  a range wider than the screen, so a selection whose shoots sat further along answered with "No
  shoots from 27 Oct to 9 Nov - the nearest shoot is on 11 Nov" and a button to go there. That is the
  right answer for somebody who scrolled into an empty stretch and the wrong one for somebody who has
  just said which project they want to see, so the board goes to the first day the selection has a
  shoot on - only where none of it is on screen already, and only on the selection changing. Scrolling
  away from a selection afterwards is still the reader's own, and the empty state still says so -
  **but not while the board is moving.** Scrolling a long range crosses whatever empty stretches it
  has, and the wash was appearing and going again on the way past; it now waits for the scroll to
  settle, so travelling through empty days is a plain scroll and the message is only for the days the
  reader has come to rest in.
  [ShootBoardPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/shoot-board/ShootBoardPage.js),
  [shoot-board/read.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/shoot-board/read.js)

- **The attendance Dashboard has a Permission card, so an approved hour off is no longer read as an
  absence.** Somebody with an approved permission is counted against **Absent** on a day their
  session falls short, and the figure alone could not tell the two apart. **Permission** now sits
  beside Absent as a headline card: it counts the days a permission was taken over the range, carries
  an arrow like the rest (neither good nor bad - it is approved time off), and pressing it lists
  exactly those people in the Employees table, most first, the way every other card narrows it. The
  Employees table and the Day by Day strip each carry the figure as a column beside Absent. The
  headline row holds all seven cards on one line on a wide screen (and breaks 4 + 3 before that)
  rather than leaving the new one alone on a row of its own. Nothing is
  counted twice: the figure was already tallied per day, per branch and per employee by the overview -
  it had simply never been shown.
  [AdminAttendanceDashboard.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AdminAttendanceDashboard.js),
  [AdminAttendanceEmployees.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AdminAttendanceEmployees.js),
  [attendance/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js)

- **Speak-up and Speak-up Review carry the tick boxes, with Export and Delete.** Both screens were
  the only registers in the application without them. `ADMIN / Table Select All` ("Select Table Rows
  in Bulk") decides whether the boxes are drawn at all, as everywhere else, so this is a Super
  Admin's until the studio ticks that row onto a role. The two Deletes are deliberately not the same
  act: on **Speak-up** it is taking back your own, reaching only your rows and only while a reviewer
  has not answered them — an answered one is refused with the reason, since the decision is the
  studio's record of what was raised and answered; on **Speak-up Review** it is HR clearing a record
  it has finished with, reaching any row whatever its state. The attachment goes with the row; the
  HRM task an Approved & Assigned Speak-up became stays on the Tasks board, because that is work
  somebody was given. A selection half of which may not go reports each refusal against its own row
  and clears the ticks on the ones that went, the way every other table's does.
  [SpeakUpPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/SpeakUpPanel.js),
  [SpeakUpReviewPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/SpeakUpReviewPanel.js),
  [speak-up/routes.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/speak-up/routes.js)

- **A referral instalment is now paid through payroll, as the referrer's Referral Bonus, and stops
  when the employee it was for leaves.** Two changes to HRM → Employee Referral, both of which the
  studio asked for.
  **Payroll pays it.** Payroll → Main Page carries a new **Referral Bonus** earning (after Incentive,
  with the **Referral ID**s beside it) holding the referral instalments due to that employee that
  month for a hire they introduced — brought in on Generate and Refresh like Salary Advance and
  Policy Breach Deduction are, never typed, counted in Total Earned Salary and printed on the payslip.
  Paying the month records those instalments as paid on the referral register, so the register's own
  **Mark paid** is gone (and its endpoint with it): money recordable in two places is money that can
  be handed over twice. An instalment reaches payroll **only where both people are still working** —
  the referrer, because the money is theirs and there is nobody to pay once they have gone, and the
  employee they referred, because the bonus is for that person staying.
  **Either of the two leaving ends the instalments still to come** — the hire, because the bonus is for
  them staying, and the referrer, because the money is theirs and there is nobody to pay once they have
  gone (a referrer deleted from the repository counts as gone). Nothing paid yet, and the referral is
  **off the register altogether** — nothing was earned and nothing is owed. One instalment paid, and it
  stays under **Settled**, the unpaid ones reading *stopped · employee left* / *referrer left* /
  *both left* so the register says which; what was paid stands either way, because money that has left
  is a fact. While **both are still here** a half-paid referral stays **Outstanding** — it is not
  settled until the last instalment is handed over. All of it is read live from the two employees'
  statuses (the studio's own `countsAsWorking` list), so nothing has to be written when somebody is
  relieved and somebody who rejoins is simply due again.
  **A reopened month owes it again.** The instalment records the payroll row that paid it
  (`employee_referral_payout.payroll_entry_id`), so setting a paid month back to Pending puts exactly
  that month's instalments back to Pending and the next Refresh reads them as due - without the link
  the figure was recomputed from what was still Pending, which was nothing, and the studio was
  quietly short the bonus when the month was paid again. A paid row also reads its **Referral ID**s
  through that link rather than by recomputing what is still due. And a row is paid **only with the
  figure it was worked out with**: if a referral was added, or somebody relieved, since the month was
  generated or refreshed, paying it is refused (409) and asks for a Refresh first, rather than paying
  an amount whose instalments no longer match it.
  Two migrations, `20261024160000_payroll_referral_bonus` and
  `20261024170000_referral_payout_payroll_entry` (both need `migrate deploy`). No permission changed;
  the register now needs only `HRM / Employee Referral` at Read. Two notes for the studio: a leaver's
  last part-month carries no referral bonus, because they are no longer working when it is read; and
  the **Referral ID**s now ride on payroll rows, so whoever may read a payroll row sees those codes
  (identifiers only - no referral names or amounts beyond the figure itself) without holding
  `HRM / Employee Referral`.
  [referrals/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/referrals/service.js),
  [payroll-register/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/service.js),
  [PayrollMainSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollMainSection.js),
  [EmployeeReferralsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeReferralsPage.js)

- **File in can be saved service by service: fill in the cards that are copied, mark it pending, and
  finish the rest later.** Production → a shoot → **Execution** → **File in** asks for the footage of
  every service the shoot booked - the link, who backed it up, the number of files, the size and the
  first and last file name - and **Complete photo copy** still wants all of them, because the step
  says the whole shoot is in. The copying itself happens card by card over hours, often by different
  people, and until now there was nowhere to put the first three services while the fourth was still
  being read: the only button refused the lot, so the answers were kept on paper and typed again at
  the end. **Mark as pending** now sits beside it, and only while something is still missing - once
  every service is answered there is nothing to leave pending, so there is one button to press. It
  keeps what is filled in, leaves the step on File in, says what it did ("Saved as it stands. 1
  service still to fill in, then complete photo copy."), and the form reopens on what it kept.
  **Complete photo copy** is also no longer a dead button: pressed with gaps it marks the missing
  answers **Required** on each service and names Mark as pending as the other way out, instead of
  sitting disabled with no reason given. What is saved is **the card as it was left**: every answer
  typed is written and a box left empty is written as empty, so reopening the step shows exactly what
  was there - clearing a box on an already-saved service and saving keeps it cleared, rather than
  bringing the old value back on the next open. A service emptied out altogether has its answer
  removed, which is how one answered by mistake is taken back. Completing the step is still what
  holds the record to being whole: every answer of every service, so a half-written row can never be
  read as a finished one. One migration, widening only, makes the five answers nullable:
  `20261024150000_footage_answers_nullable` (needs `migrate deploy`). The production **sheet import**
  reads a part-filled File in correctly too: it skips the photo copy only where the app holds a
  finished one, so a pending row is replaced rather than leaving the sheet's footage dropped while
  the step still moved to done. The save is the step's
  own people (the Production Coordinator, the shoot's team and crew, the Production Manager), only
  while the shoot is on File in, and it writes **File in saved** to the shoot's Activity. The write
  locks the shoot's production row and is refused if the step moved on meanwhile, so a save racing
  somebody else's Complete photo copy is told rather than writing into a finished shoot.
  `PATCH /api/project-management/production/shoots/:shootId/footage`, under the board's existing
  `PROJECT / Production` guard at Read & Write - no new permission.
  [ProductionStepForm.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionStepForm.js),
  [production/execution.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/execution.js)

- **A production plan can be marked as pending: what is filled in is saved and the rest is left for
  later.** A shoot with several services is rarely crewed in one sitting, and until now the only
  button was **Submit plan**, which the server refuses until a Production Coordinator, the travel
  mode (outdoor shoots) and a person on every service are all answered - so a half-filled plan could
  not be put down at all and the crewing was retyped at the next attempt. **Mark as pending** now
  sits beside it while the plan is unsubmitted: it saves the plan exactly as it stands, asks for
  none of it, and leaves the shoot pending with its tile counting what has been answered. Submit
  plan is unchanged and still the one that finishes the plan; once submitted there is one button
  again, Save changes, because a submitted plan is held to being complete. No permission changed -
  this is the same `PROJECT_MANAGEMENT / Production` write the plan already needed.
  [ProductionShootPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionShootPanel.js)
- **Payroll has a Policy Breach section: a fine taken from salary over months, shown on the payroll
  and the payslip.** HRM → Payroll → **Policy Breach** records an employee, an amount, a start month
  and year, a number of months and a reason (`PB-ID-0001`); the amount is split evenly over the months
  and each month's share appears on the Main Page as **Policy Breach Deduction** and **Policy Breach
  ID** in the Deductions band, is added to Total Deductions, and prints on the payslip as **Policy
  Breach** (a new built-in Edit Payslip item that can be renamed or turned off, not deleted). It runs
  exactly as Recovery does - Active / Completed from the payroll, Skip on the Main Page lengthens the
  run, Payment History, refused into a paid or frozen month - without Convert to Recovery. The
  existing **Policy Breach Leaves** (loss-of-pay days typed on a row) are unchanged and separate.
  New permission `HRM / Payroll Policy Breach`, granted to SUPER_ADMIN only by migration
  `20261024120000_hrm_payroll_policy_breach` (two new tables, `payroll_entry.policy_breach_deduction`
  defaulting to 0, so no existing figure moves); the studio may want to grant it in Role Management
  to whoever already holds `HRM / Payroll Recovery`. Skipping a month's policy breach on the Main
  Page needs it at Read / Write beside `HRM / Payroll Register`. The Policy Breach screen is the
  Recovery section with `kind="policy-breach"`.
  [payroll-policy-breach/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-policy-breach/service.js),
  [PayrollRecoverySection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollRecoverySection.js),
  [PayrollMainSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollMainSection.js)
- **Every project row can jump to the same project on another screen.** Bookings & Converted,
  Projects, Pre Production, Production and Post Production each carry one **Jump to** line in a
  row's ⋮, with the other four boards inside it - a submenu off a chevron, the way the table's own
  **Freeze Columns** is built, so the menu's own Edit and Update status are not buried under four
  near-identical lines that all begin with the same two words. Nothing is offered where no other
  board applies, rather than an empty line to open.
  Two things decide what is offered, and both have to be true: the viewer holds that board's
  permission, and the project is actually on it - so somebody with Production and Post Production
  alone sees one entry on each, and a project with no production raised is never offered a jump to
  Production. Every live project is on Bookings & Converted and on Projects, so those two are
  offered to whoever holds `SALES / Sales Manager` or `PROJECT / Projects`. Arriving **filters that board to the project** - its Event ID goes into the filter
  row, so the project is the row on screen, the box says why, and clearing it gives the whole board
  back. The board comes to **All** first where the project sits on a tab the reader is not looking
  at, since a filter over the wrong tab finds nothing. Nothing is opened, and the address lets the
  project go so a reload does not filter all over again.
  [boardJumps.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/boardJumps.mjs),
  [projectBoards.js](../backend/src/services/projectBoards.js)

- **A shoot opened from the calendar now says who is going.** The window the diary opens is the
  Shoot Board's own card, which draws the Production Coordinator, the Production Team and each
  service with its person and assistants - and showed none of them, because the calendar's feed
  never read them. So a shoot could say where it was and when, and nothing about the crew, which is
  the first thing anybody opens it to find out. One shape for both screens now
  (`services/productionTeam.js`), so the board and the diary cannot come to say different things.
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/schedule/calendar/service.js),
  [schedule.js](../frontend/src/lib/schedule.js)


- **A shoot's pre-production plan can carry a cover image.** Project & Shoot, at the top of each
  shoot's form, has an optional **Cover Image**: pick one and it is compressed (600 KB at 2000px)
  and stored in R2 with that shoot when the plan is saved; replacing or removing it deletes the old
  one. Not mandatory and not counted towards Planned. Nothing reads it yet - it is being collected
  for later use. Same permission as the rest of the form (`PROJECT / Pre Production`, Read / Write).
  **Migration** `20261023130000_pre_production_cover_image` adds `project_pre_production.cover_image_url`.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js),
  [formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js)
- **Bulk Update on Leads & Followups can move the ticked leads to another vertical.** A new
  **Vertical** field (the other two verticals; blank keeps them where they are) sits beside Lead
  Status, and the statuses on offer follow the vertical chosen. Choosing one shows a warning in the
  dialog, and pressing Update asks once more - "Data may be lost" - before anything moves. Moving
  **clears** what only the old vertical asks (Dum Dum's groom, bride and reference; Qua Qua's baby or
  mother, date of birth / EDOD, shoot type, IH/OH, shoot ID, contact repeated and its newborn and
  birthday occasions; Corp's company details) and the old vertical's custom fields; everything the
  verticals share stays. A lead whose number is already an enquiry in the target vertical is left
  where it is and counted in the result. Qua Qua's Converted & Followup becomes Converted elsewhere
  (and so loses its next follow-up). The Enquiry ID is kept. Same permission as Bulk Update
  (`SALES / CRM Lead Select All`, Read / Write); no migration. **The lead popup's Client Details now
  carry Vertical and Assign To on every vertical** (on Leads & Followups and in Contacts), in full
  rows of three. Picking another vertical only marks it; pressing Update gives the same warning, and
  on confirming saves the popup's other edits and then moves that one lead - refused, naming the
  enquiry, when its number is already in the target vertical. That needs only `SALES / CRM Leads` at
  Read / Write, as editing the lead does (`POST /api/sales/crm-leads/:id/vertical`). Assign To picks
  from the Sales roster and is saved with Update like the fields around it.
  [crmLeadService.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/crmLeadService.js),
  [CRMPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CRMPage.js)
- **Holidays can be declared for one branch, several, or all.** Settings → Holidays' dialog asks
  **Holiday applies to**: All branches, or Specific branches picked from the ones your role reaches
  for Holidays; All branches is offered only to somebody reaching every branch. A branch's holiday
  shows on the Calendar of its own people, named with whose it is ("Pongal · Madurai"), and
  attendance counts it as a holiday - out of the hours target, never an absence - for them alone;
  everybody else's day is unchanged. Whose branch you are is your employee record's, else your
  login's, and with neither you observe the studio-wide holidays only. Every holiday declared before
  this stays the studio's: nothing already declared changes meaning. Two branches may each have a
  holiday on one day; the same branch twice, or the studio's beside a branch's, is refused. The list
  shows each holiday's scope, a **Show holidays for** filter reads the month as one branch sees it,
  and a reader whose roles reach some branches sees those and the studio's. Payroll's working-day
  divisor and Nebula's working-day counts still count the studio-wide holidays only, having no one
  employee in scope. Migration `20261023100000_branch_wise_holidays`: a link table, and the
  one-holiday-per-day index dropped; no row rewritten. No new permission - `SETTINGS / Holidays`
  decides, with its roles' branches
  ([holidayCalendar.js](../backend/src/services/holidayCalendar.js),
  [holidays/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/holidays/controller.js),
  [HolidaysPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/HolidaysPanel.js),
  [attendance/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js)).
- **Pre Production tracks the project's hard disk on General, and handing it over starts it on
  Client Storage.** General asks **Hard Disk Status** beside Storage Needed - Not Received, Received
  or Handed Over - on any project whose sale said storage is needed. The first two are the
  coordinator's own tracking; **Handed Over** moves the project's Client Storage record from Yet to
  Receive to Yet to Start, the first step of the backup flow, and only a record still sitting at Yet
  to Receive is moved, so a disk already backed up is never pulled back to the beginning. Three
  answers rather than the eight Client Storage runs on: anyone with Pre Production write can give
  them, while the rest of the flow stays with Client Storage and its own permission. The row of
  "Move to Yet to Start", "Move to Hand In" buttons that used to walk a disk through the whole flow
  from General is gone, along with the route behind it, so this board sets the one status it is
  allowed to and no other; the disk's id, status and holder stay on General, read-only. Handing it
  over is logged on the project as it was before.
  [PreProductionGeneral.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionGeneral.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js),
  [migration](../backend/prisma/migrations/20261023110000_project_hard_disk_status/migration.sql)
- **A quotation can be shared with colleagues, who can then read and edit it.** The Quotation
  Generator has a **Share with** picker under Quotation Brand: the employees chosen see the
  quotation on their own Quotations register, with every version of it, and can raise the next
  version or edit the draft - without needing Show All Projects or being named on the enquiry. The
  **Sharing never raises a version**: on a quotation that already exists the picker saves itself
  (`PUT /api/sales/quotations/:id/shares`), because a version is the document the client receives
  and who at the studio can open it is not part of it. The
  share belongs to the whole quotation, so it is the same list whichever version is open, and it
  stays with the people whose own work the quotation is: somebody it was shared with edits it and
  reads the list, but cannot pass it on or drop a colleague from it. Anyone who can already edit a
  quotation can share it, so there is no new permission to grant; somebody whose roles do not open
  Quotations is marked in the picker, because a share cannot grant them the screen.
  [QuotationGeneratorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationGeneratorPanel.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js),
  [migration](../backend/prisma/migrations/20261022160000_quotation_shares/migration.sql)
- **Preview a quotation before generating it.** The Quotation Generator's footer now has **Preview**
  between Save Draft and Generate Quotation (an eye icon on a phone). It opens the client's copy of
  the quotation as it stands in a new tab - every unsaved edit, the brand, shoots, services,
  deliverables, discounts and Round Off, notes and Tamil included - while the generator stays open
  in the first tab exactly as it was. Leave that tab open and keep editing: a moment after you stop
  (0.8 s) the same tab brings itself up to date with the whole form - no need to press Preview again,
  though a press still updates it at once and brings it forward - and the generator's footer says
  "Updating preview…", "Preview up to date" (only once the tab has drawn it) or "Preview not updated"
  with Retry. The same pause auto-saves your edits in this browser tab, so a reload of Quotations
  reopens the quotation you were editing (`?edit=`, like `?duplicate=`) with your unsaved changes put
