  unchanged. See [AddShootDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/AddShootDialog.js).

- **Image Selection dashboard: Client Submitted counts a project once any selection item is
  submitted, and each row names its submitted items.** It used to count only projects with every
  item submitted, so Retouches sent while Frames was still being picked sat under Client In
  Progress. The card and its list now read a flag of their own ("at least one item sent"); the
  Status pill is unchanged and still says Selecting until every item is in. Under the Selected count
  each row lists what the client has submitted, with a tick on each item already copied out
  ([imageSelectionDashboard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/imageSelectionDashboard.mjs),
  [DashboardRecentProjects.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/dashboard/DashboardRecentProjects.js)).

- **Photo Selection Submitted notification: the wording lists each submitted category with its own
  count and the total.** The template's default now reads Project, Client, Event, a Submitted
  Categories block ("- Retouches: 5 photos selected", one line per item this submission sent - one
  for an individual Submit, every item a Submit All sent), Total Selected and Submitted At, each
  count read from that item's own picks; `{category breakdown}` and `{total selected count}` are the
  new placeholders, `{deliverables}` and `{selected count}` the same facts on one line
  ([photoSelection.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/automatic-whatsapp/photoSelection.js)).
- **Settings → User Settings has an "Automatic WhatsApp Message" entry, with Attendance WhatsApp
  Report inside it.** The rail reads WhatsApp, then Automatic WhatsApp Message (a group, holding
  Attendance WhatsApp Report), then WhatsApp Activity Log. The report page itself is unchanged -
  its time, Priority 1 and fallback order, group name, Save and Clear, and the daily send - and it
  keeps its id, so a link that opened it before opens it still, with the group unfolded. Nothing
  else moved; the group is there so the next message the app sends on its own has a place beside
  this one ([SettingsOverlay.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/SettingsOverlay.js)).

- **Offboarding hands over only the work still in progress.** Every role a leaver held on an
  unfinished project used to move to the person taking over, including parts already done. Now each
  role moves only while its own part is still open: **CRM** never (their part ends when the sale
  becomes a project; their open leads still move); **Pre Production Coordinator** until Pre
  Production is set Planned or Rejected, or every shoot's production plan is submitted; **Production
  Manager** until every shoot is completed, unless Production is set Rejected; a **gift's holder**
  until it is sent; **Project Manager, Creative Manager, Post Production Coordinator** until the
  project is finished. Done parts keep the leaver's name. The hand-over pop-up lists only these
  roles. Shoots, tasks, leads, candidates and approvals are unchanged.
  [handover.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/separations/handover.js).

- **Send WhatsApp shows only for somebody whose WhatsApp is linked.** In the onboarding invite, the
  application form invite, a new login, a client login and a CRD link, the button was drawn for
  everybody and greyed with a reason for anybody who had not linked their WhatsApp (or had it
  switched off) - who could only be refused. It is now not drawn at all for them; they copy the
  message as before. It appears once the session confirms WhatsApp is on for the studio and for them
  and their own WhatsApp is linked, and stays hidden if that cannot be read. The server still checks
  every send.
  [useWhatsappSender.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/useWhatsappSender.js),
  [SendWhatsAppButton.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/SendWhatsAppButton.js).

- **The Employee Repository screen is titled "User Management".** The sidebar entry under HRM, the
  heading over the register and over Administration's Users and Roles (which share it), and the
  sentences that pointed to the screen by name ("Maintained by HR in User Management", "Add one in
  HRM → User Management first") now say User Management. Only the words changed: the route is still
  `/employees`, the permission is still `HRM / Employee Repository` in Role Management, and the
  documentation keeps calling the module the Employee Repository
  ([navigation.mjs](../frontend/src/constants/navigation.mjs)).

- **Image Selection → Photo Selection: the button beside Download Selected reads "View Missing".**
  It used to read "See missing (116)"; the label is now the two words alone, and the number of
  originals that could not be found stays in the dialog the button opens, which lists each of them
  with where its record says it lives. Nothing else about the button changed: same place, same
  size, same dialog, same detection of a missing original and the same download of the rest
  ([DownloadSelectedButton.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/DownloadSelectedButton.js)).

- **Production has an Execution tab.** A project moves from Planned to **Execution** once any of its
  shoots' day has begun - a step past the first done (Started from Studio, or the pineapple meeting
  for an indoor shoot) - and stays there through shooting, the return and File in, until every shoot
  is Completed. It used to fall under Work in Progress with the projects still being planned. A shoot
  day paused stays in Execution; a hold still moves the project to Hold, and a status set by hand
  still wins. Shown with its percentage, like Work in Progress, in violet.
  [productionBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionBoard.mjs),
  [ProductionProjectPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionProjectPanel.js).

- **Every Yes / No on the Pre Production form starts on No.** Questions whose answer is stored as
  "not answered yet" - Getting Dresses Images, Getting Decor Images, Post Wedding Gift and the like -
  opened with neither picked. They now open on No, as the intro calls already did; an answer already
  given is kept, and saving writes the No.
  [yesNoField.js](../frontend/src/constants/yesNoField.js),
  [PreProductionFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionFormPanel.js).

- **Every time field reads AM / PM, whatever the computer's clock setting.** The browser's own time
  box follows the operating system, so a Windows machine set to 24 hours showed "14:00". `TimeField`
  now draws the app's 12-hour clock picker by default - the one CRD, Block Period and attendance
  requests already used - so every schema form and dialog shows "2:00 PM". The value saved is
  unchanged (`HH:MM`); `twelveHour={false}` keeps the browser's box where one is wanted.
  [TimeField.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/TimeField.js).

- **Pre Production asks "Concepts Needed" (Yes / No) before the concept list.** The list shows only on
  Yes; saving No empties it. A shoot that needs a concept counts as pending until one has a
  reference. The answer is the existing `concepts_needed` column, which had been set from the list
  alone - no migration.
  [formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js),
  [PreProductionFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionFormPanel.js),
  [preProductionProgress.js](../frontend/src/lib/preProductionProgress.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js).

- **Pre Production no longer asks for Google Review, and an indoor shoot is asked its branch instead
  of travel, location and studio start.** Google Review is gone from the Qua Qua checklist and its import
  template; what was saved stays on the record. A Studio / In-House shoot (the same rule Production
  uses for its steps) has no Travel & Accommodation section and no Shoot Date or Studio Start Date or
  Time - its shoot date stays the one set in Edit Project. In place of its Location it is asked
  **which branch** the shoot is at (a dropdown of the working branches, starting on the project's
  branch), and its progress counts only what it is asked. **Migration**
  `20261017100000_pre_production_shoot_branch` adds `project_pre_production.shoot_branch_id`
  (nullable, linked to `branch`); existing rows are left empty. The Pre
  Production row now carries `indoor`.
  [formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js),
  [preProductionProgress.js](../frontend/src/lib/preProductionProgress.js),
  [preProductionVerticalFields.js](../frontend/src/constants/preProductionVerticalFields.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js).

- **A reassigned task is Pending for the person it is given to; the Reassigned tab is the
  previous holder's.** Reassigning a task (or a leaver's handover) used to set its status to
  Reassigned, so it landed in the new holder's Reassigned tab instead of their Pending one. It is
  now written as Pending, and the Reassigned tab lists only the tasks the reader has passed on to
  somebody else - each row says who holds it now. Tasks reassigned before this change are not
  rewritten; they read as Pending. No migration.
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/tasks/service.js),
  [handover.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/separations/handover.js),
  [taskConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/taskConfig.js).

- **A pending Pre Production follow-up's actions are in a ⋮ menu.** Mark done, Edit and Delete were
  three buttons under each follow-up; they are now one ⋮ beside its date, shown only to someone who may
  change Pre Production. Delete still asks first.
  [PreProductionFollowups.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionFollowups.js).

- **Pre Production's and Production's "Waiting for Client" tab is called "Follow-up" again, and it
  lists the follow-ups that are due - today's and overdue ones, not those still ahead.** On Pre
  Production a project is listed once its earliest pending follow-up (a shoot's WCR date is one of
  them) is today or past; on Production, once a shoot's plan is on WCR with its Next Followup Date
  today or past. A follow-up set for tomorrow appears tomorrow. Before, Pre Production listed only
  projects with a shoot on WCR, whatever its date, and missed those with only a follow-up. The
  project still shows under its own status too.
  [PreProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionPage.js),
  [productionBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionBoard.mjs).

- **Calendar: Week is laid out as the Shoot Board.** Each booking is a bar over the days it covers,
  and the bars are stacked in lines so none sits on another. A project's shoots on days one after
  another - several on one day included - are one continuous bar on one line ("Reception · Wedding",
  Friday to Saturday) rather than one at the top of one day and the other at the bottom of the next;
  a day with no shoot of that project ends the run. Meetings, interviews, blocked periods, holidays
  and attendance stay a bar of one day. Clicking a bar opens the shoot window with all its shoots, by
  day. Month and Day are unchanged (`CalendarWeekLanes.js`, `lib/weekLanes.mjs`).

- **Calendar: Month shows only its own days.** The days of the month before and after, which filled
  out the first and last weeks, are now blank cells - no date, nothing booked, no ⋮ - so the weekdays
  still line up. "Showing … booked" counts only the month's own days. Week and Day are unchanged.

- **Attendance: the login and logout selfie is kept as it was seen.** A front camera's preview is a
  mirror, and the photo used to come out the other way round from what the person lined up. It is now
  drawn mirrored too, so the saved selfie matches the preview. Photos of things (the shared camera)
  stay the true picture.

- **The attendance calculator answers in days only.** `GET /api/hrm/attendance/calculator` no longer
  returns a `salary` block (monthly, per day, deduction, payable). It was worked over the period's
  calendar days, so it disagreed with Payroll → Main Page, which works the salary out itself under
  each month's own LOP divisor and rounding - and no screen read it. The days it returns are
  unchanged, and they are all the Main Page takes from it (days away, Casual Leave, comp-offs, the
  irregularity penalty); its pay cycle still comes from Payroll rules. Every payroll figure is the
  same before and after.

- **Payroll rules: Start Date and End Date apart.** Settings → Employee → Payroll rules → Attendance
  calculator shows **Start Date**, the one day typed, and **End Date** beside it, worked out and read
  only: the day before the start in the next month ("Last day" for a start of 1). What is saved is
  unchanged - still the one day.

- **Calendar: Add Meet asks for no lead.** The Lead field is gone: Add Meet books a plain Google Meet
  that belongs to no lead - an internal catch-up, a vendor, a call not yet a lead. It is seen by
  whoever booked it, by a guest whose sign-in email is on it, and by a Super Admin, and only whoever
  booked it may cancel it (Cancel meeting is not offered to a guest). Meetings about a client are
  still booked from inside the lead and linked to it as before. `sales_crm_meeting.enquiry_id` becomes
  nullable (migration `20261015090000_meeting_without_lead`; existing rows unchanged). New
  `POST /api/sales/crm-meetings` and `DELETE /api/sales/crm-meetings/:id`, under `SALES / CRM Leads`
  as Add Meet already was; the lead search that fed the picker (`GET /api/sales/crm-meetings/leads`)
  is removed. No permission changes.

- **Calendar: no gap after a filter's arrow.** The source, branch, period and view switches in the
  calendar header no longer carry fixed widths; each is as wide as its longest option, so the arrow
  sits beside its label and the next filter follows straight after. A long branch name is cut short
  at 12rem so the row still fits a phone.

- **The offer letter is designed as a letterhead.** One deep navy accent: the studio's name and
  address right of the logo over a navy rule (no box); OFFER LETTER centred, bold and a size up;
  From and To led by small black labels, the date on one line ("Date : 01/06/2025"); the subject
  unboxed and in black - its SUBJECT label and the line itself on one line, the same size, no rule;
  each section's title bold in the letter's own type and size (no capitals or spacing) over a
  hairline; Employment Details and Compensation as quiet label : value rows; bullets and numbers in
  navy; the signatory's company in navy; one type scale throughout - 18px the title, 14px the
  studio's name, 12px everything read (section titles, the subject and its label, the date), 10px
  the From and To labels and the letterhead address. The words, the sections and their order are
  unchanged, still on A4 with its 12mm margins - so the Settings preview, My Profile and the PDF all
  take it. No permission changes. The subject line "Offer of Employment for the Position of" is in
  regular weight, with only its SUBJECT label and the position's name bold.

- **The offer letter's sections are titled, not numbered.** "1. Employment Details", "2. Compensation"
  and every section after them print as their titles alone; bullets and the numbers of numbered points
  inside a section are unchanged. The Sections list in Settings drops the numbers it showed to match.
  No permission changes.

- **Certificate settings lose their explanation line.** Experience, Employment and Offer Letter under
  Settings → Employee → Certificate no longer print "The signature prints above the authorised
  signatory's name and designation… change them in Settings → Organization." under the signature
  fields. No permission changes.

- **A4 previews go on to a second page instead of scrolling.** The payslip template's, the
  certificates', the offer letter's and Employee Repository → Generate's previews showed one A4 sheet
  whatever the document's length, the rest scrolling inside it. A document longer than a sheet now
  shows as many A4 sheets as it prints, one under the other, broken between lines as a printer breaks
  them (the document is laid out in page-sized columns, a row, a heading or the signature kept whole),
  with "2 pages, as it prints." under them. The pages are laid out with blank space between them, so
  a sheet scaled down a fraction off shows nothing of the page before - no thin line down its left. The sheets still run nothing; one hidden copy, script-free,
  is read to count the pages (`A4DocumentPreview`). Printing and the PDF are unchanged - they already
  paginate. No permission changes.

- **Reviews → Salary timeline: every review card is open.** The increment, the salary it brought and
  the remark are always shown; the Show details / Hide details arrow is gone. Edit and Delete stay on
  the card's ⋮. No permission changes.

- **Attendance → Dashboard: a pressed card keeps its filter.** Pressing a card narrows the employee
  table to it and it stays narrowed - pressing it again, or double-clicking it, no longer lets go; only
  pressing another card moves the filter, and the chip beside Employees (×) clears it. No permission
  changes.

### Fixed
- **A link that opens a project's form on Projects opens it, rather than only filtering to it.** The
  table's landing on a linked project cleared `?project=` before the projects had loaded, and the
  `&edit=1` request went with it - so the calendar's Update › Project and Payment, and Overall Status's
  Project Initiation Update, left the board filtered to the project with no form open. The request is
  now held until the list is in, then opens the form (on its Payments tab for `&view=payments`).
  [ProjectsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectsPage.js)
- **Production Schedule no longer crashes on opening.** It opens on **Upcoming**, a range with no last
  day, and the Custom date boxes were filled from that missing day ("Cannot read properties of null").
  They now start from the first day, or empty for Unknown date.
  [ShootDateRangeFilter.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/shoot-board/ShootDateRangeFilter.js)
- **Somebody who has left is no longer counted Absent after their last day.** Attendance counted a
  person from their joining day with no end, so an offboarded employee who had worked a day in the range
  - or one still marked Active after their Date of Relieving - showed as **Absent** on the calendar's
  Team Attendance, the Attendance Dashboard and the register for every day after they left. Now each
  person is counted only up to and including their **Date of Relieving**: after it they are not Absent,
  not owed a day and not on the roster - unless they actually logged in that day, which still counts.
  The days before they left are unchanged, so past attendance still reads as it was. Leave and
  permissions taken are counted the same way.
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js)
- **A WhatsApp message sent from the app no longer shows "Waiting for this message. Learn more" on
  the sender's own phone and WhatsApp Web.** The recipient had it - and could reply - but the
  sender's other devices could not read their copy and asked the app's linked device to send it
  again, which it answered only for messages kept in the CRM's chat table, and only once they were
  saved. So Interview Welcome, group messages and logins handed over were never answered, and a
  New Lead Welcome asked for in the first moment was not either. Every message the linked device
  sends is now remembered in memory for a day and answered from there, and retries are counted
  (Baileys' `msgRetryCounterCache`) so a device that can never read one is not answered for ever.
  Nothing extra is sent to anybody. Messages already showing the placeholder stay as they are.
  [sessionManager.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/whatsapp-chat/sessionManager.js)
- **The client-chats test can no longer empty tables.** Its clean-up read and deleted by
  `F.project?.id` / `F.client?.id`; had its setup failed, that would have removed every chat thread,
  their notifications, client notifications, users and projects - the same fault that deleted the
  local logins on 28 Oct. Each now passes `{ in: [id].filter(Boolean) }`, and
  [test-cleanup-never-unfiltered.test.js](../backend/test/test-cleanup-never-unfiltered.test.js)
  now catches the pattern in a `findMany` too. Tests only; nothing in production is affected.
- **Only the CRM side waits for Send Back to edit a booking; everybody else edits as before.** Send
  Back had locked editing a project for everyone who does not hold PROJECT / Projects Read / Write -
  so a branch administrator or the project's own Project Manager without it could no longer edit a
  booking, and Bookings & Converted offered Edit to nobody until a project was sent back. Now the
  lock applies only to somebody whose one way to edit is SALES / Booking Edit (the CRM side): they
  edit from Bookings & Converted only while Projects has sent the project back, and that one save
  locks it to them again. The people the project is staffed to, a branch administrator, whoever
  works every project (Show All Projects) and whoever plans projects edit any time, sent back or
  not, as they did before Send Back. The server holds the same rule.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js),
  [SalesManagerPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SalesManagerPage.js)
- **A crew member's calendar shows the shoots they are on again, as the Shoot Board does.** Somebody
  holding Production and Shoot Board but not Projects, Pre Production, Post Production or Sales
  Manager saw none of their shoots on the calendar's All view: the server sent the shoots they are
  named on (the Shoot Board's own rule), and the page then dropped every one for want of a project
  source. All now keeps every shoot the server sent, since the server has already narrowed them to
  the viewer's own. Nobody sees a shoot they did not before.
  [meetingSources.js](../frontend/src/lib/meetingSources.js)
- **Edit Shoot on a project's plan now keeps Location: Multiple.** The dialog joined the places
  ("Chennai + Madurai") but the save left out each shoot's own place, so the shoot was kept at one
  place, reopened on Single, and Pre Production asked one Location Address. A shoot saved this way
  before the fix needs Edit Shoot → Multiple → Save once more.
  [useProjectPlan.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/useProjectPlan.js)
- **A failed test can no longer empty a table, and the schema file is back in its own layout.** Five
  backend test files cleaned up with `deleteMany({ where: { id: F.client?.id } })`; when the test's
  setup had failed (on a database behind its migrations), the id was `undefined`, Prisma dropped the
  filter, and the clean-up deleted every user - with their roles, attendance and notifications through
  the foreign keys - and every pre-production record. Each now passes `{ in: [id].filter(Boolean) }`,
  which matches nothing when there is nothing to remove, and
  [test-cleanup-never-unfiltered.test.js](../backend/test/test-cleanup-never-unfiltered.test.js)
  fails on the pattern anywhere in `test/` or `scripts/`. Separately, `schema.prisma` had been
  re-aligned by `prisma format`, which broke the tests that read it as text (`speak-up-schema` among
  them); it is develop's file again with only the employee WhatsApp groups models and the task
  status comments added. No production effect: tests never run against the VPS database.
  [schema.prisma](../backend/prisma/schema.prisma)
- **Payment Requests name who raised them again.** Every request opened from the list read
  "Raised by —" and its Raised By section had no name, because the list's who-did-it step read the
  request's `requestedBy` - the employee record - as a login id, found nobody, and wrote `null` over
  the name the request already carried. It now leaves a field holding a record alone. Raised By now
  reads **Employee Name, Employee ID, Department, Branch**, in that order.
  [userNames.js](../backend/src/services/userNames.js),
  [paymentRequestConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/paymentRequestConfig.js)
- **The backend test suite runs clean again (4,767 pass, none fail).** Four tests failed after the
  develop merge, none of them a fault in the application. `user-activity-log` still expected the
  any-word search develop briefly had, and is back on the rule the code follows (every word typed).
  `client-login` signed a staff token for user id 1, which `protect`'s new active-account check
  rightly refuses on a database with no user 1; it now uses the suite's own active staff account.
  `client-login-otp` retries its own status switch on a MySQL deadlock (Prisma P2034), which another
  suite's write to the user table can cause when every file runs at once; and the scene-engine test
  waits for the stand-in engine's exit to be heard instead of a fixed 200ms. Tests only.
- **Searching for `%`, `_` or `\` now finds what was typed, in every server-side search.** The
  server's searches run as MySQL `LIKE`, which read those three characters as wildcards: a typed `%`
  matched every row, `file_name` also found `fileXname`, `100%` also found `1000 photos`. The
  shared Word Chunk helper now escapes them (`likeLiteral` in
  [wordChunks.js](../backend/src/services/wordChunks.js)), which covers the ~30 searches built on
  it - projects, leads, assets, employees, vendors, cash entries, galleries, albums, AI Feature and
  more - and the five raw-SQL searches do the same (CRM lead board and Calls board filters, CRM
  reports, the AI lead lookup). Every other character - quotes, `&`, `#`, brackets, slashes, unicode,
  SQL-shaped text - was already accepted and matched as itself, on the web and the desktop, and
  still is; no search rule changed. Also: a column filter's dropdown no longer crashes on a number
  value, and on the desktop the project sidebar and group-name searches no longer crash on a row
  with no name, and AI person search ignores stray spaces. Production should keep MySQL's default
  `sql_mode` (without `NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES`), which this escape relies on - as Prisma's own does.
- **A shoot opened in Production from the calendar now has its back arrow.** It opens inside its
  project, over the project's shoot tiles, the way Pre Production already opens it, so the shoot
  form's title has the arrow back to the project's shoots and a saved Plan returns there. A shoot
  the viewer's board does not list still opens on its own, as before.
  [ProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionPage.js)
- **The client gallery now says why a shoot is empty instead of asking the client to "Select a
  Selection Setting".** That message appeared even with the selection item already open, for example
  on Post Wedding with nothing in it. It now reads one of these, in the client's words:
  - "No photos have been added for Post Wedding yet."
  - "Your photos for Post Wedding are being prepared." This shows when photos are filed for the shoot
    but still uploading or processing, or still waiting in the studio's AI Culling or AI Editing.
  - "The photos … are not ready yet." This shows when the shoot has no folder in the gallery yet.
  - "Choose a selection item to see its photos."

  The gallery's folder list now carries a per-folder `preparing` count for this. Nothing is sent on
  to Photo Selection by it, and nothing else about those photos is shown to the client.
  [galleryEmptyState.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/galleryEmptyState.mjs),
  [gallery/repository.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/gallery/repository.js)
- **A person who holds Production, and none of Projects, Pre Production or Sales Manager, now sees
  their own shoots on the calendar.** Before this, the calendar showed them no shoots at all, even
  ones they were assigned to. The shoot source in
  [calendar/service.js](../backend/src/modules/schedule/calendar/service.js) asked the shoot board's
  `boardWhere` about `viewer.id`, but the controller passes `{ userId }`, so the question was asked
  about login 0 and always answered "nothing". It now passes `viewer.userId`. The shoot appears if
  the person, or somebody reporting to them, is the project's Project Manager, Pre-Production
  Coordinator, Creative Manager, Production Manager or Post-Production Coordinator, the shoot's
  Production Coordinator, on its Production Team, or given one of its services as person or
  assistant. The login must be linked to an employee. No permission changed and no role needs
  re-saving. `test/schedule-calendar.test.js` had pinned the wrong field and is corrected;
  `test/calendar-production-shoots.test.js` runs the source with the controller's real viewer.
- **The client gallery's People tab no longer flashes faded while scrolling, and a photo whose
  preview is missing shows a clean "Preview unavailable" tile.** Every further page of photos loaded
  on scroll dimmed the whole grid already on screen and snapped it back, so a gallery of hundreds of
  photos flickered faded on every scroll; only a new answer (another person or scene) dims it now,
  and the next page is added below behind the grid's placeholder tiles. A thumbnail whose file is
  gone from storage drew the browser's broken-image icon with its file name over the tile, or
  pulsed as loading for good; it now shows a quiet icon, and its tick and menu still work. The
  missing files themselves are not restored by this - run `npm run audit:derivatives` on the server
  to see which galleries lost previews, and `npm run recover:derivatives` to rebuild them.
  [PeoplePanel.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/PeoplePanel.js),
  [PublicGalleryLazyImage.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/PublicGalleryLazyImage.js)
- **An offboarded employee goes InActive and is signed out at once.** Submitting the offboarding
  form left anybody whose last working day was today or later in Serving Notice, still signed in,
  and even somebody moved to InActive kept a working app for up to 7 days, because a staff sign-in
  was only ever checked for its signature. Submitting offboarding now relieves at once, whatever the
  last working day - the status lands, the row moves to InActive and the login closes; there is no
  notice period to serve - and every request now checks that the account is still active, as client
  logins always were. The employee's open app signs itself out within seconds (on its next request -
  the bell and heartbeat ask within a minute, with nothing touched) and lands on the login page,
  where signing in again is refused. The same applies to a deleted employee. Anybody already
  serving notice from before this change is relieved by the next save of their offboarding, or the
  day after their last working day. Approving a resignation form (the offboarding invite) takes the
  same path, `recordSeparation`, so it too relieves at once rather than starting a notice period.
  No migration, no permission change.
  [authMiddleware.js](../backend/src/middleware/authMiddleware.js),
  [separations/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/separations/controller.js)
- **The attendance ledgers' coalescing test no longer fails on a busy machine.** `npm test` failed
  roughly one run in ten on "asks for a rebuild while one runs come to one more run" with
  `2 !== 3` - and the coalescer was right every time. The test slept 60ms for the first rebuild to
  come and go, then 5ms to be inside the second; both are long enough on an idle machine and neither
  is under a full suite, where the first `setImmediate` can be starved past 60ms. The run was then
  still going when the next five asks arrived, so `again` folded all five into **one** more run
  instead of two. Each fake rebuild now hangs until the test releases it, and the test waits for a
  run to have *started* rather than for a number of milliseconds: nothing in it measures time, so it
  reads the same loaded or idle, and it now also checks that four asks during one run earn exactly
  one more run rather than four. No production code changed.
  [attendance-ledgers.test.js](../backend/test/attendance-ledgers.test.js)
- **A column of IDs, phone numbers or email addresses no longer offers a dropdown to pick from.** Any
  table's filter row offers a list where the column's values are a set and a typed box where they are
  not, worked out from the rows loaded - but the only test was "40 distinct values or fewer", so a
  column of **one value per row** was offered as a menu of every row: an Employee ID, an Event ID, a
  contact number, a login email. Worse, the control depended on how big the studio had grown - a
  column of 20 employee IDs was a menu of 20 IDs in a studio of 20 and a text box in a studio of 41,
  the same screen flipping silently at the 41st hire, which is how develop and production came to
  disagree about the Employee Repository. One value per row now reads as an identifier and keeps the
  typed box: nine in ten values distinct, counted over the rows that hold something, and only from
  eight rows up - so two people sharing a surname do not turn a column of names back into a menu of
  names, and a three-row table's Department column is not mistaken for an identifier. Genuine sets are
  untouched (Status, Designation, Department, Vertical, Gender, Blood Group, Work Type, the
  locations), and a column that knows better still says so itself (`filter: "text"`, or the
  `listFilters` allow-list). One rule in one place, so every one of the application's 37 filtered
  tables is answered the same way rather than each screen being brought into line by hand.
  [tableCells.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/tableCells.js)

- **A downloaded quotation PDF now always carries its pictures, and is about 35-45% smaller.** The
  PDF renderer waited at most two seconds for the page's pictures and then printed whatever had
  arrived. Every picture now passes through the JPEG conversion first, so on a slow storage
  response a cover or collage photograph printed blank, and nothing said so. The renderer now waits
  for every picture the page asks for, CSS backgrounds included, and for the fonts. A picture still
  loading after 20 seconds fails the download with an error instead of printing a quotation with
  holes in it, and pressing Download again retries. The PDF also stops printing blurred shadows,
  which Chrome writes as print-resolution bitmaps: the cards' soft drop-shadows were 35-45% of every
  file. Measured on three local quotations: 944 KB → 645 KB, 1,452 KB → 792 KB, 1,108 KB → 681 KB.
  Sharp shadows, such as the timeline dots' halos and 1px rings, stay, and the client's link keeps
  every shadow. Download in Version History and the ready dialog now reads *Preparing PDF...*
  while the file renders, the other Download buttons wait until it is done, and a dropped
  connection says so in plain words. No API, permission or data changed.
  [quotationPdfService.js](../backend/src/services/quotationPdfService.js),
  [QuotationVersionsDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationVersionsDialog.js),
  [QuotationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationPage.js)
- **The Payroll Main Page no longer slides up off the screen when scrolled.** The Payment cells'
  dropdowns and date fields keep a hidden label for screen readers, and it was positioned against
  the app shell rather than the field, so the labels of rows further down stretched the shell past
  the window and the whole page - title, tabs and column headers - scrolled up, leaving a blank band
  under the table. `Dropdown`, `DateField`, `MonthField` and `MultiSelectField` now hold their hidden
  label inside the field (`relative` wrapper), which fixes it on every table that puts one in a cell.
  [Dropdown.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/Dropdown.js),
  [hidden-label-contained.test.mjs](../frontend/test/hidden-label-contained.test.mjs)
- **A Branch Admin now actually sees the records of the branches their role reaches.** The tick
  carries `ADMIN / Branch Administration`, but `reachableBranchIds` looked for roles *granting* it
  by reading the role matrix - where a tick-carried permission has no row - so it answered "no
  roles", found no branches to apply the permission to, and left the administrator seeing only the
  work their own name was on. The one permission whose whole job is "see every record in these
  branches" widened nobody. The tick is read beside the grants now, so both ways of holding it reach
  the same branches.
  [iam.service.js](../backend/src/services/iam.service.js)
- **Booking a project, client login and all, needs only the booking's own permission.** Making a
  client login asked for `ADMIN / User Management` in four places - with the project, afterwards on
  Edit Sale Details, reading the one a project has, and sending it on WhatsApp - on the reading that
  making an account is User Management's act. That is true of a *staff* account; a client login
  reaches one project's portal and nothing of the studio's, and making it is the last step of
  booking that project. So a sales person filled the Client Credentials section in, pressed save,
  and **the whole project was refused** with a 403 naming a permission the Sales screen never
  mentions. The section was also hidden from them on the form - and because the left rail lists only
  what is on screen, losing that one entry left a single entry, which the form panel draws no rail
  for at all, so the rail disappeared too. All of it now answers to the booking: `SALES / Sales
  Manager` on Create Project, the project's own editor afterwards.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js),
  [CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js)

- **Saving a quotation that has not changed no longer raises a version.** A version means "this
  replaces what I sent you", but opening a quotation and saving it raised one whatever had been
  touched - so changing only who it is shared with left a chain of identical documents and moved the
  client's link onto the newest of them. The save now compares the document it was opened on - the
  client's details, the lines and their quantities, the figures, the notes - and says "Nothing
  changed, so no new version was raised" when they match. The form's own working is not part of
  that: each line's rate filled in from the catalogue, the catalogue row behind it, the brand
  snapshot and the marker saying which discount box was typed all arrive when an older quotation is
  reopened, and comparing them would have made every save look like a change. Changing anything the
  client reads still raises a version, as before.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js)

- **Searching a board finds a shoot as well as a project.** Pre Production, Production, Post
  Production, Quotations and Feedback list a project with its shoots under it, and a column filter
  was asking each shoot the same question as its project. A search for an event id found the project
  and then hid every shoot beneath it, and a search for a shoot id came back empty, because the
  project row does not carry one. Now a project matched brings all its shoots, a shoot matched
  brings that shoot alone, and the project it belongs to opens on it.
  [DataTable.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/DataTable.js)

- **A production plan no longer has to fill in the travel detail to be submitted.** Picking Other
  and leaving the box beside it empty refused the save with "A submitted plan needs its travel
  detail", as did Own or Car without a number plate and Office Vehicle without a vehicle - and a
  plan already submitted could not be saved at all until they were filled. Only the Travel Mode
  itself is mandatory now, beside the Production Coordinator and each service's person; the plate,
  the vehicle and the line saying how are recorded when they are known.
  [travel.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/travel.js),
  [plan.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/plan.js)
- **Clear all sits level with the Choose Services / Choose Deliverables box.** It was lined up with
  the bottom of the picker, so whenever the picker printed a line under its box ("No services
  available", loading, no match) the button sank below the box. It is now aligned to the box itself
  - the same top and the same height - whether or not that line shows; on a phone it still stacks
  under the picker ([ProjectServiceCreationSection.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectServiceCreationSection.js)).
- **Tamil prints correctly in quotation PDFs, and the PDFs are about a third of the size.** Tamil -
  names, events such as "Suvarna Daanam (சுவர்ண தானம்)", notes - read correctly online but not in the
  PDF: none of the quotation's fonts has Tamil, so the browser drew it with whatever the machine had
  (Nirmala UI on Windows), and the Linux server that prints the PDF has none. The quotation now
  carries Noto Serif Tamil and Noto Sans Tamil (SIL Open Font License) with the page, after each of
  its own faces, so the English typography is unchanged and the Tamil is embedded in the PDF from
  the page itself; nothing needs installing on the VPS. Separately, the PDF stored the WebP
  photographs as raw pixels - a 186 KB cover became 3.8 MB - so the printer is now handed them as
  JPEG no wider than 1280px (fetched with a 25 MB cap, a 50-megapixel limit and three at a time); a
  test quotation went from 5,875 KB to 1,663 KB with text, links and layout unchanged - and its
  closing photograph, which the slower raw-pixel render had been printing blank, now prints. The client's link still serves the original pictures
  ([quotationFonts.js](../frontend/src/app/q/quotationFonts.js),
  [pdfImageCompression.js](../backend/src/services/pdfImageCompression.js)).
- **Clients can Review & Submit from inside a card, and the sent message names the studio.** In the
  client gallery, opening a card (card 1, card 2...) replaced the screen that held Review & Submit,
  so a client had to go back to the card list to send their selection. An open card now ends in
  the card list's own footer - overall completion, Review & Submit and, when two items are ready,
  Submit All - the same component, the same rule (enabled once a photo is picked for the item,
  replaced by "submitted" once it is sent) and the same review; the photos scroll above it. On the
  card list the footer now starts after the sidebar instead of running under it, so the sidebar
  keeps its full height on a desktop. After a successful send the snackbar reads "Album sent to <Global Name>", from Settings
  -> Branding's Global Name; with none set it still says "your photographer". A failed send shows
  its error and never the success message. No API change
  ([SelectionFooter.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/SelectionFooter.js),
  [FolderGrid.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/FolderGrid.js),
  [ReviewSubmitButton.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/ReviewSubmitButton.js),
  [clientGalleryHome.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/clientGalleryHome.mjs)).
- **Review & Share saves your Photo Selection changes first, and a new selection item starts at a
  limit of 1.** Review & Share in the Selection Settings rail used to open the WhatsApp template
  straight away, and the template replaces the rail, so limits, checkboxes and an expiry date not
  yet saved with Save Changes - and an item typed into an add row without pressing + - were lost.
  It now saves all of them, then publishes if needed, and opens only once every step has worked; a
  refused limit, a failed save or a refused publish keeps you on the rail with the error shown and
  your edits in place, and a second press while it runs does nothing. On the desktop it also waits
  for a limit still being saved from its box. An item typed with the Limits box left empty now gets
  1 instead of the studio default of 50, on the web and the desktop, and a typed limit out of range
  is marked and refused rather than quietly replaced. Saved limits are untouched; no API or
  database change ([ImageSelectionSettingsPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/ImageSelectionSettingsPanel.js),
  [imageSelectionSettings.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/imageSelectionSettings.mjs); desktop:
  `ProjectWorkspace.jsx`, `src/lib/saveThenShare.js`).
- **Reports & Analytics and Attendance read a day as the studio's day, midnight to midnight in
  Asia/Kolkata.** Every measured timestamp is stored as UTC, and the reports bounded a range and
  grouped a day on the raw value - so "23 Sept to 22 Oct" actually ran from 05:30 on the 23rd to 05:29
  on the 23rd of October, and anything done between midnight and half past five in the morning was
  filed under the day before. Application Usage's Usage and Inactive Time Track, WhatsApp Usage,
  Work Hours, the Summary's calls-by-day and the attendance register's derived days now all share one
  rule for what a day is, and a range named in the filter bar is the range the figures cover.
  [studioDay.js](../backend/src/services/studioDay.js),
  [crm-reports/filters.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-reports/filters.js),
  [crm-reports/service.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-reports/service.js),
  [attendance/service.js](../backend/src/modules/schedule/attendance/service.js)
- **Refreshing the page keeps Settings open on the section you were on.** Settings is drawn over
  whatever page is open, so a reload used to close it and leave you on the page underneath. The open
  section is now kept in the address (`?settings=activity-log-purge`): a reload, or a link to it,
  opens Settings on that section again, on any page; closing Settings takes it out of the address.
  [globalSettings.js](../frontend/src/lib/globalSettings.js),
  [AppTopbar.js](../frontend/src/components/app-shell/AppTopbar.js)
- **A table that finds nothing says so on a phone too.** The "No matching records" and loading
  messages were centred across the table's full width, so on a narrow screen a wide table showed a
  blank area and its message - and any Clear filters button - sat off to the right, out of reach.
  They now stay centred in the part of the table you can see, wherever it is scrolled. Every table.
  [DataTable.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/DataTable.js)

- **The calendar no longer shows the shoots of deleted projects.** A deleted shoot was left out, but
  a live shoot whose project had been deleted was still drawn - 33 of them on the dev data. The
  calendar now leaves out both, as the project boards do. The calendar footer's "Use a day's ⋮ to
  start something on it…" hint is removed.
  [calendar/service.js](../backend/src/modules/schedule/calendar/service.js),
  [MeetingsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/MeetingsPage.js).

- **Calendar: a day's bookings use the whole day.** On Week and Month a day's list was held to about
  three entries and scrolled inside that, leaving the rest of a tall Week day empty. It now fills the
  day - on Week the full height, so a day's shoots stack one below another - and scrolls only once the
  day is full; a crowded day still never stretches the month's rows.

- **Calendar: a six-week month keeps its week lines.** A month that needs six rows - November 2026
  starts on a Sunday - squeezed each week below the height of its day cells on a shorter screen, so
  the cells spilled into the week beneath: the lines between the weeks vanished and the last week ran
  off the bottom. A week row is now never shorter than its days; the calendar scrolls instead.

- **A4 previews no longer stretch the page they sit on.** The A4 preview's hidden measuring copy
  hung outside its box and, a page tall, stretched the page holding it - a second scrollbar and an
  empty band beneath. It is now kept inside the preview, for every A4 preview (certificates, payslip
  and offer letter settings).

- **Edit Sale Details shows the project's own Schedule Payment, not the default row.** A booking
  created on Bookings & Converted with a payment schedule reopened showing a single "Advance · Slot
  Booking · 5%": the sale's form seeded the defaults and never read the project's saved rows, and it
  sent `null` on save - so a row typed over them was dropped too. (The rows were being saved all
  along: Create Project writes them, and Projects → Start / Edit Project already read them.) The form
  now loads the saved schedule, worked rows included, and sends it back. Who may **change** one is
  now two answers: **`SALES / Booking Edit`**, since a schedule is agreed when the sale is and a CRM
  correcting a booking has to be able to correct its schedule with it; or `PROJECT / Projects` plus
  this project's own started rule, as before. The section is a form for somebody who may change it and
  a **reading** - no boxes, nothing to add or remove - for everybody else, rather than a form whose
  save would be refused. A project booked
  before schedules were kept still opens on the defaults.
  [CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js),
  [SchedulePaymentSection.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/SchedulePaymentSection.js),
  [SalesManagerPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SalesManagerPage.js),
  [ProjectsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectsPage.js).

- **Edit Sale Details shows the project's own Schedule Payment, not the default row.** A booking
  created on Bookings & Converted with a payment schedule reopened showing a single "Advance · Slot
  Booking · 5%": the sale's form seeded the defaults and never read the project's saved rows, and it
  sent `null` on save - so a row typed over them was dropped too. (The rows were being saved all
  along: Create Project writes them, and Projects → Start / Edit Project already read them.) The form
  now loads the saved schedule, worked rows included, and sends it back. Who may **change** one is
  now two answers: **`SALES / Booking Edit`**, since a schedule is agreed when the sale is and a CRM
  correcting a booking has to be able to correct its schedule with it; or `PROJECT / Projects` plus
  this project's own started rule, as before. The section is a form for somebody who may change it and
  a **reading** - no boxes, nothing to add or remove - for everybody else, rather than a form whose
  save would be refused. A project booked
  before schedules were kept still opens on the defaults.
  [CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js),
  [SchedulePaymentSection.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/SchedulePaymentSection.js),
  [SalesManagerPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SalesManagerPage.js),
  [ProjectsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectsPage.js).

- **The photo-selection WhatsApp notice says 12:00 pm, not 0:00 pm.** Its "Submitted At" line asked
  `Intl` for `hour12: true` on `en-GB`, which ICU answers with the h11 cycle - so noon read "0:00 pm"
  and midnight "0:00 am". It now names the cycle (`hourCycle: "h12"`), as the studio clock does. The
  other two places that format a 12-hour time use `en-US` and `en-IN`, which are unaffected.
  [photoSelection.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/automatic-whatsapp/photoSelection.js).

- **`sales-quotation-presentation.test.js` passes again, so `develop` can be promoted.** It still
  expected the client's copy to have four section switches after the quotation change added the
  Pricing & Total card's own four - the card, its GST line, its payment link and its validity line -
  so CI failed with `develop is broken`. The test now expects all eight, each on unless a stored
  `false` turns it off, as the code already did. Tests and one comment only - no application
  behaviour changed.
  [sales-quotation-presentation.test.js](../backend/test/sales-quotation-presentation.test.js).

- **Refreshing the page keeps Settings open on the section you were on.** Settings is drawn over
  whatever page is open, so a reload used to close it and leave you on the page underneath. The open
  section is now kept in the address (`?settings=activity-log-purge`): a reload, or a link to it,
  opens Settings on that section again, on any page; closing Settings takes it out of the address.
  [globalSettings.js](../frontend/src/lib/globalSettings.js),
  [AppTopbar.js](../frontend/src/components/app-shell/AppTopbar.js)
- **A table that finds nothing says so on a phone too.** The "No matching records" and loading
  messages were centred across the table's full width, so on a narrow screen a wide table showed a
  blank area and its message - and any Clear filters button - sat off to the right, out of reach.
  They now stay centred in the part of the table you can see, wherever it is scrolled. Every table.
  [DataTable.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/DataTable.js)

- **The calendar no longer shows the shoots of deleted projects.** A deleted shoot was left out, but
  a live shoot whose project had been deleted was still drawn - 33 of them on the dev data. The
  calendar now leaves out both, as the project boards do. The calendar footer's "Use a day's ⋮ to
  start something on it…" hint is removed.
  [calendar/service.js](../backend/src/modules/schedule/calendar/service.js),
  [MeetingsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/MeetingsPage.js).

- **Calendar: a day's bookings use the whole day.** On Week and Month a day's list was held to about
  three entries and scrolled inside that, leaving the rest of a tall Week day empty. It now fills the
  day - on Week the full height, so a day's shoots stack one below another - and scrolls only once the
  day is full; a crowded day still never stretches the month's rows.

- **Calendar: a six-week month keeps its week lines.** A month that needs six rows - November 2026
  starts on a Sunday - squeezed each week below the height of its day cells on a shorter screen, so
  the cells spilled into the week beneath: the lines between the weeks vanished and the last week ran
  off the bottom. A week row is now never shorter than its days; the calendar scrolls instead.

- **A4 previews no longer stretch the page they sit on.** The A4 preview's hidden measuring copy
  hung outside its box and, a page tall, stretched the page holding it - a second scrollbar and an
  empty band beneath. It is now kept inside the preview, for every A4 preview (certificates, payslip
  and offer letter settings).

- **Image Selection: downloading one selection item no longer clears the others from Yet to
  Download.** A download was one stamp on the project, so the desktop copy of Retouches alone, or
  the browser's Download Selected of one shoot folder, marked the whole project downloaded - Frames
  dropped off Yet to Download unsent and the project counted as Downloaded. Each selection item now
  carries its own download stamp (`image_selection_deliverable_config.selected_downloaded_at`,
  migration `20261020150000_deliverable_selected_downloaded_at`, filled from the project's stamp for
  everything already downloaded), a run stamps only the items it covered (the desktop copy its one
  item; the browser run the items whose every pick sits in the folder it took, which it now names
  to the server), and the dashboard judges item by item: Yet to Download lists exactly the submitted
  items not yet copied out since they were sent, Downloaded means every one has been, and a new
  submission of an item puts that item back without touching the rest. The project's own stamp
  moves only once every item is up to date and still serves a gallery without items
  ([classify.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/dashboard/classify.js),
  [gallery/repository.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/gallery/repository.js)).
- **Interview → Onboarded: the onboarding invite opens in front of the candidate's form, not behind
  it.** Marking a candidate Onboarded from inside their popup opened the invite dialog - with its
  message template - at the page's own level, underneath the full-screen form it was opened from,
  so it looked as if nothing had happened. The invite dialog now takes a stacking layer, and the
  Interview screen opens it over the form when the form is open and from the page otherwise - the
  rule its resend dialog already followed
  ([OnboardingInviteDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/OnboardingInviteDialog.js)).

- **An event's guest join page no longer shows a CORS error, and its veil now follows the cover.**
  The page darkens the cover more or less depending on how bright it is where the event name sits.
  It used to measure that in the guest's browser by reading the cover from the image host. The host
  sends no CORS headers, so the browser refused the read, logged an error on every visit and always
  fell back to the middle veil. The server now measures the cover from its own storage and sends the
  level with the event (`coverVeil`), so a bright cover gets the deeper veil and a dark one the
  lighter veil, as intended. Each cover is read once per server process and cached. A cover that
  cannot be read, or that takes more than 1.5 seconds on a guest's first visit, keeps the middle veil
  it always had. See [coverVeil.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/public/coverVeil.js) and
  [GuestLanding.js](../frontend/src/components/ai-feature/guest/GuestLanding.js).

- **Reports & Analytics' Application Usage lists every active employee who used the application.**
  It used to build its rows from the CRM's lead activity, so only the sales team appeared. Now every
  **active employee** is listed: an employee who is not archived and still working, by their login
  where they have one. Those with app time in the range come first. It is kept to the people the reader may see and the employee
  filter, like Work Hours. Anyone without CRM activity shows zero Actions beside their Usage,
  Inactive and last sign-in. Every other active employee is listed too, with **0m**, so nobody who
  skipped the application goes missing. Employees who have left, and logins with no employee behind
  them, are not listed.
  [crm-reports/service.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-reports/service.js).
- **Calendar: a day's bookings use the whole day.** On Week and Month a day's list was held to about
  three entries and scrolled inside that, leaving the rest of a tall Week day empty. It now fills the
  day - on Week the full height, so a day's shoots stack one below another - and scrolls only once the
  day is full; a crowded day still never stretches the month's rows.

- **Calendar: a six-week month keeps its week lines.** A month that needs six rows - November 2026
  starts on a Sunday - squeezed each week below the height of its day cells on a shorter screen, so
  the cells spilled into the week beneath: the lines between the weeks vanished and the last week ran
  off the bottom. A week row is now never shorter than its days; the calendar scrolls instead.

- **A4 previews no longer stretch the page they sit on.** The A4 preview's hidden measuring copy
  hung outside its box and, a page tall, stretched the page holding it - a second scrollbar and an
  empty band beneath. It is now kept inside the preview, for every A4 preview (certificates, payslip
  and offer letter settings).

- **Tables name who created or changed a row instead of showing a user id.** A Created By / Updated
  By / Decided By field holds a **user** id. The tables' optional columns used to show that raw
  number, on screen and in exports. Every list now sends the person's name beside it, read through
  that user: their linked employee's name, or the user's own name when no employee is linked (never
  the employee with the same number). The shared table no longer offers a raw user-id field as a
  column, and heads the name column "Created By" and so on.
  - **Covers:** Assets, Asset Requests, Client Storage, Vendors, Accounts cash entries, Payment
    Requests, Extra Quotations, Quotations, Projects (Projects, Pre Production, Bookings &
    Converted), Interview candidates and AI Feature events.
  - **Now the employee name too:** Pre Production's Last Updated By, and the Added By / Requested By
    / Decided By names already shown on Vendors, Client Storage and Asset Requests (these used the
    login name before).
  [userNames.js](../backend/src/services/userNames.js),
  [DataTable.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/DataTable.js).

- **My Profile → Offer Letter shows the whole letter.** The A4 preview's hidden measuring copy hung
  outside its box and stretched the page, so the letter sat in a short window with a second scrollbar
  and an empty band beneath. It is now kept inside the preview (every A4 preview - certificates,
  payslip and offer letter settings - gets the same fix), and the profile shows the letter at a
  letter's width, centred.

- **A ⋮ submenu fits its longest choice.** Employee Repository's ⋮ → Generate drew "Employment
  Certificate" running into the flyout's edge: every submenu had one fixed width and its choices never
  wrap. A submenu is now as wide as its longest choice - never narrower than before, never wider than
  the screen - unless a row asks for a width of its own (`OptionsMenu`). No permission changes.

- **Edit Payslip → Add offers Payslip Info, not Personal and PF details.** The two were merged into
  one Payslip Info everywhere else - Edit Payslip's list and Edit Employee - but Add still asked for
  Personal details or PF details. It now offers Payslip Info, Earnings and Deductions, with no
  explanation line under the choice; an item added to Payslip Info is kept with the personal details.
  No permission changes.

- **My Profile's payslip notice reads in the dark themes.** The blue notice above the payslips ("…
  payslip will be generated on …") - and the Offer Letter's, and the Attendance Register's On break
  chip - kept their dark sky-blue text on the band the dark themes already darken, so it read dark on
  dark. The dark themes now lift sky text as they lift blue and indigo (`globals.css`). No
  permission changes.

- **Five lint warnings cleared.** An unneeded `useMemo` dependency in `useCredentialForm`, and three
  `x || []` lists rebuilt on every render in `AttendanceRequestFormPanel` and `ClientProofViewer` (now
  held in `useMemo`), plus an unused `next/image` import in `AppSidebar`. No behaviour changes.

- **The call-transcript Python test runs on Windows too.** It asked for `python3`, which a Windows
  install names `python`, so it read no output and failed with "Unexpected end of JSON input"; it now
  asks for `python` on Windows and `python3` elsewhere. The app's own interpreter search is unchanged.
  (On a Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true`, tests that read source as text with `
` in their
  patterns fail on CRLF line endings; set `core.autocrlf=input` and check out again to run them.)

- **No more hydration error from a popup opened inside Settings.** Edit Payslip's Add and Rename popups
  are forms, opened inside Settings - itself a form - so they were a `<form>` inside a `<form>`, which
  HTML forbids and React reported as a hydration error. The shared `Dialog` now draws a form dialog
  straight into `<body>`, as `SchemaFormPanel` already does, and stops its submit there, so Enter in a
  popup never submits the screen behind it. Every form dialog in the app gets the same. No
  permission changes.

- **Attendance login, logout and breaks say why they were refused, instead of "Validation failed".**
  The attendance endpoints now answer with the first real reason, and the capture's evidence has
  words a person can act on - most often a location reported more than 100 km out (a laptop or
  desktop with no GPS or Wi-Fi fix, or a VPN): "Your location is too rough to record ... Turn on precise
  location for this site, switch off any VPN, or use your phone". A position that is not a real place,
  and a selfie too large to send, are named too; every field's reasons still come back in `errors`.
  The selfie was already shrunk to 480px (about 36 KB) before sending, so its size was never the
  cause. No permission changes.

## 1.1.52 — 2026-10-14

### Added

- **Clients chat with the studio from their app, and the team answers on Sales -> Client Chats.** A
  client picks a topic - Pre Production, Payment, Production, Shoot details, Quotation or Other - and
  writes; the people who answer that topic are told in the bell (Payment: Accounts; the shoot topics:
  the project's manager and coordinators; Quotation: its CRM), the chat shows on Client Chats with the
  unanswered ones marked, and the team's reply reaches the client's phone and bell. Chats can be marked
  resolved and reopen when either side writes. New permission `SALES / Client Chats` (granted to Super
  Admin; others in Role Management); migration `20261028150000_client_chat`.
  ([chats/service.js](../backend/src/modules/client/chats/service.js),
  [ClientChatsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/ClientChatsPage.js))
- **Referral offers, on their own tab.** Sales -> Client Offers has two tabs: Home offers (the Home
  page of the clients' app, as before) and Referral offers, shown above the Refer a friend form on the
  app's Referrals page - "refer a friend and get 1% off". Each offer keeps its place; every existing
  offer stays on Home. Migration `20261028190000_client_offer_placement`.
  ([service.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/client-offers/service.js),
  [ClientOffersPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/ClientOffersPage.js))
- **Referral coins, Claim offers and Client app settings.** A client earns coins when a friend they
  referred from the app becomes a booking - once per referral, at the rate set on Sales -> Client
  Offers -> Client app settings (20 to start). The app shows the coins beside Chat with us and on
  Referrals, and Profile -> Claim offers lists the live offers to claim on WhatsApp. The same settings
  hold the WhatsApp number offers are asked about and claimed on (starting with the studio's office
  number; empty falls back to the branch phone). New `GET /api/client/coins`; migration
  `20261028180000_client_rewards`.
  ([rewards.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/rewards.js),
  [settings.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/client-offers/settings.js))
- **Nebula answers a client's chat first.** Each client message gets a reply from Nebula, written
  only from that client's own booking - shoots and dates, paid and balance due, project manager - and
  marked "Nebula (AI assistant)". Changes, prices, refunds, complaints and anything it does not know are
  handed to the team: the client is told the team will reply, and the chat stays unanswered in Client
  Chats and the bells. Nebula keeps out of a chat a person answered in the last half hour, and stays
  silent when the AI is off or unreachable. Off with `CLIENT_CHAT_AI=false` (or `AI_ENABLED=false`).
  ([chats/assistant.js](../backend/src/modules/client/chats/assistant.js))
- **The CRD document wears the client app's look inside the app and client website.** Opened with
  `#embed=app`, the form drops its logo bar and shows one centred column: the sections as pills on
  top, each section a white card, choices as tiles, gold buttons - on a phone and on a computer alike.
  The link opened on its own is unchanged. ([crdAppEmbed.css](../frontend/src/components/sales/crdAppEmbed.css))
- **The client joins their event's WhatsApp group from their app.** Pre Production -> General takes
  the group's invite link (https://chat.whatsapp.com/...) under the linked group, and the client's
  booking shows a WhatsApp group button beside its payments. Migration
  `20261028140000_project_whatsapp_invite_link` adds one nullable column to `sales_project`.
  ([ProjectWhatsappGroupField.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectWhatsappGroupField.js))
- **Sales -> Client Offers: the studio's offers on the Home page of the clients' app.** The team adds
  an offer - the studio's poster, square (1080 x 1080), portrait (1080 x 1350) or story (1080 x 1920),
  checked by shape on the form and on the server, any other size refused with the size it is - and
  while it is on and within its dates every client sees it on Home, whole at its own shape, and can ask
  about it on WhatsApp (their branch's number). Offers can be switched off, scheduled, edited or
  removed. New permission `SALES / Client Offers` (granted to Super Admin; others in Role Management);
  migrations `20261028120000_client_offer`, `20261028130000_client_offers_permission` and
  `20261028170000_client_offer_poster_size` (the poster's width and height). ([ClientOffersPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/ClientOffersPage.js))
- **Clients refer a friend from their app, and the referral lands in the CRM.** The app's Referrals
  tab takes a friend's name, mobile and what the shoot is for (wedding, baby/kids/family, corporate)
  and files a lead - source "Referral", the client as its reference, in the client's own branch, for
  their project's CRM, who is told. A number already in touch with the studio for that kind of event
  is not filed twice. The client sees their referrals with where each stands (new, in talks, booked).
  ([referrals.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/referrals.js))
- **The client's app shows their signed quotation in full, and their gallery in the app's look.**
  `GET /api/client/quotation/view` answers the quotation page and a 30-minute pass, so it opens
  though its public link has lapsed (for that client only; nothing is renewed), without Download.
  A gallery opened from the app (`#embed=app`) drops its own header and takes the app's colours and
  motion, and each Image Selection item reports how many photos it has, so a shoot with none is not
  asked of the client. ([PublicQuotationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/PublicQuotationPage.js),
  [appEmbed.css](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/appEmbed.css))
- **A vendor on a production service says whether they have confirmed, and a waiting vendor keeps the
  shoot off Planned.** A vendor in a service's **Person** seat was asked for a camera, which is the
  studio's and not theirs. That seat now asks **Status** instead - **Waiting** or **Confirmed** - and
  a vendor newly chosen starts on Waiting. A service whose vendor is Waiting counts as unfilled, so
  the shoot reads **Work in Progress** until every vendor on it is Confirmed; an employee in that seat
  is asked for the camera exactly as before, and carries no status. Choosing a vendor clears the
  camera that employee had, and going back to an employee clears the status. Assistants have neither.
  **Migration** `20261022100000_service_crew_vendor_status` adds
  `project_production_service_crew.vendor_status` (nullable); existing crew rows are left empty, which
  reads as waiting for a vendor.
  [crew.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/crew.js),
  [plan.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/plan.js),
  [planCompleteness.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/planCompleteness.js),
  [ProductionServiceCrew.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionServiceCrew.js).

- **A permission of its own for editing a booking: `SALES / Booking Edit` ("Edit Bookings").**
  Changing a booking on **Bookings & Converted** - or on Projects - answered only to the record: the
  four seats the project is staffed to, `ADMIN / Branch Administration`, or `PROJECT / Show All
  Projects`. So `SALES / Sales Manager` Read / Write let a CRM **create** a booking and never edit
  one, and the only grantable fix was Show All Projects, which also hands over every project on
  Projects, Pre Production and Production. Ticking **Edit Bookings** at Read / Write now lets a role
  edit the bookings it can already see (their sale details and client login), with Sales Manager
  Read / Write beside it - it widens no reading, and Read alone grants nothing.
  It takes nothing away - everybody who could edit a booking still can - **deleting** one stays its
  Project Manager's, and the plan keeps its own rule. The row's Edit and
  `PATCH /api/sales/projects/:id` read the same rule, so the menu cannot offer an edit the server
  refuses. **Migration** `20261021120000_booking_edit_permission` adds the permission and grants it to
  **SUPER_ADMIN only**; grant it to other roles in Admin → Role Management. The studio may want it for
  the CRM / Sales roles that raise bookings.
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js),
  [permission-catalogue.js](../backend/prisma/seeds/permission-catalogue.js),
  [SalesManagerPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SalesManagerPage.js),
  [ProjectsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectsPage.js).

- **The CRD document asks about every shoot, one event each.** The client's CRD form, Dum Dum and
  Qua Qua alike, now has one event per shoot of the project, so five shoots means five events. Each
  is titled by its shoot (for example "Event 2: Haldi") and asks its own **Date**, **Start Time** and
  **End Time** as three separate fields, as the shoot keeps them, plus an Event Address Link. The
  times use the 12-hour clock picker.
  - The shoot's date and times fill in where known, and the client can correct them.
  - None of it is required.
  - The list follows the project: a shoot added later gets an event, a deleted one loses it, and
    what the client typed stays with its shoot.
  - Before, Dum Dum asked one event filled from the Main Event shoot, and Qua Qua asked none. A
    document with no shoots behind it still asks the one event.
  - The studio's View, on CRD Documents and on the Overall Status tab, lists every event.
  - No database change: the events are stored inside the document.
  [events.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crd-documents/events.js),
  [crdDocumentShared.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/crdDocumentShared.js),
  [CrdDocumentResponse.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CrdDocumentResponse.js).

- **Duplicate a shoot on Projects and Bookings & Converted.** In Start / Edit Project and in Create
  / Edit Project, each row of the Shoot List's ⋮ now offers **Duplicate** between Edit and Delete.
  It opens the shoot dialog as **Duplicate Shoot**, filled with every detail of the shoot copied:
  shoot, date, place, district and state, types, session timing, food, accommodation, travel and
  preference. Change anything, then **Save** adds it as a new shoot, never as the Main Event.
  Shoots a quotation priced stay as they are, with no Duplicate, like Edit and Delete.
  [AddShootDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/AddShootDialog.js),
  [useProjectPlan.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/useProjectPlan.js),
  [CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js).

- **A Pre Production shoot's Event Timing shows the shoot's date, editable both ways.** A **Shoot
  Date** field now leads the Event Timing section. It is the shoot's own date, the same one Edit
  Project shows, so a change on either screen appears on the other. Giving a date here makes Edit
  Project read **Shoot Date Known: Yes** with that date, and clearing it makes it read No. No new
  column: it writes `project_shoot.date_created`, which Production's three-day Execution rule and
  Image Selection also read.
  [formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js).

- **Bus, Train and Flight plans now have a Ticket Status: Yet to Take, Taken or On the Fly.** On a
  shoot's production plan, picking a ticket travel mode asks where the tickets stand:
  - **Yet to Take** means nothing is bought yet, so the plan stays Work in Progress.
  - **Taken** opens the Tickets upload, and the plan is complete once a ticket is attached.
  - **On the Fly** means bought on the way, with nothing to attach, so the plan can be complete.
  Other travel modes don't ask it. Plans saved before keep no status and read as they did: an
  attached ticket completes them. New nullable column `project_production.ticket_status`.
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate`.
  [travel.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/travel.js),
  [productionFormConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/productionFormConfig.js),
  [20261015100000_production_ticket_status](../backend/prisma/migrations/20261015100000_production_ticket_status/migration.sql).

- **Download invoice on a cash received row in Accounts Manager.** The ⋮ on any Cash Received
  entry now offers **Download invoice**, the same PDF a project's Payments tab downloads. Money
  spent has none. Anyone who can see the table can use it (`ACCOUNTS / Cash Management` Read).
  [AccountsTable.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/AccountsTable.js).

- **The Overall Status shows the project's CRD document under Pre Production, with a read-only
  View.** Only when the project's CRD Document is applicable: one marked Not Applicable, or not yet
  answered, shows nothing. The Pre Production stage reads **Submitted** or **Not submitted**, and
  once submitted, **View** opens what the client sent, read-only, with no share link offered or made.
  It works on all four screens that show the Overall Status: Projects, Bookings & Converted, Pre
  Production and Production. Reading it needs the same permissions as the Overall Status (anyone
  who reads the project register), held to the projects that reader may reach. Issuing and sharing
  links stays on the CRD Documents page.
  [ProjectStageView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectStageView.js),
  [CrdDocumentViewPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CrdDocumentViewPanel.js),
  [stage.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/stage.js).

- **A project's Overall Status on every screen that opens one.** The Overall Status tab shows where
  the whole project stands, stage by stage: Project Initiation, Pre Production, Production, Post
  Production and Delivered. It now appears on the record **Bookings & Converted** opens, on the
  **Pre Production** project panel (between Shoots and Activity), and on the **Production** project
  panel (beside Shoots), as well as on Projects. Outside Projects it is read-only; updating a stage
  stays with whoever plans projects. Reading it now needs any permission that reads the project
  register (Sales Manager, Projects, Pre Production, Production, Post Production and the rest), not
  only `PROJECT / Projects`, and each project is still narrowed to the ones the reader may reach.
  [ProjectStageView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectStageView.js),
  [routes.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/routes.js).

- **Bookings & Converted opens a booking row to its shoots, as Projects does.** The ▸ at the start of
  a row lists that booking's shoots underneath, one row each, with the shoot's own type, Shoot ID,
  name and place, and date and time in the matching columns. Clicking or double-clicking a shoot
  row opens its booking, and ticks stay on the bookings. The table keeps its own columns.
