  [SalesManagerPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SalesManagerPage.js),
  [ProjectDataTable.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/ProjectDataTable.js).

- **A pending Pre Production follow-up can now be edited or deleted.** Beside **Mark done**, each
  pending follow-up in a project's Follow-ups column has **Edit**, which changes its date and remarks
  in place, and **Delete**, which asks first. Both are logged on the project's Activity. A follow-up
  already marked done stays as it was. They need `PROJECT / Pre Production` Read / Write, as adding
  one does; no new permission.
  [PreProductionFollowups.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionFollowups.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js).

- **An invoice PDF for every cash received on a project.** On a project's Payments tab, each Cash
  Received row has a download button. It saves that payment's invoice as a PDF, laid out like this:
  - "Invoice" at the top, with the invoice number (the entry's own received number) and the date of
    issue, and the studio's logo on the right (the app's own mark when none is uploaded)
  - the studio's name, plus the address, phone, email and GSTIN of the branch the money was
    received at (Head Office when the entry has none), beside **Bill to**: the enquiry's name (a
    Dum Dum lead's groom and bride, "Kavin and Thangamani", or a Qua Qua lead's one name; the
    WhatsApp group name only when there is no lead name to use), phone, email and the project's
    Event ID
  - what the payment was for, its mode and reference, who received it, and the amount in figures
    and words
  It is a white A4 page headed by a large "Invoice", with two thin grey parallel lines sweeping
  down its left side, set in from the edge. The payment details are a
  two-column box, with labels on the left and values on the right: Towards, Payment mode, Received
  by, Amount received (with the amount in words beneath it) and **Total due**. Total due is what the project still owed just
  after this payment: the converted value plus approved extras, less everything received up to and
  including it, so an older invoice keeps its own figure. "Thank you for your business" and the
  computer-generated note sit at the foot of the page, so the content is spread down the page rather
  than packed at the top. There is no due date and no tax
  lines. Anyone who can see the Payments tab can download it (`ACCOUNTS / Cash Management` Read), and money spent has
  none.
  [receipt.js](../backend/src/modules/accounts/cash-entries/receipt.js),
  [paymentReceiptPdf.js](../backend/src/services/paymentReceiptPdf.js),
  [ProjectPaymentsView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectPaymentsView.js).

- **Update status on a project row's ⋮ menu, on Projects.** It sets one project's status without
  ticking it, using the same five choices and the same rules as Update over ticked projects. It is
  offered only to people who may plan projects. A started project can still be changed only by its
  Project Manager or a branch administrator; anyone else is told so instead.
  [ProjectDataTable.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/ProjectDataTable.js),
  [ProjectsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectsPage.js).

- **A project's Payments tab shows its Accounts status above the signed quotation.** It opens on
  where the project stands with the money it is booked to receive - **Hold**, **Overdue**, **Due** or
  **Active** - the same as on Accounts Manager.
  [ProjectPaymentsView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectPaymentsView.js).

- **An Activity tab on a project, on Projects and on Pre Production, as Production's shoots have.**
  Every change made from either screen is now recorded - what was done, the shoot it was about,
  who did it and when - and listed newest first. **Projects** (Start / Edit Project, and the record a
  double click opens, after Overall Status): the project created, its sale details or project details
  saved, its status changed (alone or with Update over ticked projects), shoots added, edited or
  removed, services and deliverables changed, the advance recorded, the payment schedule saved, and its
  Production status set by hand. **Pre Production** (the project's panel, beside Shoots): a shoot's
  details saved, its status changed (WCR with its next follow-up, Hold, Rejected, with the remarks),
  follow-ups added or done, General saved, a gift's or storage's status changed, the WhatsApp group
  linked, and the project's Pre Production status set by hand. Start Project's autosaved drafts are
  not listed. Nothing done before this release was recorded. **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`
  (`20261014110000_project_activity`: one new table).
  [projectActivity.js](../backend/src/services/projectActivity.js),
  [ProjectActivityTab.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectActivityTab.js).

- **A Follow-up tab on Pre Production and Production, and no remarks on the shoot tiles.** Each board
  gains a **Follow-up** tab listing every project with a shoot on WCR (waiting for the client's reply)
  - Pre Production's WCR shoots on its board, Production's on its own. A project stays under its own
  status tab as well, so it is found either way. The shoot tiles on both boards now show the status
  alone, never the remarks behind it (WCR, Hold, Rejected): those are read where the status is set -
  the shoot's form, or the Plan tab.
  [PreProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionPage.js),
  [productionBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionBoard.mjs).

- **Production's plan can be set to WCR - waiting for the client's reply - with the next follow-up
  date, as Pre Production's shoots can.** The Status at the bottom of a shoot's Plan tab now offers WCR
  beside Hold and Rejected. WCR asks the **Next Followup Date** (not in the past) and its **Remarks**;
  both are saved with the shoot and shown - the tile and the board's row read **"WCR · follow up 20
  Oct 2026"**, and the Plan tab opens on the date and remarks. Setting any other status
  clears the date. WCR holds nothing: the project's Production status goes on from its shoots.
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (`20261014090000_production_wcr_followup`: one nullable
  column on `project_production`).
  [plan.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/plan.js),
  [ProductionPlanStatusField.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionPlanStatusField.js).

- **Projects and Pre Production open a project row to its shoots, as Production does.** The ▸ at the
  start of a project row shows its shoots underneath, one row each. On **Pre Production** a shoot row
  shows its Shoot ID, name and place, date and time, its own status (Planned, Work in Progress, WCR,
  Hold, Rejected) and how much of it is filled, and a double click opens straight to that shoot's
  form. On **Projects** (Project Management) it shows its Shoot ID, name and place, type, date and
  time, session, district and state, and its services and deliverables; a double click or its ⋮
  opens the project, which has no shoot screen of its own. Tick boxes, Update and the row menus stay
  on the projects, and searching, filtering and the tabs still work on projects - a project found
  brings its shoots with it. Sales Manager's register, which shares the Projects table, is unchanged.
  [PreProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionPage.js),
  [ProjectDataTable.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/ProjectDataTable.js).

- **Remarks written in Settings now fill a quotation line's Remarks.** When a service or deliverable
  is added to a quotation, its Remarks from Settings → Project appear in that line's Remarks box,
  ready to edit or clear for that quotation alone - Settings is never changed from the quotation, and
  the next quotation starts from the Settings words again. Saved quotations, drafts and versions keep
  the remarks they were saved with, and the client's copy and PDF print them under the line as before.
  A new deliverable line's name no longer repeats its Settings note, since the note is now its
  editable remark. See [QuotationGeneratorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationGeneratorPanel.js).

- **Quotations can be saved as drafts and finished later.** The Quotation Generator has a **Save
  Draft** button beside **Generate Quotation**: it keeps everything typed so far under a quotation
  number of its own, asking only for the Assigned Branch, and the generator stays open to carry on.
  Saving again updates the same draft; the new **Draft** tab on the Quotations register lists every
  draft, and **Edit** reopens one. **Generate Quotation** then issues it under the same number with
  the usual link and share dialog. A draft is never seen by a client - no link, PDF or payment page -
  cannot be booked as a project, and does not appear under All or the brand tabs until it is
  generated. No new permission and no migration: it uses `SALES / Quotation Management` and the
  existing `sales_quotation.status` column. See
  [QuotationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationPage.js) and
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js).

- **The Visual Curation desktop app can be downloaded from the sidebar.** A download icon sits
  beside the Visual Curation heading, next to its collapse arrow, and opens a dialog offering the
  Windows installer on one card - version, type and size; nothing downloads until **Download for
  Windows** is pressed, and the app's snackbar then says the download started (or that the file is
  missing from where it was published). The installer's address comes from
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_DESKTOP_WINDOWS_URL` (https, `.exe` or `.msi`), with optional
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_DESKTOP_WINDOWS_VERSION` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_DESKTOP_WINDOWS_SIZE_BYTES`, set at build
  time; until it is set the dialog says the app is not published yet and offers no link
  ([DesktopAppDownloadDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/app-shell/DesktopAppDownloadDialog.js),
  [desktopRelease.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/desktopRelease.mjs)). The shared
  [Dialog](../frontend/src/components/ui/Dialog.js) takes an optional `icon` drawn before its
  title. No new permission: the icon is
  shown only to people who already see the Visual Curation section. macOS is not offered — the
  desktop app is built for Windows only.

- **AI Feature Share with guests: the link and the PIN are made for you, the PIN can be switched
  on or off, and both can be replaced on purpose - on the web and in the desktop app.** The event
  link and the PIN are fields with their actions inside them, as Image Selection's Client URL and
  Access PIN are: Event link has Copy, Open and **New link code**; Access PIN has Copy and **Reset
  PIN**. Neither value is ever typed - the server makes them (`PATCH /api/ai-feature/events/:id/share`
  takes only `requirePin`, `newPin` and `newCode`, [share/service.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/share/service.js))
  - and opening or reloading the dialog never changes them. **Require a PIN to open** sits beside
  Access PIN (on by default for a new link) and applies at once: off, the guest join stops asking
  and no PIN is shown, sent or printed; on, the server makes a PIN. New link code draws a fresh unique code after a confirmation that says the old
  link, and any QR or poster printed with it, stop opening; the PIN stays. Reset PIN draws a
  different PIN after a confirmation that guests who have not joined need the new one; the link
  stays. Guests already signed in stay in through either. It all stays in the one Share with guests
  popup, whose footer is now QR Template and Done: the Link and PIN card, the Regenerate button and
  the Revoke link button are gone from it (a link revoked before still shows that, and can be
  generated again). QR Template's Print PIN only chooses whether the PIN is printed, and the
  template re-reads the link when its window regains focus. One reusable field on each side
  ([ActionField.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/ActionField.js), the desktop's
  `components/ui/ActionField.jsx`). No migration; no new permission - these need AI Feature Read /
  Write.
- **QR Template: print an AI Feature event's guest link as a ready-made poster, in one of ten
  designs - on the web and in the desktop app.** Share with guests has a new **QR Template** button
  beside Revoke link. It opens a gallery of ten designs (Ivory Classic, Botanical Green, Black &
  Gold, Soft Geometric, Modern Type, Blush Floral, Navy & Cyan, Warm Editorial, Sage Minimal,
  Midnight Glow) with a live preview; the heading, lines and event name can be edited, the PIN can
  be left off, and every design is the same A1 portrait page (594 × 841 mm): a 7016 × 9933 px PNG
  at 300 dpi or a one-page A1 PDF (150 dpi only on a device that cannot draw the 300 dpi page, and
  the download says so). The QR fills its white card - the card is the code's quiet zone, so the modules are
  about 80% of it, centred, on the previews and in every download alike. The QR is the event's
  real guest link, drawn sharp from the server's own QR grid
  (`GET /api/ai-feature/events/:id/share/poster`, [share/poster.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/share/poster.js));
  the logo is the studio's Global Logo from Settings → Branding Logo, or the app's own mark when
  none is set or it will not load. A revoked or expired link makes no poster. The desktop saves
  into a folder the studio picks, written by a new `save_generated_file` command (PNG/PDF only,
  never over an existing file). The designs are drawn in [qrPoster.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/qrPoster.mjs),
  which the desktop mirrors. Readable by anyone with AI Feature Read - the same people who can
  already open Share; no new permission, no migration. The desktop needs a rebuild for its new
  save command.

- **Every AI Feature event's Project Dashboard now has its own Detection & Storage, and the AI
  Feature no longer shows videos anywhere on its dashboards - on the web and in the desktop app.**
  An event's first tab is renamed **Project Dashboard** (it was Overview) and the module's section
  menu says **Dashboard** (it was Overview); links and remembered tabs open them as before. The
  Project Dashboard keeps its cards, AI processing and Sub events, and adds the Detection & Storage
  panel for that event alone - storage used, faces detected, people, face matches, unmatched faces,
  guests and uploads in the last 24 hours - counted by the server for that event
  (`GET /api/ai-feature/events/:id/detection`, the studio dashboard's own reads given the event id,
  [overview/repository.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/overview/repository.js)), never filtered
  from the studio's totals. Archived events stays on the studio dashboard only. The Videos tile and
  the Videos row are gone; an older event that still holds a video names it as an "other file" on
  the storage line rather than counting it as a photo. Video uploads were already refused by the
  server. The figures are readable by anyone with AI Feature Read, as the studio dashboard's
  already are; no new permission, no migration.

- **Pre Production and Production: set a project's status by hand - one project, or several ticked
  at once.** Each board's project rows take tick boxes, with an **Update** button over the selection
  (no Delete), and each project row's ⋮ gains **Update status** for that one project. Either opens the
  same dialog: **Planned**, **Hold** or **Rejected** (Hold and Rejected ask for remarks; Planned is
  not an exception and asks for none), or **Automatic** - back to being worked out
  from the shoots, which is how a status set
  here is changed or cleared later. Only the project's overall status for that board changes; every
  shoot keeps its own, and the dialog says so. A project you do not run - its Pre Production
  Coordinator, or its Production Manager - is left alone and counted, unless you work every project.
  The reason stays with it: opening a project set by hand on that board shows **"Pre Production
  set to On Hold by … on …"** with the remarks at the top of its panel, and Pre Production's Info panel lists
  them as Status Remarks. Both boards gain a **Rejected** tab. Tick boxes follow the usual `ADMIN / Table Select All`;
  setting the status needs the board's own Read / Write. **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`
  (`20261013180000_project_department_status`: eight nullable columns on `sales_project`).
  [DepartmentStatusDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/DepartmentStatusDialog.js),
  [departmentStatus.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/departmentStatus.js).

- **Accounts Manager now shows what projects are due to pay: Due, Overdue and On Hold.** A project's
  Schedule Payment is now **saved** - until now the rows on Create Project and Start / Edit Project
  lived only in the open form and were lost when it closed. Accounts Manager's status bar gains three
  tabs after All / Received / Spent: **Due** (within five days of its date), **Overdue** and
  **On Hold**, listing those payments; any other payment is **Active**, and so is a project's Accounts
  status when none of its payments is held, overdue or due. A double click reads one in the usual read-only view, as a cash entry is read: its
  project, and the due date, due amount and remarks.
  The row's ⋮ offers **View** (the same read) and **Record**, which opens it to work: a Status - **Clear** opens Cash Received with the project and the pending amount
  filled in and links the receipt to the payment - it then sits under Received; **Partially paid**
  asks the amount paid, shows what is left and needs the date that rest is due, then records the paid
  amount the same way - the paid part is under Received and the rest is a payment of its own, **Due**
  until that date passes; **On Hold** asks remarks and puts **On Hold (Accounts)** beside the
  project's name everywhere, and the project's Accounts status reads Hold. Beside every panel title
  on the project - Start / Edit Project, Pre Production, Production, the Projects list - a project
  owed money now reads **Overdue (Accounts)** (red) or **Due (Accounts)** (amber); Overdue when it has
  both, nothing once Delivered. Re-saving a project never
  changes a payment Accounts has already worked.
  No new permission: the tabs are Accounts Manager's own (`ACCOUNTS / Cash Management` - Read to see
  them, Read / Write to work a payment), the permission that already records the cash that clears it.
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (`20261014120000_drop_payment_followup` drops the four
  follow-up columns the first version added, unused now; `20261013170000_project_payment_schedule`: two new tables,
  one nullable column on `cash_entry`). It stops before changing anything if a table
  of either name already exists. Schedules typed before this release were never stored and are not
  carried over. Payment schedule categories in use can no longer be deleted in Field Settings, and a
  rename follows into saved schedules.
  [AccountsManagerPage.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/AccountsManagerPage.js),
  [ScheduledPaymentPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/ScheduledPaymentPanel.js),
  [scheduled-payments/](../backend/src/modules/accounts/scheduled-payments/),
  [paymentSchedule.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/paymentSchedule.js).

- **Production's Plan tab opens on the project and shoot as already known, as Pre Production's form
  does.** A read-only **Project & Shoot** section at the top of the Plan: the project (Event ID,
  client and number, vertical, main event date, CRM, Project Manager, Pre Production Coordinator,
  Creative Manager, Production Manager) and the shoot (ID, type, date, time, session, place, district,
  state, who pays travel and accommodation), side by side. Nothing here is edited; each value is
  changed where it is owned. Same permission as the shoot (PROJECT / Production at Read).
  [ProductionContextSummary.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionContextSummary.js),
  [read.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/read.js) `contextSummary`.

- **Customer Issues and Feedback: give feedback to several at once.** On Yet to be done, somebody who
  may give feedback can tick the projects and shoots waiting for it and press **Give Feedback (n)**:
  one Review, its Assign to for Average or Poor, and one Feedback, given to each. Each is saved as its
  own feedback through the same request as Give Feedback - its own checks, version and task - one at
  a time, counting up; any refused stays ticked and the popup stays open with the reason and what was
  typed. Who was appreciated or not on a shoot belongs to that shoot, so it is given one by one as
  before. The ticked rows offer Give Feedback alone - no Export; the table's own Export stays. Tick
  boxes need `ADMIN / Table Select All`, as every table's do. No new endpoint, no
  permission changes.

- **Experience and employment certificates can be generated from the Employee Repository.** In
  Administration, the ⋮ of anybody **Active** (as the Active tab counts them - working, not serving
  notice) has **Generate → Employment Certificate**, which opens straight on the filled certificate
  with Download PDF - nothing is asked. The ⋮ of anybody **InActive** (Relieved, Absconded, Long
  Leave, Fired) or **Serving Notice** has **Generate → Experience Certificate**. It asks for a brief summary of their duties (optional - left empty, the duties line is left out of the certificate), then shows the
  filled certificate on an A4 sheet with **Download PDF**: **Mr.** or **Ms.** by their gender, their
  name, designation, department, date of joining and last working date from their record, the duties
  as typed, and the e-signature, signatory and note set in Settings → Employee → Certificate →
  Experience. Each certificate takes its signatory and note from its own Settings section. Nothing
  is stored. Behind `HRM / Employee Management` Read / Write, for employees the user may change - the
  same as the rest of that ⋮. New `POST /api/hrm/employees/:id/certificates/:kind` (and `/pdf`),
  `:kind` being `experience` or `employment`. [EmployeeCertificateDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeCertificateDialog.js),
  [certificates.controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/employees/certificates.controller.js).
- **Settings → Employee → Certificate → Experience shows the experience certificate on an A4 sheet.**
  Like the Payslip's preview, it carries the company logo, name and head-office address the payslip
  uses, with the employee's details as bracketed blanks for now. Above the sheet: **E-Signature**,
  an image upload printed above the authorised signatory; below it, the **Authorized Signatory Name**
  and **Designation**, typed and printed under the signature (blank prints the bracketed blank); and
  a **Note**, printed at the end of the certificate. The sheet follows both as they are edited; **Save** keeps them. Administrators only.
  **Employment** is the same - its own E-Signature, signatory, note and A4 preview - with the
  employment certificate's wording ("...is currently employed with [Company Name], located in
  [Company Location], as a [Designation] in the [Department] since [Date of Joining]... issued upon
  the employee's request for official purposes"); the experience certificate opens "...was employed
  with [Company Name], located in [Company Location], as a... from [Date of Joining] to [Last Working
  Date]". The location is the city of the employee's branch (the head office's where it has none), generated from the Employee Repository for somebody Active. Migration `20261013150000_certificate_settings`
  adds the eight nullable `hrm_settings` columns, four per certificate
  (`experience_certificate_*`, `employment_certificate_*`: signature URL, note, signatory name and
  designation). New `/api/settings/certificates` (administrators only). **Deploy:** stop the API, run
  `npx prisma migrate deploy` and `npx prisma generate`, then start it again.
  [ExperienceCertificatePanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/ExperienceCertificatePanel.js),
  [experienceCertificate.js](../backend/src/services/experienceCertificate.js),
  [certificates controller](../backend/src/modules/settings/certificates/controller.js).
- **Settings → Employee has a Certificate group: Experience, Employment and Offer Letter.** It sits
  after Payroll rules and before Wishes and is shown to administrators only. Each of its three
  sections is empty for now ("Experience certificate settings will appear here.") - their settings
  are added next. No permission changed.
  [CertificateSettingsPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/CertificateSettingsPanel.js),
  [SettingsOverlay.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/SettingsOverlay.js).
- **Attendance → Dashboard: a Work Mode column.** The employee table shows how each person worked -
  Office, Work from home, Field work or Flexible Shift - right after Check In: the latest day in the
  range that says, the day itself over one day, as the location links are; a dash where nothing was
  marked. The overview's employee rows carry it as `workMode`. No permission changes.

- **Import rows with errors: a cell the old sheet got wrong comes in empty instead of costing the whole
  row.** A new tick in the Pre Production import dialog. A decade of typing leaves cells no import can
  read - a location pasted into Shoot Date, "Finished" in Project Status, "two" in Session Hours - and
  one of them used to throw the entire row away. Ticked, the import **empties only the cells it cannot
  read**, brings the row in as the file wrote the rest, and lists in the summary which columns were
  emptied, by row, so they can be filled in on the board. The seven a record cannot do without - Event
  ID, Client Name, Branch, Shoot ID and Shoot Name - can never be emptied, so a row missing one is
  still refused and says which. Unticked, nothing changes.

  The option lives in the import every module shares, so any table's import can offer it. Two things
  the old sheet does are now read rather than refused whether or not it is ticked: a **Client Number
  cell holding two numbers** ("9443634232 / 9876543210") gives the first, since a project holds one;
  and a booking with **several shoots of one name** (three "Rituals") pairs its sheet rows with its
  shoots one for one - the Shoot Date picks one where it says so, else one with no date of its own, else
  the first not yet linked - instead of refusing those rows as ambiguous. A cell holding two numbers
  reads each in turn and takes the first it can read.
  [tableImport.js](../backend/src/services/tableImport.js),
  [import.service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/import.service.js),
  [ImportDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/ImportDialog.js).

- **Pre Production → Import takes the booking's gifts, sales remarks, validity, client storage and its
  own date: ten columns at the end of every template.** They belong to the **booking** rather than to
  the shoot each row carries, which is why they sit at the end; one booking's rows all repeat them.

  **Welcome Gift** and **Shoot Completed Gift** take `Applicable` or `Not Applicable` (read whatever
  the case, and a plain Yes / No too), each with an **Assignee Employee Code** read like every other
  people cell - a code, a login or the name as HRM has it, and somebody who has left kept by name. A
  gift carries its tracking with it, through the General panel's own rule: Applicable with no status
  yet becomes **Yet To Sent**, which is what puts it on the Client Gifts tab, and Not Applicable clears
  the status, the dates and the assignee - so a sheet saying "no gift" cannot leave somebody named on
  one nobody is giving. **Sales Pre Production**, **Sales Production** and **Sales Post Production
  Remarks** are the sales note each stage reads on the project, **Project Validity (In Months)** a
  whole number of months, and **Storage Needed** `Yes` or `No`. All of these are the studio's own
  answers, so on a project already in the app only one it has not given is filled in; the sheet never
  overrules a studio that has since said otherwise.

  **Storage Needed = Yes raises the project's Client Storage record**, through the same call a project
  starting in the app makes: the register numbers it and links it to the project and its earliest
  shoot, so an imported disc and one booked here are the same record. **Received The Storage** = Yes
  then marks that record **Delivered**, the end of the register's flow, written straight rather than
  walked through the eight moves in between - the sheet is the record of a disc already seen through,
  and those moves never happened in the app, so the record carries no hand-in, backup or transit
  detail. Delivered only where the register would let a disc rest there: a project with a shoot still
  to come sends a delivered disc back round for that shoot, so its record stays at Yet to Receive. A
  record the studio has already moved on, or removed with a reason, is left exactly as it is.

- **Pre Production → Import takes the booking's own date: a Date Created column at the end of every
  template.** The day the booking was made, as the studio's old sheet has it, written to the project's
  own date - the one every "newest first" list sorts by - so an imported booking sits where it belongs
  instead of on the day the file was uploaded. The same date goes on every row of one booking, like its
  Event ID and client name, which is why the column sits at the end rather than among the shoot's. It
  is taken on a project the file creates **and** on one already in the app, because nothing in the app
  edits that date; left empty, the project keeps the date it has. Read like every other date -
  DD-MM-YYYY, or the day first with the month by name ("6 Sept 2026") - and a placeholder (WCR, N/A,
  IN OLD SHEET) comes in empty. A date after today is refused, since a mistyped year would file the
  project ahead of every live one where nothing in the app can correct it. No migration, no permission
  change.
  [importColumns.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/importColumns.js),
  [import.service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/import.service.js).

### Removed

- **The Sl. No. column is gone from every table.** Accounts Manager, Payment Requests, Tasks,
  Interviews, Speak Up and Employee Reviews no longer have it. Employees and Attendance had already
  dropped it. A row number renumbers itself whenever a table is sorted or filtered, so it never
  pointed to the same record twice; each record's own ID is the number to quote. The shared column
  builder no longer makes one.
  [tableCells.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/tableCells.js).

- **An AI Feature event's Sub Events tab no longer shows the "No sub events yet." panel when it is
  empty - on the web and in the desktop app.** The heading, the "Split the event into its
  ceremonies..." line and the "Add the first one" button are gone
  ([SubEventsTab.js](../frontend/src/components/ai-feature/event/tabs/SubEventsTab.js)); an empty
  tab shows only its count and **+ Add Sub Event**, which adds the first one as before. The tab,
  adding, editing, reordering and removing sub-events, and every record are unchanged.

- **AI Editing no longer says "In Photo Selection" or "Sent to Photo Selection" anywhere - not
  under a tile, not under the photo in the editor, on the web or in the desktop app.** AI Editing
  and Photo Selection are separate workspaces with no link between them on this tab, so the line
  under a photo now names the one place it can be sent from here - "Sent to Signature Album" - and
  nothing else; the file name, the Not edited / Edited status, the preview and the tick are as they
  were. The server's own `inPhotoSelection` and `sentToPhotos` fields stay as they are (the gallery's
  listing rule, now read from one shared helper beside `cullEligible` instead of a copy), and no
  record, relationship or transfer changed. The desktop's AI Culling "Send photos" dialog no longer
  says that photos sent to AI Editing "go on to Photo Selection from there", and names Photo
  Selection as the one way in.
  [imageSelectionEditing.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/imageSelectionEditing.mjs),
  [editingState.js](../../Image-Selection_Desktop---BCT/src/modules/image-selection/editing/editingState.js),
  [gallery/repository.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/gallery/repository.js),
  [sendPlan.js](../../Image-Selection_Desktop---BCT/src/modules/image-selection/culling/sendPlan.js).

- **AI Editing no longer sends photos to Photo Selection - its one way on is the Signature
  Album.** The "Send to Photo Selection" button is gone from the editor and from the bay's bulk
  bar on the web and in the desktop app, the service calls are gone, and the server no longer
  mounts `POST .../ai-editing/send-to-photo-selection`. Photo Selection is filled by AI Culling's
  send of a finalized run's Keeps, which is unchanged (it still runs through the editing service's
  own function, so an edited Keep is compressed as before); nothing in AI Editing - a save, a
  render, a desktop hand-over, a reset - moves a photo into Photo Selection on its own, and that
  was checked. Roles that could send there from AI Editing needed Project Management Read / Write;
  no permission changes hands.
  [ai-editing/routes.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-editing/routes.js),
  [SendPhotosActions.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/SendPhotosActions.js),
  [ai-editing.service.js](../frontend/src/services/image-selection/ai-editing.service.js),
  [SendPhotosActions.jsx](../../Image-Selection_Desktop---BCT/src/modules/image-selection/SendPhotosActions.jsx).

- **HRM → Payroll: no Payslip section.** The empty Payslip entry in the Payroll page's section menu is
  gone - Main Page, Advance Salary and Recovery remain, each on its own permission; an employee's own
  payslips stay in My Profile → Payslip. A login holding none of the three is told it has no Payroll
  section to open. No permission changes.

- **Payroll → Main Page: no Export or Delete over ticked rows.** Ticking rows now offers Mark Paid
  alone; the table's own Export (the whole month) stays. `DataTable`'s `selection` takes a new
  `exportable: false` to leave Export off a selection - on by default, so every other table is as it
  was. The register's bulk-delete endpoint is unchanged and still guarded. No permission changes.

- **Payroll → Main Page: no Cost Centre column.** The column and its in-cell picker are gone from
  the register; a row's Cost Centre is still chosen in its edit form (from every branch) and still
  prints on the payslip. Nothing stored changes. No permission changes.

- **Prior Month Adjustment is gone from Payroll → Main Page.** No Adjustments button or dialog, no
  Prior Month Adjustment column, and no line on the payslip or in Edit Payslip; Net Salary is Total
  Earned less Total Deductions. Late changes to a closed month are no longer rechecked. The
  `/api/hrm/payroll-register/adjustments` routes and `adjustments.js` are removed, and migration
  `20261012320000_drop_prior_adjustment` drops `payroll_adjustment` and `payroll_entry`'s
  `prior_adjustment` and `late_changes_tracked` - **any pending or approved adjustment on the server
  is discarded** when it is deployed. No permission changes.

- **Service lines no longer show a Size on any Service Creation screen** - the Quotation Generator,
  Create Project (Bookings), Edit Sale Details (Converted) and Start Project. A service is priced at
  its one Settings Price, so a line's size decided nothing; Services and Remarks take the freed
  width. A size a line already holds is kept, saved and shown nowhere new; nothing is cleared and
  no default is set. A deliverable line's Size is its own field and stays. No backend or database
  change.
  [ProjectServiceCreationSection.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectServiceCreationSection.js).

- **The Quotation Generator, Create Project (Bookings) and Edit Sale Details (Converted) no longer
  show a Session Timing column on their service lines.** A service is priced at its one Settings
  Price, so the session decided nothing there; the lines now read Services, Quantity, Size, Remarks
  (and Complimentary on a quotation) with Remove, priced and totalled as before. Each new line still
  starts on its shoot's session and saves it, so stored allocations, conversion and everything that
  reads the session are unchanged, and saved quotations and projects open as they were. An hourly
  service's hours and minutes, which shared that column, are no longer edited on these three screens.
  Project Management's Start Project keeps the column. No backend or database change.
  [ProjectServiceCreationSection.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectServiceCreationSection.js)
  (`sessionTimingColumn`).

- **Settings → Project → Services no longer asks Shoot Type, Session Timing, Duration or Size; a
  service has one Price, quoted on every shoot.** The four columns, their filters and sorting, the
  pricing rows folded under each service, the dialog's pricing-line editor and its "Size (Wall or TV
  etc...)" question are gone; Services, Price, Deliverable Added, Complimentary, Remarks and Edit /
  Duplicate / Delete stay. The Quotation Generator now stamps a service's single Price on whatever
  shoot it is added to, and changing a line's Session Timing or a shoot's type or session no longer
  reprices it; the CRM Quotation Calculator lists each service as one line at that price. A service
  that was priced only per session (360 PhotoBooth, for example) shows Price "—" and quotes ₹0 with
  "Not priced in Settings" until its Price is entered once. **Deliverable Added now maps one list of
  deliverables per service**, brought in whenever the service is added to a shoot whatever its
  session; a service whose mapping rode on its pricing lines reads as every variant those lines
  named until it is next saved. Saved quotations keep the prices they were stamped with, and every
  service keeps its id. Nothing is deleted: each service's stored pricing lines, timings, shoot
  types, durations and size answer stay in the database untouched (an edit no longer sends them;
  Duplicate still copies them), and Edit Shoot, Production and the project screens are unchanged.
  **Migration** `20261009120000_service_deliverables` adds one nullable JSON column,
  `project_service_definition.deliverables`; no row is written. No permission change — the endpoints
  stay behind `PROJECT / Projects`. Calculator drafts saved against a per-session line reopen with
  that service's option to pick again.
  [ServiceDefinitionDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ServiceDefinitionDialog.js),
  [ProjectSettingsPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectSettingsPanel.js),
  [QuotationGeneratorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationGeneratorPanel.js),
  [servicePricing.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/servicePricing.mjs),
  [projects/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js),
  [quotation-calculator/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/quotation-calculator/controller.js).

- **Customer Issues and Feedback asks only for the New Project Feedback.** Every project created in
  Bookings & Converted (Create Project) still waits on Yet to be done until a writer's Give Feedback
  saves its Review and Feedback (an Average or Poor one assigned to somebody as a task). It no longer
  comes back for a Production Completion Feedback once Production completes, or a Project Completed
  Feedback after that: those two forms are gone, with `GET /projects/:projectId/people` under
  `/api/project-management/feedback`, and `POST /` takes only `{ projectId, review, feedback,
  assignees }`. Feedback already given at the removed
  stages stays in the database and is still listed with its stage. No migration and no permission
  change. [service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/feedback/service.js),
  [FeedbackFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackFormPanel.js),
  [project-feedback.test.js](../backend/test/project-feedback.test.js).
- **Daily quotes are gone: nothing is shown after a login any more, and Attendance Rules no longer
  lists them.** The card after Login says only the time (and any outside-office flag). The
  `/api/hrm/attendance/quotes` endpoints are removed; the quotes already recorded stay in the
  database, untouched. [EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/controller.js).
- **The shoot cards on the client page no longer carry the camera picture.** Each card now
  opens straight on the shoot's name, date and status.
  [ProjectTracker.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/ProjectTracker.js).
- **The client page shows the Shoot Completed Gift on Production only.** It no longer appears on
  Pre Production, before the shoot has happened, nor is it repeated on Post Production and
  Delivered; the Welcome Gift stays on Pre Production.
  [projectTracking.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/projectTracking.mjs).
- **The client page's stage card no longer shows the progress ring ("0/1").** The card's header
  carries the stage's state chip instead, and the count stays as the line under the heading
  ("0 of 1 shot so far"). [ProjectTracker.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/ProjectTracker.js).

- **Accounts → ⋮ → Settings and the second bank-account list behind it are gone.** The studio's
  accounts were kept in two places - that list, and the account on each branch - typed by different
  hands, behind different permissions (the panel asked for `HRM / Employee Management`, its rows
  being HRM master data), with nothing to say which was right. The branch register is the only one
  now. The three screens that offered it - **received into** on a cash entry, a payment request and
  a project's advance - read the branch accounts instead, each listed as its bank, the last four
  digits of the number and its branch ("HDFC — Erode · ••••7890 · Erode TN"); open branches only.
  Entries already recorded keep the account name they were saved with, which is text on the record
  by design. The `bank_account` **table and its rows are left untouched**: those rows name no
  branch, so nothing can work out where each belongs, and nothing reads them any more. The Bank
  Account Types list in Field Settings also now has nothing reading it - say the word and it goes
  too. **Who may maintain the accounts has changed with them:** it was `HRM / Employee Management`
  (the retired panel's own gate), and it is now `SETTINGS / Organization`, so anybody in Accounts or
  HR who used to add an account must either hold that or ask whoever does - grant it in Role
  Management if the studio wants them to keep doing it. The "received into" box on an entry says
  where accounts come from when there are none: *Add an account in Settings → Organization →
  Branches*. Reading is unchanged: the three screens keep their own permissions. [AccountsManagerPage.js](../frontend/src/components/accounts/AccountsManagerPage.js),
  [master-data/definitions.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/master-data/definitions.js),
  [branchBankAccounts.js](../backend/src/services/branchBankAccounts.js). No migration.

- **WRC (Waiting for Client Reply) is gone from Pre Production, end to end.** The shoot's own
  toggle, its amber badge on the shoot cards, the board's project-level rollup column, the info
  panels, and the `waitingSince` aging timestamp behind all of it - none of it is asked for, shown
  or saved any more, and both columns are dropped.
  [formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js),
  [PreProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionPage.js),
  [PreProductionProjectPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionProjectPanel.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate`.

- **Number Plate is gone from Pre Production's Dum Dum vertical fields.** It is no longer asked for
  on the shoot form, the API neither returns nor saves it, and its column is dropped rather than
  left unread.
  [preProductionVerticalFields.js](../frontend/src/constants/preProductionVerticalFields.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate`.

### Changed

- **A client sees what their booking includes: its services and deliverables.** New client route
  `GET /api/client/package` answers the booking's shoots in the order they run, each with its services
  (name, how many, the session or hours) and its deliverables (name, how many, photos, size / frame /
  length), as Project Management holds them now - only the client's own booking, and no prices, team
  or remarks. The client app opens them from Services and Deliverables beside the WhatsApp group on
  each booking. ([portal/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/controller.js))
- **A client opens a referral from Your referrals to see where it stands.** The client app's list now
  carries each friend's number (as the client gave it) and what the referral was for (Wedding, Baby /
  kids / family, Corporate event), for a detail sheet: who, the shoot, when, and Sent -> Studio in touch
  -> Booked (or Closed), with the coins it earned. A friend referred for several kinds of shoot - a
  lead a kind in the CRM - is listed once, each kind with its shoots and where it stands, as far as
  their furthest kind. Nothing the studio wrote on the lead is sent.
  ([portal/referrals.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/referrals.js))
- **A client's referral names the shoots their friend is planning - of one kind or several.** The
  client app offers Wedding, Baby / Kids and Corporate to tick, as many as apply, each with that
  brand's own shoots - Settings -> Fields -> Shoot Types, the list the CRM's Add Lead and the Quotation
  Generator use. A lead belongs to one vertical, so a referral for more than one kind is filed as one
  lead a kind, each with its own "Type of Event Planned" (the shoots named, "Bride Haldi, Groom Haldi",
  or the kind when none is). A kind the friend is already in touch with the studio about is left out
  and the client told; the others are still filed. A shoot not on its brand's list is dropped. An app
  sending the single `kind` it did before is still read. ([portal/referrals.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/referrals.js))
- **Client Offers lists offers as a compact table, not large poster cards.** One slim row an offer -
  a small thumbnail at the poster's own shape, its size, its dates, its status and Edit / Remove - so
  twenty offers fit where three used to; clicking a thumbnail opens the poster full size. Home offers
  and Referral offers alike; two lines a row on a narrow screen.
  ([ClientOffersPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/ClientOffersPage.js))
- **Client Offers: the poster's size is chosen, and a poster of another size is resized to it.**
  Square (1080 x 1080), Portrait (1080 x 1350) and Story (1080 x 1920) are now buttons. A poster
  already one of them goes as it is; any other - the earlier 1200 x 675 posters among them - is no
  longer refused but resized in the browser to the chosen size, either fitted whole (the space around
  it filled with a soft blurred copy of the poster) or filling the frame with its edges cropped, and
  the preview shows exactly what clients will see. Referral offers are different: the client app shows
  them as a wide banner at the top of Referrals, so a referral offer takes any image size, as it is,
  with nothing to choose. ([ClientOffersPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/ClientOffersPage.js),
  [client-offers/service.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/client-offers/service.js))
- **A production plan's services now sit under People.** Each service, with its Person, Assistants
  and Camera, follows the Production Coordinator in the People section, since together they are
  the shoot's production team. Services is no longer a section of its own. Nothing else about them
  changed.
  [productionFormConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/productionFormConfig.js).

- **Pre Production's and Production's Follow-up tab is now "Waiting for Client".** It is the same
  tab with a clearer name: every project with a shoot on WCR, which is waiting for the client's
  reply. Someone who had it open last time lands on All once, then picks it again.
  [PreProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionPage.js),
  [productionBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionBoard.mjs).

- **A shoot's Execution opens three days before the shoot, not as soon as its plan is submitted.**
  On Production, the Execution tab now stays shut until both are true: the plan is submitted and the
  shoot is three days away. Until then it says the date it opens on, for example "The steps open on
  17 Oct 2026, three days before the shoot." The server refuses a step, a shoot status or a step's
  photo the same way. A shoot with no date opens on its plan alone, and one whose day has already
  begun stays open. Tickets are not affected.
  [steps.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/steps.js),
  [ProductionExecutionTab.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionExecutionTab.js).

- **Pre Production's and Production's ⋮ now read Edit and Update status.** On a project row, ⋮
  offers **Edit**, which opens the project's shoots (it was "Update" on Pre Production and "Open"
  on Production), and **Update status** for its overall status. A shoot row's ⋮ offers **Edit**
  (it was "Open"). Someone who may only read sees **View** in place of Edit, and no Update status.
  [PreProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionPage.js),
  [ProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionPage.js).

- **Pre Production and Production panels are titled by the project, with the board and the ID
  beneath.** A shoot's form now carries the project's name as its title. Underneath it reads
  "Pre Production | *Shoot ID* · shoot · date" or "Production | *Shoot ID* · shoot · date". A
  project's panel on either board reads "Pre Production | *Event ID* · …" or "Production | *Event ID*
  · …" under the name. Before, a shoot's form was titled with its Shoot ID and shoot name, and the
  project's name sat underneath.
  [PreProductionFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionFormPanel.js),
  [ProductionShootPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionShootPanel.js).

- **A production plan no longer has a Production Team field; the team is the people on the
  services.** A shoot's production team is its Production Coordinator plus whoever is assigned to
  each service (Person and Assistants), so the separate Production Team picker is gone from the Plan
  tab, and the plan no longer counts it towards complete. A service's Person and Assistants offer
  employees and only the vendors marked **Can be a production team member? Yes** (Asset Management →
  Vendors → Capabilities); the server refuses any other vendor newly added, and one already on a
  service stays. A team named on older plans, or from the imported sheet, stays on record and still
  lets those people run the shoot's steps; it is just no longer edited.
  [productionPlan.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionPlan.mjs),
  [plan.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/plan.js),
  [planCompleteness.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/planCompleteness.js).

- **A project's Overall Status tab now follows a Pre Production or Production status set by hand.**
  When someone sets the overall status from Update status on either board, the matching stage on
  the Overall Status tab shows it, with who set it, when and any remarks. **Planned** set on Pre
  Production marks the Pre Production stage done even before every production plan is submitted.
  **Planned** set on Production is shown but doesn't finish Production, which still needs the shoots
  to be shot. **Hold** and **Rejected** show on their stage. It changes only the overall status:
  every shoot keeps its own. The reverse now holds too: the project's own status no longer finishes
  those stages. Before, setting a project Completed or Delivered, or the old Work in Progress - Post
  Production, marked Pre Production and Production done on this tab whatever their own status said.
  Each level is now independent: the project's status, the overall Pre Production and Production
  statuses, and the shoots.
  [stage.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/stage.js),
  [ProjectStageView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectStageView.js).

- **A Pre Production shoot now starts at Yet to Start, as a Production shoot does.** It reads Yet to
  Start until someone fills a Pre Production detail, then Work in Progress, then Planned once every
  detail is filled. The event start and end times that come over from the sale don't count as work
  started. A project's Pre Production status now rolls up from its shoots the same way Production's
  does:
  - **Yet to Start** when every shoot is Yet to Start
  - **Planned** when every shoot is Planned
  - **Work in Progress** otherwise, including whenever any shoot is in Work in Progress
  Before, an untouched shoot read Work in Progress. A project whose shoots carried only the sale's
  event times also read Work in Progress before anyone had worked on it. Hold, and a status set by
  hand, still come first.
  [preProductionProgress.js](../frontend/src/lib/preProductionProgress.js).

- **Accounts Manager's column filters offer a tick-list only where it makes sense.** Type,
  Category, Branch, Payment Mode, Received Account, Paid From Account and Received / Paid By still
  filter by ticking values. Every other column - Entry ID, Client Name, Event ID, Shoot ID, Amount,
  Transaction ID, Payment To, Employee ID, remarks and Description - now takes typed text, and Date
  keeps its date picker. Before, any column with 40 or fewer different values on the page became a
  tick-list, which on a short cash book was nearly all of them. Other tables keep their current
  filters; a table can now name its tick-list columns through `listFilters`.
  [accountsConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/accountsConfig.js),
  [tableCells.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/tableCells.js).

- **A project's status is now one of five: Yet to Start, In Progress, Completed, On Hold and
  Rejected.** They are all the bulk Update offers, and the Projects page has one tab for each.
  Start Project now sets In Progress, and a Pre Production sheet import brings rows in as In Progress.
  Existing projects keep the status they have - nothing is rewritten - and a project on an old
  status (Delivered, Work in Progress - Pre & Production, Cancelled & Refunded...) is listed under
  All only, until someone gives it one of the five. Behind the scenes Work in Progress still counts
  as In Progress and Delivered as Completed, for the status colours, the hold and payment badges,
  Overall Feedback, Image Selection and an employee's handover.
  [projectStatuses.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/projectStatuses.mjs),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js).

- **A quotation's discount is capped at 15%, and the client never sees the percentage.** In the
  Quotation Generator the Discount can come to at most 15% of the service and performance cost
  (e.g. ₹19,381 of ₹1,29,204). Typing more shows the limit in red, applies no more than 15% to the
  total, and refuses Save Draft and Generate Quotation until it is lowered. Extra Discounts (a Diwali
  offer, a management concession) are not held to the 15% and can sit beside a full 15% discount -
  only, as before, never taking the total below ₹0. The API refuses the same on every save, whatever sends it, and the CRM Quotation
  Calculator now offers 0-15%. The client's quotation link, its PDF and print now show
  **Discount - ₹19,381** with no percentage, and the link's data no longer carries one. Quotations
  already saved above 15% are left exactly as they are; editing one asks for the discount to be
  lowered first. See [quotationDiscount.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/quotationDiscount.mjs) and
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js).

- **The expiry countdown and Download button on a client's quotation read in a deeper gold.** The "Expires in" chip in
  the bottom-right corner of the quotation link keeps its gold box, but its words and clock are now
  the darker gold the page already uses, so the time left is easy to read. The Download button's
  arrow at the top right takes the same darker gold. See
  [PublicQuotationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/PublicQuotationPage.js).

- **AI Feature Create Event: the Media / AI step asks only what a studio needs to decide - photos
  only, always compressed, no originals kept - on the web and in the desktop app.** The step (and an
  event's own Settings, which draw the same form) no longer shows the face-matching thresholds
  (minimum face quality, high / medium similarity, same-person threshold), the medium / low
  confidence actions or the cosine-similarity note, nor Video upload, Keep original files or the
  Compression block. Face matching is unchanged: each new event still takes its thresholds from
  the studio defaults ([settingsDefaults.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/shared/settingsDefaults.js) - 0.35 / 0.62 / 0.48 / 0.55,
  medium to the review queue, low hidden, or the studio's own values under Event Default Settings
  → Face Matching), and an existing event keeps the values it saved. Uploads are now **photos
  only**: the web and desktop pickers offer photos, a video dropped in is listed as skipped, and the
  server refuses one with a 415 before storing anything ([media/service.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/media/service.js)).
  The event's Media tab no longer has the Photos and videos / Photos / Videos filter
  ([MediaTab.js](../frontend/src/components/ai-feature/event/tabs/MediaTab.js), and the desktop's):
  a folder lists everything in it, an older event's video rows included, and the upload area says
  "Photos only (JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC)".
  **No original is ever stored**: only the compressed preview and thumbnail reach R2, whatever an
  older event saved, and a photo that cannot be read fails with nothing stored rather than being
  filed whole. Compression has no off switch any more (also gone from Event Default Settings →
  Media Upload and Visual Curation Settings → Compression); the presets stay where they were.
  `videoUpload`, `keepOriginals` and `compressionEnabled` are dropped on read, not rewritten in the
  database; videos and originals uploaded before this are still listed, served and deletable. No
  migration, no new permission.

- **On a shoot folder (a root folder such as "wedding"), AI Culling's setup no longer shows the
  AI culling mode cards - Assisted, Balanced, Strict and Target count; a card folder inside it
  still does.** Everything above them, "Analyze on this computer" in the desktop app and Start AI
  Culling stay where they were, and a run started there uses the mode the screen already holds
  (Assisted). Web ([CullingWorkspace.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/culling/CullingWorkspace.js),
  told by the project workspace that the folder has no parent) and desktop alike; the modes, the
  engine and the server are unchanged.

- **AI Culling no longer shows a "People in these photos" section or asks who each person is: a
  photo is judged on how its people look in it, not on who they are.** The section, with its role
  dropdowns, is gone from the Photo Culling tab on the web and in the desktop app (the strip, the
  desktop face avatar and both apps' people loaders were deleted; the client gallery's People
  filter is untouched). Underneath, the subject stage
  ([analysis/subjects.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/analysis/subjects.js))
  stopped reading the person's role and how often they were photographed: the main subject is the
  largest, most central face in the frame, each face's open eyes count by that prominence, "Main
  face's eyes closed" (formerly "Important person blinked") is raised only when a prominent face
  blinks, and "Clear main subject" (formerly "Important people present") when the frame has one -
  so the Keeps coverage line's "key people" now counts frames with a clear subject. The reason
  codes keep their names, so learned photographer preferences carry over unchanged; duplicate and
  burst ranking, finalizing and sending to AI Editing are untouched. Nothing was dropped from the
  database: roles already stored stay on `image_selection_face_person.role`, and
  `PATCH …/ai-culling/people/:personId` still accepts one from an older desktop build, but no run
  reads it. Runs already finished keep their scores until they are re-run. No permission changed.

- **AI Culling's review and AI Editing's bay are one continuous gallery - no more Previous / Next.**
  The first batch loads, the next appends as you near the end, until every photo is shown ("All 154
  photos shown"); a failed batch says why with Retry. Both apps share one hook over the existing paged
  endpoints ([useIncrementalPages](../frontend/src/components/shared/useIncrementalPages.js), driven by
  the existing `useInfiniteScroll` sentinel on the pane that actually scrolls): a batch at a time,
  cards keyed by id so an overlapping or retried batch never draws one twice, and an answer to an
  older folder, search, filter or sort dropped. Filters, scenes, sorts and search stay the server's,
  over the whole run or bay. A Keep / Maybe / Reject lands on its card in place, polling and changes
  re-read what is loaded in place (never back to the top), and ticks survive every batch ("Select all
  on page" is now "Select all loaded"). In the editor, Right off the last loaded photo loads the next
  batch and moves on, End loads the rest and opens the last photo, and leaving the editor puts the bay
  back where it was scrolled. Tiles keep their lazy-loaded thumbnails; no original is fetched. The AI
  Editing list now breaks sort ties by id, so no photo repeats or goes missing between batches.
- **AI Culling's Send Photos sends every Keep with no count, and "AI Editing + Signature Album"
  keeps the album up to date with each saved edit, individually or in bulk.** The dialog lost its
  count fields: every photo a finalized run kept goes, in the run's order, read by the server from
  the run itself, and the line above Send says how many and where. The standalone Signature Album
  destination there is now **AI Editing + Signature Album**: the Keeps join the editing bay enrolled
  for automatic album sync (`image_selection_edit.album_sync_at`) and are placed in the album now -
  as the album's own copies from the originals on the desktop, by reference on the web. From then on
  every render that saves - Apply, Apply to selected, Apply to all, on the server or rendered on the
  desktop from the original - queues one `album-sync` job per edit version on the AI Editing queue
  ([service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-editing/service.js) `syncToAlbum`): the
  saved master is compressed to the studio's Signature Album preset and written into the photo's ONE
  album copy (`signatureAlbum.service.syncEditedCopy`) - the by-reference entry swapped in place
  (same item, chapter, order, favourite and framing), an existing copy updated in place, never a
  second entry. Unsaved changes, renders in flight, failed renders and photos never edited leave the
  album as it is. Syncs retry on the queue, are recovered at start, and record why one gave up
  (`album_sync_error`); the editor says where each photo stands ("Signature Album: updating…", "In
  the Signature Album - this edit", "…update failed" with Retry, `POST …/ai-editing/album-sync/retry`).
  Enrolling needs the Signature Album's write permission as well as AI Editing's; the web's keeps row
  offers the same combined send. The AI Culling header's expand icon is removed too (the review no
  longer has a full-width toggle). Migration `20261015090000_ai_editing_album_sync` (two nullable
  columns); no permission changes. Photos sent to AI Editing alone, and manual Send to Signature
  Album of photos not enrolled, behave as before.
- **AI Culling sends photos on only from a finalized run, and the desktop's Send Photos makes the
  Signature Album's own copies with the album's compression.** Every send out of AI Culling - to AI
  Editing, Photo Selection or the Signature Album, the run's Keeps or photos ticked in its review -
  is refused by the server (409 `notFinalized`) until the run is finalized, through one rule
  ([finalizedKeeps.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/finalizedKeeps.js)); both
  apps hold the buttons with the reason beside them, and a photo still held for culling is no
  longer added to the AI Editing bay (`notCulled`). On the desktop the Signature Album now gets
  copies compressed from each original on the workstation with the studio's **Signature Album**
  preset (the album's own uploader's recipe), not Photo Selection's previews: the server lists what
  still needs a copy (`POST /signature-albums/projects/:projectId/import/plan`), the desktop finds
  each original with its one resolver, the transfer queue compresses it and uploads only the
  thumbnail and preview, tagged with the photo it was made from - one copy per photo per album
  (`signature_album_photo.source_upload_id`, unique per album), so a retry or a second send stores
  nothing twice and answers 200 with the copy already there. An original the workstation cannot
  open is reported by name and never replaced by a preview. The web, which cannot read originals,
  still adds the photos by reference and says so. The Send Photos dialog lost the paragraphs under
  each destination; its counts are compact fields on the title's line, checked from 1 to the run's
  kept count, and the line under them names what will go or which count is wrong. Both culling
  import routes now also need AI Culling's permission (`IMAGE_SELECTION / Project Management`,
  READ) besides the album's. A failed send in the desktop dialog now says why instead of throwing.
  Migration `20261014090000_signature_album_photo_source` (additive, nullable column + unique
  index); no permission changes.

  measures), the photo centred in it, so neither the compare mode nor a portrait or landscape photo
  moves the "3 of 20" row or the action bar under it - they used to follow each frame's own height.
  The Previous / Next buttons and the "3 of 20" counter moved from above the photo to directly

  move between photos. Auto Edit and the style no longer scroll away: only the sections below
  them scroll. AI tools, Retouching and Basic adjustments each have a switch in their header,
  showing on, off or a partial state read off the photo's own recipe: AI tools and Retouching switch
  every tool this server can run on (each kept at its settings if it was on, else its defaults) or

  hands every exposure and white-balance slider left at 0 to the AI (Auto) and back - it never

  their own sliders. Each switch changes only its own section, saves like any slider and never opens
  or shuts its fold. The desktop's Retouching fold now opens on its own only when a photo arrives
  with a region on, as the web's always has.

- **Originals are never quietly replaced by previews: a web Apply in AI Editing on a photo the
  desktop app added now waits for that app - or asks before rendering from the 1600px preview - a
  culling run marks a photo the workstation could not open instead of measuring its preview, and the
  retired chunked original uploader is gone.** The desktop records each original's BLAKE3 checksum
  beside its size when it adds a photo (`source_checksum`; a stored size of 0 now means "unknown" and
  goes out as `null`) and verifies the file against both before any local analysis or edit.
  `POST …/ai-editing/photos/:uploadId/render` and `/batch-apply` take `source: "desktop" | "preview"`
  (default desktop): a desktop-registered photo becomes `WAITING_FOR_DESKTOP` when
  `DESKTOP_AI_ENABLED` is on (the desktop drains `GET …/ai-editing/pending`), answers 409
  `requiresSourceChoice` when it is off, and renders from the preview only on an explicit
  `source: "preview"`; `POST …/photos/:uploadId/local-source` fails an edit with a named state
  (`LOCAL_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` / `_CHANGED` / `_UNREADABLE`, `error_code`) and the studio's words
  (desktop-registered photos only; `fromStatus` keeps a stale drain report off an edit the web
  rendered since; both desktop routes rate-limited per person); the
  batch answers `waitingForDesktop` and `requiresSourceChoice` counts, the bay's counts a
  `waitingForDesktop` total. Culling signals take `localSource` for the same three states, stamping
  both stages so no server stage reads that photo's preview in the original's place. `POST /initiate`,
  `PUT /:uploadId/chunks/:chunkIndex` and `POST /:uploadId/complete` answer 410, their disk staging
  is removed and `.incoming` / `.chunks` are swept once at boot; `/uploads/image-selection/*` is never
  served statically (the rest of `/uploads` is unchanged); deleting a project or folder now also
  removes its AI Editing objects from the bucket. No new permission rows: every new route sits under
  the existing `IMAGE_SELECTION / AI Editing` guard (the desktop-only ones behind
  `DESKTOP_AI_ENABLED`), so no role needs anything granted in Role Management.

- **AI Editing renders on the desktop from the original, and only the edited photo is uploaded.**
  The server never holds an uploaded photo's original (uploads arrive as the compressed preview
  and thumbnail), so its render started from the 1600 px preview. The Virtual Curation desktop app
  holds the originals where they live - storage root plus relative trail, the same resolution AI
  Culling uses - and now renders the edit there: the server's own editing engine, fetched and
  verified like the face engine's script (`GET /api/desktop/runtime/edit-engine.py`, named in the
  runtime manifest's `editEngine`), runs in the app's managed runtime over the original (a RAW
  through its embedded JPEG, upright, capped at the engine's edge) and hands over only the edited
  master - `POST …/ai-editing/photos/:uploadId/output`, behind the desktop hand-off switch
  (`DESKTOP_AI_ENABLED`; capabilities now answer `editingLocal`). The server stores it exactly as
  its own render (versioned keys, display pair at Image Selection's preset, `sourceKind`
  ORIGINAL_LOCAL, previous version released), so the web, the sends, Reset and the bay's counts
  see one kind of edit. Apply, Apply to selected and Apply to all render on the desktop when the
  photo's original is on that computer, with the engine's stages shown; a photo it cannot find
  renders on the server from the preview, as before. Nothing of the original is uploaded, the
  Photo Selection and Signature Album flows and their compression are untouched, and the web's
  AI Editing tab is unchanged (it shows the desktop's result; its own Apply still renders on the
  server from the preview). Each photo now answers `originalPath`, `storageRootId` and
  `localRenderable`. Found and fixed on the way: after any Auto Edit render, both apps read the
  edit as "changes not applied" and held the sends back, because the engine wrote its small
  scene-aware contrast and vibrance push onto the photographer's sliders and the panels compared
  a slider left to the AI against the number the render chose. The push now stays on the pixels
  and is reported on its own (`appliedRecipe.autoColor`), and both panels decide "unapplied" by the
  server's own rule (`recipeMatchesApplied`, mirrored and held by tests).
  [ai-editing/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-editing/service.js),
  [ai-editing/routes.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-editing/routes.js),
  [desktop/runtime.js](../backend/src/modules/desktop/runtime.js); desktop `src-tauri/src/ai.rs`,
  `editing/localEditing.js`, `editing/EditingPanel.jsx`.

- **Photo Culling reads faces, scenes and bursts like a professional culler, on the web and the
  desktop alike.** Culling V2:
  - **Faces, without AWS:** eyes are measured from 68 facial landmarks, so half-closed eyes are
    told from open and closed ones. Other new measurements: a face turned away, the face's own
    sharpness, and the expression (FER+).
  - **Blur:** a frame that is blurred overall but has a sharp face is no longer rejected for blur.
  - **Bursts:** the best frame of a burst is chosen on a balance of sharpness, open eyes,
    expression and face quality, not sharpness first. Marking a different best re-derives both
    frames' calls, and a photographer's own decision is never overridden.
  - **Similar series:** frames of the same set-up (the scene engine's image embedding) form a new
    kind of group, opened in the compare dialog. Their alternates are never rejected for being
    alternates.
  - **Scenes:** the scene profile is v2, with 18 wedding and event scenes. It measured 71% on the
    studio's own shoots against 48% for v1. Scene analysis is on by default wherever the face
    engine is.
  - **Only measured scenes count:** a scene counts toward a decision only when it was validated on
    the studio's own hand-labelled photos: Couple, Bride portrait, Family, Group, Details and Kids.
    That decision means a Target Count guarantee, the coverage line, or a learned taste.
    - Ceremony was called 11 times there and wrong every time. Emotional, Getting ready, Groom
      portrait, Food and others were not validated either.
    - Unvalidated scenes are still shown as the AI's guess and can still be filtered on.
    - No confidence is altered.
  - **Model integrity:** the face models are now fetched at a fixed Hub revision and checked against
    their sha256 on download and at every load.
    - The check needs no network once the files are on disk.
    - A substituted core model stops the face engine instead of running.
    - `AI_FACE_VERIFY_MODELS=0` accepts a deliberately different local copy.
  - **Target Count:** keeps exactly N photos. The photographer's own Keeps count first and their
    Rejects are never picked. The selection covers every moment of the story, a moment being a
    run of photos with no gap over three minutes, and spreads across similar series.
  - **Learned taste:** a single decision counts for more than a bulk one, and a reject that only
    lost to a twin teaches nothing. A taste can belong to one scene. The frame a photographer picks
    as a burst's best shifts that photographer's keeper balance by a bounded amount.
  - **Separate scores:** the photo's own quality is stored apart from its decision score, and the
    explanation says what moved one from the other.
  - **Training:** the training features are now `features_v2` (69 signals). A model trained on v1
    is refused rather than misread.
  - **Desktop:** the desktop app's local engine (1.1.0) installs the same optional models,
    verified against the server's digests.

  Files:
  [analysis/](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/analysis/),
  [face_engine.py](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/face-engine/face_engine.py),
  [learning/featureSet.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/learning/featureSet.js),
  [imageSelectionCulling.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/imageSelectionCulling.mjs).

  **Deploy:**
  - `npx prisma migrate deploy`. This applies two additive migrations:
    `20261009090000_culling_v2_signals` (five nullable columns) and
    `20261010090000_culling_similar_groups` (two nullable columns, an index and a key). Then run
    `npx prisma generate`.
  - With `AI_FACE_ENGINE_ENABLED=true`, the face engine fetches `1k3d68.onnx` (about 144 MB) and
    `emotion-ferplus-8.onnx` (about 35 MB) from the Hugging Face Hub once, and keeps each only if
    its sha256 matches. `AI_FACE_SIGNALS=v1` keeps the old engine.
  - `AI_CULLING_PROVIDER` and `AI_CULLING_SCENE_ENABLED` now default to `auto`. Set `false` or
    `none` to keep the old behaviour.
  - No permission changes.

- **AI Culling stays optional, says so when it fails, and a download names every original it could
  not find.** Photo Selection never needed a cull: photos uploaded straight into it are published
  as they are, and only a finalized run ever hides anything (non-Keep photos, never one the client
  already picked). Three gaps are closed.
  - A failed run now says that nothing was hidden, and offers **Continue to Photo Selection**
    beside starting a new run. Web and desktop.
  - "Download Selected" lists every missing original by name and where its record says it lives,
    under **See missing (N)**, and still saves the rest. The desktop app also lists copies that
    failed, with the reason; its copy events now carry the source path.
  - The old chunked upload route, which neither app calls any more, no longer keeps the uploaded
    original on the server after its thumbnail and preview are made, unless
    `STORE_ORIGINAL_IMAGES=true`. Originals belong in the studio's Original Storage only. A
    registered original is never touched, and files already kept stay.

  [CullingWorkspace.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/culling/CullingWorkspace.js),
  [MissingOriginalsDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/MissingOriginalsDialog.js),
  [processing/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/processing/service.js).
  **Access:** unchanged, no new permission. **Deploy:** nothing to run. If production sets
  `STORE_ORIGINAL_IMAGES` to keep browser originals, that still works with `"true"`; any other
  value now removes them.

- **The Photo Culling tab now shows where the cull stands at every step, and the review is a
  full culling workspace.** Instead of one placeholder, the tab draws a state for each moment,
  from the server's own counts: a folder with no photos says so with 0 photos / 0 ready and an
  Upload Photos button that opens Photo Selection's uploader on the same folder (uploads still
  compress before anything is sent); photos still uploading or processing are counted - including
  files an upload has announced but not yet sent - and the tab moves on by itself; Ready shows
  the photo count, the four modes as cards and Start; a running cull lists Technical, Faces,
  People, Scene and framing, Similar photos and Ranking and story as done, in progress, waiting or
  not used on this run, with the bar and the photos analyzed. The review opens with Keep, Maybe,
