  Reject and Pending, the AI's confidence (high / medium / low and the average) and Finalize;
  tiles carry their two most telling reasons (concerns first) and their place in a burst or
  duplicate group; opening a photo shows the AI's recommendation, what it rested on (the mode's
  score line, or the rule - another frame of the duplicate, Strict's burst rule, severe blur,
  Target Count), what speaks for and against it, its scores, and the photographer's own decision
  above it, with Keep / Maybe / Reject there and 1/2/3/0 and arrows working inside. Finalize lists
  what it never does (your decisions count as made, client picks stay, nothing is deleted) and
  its notice offers Reopen. The review can take the full width for a while; the folder tree and
  the project panel come back on the way out. "What culling has learned from you" is a compact AI
  preferences section below the review. The desktop app draws the same states with its own kit.
  `GET /ai-culling` answers `photoCounts`, `confidence` and `engines` beside everything it
  answered before ([CullingWorkspace.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/culling/CullingWorkspace.js),
  [imageSelectionCulling.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/imageSelectionCulling.mjs),
  [ai-culling/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/service.js)). No new
  permission, route, migration or environment variable.
- **The Image Selection Desktop app now has the Photo Culling tab too, over the same backend.**
  Opening a project's Photo Culling tab on the desktop shows the web's workspace — the folder
  selected in the tree (or the project root) as the scope, the four modes, live progress, the
  review grid with the same keys, filters, bulk bar, duplicate/burst compare and zoom preview,
  and finalize and reopen with the same confirmations — all through `/api/image-selection/
  projects/:projectId/ai-culling`, so a cull started on one app is reviewed on the other. The
  server still analyzes the previews; the desktop neither reads nor uploads an original for it
  (desktop repo `src/modules/image-selection/culling/`). The desktop backend hand-off branch
  (capabilities, runtime manifest and face-ingest routes) is merged into this branch so the two
  apps share one backend ([PROJECT-STATE.md](project-state/PROJECT-STATE.md)).
- **A culling run cannot start over photos another run is still working on, and a finished
  run's finalize settles only the photos it analyzed.** Starting Photo Culling on the whole
  project while a shoot's run is still analyzing (or the other way round, or a card under a
  shoot that is running) is refused with the scope that is busy named; shoots that share no
  photos still run side by side, and two Starts at the same moment (a double click, the web and
  the desktop) make one run because the check and the create hold the project's row lock. A run
  now records when it finished listing its photos
  (`seeded_at`): photos processed after that are not pulled in by a retry — the workspace says
  "N photos were processed after this run started" and finalizing never hides them. Finalize
  stamps every non-Keep photo it analyzed with its own session (`cull_rejected_session_id`),
  lifting any older stamp on those photos, and Reopen hands each photo that run settled back to the
  newest other finalized run's verdict (hidden again if that run did not keep it), so a
  project-wide cull and a shoot cull finalized over the same photos no longer undo each other
  ([ai-culling/repository.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/repository.js),
  migration `20261002090000_culling_stamp_ownership`, which hands existing stamps to the newest
  finalized run that rejected the photo and lifts any stamp no finalized run owns). The review
  grid's Keep / Maybe / Reject buttons and checkboxes are always on screen and thumb-sized on a
  phone, every card has a Preview button (a double-click on the photo does the same on a
  desktop), each card shows the AI's confidence beside its score and the AI's own answer under an
  override, the header names the run's mode and target, the Finalize confirmation says how many
  photos will be hidden and how many stay (and, in Assisted mode, that every photo not marked
  Keep counts as hidden), keyboard shortcuts keep working after a button click but never fire
  inside a text field, polling pauses in a background tab and refreshes on return, and the
  gallery header's publish counts refresh after a finalize or reopen
  ([CullingReviewGallery.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/culling/CullingReviewGallery.js),
  [CullingWorkspace.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/culling/CullingWorkspace.js)).
- **The Visual Curation dashboards keep themselves current; the web has no Refresh button, the
  desktop keeps one as a fallback.** Image Selection, AI Feature and Album Proofing dashboards on
  the web re-read quietly — the figures stay on screen and swap in — when the tab comes back to the
  front after ten seconds away, when the network comes back, when an upload from that browser
  lands, and on a light interval while in front (a minute; half a minute on the AI Feature, whose
  figures the engine changes in the background). A range change is quiet too, so the cards never
  drop to skeletons once they have shown a figure; a background read that fails keeps the figures
  and shows a notice. One shared hook, `components/shared/useAutoRefresh.js`, on one policy,
  `lib/refreshPolicy.mjs`; nothing else changed — a dashboard read never starts an upload, a
  compression or a processing job. The desktop app follows the same policy, adds a re-read when a
  transfer run in its local ledger lands, and keeps its Refresh button because it holds state the
  server cannot push; pressing it is a quiet read that turns the icon rather than blanking the page
  ([ImageSelectionDashboardPage.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/dashboard/ImageSelectionDashboardPage.js),
  [useAutoRefresh.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/useAutoRefresh.js)).
- **The AI Feature's Overview is now a dashboard in the Image Selection dashboard's family, on the
  web and the desktop alike.** The sixteen tiles are ten cards — Total, Active, Upcoming and
  Completed Events, Processing, Total and Processed Photos, Failed, People Detected, Archived Events
  — each a filter on the Recent Events table beneath (event and type, date, photos, processed,
  people, faces, a progress bar, status and last activity, with the standard filter row and
  sorting); then AI Processing Progress (the events with photos queued or running, processed over
  total, failures in red) beside Detection & Storage (storage used, faces detected, people, face
  matches, unmatched faces, videos, guests and recent uploads). A range picker — Lifetime, This
  Month, This Week, 3 and 6 Months, as Image Selection offers — scopes the caption's period
  figures (events created, photos uploaded and processed) and gives each card its arrow against
  where the figure stood when the range began, reconstructed from the rows' own dates as Image
  Selection does; the queue and the failures, which have no past to read, show no arrow rather than
  an invented one. The page still re-reads every half minute while in front, Create Event still
  goes to the Events list, and a double click opens the event. `GET /api/ai-feature/overview` takes
  `?range=` and answers the new figures beside every key it answered before, so an older desktop
  build keeps working — the one change there is that `recentEvents[].mediaCount` now counts what the
  Media tab lists, as the events list already did, rather than every stored row ([AiOverviewPage.js](../frontend/src/components/ai-feature/overview/AiOverviewPage.js),
  [overview/service.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/overview/service.js)). The pieces the three
  dashboards share — the card grid, the range bar, the table heading, the progress list, the figure
  list, the progress bar, the empty-studio section and the range vocabulary — moved to
  `components/shared/Dashboard*.js` and `lib/dashboardRange.mjs` (and `src/services/dashboardRange.js`
  on the server); the Image Selection dashboard reads them from there and draws exactly what it drew.
- **The AI Feature's photo viewer is a clean layer over the gallery: the file name, its faces and
  size, previous and next, and Delete - no Processed badge.** Opening a photo from Media used to
  cover the screen in a permanent near-black page with a processing pill under the picture. The
  viewer is now a neutral translucent backdrop that only takes the eye to the photo, with the
  controls on the application's own surfaces - white with a hairline, dark text - which the dark
  themes repaint as they repaint everything else, so it follows whichever theme is on. The title
  bar reads the file name with faces and size beneath it and a 40 px Close; the arrows sit in a
  lane either side of the picture, never on it; the picture keeps its ratio inside the viewport;
  Escape closes, the arrows move, and the Delete key only opens the confirmation. Delete is a
  quiet destructive button (trash icon, red text on a white surface) that asks first; a confirmed
  delete removes the photo for real - its faces, crops, matches, storage and row, through the same
  server discard as before - takes it out of the gallery in place without reloading the list, so
  the folder, scroll position and filters stay exactly as they were, and moves the viewer to the
  photo that slid into its place (the previous one when it was last; closed when none is left).
  The folder counts and the event's All Photos total are read again from the server. A photo
  whose face processing failed says so in words; nothing else about processing is shown
  ([Lightbox.js](../frontend/src/components/ai-feature/shared/Lightbox.js),
  [MediaLightbox.js](../frontend/src/components/ai-feature/event/MediaLightbox.js),
  [MediaTab.js](../frontend/src/components/ai-feature/event/tabs/MediaTab.js)). The desktop app's
  viewer is the same. The People and Face Recognition screens open the same viewer without Delete,
  as before.
- **Every Visual Curation upload - Image Selection, Album Proofing, Signature Album and the AI
  Feature, on the web and on the desktop - now compresses to one shared set of presets before a
  byte leaves the machine, and the studio picks each module's Preview quality and Thumbnail quality
  in one place.** Image Selection's ⋮ → Settings has a Processing / Compression section with a card
  per module: two pickers over the same five presets (Preview: High 2048px ~300 KB, Standard 1600px
  ~200 KB, Compact 1200px ~150 KB, Light 1000px ~100 KB, Smallest 800px ~50 KB; Thumbnail: High
  640px, Standard 480px, Compact 360px, Light 240px, Smallest 160px, WebP) and Restore recommended
  defaults - Image Selection starts on Standard / Standard, which is exactly the preview and
  thumbnail it has always made, and Album Proofing, the Signature Album and the AI Feature on High /
  Standard, because spread text, a premium album and a face all want the detail. Each change saves
  itself and applies to future uploads only; nothing already stored is recompressed and no link
  changes ([CompressionSettingsSection.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/compression/CompressionSettingsSection.js),
  the presets in [imagePresets.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/imagePresets.mjs) and
  [imagePresets.js](../backend/src/services/imagePresets.js), kept identical by a test). The three
  studio modules are one new nullable column, `compression`, on the Image Selection settings row
  (migration `20260930100000_visual_curation_compression_settings`), read by every uploader through
  `GET /api/image-selection/compression` (any of Project Management, Album Proofing, Signature Album
  or ADMIN / System Settings at Read) and saved with ADMIN / System Settings; the AI Feature card edits the very same
  Event Default Settings → Media Upload keys, which now read as the two presets with the concurrency
  and thumbnail format under Show advanced instead of seven bare numbers, and an event's own
  settings draw the same two pickers - a new event still takes its copy, an existing one keeps its
  own. The per-machine Preview quality Image Selection used to keep in the browser is gone: every
  machine in the studio now makes the same picture. Under the hood there is one browser engine
  ([imageDerivatives.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/imageDerivatives.mjs)): the original is decoded once
  with its EXIF orientation folded in, the preview and the thumbnail are both cut from that one
  frame - the AI Feature's thumbnail used to be re-derived from the already-compressed preview, on
  the web and on the desktop, and no longer is: the AI worker runs the same engine and sends the
  thumbnail beside the preview, and the server keeps it when it fits the event's preset
  ([derivatives.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/media/derivatives.js)). The AI Feature never
  steps a preview down to hit a size, so the frame face recognition reads keeps its detail; a
  guest's photo from the event page is optimized on the phone the same way (a guest's word is
  never taken for a photo's identity or size, the guest upload has its own rate limit, and every
  self-saving card offers Undo in its notice); a photo that decodes but cannot be encoded fails
  and can be retried, never sent whole in its place (only a format the browser cannot decode at
  all - HEIC, TIFF - goes whole for the server to convert, as before); "Keep original files" no
  longer files an optimized preview as an original; and every file the server keeps byte for byte
  - a client's preview or thumbnail, the Image Selection derivative route's two files - is walked
  from its first byte to its last so it is nothing but a plain JPEG or WebP. The Signature Album, which
  ignored any preset, follows its own; Album Proofing follows its own rather than Image Selection's;
  the legacy server-side worker (NAS registration, album import, Regenerate previews) reads the same
  record. The desktop app reads the studio's and the event's presets before each run, carries the
  recipe with the run, cuts its thumbnail from the original decode and sends it with AI media
  ([processor.rs](../../Image-Selection_Desktop---BCT/src-tauri/src/processor.rs)). Versioning,
  originals-on-NAS, client galleries, downloads, face data and every existing URL are untouched.

- **AI Feature → Media's folder panel now looks and behaves like Photo Selection's, and the
  Media workspace scrolls in two panes instead of one.** The left column is Image Selection's
  folder panel - a FOLDERS heading and a full-width **New Folder** button that stay put, then All
  Photos as the system row (a library icon, its count, no menu, the same blue selected state) and
  the event's folders under a hairline, each an amber folder with its count, a single ellipsised
  line with the full name on hover, and a ⋮ that appears on hover with Rename and Delete and never
  selects the folder it belongs to. The panel is 210 px wide and only its list scrolls; the gallery
  beside it scrolls on its own, so scrolling a thousand photos leaves the folder list where it was,
  scrolling fifty folders leaves the gallery where it was, and the event header and tabs never
  move (from `md` up; a phone still scrolls the page). Opening a folder and coming back lands the
  gallery where it was left, as far as the pages already read allow; nothing in the panel - a menu,
  a scroll - re-renders the gallery. The panel is a new shared primitive,
  [FolderNav.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/FolderNav.js), data-agnostic and able to draw a
  tree; AI folders are one level deep, so it draws a flat list and invents no hierarchy, and
  Image Selection's own tree is untouched. Both scroll panes use a thin, scoped scrollbar; nothing
  global changed ([MediaTab.js](../frontend/src/components/ai-feature/event/tabs/MediaTab.js),
  [AiEventWorkspacePage.js](../frontend/src/components/ai-feature/event/AiEventWorkspacePage.js)).
  The upload workspace, compression, counts and the AI pipeline are exactly as they were. The
  Virtual Curation desktop has the same panel and the same scroll ownership.
- **AI Feature → Media is folder-first: there is no "Unfiled" any more, and no status badge on
  every photo.** The folder list is All Photos and the studio's own folders, nothing else. A photo
  is uploaded into the folder that is open - All Photos is one combined grid of every folder and
  takes no uploads of its own; with a folder open the upload area is right there, and with none the
  pane asks you to pick or create one. An event with no folder yet shows one thing: "No folders yet
  - Create your first folder to begin uploading photos", and the folder you create opens with its
  upload area ready. The server refuses a staff upload that names no folder, in the same words
  ("Select or create a folder before uploading media."), before anything is stored; a guest's
  upload from the event page is unchanged and is listed under All Photos like every other photo
  ([MediaTab.js](../frontend/src/components/ai-feature/event/tabs/MediaTab.js),
  [media/service.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/media/service.js)). Photos already in no
  folder - from before, from a guest, or from a folder that was removed - stay exactly where they
  are and are still shown under All Photos; removing a folder still keeps its photos in the event,
  as it always did. The green "Processed" (and Queued / Processing / Failed) pill has gone from
  every card: a card is the photo. When photos could not be processed for faces, one line above the
  grid says how many in the event, Show them narrows the grid to just those, and Retry face
  processing is offered to those who hold AI Face Management; the status itself is unchanged
  underneath and still drives the worker, Overview and retries. The Upload button has left the
  event header - uploading lives on the Media tab.
- **The Signature Album tab now opens the album workspace straight away - there is no "Create
  Signature Album" step any more.** A project that has never had an album gets one made behind the
  normal loading state the first time somebody with Signature Album write access opens the tab
  ([useSignatureAlbum.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/useSignatureAlbum.js)):
  the existing create, so the album starts as the server's own Draft with the studio defaults, is not
  published, has no client link yet, and its PIN, download and share settings are what a new album
  always had. Opening the tab again, reloading, or the web and the desktop opening it at the same
  moment never makes a second album: the album is unique per project and a create that loses that
  race now answers the same 409 as one that finds the album already there, instead of a 500
  ([signatureAlbum.service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/signature-album/signatureAlbum.service.js)).
  An album that already exists is loaded exactly as it is. If the album cannot be loaded or started,
  the workspace says so with Retry; a read-only login with no album sees why nothing is shown yet.
  The same behaviour ships in the Virtual Curation desktop.

- **A Production shoot reads Planned once its plan is complete, automatically - and "WIP" now reads
  Work in Progress everywhere.** It read WIP from the first thing put on the plan until the shoot
  started, and as soon as a plan was submitted it could read Planned with only a Production
  Coordinator on it. Now a plan reads **Planned** when it is submitted and complete - Production
  Coordinator, at least one Production Team member, an outdoor shoot's travel mode with its detail (a
  number plate, the office vehicle, a ticket, a line for Other), and a Person and camera on every
  service (Remarks and assistants are never needed) - and nothing has been done on the day yet. Until
  then it reads **Work in Progress**, the Plan tab says what is still to fill, and the shoot's tile
  and the board's Progress column show the plan's own progress - "Plan: 3 of 7 filled" - instead of
  the day's steps at 0%; the steps take over once it is Planned. A project reads
  Planned when every one of its shoots is, with a **Planned** tab on the board. Hold and Rejected are
  still the only statuses set by hand. Production's "WIP" - on the board, the tabs, the tiles and the
  Plan's Status - is spelt out as **Work in Progress (n%)**, as Pre Production's is.
  [productionBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionBoard.mjs),
  [planCompleteness.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/planCompleteness.js).

- **A Pre Production shoot reads Planned once everything it asks is filled.** It read Work in
  Progress however complete it was - only its progress bar showed it was done - so a coordinator who
  had filled every field still saw Work in Progress. Now a shoot with nothing left reads **Planned**,
  and the automatic choice in its Status dropdown says the same; WCR, Hold and Rejected set by hand
  still show as before. The project still reads Planned only once every one of its shoots is.
  [preProductionProgress.js](../frontend/src/lib/preProductionProgress.js).

- **Every screen's data now travels compressed - the big lists arrive about 20 times smaller.** The
  server sent every response uncompressed, so the Projects list and the Pre Production board went out
  as megabytes at the studio's volume (about 11 MB and 17 MB for 4,000 projects and 6,000 shoots).
  Responses are now gzipped for the browser, which every browser asks for: measured on a copy of the
  data, the Projects list fell from 1.7 MB to 91 KB and the Pre Production rows from 2.6 MB to 132 KB
  (95% smaller). Nothing on any screen changes. The AI replies and the photo-upload progress, which
  stream as they happen, are left uncompressed so they still arrive live.
  [compressResponses.js](../backend/src/middleware/compressResponses.js). New dependency
  `compression` (Express's own) - **Deploy:** `npm install` in `backend` (the pipeline runs it).

- **One shoot on Hold puts its department's project status on Hold; the project's own status changes
  only the project.** Pre Production's project status reads **Hold** when any of its shoots is on
  Hold, and Production's when any shoot's plan or shoot day is held, else what the shoots' work says
  as before; each board gains a **Hold** tab. A Rejected shoot shows Rejected on that shoot only.
  Setting the project's status - on the project or through Projects → Update - changes the project
  alone: never a shoot, and never Pre Production's, Production's or Accounts' status, which each go on
  reading their own shoots and payments (the Update dialog says so). A held shoot shows Hold on its
  own tile - the status alone, its remarks kept in the shoot's form - and a Delivered project shows no
  "On Hold (…)" badge.
  [projectHolds.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/projectHolds.mjs),
  [preProductionProgress.js](../frontend/src/lib/preProductionProgress.js),
  [productionBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionBoard.mjs). No migration.

- **A Production board row expands to its shoots.** The ▸ at the start of a project's row shows its
  shoots under it, in the order they happen - Shoot ID, name (★ for the main event), time,
  coordinator, place, step progress, date and the shoot's own status - each column headed for both
  ("Client / Shoot", "Next Shoot / Date"). Double-clicking a shoot row opens that shoot's production
  panel; a project row still opens its tiles.
  [ProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionPage.js).

- **Production's Activity tab lists the newest action first.**
  [production/read.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/read.js) `listActivity`.

- **Production's statuses: each shoot's and the project's.** A shoot reads, first that applies:
  **Hold** / **Rejected** (the plan, set by hand in the Status dropdown at the bottom of the Plan tab,
  remarks required, saved with Submit plan / Save changes), **Shoot Hold** / **Shoot Paused** /
  **Shoot Rejected** (the shoot day's, from the Shoot status step), **Completed** (File in done),
  **Shoot completed (Footage pending)** (the team is back, File in next), **Shoot completed** (marked
  Completed, on the way back), **Shoot started**, **WIP** (something on the plan, submitted or not -
  a shoot has no Planned) or **Yet to Start**. The project reads **Yet to Start**, **WIP (n%)** (the average of its
  shoots' step progress) or **Completed**, beside its name in its panel and in the board's Status
  column, and the board's tabs are All / Yet to Start / WIP / Completed. A plan on Hold also shows
  across the project as **On Hold (Production)**. **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (four
  `plan_status*` columns on `project_production`).
  [productionBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionBoard.mjs),
  [ProductionPlanStatusField.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionPlanStatusField.js),
  [production/plan.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/plan.js) `setPlanStatus`.

- **The Production board lists projects, with their shoots as tiles.** One row per project - Event
  ID, client, vertical, Production Manager, shoots, shoots done ("2/4 Done"), the next shoot's date and
  the project's status - with its own tabs (see the statuses entry above).
  Opening a project shows its shoots as tiles - the same tiles as Pre Production's, from one shared
  component - in the order they happen, the main event first on its day and tagged ★ Main Event: its
  status, date, time, place and coordinator, and a footer with how far through its own steps it is
  ("Next: Shoot started", 30%). A tile opens that shoot's production panel; closing it comes back to
  the tiles. The Shoot Board's cards show the
  ★ Main Event tag too.
  [ProductionProjectPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionProjectPanel.js),
  [ProjectShootTile.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectShootTile.js),
  [productionBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/productionBoard.mjs).

- **Pre Production's statuses: each shoot's and the project's.** A shoot is **Work in Progress** (a
  shoot has no Yet to Start or Planned of its own - how much is filled is its tile's bar), or set by hand in the **Status** section at the
  bottom of its form - one dropdown listing the details' own status first, then **WCR** (waiting for
  the client's reply - asks the Next Followup Date, which joins the project's follow-ups on the right),
  **Hold** and **Rejected** (each needs its remarks, shown on the shoot's tile) - saved with the form. The project's pre production status comes from its shoots' details only -
  **Yet to Start**, **Work in Progress (n%)** with the average of the shoots' progress, or **Planned** - and is the
  board's tabs and status column and the pill beside the project's name in its panel's title. A shoot on Hold shows across the
  project: the badge beside its name in every panel, and the Projects list's status, read **On Hold
  (Pre-Production)**, **On Hold (Production)** or both. **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`
  (four `shoot_status*` columns on `project_pre_production`).
  [PreProductionShootStatus.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionShootStatus.js),
  [preProductionProgress.js](../frontend/src/lib/preProductionProgress.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js) `setShootStatus`,
  [projectHolds.js](../backend/src/services/projectHolds.js).

- **The Projects page has an On Hold tab.** Between In Progress and Completed, with its count, listing
  the projects whose status is On Hold.
  [ProjectsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectsPage.js).

- **Projects → Update status over the ticked projects.** Tick projects and press **Update**
  beside Export: one Project Status for all of them, from the same ten the project carries. Each
  project is changed under the same rule as editing it alone - in your reach, and once started only by
  its Project Manager, a branch administrator or someone who works every project; the rest are left
  alone and counted. Only the project changes - never a shoot; Delivered and On Hold carry through
  to the departments' project statuses (see the entry above). Until now a status could only change by Start
  Project or by import. No database change.
  [ProjectBulkStatusDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectBulkStatusDialog.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js) `bulkUpdateProjectStatus`.

- **Edit Payslip's Add is a popup, like Add Speak-up.** It opened as a full-screen form panel; it is
  now a centred popup over Settings (`PayslipItemDialog`, in place of `PayslipItemFormPanel`) with the
  same fields - Add to, a line saying where it shows, Label, Input type, and a Dropdown's options -
  and Discard / Add. Same rules and the same requests. No permission changes.

- **Employee Preference: Exclude From Attendance turns Flexible Shift off.** Ticking Exclude unticks
  and disables Allow Flexible Shift, which says why - it only says how somebody's attendance is
  counted. The server keeps to it too: a login saved as excluded is saved without Flexible Shift. No
  permission changes.

- **A payslip is named for the month before it is paid.** November's payroll (pay cycle 25 Sep -
  24 Oct, paid in November) is now the **October 2026** payslip: on the payslip ("Payslip for the month
  of October 2026"), in My Profile → Payslip's table and its "will be generated on" line, and in the
  PDF's file name (`payslip-2026-10.pdf`). Payroll → Main Page, and the requests themselves, keep the
  payroll month. No permission changes.

- **The payslip template's preview is the PDF itself, on an A4 sheet.** Payroll rules → Payslip
  template now shows the very HTML the sample PDF is printed from (`GET .../payslip-template` answers
  it as `html`), on an A4 page with the PDF's 12mm margin, scaled to the panel's width, in a sandboxed
  frame - so the preview and the download cannot differ. The sheet stays paper white, margins
  included, in the dark theme too. The React copy of the payslip
  (`PayslipTemplatePreview`) and the frontend's sample, totals and Net-Pay-in-words helpers are gone;
  the server's `payslipPdfService` is the one layout. A new shared `A4DocumentPreview` draws the sheet.
  No permission changes.

- **Edit Payslip starts with Salary, LOP Deduction, Salary Advance and Recovery alone.** Every other
  item - Emp Code, PAN, the PF details, Residential Status, Cost Centre, Incentive, Other Deductions -
  is off the list and off every payslip until somebody adds it: typing one of those names in **Add**
  (in its group) brings that item back with what was typed into it; any other name is a new item.
  Edit Employee → Payslip Details → Payslip Info asks only for what Edit Payslip lists and has on.
  Nothing stored is removed. No migration, no permission changes.

- **Edit Payslip: Personal details and PF details are one group, Payslip Info.** As Edit Employee →
  Payslip Details shows them: the personal details first, then the PF details, under one heading -
  three groups in all, with Earnings and Deductions. Add still asks Personal or PF, since a PF detail
  is left off a payslip that carries the personal details only. No permission changes.

- **Edit Employee: Payslip Info, one entry on the rail.** Personal Details and PF Details are one
  section now, named Payslip Info - the personal details, Residential Status and the added ones, then
  the PF details - and it is a top-level entry of its own, like Reviews, with no "Payslip Details"
  group around it; the page is titled Payslip Info. Same fields, same rules: the PF details are still
  required when the payslip carries them and disabled when it does not. No permission changes.

- **Edit Payslip: Salary, LOP Deduction, Salary Advance and Recovery cannot be deleted.** Their ⋮
  offers Edit alone, and the server refuses a delete (`UNDELETABLE_ITEMS`); they can still be renamed
  or turned off. One deleted before this reads as not deleted. No permission changes.

- **Edit Payslip: a ⋮ on every item, with Edit and Delete.** The delete button gave way to a ⋮
  menu (Read / Write only) holding **Edit** - rename the item in a small dialog - and **Delete**, as
  before. Any item can be renamed: an added detail or Earnings / Deductions column takes the new name
  as its own, and one of the payslip's own items (Emp Code, Salary...) prints under it on every
  payslip, the preview and the sample PDF (`PUT /api/hrm/payslip-fields/built-in { label, name }`,
  kept in `hrm_settings.payslip_built_in_items`). A name the payslip already carries is refused. No
  migration, no permission changes.

- **Settings: Wishes now sits under Employee.** The whole Wishes group - Wishes Scheduler, Birthday
  Wishes and Anniversary Wishes - moved from its own place on the rail into Employee, after Payroll
  rules, as a group of its own. Same screens, same ids, same `SETTINGS / Wishes` permission.

- **Edit Payslip: its four groups flow in two columns.** Personal details fills the first column and
  PF details, Earnings and Deductions stack in the second, each straight below the last - no empty
  space beside a long group. One column on a phone, as before.

- **A detail added in Edit Payslip prints on every payslip at once.** An employee's payslip used to
  leave an added Personal or PF detail off until something had been typed into it for them; it now
  lists every added detail still offered, with "-" where nothing is typed yet - as the preview shows
  it, and as the payslip's own details already did. One turned off in Edit Payslip still prints
  nowhere. No permission changes.

- **Base Salary is now Salary, on Payroll → Main Page and on the payslip.** The Main Page column,
  the row form's heading and typed-figure note and the day's-pay line say Salary, and so does the
  payslip's first earning (it was "Basic Salary") - in Edit Payslip, the preview, the sample PDF and
  every employee's payslip. Wording only - the figure is still the row's Salary, the employee's Total
  Salary editable for the month. No permission changes.

- **The payslip template moved to Settings → Payroll rules, below Edit Payslip.** Its preview and
  Download sample PDF now sit under Edit Payslip and are read again after every change made there, so
  a detail turned on or added shows straight away. They answer to `HRM / Payroll Register` Read like
  the rest of Payroll rules (`GET /api/hrm/payroll-register/payslip-template` and
  `/payslip-template/sample.pdf`). Settings → Template Settings is removed, with
  `/api/settings/template-settings` and its unused `PUT /payslip`. The `SETTINGS / Template Settings`
  permission stays in the catalogue but no longer guards anything - the studio may retire it, or leave
  it unticked, in Role Management. No migration.

- **Payroll → Main Page: the Freeze column is now Hold.** The column, its switch, the On hold status,
  the notices, the edit form's note and the server's refusals for a held row say Hold / on hold /
  Switch off Hold instead of Freeze / frozen / Unfreeze. Wording only - the switch works as before, and
  the code and the `payroll_entry.frozen` column keep their names. No permission changes.

- **Payroll Base Salary is the employee's Total Salary, every month.** Each month's row brings in the
  Total Salary as the reviews left it - no longer split by the share of the pay cycle each salary was
  in force when a review fell inside it. It stays editable on the row; an edit is that month's alone,
  and the next month starts from the Total Salary again. Unpaid rows that were not edited take the
  Total Salary the next time their month opens; paid and frozen rows keep what they hold. Migration
  `20261013100000_drop_base_salary_breakdown` drops `payroll_entry.base_salary_breakdown`, and the
  edit form's split-salary note is gone. No permission changes.

- **"Generate payslips on" moved from Settings → Template Settings to Settings → Payroll rules**, above
  Edit Payslip, with its own Save. It now answers to `HRM / Payroll Register` (Read shows it, Read /
  Write changes it, every-branch reach to save) through `GET`/`PUT /api/hrm/payroll-register/payslip-generation`;
  Template Settings' payslip endpoint no longer reads or takes it, and the Template Settings page is
  the preview and Download sample PDF alone. The saved value is unchanged; no migration, no new
  permission.

- **Branches: there is always one head office.** The payslip prints the head office's address, so a
  branch added while there is none starts as the head office and has to be it; the head office's
  switch is locked on - it moves by turning Head office on for another branch - and its menu offers
  no Disable. The server holds the same rule (400). Template Settings no longer shows the notes about
  where the logo and address come from, nor the "Employee details on the payslip" choice - which
  items the payslip carries is Edit Payslip's; the saved choice stays as it was.

- **Template Settings: the payslip's heading comes from Branding and the Head Office.** The logo is
  the Global Logo in Settings → Organization → Branding Logo (its light-theme file - a payslip prints
  on white), or with none uploaded the app's default mark (`beam-craft-black-text.svg`, the one every
  screen falls back to); the company name is the Studio Name beside it; the address is the main
  address of the branch marked Head Office in Organization → Branches - Address line 1, "Erode -
  638011", then the state, never Address line 2. The Logo upload, Company Name and Address boxes are
  gone from Template Settings; it says where each comes from, and says so when no Global Logo is
  uploaded or no branch is marked Head Office. **YTD is gone from the payslip**: Earnings beside
  Deductions carry the month's amount alone, the Year to date line is dropped, and with it the
  Financial year starts in setting. In its place Template Settings now chooses **which of the
  employee's details the payslip carries** - *Personal details only* (PF No., ESI No., EPS No. and UAN
  left off, the rows kept three pairs wide) or *Personal details and PF details* (the default) -
  saved as `hrm_settings.payslip_details` (migration `20261012260000_payslip_details_setting`) by
  `PUT /payslip { details }`. `payslip_company_name`, `payslip_address`, `payslip_logo_url` and
  `payslip_financial_year_start_month` are no longer read, and left in place rather than dropped. No
  migration, no new permission.
  [payslipHeading.js](../backend/src/services/payslipHeading.js).

- **Employee Repository: Serving Notice.** A new tab after Active holds whoever is serving their
  notice. Offboarding somebody with a Proposed Last Working Date of today or later no longer relieves
  them on the spot: their status and login stay as they were - they keep marking attendance and are
  offered by every picker - while the relieving date is set at once, so payroll and attendance stop
  counting after it. The day after that date the server relieves them (`separations/relieve.js`,
  every five minutes): Relieved, Fired or Absconded lands, the login closes, and the row moves to
  InActive. A date already past relieves at once, as does offboarding a hire never taken on; moving
  the date past today on an offboarding already relieved puts them back to work for the notice left;
  removing an offboarding still being served has no login to reopen. **Withdraw Notice** on the row
  (the Move to Active endpoint, with a required reason) removes the offboarding and the last working
  day of somebody still serving and leaves them working as they are. Direct reports and pending work
  still move when the offboarding is saved. Migration `20261012220000_serving_notice` adds
  `employee_separation.relieved_at` and marks every earlier separation relieved - so anybody already
  relieved with a last working day still ahead stays in InActive until their offboarding is opened
  and saved again. No new permission: the tab is `HRM / Employee Management`, as the page is.
  [relieve.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/separations/relieve.js),
  [EmployeeVerificationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeVerificationPage.js).

- **A booking the old sheet names no CRM or Pre Production Coordinator for now imports.** Both cells may
  be left empty in Pre Production → Import - every people cell may - where before either one empty cell
  refused the whole row. Their headings are still part of the template, so a file that drops the column
  is refused rather than quietly importing a file's worth of projects with nobody on them, and the
  project form still asks for a CRM, so nothing the studio types changes. A project with **no Pre
  Production Coordinator** raises no pre production row, so that row's pre production answers have
  nowhere to go and are not stored: the project and its shoot still import, and naming a coordinator and
  uploading the file again stores the answers then. Migration
  `20261012170000_project_crm_name_optional` lets `sales_project.crm_name` be NULL (it was the only one
  of the two that could not); no existing row is touched. **Run `npx prisma migrate deploy` with the
  code.** No permission change.
  [importColumns.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/importColumns.js),
  [migration.sql](../backend/prisma/migrations/20261012170000_project_crm_name_optional/migration.sql).

- **A project On Hold says so beside its name in every panel that works on it.** Start / Edit
  Project, the project record, Pre Production's project panel, shoot form and General, and a shoot's
  Production panel now show an amber **On Hold** badge right after the title while the project's
  status is On Hold, so nobody updates a held project without seeing it. Any other status shows
  nothing. (Post Production has no panel yet.)
  [ProjectHoldBadge.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectHoldBadge.js),
  [SchemaFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/schema-form/SchemaFormPanel.js).

- **The Shoot Board shows each day's free shooters, and a shoot's overview shows who is on it.**
  Under every date, a small count says how many shooters (employees with a shooting skill) have no
  shoot at all that day - anyone named on any of the studio's shoots that date, as Production
  Coordinator, on the Production Team or on a service's crew, counts as busy; a tap lists their
  names. Opening a shoot's bar now shows, on each shoot card, its Production Team and each service
  with its person and assistants (vendors as "EXT - name"). No database change.
  [freeShooters.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/shoot-board/freeShooters.js),
  [ShootTimeline.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/shoot-board/ShootTimeline.js),
  [ShootBoardCard.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/shoot-board/ShootBoardCard.js).

- **Production's service crew lists only shooters.** On a shoot's Plan, each service's Person and
  Assistant dropdowns now offer only employees holding at least one shooting skill on their profile -
  Candid Photographer, Candid Videographer, Drone, Indoor Shoot, Outdoor Shoot, Photography,
  Traditional Videographer or Traditional Photographer (the older "Candid Photography" / "Candid
  Videography" spellings count too) - plus the vendors. Anyone already chosen stays listed, and
  saving refuses a non-shooter newly named, saying to add a skill on the employee's profile. The
  Production Team and Coordinator lists are unchanged. Employees need their skills filled in on their
  profile to appear. No database change.
  [crew.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/crew.js),
  [ProductionServiceCrew.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionServiceCrew.js).

- **An indoor shoot skips Production's travel steps, and Photo copy is now File in.** A shoot whose
  Shoot Type is Studio / In-House has no Started from studio, Reached shoot place, Started from venue
  or Reached studio: it runs six steps, Pineapple meeting to File in, and sends only the Shoot
  completed WhatsApp message. A shoot with no type, or an imported stray value, is treated as outdoor
  and keeps all ten. Indoor shoots already sitting on a travel step continue from the next step they
  have (Pineapple meeting, or File in after the shoot); nothing stored is rewritten, so a shoot whose
  type changes later follows its new type. "Photo copy" is renamed **File in** everywhere it is shown;
  Production → Import still reads "Photo copy" in older sheets. No database change.
  [steps.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/steps.js),
  [ProductionExecutionTab.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionExecutionTab.js).

- **A client already in the app is kept, holds both its own IDs and the sheet's, and its shoots are
  updated from the sheet - so its production and post production rows can be imported.** Pre
  Production → Import used to refuse a row whose client name matched exactly one project typed into
  the app, or - with Replace ticked - skip it when that project had payments or an Image Selection
  gallery; either way the sheet's row was thrown away and its Event and Shoot IDs were saved nowhere,
  so the Production import could not find that project's shoots.

  Now such a project is **kept** and **linked**: it keeps its own Event ID and is given the sheet's
  beside it (`sheet_event_id`), and each sheet row is linked to the shoot of that project **with the
  same name**, which keeps its own Shoot ID and is given the sheet's (`sheet_shoot_id`). A sheet shoot
  with no shoot of that name is added as a new one; two shoots of one name are told apart by the Shoot
  Date, and refused by name where it cannot say which, to be linked on the board.

  What each side keeps depends on what the record is for. The **project** keeps what the app holds and
  the sheet fills only what is empty - a client number or value, people not yet named - and its client
  name is never changed, because that is what a client is found by and the app's payments and gallery
  hang off it. The **shoot, and its pre production answers, are written from the sheet**, which is the
  studio's record of when and where a shoot ran: a Shoot Date, place, district, state, shoot type,
  session timing or checklist answer the sheet gives **replaces** the app's, and only a cell the sheet
  leaves empty is left alone.

  Replace still deletes and re-imports a project it may, and now **links** - instead of skipping - one
  with payments or a gallery, or one the importer may not delete; the result says how many projects
  were kept this way and why. A client found only by its number, or one name on two projects, is still
  refused. One thing to check in the result: a client who booked **twice under the same name**, with
  only one booking typed into the app, has that booking linked to whichever Event ID the file names
  first - every project linked by name is listed, so it can be checked. No migration, no permission
  change.
  [import.service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/import.service.js),
  [ImportDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/ImportDialog.js).

- **Production → Import reads the old sheet the way Pre Production → Import does, and keeps the name of
  somebody who has left.** The old sheet's placeholders (IN OLD SHEET, WCR, NA, N/A, NIL, #REF!, TBD
  and blank cells) now come in empty - before, "N/A" in Plan Remarks was saved as text and "WCR" in
  Production Step refused the row - in a cell and inside the team list. A Production Coordinator,
  Production Team member or Footage Backup By cell takes an **Employee Code or the name as HRM has
  it**; a name that is no working employee's - somebody who has left - is **kept as written** with
  nothing linked, and the board, the shoot board and the WhatsApp messages print it. The plan form
  lists them read-only under **No longer with the studio**, and Save Plan leaves a coordinator or team
  member kept this way where they are (its form cannot pick them, so a save no longer reads as "clear
  the coordinator", even on a submitted plan) - choosing a real coordinator replaces the name; a name
  kept on the team has no remove button yet. Pre Production's people cells use
  the same shared reader (`services/importPeople.js`). The template headings are unchanged. Migration
  `20261012100000_production_leaver_names` adds three nullable columns
  (`project_production.production_coordinator_name`, `project_production_team_member.employee_name`,
  `project_production_footage.backed_up_by_name`) and touches no existing row; **run `npx prisma
  migrate deploy` with the code.** Needs no new permission. A shoot still has production only once its
  project has a working Production Manager (Pre Production import), and a name-only manager cannot
  raise it.
  [import.service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/import.service.js),
  [importPeople.js](../backend/src/services/importPeople.js),
  [migration.sql](../backend/prisma/migrations/20261012100000_production_leaver_names/migration.sql).

- **The client photo-selection gallery has a cleaner, more premium look.** The client's name is
  centred over the content pane, with the status badge and "1 out of 1 Images Selected for Frame"
  on one line under it; All Photos / People β / Selected stay underlined on their divider with
  "Photo selection will expire on ..." on the right of the same row (on a phone the badge takes
  its own line, the expiry is centred under the tabs, and the tab gap narrows so all three fit at
  320px); each folder card reads
  "52 photos · 5 selected" with a full-width strip of five equal, cropped thumbnails, the last one
  a real photo carrying "+48" for everything it stands for (on a phone the card stacks, with Select
  Photos full width under the strip). Pressing the strip opens the folder
  just as Select Photos does - it never picks or unpicks a photo. The footer puts "Overall
  completion" and "9 of 10 Photos" on one line over a thicker bar; on phones its two buttons share
  a row at 44px with lighter 13px labels.
  The folder list now returns each card's first five photos (thumbnails only - R2 or the
  session-checked thumbnail route, never an original) from the query it already ran, so the strip
  costs no extra request. Selection, review and submission are unchanged. Shared `Tabs` gained an
  `inline` size, which the gallery's tab row now uses instead of hand-typed buttons.
  [FolderCards.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/FolderCards.js),
  [FolderCardList.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/FolderCardList.js),
  [gallery/repository.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/gallery/repository.js).

- **Payroll Main Page: the Freeze switch stands alone.** The word "Freeze" / "Frozen" beside each row's
  switch is gone - the column is headed Freeze, the switch's state shows it, its hover says what it
  does, and a screen reader still hears "Freeze <name>'s row".
  [PayrollMainSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollMainSection.js).

- **A payroll month appears only after its pay cycle ends.** On HRM → Payroll → Main Page, a month
  whose pay cycle has not ended shows no payroll and gets no rows: November (cycle 25 Sep - 24 Oct) is
  made from 25 Oct, when its attendance is complete. Until then the table says when it will be made,
  and the header reads "Made from 25 Oct 2026, after the pay cycle ends"; rows made for such a month
  before this change are not shown until then either (they are left in place, and brought up to date
  once the cycle ends). Previously the month after the one being paid was filled in ahead of its
  cycle. `cycleGate` in [payroll-register/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/service.js).
  No migration, no permission change.

- **A leave counts working days only, and its form says so under the Leave Type.** A leave over 10-12
  Oct with Sunday the 11th a weekly off is **2 days**, not 3: a weekly off or a holiday the studio
  declared in the range is no day of leave. The Leave form - quick dialog and HRM → Request - now asks
  **Leave Type** under the From and To dates, and under it says **Leave days: 2 days - Sun 11 Oct
  (weekly off) not counted**, then **Available CL**, then the Loss of Pay warning (Casual Leave past the
  balance) or note (a Loss of Pay leave); the plain span ("3 days") is no longer shown for a leave.
  Request lists count a leave's days the same way. The Casual Leave balance and payroll already left
  weekly offs and holidays out - this makes the number on screen agree with them. No migration.
  [CasualLeaveBalance.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/CasualLeaveBalance.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js).

- **Payroll's Main Page keeps itself up to date - Generate payroll and Refresh payroll are gone.**
  Opening a month, or reloading the page, brings it up to date for somebody with Read / Write: the
  **month still being paid** - until its payable date passes, so October (payable 10 Oct) until 10 Oct,
  November from the 11th - and **every month after it** get a row for every working employee and have
  every row not paid or frozen read again from attendance, the salary on record, Advance Salary and
  Recovery. So a change to attendance, Attendance Rules (Casual Leave, Permissions...) or Payroll
  rules reaches the current and later months, and **an earlier month is left as it was** - filled in
  once, only where it has no rows, and never read again. Rows are made no further ahead than the month
  after the one being paid ("Fills in nearer its pay cycle" beyond that). A row is written only when a
  figure actually changes, so its "updated by" stays meaningful. A **Base Salary or Attendance Leaves
  typed by hand** on a row is now remembered and kept as typed through every update (before, Refresh
  replaced it) - the row's form says so and offers **Use the calculated figures again** - and an update
  never writes over a figure typed while it ran; paid and frozen rows stay settled as before. The
  header says "Up to date", "Earlier month - not updated" or, after a failure, "Not updated - showing
  stored figures" with Try again, and an employee added on opening is announced. A removed row comes
  back with the month's next update while the person is still a working employee - change their
  employment status to keep them off. `POST /sync` replaces `POST /generate` and `POST /refresh`;
  migration `20261010220000_payroll_entry_typed_figures` adds `payroll_entry.base_salary_typed` and
  `attendance_leaves_typed` (existing rows unmarked). No permission change.
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/service.js),
  [settingsVersions.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/settingsVersions.js),
  [PayrollMainSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollMainSection.js).

- **Each section of Attendance Rules saves on its own.** Settings → Employee → Attendance Rules -
  Working day, Casual Leave, Permissions and Comp-Off - has a **Save** at the foot of every section in
  place of one Save for the page. A section's Save is on only while it has changes, sends that
  section's fields alone, and says "Casual Leave saved."; changing the start date or the Casual Leave
  policy is still confirmed first. The server reads the sections not sent as they are stored and
  checks the one sent against them (a shift end before the stored start is refused), and a value
  that contradicts itself is still refused before anything is read. An unsaved edit in another
  section is kept when one section saves.
  [AttendanceRulesPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRulesPanel.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/controller.js).

- **A comp-off is earned by a full day's work on a weekly off or a declared holiday.** The days that
  earn one are now the **weekly offs set in Attendance Rules** plus the holidays declared in Settings
  → Holidays - before, every Sunday and the declared holidays, whatever the weekly offs were. So a
  Saturday the studio gives off earns one, and a Sunday it does not give off no longer does. And only a
  **full day** counts: the worked time - login to logout, less the time logged out in between - has
  to reach Attendance Rules' **Full day**; a shorter day, or one never logged out of, earns nothing.
  The comp-off picker offers only the days that qualify, and a claim on any other is refused saying
  why ("You worked 5h 30m on 4 Oct 2026. A comp-off needs a full day (8h 30m)."). Comp-offs already
  raised or approved are left as they are. No migration, no permission change.
  [attendanceRules.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/attendanceRules.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/controller.js).

- **Feedback IDs are one per project, versioned per feedback: `DBS-FB-00001-01`.** A project
  (an Event ID) now has a single Feedback ID, `DBS-FB-00001`, given with its first feedback, and each
  of its feedbacks is a version of it: **-01** is always its New Project Feedback (kept for it even
  when a shoot's feedback is given first), **-02, -03 ...** its Shoot Completion Feedbacks in the
  order they are given, and the **Overall Feedback is the last** (a shoot added to the project after
  it is numbered after it; nothing is renumbered). To keep it last, the Overall
  Feedback now opens - on Yet to be done and on save - only once Production has completed every shoot,
  **every shoot's feedback has been given, and the project is Delivered** (listed under **Projects →
  Completed**); before, it opened once the shoots were completed. A save that comes too early is told
  which of the three is missing.
  The feedback already given is **renumbered** this way by migration
  `20261010120000_project_feedback_versions` (projects in the order their first feedback was given;
  within one, New Project first, Overall last), which also rewrites the old ID quoted in each Average /
  Poor review's task, and sets the counter to the number of projects. WhatsApp messages already sent
  keep the old ID. Adds `sales_project.feedback_code` (unique) and `project_feedback.feedback_version`
  (unique per project). On the Feedback page, a tab holding several of one project's feedbacks
  shows them as the Quotations register shows a chain: one row - the highest version - with a
  **Versions** count after the Feedback ID, and the others folded under its chevron, newest first
  (Yet to be done stays one row per waiting feedback). Rehearsed on a copy of the database.
  **Deploy the code with the migration**:
  the old code saving a feedback after the migration is refused (no version to write). No permission
  change.
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/feedback/service.js),
  [migration.sql](../backend/prisma/migrations/20261010120000_project_feedback_versions/migration.sql).

- **Payroll is off the sidebar for now.** HRM → Payroll is marked `hidden`, like the Attendance
  Register and Events: nobody sees it in the menu, Super Admin included. The screen, its route and
  its permission (`HRM / Payroll`) are unchanged — Role Management still grants it by name, and it
  returns by removing `hidden`. [navigation.mjs](../frontend/src/constants/navigation.mjs)
- **The feedback form's line reads as a question.** "New Project Feedback: Rate <project> and say how
  it went?" - a capital R, and a question mark in place of the full stop.
  [FeedbackFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackFormPanel.js)
- **Payroll → Main Page picks its month in one place.** The month and year dropdowns - a narrow list
  that cut "September" off and scrolled sideways, and a year list of only four - are one **MonthField**
  in the header and in the Generate dialog: a button reading "October 2026" that opens the year
  between two arrows over a 3 x 4 grid of the months, the selected one filled and this month ringed.
  The years run from 2026, the studio's first payroll year, to ten years ahead (2026 to 2036 today,
  moving on each year). A new shared `MonthField` component.
  [MonthField.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/MonthField.js)
- **Advance Salary's and Recovery's statuses now follow the payroll, not the calendar.** An advance
  reads **Pending** until the payroll it comes off is marked **Paid** on the Main Page, then
  **Deducted** - it used to turn Deducted on the 1st of its month, days before payday, and stay so
  even if that month was held. A recovery reads **Active** until every instalment month is Paid, then
  **Completed** - it used to complete on its end date, even with an instalment unpaid, and to stay
  Active for weeks after the last one was paid. Recovery gains a **Deducted** column ("3 of 5"), also
  in its info panel. The tabs, the list and the Payment History now always agree. No migration and no
  permission change. [payroll-recovery/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-recovery/service.js)
- **A payroll month is now named for the month it is paid in.** October's payroll is the pay cycle
  that ended in September - 25 Aug to 24 Sep with the cycle on the 25th - payable on 10 Oct, where it
  used to be 25 Sep - 24 Oct payable on 10 Nov. The days between a cycle's end and its payday do not
  change; only which month a cycle is filed under does, so Generate, Refresh, the Main Page's Pay
  cycle and Payable on line, an advance's From Month and a recovery's months all follow it. Months
  already generated keep the days their rows were read over until **Refresh payroll** reads them
  again. A change in Payroll rules now starts with the payroll month whose cycle is **running** - on
  9 October, November's (25 Sep - 24 Oct) - since October's cycle is over and it may already be paid;
  both Settings confirmations name that month. [settingsVersions.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/settingsVersions.js)
- **Payroll → Advance Salary and Recovery open a row the way every register does.** One tap shows
  the advance or recovery in the info panel beside the table - amount, employee, month or schedule,
  months skipped on the Main Page, the advances a recovery was converted from, and when it was added
  and last changed; two taps open it full screen, read-only. A double tap no longer opens the edit
  form: Edit is in the panel's header and the row's ⋮, for Read / Write. Advance Salary's Skipped
  column is now Skipped Months, as on Recovery. No server change and no permission change.
  [infoPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/infoPanelConfig.js),
  [PayrollAdvanceSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollAdvanceSection.js),
  [PayrollRecoverySection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollRecoverySection.js)
- **Payroll → Main Page refreshes the whole month with one button.** **Refresh payroll**, left of
  Generate payroll, brings every unpaid row of the month on screen in again - the base salary,
  attendance leaves over the pay cycle as Payroll rules set it now, salary advance and recovery
  deduction - after asking first with the days it reads and how many rows it touches. Paid rows stay
  settled. Incentive, the other typed figures, the extra columns and the payment are kept. It
  replaces the per-row **Refresh from attendance** in each row's ⋮, and is how a month generated
  before a change of cycle day takes the new days. `POST /api/hrm/payroll-register/:id/refresh` is
  replaced by `POST /api/hrm/payroll-register/refresh { year, month }`, under the same
  `HRM / Payroll Register` Read / Write; no migration and no permission change.
  [PayrollMainSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollMainSection.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/service.js)
- **The Attendance calculator has a Save button, and its days apply from the current month on.**
  Start and End (Date) and Payable Date (Following Month) no longer save as a field is left: **Save**
  asks first, naming the month the change starts from. Like the salary rules, a new cycle day or
  payable day applies to the current month's payroll and later; every earlier month - generated or
  not - keeps the days it had, so its pay cycle and payable date on the Main Page never move. A month
  now starts the day after the month before it ended, so changing the cycle day neither skips nor
  repeats a day (from 25 to 1 in October: September stays 25 Jul - 24 Aug, October runs 25 Aug -
  30 Sep). A new cycle day is refused while a later month is already generated (it would skip or
  repeat days against it) - remove that month's rows first, or change it once that month is the
  current one. The Generate dialog asks the server for the chosen month's days instead of working them
  out itself. Migration `20261009180000_hrm_payroll_cycle_versions` adds the two days to the rule
  versions; after pulling run `npx prisma migrate deploy` and `npx prisma generate` in `backend`.
  [AttendanceCalculatorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/AttendanceCalculatorPanel.js),
  [settingsVersions.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/settingsVersions.js).
- **Changing the Payroll rules no longer touches past months.** A change to the day rate or the
  rounding in Settings → Payroll rules now applies from the **current month's payroll on** - this
  month and every later one, generated or not. Every earlier month keeps the rules it had, even one
  not yet paid or generated late (August generated in October still uses August's rules); paid months
  never change, as before. The Save's confirmation names the month it starts from. Each change is
  kept as a version effective from its month (`payroll_rule_version`, migration
  `20261009160000_hrm_payroll_rule_versions`); the first change also records the rules as they were
  before it. After pulling run `npx prisma migrate deploy` and `npx prisma generate` in `backend`.
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/service.js),
  [PayrollRulesPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/PayrollRulesPanel.js).
- **The Attendance calculator is inside Settings → Employee → Payroll rules.** The pay cycle
  (Start and End date) and the Payable Date now sit at the top of Payroll rules, above the salary
  calculation rules, so everything the payroll is worked out by is in one place; the separate
  Attendance calculator entry is gone. Access is unchanged: the calculator is still for
  administrators only, and the salary rules for `HRM / Payroll Register` - Payroll rules is offered
  to anybody holding either and shows only the part they hold. No migration and no permission change.
  [PayrollRulesPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/PayrollRulesPanel.js),
  [SettingsOverlay.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/SettingsOverlay.js).

- **Payroll's Main Page groups its columns under the sheet's headings.** A band above the column
  names now says what each set of columns is - Employee Details, Earnings, Deductions, Salary and
  Payment - as on the studio's payroll sheet (whose last band reads "Remarks"; it is Payment here,
  since a Remarks column already sits under Deductions). Hiding, filtering and the CSV work on the
  columns as before, and a column is dragged only within its own band. The shared table takes such
  groups from any page (`{ id, header, columns: [...] }`): the header rows stack as they stick, the
  filter row sits under them, and a band is a label that can't be sorted, dragged, resized or hidden.
  Tables without groups are unchanged.
  No migration and no permission change.
  [PayrollMainSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollMainSection.js),
  [DataTable.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/DataTable.js).
- **Edited cells read in the table's own type.** On Payroll → Main Page the editable cells drew
  their values larger, bolder and centred - the button and field sizes of a form - beside the plain
  cells. They now take the table's font size, line height and weight and sit left like the rest,
  the value, the box it opens and the status, mode, account and date controls alike.
  [EditableCell.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/EditableCell.js).
- **Links in tables read on the dark themes.** A table's link - the Attendance Dashboard's "View on
  map", a stored file - was a dark sky blue that all but vanished on a dark table; it is now the
  house blue, which the dark themes lift to their light accent, and stays a deep blue on the light
  theme. [tableCells.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/tableCells.js).
- **Payroll → Main Page is edited in its cells, like the sheet.** For somebody with
  `HRM / Payroll Register` Read / Write, Base Salary, Incentive, Attendance Leaves, Policy Breach
  Leaves, Salary Advance, Other Deductions and Remarks open a box in place on a click (Enter or
  leaving the cell saves, Escape puts it back), and Payment Status, Mode, From and Date are chosen in
  the cell itself. Each change saves at once and the row's totals, net and rounded salary update with
  it; a refusal shows in the cell without losing what was typed. A paid month's figures stay
  settled - only its payment cells edit. The worked-out columns, Recovery Deduction (Payroll →
  Recovery's) and the employee's details are not editable. The Base Salary can now be corrected by
  hand; Refresh from attendance brings the employee's salary in again. The ⋮ Edit form is still there.
  The cell is one shared component for any table: [EditableCell.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/EditableCell.js),
  [PayrollMainSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollMainSection.js).
- **Nobody is marked Absent before the shift starts.** Today, somebody who has not logged in yet
  reads **Yet to log in** until the shift start set in Settings → Employee → Attendance Rules, and
  counts as neither absent nor present; from the shift start on, still not logged in, they are
  Absent. A login after that makes the day On time (inside the late grace) or Late (after it) - both
  present. Past days, holidays, weekly offs and leave are unchanged.
  [attendanceRules.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/attendanceRules.js).

- **Deleting ticked projects on Projects or Sales Manager now deletes them permanently.** The ⋯
  menu's single Delete is unchanged: it hides the project and an import can still restore it. A
  selection runs that same delete first - the client's login off, the Image Selection gallery
  purged, the hard discs off Client Storage, with the same rule for who may delete which project -
  and then removes the project row, taking its shoots, pre production, production, deliverables,
  post production, extra quotations, feedback, attachments and CRD document with it, and the stored
  attachment and production files after. Payments, payment-request expenses and client storage
  discs are kept, with their project cleared. The confirmation says it cannot be undone. Nothing
  new to grant: it answers to the screen's own permission, `ADMIN / Table Select All` and
  `mayDeleteProject`, as the bulk delete did. (`hardDeleteProjectRecord`.)

- **Pre Production → Import takes the old sheet as it is and leaves unknown details empty.** The
  sheet's placeholders - IN OLD SHEET, WCR, NA, N/A, NIL, #REF!, TBD - come in empty in every
  column instead of refusing the row; times are read the way the sheet writes them (6:15 PM,
  11:00:00 AM, 10.30 am, 11:OO AM); a cell that is not a Yes/No or a link comes in empty, and a link
  is taken from text around it; a date may also be written with the month by name, day first ("6 Sept 2026", "8-Aug-2026"); "Pending" and "Yet to Start" are Work in Progress - Pre & Production and "Completed" - the sheet's word for a shoot done - is Work in Progress - Post Production; a people column takes an Employee Code or a name that is exactly one active employee's, and any other name - somebody who has left - is kept as written with nobody linked; and a 10-digit
  number, or one starting 91, is an Indian number (+91). A shoot's place, district, state, shoot
  type and session timing may now be empty - left for the shoot form, which still asks for all of
  them - rather than required or given an invented default. Only Event ID, Client Name, Client
  Number, Branch, Shoot ID and Shoot Name are needed - and the Client Number may be empty too, to be
  added on the project (WhatsApp and the client login already say when a project has none). A
  number from abroad written without its "+" (a Malaysian 60…) is kept as written with the "+";
  an event's start and end are taken as written, so a 10 PM to 4 AM reception imports; and a clock
  time typed into a date column comes in empty.
  [importColumns.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/importColumns.js),
  [import.service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/import.service.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (migration `20261010120000_shoot_place_type_optional`:
  four `project_shoot` columns made nullable) and `20261010130000_project_client_number_optional`
  (`sales_project.client_main_number` made nullable); no data touched. Then `npx prisma generate`.

- **Converted leads no longer appear in Today, Yesterday or Overall Pending Followups, on any
  vertical.** Dum Dum and Corp already cleared a converted lead's next follow-up; a Converted Qua Qua
  lead could keep one and so showed up on the pending tabs. Now plain Converted is left off all
  three (the counts and the CRM dashboard's follow-ups outstanding with them); Converted & Followup
  still shows. A Qua Qua lead's date itself is kept. No permission change.
  [leadQueryService.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/leadQueryService.js)

- **A lead's Source now says how it came in: Manual Entry, CSV Import or Google Sheet
  Integration** (and Callyzer, as before). Add Lead and Bulk Entry used to leave Source blank, and the
  CSV import and the sheet sync copied the file's own Source cell (Instagram, a campaign name); both
  now ignore that column. A lead that already has a Source keeps it when the sheet is re-read. The
  labels are named once in `leadSources.js`. Migration `20261009130000_crm_lead_source_labels` puts
  stored leads on them: sheet leads (spreadsheet link) -> Google Sheet Integration; CSV leads
  (`csv-` import key, or "CSV import") -> CSV Import; blank -> Manual Entry. A CSV row that brought
  its own Enquiry ID and Source left no mark and keeps what it has; Callyzer and other values are
  untouched. Data only. The sheet itself is never written.
  [leadSources.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/leadSources.js)

- **A task's ⋮ now reads View, Edit Task, Duplicate Task, Cancel Task, Delete Task** - the two that
  end a task last. Cancel Task used to sit above Edit Task. Start, Mark Complete and Reassign, for the
  person holding the task, still follow View. [TasksPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/TasksPage.js)

- **A table's tick-box column now stays pinned on the left whenever the table has one**, while the
  rest scrolls sideways — with no columns frozen as well. Freeze Columns is unchanged: it still
  counts only the data columns, and with nothing frozen nothing else is pinned.
  [tableLayout.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/tableLayout.js)

- **A Super Admin can delete attendance requests permanently, over a selection.** Ticking requests on
  Attendance → Requests now offers **Delete (n)** beside Export — to a Super Admin alone (the
  SUPER_ADMIN column or an active SUPER_ADMIN role); nobody else sees it, and the server refuses it
  to anybody else. It removes the requests from the database with their approvals, history and
  notifications, whatever their status, and cannot be undone: approved leave, on-duty and comp-off
  stop counting in attendance, while a corrected day keeps its corrected status. The row's own
  Delete is unchanged — it still marks one's own request Deleted and keeps it. The check is one
  shared `isSuperAdmin` (`services/administrator.js`), now also behind Tasks' Super Admin rules and
  returned by `GET /api/user/permissions`. No new permission or migration.
  [routes.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/routes.js),
  [AttendanceRequestsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestsPage.js)

- **The selection bar in the title bar no longer has a × to clear the selection**, on every table.
  It read as a stray close button beside Export (n) and Delete (n). The table's header checkbox
  clears a selection instead — pressed with anything ticked, it unticks every row on screen.
  [TableSelectionActions.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/TableSelectionActions.js)

- **A Super Admin can now reassign any open task**, from the task's ⋮ menu or its panel — before,
  only the person holding it could. The task's history records the holder it was taken from and
  the Super Admin who moved it ("Reassigned from A to B by C"), and the holder it was taken off is
  notified alongside the new holder and the giver. Starting, completing and cancelling stay with
  the task's own two people. No other role gains it. **"Super Admin" now means either kind**: the
  account whose own role column is SUPER_ADMIN, or one given the SUPER_ADMIN role in Role Management
  — the second used to be treated as an ordinary user here, for Edit and Delete too. The task menu's
  entries also lose their
  trailing "…" (Reassign, Cancel Task, Edit Task, Duplicate Task, Delete Task).
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/tasks/service.js),
  [TasksPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/TasksPage.js)

- **A lead's status now decides which follow-up date it needs.** CNA, Interested, Followup and
  Converted & Followup cannot be saved from the lead popup or Add Lead without a **Next Follow-up
  Date** (CNA and Proceed Next included, unless that press is the one that rejects the lead).
  Invalid and Rejected take no next follow-up, and neither does **Converted on Dum Dum and Corp**:
  the date is cleared, so those leads leave the Pending Followups tabs. A Converted **Qua Qua** lead
  keeps an optional next follow-up (the client comes back for the next shoot) and shows on the
  pending tabs when it is due. Moving a lead to **Converted** also sets its **Last Follow-up Date** to
  that day on every vertical, whether it is converted from the popup, Bulk Update (where the date is
  filled with today and can be changed) or a project save. Converted & Followup keeps its follow-ups.
  No permission change.
  [CRMPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CRMPage.js),
  [crmLeadService.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/crmLeadService.js)

- **Today, Yesterday and Overall Pending Followups now list every lead whose Next Followup Date
  matches, whatever its status.** They used to show only leads at status Followup, so a call booked
  on a lead at any other status was on no pending tab. Overall Pending is every lead dated today or
  earlier; a lead with no follow-up date is no longer counted in it. The CRM dashboard's follow-ups
  outstanding figure reads the same count. No permission change.
  [leadQueryService.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/leadQueryService.js)

- **The installed app takes the studio's name and favicon from Settings → Branding.** Installing
