  DBS Operations OS to a home screen or dock now names it after the studio and uses an icon drawn
  from the uploaded favicon - on Android, desktop Chrome/Edge and iPhone alike - instead of always
  "DBS Operations OS" and the bundled mark. The new public `/api/public/app-icon/<variant>.png`
  draws each size with `sharp` (the mark centred on a white square, Android's maskable pair at
  70%), reads only the studio's own upload - never fetches an address it was handed - and is rate
  limited per caller. With no studio name or favicon, or the API unreachable or unable to draw it,
  the bundled name and icons are used. The manifest is re-read every minute, so a change reaches
  the next install; an app already installed keeps its icon until it is installed again. No
  migration, no new permission
  ([manifest.js](../frontend/src/app/manifest.js),
  [appIcon.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/settings/appIcon.js)).

- **A login now lasts 18 hours instead of 24: somebody who has not logged out by then has that day
  marked Absent.** Nothing else about the rule changed - it runs from the **latest** login of the
  day, is exact to the minute and crosses midnight, so a 9:30 login can be logged out of until 3:29
  the next morning (it was 9:29), and logging in again restarts the clock. Past them, a day
  attendance was owed on reads **Absent** until an approved Attendance Regularization says what it
  was; a holiday, a weekly off or a day of leave still reads as the calendar says. Twenty-four hours
  let a day that ended at six in the evening stay "at work" until nine the next morning, into the
  following shift. The number lives in one place (`SESSION_VALID_HOURS`) and the server's refusal and
  the dashboard's notice are both built from it, so neither can be left saying the old figure.
  [attendanceRules.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/attendanceRules.js).
  **On deploy:** any login still open between its 18th and 24th hour becomes an expired login the
  moment this ships - those days read Absent and can no longer be logged out of, and the way back
  is an Attendance Regularization per day, as for any other missed logout. Nothing is written to the
  database by the change itself; the reading is worked out on the fly.

- **Client Name is the WhatsApp group name for every vertical.** Pre Production, Production, Shoot
  Board, Client Gifts, Feedback, Accounts, Payment Requests, Client Storage, Image Selection's
  dashboard, the Calendar and the Contacts directory showed the generator's own Client Name for a
  Qua Qua or Corp project ("Kavya") but the whole group name for a Dum Dum one, or for any project
  typed or imported without the generator - so one column mixed the two. They all show the
  WhatsApp group name now. The client's own gallery page and CRD form still greet them by their
  names. [projectClientNames.js](../backend/src/services/projectClientNames.js). No migration.

- **The Shoot Board's timeline zooms: − and + beside Today change how wide a day is.** The range
  filter decides which days are loaded, zoom how many of them are on screen at once, through five
  steps - roughly a working week, a fortnight, three weeks and a month on a laptop - so a month can
  be read at a glance instead of scrolled through four screens at a time. **Zoomed out, the whole of
  Next 30 days is on one screen**, and that is where it stops: thinner days than a month's worth are
  not worth reading, so a **longer range scrolls at the narrowest level** rather than being squeezed
  onto one screen. Only the day columns scale: the project column and the shoot bars stay the size
  they are, because this is the width of a day rather than the browser's zoom. **The day headers give
  way as the days narrow** instead of being cut off - the weekday shortens to a letter, the date's
  circle goes, and at the narrowest the date stands alone with the month named on the 1st - so a day
  is always still a dated column. The line above the board says which of the three states it is in -
  every day on screen, days as narrow as their dates can be read, or more days to the side - so a −
  that has stopped reads as finished rather than broken. A zoom keeps the day you were looking at
  rather than landing somewhere else in the month, and the level stays put when the date range
  changes. **Today moved to the left of the row**, where the eye starts, and stays there greyed when
  the board is already on today rather than appearing and disappearing; the controls at the right are
  now two bordered groups - how wide a day is, and which days are shown - instead of six loose icons,
  and zoom is a plain − and + rather than two magnifying glasses that differed only by the sign
  inside the lens. A control with nothing to do - Today on today, − at the narrowest - is now greyed
  rather than looking exactly like a live one. The pill is a new shared `ControlGroup`, so a pager or
  a month stepper elsewhere can be drawn the same way.
  [ControlGroup.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/ControlGroup.js).
- **The Shoot Board's Custom dates no longer grey out most of the calendar.** **To** was held to the
  From day and to the 92nd day after it, so with a From in the past everything before it and
  everything past day 92 was unpickable with nothing saying why - and picking an earlier From meant
  clearing To first. Every day is now pickable on both boxes and the rule is a sentence on the field
  ("The last day comes before the first", "Pick at most 92 days"); a pair that does not make a range
  leaves the board on the range it is already showing, as it did before.
  [ShootBoardPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/shoot-board/ShootBoardPage.js). [ShootTimeline.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/shoot-board/ShootTimeline.js),
  [shootBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/shootBoard.mjs). No migration, no new permission - it is a
  view control on a screen `PROJECT / Shoot Board` already opens.

- **A leave request can now be edited, taken back or deleted by the person who raised it, and sent
  back to them by an approver.** Each row's ⋮ offers the raiser **View, Edit, Revert back** and
  **Delete** in place of Withdraw, Cancel Leave and Apply again, and the approver **Approve, Reject**
  and **Send back** in place of Approve and Reject. A request now has six statuses - Pending, Send
  Back, Approved, Rejected, Reverted and Deleted - with a **Send Back** tab beside Pending for the
  raiser; Reverted, Deleted and the older Cancelled rows are found under All, each saying what it is,
  so the Rejected tab counts refusals and nothing else.
  - **An approver may change their own rejection to an approval, never an approval to a rejection.**
    A refusal they want to reconsider stays in their queue with Approve on it. An approval given is
    an approval given: undoing one is the raiser's to do by editing, or HR's by correcting the day.
  - **Editing clears every answer and asks all the approvers again.** An approval of 20-22 October is
    not an approval of 2-3 November, so an edited request goes back to Pending whatever it was -
    which means editing an **approved** leave stops those days reading "On leave" until it is
    approved again. The form says so when it saves. An edit runs every rule raising a request runs,
    so it cannot be a way round one.
  - **Send back returns a request to be fixed, with a required reason.** It is the answer for a
    request that is nearly right - the wrong dates, a reason nobody can act on - which until now had
    to be rejected. Every approval given so far is cleared and the request leaves the approvers'
    queues until the raiser sends it again.
  - **Delete deletes nothing.** The row stays and reads Deleted to whoever raised it, and is gone
    from the approvers' queues. Only an approved request ever counted towards the register, the
    reports or a leave balance, so a deleted one costs nothing by staying - and the old Withdraw
    really did delete the row, taking the approvers' answers with it.
  - **A Checkout Correction or an Attendance Regularization freezes once it is approved**, because
    approving one has already written onto the day - the session's checkout, or the day's status -
    and nothing undoes that. Such a row offers View alone, and the way to change the day is a fresh
    request for it. Every other kind stays editable.
  - Requests already in the database are untouched: a **Cancelled** row keeps reading Cancelled and
    is nobody's to act on. No new permission - `HRM / Requests` or `HRM / Employee Attendance` at
    Read is still all any of this asks, and who may answer a request is still the approvers named on
    it. [AttendanceRequestsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestsPage.js),
  [attendanceRequestStatus.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/attendanceRequestStatus.mjs),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/controller.js).

- **The Quotation Calculator is a screen of its own, opened in a new tab.** It was a dialog over
  the lead popup; pricing a quotation is not a question somebody answers in a moment and dismisses -
  it is a screen they sit on, with the catalogue, the bookings for a date and a dozen rows, and on a
  phone a dialog that tall was a page with a border drawn round it. The lead popup's **Quotation
  Calculator** button opens `/sales/quotation-calculator?lead=<enquiry id>` in a **tab of its own**,
  carrying the lead and **leaving the lead open behind it** - the pricing is read off the lead, so
  taking the one tab to the calculator meant going back and opening the lead again to check
  anything. **Back** closes that tab, or goes to the leads screen where the browser will not close
  it. Nothing about the pricing changed: the
  same arithmetic, the same catalogue, the same Apply to Quotation handing its rows to the Quotation
  Generator with nothing saved until Generate Quotation. Opened without a lead it still prices, and
  an **Enquiry ID** picker appears so the figures can reach a quotation - shown only to somebody who
  may read that list (`SALES / Sales Manager`), since the page itself answers to Quotation
  Management and a picker nobody can load is worse than none.
  [QuotationCalculatorPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationCalculatorPage.js),
  [CRMPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CRMPage.js). No migration.
  **Access:** no new permission - the route answers to the same `SALES / Quotation Management` the
  generator does, so whoever could price yesterday can price today. **It is deliberately not in the
  sidebar:** two menu screens may not share a permission, or Role Management could not grant one
  without the other, so it is a guarded route reached from a lead - the shape
  `/sales/crd-documents` already has. Say the word if you would rather it were listed, and it needs
  a `SALES / Quotation Calculator` permission of its own, seeded and migrated, ticked per role.
- **The Quotation Generator no longer invents a price.** A service or deliverable that Settings
  configures no price for - no pricing line for the shoot, no size or variant price, no flat
  price, no package price - used to be charged at the studio's blanket ₹2,000 service or ₹1,000
  deliverable rate; it is now ₹0, and the line says what it is charged. No GST rate is assumed
  either: the brand's or the studio's configured rate is the one used, and the client's copy prints
  no GST line where a quotation carries none, instead of "+ 18%". The server's own defaults (2000,
  1000, 20%, 18%) are gone with them: settings that are not stored answer as nothing. Every line
  is now saved with the price it is charged at, ₹0 included. A quotation saved before this keeps
  the prices it was saved with - its unpriced lines are stamped, as it opens, with the figure its
  own saved rates charged them at - so its total, client view, PDF and register entry are
  unchanged. Configured prices, package prices, Session Timing repricing, complimentary lines,
  discounts and the order they come off in are unchanged. See
  [quotationBrand.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/quotationBrand.mjs).

- **The client's quotation header reads as one set, and Event Type names the Main Event.** The ten
  cards under the client's name used three type styles - a typewriter face for Quotation ID,
  Contact Number and Enquiry ID, italics for Event Venue and Event Type - and every value now uses
  the Client Name's; the labels above them are unchanged. Event Type, which listed as many events
  as fitted, now names the Main Event and counts the rest: "Wedding", "Wedding +1 event", "Wedding
  +2 events". The Main Event is the one the quotation already marks (its first event on a quotation
  from before that), and the count is every other event, a repeated type included. Nothing about
  the quotation, its events or its PDF changes but how this card reads. See
  [PublicQuotationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/PublicQuotationPage.js) and
  [quotationEventTypes.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/quotationEventTypes.mjs).

- **Add Shoot's selected shoots can each be duplicated or removed from a ⋯ menu that is always in
  view.** With several shoots added, the list is wider than the dialog and its Remove link sat at
  the far right, reachable only by scrolling sideways. The list keeps its layout and still scrolls
  sideways; each row now ends in a ⋯ pinned to the right edge of the list, opening **Duplicate** - a
  copy of the row straight after it, every value kept, never the Main Event, so the mark stays on
  the one shoot that had it - and **Remove**. Both change the list in the dialog only; nothing is
  written until Save, exactly as before, and past a dozen rows the list scrolls down inside itself
  rather than growing the dialog. The same dialog serves the Quotation Generator, Booking,
  Converted and Start Project, so all four behave alike. See
  [AddShootDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/AddShootDialog.js).

- **A feedback's assigned issues say who has them and where they stand.** In Customer Issues and
  Feedback's info panel and View, the one "Assigned Issues" line ("Review (Average) - Anitha
  Ravichandran, DBS-TK-00043: Open") is now fields of their own for each Average or Poor review:
  **Assigned To**, **Task Status** (the task's own progress in HRM → Tasks - Pending, In Progress,
  Completed, Reassigned, Cancelled), **Task ID**, **Outcome** (Open, Issues sorted, Rejected) and
  Remarks once written. Several issues are each named by their review ("Sales (Poor) - Assigned
  To"); an unassigned one reads "Nobody". The server now sends each issue's task status
  ([feedbackRecord.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/feedbackRecord.mjs),
  [feedback/service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/feedback/service.js)).
- **Project Management → Feedback is now "Customer Issues and Feedback".** The sidebar entry, the page
  heading and the name Role Management lists it under (which it takes from the sidebar). The address
  (`/project-management/feedback`), the sidebar id and the `PROJECT / Feedback` permission are
  unchanged, so links, saved sidebar layouts and role grants carry on as they were
  ([navigation.mjs](../frontend/src/constants/navigation.mjs),
  [FeedbackPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackPage.js)).
- **The Attendance WhatsApp Report's send time is set in Settings.** Settings → User Settings →
  Attendance WhatsApp Report → **Sends daily at** is a time an administrator edits (hour, minute,
  am/pm, India time) and saves, where it was fixed in the code. Stored in the new
  `hrm_settings.attendance_report_send_at` (migration `20261008140000_attendance_report_send_at`, one
  nullable column - empty is the default, 10:00 am since the change below, so nothing changes until
  somebody saves a time), read by the
  sender every minute, so a change applies at once: a day already sent is not sent again, a day not
  yet sent goes at the new time. `PUT /api/hrm/attendance/report-group/send-at` `{ sendAt: "HH:MM" }`
  (or `""` for the default), administrators only, like the group name. The server's
  `ATTENDANCE_REPORT_SEND_AT` testing override still wins, and the page then shows the time as fixed
  on the server instead of offering to change it
  ([reportGroup.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/reportGroup.js),
  [AttendanceWhatsAppReportPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/AttendanceWhatsAppReportPanel.js)).

- **The Attendance Register's daily WhatsApp report now sends at 10:00 am**, studio time, every day -
  it was 9:45. The retry window is unchanged at 135 minutes from the send time, so a WhatsApp that is
  down at ten is still tried every five minutes until a quarter past twelve and then the day is let
  go; that used to end at noon. It is the **default**, which the Settings panel above now lets an
  administrator change: a studio that has never set a time gets 10:00, and one that has keeps what it
  saved. [reportGroup.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/reportGroup.js).
  **Deploy:** nothing to run, **but check the server's `.env`**: `ATTENDANCE_REPORT_SEND_AT` overrides
  this and is read on every check, so a value left in there from testing keeps the old time whatever
  the code says. Remove it, or set it to `10:00`.

- **The CRM board's columns stand in the pipeline's order rather than by size.** Unassigned, Yet to
  connect, Followup, Interested, CNA, Converted & Followup, Converted, Rejected, Invalid — read left
  to right, that is the question a pipeline board exists to answer, where a lead goes next, which is
  not a question the biggest column answers. They were ordered by how many leads each held, largest
  first, and re-sorted as the counts arrived: the board visibly rearranged itself as the columns
  answered, and one could move out from under somebody reading it. The heading still carries each
  column's count. This is the **board's** order and not the status pills', which keep the order a
  status is offered in inside the lead popup and the info panel — two different questions. A status
  the board's list does not name falls in after the named ones rather than having no column at all.
  [CRMPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CRMPage.js),
  [CrmKanbanBoard.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CrmKanbanBoard.js). No migration.

- **An enquiry can be booked as a project more than once.** Create Project's enquiry picker used to
  leave out every enquiry that already had a live project, which meant the studio could not book the
  same client again - a second wedding, another event on the one enquiry - because an id cannot be
  typed past a filter that excludes it. Those enquiries are offered now, each carrying a quiet
  **"1 project" / "2 projects"** beside its id, so a second booking is a choice somebody makes rather
  than one they make by accident from a stale tab. Nothing in the database ever held the
  one-project-per-enquiry rule, so the picker was the whole of it and it was never an enforcement:
  two people booking at once already produced a second project, silently. Deleted projects are not
  counted - a booking somebody undid is not one the enquiry has. The lead popup's **Converted
  History** tab already lists several projects against one lead.
  [projects/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js),
  [EnquiryCombobox.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/EnquiryCombobox.js). No migration.

- **The vertical is called Vertical everywhere, and Dum Dum reads DD - not Product and not WED.**
  Pre Production's table, its CSV export, both info panels, the shoot summary and the panel
  descriptions said "Product" and showed the stored code, so a Dum Dum project read "WED"; they
  now say Vertical and show DD / QQ / Corp, the way the Projects register already did. The same
  stored code had leaked onto CRM's bookings table and a project's Branch fallback (now DD), the
  Meetings register and its record (now Dum Dum / Qua Qua / Corp, matching the leads beside them -
  which also makes the Verticals filter find project rows), the project Status tab's Vertical when
  the vertical record is not linked, and the AI assistant's project summary. The sale form's
  "Product (Group Type)" is now "Vertical". `WED` itself is unchanged where it belongs: the stored
  value and the WhatsApp group name. Client Storage's own free-text "Product" field is a different
  thing and keeps its name.
  [PreProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionPage.js),
  [infoPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/infoPanelConfig.js),
  [SaleDetailsSection.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SaleDetailsSection.js),
  [meetingSources.js](../frontend/src/lib/meetingSources.js),
  [stage.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/stage.js). No migration.

- **Closing On duty / travel opened from Login goes back to Login.** The ✕ or Cancel on the Mark
  on-duty / travel box, when it was opened from the Login box's On-duty / Travel button, now returns
  to the Login box instead of leaving the login altogether; raising the request still closes both.
  [EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js).
- **On duty / travel can no longer be marked for a day that has already passed.** In the Mark
  on-duty / travel dialog both calendars now start at today, and a past From date is refused - by the
  form before it is sent, and by the server. Leave is unchanged: it can still be applied for a day
  already gone. [AttendanceRequestDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestDialog.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/controller.js).
- **HRM → Employee Attendance is now called Attendance.** The sidebar entry and the page's heading
  read Attendance. The address (`/hrm/employee-attendance`) and the `HRM / Employee Attendance`
  permission are unchanged, so bookmarks and role grants keep working.
  [navigation.mjs](../frontend/src/constants/navigation.mjs),
  [EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js).
- **A half day now runs from "Half day from" up to the full day, and "Half day up to" is gone.**
  Settings → Attendance Rules no longer has a Half day up to field. A day worked from Half day from
  (240 minutes by default) up to, but not including, the Full day (510) reads **Half day**; under
  Half day from it reads Absent, as before. Half day is read first, so a day short of the full day
  is a Half day even if it was also late or cut early - Late and Early exit are now said only of a
  day that still reaches the full day (10:30 to 18:30 is a Half day; 10:30 to 19:00 is Late). Every day already recorded is read
  again under the new rule, on the register, the employee's own page, the calendar and the monthly
  counts. Half day from must now be less than the full day. Migration
  `20261008120000_attendance_half_day_up_to_full_day` drops `attendance_settings.half_day_max_minutes`.
  **Deploy:** stop the API, run `npx prisma migrate deploy` and `npx prisma generate`, then start it
  again - an API left running reads the dropped column and fails on attendance until it restarts.
  [attendanceRules.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/attendanceRules.js),
  [AttendanceRulesPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRulesPanel.js).
- **The Feedback page lists each project once, as its latest feedback stage.** A project's New Project,
  Production Completion and Project Completed Feedback are three feedbacks, each with its own ID, and
  each used to stay on the tab its own review sent it to - so a project with all three given still
  showed its New Project Feedback under Completed. Now, once a later stage is waiting or given, the
  earlier stages leave the tabs: the row is the latest stage, on that stage's tab, and the earlier
  ones are read in its info panel and View. A feedback still under Issues is the exception - it stays
  on Issues until it is sorted or rejected, because it still needs the team.
  [feedbackRecord.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/feedbackRecord.mjs),
  [FeedbackPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackPage.js).
- **The Attendance Register's Break and Permissions cards now show who is on one right now.** They
  used to count everybody who had taken a break, or held an approved permission, at any point today;
  now each counts - and, when pressed, lists - only the people whose break is running, or who are
  inside their permission's time window, at this moment. A break that has ended, or a permission over
  or still to come, is not counted. The table still shows each person's break time and permission
  times for the day, with **On break** or **On permission** beside the one running now. The summary
  fields are `onBreak` (was `breaks`) and `onPermission`; the day's `permission` count stays for the
  Send report.
  [AttendanceRegisterPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRegisterPage.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js).
- **The Attendance Register's Today's Attendance table opens in a new column order:** Employee,
  Login location, Status, Branch, Login, Logout, Worked, Permission, Break. Anybody can still drag
  the columns into their own order, and somebody who already has is kept on theirs.
  [AttendanceRegisterPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRegisterPage.js).
- **A branch's "Google Review URL" is now called "Review Link".** Settings → Organization → Branches →
  External URLs shows it, and offers it in the + Add external URL dropdown, as Review Link. Only the
  name changed - the link a branch already holds is kept, and the feedback thank-you message still
  uses it for its review request.
  [BranchesPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/BranchesPanel.js).
- **The message sent to a client whose feedback is filed under Issues has new wording.** It now reads:
  "Thank you for sharing your feedback about your project. We’ve received it and will review the issues
  you raised. Our team will get back to you soon." and asks them to mention the Feedback ID if they
  contact the studio. The stored Feedback Issues template is replaced only where it still held the old
  default, so a message already reworded in Settings → Message Templates is kept; the app's own
  fallback says the same.
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`.
  [feedbackMessage.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/feedbackMessage.mjs),
  [migration](../backend/prisma/migrations/20261008100000_feedback_issues_message_wording/migration.sql).
- **An expired link no longer says anything about what it was for.** The expired page every client
  link lapses to - quotation (and its Terms and Payment pages), Photo Selection, Signature Album,
  Album Proofing and event gallery - used to show a card naming the link's type, the client and the
  day it expired. It now shows only the logo, "This link has expired", "This link is no longer
  active." and whom to ask for a new link. The server stopped sending those details too: every
  expired answer is the same 410 with an empty `expiredLink` and one message for every kind of link
  ("This link has expired. Please contact the studio for a new link." - no longer "This quotation
  link…", "This gallery link…"), and the gallery no longer looks the client's name up to fill it. See
  [ExpiredClientLink.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/ExpiredClientLink.js) and
  [expiredLink.js](../backend/src/services/expiredLink.js). Active links, PINs, expiry and renewal
  are unchanged.

- **A deliverable reads by its brand and size from the quotation through to the project.** A
  quotation line such as `Painting - textra - 12x6 - 2` used to arrive on the project as
  `Painting`, and two brands or sizes of the same deliverable on one shoot stopped the project
  from being created. Every screen that lists deliverable lines - Quotation Generator, Create
  Project / booking, the project's edit screen, the project table's Post Production Deliverables
  column and the info panel - now names them through one formatter,
  [deliverableBrands.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/deliverableBrands.mjs), and the project pickers list
  each brand and size the way the quotation's does, searchable by any of them. A project line keeps
  the variant it was sold as in three new nullable columns on `project_shoot_deliverable`
  (`brand_name`, `frame_inches`, `video_length`, beside the existing `size`) - migration
  `20261007120000_project_deliverable_variant_snapshot`, additive, run with `prisma migrate deploy`.
  A shoot now holds one line per variant of a deliverable, not one per deliverable. A deliverable
  with no brands names itself by the brand and size it was given before brands existed. Pricing,
  quantities, complimentary lines and totals are unchanged, and lines saved earlier read by the
  deliverable's name as before. No permission changed.
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate`.

- **Feedback is now asked for on each project as soon as it is created - "New Project
  Feedback" - instead of on each shoot Production completes, and the feedback given on shoots is
  removed.** Every project created in Sales & CRM → Bookings & Converted appears under Project
  Management → Feedback → Yet to be done; Give Feedback rates the project as a whole (the form names
  the project and shows its Event ID, client, status, main event date, branch and CRM), and the
  review files it under Completed or Issues as before. One per project: once given, the project
  leaves Yet to be done, and a second is refused - also when two people save at once. Completed
  shoots no longer come in, the table's Shoot ID and Shoot columns and the Shoot section of the info
  panel are gone, and the client's message thanks them for feedback on "your project". A feedback's
  View and info panel read Project first, then **New Project Feedback**, then **Production
  Completion Feedback** and **Project Completed Feedback**, both locked until they open: greyed and
  unclickable in the View's sidebar, with nothing of them shown, and a one-line reason in
  the info panel - a new `locked` section option in the shared record view
  ([RecordDetails.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/RecordDetails.js)) and a `disabled`
  section in every form panel's sidebar ([SchemaFormSidebar.js](../frontend/src/components/schema-form/SchemaFormSidebar.js)). Existing live
  projects with no feedback appear in Yet to be done too. No new permission - still
  PROJECT / Feedback.
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` - this **deletes every feedback given on a shoot** (the
  studio's decision; Feedback IDs are not reused), drops `project_feedback.shoot_id` and adds a
  unique `project_id` - then `npx prisma generate` and restart the API.
  [FeedbackPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackPage.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/feedback/service.js),
  [migration](../backend/prisma/migrations/20261007180000_project_feedback_new_project/migration.sql).
- **"Attendance regularization" is now spelled "Attendance Regularization"** wherever the request
  type is shown - Raise Request, the request tables, the approve and reject dialog and its
  notifications. [attendanceRequestConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/attendanceRequestConfig.js).
- **A client's username is now their mobile number.** Create Project → Client Credentials (and
  Edit Sale Details for a project booked without a login) no longer asks for a Username: it shows
  the ten digits of the Client Main Number, without the country code, and the server makes the
  login with that - a username sent from the browser is ignored. A number already used as a login
  username, such as a client booking a second project, is refused with a message saying so.
  [ClientCredentialsSection.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/ClientCredentialsSection.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js). No migration.
- **The Login, Logout and break selfie now opens the camera inside the circle itself.** Pressing
  Login shows the live camera straight away in the round frame, and the camera button on it takes
  the picture; once taken, the photo fills the circle and the same button retakes it. There is no
  separate camera window and no Open camera step any more.
  [EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js).
- **Approving or rejecting an attendance regularization now shows the day's current status and
  what it would change to.** The decision dialog lists Current Status and Change To above the
  employee's reason, so the approver sees the change being asked for without opening the request.
  [attendanceRequests.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/attendanceRequests.js).
- **Nebula's follow-up questions no longer slow down as a conversation grows, and keep their
  topic.** Answers already streamed word by word; the wait was before the first word, while the
  model read the prompt - and each question's figures sat ahead of the conversation, so the whole
  conversation was read afresh every time (17 seconds after three exchanges, 27 after six, on a
  laptop without a GPU). The figures now sit beside the question, so the model reuses what it read
  last time and a follow-up waits the same ~14 seconds however long the chat is. Follow-ups also
  answer from the right figures: "which of them is the oldest?" after a question about leave
  requests looked up nothing and described the oldest employee with invented tenures, and "who has
  the most pending?" one question later was refused as off-topic.
  [orchestrator.js](../backend/src/services/ai/orchestrator.js),
  [intent.js](../backend/src/services/ai/intent.js),
  [requests.js](../backend/src/services/ai/tools/requests.js).
- **Nebula keeps your conversation when you move to another section, and forgets it after 30
  minutes of quiet.** A conversation started in Projects was gone from the panel the moment you
  opened HRM - it was kept per section. It is now one thread across the app, with a small "Now in
  HRM" line where the conversation moved, so it is clear which section answered. It is cleared 30
  minutes after the last question or answer - opening the panel does not keep it alive, and an open
  panel says so - and still on a refresh. **New chat**, above the thread once there is one, starts
  again straight away, with Undo on the notice. Each answer is still limited to what that section
  lets you see.
  [sessionChats.js](../frontend/src/lib/ai/sessionChats.js),
  [AIAssistant.js](../frontend/src/components/ai/AIAssistant.js).
- **Nebula can tell you which HRM requests are still pending - the ones you may see on HRM →
  Requests, and no others.** "Is there any raise request in the HRM still pending" was refused as
  "outside the CRM"; it is now a lookup from every panel: your own requests and the ones you are
  named as an approver on (every colleague's with HRM / All Requests), pending unless you ask for
  approved, rejected or cancelled, with how many are waiting on your answer. It opens with HRM /
  Employee Attendance or HRM / Requests, the requests screen's own pair, and never sends the reason
  somebody wrote. A refusal now names the panel's own subject - an HRM panel no longer says
  "outside the CRM". No new permission and no migration.
  [requests.js](../backend/src/services/ai/tools/requests.js),
  [intent.js](../backend/src/services/ai/intent.js),
  [modules.js](../backend/src/services/ai/modules.js),
  [ai/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/ai/controller.js).
- **Nebula can tell you who is present today - inside every access rule - and counts projects per
  manager.** Asked "how many of them are present today" after a project list, it answered "both are
  present" from no data at all: attendance words were not recognised as a question about records, so
  nothing was looked up, and it had no attendance to look at anyway. Now attendance is a lookup
  offered beside whichever panel is open, and each rule is checked in code: **HRM / Employee
  Attendance** at Read to ask at all; your **own day** always; **anybody else's only with HRM /
  Attendance Approval** at Read (the Attendance Register's rule); and only **within that grant's data
  scope** - the branches its roles reach and your team - which is narrower than the register screen;
  **today or the last 31 days**, never the future; name, status and times only. Statuses come from
  the register's own reckoning, read once a minute at most. **Ranges too** - "the last five working
  days records of Mukesh", "last week", "28 Sep to 2 Oct": each person's totals as the **Attendance
  Dashboard** counts them (`attendanceOverview`), over the studio's own working days (its weekly offs
  and holidays), with the working days and the days that are none of present, absent or on leave (a
  login never logged out) stated - so Nebula's figures are the Dashboard's, not a guess at the gap.
  People are recognised by their own names among those within reach, not guessed from unusual
  words; with nobody named, only totals for everyone within reach - never a colleague's line. Attendance words count only in context
  ("is Arun present", "present today", "how many ... absent") - "present the pipeline" and "how many
  leads came in today" are not attendance. Asked about attendance without access, Nebula says it
  cannot see it.
  The project summary now has **one line per project manager** (with their statuses), by the linked
  employee - it had read the status total (2) as Arun's count (1).
  [tools/attendance.js](../backend/src/services/ai/tools/attendance.js),
  [modules.js](../backend/src/services/ai/modules.js),
  [accessContext.js](../backend/src/services/ai/accessContext.js),
  [intent.js](../backend/src/services/ai/intent.js),
  [read.service.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/read.service.js).

- **Nebula now follows one workflow: ask → qwen3:8b understands → RBAC and record scope →
  read-only lookup → answer.** The model is **qwen3:8b** (was `qwen3:1.7b`). Every lookup now checks
  the record as well as the module: lead search carries the CRM board's own branch/owner scope into
  its SQL, and a single lead - its details, activity, call logs, transcripts - is "not found" unless
  the board would show it to that person. Nebula is **read-only**: it answers, summarises and
  explains, and changes nothing - the one write it had (adding a remark after a confirm card) is
  gone, with its card, `/api/ai/confirm` and the action-plan sweep, and the tool registry refuses
  any tool that is not READ. The **lead assistant** inside a lead follows the same rules: it reads
  only a lead the person may see, runs under the same rate and queue limits, honours `AI_ENABLED`,
  and needs `SALES / CRM Leads` at **Read** (it asked Read/Write before only because its questions
  are POSTs), so a role holding CRM Leads at Read alone can now ask about the leads it can see. A
  call transcript is its lead's: out of reach - or tied to no lead, for anybody the scope narrows -
  it answers "no longer exists", the same as a missing one. A reader who closes the panel mid-answer
  now cancels the generation instead of leaving it holding one of the assistant's few slots, and a
  refusal before the answer starts (a lead out of reach, the assistant switched off, too busy) shows
  the server's own reason rather than "responded 404".
  [tools/sales.js](../backend/src/services/ai/tools/sales.js),
  [tools/registry.js](../backend/src/services/ai/tools/registry.js),
  [crm-ai/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-ai/controller.js),
  [AI-CONTEXT.md](project-state/AI-CONTEXT.md).
  **Deploy:** `ollama pull qwen3:8b` on the server (~5.2GB, ~6GB RAM; slow on a small CPU-only box -
  set `OLLAMA_MODEL` to a smaller model there if it cannot carry it). The `ai_action_plan` table is
  left in place, unused.

- **The client's sign-in and project pages are designed as the studio's own: a contact sheet in
  gold.** A three-colour palette defined once on the client pages (`app/client/layout.js`) - **gold
  #D6B11A** for every action and the stage being worked on, **sand #E4C9B0** for developed frames
  and the page's warm ground, **earth #856B50** for text and the sign-in's panel - with Cormorant
  Garamond for the page's voice (the project's name, a stage's name) and Plus Jakarta Sans for the
  rest, the two faces the client's quotation already uses. Gold carries dark ink, never white, and
  is never thin text on white. **The project page** keeps the studio's mark and **Sign out** fixed
  at the top on a blurred band of sand as the page scrolls, and opens straight onto its five stages as frames
  on a strip of film: the stages done developed in sand with an earth tick, the one being worked on
  gold with a slow sheen crossing it, the rest blank negatives. Under it, the stage's sheet: a gold
  ring showing how far through its shoots it is, **Your team** - the people looking after it, by
  name, with their initials - its details with an icon each (status, Event ID, branch, vertical,
  event date), **Gifts from the studio** as gift cards, and **Your shoots** as photo prints with
  the date written under each in the serif. As it opens the strip winds in, its frames develop in
  order and the ring draws itself to where the stage stands - one moment, and still for anybody
  whose device asks for less motion. On a phone the strip swipes and opens on the frame being worked
  on. Every stage reached so far can be tapped to open its own sheet, so a finished stage - its
  team, its details, its shoots - stays readable after it is over; the stage being worked on is the
  way back, and a stage still to come is no button. The studio's mark and **Sign out** (on a phone
  its gold sign-out icon alone; wider, a deep ink pill with the icon and the words) stay fixed at
  the top, and once the strip has scrolled away, scrolling back up slides a copy of it down under
  that bar (scrolling down tucks it away again, and a stage tapped on it opens that stage's sheet
  and brings it into view; on a phone both strips keep the stage being read in their middle, and a
  swipe along one moves the other), so where the project stands is always a flick away. The
  project's own name is not shown. The CRD document sits under the **Pre Production** sheet only -
  it is part of planning the shoots - as an invitation: a deep earth card, **CRD Document**, with a
  gold **Complete**. **Sign in** has its own frame instead of the studio's login: an earth panel
  with the line "Your day, frame by frame." and the pictures from Client page images drifting past on a
  strip (warm exposures of the palette until there are any), the form on a glass card over the
  same dark ground that runs under the whole page - about half white, the ground and its gold light
  blurred through it, every word on it in the studio's ink (a grey fades on half-white glass), its
  fields whiter panes - drawn in from the screen's edges, and on a phone rising over the strip's
  foot. The studio's mark is fixed at the screen's top left, on a translucent blurred band of the
  dark ground as the page scrolls under it on a phone, in its light lettering: with no logo uploaded, a dark surface's mark (`AppLogo surface="dark"`) is now the
  white-lettered bundled one rather than the theme's choice. Status pills keep their own colours. Built from
  the shared pieces - `FilmStrip` (new, `components/client`), `DashboardCard` takes an optional `id` and
  `titleClassName` - so no studio screen changes, and `TextField`'s `prefix` / `suffix` now centre
  on the box whatever its height (the ₹ and % fields look as before). [ProjectTracker.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/ProjectTracker.js),
  [FilmStrip.js](../frontend/src/components/client/FilmStrip.js),
  [ClientAuthLayout.js](../frontend/src/components/client/ClientAuthLayout.js),
  [app/client/layout.js](../frontend/src/app/client/layout.js).
- **The CRD form a client fills in from their link fits a phone.** On a phone the header is a
  compact strip (the logo smaller, the title in two short lines) instead of a sixth of the screen,
  and the bar underneath is one slim progress line over **Save Draft** and **Submit** side by side
  (Qua Qua's **Back / Save Draft / Submit** too), kept clear of the iPhone home bar - so a 360px
  phone shows about a quarter more of the form at a time. Every field is 16px and thumb-high there,
  which also stops iOS zooming the page in on each tap; the section tabs keep the one being read in
  view, with a fade at the edge saying there are more; and the Terms read in the page's own scroll
  rather than in a box scrolling inside it. Tablet and desktop are unchanged. Both verticals now
  draw one shared header and footer (`CrdDocumentHeader`, `CrdDocumentFooter`) instead of a copy
  each. The larger fields are scoped to this page (`.crd-public-form` in `globals.css`) - no studio
  screen moves. [crdDocumentShared.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/crdDocumentShared.js),
  [globals.css](../frontend/src/app/globals.css).
- **CRD Documents: Create Link, then a ready-to-send message.** A row whose link has not gone out
  now offers **Create Link**; creating it moves the row to **Yet To Receive** straight away and
  opens **CRD Link Ready** - the link written as a message in the new **CRD Document Link**
  template (Settings → Message Templates), with **Copy message**, **Send WhatsApp** and **Done**.
  Send WhatsApp posts the message into the **project's own WhatsApp group** from the sender's
  WhatsApp: the group linked to the project on Pre Production → General (where Production's
  messages go), else Image Selection's link for the sale, else the one group in their WhatsApp
  named like the project and held by no other project. The button names the group before anything
  is sent, and a match by name is not saved anywhere - linking stays Pre Production's and Image
  Selection's, under their own permissions. A row already sent offers
  **Send Link** to open the same dialog again. It replaces the old dialog that opened `wa.me` on
  the client's number, and fixes Send Link leaving a document raised by the project on "Link Not
  sent". People with CRD Documents may now read message templates, so the dialog uses the
  studio's wording. [CrdLinkReadyDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CrdLinkReadyDialog.js),
  [CrdDocumentsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CrdDocumentsPage.js),
  [groupSend.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crd-documents/groupSend.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (adds the CRD Document Link template if absent).
- **Attendance WhatsApp Report, laid out afresh.** Settings → User Settings → Attendance WhatsApp
  Report opens on an at-a-glance strip (`RecordSummaryCard`): when it sends, and whether today's
  report went and who sent it. Below it, **Who sends it** and **Where it goes**
  are two `DashboardCard`s side by side from `lg` at the same height, stacked (sender first) below
  that. The group name's Save and Clear sit on one row with the field; Clear is a secondary button
  now, since it already asks before clearing. Only existing components and styles are used, and
  nothing about what the panel does has changed
  ([AttendanceWhatsAppReportPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/AttendanceWhatsAppReportPanel.js)).
- **The account menu no longer offers Raise Request to an administrator.** It was shown greyed out
  with a tooltip, since administrators do not raise leave, permission or comp-off requests of their
  own; a row they can never use is now left out. Everybody else who can raise a request still sees
  it. The Raise Request button on HRM → Request is unchanged
  ([AppTopbar.js](../frontend/src/components/app-shell/AppTopbar.js)).
- **A vendor can have several Vendor Types.** Vendors → Add Vendor → Business Details → **Vendor
  Type** is a searchable multi-select now - a studio that shoots and edits is both a Photographer
  and an Editor. At least one is still required, and the form says so on the field before saving.
  The types are stored in the one column joined by ", " ("Photographer, Editor"), the way an
  employee's Skills are, and every path reads them that way: the vendor list's Vendor Type filter
  finds a vendor by any one of its types (a whole entry - "Editor" does not match "Photo Editor"),
  a spreadsheet import takes several in one cell ("Photographer; Editor"), and Settings → Fields →
  Vendor Types counts a vendor as using every type it names and renames a type inside the list.
  Existing vendors keep their single type unchanged. A Vendor Type's name can no longer contain a
  comma, which the column could not tell apart. Migration `20261001100000_vendor_type_multiple`
  widens `vendor.vendor_type` from 100 to 500 characters - a quick table rebuild that cannot fail
  on existing data. No permission changes. Like Skills, this is text rather than a junction table
  of ids (Rule 5), which a later change could add. On the same form, **Preferred Languages** and
  **Skills** now show their chosen entries as chips **inside** the input box, each with its own ×,
  rather than in a row under it (Languages) or only as a count (Skills); Backspace in an empty box
  takes the last one off. Languages is the shared chips field (`EmailChipsField`, which now takes
  its entry check and separators as props - a space no longer splits "Old English"), and Skills
  keeps its grouped list with the chips in its search box (`SearchableMultiSelect`'s new `chips`).
  Every other form using either field is unchanged. Capabilities also has a new **Supported
  Branches** field: a searchable multi-select of the studio's active branches, re-read when a
  branch is saved in Settings, and listed by name in the vendor's details. It is stored as links to
  the branches - a new `vendor_branch` table of vendor and branch ids (migration
  `20261001110000_vendor_supported_branches`, a new empty table) - never as names, so renaming a
  branch needs nothing; the server refuses a branch that is not active. Any active branch can be
  chosen, as vendors belong to the studio rather than to one branch. Existing vendors start with
  none, and the spreadsheet import does not set them. After it, Capabilities asks **"Can be a
  production team member?"** with a **Yes / No** radio - one answer only, and **No** unless somebody
  says Yes: the form opens with No chosen, every existing vendor reads as No, and a vendor imported
  or created without it is No (migration `20261001120000_vendor_production_team_member` adds the
  column with a default of No). A spreadsheet import takes it as a column, reading Yes, No, Y, N,
  True or False
  ([VendorFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/assets/VendorFormPanel.js),
  [vendors.controller.js](../backend/src/modules/assets/vendors.controller.js),
  [definitions.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/master-data/definitions.js)).
- **An Incorrect login now counts as Absent on the Self Dashboard, and its own card is gone.** A
  login nobody logged out of within 24 hours, on a day that was owed, was shown as a separate
  **Incorrect Login** figure - neither present nor absent. It now counts in **Absent**: the day
  was not attended, and until a Correction says otherwise there is nothing to show it was. The day
  list still names each one "Incorrect login", so the reason is not lost, and a Correction raised
  for it works as before. Both the short-range and the figures-only (long-range) totals count it
  the same way, so the card does not change meaning with the range chosen
  ([service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js),
  [EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js)).

- **A payment received through the "Other" mode no longer asks who received it, and that mode's box
  is now Remarks.** In both places money in is recorded - Accounts → Cash Entry (Cash Received) and
  **Payment Received** on the form that books a project, which Create Project, Bookings & Converted
  and Quotations all share - choosing a payment mode that carries a remark ("Other" out of the box,
  set per mode in Settings → Field Settings → Accounts → Payment Mode) drops the **Receiver** box.
  There the remark says what the payment actually was and the person filing it is the person it
  happened to, so Receiver asked the form to repeat what the login already says. Nothing is stored in
  its place: nobody is asked, so the answer is unknown rather than a guess at it. **Every other mode
  is exactly as it was** - money received by cash, UPI or a transfer still names who took it, and
  money out always names who paid it. **Payment Mode Details** is renamed **Remarks** - the same box
  and the same stored value, still required wherever it appears, because that is what it always was:
  a remark about the *mode*. The entry's **Description** is a different question - about the payment
  as a whole - and stays optional; the table and the info panel call the first one **Payment Mode
  Remarks**, where the two sit side by side with nothing else to tell them apart.
  [accountsConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/accountsConfig.js),
  [cash-entries/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/accounts/cash-entries/controller.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate` - `handler_name` becomes
  nullable, which touches no existing row.
  **Two consequences, and both are limited to an "Other"-mode receipt.** `handlerEmployeeId` is one
  of the columns `dataScope` narrows the cash book by, so such an entry is reached through **whoever
  created it** (and their managers, whose reach includes their team's logins) rather than through a
  receiver it does not name. In practice that is the same person - the one who files a receipt is the
  one taking the money - but somebody only *named* as the receiver would not see it. Branch reach
  does not widen it either, this module declaring owner columns, so only an `ADMIN / Branch
  Administration` holder sees by branch. And a report grouped by Received / Paid By shows nothing for
  those entries; the column keeps that name, because the entries filed before this do carry a
  receiver. Entries already filed keep theirs, and an edit cannot erase it - the save leaves that
  column untouched rather than writing a blank over it, which is also what keeps a receiver when a
  mode is changed to Other afterwards. An approved payment request that returns money to the studio
  still records who took it: the rule is that a receiver is not insisted on, not that one is
  discarded.
  **Imports:** the spreadsheet column is headed **Remarks** now and **"Payment Mode Details" still
  reads**, so a file the studio saved before the rename imports exactly as it did - a column may now
  carry `aliases`, which both importers honour.

- **CRM Leads and Follow-ups pick Table or Board from a dropdown.** The two tabs beside My Leads
  are now one compact dropdown, styled like the CRM board switch next to it; the choice is still
  remembered per person, and still not offered on the Call Box.
  [CRMPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CRMPage.js).

- **A project's tabs are renamed: Details is now Identification, Status is now Overall Status, and
  the first stage on it is Project Initiation** (was Project started) - in Start / Edit Project and in
  the record a double-click opens. Other modules' record views still say Details.
  [StartProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/StartProjectFormPanel.js),
  [ProjectDataTable.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/ProjectDataTable.js),
  [stage.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/stage.js).

- **The project's Status tab shows each status beside its name, in the house status colours.**
  A stage's tag and each shoot's status now sit right after the name, with Update alone on the
  right, and the colours mean one thing everywhere: grey not started, blue in progress, amber
  waiting or stopped (Awaiting plan, Plan pending, Paused, On hold), green done, red rejected.
  "Awaiting plan" / "Plan submitted" are pills now, and Production's pills (board and panel too)
  move Paused / On hold from grey to amber and Done to the same green as elsewhere.
  [ProjectStageView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectStageView.js),
  [ProductionPendingPill.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionPendingPill.js).

- **Production's service crew lists only people free at that time.** On a shoot's Plan, each
  service's Person and Assistant dropdowns leave out employees who are already a service's person or
  assistant on another shoot whose time overlaps - by time, not by day: a shoot running 7:00 pm to
  1:00 am leaves its crew free for one at 7:00 pm the next day, back-to-back shoots are free, and a
  shoot without both a start and an end time clashes with nothing. Someone already on the plan
  stays listed, and saving refuses a busy person newly named. The Production Team and Coordinator
  lists are unchanged. No database change.
  [availability.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/availability.js),
  [ProductionServiceCrew.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionServiceCrew.js).

- **Production: the whole shoot team runs the steps, there are three new steps, and the phone
  shows numbered steps.** Besides the Production Coordinator and Manager, the plan's **Production
  Team** and the **employees given a service** (person or assistant) now see the shoot on the
  Production board and can complete its current step - whoever completes it first completes it for
  everyone, logged under their name. Only the Production Manager still edits the plan. They need
  `PROJECT / Production` at **Read / Write** on their role to complete steps; no role was changed -
  the studio may want to grant it to the roles its shoot crews hold. The day now has ten steps, and
  **Shoot started** now asks for a photo of its own; after it come **Happening now** (at least two photos, moved out of Shoot started) and
  **Happy clients** (a photo), then Shoot status, then **Started from venue** (a photo, the trip
  back) before Reached studio; each new step takes an optional remark. Shoots already under way
  carry on from their own step. A **Paused** or **On hold** shoot stays on Shoot status, and its
  dropdown then offers **Started**, Rejected or Completed: Started, with its remarks, sends the
  shoot back to **Happening now**, and Happening now and Happy clients are worked once more (the
  photos already taken are kept and count) before the status comes round again. None of it sends a
  WhatsApp message - Shoot completed is still sent once, on Completed. **Photo copy** is now
  answered **per service** booked on the shoot (or once for a shoot with none): footage URL, backup
  done by, no. of files, size, first and last file name (all required), and optional remarks. Shoots that
  finished Photo copy before keep their single answer. On a phone the step bar is numbered circles instead of thin bars.
  [steps.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/steps.js),
  [access.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/access.js),
  [ProductionStepForm.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionStepForm.js),
  [StepRail.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/StepRail.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (six new columns on `project_production`, and the new
  `project_production_footage` table), then
  `npx prisma generate`.

- **WhatsApp chat files are no longer saved by the CRM - View and Download fetch them from
  WhatsApp.** Photos, voice notes, videos and documents a client sends, and files sent from the
  CRM, used to be copied into R2 (`crm/whatsapp-chat/`). Now nothing is kept: each file in the
  thread shows its name, size and WhatsApp's small preview, and **View** (or **Play** for audio)
  and **Download** ask WhatsApp for it at that moment, passing it straight to the browser -
  Download saves it to the user's own computer. WhatsApp keeps media for a few weeks; an older
  file says to open it on the phone. Sending files from the CRM works as before.
  [mediaOnDemand.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/whatsapp-chat/mediaOnDemand.js),
  [WhatsAppChatPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/WhatsAppChatPanel.js).
  `WHATSAPP_MEDIA_DIR` is no longer read. **After deploying**, on the VPS:
  `node scripts/one-off/purgeWhatsappChatMedia.js` (dry run: count and size), then
  `--execute` to delete the old copies under `crm/whatsapp-chat/` and clear their stored paths.
  Only that folder is touched; remark attachments are not. The delete cannot be undone.

- **Six more places an image can be attached now compress it the same way the rest of the app
  does, instead of storing it at full camera size.** A CRM lead's remark attachment, a WhatsApp
  photo sent to or received from a client, a Speak-up attachment, and a project attachment were
  the only upload paths left that kept a phone photo's full several megabytes forever; they are
  re-encoded to WebP (EXIF and GPS tags stripped, capped at 150KB/1600px) the moment they are
  stored, like every other photo already was. A photo that cannot be compressed - corrupted, or a
  format the compressor cannot read - is still stored as received rather than refused. Project
  attachments are served straight off disk, so a compressed one is renamed to `.webp` to match its
  new bytes; the other paths read the stored content type back instead, so nothing else changes
  for them. Deliberately left alone: the favicon upload and the AI Feature guest "Find My Photos"
  selfie, both already decided exceptions.
  [crmMediaStore.js](../backend/src/services/crmMediaStore.js),
  [speak-up/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/speak-up/controller.js),
  [project-attachments/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/project-attachments/controller.js).

- **Started projects missing their pre production rows get them.** A project started with a Pre
  Production Coordinator but written outside the app's own save (an import, a script, copied data)
  had no pre production rows, so Pre Production had nothing to open for it - even for a Super
  Admin, whose Status tab Update said they were not allowed. **Migration**
  `20261005120000_backfill_project_pre_production_again` raises them by the same rule as
  `ensureProjectPreProduction` (`INSERT IGNORE`, replayable; existing rows untouched). The Status
  tab's message for an empty pre production now says why it can be empty.
  [migration.sql](../backend/prisma/migrations/20261005120000_backfill_project_pre_production_again/migration.sql).

- **A Google Sheet integration never deletes what it imported — only a person does.** Deleting or
  unlinking a sheet used to delete everything that sheet had brought in: soft for CRM leads, hard for
  interview candidates. That cost more than it was worth once the records had been worked — a lead
  quoted and converted, a candidate with rounds booked and a screening form out with them, gone
  because somebody tidied up an integration. On the leads side it also bypassed the refusal that
  normally protects exactly those leads, because a soft delete never reaches a foreign key. Unlinking
  now stops the sync and touches nothing else: the link is still soft-deleted so the poller stops and
  Restore still works, and the row ledgers still remember what was imported so re-linking does not
  import it all again. The same holds for a row removed from the spreadsheet and for a sync that fails
  halfway — **once a row is in, only manual deletion removes it**
  ([google-sheet-links/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/google-sheet-links/controller.js),
  [interview/sheetLinksController.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/interview/sheetLinksController.js)).
  Manual deletion is a **hard** delete on both the single and the bulk path, and a deleted row **stays
  deleted** — the ledger outlives the record, so the next sync does not put them back. A CRM lead
  carrying a project, a quotation or a CRD document is still refused and named back to you.

- **The phone number is the only thing that decides a duplicate on a sheet import.** Both importers
  fell through a chain — the interview one on `phone || email || sourceRowId`, the CRM one on
  `sourceId || phone || contactNumber || email || shootId` — which got both halves wrong: two real
  people sharing an office email read as one, and one real person whose row id changed read as two. A
  row whose number is already in the register is not imported; a row whose number is new **is**
  imported, whatever else disagrees — a respelled name, a reused email, a moved row. A row with **no
  number at all** is refused and named in the sync summary, since it is the one case the rule cannot
  be applied to; every other unreadable value is still blanked with the row going in
  ([interview/sheetImport.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/interview/sheetImport.js),
  [crm-leads/googleSheetsService.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/googleSheetsService.js)).

- **The expired-link page is redesigned: an hourglass card that says what lapsed, whose, and when.**
  The one page every client link lapses to (quotation, Photo Selection, Signature Album, album
  proofing, event gallery) is now a centred white card on a flat light background: the studio's
  logo, a drawn hourglass run out with a small cross badge (an inline SVG, decorative and hidden
  from screen readers - the heading says it in words), "This link has expired", and a panel of
  up to three rows - Type, Client, Expired on - each left out when the server did not send it.
  A type that ever arrives as a code (`SIGNATURE_ALBUM`) is shown as words; the studio is named
  from Settings → Branding. On a phone the card is nearly full width (up to 430px) with the mark,
  hourglass, heading and rows sized for the phone rather than shrunk from the desktop card. The
  rows share one grid - a 44px icon column, the label, the value right-aligned - so icons, labels
  and values line up down the panel; the date never breaks, and a client name too long for the row
  ends in an ellipsis with the full name on hover. A quotation's
  pages are laid out 1112px wide, so the card also pulls a phone's zoom back to actual size before
  freeing pinch-zoom again - without that a phone could keep the page zoomed out and draw the card
  small and far away. The card settles in once (320ms, off under reduced motion). There is no Contact
  button: the studio keeps no public phone, email or WhatsApp, and a button that reaches no one
  was left out. Expiry detection, the 410 responses, tokens and the live countdown on an open
  link are untouched. [ExpiredClientLink.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/ExpiredClientLink.js).

- **The Signature Album gallery deletes by selection, picked the way the client gallery picks.**
  A click or tap anywhere on a photo picks it (shift-click picks a run), drawn with the Photo
  Selection client gallery's own round tick - now one shared `SelectionTick`, which that gallery
  draws exactly as before - its blue ring and a light wash; the per-tile delete icon is gone.
  The bar reads "3 Selected · Select All · Clear · Delete". **Select All** takes every photo the
  search matches - asked of the server, since the gallery loads 24 at a time - and says so while
  searching ("Select All 8 Results"), turning into Deselect All once they are all picked; the pick
  is kept across searches. **Delete** asks first ("Delete 3 selected photos?", "Delete all 54
  photos?", warning when the album's cover is among them) and deletes in one request through the
  same path as a single delete: files purged first, then the rows, which takes each photo out of
  the album with its placement and saved position; others keep theirs. All of a request's photos
  must be the album's or none is touched, and a cloud failure deletes nothing and leaves the pick
  in place. The sort arrow beside search is unchanged.
  [AlbumGallery.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/AlbumGallery.js),
  [GalleryGrid.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/GalleryGrid.js),
  [SelectionTick.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/SelectionTick.js),
  [signatureAlbum.service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/signature-album/signatureAlbum.service.js)
  (`listPhotoIds`, `deletePhotos`). No new permission: both routes sit under `IMAGE_SELECTION /
  Signature Album` (reading the ids needs Read, deleting Read & Write).

- **The heading over a Signature Album's photos now reads "Album" instead of "Gallery".** It is
  the name of the chapter every upload lands in, which the server now creates as "Album"; existing
  albums are renamed by migration. Only that heading changes - the photo count, layout and type
  are as they were, and nothing else in the app named "Gallery" is touched.
  [signatureAlbum.service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/signature-album/signatureAlbum.service.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (`20261003110000_signature_album_chapter_album_heading`:
  renames the chapter the server made - an album's only chapter, named "Gallery" and holding only
  album uploads - to "Album"; a chapter the studio named "Gallery" itself keeps its name).

- **New Signature Albums start on a Curated layout that frames every photo by its own shape.** A
  photo is read as Landscape, Portrait or Square (within 10% of square) from the width and height
  the upload already stores - the decoded image's, so already upright by its EXIF rotation - and
  drawn in a 3:2, 2:3 or 1:1 frame. Each row's frames share one height by taking widths in
  proportion to their shapes, so a portrait beside a landscape keeps a portrait frame and the row
  still lines up, on a phone as on a laptop. Rows follow a one-two-three-two rhythm, only a
  landscape stands alone at full width, a row never gets wider than two landscapes or three
  squares, a pair of portraits takes a third photo rather than tower over the page, and photos are
  never reordered. The crop is cover-from-centre and Edit Album Preview's drag-to-reposition still
  moves it; the preview, the client page and the PDF draw the same rows. **Existing albums and
  chapters are untouched** - layout is drawn from each album's saved style, and theirs is not
  changed; the studio can switch any album or chapter to Curated in Design. No new columns and no
  change to the upload or compression path.
  [signatureAlbum.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/signatureAlbum.mjs) (`orientationOf`, `curatedRows`),
  [AlbumPhotoLayout.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/client/AlbumPhotoLayout.js),
  [signatureAlbum.constants.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/signature-album/signatureAlbum.constants.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (`20261003100000_signature_album_curated_layout`: moves
  Settings → Signature Album → Default Gallery Layout from Editorial to Curated where it still says
  Editorial, and the two column defaults), then `npx prisma generate`.

- **The client quotation's Event Type box names every event type, not only the first.** The dark
  proposal header's Event Type now reads the quotation's own events - the Main Event first, then the
  rest in order, each type once - and shows as many as fit the box on one line, then "+N" for the
  events not named: "Wedding, Post Wedding +3". The count is the quotation's actual events, duplicates
  included - two Bride Haldi events and a Bride Making with one name shown read "Bride Haldi +2". The box measures itself, so the answer is the same on a laptop,
  a phone and in the PDF (the sheet is the same width in all three); before it has measured it shows
  the Main Event and the next. A quotation with no Main Event starts with its first event. The box,
  the card and everything else on the page are unchanged
  ([quotationEventTypes.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/quotationEventTypes.mjs),
  [PublicQuotationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/PublicQuotationPage.js)).

- **A Full Session is 8-10 hours, not 10-12.** The Full Session duration reads "8-10 Hours (Full)"
  everywhere it is shown: Service Settings' pricing lines, the Quotation Calculator and Generator,
  the shoot form, the client's quotation page and its PDF ("Full Session (8-10 Hours)")
  ([servicePricing.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/servicePricing.mjs),
  [AddShootDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/AddShootDialog.js),
  [PublicQuotationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/PublicQuotationPage.js)). Existing services
  and quotations that stored the old text are updated by migration
  `20261001100000_full_session_eight_to_ten_hours`, which replaces only that exact duration value
  inside each service's pricing and each quotation's saved copy - prices, sizes, shoot types, Half
  Session and everything else stay as they were. **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`.

- **"Waiting for me" is shown only to approvers.** HRM → Request showed the Waiting for me tab to
  everybody who is not an administrator; it now appears for everybody named as a Leave Approver or
  Permission Approver on at least one employee's record - whether or not anything is waiting yet,
  and even where their role also sees everybody's requests - and for nobody else: Ajith kumar,
  approver to Dhinakar, has it; Dhinakar, approver to nobody, does not. It lists only the requests
  waiting on them. Anybody with a request already in their queue keeps the tab so it stays reachable. The list endpoint's team answer carries `isApprover`
  ([AttendanceRequestsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestsPage.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js)).

- **On-duty / Travel is now a button in the attendance Login's Work mode.** The separate "Working
  away today? Mark on-duty / travel" line under the modes is gone; the Work mode group shows Office,
  Work from home, Client site and On-duty / Travel two by two. On-duty / Travel still opens the
  on-duty request for approval exactly as the link did - it is not a fourth stored work mode, and
  logins, the three modes and their records are unchanged
  ([EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js)).

- **Image Selection's tabs follow what each project was actually sold.** On a project linked to
  Project Management, **Photo Culling** is now always there; **Photo Selection** appears once the
  project is allocated at least one deliverable whose master in Settings → Deliverables answers
  Yes for Image Selection (Retouches, Frames, …) - the same deliverables that are its Selection
  Items - rather than needing a service named "Photo Selection" allocated; and **Signature Album**
  is earned exactly as before. A Yes on a master deliverable the project was never allocated earns
  nothing. Selection Items, their limits and the client's selections are unchanged: a deliverable
  added later joins the same project's items, and one removed is retired, never deleted
  ([imageSelectionTabs.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/imageSelectionTabs.mjs),
  [ImageSelectionProjectWorkspace.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/ImageSelectionProjectWorkspace.js)).
  Manual projects keep the tabs ticked when they were created. No migration and no new permission.

- **A production project appears in Image Selection only once its first shoot has.** An In
  Progress project used to be listed in the Image Selection sidebar straight away, and opened
  empty until a shoot's day had passed. It is now listed from the day after its first shoot - the
  same day that shoot's folder appears, by the same rule
  ([shoot-visibility.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/shoot-visibility.js),
  [projects/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/projects/service.js)) - and each
  later shoot still appears on its own day inside it. A project with no shoots, or only shoots
  still to come, is held back rather than removed: its Image Selection project is created as
  before, nothing in it is changed or deleted, and it is listed the day its first shoot passes.
  The Image Selection dashboard counts only what the sidebar lists, so a card never counts a
  project its drill-through cannot show. Manual projects and the archived list are unchanged. No migration and no new permission.

- **The Quotation Summary's discount can be typed as a percentage or as rupees.** Discount now
  shows two boxes side by side - the percentage (`%`) and the rupees it comes to (`₹`) - and either
  can be typed into; the other follows at once (20% of ₹20,000 shows ₹4,000; ₹5,000 shows 25%). The
  box typed last is kept when the services change: 20% stays 20% and its rupees move, ₹4,000 stays
  ₹4,000 and its percentage moves. Rupees above service + performance cost are refused before the
  quotation is generated, and on the server. The discount is still taken off the same figure in the
  same order - Performance Cost added first, extra discounts taken off after, GST stated on top -
  and a percentage is worked out exactly as before, so every existing quotation opens, edits,
  duplicates and prints with the same total. One calculation now serves the generator, the CRM
  Quotation Calculator and the client's copy
  ([quotationDiscount.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/quotationDiscount.mjs),
  [QuotationGeneratorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationGeneratorPanel.js));
  `TextField` gains `prefix` / `suffix` for the ₹ and %. The payload gains `discountInputSource`, so
  a discount typed in rupees reopens on the same rupees; the `discount` column keeps holding a
  percentage. No migration and no new permission: the quotation routes' existing guards cover it.

- **The daily attendance report's WhatsApp group is now a name an administrator types, not a group
  picked from one person's own WhatsApp - and every other employee with Allow WhatsApp ticked is an
  automatic fallback for Priority 1, tried in order.** In Settings → User Settings → Attendance
  WhatsApp Report, **Group name** replaces the old "Link the group" picker: type the group's name
  once, and at 9:45 am each try - Priority 1 first, then, in order, everyone else with Allow
  WhatsApp who is currently connected - has *their own* joined WhatsApp groups searched for one
  matching that name, and sends there if found. Nobody has to be picked as a second or third sender:
  any Allow-WhatsApp employee may connect their own WhatsApp from this page, since any of them may
  be needed the day the one before them cannot send - not connected, no group of that name among
  their own, no longer an active login, or refused by WhatsApp. The send still goes out once, from
  the first who actually can, and stops rather than risk sending twice on a failure that may have
  delivered. The page also shows whether today's report went out cleanly, through someone further
  down the list, or not at all: **"Sent, but only after: ..."** names who could not before the one
  who did, and **"All eligible numbers failed to send today's report: ..."** names every one of them
  when nobody could. Naming or clearing the group is an administrator's alone; connecting is any
  Allow-WhatsApp employee's, from a plain pairing dialog with nothing left to pick.
  [reportGroup.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/reportGroup.js),
