  [AttendanceWhatsAppReportPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/AttendanceWhatsAppReportPanel.js),
  [AttendanceReportGroupDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceReportGroupDialog.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate`.

- **The daily attendance report on WhatsApp has one sender again, chosen from the employees allowed
  WhatsApp, and its group is linked from Settings alone.** This replaces the three senders in the
  entry further down. In Settings → User Settings → Attendance WhatsApp Report an administrator
  picks one person, **Priority 1**, and the list offers only active employees with **Allow
  WhatsApp** ticked on their Login Credentials - the server refuses anybody else, too. The report
  goes from that person's WhatsApp; there is no second or third to fall back on, so where it cannot
  send the reason is kept and it is tried again five minutes later, as before. The status box is
  gone from that page. The **Attendance Register no longer has a WhatsApp button**: the chosen
  sender links the group with **Link the group** on the Settings page, which now opens for them
  even without the Attendance WhatsApp Report permission. Anybody who was Priority 2 or 3 is no
  longer a sender; those two columns stay on the database, unread, and are cleared the next time
  the sender is saved - nothing to migrate
  ([reportGroup.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/reportGroup.js),
  [AttendanceWhatsAppReportPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/AttendanceWhatsAppReportPanel.js),
  [SettingsOverlay.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/SettingsOverlay.js)).
- **An administrator's Employee Attendance now opens on a Dashboard of every employee's
  attendance, over any range, instead of a Self Dashboard of their own.** Administrators do not
  mark their own day, so that tab showed them figures about attendance they never marked. The
  switch now reads **Dashboard** for them. Its filters are the Sales → Reports & Analytics row -
  **From** and **To** dates (the last thirty days to begin with), **Employee** as a searchable multi-select, and a
  branch, then **Apply** or **Reset**, with a line saying what the figures on screen were built
  from - so **past periods can be read, not only today**. Below them it reads like the Image
  Selection dashboard: six cards (Present, Absent, On Leave, Late, Half Day, Early Exit), each with
  an arrow against the period of the same length just
  before it; pressing a card narrows the **Employees** table under them to the people it counted,
  most first, and that table has every employee's own figures for the range: their average
  **Check In** and **Check Out** time, hours **Worked** (check-in to check-out, less any time
  logged out between two logins), **Break Time** (shown beside Worked, not taken off it) and
  attendance rate. **Day by Day** and **By Branch** sit below. A range with nothing recorded says so rather
  than showing a row of zeros. Nothing changes for anybody else: their tab still reads Self Dashboard
  and shows their own attendance, and its date-range picker is now always there. The figures come
  from a new administrators-only endpoint, `GET /api/hrm/attendance/overview`, that judges every
  day with the same rules the register and the summary use, so a count here and the register's
  card for a day in the range cannot disagree. Image Selection's dashboard card is now the shared
  `SummaryCard` both dashboards draw with - it looks exactly as before
  ([AdminAttendanceDashboard.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AdminAttendanceDashboard.js),
  [AdminAttendanceEmployees.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AdminAttendanceEmployees.js),
  [SummaryCard.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/SummaryCard.js),
  [attendance/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js)).

- **Getting Dresses Images, Getting Decor Images and Post Wedding Gift are plain yes/no questions
  now, not a Pending/Completed status.** Drawn as the same Yes/No radio pair every other checklist
  toggle already uses (Site Visit, Team Reached Message, ...), on the shoot form, the info panel and
  the board's completion count alike. An existing "Completed" answer became Yes and "Pending"
  became No - it was a deliberate choice, never the placeholder a blank row starts on - and an
  already-blank row stays unanswered; the three columns changed type from text to boolean.
  [preProductionVerticalFields.js](../frontend/src/constants/preProductionVerticalFields.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate`.

- **Production Master and Production Team Allocation are gone from Pre Production.** Both questions
  are removed from the Dum Dum and Qua Qua checklists on the shoot form and no longer count towards a
  shoot's completion, and the pre production API neither returns nor saves them (a save still
  sending them is accepted with those two ignored). The `production_master` and
  `production_team_allocation` columns are left in the database untouched.
  [preProductionVerticalFields.js](../frontend/src/constants/preProductionVerticalFields.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)
- **Pre Production's General panel can be edited by anyone with `PROJECT / Pre Production`
  Read / Write.** Production Manager, Welcome Kit and Shoot Completed Gift (with who takes care of
  them and their Status), Hard Disk (Storage Needed and moving the disk) and CRD Document used to
  need `PROJECT / Projects`, `PROJECT / Client Gifts` and `ASSET / Client Storage` Read / Write, so a
  pre production coordinator holding only the screen's own permission saw them all read-only. They
  now save through new routes under the pre production router, which reuse the same logic and are
  held to those fields and to that project's own disk; the rest of the project is still Projects'.
  Pre Production at Read still sees them read-only. No permission or role changes are needed.
  Saving a switch on or off no longer flashes "Complete required fields: Reason for the change"
  before "General saved": the reason is cleared only once the saved project has been reloaded.
  [PreProductionGeneral.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionGeneral.js),
  [pre-production/routes.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/routes.js)
- **Pre Production's General shows Welcome Kit, Shoot Completed Gift, Hard Disk and CRD Document
  only when the project has them.** An item is listed - in the General bar and in the panel it opens
  - when it is Applicable (Storage Needed: Yes) on the project, and can be switched to Not
  Applicable there with a reason as before. Once switched off with a reason it stays listed,
  showing Not Applicable and that reason; an item that was never applicable is not shown at all.
  [PreProductionGeneral.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionGeneral.js)
- **Start and Edit Project ask who takes care of a gift only once that gift is Applicable.** The
  Welcome Gift and Shoot Completed Gift "Assigned To" dropdowns used to sit on the form greyed out
  when the gift was Not Applicable; now they appear only when the answer is Applicable, as Pre
  Production's General panel already did. Turning a gift to Not Applicable still clears the name.
  [StartProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/StartProjectFormPanel.js)
- **Signed Quotation can now be corrected on Start Project as well as Edit Project.** It is the
  box at the top of Shedule Payment. The corrected figure is the one the Payments tab's Initial
  signed and Total signed, CRM's Converted Amount, the projects table and payment receipts all show,
  since they read the same field. Who may change it is unchanged - anyone with `PROJECT / Projects`
  `READ_WRITE` who may edit the project.
  [StartProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/StartProjectFormPanel.js)
- **Add Shoot takes several shoots at once on every screen, and Edit on a shoot opens that same
  dialog instead of editing the row in place.** Create Project and a project's Shoot Creation now
  offer the multi-select Shoot field the Quotation Generator had - pick several, fill the details
  once, and each becomes its own shoot row. Edit on a shoot, in the Quotation Generator and on the
  project screens alike, opens the Add Shoot dialog on that shoot; the shoot list no longer turns
  into inline inputs, so a shoot is changed through the same fields and checks that added it. A
  shoot saved with an old Shoot Type ("Candid", "Traditional") now opens on Studio / In-House
  instead of with neither radio selected.
  [AddShootDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/AddShootDialog.js),
  [ProjectShootList.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectShootList.js)
- **Every "discard unsaved work" pop-up now makes staying - Keep editing, Go Back, Stay - the
  button that draws the eye, and Discard the plain secondary one**, everywhere that question is
  asked: Employee Details' close dialog, the settings rail, CRM lead popups, interview dialogs, event
  wizards and more. It used to be the other way in most of them (Discard styled red and prominent,
  staying an unstyled plain button), which nudges toward throwing work away rather than keeping it. A
  genuine action confirmation - cancelling a screening form, disconnecting WhatsApp over its usage
  limit - is unchanged: there Confirm is still the thing somebody came to do. New `primaryAction`
  prop on `ConfirmDialog` (`"confirm"`, the default, renders exactly as before; `"cancel"` swaps
  which button is emphasised), which `useUnsavedGuard`'s dialog now sets by default.
  [ConfirmDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/ui/ConfirmDialog.js),
  [useUnsavedGuard.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/useUnsavedGuard.js),
  [EmployeeFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeFormPanel.js). No migration.

- **Every Speak-up now carries its own code, `DBS-SPK-00001`.** Studio-wide and confidential to HR,
  so neither a vertical nor a branch - one run of numbers, five digits rather than the usual six.
  Shown first on both "My Speak-ups" and Speak-up Review, in the table and in the double-click
  detail view. Existing rows keep none until `scripts/renumberIdentifiers.js --only=SPEAK_UP
  --apply` backfills them, oldest first.
  [identifiers.js](../backend/src/services/identifiers.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/speak-up/controller.js),
  [speakUpConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/speakUpConfig.js). **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate
  deploy`, then `npx prisma generate`.

- **The "This number is already an enquiry" pop-up now shows who each existing lead is assigned
  to**, or "Not assigned" when nobody has it, so whoever typed the number knows who to talk to.
  The name is the owner's current name, the same one the board shows. No new permission: the
  duplicate check keeps its existing SALES → CRM Leads guard.
  [DuplicateEnquiryDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/DuplicateEnquiryDialog.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/controller.js)

- **The daily attendance report on WhatsApp now has three senders, chosen by an administrator and tried in order.** In Settings → User Settings → Attendance WhatsApp Report an administrator picks Priority 1, 2 and 3 from the studio's active employees. Only those three get the WhatsApp button, on the Attendance Register, that connects their own WhatsApp and links the group; nobody else can link it, and an administrator can unlink it from Settings. There is one group for all three: while it is linked, nobody can switch the report to another - the dialog shows that group alone, and whether the sender's WhatsApp is in it - so it has to be unlinked first. A chosen sender's Unlink also disconnects their WhatsApp from the app (it leaves Linked devices on their phone), so it has to be linked again for Sales chat and Image Selection too. At the send time the report goes from Priority 1's WhatsApp, and where that cannot send (not connected, switched off, login deactivated, not in the group) straight away from Priority 2's, then 3's - still once a day. A failure that may have delivered it, such as a timeout, is not handed on, so the group never gets it twice. The status shows each priority's connection and who sent today's report. The report's status - when it goes, each priority's WhatsApp, how today's went - is now on that Settings page, and the WhatsApp button's dialog opens straight on the pairing code or the group list. The Attendance WhatsApp Report permission now only opens the Settings page, read-only. See [reportGroup.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/reportGroup.js), [AttendanceReportGroupLink.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceReportGroupLink.js) and [AttendanceWhatsAppReportPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/AttendanceWhatsAppReportPanel.js).
- **An administrator's Request screen has the same five tabs as everybody's.** Instead of one **All
  Requests** tab, an administrator now sees **All, Pending, Approved, Rejected** and **Waiting for
  me** - the four status tabs over everybody's requests (who raised each still shown, Approve and
  Reject still only where they are a named approver, their own requests keeping Withdraw, Cancel and
  Apply again), and Waiting for me their own queue. It opens on Waiting for me when something is
  waiting on them, All otherwise. Nothing changes for anybody else
  ([AttendanceRequestsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestsPage.js)).

- **"Unverified" is no longer shown where no office was measured against.** A location verdict
  appears only where a distance was actually measured from a branch's office point; with none
  recorded - the case now that Rules has no office section - there is nothing to verify against,
  and "Unverified" on every capture said nothing. The Break Summary's Break In / Break Off Location
  show where each was taken (they read only "Unverified" before), and the check-in card no longer
  warns that the location "could not be confirmed". Where an office point exists, the verdict and
  distance still show ([EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js)).

- **Rules no longer has an Office locations section, for now.** The dialog from the account menu's
  **Rules** holds the working day and the check-in quotes only. Nothing changes on the server: an
  office already recorded is kept and still measured against, and the office-location endpoints
  stay; there is simply no screen to set one, so a branch without one records every capture as
  unverified ([AttendanceRulesPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRulesPanel.js)).

- **The Self Dashboard no longer shows "My month so far" and "Days finished properly".** The two
  panels under the KPI cards - days marked, finished properly, hours worked, where you worked, and
  the checked-out ring - are gone; the KPI cards above them stay, less **Attended** and **On time**:
  seven figures now (Working days, Present, Late, Half day, Early exit, Absent, On leave), all in
  one row on a wide screen
  ([EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js)).

- **Employee Repository's header fits a phone.** Add Employee and Create Onboarding Invite share one
  full-width row beside Nebula and the ⋮ instead of wrapping into an uneven second line, the invite
  reading **Invite** there (its full name, for screen readers, is unchanged). The divider left of
  the Administration switch shows only where it sits beside the title - which also tidies the Users
  and Roles screens that share it. On **Tasks**, **Assign Task** reads as its name on every screen,
  compact on a phone and never shrinking or wrapping - on the narrowest phones it drops below the
  title rather than squeezing - and the view switch loses its divider if it wraps under the title. Neither header button carries an
  `aria-label`: the header's stylesheet squares any button that does into a 36px icon, which crushed
  their words on every screen. From a tablet up nothing moves
  ([EmployeeVerificationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeVerificationPage.js),
  [AdministrationSwitch.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/AdministrationSwitch.js),
  [TasksPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/TasksPage.js)).

- **An administrator links the WhatsApp report's group from Settings, not the Attendance Register.**
  The register header's WhatsApp button (Link the group / the linked group) is gone for an
  administrator; it moved to **Settings → Employee → Attendance WhatsApp Report**, which shows the
  group the daily report goes to and from whose WhatsApp, with **Link the group** / **Change group**
  opening the same dialog (the report's status, pairing, the group list, unlink). That page is
  offered to whoever holds `HRM / Attendance WhatsApp Report`; a holder who is not an administrator
  keeps the button on the register as well
  ([AttendanceWhatsAppReportPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/AttendanceWhatsAppReportPanel.js),
  [SettingsOverlay.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/SettingsOverlay.js),
  [AttendanceRegisterPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRegisterPage.js)).

- **Raise Request is disabled for an administrator.** On the Leave or Comp-Off Request screen's header
  and in the account menu, an administrator (the server's `isAdministrator`) sees Raise Request
  greyed out and not pressable, with "Administrators do not raise leave or comp-off requests" on
  hover; it stays off while the permissions load. Everybody else raises requests as before
  ([AttendanceRequestsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestsPage.js),
  [AppTopbar.js](../frontend/src/components/app-shell/AppTopbar.js)).

- **"Leave or Comp-Off Request" is the last of Employee Attendance's sections.** The section switch
  reads Self Dashboard, Attendance Register, Events, then Leave or Comp-Off Request
  ([EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js)).

- **Approving a request asks for no remarks; rejecting still requires a reason.** The Approve dialog
  has no Remarks box any more - just the request and Approve - and the server keeps no remarks on an
  approval even if some are sent. The Reject dialog keeps its required "Reason for rejection", Reject
  staying disabled until one is written, and the server refuses a rejection without one
  ([attendanceRequests.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/attendanceRequests.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/controller.js)).

- **Every row of the requests table is the same height.** A request with nothing left to do on it -
  approved by all its approvers, say - had no ⋮ in its last cell, and its row shrank below the pending
  ones beside it. The empty cell now keeps the ⋮'s 32px square, so rows no longer change height as
  requests are approved ([AttendanceRequestsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestsPage.js)).

- **Employee Attendance stays on its section through a refresh.** The open section - Self Dashboard,
  Leave or Comp-Off Request, Attendance Register or Events - is kept in the address
  (`?section=request`, `register`, `events`; the bare address for the dashboard) rather than in the
  page's memory, so a refresh, Back or a bookmark opens the same section instead of dropping back to
  the Self Dashboard. While the permissions load after a refresh the section stands, so the dashboard
  does not flash up first ([EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js)).

- **Employee Attendance's Request section is "Leave or Comp-Off Request".** The section switch, the
  screen's own title where `/hrm/requests` opens it alone, and the menu registry's name for it - which
  is also what Role Management calls `HRM / Requests` - all read "Leave or Comp-Off Request"
  ([EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js),
  [AttendanceRequestsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestsPage.js),
  [navigation.mjs](../frontend/src/constants/navigation.mjs)).

- **The Attendance Register has two headline cards: Present and Leave.** The Employees card is gone,
  and Absent reads **Leave** - everybody away today, on approved leave (a comp-off included) or not in
  without one. The table's Status column and the filter chip say Present or Leave to match, and an
  empty Leave filter says "Nobody is on leave today." A filter is let go of by pressing its card
  again or the chip's ×; the two cards sit side by side at every size
  ([AttendanceRegisterPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRegisterPage.js)).

- **The Attendance Register's WhatsApp dialog shows where the daily report stands.** At the top of
  the dialog behind the header's WhatsApp button (Link the group / the linked group): your own
  WhatsApp - Connected, with the number, or Not connected; the group, or None linked; when it sends
  and from whose WhatsApp; whether that WhatsApp is connected ("Not connected - the report cannot
  go"); and today's send - Sent, Not sent and why, or Not sent yet. Read afresh each time the dialog
  opens. This is where the status went when its line was taken off the page
  ([AttendanceReportGroupDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceReportGroupDialog.js)).

- **The Attendance calculator has Monthly, Weekly, Daily and Hourly tabs.** The shared tab bar sits
  above the two fields: **Monthly** is selected and is what the fields are; **Weekly**, **Daily** and
  **Hourly** are shown greyed and disabled ("Coming soon" on hover) until each has settings of its
  own. The shared `Tabs` component takes an optional `disabled` (and `title`) per tab for this; every
  other tab bar is unchanged ([AttendanceCalculatorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/AttendanceCalculatorPanel.js),
  [Tabs.js](../frontend/src/components/ui/Tabs.js)).

- **Settings → Employee → Attendance calculator is two days of the month.** **Start and End (Date)**
  - one day, 25 by default, with "This calculates 25th to 25th every month" beneath - and **Payable
  Date (Following Month)** - 10 by default, with how many days' salary that holds back beneath ("15
  days salary will be on hold": from the end of the latest cycle to its payday, 25 Sep to 10 Oct).
  Each is typed as a number, 1 to 31, and saved as the box is left or Enter is pressed; a short
  month's missing day is its last. The two start and end date pickers are gone, and with them the
  columns `pay_period_start` and `pay_period_end`: migration `20260929130000_hrm_pay_cycle_day` adds
  `pay_cycle_day` (default 25) and drops them. `GET` / `PUT /api/hrm/attendance/calculator/period` is
  `{ cycleDay, paybackDay }` ([AttendanceCalculatorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/AttendanceCalculatorPanel.js),
  [calculator.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/calculator.js)). **Deploy:** `npx prisma
  migrate deploy`, `npx prisma generate`, and restart the backend.

- **The Attendance Report says Leave and Uninformed Leave, and lists no present names.** The
  message - the daily WhatsApp send and the Send dialog alike - now reads Total employees, Present (a
  count only), **Leave** (whoever is away with an approved request - leave, or a comp-off, tagged
  "Comp-off for ... worked"), **Uninformed Leave** (whoever was expected and is not in without one, a
  day too short to count included) and Permission, then the Leave, Uninformed Leave and Permission
  lists. The Present list and the Absent line and list are gone from the default wording. New
  placeholders `{leave count}`, `{leave list}`, `{uninformed leave count}`, `{uninformed leave list}`;
  the older ones still answer. Migration `20260929120000_attendance_report_leave_and_uninformed`
  updates the stored wording only where nobody has reworded it
  ([attendanceReport.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/attendanceReport.mjs),
  [reportText.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/reportText.js)). **Deploy:** `npx prisma
  migrate deploy`.

- **The Attendance Register opens straight on its cards.** The caption line ("Every active employee
  across all branches · today, ... · as of ...") and the daily WhatsApp report's status line under it
  (where it goes, whether today's was sent, and the warning when the sender's WhatsApp is not
  connected) are gone. The header's WhatsApp button - Link the group, or the linked group's name to
  change or unlink it - stays for whoever holds the Attendance WhatsApp Report permission, and the
  9:45 am send is unchanged
  ([AttendanceRegisterPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRegisterPage.js)).

- **HRM → Events can be filtered by date.** The header carries the shared date-range switch the CRM
  board uses - All Time, Today, Yesterday, This Week, This Month, and Custom Date with From and To -
  and the events shown are those **posted** in the range (an event has no day of its own any more).
  The server filters (`GET /api/hrm/events?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD`, both ends counted, read on
  the studio's clock whatever the server's), so a post older than the latest two hundred is still
  found; a range with none says "No events posted in this range". Posting under a range reads the
  list again, since the range may not take in today
  ([EventsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EventsPage.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/events/controller.js)).

- **Upload Event no longer asks for the event date, and the description is optional.** An event is
  posted with its photos and a title; Title now takes the row the date shared, and Description has
  no required mark. The server takes an event with no date (stored empty) and no description (stored
  as ""), and still checks a date as a real day where a caller sends one. An event without a
  description shows none on its card or in its full view. **The cards show no date** - the blue day
  under the title is gone, for events posted with one as well. This
  replaces the earlier rule that the date was required
  ([EventsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EventsPage.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/events/controller.js)). No migration.

- **Attendance Calculator and Attendance Logs are off Role Management.** The two HRM permissions are
  deleted, with every grant of them (migration
  `20260929110000_remove_attendance_calculator_and_logs_permissions`; `role_permission` and the
  Branch Admin set cascade), and the catalogue no longer lists them. What they opened is an
  administrator's alone again, as it was before they were permissions: Settings → Employee →
  Attendance calculator and its endpoints (`requireCalculatorAccess` asks `isAdministrator`), and the
  Self Dashboard's Login Summary and Break Summary with the Break Summary's endpoint
  (`seesAttendanceLogs`). Attendance Rules, All Requests and Attendance WhatsApp Report stay in Role
  Management. **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`.

- **Sending the attendance report to WhatsApp is its own permission: HRM → Attendance WhatsApp
  Report.** Holding it is what shows the Attendance Register's WhatsApp button (Link the group / the
  linked group) and opens the pairing, group list, link and unlink behind it - it used to be Read /
  Write on Attendance Approval. The 9:45 am send also checks that whoever linked the group still
  holds it; taken away, the report stops and the page says why ("... no longer has the Attendance
  WhatsApp Report permission. Link the group again from an account that has it."). Migration
  `20260929100000_attendance_whatsapp_report_permission` adds it and grants it to the SUPER_ADMIN
  role and every administrator role only; the studio grants it in Role Management to whoever should
  send the report. Seeing where the report goes still needs only the register itself
  ([reportGroup.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/reportGroup.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/controller.js)). **Deploy:** `npx prisma
  migrate deploy`.

- **The Attendance Report's present list is names only.** Each line is the person and their ID -
  "1. Arun Kumar (DBS-4)" - without the login and logout times or the day's status ("- Late", "- Not
  logged out") after it, in the daily WhatsApp message and the Send dialog alike
  ([attendanceReport.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/attendanceReport.mjs),
  [reportText.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/reportText.js)). For testing at another hour,
  the send time can be set with `ATTENDANCE_REPORT_SEND_AT=HH:MM` in the backend's `.env` (default
  09:45); the window for retries is the 2¼ hours after it.

- **The Attendance Register sends its daily report to a WhatsApp group automatically, at 9:45 am.**
  An Attendance Approval holder at Read / Write links the group from the register's header: **Link
  the group** where none is linked (the linked group's name, to change or unlink it, where one is).
  The dialog is Image Selection's group link rebuilt for this - the pairing code while their own
  WhatsApp is not linked, then their groups with a search - and the report is sent from **their**
  WhatsApp, Baileys' `sendMessageToGroup`, the path Image Selection's manual "Send to Group" uses.
  WhatsApp sessions belong to a person, so whoever links the group is its sender and has to stay
  linked. A line under the caption says where the report goes and how today's went ("sent today",
  or "not sent today - " and why), and warns when the sender's WhatsApp is not connected; anybody
  who can read the register sees it. The text is the Send message's - the studio's
  `ATTENDANCE_DAILY_REPORT` wording, or the default - built on the server by a copy of the screen's
  builder (`reportText.js`, held to the same output by a test) with times in studio time. **The
  schedule:** a one-minute timer in the API process (the only one holding WhatsApp sockets) sends at
  9:45 am Asia/Kolkata every day, weekends and holidays included; a WhatsApp not connected at 9:45
  is tried again every five minutes until noon, then the day is let go; each try is claimed with a
  conditional update and a send stamps the day, so a restart or two processes never send twice.
  Both WhatsApp chat switches are honoured. `ATTENDANCE_REPORT_AUTOSEND=false` turns the timer off.
  New columns on `hrm_settings` - the group, its name, the sender (`user`, SET NULL), when linked,
  the last day sent, the last try and its error - in migration
  `20260929090000_attendance_report_whatsapp_group`. New endpoints under
  `/api/hrm/attendance/report-group` (status; the linker's session and pairing; their groups; link;
  unlink), the group checked against the linker's own groups before it is saved. Image Selection's
  pairing hook is now the shared `useWhatsappPairingSession`, told which endpoints to call
  ([reportGroup.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/reportGroup.js),
  [AttendanceReportGroupDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceReportGroupDialog.js),
  [AttendanceRegisterPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRegisterPage.js)).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, `npx prisma generate`, and restart the backend.

- **An administrator's Employee Attendance header has no Break In or Login / Logout.** For a login
  the server calls an administrator (`isAdministrator` from `usePermissions()`), the Self Dashboard's
  header shows only the section switch; the buttons are held back while the permissions load, so
  they never flash up for an administrator. Everybody else keeps both, unchanged
  ([EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js)).

- **An administrator's Request screen has no "Waiting for me" tab.** For a login holding `HRM / All
  Requests` the tabs are All, Pending, Approved and Rejected over everybody's requests; what waits on
  them is already there, marked "Approval pending" in the Decide column, with Approve and Reject in
  the row's ⋮. Where something waits for their answer the screen opens on Pending (it used to open on
  Waiting for me). Everybody else keeps Waiting for me exactly as it was
  ([AttendanceRequestsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestsPage.js)).

- **The Request screen's Decide column shows answers, not buttons.** Where a request is still yours
  to answer it reads an amber **● Approval pending**, with "Waiting on you" or "Waiting on you and 2
  more" beneath - in the same style as the green **✓ You approved** / "Waiting on 1 more" beside it.
  Approve and Reject are no longer buttons on the row; they are in the row's ⋮, as they already were
  ([AttendanceRequestsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestsPage.js)).

- **The Attendance Register's Send button is hidden for now.** One switch, `SHOW_SEND` in
  [AttendanceRegisterPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRegisterPage.js), is off; the
  report behind it (the dialog, and its wording in Settings → Templates) is kept whole, and setting
  the switch back to `true` returns the button.

- **The Attendance Report no longer mentions Late.** The Send message's default wording drops the
  "Late: {late count}" line and the "Late:" list; it now reads Total employees, Present, Absent and
  Permission, then the Present, Absent and Permission lists. Migration
  `20260928220000_attendance_report_drop_late` updates the stored wording only where nobody has
  reworded it; `{late count}` and `{late list}` stay available in Settings → Templates for anybody
  who wants them back ([attendanceReport.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/attendanceReport.mjs)).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`.

- **Attendance Register and Events are sections of Employee Attendance.** Employee Attendance's
  section switch now reads Self Dashboard, Request, **Attendance Register** and **Events**; each of
  the two new ones is the whole screen, under the Employee Attendance heading with the switch beside
  it, as Request already was. They are offered only to a login holding the screen's own permission -
  `HRM / Attendance Approval` for the register, `HRM / Events` for the events - and both are off the
  HRM menu (`hidden` in `navigation.mjs`). Their routes stay, so a bookmark or the event notification's
  link still opens them alone, and both permissions still appear on the Roles screen under their
  names. `?section=register` and `?section=events` open those sections directly, as
  `?section=request` does ([EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js),
  [navigation.mjs](../frontend/src/constants/navigation.mjs)).

- **Somebody can log in and out more than once a day.** After a logout, Employee Attendance's header
  offers **Login** again (it used to say "Day complete"), with the same selfie, location and
  server time as the first login; the check-in card then reads "You're logged in again". The day
  stays one attendance record - its login is the **first** login (lateness is judged on it) and its
  logout the **latest** logout - so the register, the statuses, corrections and the calculator read
  it as before. **Time logged out between a logout and the next login is not worked**: 9:00-13:00
  and 14:00-18:00 is 8 hours, not 9 - new `away_minutes` on `attendance_session` adds up the gaps and
  `workedMinutes` takes them off, which the Schedule's own attendance reading now uses as well;
  `login_count` counts the logins (migration `20260928200000_attendance_relogin`, both defaulted, so
  every earlier day reads as before). Every login and logout is still its own event with its own
  photograph and position; the register keeps the day's first check-in photograph, and today's
  logout place is the latest logout's. A login while logged in, or a logout while logged out, is
  refused with a sentence saying which. Checked end to end through the controller: login, logout,
  login again after an hour away, logout - four events, two logins, 5 hours spanned, 4 worked
  ([controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/controller.js),
  [attendanceRules.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/attendanceRules.js),
  [EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js)).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate`.

- **The Attendance Register counts people on leave as Absent.** The On leave headline card is gone:
  three cards now - Employees, Present, Absent - in **one row at every size**, compact on a phone
  (less padding, a smaller figure, no "people" below a tablet, so the row fits a
  300px screen) and the Image Selection size from a tablet up. Absent counts the absent plus everybody on
  approved leave, a comp-off included, and its filter shows them all. In Today's Attendance the
  **Status column says only Present or Absent** - green or red - rather than the day's finer reading
  (Late, Not logged out, On leave ...), and filters and sorts by those two words; a holiday or
  weekly off keeps its own name. The **Send** message follows:
  `{absent count}` and `{absent list}` include them, each tagged in the list - "Karthik Selvam
  (DBS-6) - On leave", "Divya S (DBS-7) - Comp-off for Sun, 20 Sep worked" - and the default wording
  drops its separate On leave and Comp-off lines and sections, which would name the same people
  twice. Migration `20260928180000_attendance_report_leave_is_absent` updates the stored wording
  only where nobody has reworded it; `{on leave count}`, `{on leave list}`, `{comp-off count}` and
  `{comp-off list}` stay available for a studio that wants the breakdown. The server's own counts
  are unchanged ([AttendanceRegisterPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRegisterPage.js),
  [attendanceReport.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/attendanceReport.mjs)). **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate
  deploy`.

- **The Attendance Register is laid out like Image Selection → Dashboard.** The header carries
  **Send** (there is no Refresh button - opening the page reads it). On the tinted dashboard canvas: a caption line
  ("Every active employee across all branches · today, Mon 28 Sep 2026 · as of 10:42 am"); four
  headline cards in the Image Selection style - Employees, Present, Absent, On leave, each "N people"
  no trend arrows - which are **filters**: pressing Present narrows
  the list below to the people present, pressing it again or pressing Employees lets go, and the
  pressed card is named as a chip above the list with × to clear it; the birthdays and anniversaries
  notice, where it was; then **Today's Attendance**, a **table** in the place Recent Projects has and
  built the same way - the shared `DataTable` with its filter row, sorting, Table Options and a
  footer count ("2 of 6 employees · Present"), fifteen rows tall and scrolling for the rest. Its
  columns: **Employee** (check-in photo or initials, and name), **Branch**, **Status** (a pill in the
  group's colour - green present, red absent, blue on leave), **Login**, **Logout**, **Worked** (in
  red for a login too short to count) and **Login location**. Rows run present first, then absent,
  on leave and anybody not expected today, each by name, until a column is sorted; a click picks a
  row out and nothing opens. **The login location is the district and state** - "Erode, Tamil Nadu"
  out of "Kumalankuttai, Periyasemur, Erode, Tamil Nadu, 638001" - taken as the two parts before the
  PIN code (and "India", where present), with the whole address on hover; coordinates, shown until
  the address is looked up, stay whole. The Present / Absent / On leave boxes, the person cards and
  the old compact tiles are gone, and there are no side panels. Frontend only
  ([AttendanceRegisterPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRegisterPage.js)).

- **The Attendance Register has an On leave box, below Absent.** Everybody on approved leave today -
  a comp-off included - has a card in it, in the same style as Present and Absent: its own search,
  its count in its heading, a fixed height with the cards scrolling inside. Before this they were in
  neither box and only a number on the On leave card, so a manager could not tell "excused" from
  "missed". On a day without leave it says "Nobody is on leave today.", and on a holiday or weekly
  off "Today is a holiday - nobody is expected." (or "a weekly off"). From a laptop up, Present sits
  on the left running the height of Absent and On leave stacked on the right; below that, all three
  are one above the other. No server change - it reads the statuses the register already sends
  ([AttendanceRegisterPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRegisterPage.js)).

- **The Attendance Register is two boxes of cards: Present and Absent.** The table is gone.
  **Present** holds everybody whose day counts as attended and **Absent** everybody whose day reads
  Absent - the same test the Present and Absent cards count by, so a box and its card always agree
  (they used to sort by "has a login", so somebody in for less than the half-day floor sat in
  Present while the cards counted them Absent; such a card now sits in Absent and says "Logged in for
  only 2h 4m"). The rows carry `attended` for this. Side
  by side from a laptop up, one above the other below it - each with **its own search** (name, ID,
  department or designation) above its cards and its count in its heading. Each box is a fixed
  height (26rem on a phone, 30rem from a tablet up) and its cards scroll inside it, the heading and
  search staying in place, so a full office no longer stretches the page. A box with few cards is only as
  tall as they need - the height is a cap, not a fixed size - and from a laptop up the boxes sit in
  two top-aligned columns (Present; Absent over On leave) so a short box is never stretched to its
  neighbour's height. The scrollbar there is
  a slim rounded thumb with no track or arrow buttons, toned for the light and dark themes
  (`.slim-scrollbar` in [globals.css](../frontend/src/app/globals.css)). A card is one line: the
  photograph the person checked in with (initials for somebody absent), their name and branch, and
  **where they logged in from** - the first part of the street address the check-in resolved to
  ("Kumalankuttai" out of "Kumalankuttai, Periyasemur, Erode, Tamil Nadu, 638001"), with a pin icon
  and the whole address on hover, or the coordinates, whole, until the address arrives; no
  "Unverified" or distance - and no ID and no status, the box already says whether they came. It
  opens nothing. The register's rows carry this as `loginPlace` (null for somebody who did not log
  in). Leave, holidays and weekly offs are in neither box and are
  still counted in the cards above. There are no filters above the boxes any more - no Status or
  Search, and no Date or Branch: the register is always **today, across every branch** - and the
  table's tick boxes and export are gone; **Send** still shares today and still names who was away,
  reading its own copy of it
  ([AttendanceRegisterPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRegisterPage.js)).

- **The Attendance Register's KPI cards are fewer and compact on every screen.** Four figures -
  Employees, Present, Absent and On leave - two to a row on a phone (they were seven, one per row,
  a screen of cards above the table) and all four in one row from a tablet up, each with less
  padding and a smaller figure. Late, Not checked out and Outside location are no longer cards; the
  server still counts them for the Send report
  ([AttendanceRegisterPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRegisterPage.js)).

- **Attendance's "administrators only" rights are permissions in Role Management now.** Four new
  HRM permissions, each grantable to any role: **Attendance Rules** (Read / Write changes the shift,
  weekly offs, half-day band, office locations and check-in quotes - everybody can still read the
  rules), **Attendance Logs** (the Self Dashboard's Login Summary and Break Summary, and the Break
  Summary's endpoint), **All Requests** (everybody's requests on HRM → Request's status tabs - deciding
  stays with the named approvers) and **Attendance Calculator** (Settings → Employee → Attendance
  calculator and its two endpoints). The server checks the permission instead of "is an
  administrator" (`canManageRules`, `seesAttendanceLogs`, `seesAllRequests` in
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js), `requireCalculatorAccess` in
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/controller.js)); the Settings entry for the
  calculator follows the permission. Migration `20260928120000_attendance_admin_permissions` adds the
  four and grants them Read / Write to the SUPER_ADMIN role and every active role with the
  Administrator tick - exactly who had them before, so **nobody's access changes** until a role is
  edited. The Rules dialog's read-only note now says changing the rules needs the Attendance Rules
  permission. HRM → Events was already a permission (`HRM / Events`) and is unchanged. Payback Date
  stays administrators only until it has something in it. **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`.

- **The Self Dashboard's Login Summary and Break Summary are hidden from everybody for now,
  administrators included.** One switch, `SHOW_ATTENDANCE_LOGS` in
  [EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js), is off;
  setting it back to `true` shows them to administrators again, exactly as described in the entry
  below - the server side (`canSeeLogs`, and the Break Summary endpoint's 403 for anybody else) is
  unchanged.
  An administrator's Self Dashboard also drops the date-range picker and the caption line under it
  ("This month: 1 Sept 2026 - 28 Sept 2026 ..."): it is this month's KPI cards and nothing to
  choose. Everybody else keeps both, unchanged. Decided by `isAdministrator` from
  `usePermissions()`, and held back while the permissions load so it never flashes up for an
  administrator.

- **The Self Dashboard's Login Summary and Break Summary are shown to administrators only, for
  now.** On Employee Attendance → Self Dashboard everybody else sees the date range, the KPI cards,
  the insights and the notices they act on (a day left open, a break running), without the Login
  Summary's calendar and day table, its "figures only" note, or the Break Summary. Decided on the
  server in one place, `seesAttendanceLogs` in
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js) - an administrator, the same
  reading as the attendance rules - sent to the page as `canSeeLogs` on the attendance settings;
  `GET /api/hrm/attendance/breaks` now refuses anybody else with 403. The attendance summary
  endpoint is unchanged, because the KPI cards and insights everybody keeps are drawn from it.
  Widening this to HR later is a change to that one function.

- **A clock-dial time picker, and Request correction uses it.** Every 12-hour time field - Request
  correction's "Time you finished", and a permission's From / To time - is now a field that reads
  like the time it holds (`6:30 PM`, with a clock icon) and opens a clock-face picker like a
  phone's: **SELECT TIME**, the hour and minute large at the top with **AM / PM** stacked beside
  them, and a dial below. Tap or drag the hand to the hour and the dial turns to minutes, where any
  minute can be picked; pressing the hour or minute at the top goes back to it. The keyboard icon
  swaps the dial for two boxes to type the time into, the dial answers the arrow keys and Enter,
  and **Cancel / OK** end it. In the app's blue and greys, and recoloured by the dark themes like
  every other popover. It replaces three bare dropdowns, and on Request correction the browser's own
  time box, whose 12- or 24-hour format followed the computer's regional settings. Placed like the
  calendar, so it opens on screen from a field low in a dialog. What is sent is unchanged (`HH:MM`,
  24-hour), as is the check that a correction falls after the login
  ([TimeField.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/TimeField.js),
  [twelveHourTime.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/twelveHourTime.mjs)).

- **Events, the notification bell and the Login dialog fit every screen size better.** HRM →
  Events lays its cards out one per row on a phone, two on a tablet, three on a laptop and four on
  a wide monitor; a card's "Posted by" line wraps instead of being cut, with View and Remove moving
  beneath it where the card is narrow; long titles and descriptions wrap rather than widening the
  card; and the photo viewer sizes to the visible screen on phones, with larger Previous / Next
  arrows. The bell's panel is wider from tablets up. The Login dialog's on-duty and outside-attendance links wrap on a phone and are
  full-size touch targets. On a phone narrower than 400px (down to 300px) the top bar no longer
  pushes the bell and the account button off the right edge: it shows a smaller logo
  (`AppLogo` variant `navbarCompact`) and the account button drops its chevron. The divider left
  of Employee Attendance's section switch shows only where the switch sits beside the title, not
  when it wraps under it on a phone. On a phone, Employee Attendance's **Break In** and **Login**
  now share the full width of their row in equal halves beside the Nebula icon, instead of sitting
  in a clump at its left - through a new `stretchActionsOnPhone` prop on `ModulePageHeader`, which
  no other page sets, so every other header is unchanged. From tablet width up nothing moves.
  Checked in the code against 300px, 360px, 768px and 1280px widths.

- **Login and Logout work like Break: one press opens the capture, with no separate login page.**
  On Employee Attendance, **Login** and **Logout** in the header now open a dialog - take a live
  selfie, the location is read straight after it, and the server stamps the time - exactly as
  **Break In** / **Break Off** do; the Login dialog also asks the work mode. The daily-login page
  that used to replace the dashboard (and its Back to Dashboard) is gone. What it also held has
  moved: after a login the check-in card with the day's line still appears; a day left open is
  corrected from the dashboard's notice, which now has a **Request a correction** per day; **Mark
  on-duty / travel** and **Request outside attendance** are links on the Login dialog, beside the
  refusal a login outside the office gets; leave and permission are raised from Request, and the
  policy is read under the account menu's **Rules**. Once the day is logged out the button reads
  **Day complete**, and a login with no employee record sees Login greyed out with the reason.
  One `AttendanceCaptureDialog` now serves all four marks
  ([EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js)); no
  backend change.

- **The attendance Rules moved from Employee Attendance to the account menu.** The menu under your
  name has a **Rules** item below Settings, opening the same rules in a dialog - the working day,
  each branch's office location and the check-in quotes - editable by an administrator and
  read-only for everybody else, as before. It is shown to anybody holding
  `HRM / Employee Attendance` (the permission the section needed), and Employee Attendance's
  section switch is now Self Dashboard and Request. The panel moved out of the page into
  [AttendanceRulesPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRulesPanel.js), opened by
  [AttendanceRulesDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRulesDialog.js); no backend
  change.

- **A leave, permission or comp-off request waiting on you is now a notification on the bell,
  instead of a badge in the sidebar.** When a request is raised, each approver named on it gets a
  notification - "Leave request from *name*", with its dates (and hours, for a permission) - and
  nobody else does: not the requester, not other approvers' logins, not an approver who has already
  answered. It opens Employee Attendance → Request (HRM → Request for somebody who holds only
  `HRM / Requests`), which lands on Waiting for me. It leaves that approver's bell once they approve
  or reject, and every approver's once the request is settled, withdrawn or cancelled
  ([requestNotifications.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/requestNotifications.js)). New
  type `REQUEST_WAITING`, readable with either `HRM / Requests` or `HRM / Employee Attendance` -
  `TYPE_PERMISSIONS` now takes a list meaning "any of these". **Removed:** the red count beside
  HRM → Request, the red dot on its collapsed group and on the menu button, the
  `GET /api/hrm/attendance/requests/waiting-count` endpoint behind them, and the browser's record of
  which requests had been looked at (`useSidebarBadges`, `requestNoticeSeen`). Employee Attendance
  now opens on its Request section from `?section=request`. **Migration**
  `20260927120000_request_waiting_notifications` gives every approval still pending its
  notification, so what was already waiting is not lost with the badge; data only, replayable.

- **HRM → Events lists the newest post first.** Events are ordered by when they were posted, not
  by the day the event happened, so a new post always appears at the top - an event posted today
  about something last month no longer sinks below older posts
  ([controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/events/controller.js),
  [EventsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EventsPage.js)).

- **A notification stays on the bell until it is opened, and then leaves it.** There is no Mark as
  read button - a notification can only be cleared by opening it, which takes the reader to the
  page it points at, so nothing leaves the bell unseen. Task, lead and event notifications are
  marked read on the server, which now lists unread ones only
  ([notifications.js](../backend/src/services/notifications.js)), so they stay gone on every device.
  The waiting-on-you notices (follow-ups, WhatsApp replies, calls, approvals) and meetings have no
  read state on the server, so they are hidden in that browser
  ([useDismissedNotices.js](../frontend/src/components/app-shell/useDismissedNotices.js)); one
  comes back only if it changes - a new WhatsApp reply, a follow-up moved to another day. Opening
  the bell no longer marks every notification read, since that would now empty it on sight - the
  badge counts what has not yet been read. (`OptionsMenu` items can still take an `action` -
  `{ label, onSelect }` - for a row's own button; the bell no longer uses one.)

- **HRM → Events asks for the event's date before it posts.** Event Date is marked required in
  Upload Event and Post Event stays disabled until one is chosen; the server refuses a new event
  without a `YYYY-MM-DD` day with "Choose the day of the event."
  ([EventsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EventsPage.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/events/controller.js)). The column stays nullable, so
  events already posted without a day still load and sort after the dated ones.
- **Every expired client link now shows one clear expired page.** A client who opens a lapsed
  quotation (or its Payment and Terms pages), Photo Selection gallery, Signature Album, album proof
  or event gallery link now sees the same page: the studio's logo, **This link has expired**, what
  the link was for, whose it was when that is known ("Photo Selection · Ranju Raj", "Quotation ·
  Harish", "Signature Album · Ajay & Priya"), **Expired on 28 March 2027**, and a line asking them to
  contact the studio - named from Settings → Branding - for a new link
  ([ExpiredClientLink.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/ExpiredClientLink.js),
  [expiredLink.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/expiredLink.mjs)). Each of those links already answered 410;
  the answer now also carries the link's type, the client's name and its expiry date
  ([expiredLink.js](../backend/src/services/expiredLink.js)), and nothing behind the link. It is
  checked before any PIN, so a lapsed Signature Album, gallery or proof never asks for one; there is
  no redirect, and a refresh or an old bookmark shows the same page - including a Photo Selection
  link, which used to answer "not found" from its second visit because the first had revoked it (a
  link the studio revokes before it expires still reads "not available"). An album proof whose
  album has been deleted now reads "not available" rather than "expired". An unknown or mistyped
  link keeps each page's own "not available", and a live link is untouched. No studio contact
  details are public, so there is no contact button - just the line. On a quotation's pages, which
  scale a 1080px sheet to a phone, the card switches to the phone's own width while it is shown.
  Because an expired link now names its client, the lookups behind a Photo Selection gallery and
  an album proof - which had no rate limit - are limited to 300 per address per quarter hour, as
  the other client links already were. No migration, and no permission changed.

- **A Signature Album's Require PIN is under Permissions and starts off.** In the album's right
  panel, Require PIN moved from Client Access to the top of Permissions, above Allow Download and
  Allow Social Share ([ClientPermissions.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/ClientPermissions.js));
  the Access PIN it asks for stays under Client Access, shown while it is on. A new album now starts
  with Require PIN off, so publishing it mints no PIN and the client link opens straight away; the
  studio turns it on per album, and a PIN is minted then as before
  ([signatureAlbum.service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/signature-album/signatureAlbum.service.js)).
  The studio-wide Require PIN default in the Signature Album settings no longer decides this and is
  no longer shown (its column is left in place, unread). Every existing album keeps the value it was
  saved with, and what Require PIN does - the PIN screen, the session, the reset - is unchanged. No
  migration.

- **An employee's Reviews page is now a salary timeline** instead of Upcoming / Past tabs over a
  review table. The joining salary sits at the top; each review follows in date order with its
  increment and the salary it left the employee on — Shine reviews on the right, Shadow on the
  left, unmarked ones on the line — and the next review is centred at the foot with **Mark review**,
  which opens Add Review with its date filled in. **+ Add Review** is at the top right. Below `md`
  the two sides fold into one column. The review table's filtering and CSV export go with it.
  `EmployeeReviewList.js` is removed.
  [EmployeeReviewTimeline.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeReviewTimeline.js),
  [employeeReviewTimeline.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/employeeReviewTimeline.mjs)
- **Add Review now shows the employee's Joining Salary, Total Increment and Total Salary** as they
  will be once the review is saved — total salary being the joining salary plus every increment,
  worked out by the same `reviewTotals` the record uses. Editing a review no longer counts its
  increment twice in the running total. [AddReviewDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/AddReviewDialog.js)
- **The employee form's Login Credentials page is renamed Employee Preference**, in the rail of both
  Edit and onboarding, in its title, and where the attendance request screen tells somebody where
  HR sets their approvers. The Login Credentials email template in Settings keeps its name.
  [EmployeeFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeFormPanel.js)
- **An employee's Reviews are now a page of their own in the Edit form's rail**, last, after
  Employee Details and Employee Preference, instead of the last heading under Employee Details. It
  works the way Employee Preference does: choosing it shows only the review list, and its footer is a Close
  that still asks about unsaved detail edits. Reviews are added and edited from their own dialog
  exactly as before. Add and onboarding Review are unchanged.
  [EmployeeFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeFormPanel.js)
- **The CRM field in the Leads page's Update Details is now the shared `MultiSelectField`**, the same
  multi-select as a role's Manage Users, with its search, Select all and Clear, instead of the
  page's own tick-list. Ticking several CRMs still shares the selected leads out between them in
  turn, previewed in the table below. The page's `CrmMultiSelectField` is removed.
  [CRMPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CRMPage.js)
- **A role's sub-module rows can now be changed whatever the module is set to, and the module's
  dropdown follows them.** Under Read or Read / Write the rows used to show the module's answer
  and refuse a change; now changing one turns the module Custom, keeping the other rows at the
  level they had. Whenever every row lands on one level the dropdown says so: all Read is **Read**,
  all Read & Write is **Read / Write**, and all No access is **Disabled**, which closes the module.
  The column-head radios do the same. What is saved is unchanged.
  [RoleDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/admin/RoleDialog.js)
- **The role form has one search over every module and permission, in place of a search inside each
  open module.** It sits under the Branch Admin tick, above the modules, and clears with the
  Material close icon from a new reusable `SearchField` rather than the browser's own ×. A module whose name matches shows whole;
  otherwise only its matching sub-modules show, and modules matching nothing are hidden. Matching
  modules open automatically, Disabled ones included, and clearing the search puts them back.
  Enter in the box no longer submits the form. A viewer with read-only access can now search and
  open modules to read them, where before the whole form, chevrons included, was disabled: the
  form now locks each field that changes the role instead of the whole panel.
  [RoleDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/admin/RoleDialog.js)
- **A role's modules now open and close as an accordion, from a chevron at the left end of the
  row.** It points down while a module's sub-modules are hidden and up while they are shown, and
  replaces both the "−" that closed a module from the right end and the module name as an unmarked
  second toggle. It is announced as a button with `aria-expanded`, its label says Show or Hide, and
  it names the sub-module panel it controls. A Disabled module keeps the chevron's space, so the
  names still line up. [RoleDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/admin/RoleDialog.js)
- **Who carries a role is now chosen on the role form, in a Manage Users section, instead of a
  separate dialog from the row menu.** Creating a role can now assign its users in the same save.
  The section lists the active accounts carrying the role from a new
  `GET /api/admin/roles/:roleId/users` (one query, replacing the per-account role reads the old
  dialog made), and on **Save / Update** assigns and removes only the accounts that changed, after
  the role is saved. It answers to **ADMIN / User Management** — the permission of the assign and
  remove endpoints — so it is absent without it, read-only at `READ` and editable at `READ_WRITE`;
  the old menu entry was offered on Role Management alone and then refused by those endpoints. A
  locked role's View can still be saved for its users. `RoleUsersDialog.js` is removed and
  `RolePicker` gains `readOnly`. No new permission, so no role needs re-saving.
  [RoleDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/admin/RoleDialog.js),
  [RoleManagement.js](../frontend/src/components/admin/RoleManagement.js),
  [admin/routes.js](../backend/src/modules/admin/routes.js)
- **The remark box now scrolls with the remarks instead of holding the top of the tab, on both the
  CRM lead popup and the Interview candidate popup.** It had been pinned so the box for the next
  note never had to be scrolled to; in practice a box that holds the top spends the pane's height on
  an empty textarea, on logs that are read straight down. Writing a remark is a deliberate act on
  both screens - each refuses an update without one and says so - so the box does not have to stay
  permanently in reach. Refusing a save now **scrolls that box, and the reason, back into view**
  rather than only switching to the Remarks tab: Remarks is the tab both popups open on, so
  switching to it was usually a no-op, and the pin was what had been keeping the box on screen.
  Without that, somebody who had scrolled down through a long history would have been refused for a
  box they could not see - and on the lead popup the message itself sits above the box, so it was
  already scrolling out of reach. The Add Lead form and the CRM info panel never pinned their
  composer and are unchanged; with no caller left, the `pinComposer` option is gone from
  [NotesComposer](../frontend/src/components/shared/NotesComposer.js) rather than kept as a setting
  nobody passes ([CRMPage](../frontend/src/components/sales/CRMPage.js),
  [InterviewRemarksTab](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewRemarksTab.js),
  [InterviewCandidatePopup](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewCandidatePopup.js)).

- **Anybody who sends from this application can now link their own WhatsApp, not just the CRM.** The
  session is per **user** — credentials are stored per user id and every message goes out from the phone
  that person paired, which is already how the screening form, the onboarding invite and a new joiner's
  login are sent. But the route that shows the pairing QR sat behind `SALES / CRM Leads`, so an HR user
  was told they were not linked and had nowhere to link it. Pairing and unpairing your **own** account now
  sit above that guard, beside `GET /my-session` which was lifted for the same reason, and answer to
  whichever of the three jobs actually messages anybody — CRM Leads, HRM / Interview, or
  HRM / Employee Management. A lead's conversation stays behind the CRM's permission. The candidate
  popup's WhatsApp tab shows the code when the viewer is not linked, instead of a compose box that was
  refused on send
  ([routes.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/whatsapp-chat/routes.js),
  [WhatsAppLinkCard.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/WhatsAppLinkCard.js),
  [InterviewWhatsAppTab.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewWhatsAppTab.js)).
  The pairing card is **one component** now rather than markup inside the lead panel, and it asks for a
  code only when a person presses the button: pairing is deliberately not rate limited on the server, and
  each attempt is a real registration against a number WhatsApp can ban for registering repeatedly.

- **Client Storage asks its yes/no questions with Yes / No radio buttons instead of switches.** All seven
  checks — Labeled?, Footage Backup, Final Files Copy, Harddisk Footages Back up, Folder Structure
  Checked, Final Renders, Other Files in Harddisk — on the storage form and at every step of the flow
  that asks them (Hand In, Footage Backup Done, HDD Out), plus Shoot Status Pending, which is a reading
  rather than a question and would have been the one switch left among seven pairs. The same change the
  pre production shoot form already had, through the same field helper, which now lives on its own
  ([yesNoField.js](../frontend/src/constants/yesNoField.js)) rather than in the pre production field list
  ([formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js)).

- **Switching Storage Needed to Yes no longer explains itself.** Pre-Production's General bar drew a
  dashed box reading "No hard disk record yet — saving Storage Needed as Yes raises one" the moment the
  answer was turned on, which told somebody the mechanism they had just used: they chose Yes, they are
  about to save, and the disk appears when they do. Nothing was being asked and nothing had gone wrong.
  The Hard Disk field now waits until there is a disk to show — the whole field rather than an empty
  renderer, which would have left a gap in the grid where the box was
  ([PreProductionGeneral.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionGeneral.js)).

- **In the lead popup, the remarks box now sits at the top and the remarks read newest first.** The box
  and its toolbar used to be under the whole list, so on a lead with many remarks the next note meant
  scrolling past every earlier one, and the latest remark was at the bottom. The box is now first and stays
  in view while the remarks scroll beneath it, with the most recent remark directly under it. Nothing
  about what is saved changed: the remarks are stored in the order they were written, and editing one
  still rewrites that entry. The same composer serves the candidate popup and the Add Lead and info
  panels, which get the new order too; the lead popup and the candidate popup's Remarks tab both pin the box
  ([NotesComposer.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/NotesComposer.js),
  [CRMPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CRMPage.js),
  [InterviewRemarksTab.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewRemarksTab.js)).
- **The candidate popup's Next Follow-up date no longer stretches across the whole card.** It takes one
  column of the same grid the lead popup's Follow-up Details uses: full width on a phone, half the card
  from tablet width and a third on wide screens
  ([InterviewCandidatePopup.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewCandidatePopup.js)).
- **The candidate popup now has a Call Logs tab, and Remarks reads like a lead's.** Call Logs answers
  the question the **Follow Up** stage exists to ask and the register could not: has anybody actually
  rung this candidate, when, for how long, and which of the studio's people was on it. The studio's call
  log is one table fed by the handset integration and keyed by the number dialled, so a recruiter's call
  lands in it exactly as a salesperson's does — it had only ever been read from the CRM's lead popup.
  **A recruiter is shown the call and nothing about the CRM's client**: a number that is a candidate here
  can be a client there, so the client's name, enquiry, CRM status, recording, note and raw payload are
  all stripped — `HRM / Interview` is not a grant of `CRM / Leads`. **Remarks is now the lead's
  remarks composer itself** — the collapsible entry bubbles, the bullet and numbered lists, Enter to
  post, the send button in the toolbar — not a box that resembles it. `NotesComposer` had been sitting
  unexported in the middle of `CRMPage.js`, which is how the register came to have a second, poorer
  answer to "how do I write down what was said"; it now lives in `components/shared/` and nothing about
  it changed for the lead — and it imports no service of its own, the upload and fetch behind its
  paperclip arriving from whichever module owns the bucket the files are in. Two of its controls are switched off for a candidate: the **pencil**, because
  `statusNotes` is append-only with no per-entry id and no endpoint that rewrites one, and the
  **paperclip**, because a candidate's remark has nowhere to put a file. Each bubble also carries the
  **stage** the remark was written at, which a lead's has no equivalent of — "they asked to be called
  back" means one thing at Follow Up and another at Selected. **Activity Logs** is the same log read as *what
  happened* — the stage, when it moved and who moved it — so the card no longer holds one list twice. The
  two panes also share the width better: the record was taking two thirds of the screen for a form that
  draws only the fields the candidate answered
  ([InterviewCallLogsTab.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewCallLogsTab.js),
  [InterviewRemarksTab.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewRemarksTab.js),
  [interviewInfoFormatters.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/interviewInfoFormatters.js),
  [callLogService.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/callLogService.js)).

- **Position Applied For is no longer required when the studio writes a candidate down.** Add
  Application and the candidate record still ask for it and the register still files by it, but a
  blank one is accepted: the job somebody is after is regularly unknown at the moment the application
  arrives — a walk-in, a number passed on by a friend of the studio, a CV with no covering note — and
  refusing the row for it bought either a guess typed into the field or the candidate not being
  written down at all. The server already took it as optional, so this removes a refusal the frontend
  was making on its own
  ([InterviewAddApplicationDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewAddApplicationDialog.js),
  [interviewConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/interviewConfig.js),
  [candidateRecordForm.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/candidateRecordForm.js)).
  The **candidate's own screening form still requires it**, which is where the real answer comes from.

- **Double-clicking a candidate on HRM → Interview now opens the screen where they are worked, not
  a read-only card.** One popup holds the whole errand: the fields the candidate actually filled in
  (with the empty ones one press away), a remark composer, the activity log, a WhatsApp message, and
  a Follow-up Details card where the stage is chosen. Choosing **Follow Up** asks when, directly
  under the pills; choosing **Selected**, **On Hold** or **Rejected** is answered by the remark, which
  Update requires — so the register can always say why a candidate moved. The three stages that are
  consequences of an act — Form Submission Pending, Interview Scheduled, Onboarded — offer that act
  instead, and confirming it saves the record and opens the act's own form **over** the popup, which
  stays open underneath — cancelling that form puts you back on the candidate, and only the act
  succeeding writes the stage and closes both;
  **Form Submitted** is refused outright, because that stage is the candidate answering. **Choosing a
  stage asks for its remark first**: the pill records the choice, the card says a remark is needed to
  move that candidate, the Remarks tab comes forward, and Update writes the stage and the reason
  together or neither. Pressing Update with no remark is refused in the **snackbar** rather than as a
  banner above the form — it is not a fault in a field, and a banner pushed the record down the screen
  and stayed there to be re-read. **Schedule Interview and Send Screening Form draw their form over the popup**
  rather than closing it — closing that form leaves the popup exactly as it was, and only a round
  actually booked or a form actually sent closes both. Posting a remark or sending a WhatsApp message
  no longer closes the popup either. A viewer with
  **read-only** HRM access gets the record, the log and no editable field — the guard is
  `ReadOnlyFieldset`'s own `canWrite`, and the press that opens the empty fields sits outside it, since
  reading the whole record is exactly what that viewer is there to do. The side
  drawer this replaces is gone, and the ⋮'s **Edit** / **Review** opens the same popup, so there is
  one editor for a candidate rather than two
  Answering the stage question no longer raises a second one: `Dialog` draws inside the popup rather
  than portalling out of it, so a press on **Leave the stage as it is** used to bubble to the popup's
  dimmed backdrop and put "Close without saving?" on top of its own answer — in any tab and at any
  stage. A press on the backdrop is now a press whose target *is* the backdrop
  ([InterviewCandidatePopup.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewCandidatePopup.js),
  [candidateRecordForm.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/candidateRecordForm.js),
  [InterviewPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewPage.js)).
  The **Onboarded** pill is only offered to somebody holding `HRM / Employee Management`
  READ_WRITE — the same permission the row menu's Send Onboarding Invite is gated on — and a
  read-only viewer gets the record, the log and no way to move anybody.

- **Branch reach now follows the role that granted the permission, not the person.** Somebody who
  holds CRM Leads across every branch through one role and Asset Management in one branch through
  another now sees every branch's leads and one branch's assets, where before the wider role
  silently widened the narrower one. Every call into the branch API names the `{ module, feature }`
  it is asking about; a role naming no branches contributes none, and a person's own
  `user.branch_id` no longer widens anything — work they or their team are named on still reaches
  them through `dataScope`
  ([iam.service.js](../backend/src/services/iam.service.js),
  [dataScope.service.js](../backend/src/services/dataScope.service.js)).
  **A read-only role's branches no longer scope writes**: `dataScope.resolve` takes the access level,
  so an employee write is measured against the roles that grant READ_WRITE.

- **Start Project's radio buttons now sit in a bordered box with the same title style as the
  fields around them.** Welcome Gift, Shoot Completed Gift, Storage Needed and CRD Document match
  the pre production form's Yes / No radios, through a new `variant="field"` on the shared
  `RadioGroupField`; an unanswered required group now reddens its box too
  ([RadioGroupField.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/RadioGroupField.js),
  [StartProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/StartProjectFormPanel.js)).

- **The pre production shoot form asks its yes/no questions with Yes / No radio buttons instead
  of switches.** Travel & Accommodation Needed, WRC and every checklist yes/no (Event Schedule
  Meeting, Invitation Soft Copy, Site Visit, Team Reached Message, Shoot Completion Message, Google
  Review) now show both answers side by side; what is saved is unchanged
  ([preProductionVerticalFields.js](../frontend/src/constants/preProductionVerticalFields.js),
  [formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js)).

- **A shoot's pre production status now works itself out; nobody sets it by hand.** Completion
  Status is gone from the shoot form. A shoot with no details filled is Not Started, one with every
  counted detail filled (checklist included) is Completed, and anything between is In Progress, so
  the tabs, card dots and completed counts move as details are saved. **On Hold is gone** - it
  cannot be worked out from the details - so its tab is removed. The API no longer accepts or
  returns `completionStatus`; the `completion_status` column is left in place, unread
  ([preProductionProgress.js](../frontend/src/lib/preProductionProgress.js),
  [PreProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionPage.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **A shoot card's "details pending" now counts the Dum Dum or Qua Qua checklist too.** A
  checklist question counts as done once it is Completed, an action toggle once it is on, and the
  meeting and invitation fields only when their switch is on; remarks are not counted. A shoot no
  longer reads "All details filled" while its checklist is untouched
  ([PreProductionProjectPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionProjectPanel.js)).

- **The pre production shoot form now leads with the creative work and ends with the logistics.**
