  The Dum Dum or Qua Qua checklist sits straight under Concepts, and Location and Event Timing
  come after Travel & Accommodation; Status stays last
  ([formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js)).

- **Switching a gift, the hard disk or the CRD document on or off now asks why, and keeps the
  answer.** In Pre Production's General panel, changing Welcome Kit, Shoot Completed Gift, Storage
  Needed or CRD Document between applicable and not asks for a reason before it saves; each switch
  is kept in the new `project_applicability_change` table with who made it and when, and while an
  item stays not applicable its section shows the reason it was switched off. The project save records a switch from any screen, so one
  made on Edit Project appears too, without a reason. Migration
  `20260926140000_add_project_applicability_changes`; run `prisma migrate deploy`
  ([PreProductionGeneral.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionGeneral.js),
  [projects/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js)).

- **Pre Production's General is a bar above the shoot cards that opens into an editable panel.**
  It was the first tile among the shoots. It now spans the panel above them, showing Welcome Kit,
  Shoot Completed Gift, Hard Disk and CRD Document as filled-in values; clicking it opens a panel —
  back to the shoots, follow-ups beside it — with a section for each. Every part saves through the
  screen that owns it, under that screen's permission: the gifts' Applicable and Assigned To,
  Storage Needed and CRD Document through Edit Project's save (`PROJECT / Projects` or `Show All
  Projects` at READ_WRITE — saving Storage Needed or CRD as applicable raises their records as it
  does there); a gift's Status through Client Gifts (`PROJECT / Client Gifts`), its sent and
  received dates stamping themselves; and the hard disk moves along the Client Storage flow —
  assign, hand in, backup, HDD out, in transit, delivered — with the same dialogs as the Client
  Storage screen (`ASSET / Client Storage`), now shared from `useClientStorageMoves`. A part the
  viewer may not change is shown filled in and read-only. No new permission; no role needs re-saving
  ([PreProductionGeneral.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionGeneral.js),
  [useClientStorageMoves.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/useClientStorageMoves.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **A Pre Production shoot can hold several concepts, and Location now comes before Event Timing.**
  Concepts were a yes/no toggle over one Reference and one Remarks box; the toggle is gone and the
  shoot form now shows a list added one by one with **+ Add Concept** — each with its own Reference
  and Remarks, removable — the same way an employee's qualifications are entered. The list keeps a
  fixed height and scrolls inside it once it grows past that. The read-back lists them one per line.
  Location moves above Event Timing on the form and the read-back. Existing concepts are carried
  over as the first of each shoot's list by migration
  `20260926130000_add_pre_production_concepts_list`; run `prisma migrate deploy`
  ([PreProductionFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionFormPanel.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **Pre Production follow-ups are a list beside the shoot cards, and only ask for the next date.**
  A project's follow-ups now sit in a column on the right of its Pre Production panel (under the
  cards on a phone) instead of a single form below them, and the same column stays beside a shoot
  when one is opened — its form, or its details for a reader. The board's refresh icon is gone. **Add Follow-up** asks for the Next
  Followup Date and Remarks — no Last Followup Date — and the follow-up joins the project's
  **Pending** list; **Mark done** moves it to a **Completed** list below, and a list with nothing in
  it is not shown. The earliest pending date is the project's Next
  Followup Date and the last one marked done its Last Followup Date, so the board's columns and
  overdue colouring work as before; the overdue banner above the table is gone. Follow-ups stay the project's, never a single shoot's. Existing
  follow-ups are carried over by migration `20260926120000_add_pre_production_followup_entries`
  (a next date becomes a pending follow-up, a last date one already done); run `prisma migrate
  deploy`. Guarded by the existing `PROJECT / Pre Production` — READ sees the list, READ_WRITE adds
  and marks done; no role needs re-saving
  ([PreProductionFollowups.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionFollowups.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **Pre Production is in the sidebar, under Project Management.** The board was only reachable by
  typing its address; it now sits after Projects, stays lit on the Corp, Dum Dum and Qua Qua boards
  beneath it, and shows only to roles holding `PROJECT / Pre Production` at `READ` or above — no
  new permission, and no role needs re-saving. A saved Sidebar Layout gets the entry appended to
  Project Management. Production and Post Production stay off the menu
  ([navigation.mjs](../frontend/src/constants/navigation.mjs),
  [sidebarStructure.js](../backend/src/modules/user/preferences/sidebarStructure.js)).

- **Create Project's Enquiry ID now lists CRM leads, and brings their vertical with it.** It
  searched existing projects, which is circular — only an enquiry that already had a project could
  be found, so a genuine new lead could never be picked and the field was really a free-text box. It
  now searches `sales_crm_lead` by enquiry id, name or number, leaves out any lead that already has
  a live project, and fills in the client, the number they are messaged on, the branch it is worked
  from and the **Product** from the lead's own vertical — the answer the studio gave when the lead
  was taken, so nobody is asked for it twice
  ([projects/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js),
  [CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js)).

- **Pre production's follow-up is now the project's, not each shoot's.** A coordinator rings the
  couple about the wedding, not about the Haldi and then again about the Reception, so Last Followup
  Date, Next Followup Date and Followup Remarks moved out of the per-shoot form into a Follow-up
  panel below the shoot cards, stored once per project. Existing per-shoot entries were carried
  across by the migration — the most recent contact and the soonest date owed — so no chasing was
  lost, and the old columns are kept but deprecated
  ([PreProductionProjectPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionProjectPanel.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **A manual WhatsApp group name now asks which product the sale is.** A reserved group name has
  always carried its vertical (Dum Dum → WED, Qua Qua → QQ, Corp → CORP), but typing a group name
  cleared it silently — and a project with no vertical reaches no branch board and gets no vertical
  checklist in Pre Production. Create Project and Edit Sale Details now show a required Product
  (Group Type) selector whenever no reserved name is attached, the server derives the vertical from
  it with the generator's own mapping, and editing a legacy project is how it gets backfilled
  ([CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js),
  [projects/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js)).

- **An extra quotation's files are called Attachments, not Proof.** The label on the form, the
  section heading where the record is read back, and the links on Project Payments all said
  "Proof" — a narrower word than what the field is actually used for. The stored keys are unchanged
  (`proof`, `proofUrls`), so this is what the reader sees and nothing else.

- **The role menu lists every role, ticks the ones already held, and unticking one gives it up.** It
  used to drop held roles from the list, which said the wrong thing — a role missing from a list of
  roles reads as one that does not exist or cannot be granted, not as one this account already
  carries. The menu is now the whole picture and a real toggle: tick to stage a role for Add, untick
  to remove one the account holds. Removing this way is the same call the row's Remove button makes,
  immediate and undoable, so the menu is not a quieter way to do something the row would have asked
  about first. Branch selection on a role already behaved this way and is unchanged.

- **Every new account starts on one known password instead of a generated one.** Creating login
  credentials for an employee used to mint a random 12-character password per person, which had to
  be read off the screen and passed on individually. It is now the same starting password for
  everyone, `123qweasdzxc`, and the Regenerate control is gone. The server's
  uppercase-and-symbol requirement went with it — it refused the chosen password — leaving a
  minimum length, since whatever arrives is hashed and becomes a real password.

  **This leans on a guard that is not built yet.** Accounts are created with
  `mustChangePassword: true` and the login response carries the flag, but nothing reads it: there is
  no forced change-password screen on either side. Until there is, this password stays valid on
  every account whose owner has not changed it by choice, and it is written in the repository. The
  flag is already in place, so the screen is the only piece missing.

- **The spinner is drawn as an SVG, so the moving part cannot go missing.** It was a bordered box
  whose blue arc existed only as `border-t-blue-600` overriding a full grey `border-color`, with its
  width from an arbitrary `border-[3px]` and its style resolved through a `@property` variable. Any
  one of those not landing left a plain grey ring — and a *uniform* ring that rotates looks
  completely still, because the arc is the only thing that shows movement. It is now a grey circle
  and a blue quarter-turn as two explicit strokes, which no cascade can flatten into one colour. The
  Public Gallery's own hand-rolled copy of the old markup now uses the shared component too.

- **Every full-page wait shows the same spinner in the same place.** Moving between modules drew a
  large spinner centred in the content area, and the permission check that follows drew a smaller
  one centred in a 16rem box — so the loader visibly jumped upward and shrank between two halves of
  the same wait. `Checking access…`, `Loading workspace…` and the route-change loader now all render
  through `PageLoader`, which fills whatever surface it is given, and the refusal that can follow a
  failed permission fetch sits in that same box rather than higher up. Only the words change between
  them. See [RouteGuard.js](../frontend/src/components/auth/RouteGuard.js) and
  [RequireAuth.js](../frontend/src/components/auth/RequireAuth.js).

- **The Accounts footers carry Last updated and Total rows, and no running totals.** Accounts
  Manager showed Received, Spent and Net; Payment Requests showed Pending and Approved. Both put a
  second, differently-scoped set of figures under a table that was already listing the amounts they
  summed. The reduces that fed them went with them rather than being left to recompute on every
  filter change for a value nobody shows. The CRM and Meetings footers keep their own counts and
  guidance, which read as that page's own commentary rather than a total.

- **An edit panel's button says Update; only creating still says Save.** Every form that opens for
  both adding and editing offered the same **Save**, so the control gave no clue which of the two
  the panel was doing — the heading read *Edit Vendor* while the button under it read *Save Vendor*.
  Each panel now reuses the condition its own title is already built from, so heading and button
  cannot disagree: Update Vendor, Update Storage, Update Asset, Update Account, Update Entry, Update
  Offboarding, Update Project, and a plain **Update** on the employee, shoot, role and extra
  quotation panels. Creating is untouched, and so are the settings panels — Image Selection
  Settings, Table Settings, Project Settings and Quotation Pricing have nothing to create, so
  **Save** is still the right word there.

- **A WhatsApp group name says the branch as a short code.** `Erode` → **ERD**, `Tiruppur` → **TPR**,
  `Coimbatore` → **CBE**, `Bangalore` → **BLR**, `Hyderabad` → **HYD**, `Vizag` → **VSKP**. The name
  is read in WhatsApp's own chat list, where it is truncated to a phone's width, so five characters
  spent on "Erode" are five the couple and the date lose off the end. All three shapes use it —
  `WED Premium VSKP Arun & Meena`, `QQTPR Asha`, `CORP CBE Acme`. The register spells a branch with
  its state after it and the sheets do not, so "Erode TN", "Visakhapatnam AP", "Bengaluru" and
  "Tirupur" all reach the right code; a branch with no code is left exactly as typed rather than
  dropped. **The list is held in the code, not read from the branch table**, and is deliberately
  separate from the one in `backend/src/services/identifiers.js`: that one mints enquiry ids and
  writes Tiruppur as `TUP` and Vizag as `VIZAG`, so changing it would rename the branch segment of
  every id minted afterwards and split one studio's records across two spellings.
  [whatsappGroupNameUtils.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/whatsappGroupNameUtils.js),
  [group-name-branch-code.test.mjs](../frontend/test/group-name-branch-code.test.mjs).

- **A linked sheet no longer loses a whole lead over one unreadable cell — it blanks the cell and
  keeps the row.** A row was refused outright when any single field failed to parse, and the fields
  that fail are the ones a person answers in their own words: `feb 10 th and 11 th 2027` in *When is
  the Event Planned*, `Immediate` in *When Can You Join*, a state name where a date was expected.
  Each of those took a whole enquiry with it — the name, the number, the campaign that paid for it —
  so a studio could sync ten new leads and import none of them. Now the unreadable cell is stored as
  **null** and every readable column on the row is kept as it is. It applies to both linked
  integrations and to every field that can fail: name, email, lead status, all six date columns and
  all six phone columns. **A row with no name imports too**, with the name blank — a lead is a lead,
  and a wholly empty spreadsheet row never reaches the importer anyway. Cells are blanked *before*
  the row is matched, so a phone the importer could not read is not a phone it tries to find an
  existing lead by. Deduplication is untouched: a readable phone that already belongs to a lead is
  still recognised and the row still skipped. The summary reports **"6 fields left blank"** on a line
  of its own rather than as rows skipped — nothing was skipped — and names each one by column and
  row (`row 12 — eventPlannedDate: Invalid date value`) so the sheet can be corrected. The import
  preview counts them under **Fields Left Blank** in place of *Invalid Rows*, which is now always 0.
  [googleSheetsService.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/googleSheetsService.js),
  [sheetImport.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/interview/sheetImport.js),
  `hrm_interview_candidate.name` had to be widened to nullable to honour this — it was the one
  column that could not, so a nameless row was being stored as `''`, which on this schema is exactly
  what a blank must never be
  ([20260926090000_interview_candidate_name_nullable](../backend/prisma/migrations/20260926090000_interview_candidate_name_nullable/migration.sql);
  `sales_crm_lead.name` has always been nullable). One trade-off worth stating: a **phone** that
  cannot be read is blanked like anything else, and the phone is the deduplication key. A re-sync of
  the same sheet row still matches on its source id or position, but a first sync against a lead
  somebody typed in by hand that shares only that malformed phone will now import beside it rather
  than being refused — losing the row was the previous answer, and this is the one that keeps it.
  [sheet-import-blank-bad-fields.test.js](../backend/test/sheet-import-blank-bad-fields.test.js).

### Fixed

- **The activity-log tests pass on CI.** Four tests in `activity-log-purge.test.js` and
  `user-activity-log.test.js` signed tokens - and signed in - with `JWT_SECRET`, which CI does not
  set (there is no `.env` there; locally Prisma loads it), so they failed with "secretOrPrivateKey
  must have a value" and a 500 from sign-in. They now use a test-only secret where none is set, as
  the other HTTP tests do. Tests only; no application change.

- **On the client's CRD form, a required field left blank now shows red.** After Submit with
  something missing, each blank required text field (name, Insta ID, address, city and so on) gets a
  red border and "… is required." beneath it. Its red border used to lose to the box's own grey one,
  so the client was told something was missing but couldn't see which field. Qua Qua's **Shoot
  Type** and **Branch** now say "Choose the Shoot Type." and "Choose the Branch." when left
  unanswered; before, they showed nothing. Dates and phone numbers already showed their error.
  - The **terms & conditions** box now turns red with "Tick the box to agree to the terms &
    conditions." Before, only its sentence went a shade darker, so when it was the one missing
    answer nothing looked red.
  - A missing **photo**'s "No photo" box turns red too, not only the line of text under it.
  - The notice now just says "Please fill the mandatory fields.", and the form scrolls straight to
    the first red field instead of the top of its section, so the fields show what is missing.
  [crdDocumentShared.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/crdDocumentShared.js),
  [PublicCrdDocumentFormQuaQua.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/PublicCrdDocumentFormQuaQua.js).

- **A shoot running past midnight can be saved in Pre Production, and every screen says it ends the
  next day.** A shoot from 9:00 PM to 2:00 AM is entered as its start Date, Start Time 9:00 PM and End
  Time 2:00 AM; an end earlier than the start means the next day.
  - Pre Production used to refuse it with "Event End Time cannot be before Event Start Time". It now
    saves, and the field's label reads **Event End Time (next day)** while it applies.
  - The client's CRD form labels such an event's **End Time (next day)**, and the studio's view adds
    "(next day)" to the time.
  - The Shoot Board reads "9:00 pm – 2:00 am (next day)".
  - Production's crew check already read it this way.
  [shootBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/shootBoard.mjs),
  [formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js).

- **A submitted CRD document now reads back every answer the client gave, and nothing else.** On
  ⋮ → View and on the response share link - one renderer serves both - two kinds of answer were
  stored and shown to nobody. A side's Last Name was read by nothing at all, and Qua Qua's dated
  Birthdays questions (Baby Name, Baby Date of Birth, Expected Delivery Date, Child Birthday /
  Expected Delivery Date) were drawn only for the Shoot Type's own category: a document whose Shoot
  Type was blank belonged to no category and showed none of them, and one whose Shoot Type was
  changed after the client answered showed the new category's questions instead of the ones they
  were actually asked. Every question is now read back, and the rule for whether a row appears sits
  in one place - an answer that was given is shown, a question left blank is not drawn, and a
  section with nothing under it goes with its rows rather than leaving a heading over empty space.
  The dashed placeholder row that used to stand in for an unanswered question is gone with it
  ([CrdDocumentResponse.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CrdDocumentResponse.js)).

- **The client's CRD form takes spaces in reference remarks, and a photo remark without a photo.**
  - In Photo, Video and Other Reference Links, the space typed at the end of a remark used to vanish
    at once, so words could only be split by going back and inserting one. Remarks are now kept as
    typed while the form is open and trimmed only when stored, like every other answer.
  - The Photo Reference remark was dropped unless a photo had been added. It is now kept without
    one.
  - An autosave no longer replaces what is on screen with the server's trimmed copy. Before, a
    space at the end of any answer disappeared the moment the client paused, and anything typed
    while a save was on its way was lost. Only what the server really changed, such as an uploaded
    photo turning into its stored link, is taken back.
  [crdReferenceRows.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/crdReferenceRows.mjs),
  [crdDocumentShared.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/crdDocumentShared.js).

- **Saving or syncing a Google Sheet link now reports success in the green notice: "N leads were
  added."** It used to print the whole sync summary on the red error line, so a save that worked -
  with most rows "skipped" only because they were already in the CRM - read as a failure. The notice
  now gives the number added alone, 0 included ("candidates" on the Interview sheets); the full
  summary is still on the link's own row under Last sync. A real failure stays on the error line.
  The notice now shows on every save and sync, not only the first: a second sync with the same
  answer used to set the same text the panel had already dismissed, so nothing appeared until the
  page was reopened. It is cleared as each save or sync starts.
  [GoogleSheetsIntegrationSection.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/GoogleSheetsIntegrationSection.js)

- **Generate Quotation stays shut until the quotation is complete.** The button used to be pressable
  with required fields empty and only complained afterwards. It is now disabled while Enquire ID or
  any starred field is empty, while a contact number is only partly typed (the field says "Enter the
  whole number."), while the discount is over its limit, and while a save is running - and it opens
  the moment the last one is put right. Beside the buttons (and on a tap of the shut button on a
  phone) the form names what is still missing. Save Draft is unchanged. See
  [QuotationGeneratorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationGeneratorPanel.js).

- **The backend test suite passes on a developer's Windows machine with their own database.** The
  AI tools "record not found" test stubs the signed-in user instead of needing user 1 in the
  database ([ai-tools-read.test.js](../backend/test/ai-tools-read.test.js)); the whisper
  missing-package test skips where `python3` is absent or is the Windows Store alias, and still
  runs on CI ([call-transcripts-python.test.js](../backend/test/call-transcripts-python.test.js));
  and the Reports Employee filter test no longer fails when another suite deletes its own employee
  between two reads ([report-employee-options.test.js](../backend/test/report-employee-options.test.js)).

- **The boot sweep of the retired upload staging folders reads a Windows-style upload root the same
  way on Linux.** The guard that lets the sweep run only under a folder named `image-selection`
  now splits the path on both `\` and `/`, so `D:\studio\uploads\image-selection` qualifies on every
  platform and the backend test suite passes on the Linux CI runner as it did on Windows
  ([service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/uploads/service.js)).

- **The AI Culling header stays in view while the review scrolls, as AI Editing's does.** The title,
  the folder line with its photo count and mode, the status badge and (on the desktop) Add photos sit
  in one sticky block inside the tab's own scrolling pane - the AI Editing header's pattern: flush with
  the pane's top at every width, opaque so the photos pass beneath it, no fixed positioning and no
  second scrollbar. Add photos keeps its place under the title and still opens the drop zone below.
  Layout only - web ([CullingWorkspace.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/culling/CullingWorkspace.js))
  and desktop.
- **AI Editing's header and search stay in view while the photos scroll, and the selection bar
  follows the app's theme.** The title, folder line, status chips, Add photos, Search file names and
  Select all on page now sit in one sticky block inside the tab's own scrolling pane, flush with its
  top at every width, with photos passing under its solid background - no fixed positioning and no
  second scrollbar. The bar that appears with ticked photos was a fixed navy slab; it is now the
  app's own surface (white with a border and shadow, the web's dark themes remapping it to their
  surface through the existing `[data-theme]` rules), with Edit selected as the primary button and
  the other actions as the kit's secondary ones, readable in both themes and lifted clear of a
  phone's home indicator on the web. The AI Culling review's bar keeps its look. UI only - web
  ([AiEditingWorkspace.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/editing/AiEditingWorkspace.js))
  and desktop.
- **AI Editing's face tools work on the desktop app again: under-eye correction, teeth whitening,
  eye enhancement, and the eyebrow, eye, iris, lip, teeth and facial-hair regions.** The desktop
  rendered them without the face landmark model (`buffalo_l/1k3d68.onnx`) and said it was "not
  installed on this server". The server had the model all along and offers it to the desktop in
  its runtime manifest, but the app decides "ready" from its two core face files only, so a
  workstation that installed Local AI before the landmark model was offered never fetched it.
  The desktop now reports which optional models are on disk, and when the server offers one it
  lacks it runs its usual verified download (size and SHA-256 against the manifest, nothing else
  touched) and restarts the editing engine so the next render uses it. Every missing-model note and
  reason now names the file and where it was looked for - "this server", or on the desktop "this
  computer (Settings, Local AI, Repair fetches it from the server)" - and the general tools still
  apply when a face model is absent. In the editor the actions now sit right under the photo and
  the render's notes read below them under "Notes from this render", so a render with notes no
  longer pushes Apply and Send to Signature Album out of the window; while the sliders have moved
  since, the heading says the notes describe the last render. **Deploy:** restart the backend so it
  serves the new `edit_engine.py` (the desktop re-fetches it by digest); nothing to migrate.
  [ai.rs](../../Image-Selection_Desktop---BCT/src-tauri/src/ai.rs),
  [localEngine.js](../../Image-Selection_Desktop---BCT/src/processing/ai/localEngine.js),
  [edit_engine.py](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-editing/edit_engine.py),
  [EditingPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/editing/EditingPanel.js),
  [EditingPanel.jsx](../../Image-Selection_Desktop---BCT/src/modules/image-selection/editing/EditingPanel.jsx).

- **The AI Editing editor's photo no longer breaks the layout: portrait and landscape photos sit
  in a viewer sized by the workspace, in every compare mode, on the web and in the desktop app.**
  The frame used to take the editor's full width and the photo's own ratio, so a portrait photo
  grew taller than the window and pushed Apply, Reset and Send to Signature Album out of sight,
  and Side by side did the same per panel. The frame is now bounded by the room the workspace
  has - the editor's column across, and the viewport less the headers and bars down (never under
  14rem, never over 64rem) - and its width is worked out from that height and the photo's ratio,
  so it hugs the photo: a landscape photo fills the column, a portrait one stands as tall as the
  room allows and no wider, and the whole photograph is always shown at its own ratio (object-fit
  contain), never stretched, cropped or letterboxed. The ratio is read from the preview's own
  pixels once they load (the row's recorded size stands in until then), so a workstation's as-shot
  dimensions cannot turn a portrait frame sideways. One rule serves Before / After, Split (the
  divider's geometry stays exact) and both Side by side panels (one size, level); the loading
  state takes the same frame; the zoom dialog leaves it where it is; moving from a portrait photo
  to a landscape one moves neither the sidebar nor the action bar; and the compare mode chosen is
  kept from photo to photo while Before / After stays per photo.
  [EditingPreview.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/editing/EditingPreview.js),
  [imageSelectionEditing.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/imageSelectionEditing.mjs),
  [EditingPreview.jsx](../../Image-Selection_Desktop---BCT/src/modules/image-selection/editing/EditingPreview.jsx).

- **Send to Signature Album from AI Editing never sends a stale result.** A photo whose render was
  still queued, rendering or waiting for the workstation - or whose last render had failed - used
  to fall through as "unedited" and join the album by reference, as the untouched original. The
  server now leaves such a photo where it is and counts it (`notReady`), the summary says "N not
  sent: still rendering, or the render failed. Apply again, then send." - as an error, with the
  selection kept, when nothing at all went - and the editor's own button rests while a render is
  in flight or the sliders have moved since the last Apply. What reaches
  the album is the latest successful render, compressed to the album's own preset from Settings
  (Compression, Signature Album: High 2048px / ~300 KB preview and Standard 480px thumbnail by
  default) exactly as a photo uploaded to the album is.
  [ai-editing/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-editing/service.js),
  [SendPhotosActions.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/SendPhotosActions.js).

- **`npm run prisma:generate` no longer fails with EPERM on Windows while a backend is running.**
  It used to stop the dev server and generate at once, before Windows had released the query
  engine, and it found the server by its command line, so a second `npm run dev` left in another
  terminal still held the file. It now asks Windows which processes have this backend's engine
  loaded, stops each one with the `npm run dev` it belongs to (its Redis included, nothing outside
  it), waits until the file is free, then generates and clears the 21 MB `.tmp` copies earlier
  failures left ([prismaGenerate.js](../backend/scripts/prismaGenerate.js)). Plain
  `npx prisma generate` still cannot replace a file in use; use `npm run prisma:generate` and start
  the backend again afterwards. Development only - CI and the VPS are unchanged.
- **Photos uploaded from the web or the desktop app now keep the time they were taken.** Both
  uploaders re-encode a photo before sending it, which drops its EXIF, so the server never learned
  the capture time. Bursts, similar series and story moments therefore could not form on any
  project uploaded that way, and folders could not be ordered by capture time.
  - **The fix:** each app now reads the date from the original's EXIF header and sends it beside
    the same two derivatives. The web reads only the first 256 KB of the original. The desktop
    uses the EXIF reader it already had. The original itself still never leaves the machine.
  - **The server** keeps the date only inside a sane window
    ([captureDate.js](../backend/src/services/captureDate.js), now shared with the AI Event
    uploader).
  - **Photos uploaded before this fix** still have no capture time. Their similar series form
    only from adjacent, very alike frames.
  - **Desktop batches with a turned-away face:** the server no longer refuses a desktop analysis
    batch because one face turned away gave an impossible eye reading (a real profile face measured
    23.4). The server now takes such a reading as no reading, exactly as its own runs do. Web and
    desktop gave identical signals, badges and verdicts on all 154 real test photos.
  - **Rejected optional model:** an optional face model that fails its pin is moved aside as
    `.rejected` instead of being left for InsightFace to parse.
  - **Compare chip:** the gallery's Compare chip takes a 40 px tap on touch screens, through an
    invisible hit area. Its look is unchanged.
  - **Badges after a re-run:** a culling re-run that reuses cached face results no longer drops the
    "Eyes half closed" and "Looking away" badges. A weighted "Eyes open" answer no longer sits
    beside a contradicting badge.
  - **Similar series in the group views:** the group list and the compare dialog now show the
    members of a similar series, which had come back empty.

  Files:
  [derivativeController.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/uploads/derivativeController.js),
  [imageSelectionUploadStore.js](../frontend/src/lib/imageSelectionUploadStore.js),
  [ai-culling/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/service.js).

  No migration.

- **AI Photo Culling is part of Image Selection: a staff-side triage before the client sees a
  gallery.** On a project with the Photo Culling tab switched on, a run over the selected folder
  scores every processed photo's preview for blur, exposure and near-duplicates or bursts, and, with
  AWS Rekognition configured, faces; the photographer reviews, overrides and finalizes, and only then
  are the rejected photos hidden from Photo Selection and from the publish counts. A photo the client
  already selected is never hidden, reopening a run restores everything, and nothing is ever deleted
  or moved. Only the preview derivative is analysed; no original leaves the studio. It sits behind
  `IMAGE_SELECTION / Project Management`, so the roles that run projects reach it with no new grant
  ([ai-culling/](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/),
  [CullingWorkspace.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/culling/CullingWorkspace.js)).
  Five migrations add four `image_selection_culling_*` tables and a nullable
  `image_selection_upload.cull_rejected_at`; they keep their 2026-08-31 names because development
  databases already hold them, and were rehearsed on a copy built from every committed migration
  with these five applied last, as production will run them. New dependency
  `@aws-sdk/client-rekognition`; new optional variables `AI_CULLING_*` and `AWS_*` in
  `.env.example`. The zoomable preview the workspace gallery dropped on 2026-09-03 is kept for the
  culling review alone ([ImagePreviewDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/ImagePreviewDialog.js)).

- **The progress strip at the foot of a shoot tile is readable in the dark themes.** It stayed a pale
  grey in Dark and Enhanced Dark while its text was drawn for a dark ground, so "Next: …" and the
  percentage all but vanished. The light see-through grey it uses (`bg-slate-50/70`) is now repainted
  like its `/60` and `/40` neighbours, which also fixes the album Publication card that uses it.
  [globals.css](../frontend/src/app/globals.css).

- **A Production shoot opened from its project's tiles has a way back to them.** It opened with no
  back arrow, and saving its Plan left it open, so the only way out was Close - which also dropped
  the project. Now the arrow at the top, Close, and saving or submitting the Plan all return to the
  project's shoots. Its title also shows the shoot straight away, where it read "Production" for a
  moment while the shoot loaded. A shoot opened straight from a row of the board is unchanged. [ProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionPage.js).

- **A table's "Loading..." and "nothing here" now show where you are looking.** Both span every
  column, so on a table wider than the screen - most of them on a laptop, all of them on a phone -
  they sat centred across the whole width, off to the side, and the only way to tell a table was still
  loading was to scroll across to find it. They are now held to the visible part of the table and
  stay there however far it is scrolled left or right, in every table (`DataTable` and `SimpleTable`).
  [DataTable.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/DataTable.js),
  [SimpleTable.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/SimpleTable.js).

- **The backend tests pass again after Payslip moved to My Profile.** The server's copy of the
  sidebar ([sidebarStructure.js](../backend/src/modules/user/preferences/sidebarStructure.js)) was
  missing HRM's `payslip`, which the frontend registry still lists after Payroll as a hidden entry
  (it keeps the page's title and its name in Roles), so the test that holds the two copies together
  failed and blocked `develop`. Payslip stays off the sidebar menu; only the copy changed.

- **Settings → Project: Add and Update in the Service and Deliverable dialogs now save
  immediately.** Pressing Add or Update used to only hold the change on the page until the Save at
  the bottom was pressed, so a service or deliverable that looked added was lost if the panel was
  left without saving. Each dialog now writes to the server when it is submitted - a deliverable's
  brands and variants included - closes only once the save has succeeded, says so, and refreshes the
  table in place; a failed save keeps the dialog open with everything typed and the reason shown in
  it, ready to retry, and a double-click is one save. Remove writes when it is confirmed. Saving a
  row closes only its dialog, so Settings stays open for the next one; the Save at the foot of
  Project Settings now finishes the session - it is available whenever no save is running and
  closes Settings. No backend or database change. See
  [ProjectSettingsPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectSettingsPanel.js).

- **Payroll: leavers, removed rows, mid-cycle raises and late approvals.** Four gaps on HRM → Payroll →
  Main Page, closed together:
  - **A leaver gets their last salary.** Somebody relieved on or after a pay cycle's first day gets that
    month's row (they used to drop off the roster before it was made); **After Relieving** counts the
    cycle's days after their relieving date like Before Joining, Total Leaves adds them, and attendance
    stops counting at that date - so they are paid up to their last day.
  - **A removed row stays removed.** Remove asks for a reason and marks the row rather than deleting it,
    so the month's update no longer adds the employee back; **Removed rows (n)** lists them, with who
    removed them and why, and **Restore**.
  - **A raise counts from its date.** Base Salary is each salary for its share of the cycle, from the
    joining salary and each review's increment by review date - 30,000 for 13 working days and 35,000
    for 12 of 25 is 32,400 - the split shown in the row's edit form. Where the reviews do not add up to
    the salary on record, the record's salary covers the cycle as before.
  - **Late approvals are paid.** A change to one of the last three closed months - a leave, correction or
    comp-off decided, a review or relieving date saved, Attendance Rules or holidays changed - is worked
    out again against what the month paid. The difference waits under **Adjustments (n)** until an
    administrator approves it - it then lands in the next open month (or the first after it whose row is
    not already paid or frozen) as **Prior Month Adjustment**, added to Net Salary - or rejects it with a
    reason. The paid month is never edited, and a difference approved or rejected never comes back: the
    employee row is locked while one is settled or decided, so a recheck and an approval a moment apart
    never both count it. Only rows made from this change on are tracked (`late_changes_tracked`) - rows
    made before were worked out without leavers, joiners' days or salary history and would all look
    changed - and Base Salary is compared only where the salary's history is on record, so a salary typed
    straight onto the employee is never back pay. Adjustments are kept with the employee (`Restrict`).
    Removed rows are left out of skips, advance and recovery totals, recovery history and the cycle-day
    check.
  Migration `20261012180000_payroll_lifecycle` (six columns on `payroll_entry`, new `payroll_adjustment`).
  No new permission - approving and restoring are `HRM / Payroll Register` Read / Write. The background
  coalescing ledgers used is now shared (`services/coalesce.js`).

- **A new joiner is paid for the part of the pay cycle they were employed, not the whole month.** The
  Payroll Main Page brought in the full monthly salary for everybody on the roster and counted
  attendance only from the joining date, so the days before it cost nothing: somebody who joined with
  13 of 25 working days gone was paid ₹30,000 rather than ₹14,400. A **Before Joining** column now
  holds the cycle's days before the joining date - working days where a day's pay is over working
  days, calendar days where it is over calendar days or a fixed 30 - and Total Leaves adds them, so the
  LOP deduction takes them off at the day's pay already chosen. And nobody is given a row for a month
  whose pay cycle ended before they joined (a 30 Sep joiner had an October row, for 25 Aug - 24 Sep).
  Under a fixed 30 the days are never more than 30, so a whole cycle before joining costs the month's
  pay and no more. Migration `20261012160000_payroll_entry_days_before_joining`; existing rows take
  their figure the next time their month updates (a row already made for somebody who joined after
  its cycle ended then shows the whole cycle unpaid - remove it on the Main Page), paid and frozen rows
  keep theirs.
  [payroll-register/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/service.js).

- **The client gallery is headed with the client's name, and Deselect All shows only on the
  Selected tab.** A manually named project used to head the gallery "Your gallery" because the
  public gallery read the client only from a linked Sales Manager WhatsApp group; it now falls back
  to the client name typed on the Create New Project form. The heading is the client only (the
  couple on a wedding group), never the project name, and "Your gallery" when no client is known. Deselect All sat in the footer on every tab and could clear picks the client
  could not see; it is now offered on the Selected tab only, and only once a photo is picked for the item in
  view - at zero picks it is hidden rather than greyed out. Review & Submit is unchanged. No
  schema change and no permission change - the public route is token-authenticated as before.
  [clientGalleryHome.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/clientGalleryHome.mjs),
  [FolderCards.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/FolderCards.js),
  [publication/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/publication/service.js).

- **Signed Quotation now follows the services and deliverables on Create Project and Edit Sale
  Details when no quotation is linked.** Project lines store no price, so a project booked without a
  quotation sat at ₹0 however many lines it held, and every Schedule Payment amount with it. The lines
  are now priced at their Settings prices - a service at its one Price, a deliverable at its variant's
  price (a saved line matched by its brand, size, frame and length), else its own pricing, else its
  flat price - and totalled by the Quotation Generator's own `quotationTotals` (quantity and No. of
  Count; no discount; a service's automatic deliverables are charged as their own lines, as on a
  quotation). Where the form opened with no figure, Signed Quotation follows the lines as they
  change and is saved as shown, with a note saying where it came from and how many lines Settings
  prices nothing for (they count ₹0, never an invented figure). Typing a figure stops it following
  and clearing the box hands it back. A figure the form opened with - a saved project's, a lead's, a
  duplicate's, a draft's - is never replaced; the note says what the lines come to instead. A linked
  quotation's amount stays read-only and untouched. Nothing follows while lines or Settings are
  loading or failed to load. Schedule rows remain percentages of it. No backend or database change.
  [projectLinePricing.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/projectLinePricing.mjs),
  [CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js),
  [SchedulePaymentSection.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/SchedulePaymentSection.js).

- **Converting a CRM lead no longer puts the client's budget in Signed Quotation.** With no figure
  applied to the lead by the Quotation Calculator, Create Project filled Signed Quotation - the
  figure every Schedule Payment row is a share of - from the lead's Expected / Preferred Budget,
  which is what the client hoped to spend, not what was quoted or signed. It now opens empty (the
  schedule says its amounts are zero until it is set) and is filled by picking the quotation version
  the client signed, which takes that version's saved amount, or typed. Projects already saved keep
  their figure. [SalesManagerPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/SalesManagerPage.js).

- **"Not priced in Settings" no longer appears on a service Settings does price.** The note read the
  service as it was frozen onto the line when the quotation was saved, so reopening a quotation saved
  before a service had its pricing rows called that service unpriced - "Not priced in Settings for
  Studio / In-House · Full Session" - while Settings → Services priced it; and it ignored the line's
  own price, so the summary could say a line was counted at ₹0 when it was not. It now reads each
  service and deliverable as Settings holds it now, by the line's own id (the line's copy only for one
  gone from the catalogue), and says nothing about a line that carries a price. Prices, totals and
  saved quotations are unchanged. See
  [quotationLinePricing.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/quotationLinePricing.mjs).

- **The project feedback tests follow versioned Feedback IDs.** `test/project-feedback.test.js` still
  matched the old `DBS-FB-00012` form in a task's description (now `DBS-FB-00012-04`), created a
  feedback without its required `feedbackVersion`, gave a project's New Project Feedback before
  checking it was still waiting, and left a second project's shoot feedback behind - so the tests
  after them read rows that were not theirs and failed in CI. Test-only; no behaviour changes.

- **A camera facing you now previews like a mirror.** The attendance selfie and the photo camera in
  Production's steps and Events showed a front camera or a laptop webcam un-mirrored, so moving right
  moved the picture left and centring yourself went the wrong way. The preview is now mirrored
  whenever the camera in use faces the person - asked of the camera itself, since a laptop asked for
  its back camera hands over the webcam - as the phone's own camera, WhatsApp and Meet show it. A
  phone's back camera is not mirrored, and the photo taken is never flipped: it stays the true
  picture, so text in it reads the right way round. [cameraFacing.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/cameraFacing.mjs)
- **The Attendance calculator says what a pay cycle really covers.** Under Start and End (Date) it read
  "This calculates 25th to 25th every month", but the payroll reads the 25th of one month to the 24th
  of the next (25 Sep - 24 Oct for October), so no day is counted in two months. It now says "Each pay
  cycle runs from the 25th of one month to the 24th of the next", and on the 1st "from the 1st to the
  last day of the month". Wording only - nothing is worked out differently.
  [AttendanceCalculatorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/AttendanceCalculatorPanel.js).
- **Payroll rules' menus and confirmations open above Settings.** The ⋮ on an extra column (Rename,
  Archive, Remove) and the rename, remove and "Change the payroll rules?" dialogs opened underneath
  the Settings panel, so pressing them seemed to do nothing. They now open on the layers the other
  settings panels use (`menuOverPanel`, `dialogOverPanel`).
  [PayrollComponentsPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/PayrollComponentsPanel.js),
  [PayrollRulesPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/PayrollRulesPanel.js).

- **Opening many onboarding or interview links in a row no longer ends in "Too many requests".**
  Those public forms counted every request - 60 a quarter-hour per address, and behind nginx the
  address can be the whole studio - so HR opening a day's links one after another was refused by
  about the fifteenth form. They now count only misses - any answer of 400 or above: a link that
  does not exist or has expired, a wrong email or phone at verification, a refused submission. Real
  links open as often as anyone needs; 30 misses in 15 minutes stop an address that is guessing,
  and 600 requests in all still bound a flood. The CRD form and the quotation sheet, which had no
  limit at all, get the same one; the quotation's sheet, PDF and payment details share one budget,
  so guessing cannot move to whichever was limited least, and a refused PDF that redirects back to
  the page still counts. An IPv6 connection is counted by its /64, so it cannot take a fresh budget
  per address. Pages stay public and need no sign-in. **Before deploying, set
  `TRUST_PROXY_HEADER=true` in the backend `.env` on the VPS**: without it every limit counts the
  whole studio and every client as one address, so one guesser would shut the forms for all - the
  server now warns at boot when it is off in production. No database change.
  [rateLimit.js](../backend/src/middleware/rateLimit.js).

- **A Google Sheet row is now refused as a duplicate only when its number is already in the same
  vertical.** The sheet sync matched an arriving number against every lead in the CRM, so a client
  already on Dum Dum whose number came in on a Qua Qua (or Corp) sheet was skipped as "already here"
  - or, on the older refresh path, folded onto the Dum Dum lead. Now the number is matched within the
  row's own vertical, the rule Add Lead already follows: the same number in another vertical comes in
  as its own enquiry, and a deleted lead in one vertical no longer holds back the client's enquiry in
  another. Every sync path is covered: the 2-minute auto-sync, the link sync, the preview and Refresh.
  [googleSheetsService.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/googleSheetsService.js)

- **Photos picked on an iPhone or in Safari now upload sharp and quickly.** Safari cannot encode
  WebP, so asked for it the in-browser compressor got a PNG that ignored the quality setting, missed
  the 150 KB budget at every size and shrank each photo down to as little as 320px after many slow
  encodes. Where the browser cannot encode WebP a photo is now written as JPEG, which Safari encodes
  properly, so a phone photo keeps a usable size (1600px in testing) within budget. A picture with
  transparency, such as a logo, stays PNG there as before, so it never gains a black background.
  This covers every field that compresses in the browser - the onboarding form's profile, Aadhaar
  and PAN photos, profile photo, attendance selfie, asset inspection, CRD form images, and the
  shared image, multi-image, file and camera fields. Chrome, Edge and Firefox still send WebP. The
  server already accepted JPEG; no backend or database change.
  [imageCompression.js](../frontend/src/lib/imageCompression.js).

- **Restoring a project through Pre Production → Import no longer brings back shoots the file does
  not list.** Deleting a project hid its shoots without marking them, so "Restore deleted projects
  and shoots" brought every one of them back with the project - shoots from an older sheet
  included. A restored project's shoots are now marked deleted as it comes back, and each row of
  the file restores its own; a shoot the file leaves out stays deleted. Deleted projects the file
  does not name are untouched, as before.
  [import.service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/import.service.js).

- **A sheet lead meant for someone on leave now goes to their alternative from the first day of the
  leave.** The leave check compared the leave dates with the server's local midnight, which on a
  server set to India time is 18:30 UTC the day before - so the first day of every approved leave
  (and the whole of a one-day leave) was missed, and the absent person kept receiving the Google
  Sheet's rule-assigned leads. It now uses the studio's calendar day, right whatever zone the server
  runs in. Interview candidates assigned by sheet rules are covered the same way.
  [leadCover.js](../backend/src/services/leadCover.js)

- **A WhatsApp session WhatsApp refuses with 403 now gets a fresh QR on the next Connect.** A 403
  ("Connection Failure") — WhatsApp no longer accepting the saved login, or the number being
  restricted — was retried six times like a dropped connection, and the saved credentials were
  kept, so pressing Connect again resumed the same dead login and was refused again: no QR ever
  came, and the person stayed stuck behind the link gate. It now stops at once, deletes the saved
  credentials (as a 401 logout does) and says so; the next Connect pairs from scratch. Fewer
  refused reconnects also means less of the behaviour that gets a number flagged.
  [sessionLifecycle.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/whatsapp-chat/sessionLifecycle.js)

- **On the leads board, the tab counts now follow the vertical.** Switching Dum Dum / Qua Qua / Corp
  in board view re-read every column but left the tab labels (All, Yet to connect, the pending tabs
  and the rest) showing the vertical before, because only the table's own page read set them and
  that read is off on the board. The board now reads the counts itself whenever the vertical, tab,
  filters, date range or My Leads change, or a lead is saved.
  [CRMPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CRMPage.js)

- **Attendance → Requests: "Waiting for me" now lists only what still needs your answer**, matching
  its count. It used to also list requests you had already approved or rejected while they were
  still open, so the tab could read "Waiting for me (2)" over eight rows. An answered request is
  still in All and in its status tab — Pending while other approvers have yet to answer, then
  Approved or Rejected. [AttendanceRequestsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestsPage.js)

- **A leaver's direct reports no longer end up reporting to somebody who has left.** Offboarding
  moved them to the leaver's own manager without checking that manager still worked here, so they
  could be pointed at an archived or Left employee. They now go to the nearest manager up the chain
  who is still working, and the change is refused if there is none. The hand-over pop-up's
  suggested person is worked out the same way, so the two agree.
  [reportingLine.js](../backend/src/services/reportingLine.js),
  [separations/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/separations/controller.js)

- **Reassign pending work now opens in front of the offboarding form, not behind it.** The dialog
  sat on the ordinary dialog layer, under the full-screen form it is opened from, so it could not
  be seen or used; it now takes the layer every dialog opened from a form panel uses.
  [HandOverDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/HandOverDialog.js)

- **Sorting the CRM leads board by Status or a date no longer shows some leads twice and hides
  others.** The board loads leads a page at a time; sorted by a column many leads share, the
  database could order those leads differently on each page, so page 2 repeated leads from page 1
  and skipped others - 32 of 224 on the Status sort - and the browser warned "two children with the
  same key". Every sort now ends on the enquiry id, so each lead sits on exactly one page, and a page
  scrolled in never adds a lead already on screen (one edited mid-scroll can move between pages).
  [leadQueryService.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/leadQueryService.js),
  [CRMPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CRMPage.js).

- **A Pre Production import keeps the sheet's Event ID and Shoot ID.** Importing the old booking
  sheet created each project and shoot under a new number from the app's counter
  (`DBS-BK-DD-ERD-000062`, `DBS-SID-DD-ERD-000251`), so a booking no longer read as the number the
  studio knows it by. The sheet's own IDs (`DBS-EVT-05552`, `DBS-SID-5810`) are now the project's
  and the shoot's IDs. Bookings imported before this move onto the sheet's IDs the next time the same
  file is uploaded - nothing else stores these IDs as text, so only the one column changes - and an
  ID already held by another project or shoot is refused by name. The two shapes cannot collide with
  what the app numbers itself, and `scripts/renumberIdentifiers.js` now leaves imported rows alone.
  [import.service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/import.service.js),
  `test/pre-production-import.test.js`.

- **A WhatsApp session WhatsApp refuses with 403 now gets a fresh QR on the next Connect.** A 403
  ("Connection Failure") — WhatsApp no longer accepting the saved login, or the number being
  restricted — was retried six times like a dropped connection, and the saved credentials were
  kept, so pressing Connect again resumed the same dead login and was refused again: no QR ever
  came, and the person stayed stuck behind the link gate. It now stops at once, deletes the saved
  credentials (as a 401 logout does) and says so; the next Connect pairs from scratch. Fewer
  refused reconnects also means less of the behaviour that gets a number flagged.
  [sessionLifecycle.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/whatsapp-chat/sessionLifecycle.js)

  in board view re-read every column but left the tab labels (All, Yet to connect, the pending tabs

  that read is off on the board. The board now reads the counts itself whenever the vertical, tab,
  filters, date range or My Leads change, or a lead is saved.
  [CRMPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CRMPage.js)

  Approved or Rejected. [AttendanceRequestsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestsPage.js)

  moved them to the leaver's own manager without checking that manager still worked here, so they

  who is still working, and the change is refused if there is none. The hand-over pop-up's

  [reportingLine.js](../backend/src/services/reportingLine.js),
  [separations/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/separations/controller.js)

  sat on the ordinary dialog layer, under the full-screen form it is opened from, so it could not
  be seen or used; it now takes the layer every dialog opened from a form panel uses.
  [HandOverDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/HandOverDialog.js)

  others.** The board loads leads a page at a time; sorted by a column many leads share, the
  database could order those leads differently on each page, so page 2 repeated leads from page 1
  and skipped others - 32 of 224 on the Status sort - and the browser warned "two children with the
