- **A Pre Production import keeps the sheet's Event ID and Shoot ID.** Importing the old booking
  sheet created each project and shoot under a new number from the app's counter
  (`DBS-BK-DD-ERD-000062`, `DBS-SID-DD-ERD-000251`), so a booking no longer read as the number the
  studio knows it by. The sheet's own IDs (`DBS-EVT-05552`, `DBS-SID-5810`) are now the project's
  and the shoot's IDs. Bookings imported before this move onto the sheet's IDs the next time the same
  file is uploaded - nothing else stores these IDs as text, so only the one column changes - and an
  ID already held by another project or shoot is refused by name. The two shapes cannot collide with
  what the app numbers itself, and `scripts/renumberIdentifiers.js` now leaves imported rows alone.
  [import.service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/import.service.js),
  `test/pre-production-import.test.js`.

- **`calendar-my-attendance.test.js` no longer fails CI between midnight and 05:30 in India.** It
  worked out "today" in the server's own zone - UTC on CI - while the calendar's attendance window
  rightly stops at the studio's today, so for those five and a half hours the two were a day apart.
  It now asks for the studio's day (`studioCalendarDay`), as the code does. The whole backend suite
  was then run in UTC at 01:26 and 04:26 India time and passes, so no other test depends on the hour
  that way. Tests only - no application code changed.

- **The backend tests no longer fail CI depending on the hour or on which files run together.**
  `attendance-register-cards.test.js` built its sessions off the real clock, so a run soon after
  midnight in India opened them the evening before and its 17:00 check found them past the 18-hour
  limit - it failed at night and passed by day; it now pins the clock to 11:50 on the studio's day
  for every case and passes at any hour. `data-scope-lead-children.test.js` lost its setup when
  MySQL chose one of its inserts as a deadlock victim against another test file writing the same
  tables; each of its writes is now retried on that error (P2034), as the app's own colliding
  writes are. Tests only - no application code changed.

- **Allow WhatsApp on its own now lets somebody link their WhatsApp.** The tick puts the "Link your
  WhatsApp to continue" gate in front of a person, but `POST /api/sales/whatsapp-chat/session/connect`
  only let them pair if a role held Read on CRM Leads, Interview or Employee Management — so somebody
  ticked who held none of those was stuck behind the gate on a 403 ("You don't have required
  permissions"). A ticked account now passes the pairing guard whatever its roles; everybody else is
  checked against the three features as before. The studio and per-user WhatsApp switches still
  refuse in the handler. [routes.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/whatsapp-chat/routes.js)

- **Yet to Download follows what was actually downloaded.** A project is on Yet to Download while
  the client has a submitted selection newer than the last complete download, and the stamp that
  says so (`selectedDownloadedAt`) is now written by the selection state a download saved, not by
  the moment it finished: Download Selected and the server's copy-out each read the time before
  the selections are read, so a client submission arriving while the photos are being saved keeps
  the project listed. The server copy-out no longer marks a project downloaded when some originals
  could not be copied - as the browser's Download Selected already did, only a complete run counts -
  and a stamp never moves backwards, so downloading the same selection twice cannot put a project
  back on the list. Where the download cannot be recorded (a role that may download but not change
  the project), Download Selected now says so instead of failing quietly. The card and the filtered
  table read the same stored flag, so both hold across a refresh. No migration, no permission
  change. See [DownloadSelectedButton.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/DownloadSelectedButton.js)
  and [gallery/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/gallery/service.js).

- **A quotation with several shoots no longer looks as if only the first was calculated.** Every
  shoot's lines were always in the total, each priced by its own Shoot Type and Session Timing,
  but a service Settings prices only for Studio - 360 PhotoBooth, 789 booth - added to an Outdoor
  shoot has no price there and counted ₹0 with nothing to say so, so the Outdoor shoot read as left
  out. Such a line now says "Not priced in Settings for Outdoor / On-Location · Half Session" under
  its name, and the Quotation Summary says how many lines are counted at ₹0; price them for that
  shoot type in Settings → Project → Services to charge them. Editing a shoot's Shoot Type, Session
  Timing or length now reprices that shoot's own lines for it (a line's Session Timing follows the
  shoot unless it was changed by hand; package prices and variants stay), and nothing on the other
  shoots moves; correcting a shoot's place or date reprices nothing. The CRM Quotation Calculator
  now hands over one shoot per Shoot Type and Session Timing its lines were quoted under - Studio
  Full and Outdoor Half are two shoots, each priced by its own - instead of folding them into one;
  lines quoted under one type and session still arrive as one shoot. See
  [QuotationGeneratorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationGeneratorPanel.js),
  [quotationLinePricing.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/quotationLinePricing.mjs) and
  [quotationCalculatorHandoff.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/quotationCalculatorHandoff.mjs).

- **The Quotation Generator prices a service by the session it is booked for, and by its own flat
  price.** Changing a service line's Session Timing - Half Session to Full Session - left it at the
  price it was added at, so a Full Session line could be quoted at the Half Session figure while
  bringing the Full Session deliverables. The line is now repriced from its own Session Timing, by
  the same reading that decides those deliverables. A service priced in Settings only by its flat
  price was quoted at the studio's ₹2,000 service rate instead; it now takes its own price first.
  A brand's GST is no longer overwritten by the studio's when the studio settings happen to load
  after the brand's, and a quotation reopened for editing keeps its exact percentage discount
  rather than the two-place figure, so its total no longer shifts by a few rupees. Quotations
  already saved keep the prices they were saved with until a line is changed. New quotations still
  open at no discount. See
  [QuotationGeneratorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationGeneratorPanel.js).

- **Attendance reads India time on any server.** Production runs the API on UTC, and attendance
  read every time with the server's own clock (`getHours()`), so on production a 9:38 am login
  showed as 4:08 on the admin Attendance Dashboard, nobody was judged Late (a 9:38 login read as
  4:08), a 6 pm logout read as 12:30 pm and was flagged Early Exit, "today" turned over at 5:30 am
  IST, and a time HR typed ("18:00") was saved as 18:00 UTC - 11:30 pm in the studio. Locally it was
  right only because the laptop is set to India. `minutesOfDay`, `calendarDay`, `wallClockInstant`
  (`attendanceRules.js`), the register's "inside a permission now" check and the default month
  range now read the studio's clock through `services/studioTime.js` (new `studioParts`,
  `studioMinutesOfDay`, `studioCalendarDay`, `studioInstant`; the WhatsApp report's clock uses the
  same), so the server's zone no longer matters - no `TZ` setting needed. **Stored times are
  untouched**: logins are instants and were always right, so every past day reads correctly the
  moment this deploys - Check In / Check Out, Late, Early Exit and worked hours alike. Guarded by
  `attendance-any-server-zone.test.js` (the helpers run under UTC, India, New York and UTC+14), and
  the attendance tests now write their example times as India time, so the suite passes whatever
  zone it runs in (it is UTC on CI).
  **After deploying, on production - times HR typed while the server was on UTC:**
  `node scripts/one-off/repairAttendanceTypedTimes.js` lists them (HR edits of a check-in or
  check-out, and approved checkout Corrections) without changing anything; check the list, then run
  it again with `--apply`. It touches only a time that is exactly the typed time read as UTC - the
  bug's fingerprint - moves it to that time in India, closes a break the bad checkout closed at the
  repaired one, and adds an `ADMIN_EDIT` note to the day; rows saved right or changed since are left
  alone, and a second run finds nothing. A day's check-in is repaired before its check-out, a
  checkout that would not end up after its login is listed "look at by hand" and left, one row that
  cannot be repaired does not stop the rest, and only the note's changes are read - never its
  free-text reason. A login captured between midnight and 5:30 am IST was
  filed under the previous day by the UTC server and is not moved - nothing proves what was meant -
  so look at those by hand. Other modules still read the server's clock (cash receipt date, asset
  inspection "today", album-proof expiry, lead cover, AI events) and are not part of this fix
  ([attendanceRules.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/attendanceRules.js),
  [studioTime.js](../backend/src/services/studioTime.js),
  [repairAttendanceTypedTimes.js](../backend/scripts/one-off/repairAttendanceTypedTimes.js)).

- **Editing a deliverable no longer breaks the services that bring it.** Any save of a deliverable in
  Settings → Project - a new name, brand, size, frame or price - replaced all of its brands and
  variants with new ones, so every service whose pricing lines bring that deliverable read "This
  deliverable is no longer offered" and had to have it picked again. The save now keeps every brand
  and variant the form kept, updating it in place under the same id, and removes only what was
  actually removed - so a renamed deliverable shows under its new name in every service mapped to
  it, and the message appears only for a variant that was really deleted. See
  `saveDeliverableBrands` in
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js) and `brandFormRows` in
  [deliverableBrands.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/deliverableBrands.mjs). A duplicated deliverable still
  gets brands and variants of its own. **A service already showing the message keeps showing it**:
  the variant it named was replaced by an earlier save and cannot be told apart from its
  deliverable's other variants, so pick it once more in the service's pricing line. No migration,
  no permission change.

- **`npm test` no longer deletes local rows whose ID merely starts with `TEST`.** Its start-of-run
  sweep of leftover test fixtures matched the reserved prefix `TEST_` as a `LIKE` pattern, where
  `_` is any one character, so a hand-made `TEST-EV-001` project - with its shoots, production
  rows and lead - was deleted on the next run. The sweep now escapes `_` and `%` in every prefix.
  Development and CI only; production never runs it.
  [clear-test-fixtures.js](../backend/scripts/clear-test-fixtures.js).
- **An employee's own attendance page counts from the day they joined.** Days before joining were
  listed and counted as absences - Mukesh K, who joined on 23 Sep, showed 27 absences for September
  on his own page against the Dashboard's 8. The day list now starts at the joining date (a day
  something was recorded on before it still shows, as on the register), and the working days, the
  target hours and the absences are owed from it, in both the day-by-day summary and the
  figures-only totals for long ranges - the same start the register, the Dashboard and the salary
  calculator already used. A range wholly before joining owes nothing; with no joining date on
  record, the whole range is owed as before.
  [attendance/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js).
- **The Attendance Dashboard now counts an Incorrect login on a working day as an absence, as the
  employee's own attendance page always has.** An Incorrect login - a login nobody logged out of
  within 24 hours - was counted on the Dashboard only if its status read "Absent", so it fell out of
  every column: Mukesh K's week of 28 Sep - 2 Oct showed 4 absences on the Dashboard against 5 on his
  own page. One rule now holds on every screen (`tallyRange`, beside `attendanceSummary` and
  `attendanceTotals`), and Nebula, which reads the Dashboard's figures, follows it.
  [attendance/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js).

- **The Shoot Board no longer crashes when the range is narrowed to days with no shoots in them.**
  Picking **This week** - or any preset or custom range with nothing in it - took the whole page down
  with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getDate')". The rows are built from a legend of
  every project in the shoots loaded, and each project is only then narrowed to the days on screen,
  so a project whose shoots all fall outside the window became a row with **no bars**. The empty
  state reads a row as "there is a shoot somewhere either side of these days" and works the nearest
  one out from the rows' own bars - of which such a row has none - so it asked for the name of a day
  that was not there. A project with nothing inside the days is not a row at all now, which is what
  makes the row count mean what the empty state takes it to mean; the board says "No shoots in this
  range" and offers a wider one, as it does for any empty range.
  The trigger was the gap between the two: choosing a preset sets the days immediately, while the
  shoots for them are still being fetched, so for one render the new days were held against the old
  range's shoots. The project **filter** still lists every project loaded, as before - it reads its
  own legend, not the timeline's rows.
  [shootBoard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/shootBoard.mjs). No migration.

- **Updating "Project started" from the Status tab goes back to Status instead of closing the
  project.** The editor is a form panel stacked on the project's own, and its submit also reached
  the panel underneath, which saved the project and closed everything. A form panel's submit now
  stops at its own form, so any panel opened over another is fixed the same way.
  [SchemaFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/schema-form/SchemaFormPanel.js).
- **Close and Back work again in Pre Production and Production opened from a project's Status tab,
  after something was saved.** Leaving asked for the status-history remark, and that dialog was drawn
  inside the project's panel - underneath the editor stacked on top of it - so it opened out of sight
  and the buttons looked dead. It is now drawn above every panel, and **Pre Production and
  Production no longer ask for a remark at all**: they close back to Status as on their own pages,
  and Production's **Save changes** / **Submit plan** now saves and goes back to Status instead of
  staying open on "Plan saved". Only Project started still asks for its remark.
  [ProjectStageView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectStageView.js),
  [StageUpdateRemarkDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/StageUpdateRemarkDialog.js).

- **A downloaded Signature Album PDF no longer cuts photos across pages or loses its ending.** The
  app-wide `overflow-x: hidden` on `html, body` made the page a scroll container, so the PDF was
  given only as many pages as the album's unbroken height filled. Every row a page break pushed
  down then ran off the last page: the album stopped mid-row, without its "Thank you" ending. The
  print view alone now prints as a plain block. Rows stay whole, the ending is kept on one page,
  and the space below it takes the album's own background. A 54-photo album went from 17 pages with
  a cut-off row to 24 whole pages. The client page, the studio's live preview, the API and the
  schema are unchanged.
  [AlbumFrame.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/client/AlbumFrame.js),
  [SignatureAlbumPrint.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/client/SignatureAlbumPrint.js).
- **Signature Album and the client quotation: phone layout, upload, settings and client-page fixes.**
  On a phone the album's rail (Publish, Client Access, Permissions) comes before the Gallery
  instead of after a list that loads without end. Photos landing during an upload are laid in at the
  top of the Gallery rather than sending a studio scrolled deep into it back to the first page every
  second and a half; a delete still starts again from the first page. Leaving the album mid-upload
  now does stop what has not been sent, as its prompt says. Settings → Signature Album defaults: a
  batch size outside 10-120 (or cleared) is told under its field and keeps Save shut, text fields
  stop at the server's lengths, Enter no longer submits the whole Settings form, and closing the
  panel - X, Cancel, Escape, or after Save Settings - asks first while defaults are unsaved. On the
  client's pages: a refused album or quotation download sends the browser back to the page with a
  message (`?download=failed`, from [downloadNavigation.js](../backend/src/services/downloadNavigation.js))
  instead of replacing it with JSON - a download stopped by the rate limit itself still answers
  JSON; a chapter whose next batch failed can be asked for again by its "N more"; an album without
  a PIN never shows PIN boxes, its lapsed session is reopened instead; the album PDF waits for the
  design's font sheet before printing; and the quotation's error screens are laid out for the phone
  ([DeviceViewport.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/DeviceViewport.js), the expired card's
  viewport switch, now shared) - its loading line is deliberately left in the sheet's viewport,
  since switching back to the sheet could leave a phone zoomed in.
  [AlbumGallery.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/AlbumGallery.js),
  [ImageSelectionSettingsForm.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/ImageSelectionSettingsForm.js),
  [ClientSignatureAlbum.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/client/ClientSignatureAlbum.js),
  [PublicQuotationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/PublicQuotationPage.js).

- **Signature Album: a stranger can no longer lock every client out of their PIN, and the studio
  side recovers from failures it used to get stuck on.** Wrong PIN guesses are counted per caller
  (`clientIp`) instead of per proxy - behind nginx `req.ip` is the same for everyone, so about 30
  wrong guesses from anyone locked every PIN album for every client for 15 minutes. **Deploy:** the
  per-caller count needs `TRUST_PROXY_HEADER=true` on the production server; without it every
  caller still reads as the proxy. The public quotation PDF is rate limited (20 a quarter-hour per
  address and quotation), since each fetch is a print by the headless browser Download Album also
  uses. In the studio: an album whose first load fails shows the error with **Retry** instead of a
  loader that never ends; an album upload that finishes with failures keeps **Retry N failed**
  (Photo Selection's upload card is unchanged); a Design change made just before leaving the tab is
  sent rather than dropped, and a failed design save is kept and sent with the next change;
  Read-only users can copy the Client URL and PIN again; Unpublish asks first, from the rail switch
  and from Review & Share; Allow Download and Allow Social Share wait for a save in flight like
  Require PIN; on a phone the album header shows only its status chip, so the pane no longer
  scrolls sideways; the empty album no longer promises chapters and highlights. On the client's
  page, a session that lapses during Download Album no longer leaves the button stuck on
  "preparing" once the PIN is entered again.
  [signatureAlbum.public.controller.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/signature-album/signatureAlbum.public.controller.js),
  [quotations-public/routes.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/quotations-public/routes.js),
  [SignatureAlbumWorkspace.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/SignatureAlbumWorkspace.js),
  [UploadBatchProgress.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/UploadBatchProgress.js),
  [DesignPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/DesignPanel.js),
  [SignatureAlbumRightPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/SignatureAlbumRightPanel.js),
  [ClientSignatureAlbum.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/client/ClientSignatureAlbum.js).

- **Deleting photos from a Signature Album's Gallery now confirms it, keeps keyboard focus and
  recovers from a photo already deleted elsewhere.** A delete ends in "N photos deleted." A
  keyboard user is left on the Gallery heading instead of the top of the page, since the Delete
  button goes with the selection. A selected photo that another tab or person deleted first used
  to fail every later Delete until the whole pick was cleared; it is now found and unselected,
  and Delete works again for the rest - and a pick that turns out to be gone entirely is reported
  as done, not as an error. Select All, Clear and Delete are full 40px touch targets, "Scroll for
  more" is readable (slate-500), and shift-click range selection no longer highlights the page's
  text.
  [AlbumGallery.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/AlbumGallery.js),
  [SignatureAlbumWorkspace.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/SignatureAlbumWorkspace.js),
  [GalleryGrid.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/GalleryGrid.js).

- **On a phone, the quotation link's Download button and expiry countdown are compact.** The
  client's copy is shrunk to about a third on a phone, and the two floating controls - drawn at full
  size against it - dominated the sheet. On a screen under 640px wide, Download is now a 42px disc
  with an 18px arrow, and the countdown is one slim line ("Expires in 3d 5h 54m") instead of a
  two-line chip, both 10px from the corner. Tablets and laptops are unchanged, and so are the
  countdown, the download rule and the expired page. The phone is told by the screen's own width
  (`visualViewport.width × scale`), because the route's 1112px viewport means a media query never
  fires there. [PublicQuotationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/PublicQuotationPage.js).

- **Create Project and Edit Sale Details offer the same services as the Quotation Generator.**
  All three read the one service catalogue (`GET /api/sales/service-definitions`), but the shared
  Service Creation section still narrowed Choose Services to the shoot's type on the project
  screens - only the Quotation Generator had it switched off - so a studio-only service such as 360
  PhotoBooth vanished from an outdoor shoot on a project while the quotation offered it. The switch
  is gone: Choose Services lists every active service on every shoot, on all three screens, from
  the one rule in [ProjectServiceCreationSection.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectServiceCreationSection.js);
  a service's Shoot Type stays for pricing, and Choose Deliverables keeps narrowing to the type as
  it did. A service added on a project now also starts its Session Timing the way the quotation's
  does (`defaultSessionOptionId` - the shoot's own Half or Full Session where the service offers it,
  blank otherwise, changeable after), in [CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js)
  and [useProjectPlan.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/useProjectPlan.js). No
  backend, schema, API or data change: the server never narrowed by shoot type and already
  validates the Session Timing it is sent; saved services, quotation carry-over and each shoot's
  own rows are untouched.

- **An interview candidate in Follow Up cannot be saved without a next follow-up date.** The popup
  marked Next Follow-up as required but Update and Close saved without it. The save now refuses
  first, with "Next follow-up date is required for Follow Up stage." under the field (brought into
  view), alongside the existing remark check, and the server refuses the same - and a date that is
  not a real day - with a 400. The screening-form and scheduling actions save the candidate first,
  so on a Follow Up candidate with no date they ask for it too. Other stages, and candidates already
  in the register - which still open with an empty date - are unchanged; nothing is rewritten
  ([candidateRecordForm.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/candidateRecordForm.js),
  [InterviewCandidatePopup.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewCandidatePopup.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/interview/controller.js)).

- **A deliverable or service with a long name can be added.** Settings → Project → Deliverables
  answered "Unable to add deliverable." for some names and not others: the code stored beside each
  deliverable, service and option is built from its name into a 100-character column, and a name
  long enough to make a longer code was refused by the database (P2000). A code that fits is built
  exactly as before; a longer one is cut to fit and ends in a short fingerprint of the full name, so
  the same name always finds the same row and a duplicate is still reported as one. Existing rows are
  untouched ([controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js)).

- **The Sales → Quotation register loads again in production.** It showed "Unable to load
  quotations." with every tab at 0: the list asked MySQL to sort every quotation row, each carrying
  its whole JSON payload, and once the register outgrew MySQL's sort buffer the query failed ("Out of
  sort memory", MySQL 1038). The rows are now read unsorted and put in the same order in the code -
  chain ascending, newest version first - so nothing on the screen changes. No data was affected
  ([controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js)).

- **A shared quotation link now previews as the studio, not BeamCraft.** The quotation, payment and
  terms pages titled themselves "Quotation | BeamCraft" and gave WhatsApp a BeamCraft card; they now
  take the name and logo from Settings → Branding, on the server so the preview has them in the
  first response - "Quotation | <studio name>", the studio's logo as the picture, and no name or
  picture at all rather than a borrowed one where none is set
  ([shareMetadata.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/shareMetadata.mjs)). The studio's own Download PDF no
  longer releases the file in the same moment it starts saving it, which could leave the download
  stuck or empty in some browsers, and a response that is not a PDF is refused instead of saved
  ([projects.service.js](../frontend/src/services/sales/projects.service.js)). The PDF itself, its
  content and who may download it are unchanged.

- **Employee Attendance shows only Login before the day is logged in.** The header used to show a
  greyed-out Break In beside Login before the login; it now shows Login alone, then Break In +
  Logout once logged in, Break Off + Logout during a break, and Login again after a logout (a day may
  still be logged in more than once). The buttons still follow the server's answer for today, so a
  refresh lands on the same state ([EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js)).

- **The enquiry-picker test no longer fails on a database where a lead has been booked.** Its
  "every live lead is offered" check counted leads already turned into a live project, which Create
  Project rightly leaves out (one project per enquiry), so it passed only while nothing had been
  booked. The count now applies the same rule; the picker itself is unchanged
  ([enquiry-picker.test.js](../backend/test/enquiry-picker.test.js)).

- **The Speak-up tests now pass in CI.** They borrowed whichever employees the database already
  held, and CI's database - built from the migrations and the seed - has none, so ten of them failed
  there while passing on a developer's copy. They now create two archived employees of their own
  under the `TSU-` fixture prefix and remove them when the file finishes.
  [speak-up.test.js](../backend/test/speak-up.test.js)

- **Every `/api/sales/...` router now answers for its own permission, not `SALES / CRM Leads`.**
  `salesProjectRoutes` and `salesProjectAttachmentRoutes`, mounted on the bare `/api/sales` prefix,
  each guard *everything* that reaches them - as router-level middleware, before route matching -
  not only the paths they actually serve; Express tries mounted routers in registration order, so
  any other `/api/sales/...` router mounted after these two had its requests intercepted and
  wrongly refused by whichever of the two ran first, whatever permission its own routes actually
  needed. Fifteen routers had drifted onto the wrong side of this over time - most visibly
  `/api/sales/whatsapp-chat/my-session`, deliberately built to answer for anybody signed in rather
  than only a CRM Leads holder, which silently 403'd for everyone else instead: **Require WhatsApp**
  in Login Credentials looked like it was doing nothing, because the dialog that reads this
  endpoint never got a real answer back. Every one of the fifteen is now mounted ahead of the two
  bare routers, matching the fix Callyzer's webhook already needed once for the same reason - itself
  found to have drifted back onto the wrong side without anyone noticing, which is why this is now
  pinned by a test rather than left to a comment.
  [server.js](../backend/src/server.js),
  [sales-route-mount-order.test.js](../backend/test/sales-route-mount-order.test.js). No migration.

### Added

- **AI Editing downloads the photos you actually edited, edits only the ticked photos, and loses
  its expand icon.** In the bay's bulk bar, **Download selected edited** asks the server which ticked
  photos have a saved edit - rendered at the recipe last saved, with the output still in storage -
  and downloads only those: one photo as its full-resolution JPEG master named `<name> (edited).jpg`,
  several as one ZIP. A photo marked Not edited, still rendering, failed, or changed since its last
  Apply is never included, and how many are left out and why is said before the download; an
  original or a preview never stands in. The editor has **Download edited** for the open photo,
  held while it renders or has changes not yet applied or saved. Two steps on the server
  ([download.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-editing/download.js)): `POST
  …/ai-editing/downloads/plan` (`IMAGE_SELECTION / AI Editing` READ - a viewer of the bay may
  download its edits; rate limited per person) answers what is included, what is excluded by
  reason, and a ten-minute ticket signed with a key of its own; `POST …/ai-editing/downloads/archive`
  takes only that ticket (a download cannot carry the session header), re-checks every photo's edit
  version, and streams the masters from R2 one at a time into the ZIP - never the batch in memory;
  a photo re-edited since is left out and named in `NOT-INCLUDED.txt`. The web posts the ticket into
  a hidden frame so the browser saves the file itself; the desktop app picks a folder and a new Rust
  command (`edits_download`) streams the file there. **Edit selected** opens the editor on the
  ticked photos only, walked by id with the arrows ("2 of 4"), photos on other pages fetched by id,
  a banner saying so and **Exit selected editing** back to the bay with the ticks kept; each photo
  keeps its own edit, and Apply to selected / Apply to all are unchanged. Anyone who can see the bay
  can now tick photos (to edit or download them); the album send keeps its own permission. The
  header's expand / full-width icon is gone on both apps (the editor still takes the full width
  while a photo is open). On the desktop, Add photos sits on the header's line and opens an
  "Add photos to AI Editing" panel around the existing upload zone - same pipeline, a heading,
  where the photos go, and Close; tile status chips sit on a solid base so "Not edited" reads over
  any photo. No schema, permission or migration changes.

- **The AI Editing editor walks the whole bay from the keyboard, on the web and in the desktop
  app.** With a photo open, Left / Right move to the previous / next photo and Home / End to the
  bay's first / last, in the bay's own order and across its pages (a page turns at its edge); the
  header says where the photo sits - "3 of 20" - beside Previous / Next buttons for the same moves,
  and the two rest at the bay's ends (nothing wraps, as in the culling review). The editor stays
  open throughout: every move loads that photo's own preview, recipe, render and saved / not-edited
  state, a screen reader hears "Photo 4 of 20, <file>", and Escape returns to the bay (through the
  app's one Escape stack, so a dialog or menu over the editor takes the key first). A key typed
  into a slider, a field, a menu or a dialog stays that control's, and so do the arrows on the
  compare tabs. Leaving a photo saves a change still waiting for its save - or one whose save
  failed - and writes it back into the bay, so moving away and back shows what was saved; if even
  that save fails the sliders are kept and the notice offers "Open photo", which reopens the photo
  on them with Retry; a render in flight carries on and the bay's polling picks it up.
  [AiEditingWorkspace.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/editing/AiEditingWorkspace.js),
  [EditingPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/editing/EditingPanel.js),
  [imageSelectionEditing.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/imageSelectionEditing.mjs),
  [AiEditingWorkspace.jsx](../../Image-Selection_Desktop---BCT/src/modules/image-selection/editing/AiEditingWorkspace.jsx),
  [EditingPanel.jsx](../../Image-Selection_Desktop---BCT/src/modules/image-selection/editing/EditingPanel.jsx).

- **AI Culling now begins with the import on the desktop app: drop a folder once, choose the
  culling mode once, and the run creates itself, analyzes each photo as its preview lands and
  opens for review when the last one has - no second Start, no waiting for the whole upload.**
  One panel replaces the separate upload and analysis cards: discovered, compressed, uploaded,
  analyzed, faces found, culling-ready, processing now and remaining, an overall progress of
  settled units, a time left only once a rate is known, Pause / Resume for uploads and analysis
  together, Cancel import (what landed and every result stays), Retry failed, Change mode, Let
  the server finish now and Cancel run. Balanced is the default for a project nobody has chosen
  for; the choice is remembered per project. A Target count is checked against the import and
  again against the photos that actually landed, with both numbers. The mandatory preview and
  thumbnail still go up for every photo and the originals stay on the studio's disk or NAS. The
  web shows the same import state read-only. Manual runs are unchanged.
  [CullingWorkspace.jsx](../../Image-Selection_Desktop---BCT/src/modules/image-selection/culling/CullingWorkspace.jsx),
  [ai-culling/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/service.js),

  [imageSelectionCulling.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/imageSelectionCulling.mjs).

- **AI Editing gains a Retouching section: ten regions - Facial Skin, Body Skin, Eyebrows, Eye
  Sclera, Iris and Pupil, Lips, Teeth, Hair, Facial Hair and Clothes - each a switch with one
  intensity, retouched by the same engine inside the region it finds and nowhere else.** Natural
  by default: specks and uneven tone on the skin with the pores kept, brows defined, the whites of
  the eyes cleared of redness, the iris given depth without a colour change, dry lines on the lips
  smoothed, visible teeth whitened once (Skin Retouch's own teeth slider and this one never
  stack), flyaways at the edge of the hair tamed, a beard cleaned of noise, lint on plain clothing
  removed - never a pattern, a colour or a shape. The eye, brow, lip and teeth regions need the
  face landmark model and say so when it is missing; hair, facial hair and clothes come from
  outlines the panel marks as approximate, where a face-parsing model would make them exact. A
  region the engine cannot find is left as shot and said under the preview. Old recipes are
  untouched: a region is on only when its switch is, and every tool at intensity 0 renders byte
  for byte what it did before. Contract and engine 2.1.0, mirrored on the web and the desktop.
  [recipe.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-editing/recipe.js),
  [edit_engine.py](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-editing/edit_engine.py),

- **The client gallery's People tab now has a Scene filter: one "All scenes" switch that opens to

  [scene/backfill.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/scene/backfill.js),

- **An AI Editing tab, second in every Image Selection project, edits photos with AI tools and
  sends them on; the tabs now run AI Culling, AI Editing, Photo Selection, Signature Album, and a
  project opens on AI Culling.** On the web and the desktop app alike.
  - **The flow is flexible, never forced.** From AI Culling's review, a ticked selection (Select
    all on page ticks the page) goes to AI Editing, to Photo Selection or to the Signature Album,
    and the summary sends every photo the run kept to AI Editing or the album in one step; from AI
    Editing, to Photo Selection or the album; Photo Selection and the album keep their own
    uploaders exactly as they were. A manual project from before the AI tabs existed shows AI
    Culling and AI Editing now (only an explicit untick on the project form takes either away), so
    the sends are offered on every project.
    Nothing is downloaded and re-uploaded: the server moves the photos, with a progress state and
    a notice that opens the destination.
  - **Compression is enforced on the server for everything entering Photo Selection or the
    album.** Direct uploads arrive compressed as before; a photo sent from AI Culling keeps the
    derivatives it arrived with (no second compression); an edited photo is compressed from its
    full-resolution output to the destination's own preset - a new, linked photo in the same
    folder for Photo Selection, an album upload for the album. The original is never overwritten:
    an edit is a versioned output beside it, with Before / After, re-edit and Reset.
  - **A professional wedding editing workstation, honestly reported.** Every render reads the
    photo first - the scene (the culling run's own AI label when there is one), the light, the
    cast, a bright dress or a dark suit - and says so under the preview. Auto Edit is a restrained
    photographic base aimed at the faces, never a saturation push. Ten styles (Natural Wedding,
    Warm Wedding, Luxury Wedding, Cinematic, Moody, Bright & Airy, Editorial, Film Look, Classic,
    Golden Hour), the ten basic sliders (the AI's numbers come back onto them), and folded-away
    HSL, colour balance and detail. Skin retouch keeps texture (smoothing, blemishes, under-eyes,
    skin tone, shine, skin exposure, teeth), face enhancement, denoise that keeps hair and
    jewellery, sharpening without halos, remove object by painting or by Suggest (background
    people), sky with sunset warmth, background brightness / blur / calm, smart crop. The preview
    compares Before / After, Split or Side by side, and the screen says what the engine is doing
    (`image_selection_edit.stage`). A reference photo is measured into an editing profile - "reads
    warmer, more contrast" - that the photo and any batch is moved towards. **Apply to selected /
    Apply to all** (`POST …/ai-editing/batch-apply`) render one edit across a folder or a
    selection, one queue job each with real progress from the bay's counts, each photo adapting to
    its own light so one wedding keeps one look. The engine runs in the face engine's own Python
    environment - no new install, no download; `GET …/ai-editing/capabilities` says which tools
    this server can run and the screen shows a tool it cannot run switched off with the reason. A
    render reads the studio's original when the server can open it, else the uploaded preview, and
    says which. (A dev database that applied the first cut of migration `20261011090000_ai_editing`
    before the `stage` column was added to it needs `ALTER TABLE image_selection_edit ADD COLUMN
    stage VARCHAR(60) NULL AFTER error` by hand; a database that has not applied it yet gets the
    column from the migration.)
  - **New permission `IMAGE_SELECTION / AI Editing`** (`ISAI_EDITING`), granted to `SUPER_ADMIN`
    only by the migration. The studio might want it ticked for the roles that run AI Culling
    (typically the same photographers and editors who hold Project Management); sending into
    Photo Selection still needs Project Management READ_WRITE and into the album Signature Album
    READ_WRITE. AI Culling is the tab's name on screen now (the deliverable in the Deliverables
    table is still "Photo Culling" and matches either spelling).
  - Backend [ai-editing/](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-editing/) (routes, service,
    repository, queue, worker, `edit_engine.py`, the recipe contract),
    [processing/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/processing/service.js)
    (`renderWithRecipe`, `recipeForModule`), the gallery and publication filters, `release-held`

    [SendPhotosActions.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/SendPhotosActions.js),

    `src/modules/image-selection/editing/`. Env: `AI_EDITING_ENABLED`, `AI_EDITING_EMBEDDED_WORKER`,

    `AI_EDIT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, `AI_EDIT_START_TIMEOUT_MS` (all optional).
    **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate`; the face engine's

- **Photos can be added straight into the Photo Culling tab, with the same uploader Photo
  Selection uses, and they reach Photo Selection only through culling.**
  - **Same uploader, both apps.** On the web and the desktop app, a culling subfolder shows the
    same drop zone, Choose Photos, Choose Folder, folder traversal, queue, progress, cancel, retry
    and resume as Photo Selection's uploader.
  - **No original is uploaded.** The web sends only the thumbnail and preview. The desktop
    registers originals where they are on the drive or NAS.

    client gallery. A finalized run releases them, so its Keeps appear and the rest stay culled.

  **Access:** unchanged, no new permission. Uploading and sending on need IMAGE_SELECTION /
  Project Management Read-Write, as uploading and culling always have.
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (one nullable column,
  `image_selection_upload.culling_hold_at`), then `npx prisma generate`. Ship the desktop app's
  update with it, so its Culling tab can add photos.

- **Photo Culling can now learn your studio's taste, but only once you opt in and a trained model
  has proved itself. Until then nothing changes.** Every review action is logged with how it was
  made, and so is which photos were actually seen. None of that changes a decision. A new
  ⋮ → Settings → **AI Culling Training** section holds the studio's opt-in. It is off by default,
  asks before it turns on, and records who changed it and when. Behind it are operator commands
  (`npm run culling:*`, [backend/ml/culling/README.md](../backend/ml/culling/README.md)):
  - export a pseudonymous dataset of finalized runs;
  - train a model and register it;
  - trial it in shadow, where nobody sees it;
  - promote it by a named login once its shadow report passes;
  - roll it back.

  A promoted model decides through the existing decision code, and any error falls back to the
  formula. It is one intelligence for the web and the desktop app. Both review through the same
  routes, so their feedback feeds the same dataset. Each event says which app it came from. A
  model is refused if it gets worse on either server-analyzed or desktop-analyzed runs. No real
  model exists yet; the pipeline has been proven on synthetic data only.
  [learning/](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/learning/),
  [culling-learning/](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/culling-learning/),
  [CullingTrainingConsentField.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/CullingTrainingConsentField.js),
  [useCullingViews.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/culling/useCullingViews.js).
  **Access:** no new permission. Recording what was seen uses IMAGE_SELECTION / Project
  Management Read-Write, the same as deciding. The consent section uses SETTINGS / Organization:
  Read shows it, Read-Write changes it. A studio that wants only Super Admin to decide on
  training should keep SETTINGS / Organization Read-Write to that role in Role Management.
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (three new tables and three settings columns, all
  additive), then `npx prisma generate`. Nothing else is needed: every `AI_CULLING_*` learning
  variable in `backend/.env.example` is off when empty. Set `AI_CULLING_TRAINING_HMAC_KEY`
  (`openssl rand -hex 32`) only when the studio wants to export, and set up `backend/.venv-ml`
  only on the machine that trains.

- **Culling learns your taste.** Each photographer's own Keep and Reject changes now teach culling
  what kinds of photo they keep or reject more often than it suggested — a soft candid it would
  have dropped, a scene they always cut — and the runs they start use it: a photo it moves by a
  few points (never more than eight) says **You usually keep these** or **You usually reject
  these**. It learns against the photographer's own habits, judging traits together, so a trait
  nearly every photo shares (sharp, eyes open, key people present) is never mistaken for taste, and
  it needs at least 20 changes before it does anything. A panel on the Photo Culling tab, **What
  culling has learned from you** (web and desktop), lists what it learned, switches it off for your
  runs and can **Forget what it learned** (your decisions are not touched). It is personal (learned
  from your own changes across your projects, never seen or changed by anyone else), and a run
  keeps the profile it started with, so re-opening an old run never changes its numbers. Routes `GET`/`PATCH /ai-culling/preferences` and `POST /ai-culling/preferences/reset`
  under the same `IMAGE_SELECTION / Project Management` permission (`READ` to see your own,
  `READ_WRITE` to switch or reset); migration `20261006090000_culling_preferences`
  (`image_selection_culling_preference`, session `preference_profile`). The decision log it learns
  from and a run's starter are now real links to the user (migration
  `20261006100000_culling_user_keys`: ids naming no user are cleared, then keys with
  `ON DELETE SET NULL`).
  [preferences.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/analysis/preferences.js),
  [CullingPreferencePanel.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/culling/CullingPreferencePanel.js).
- **Target Count keeps the whole story, and the review says how much of it your Keeps tell.**
  A Target Count run now guarantees, before anything else, that every key person (someone given
  a role in People in these photos, or seen in a large share of the shoot) keeps their best frame,
  and that every moment of each folder the AI is sure of — Ceremony, Decor, Details and so on —
  keeps its best frame; only then come the hours of the day and the best scores. Each photo kept
  for the story says why: **Keeps a key person**, **Covers a moment**, **Covers this hour**. After
  any run, the culling card shows a live line — "Your Keeps cover 9 of 10 scenes · 3 of 3 key
  people" — and names each scene with no Keep yet as a link that opens the review on that scene;
  the line follows your own Keep / Reject changes a moment after you make them (web and desktop).
  On a real 154-photo shoot a target of 40 kept exactly 40 and covered all 10 scenes, six of them
  kept by the new guarantee. Nothing new to install; it
  uses the scene engine when it is on and simply has fewer moments to guarantee when it is off.
  [coverage.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/analysis/coverage.js).
- **Culling now shows what moment each photo is, and explains good and bad framing.** In the
  Photo Culling review (web and desktop) each photo shows its scene under the file name —
  Getting ready, Ceremony, Couple portrait, Group photo, Kids and newborn, Details and so on — and a
  **Scene** picker beside the sort narrows the grid to one moment. The scene is the AI's guess:
  hovering it says how sure it is, and an unsure guess is not shown at all. Two new filters,
  **Likely accidental** and **Face cut off**, explain themselves on hover; a frame is only called
  accidental when it is also soft, blurred or badly exposed, because a deliberate close-up of a
  newborn's feet can look like the floor. New badges say why a photo ranks high or low —
  **Well composed**, **Striking look**, **Face cut off**, **Accidental frame** — and these signals
  only ever move a score a few points. When a scene and a filter match nothing, **Show all scenes**
  is one click away. The preview button no longer covers the Reject button on a card.
  - *For developers and deploy:* a new optional **scene engine** on the server
    ([scene_engine.py](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/scene/scene_engine.py)) runs
    the pinned CLIP ViT-B/32 image model (int8, about 89 MB, downloaded once and checksum-verified)
    with LAION's aesthetic head, on previews only, CPU by default, in the face engine's existing
    `backend/.venv-face` with no new package. Switch it on with `AI_CULLING_SCENE_ENABLED=true`; it
    needs internet once and a writable `AI_SCENE_MODEL_DIR` (see `.env.example` for the other
    `AI_SCENE_*` settings). Off or unavailable, a run skips scenes and the aesthetic score but still
    judges framing from the face boxes; a run that starts while the engine is still downloading its
    model waits at most a minute (`AI_SCENE_READY_WAIT_MS`) and goes on without scenes. Readings are cached
    per photo and engine (a second run of a 154-photo shoot took 24 s instead of 46 s), older engine
    versions' readings are pruned as photos are re-read, and composition is plain maths over the face
    boxes ([composition.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/analysis/composition.js)).
    Runs analyzed on the desktop now post their face boxes, so framing works for them too. Migration
    `20261002230000_culling_scene`; `/api/health` gains `cullingSceneEngine` (a report, never a gate).
    Nobody's access changes.
- **Culling ranks every frame in its group, and tells a burst from a stranger.** The compare
  dialog (web and desktop) shows each frame's rank in its duplicate or burst group — "#2 of 5",
  best first, technical quality first, then faces, eyes open and who is in the frame; marking another frame as
  best makes it #1 and the frames re-sort. Underneath, grouping now reads two signals instead of
  one: beside the perceptual hash, every photo carries a **structure signature** — the layout of
  the same thumbnail, so a frame whose hash bits flipped because the couple stepped sideways still
  reads as the same moment — and the people the face scan found in it. A near-identical pair is a
  duplicate only when the hash agrees and neither the layout nor the people disagree; a burst is
  confirmed by the hash, or by a somewhat looser hash with a close layout and somebody in common.
  The layout only ever qualifies the hash: unrelated real frames sit too close on it to be trusted
  alone. The desktop computes the same signature from the same
  pixels (engine `desktop-culling@1.1.0`) and posts it with its technical signals. Migration `20261002210000_culling_similarity_v2` adds `structure_signature`,
  `duplicate_rank` and `burst_rank` to the result row; runs from before keep NULL and are never
  re-interpreted. The image-embedding model the audit deferred to this phase was measured
  (CLIP ViT-B/32 ONNX on a 12-thread CPU: 352 MB and about 240 ms a frame, or 89 MB quantized at
  about 150 ms) and is **not** shipped: the similarity provider interface is ready for it when
  the studio decides to carry that download to every desktop.
  [structure.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/analysis/structure.js),
  [duplicates.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/analysis/duplicates.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate`.
- **Culling knows who is in the photo.** The Photo Culling tab (web and desktop) gains a
  **People in these photos** strip: everyone the face scan found, numbered as the whole-project
  gallery's People row numbers them, with their face and photo count, and a role for each — Main subject,
  Family, Important guest, Background, or no role (a guest, weighed by how often they appear).
  A run now has a **subject stage** between faces and grouping: for every photo it counts the
  people in it, picks the subject (the person who matters most, weighed by how large and central
  they are) and scores the photo for who is in it and how prominently; a main subject's closed eyes
  count against a photo far more than a guest's, a background face's not at all. A photo whose
  subject is a main subject, family or important guest gets the **Important people present**
  badge; that person's blink gets **Important person blinked** and the face stage's own eye badges
  give way to the weighted answer (both need a server face provider — a run analyzed on the desktop
  weighs presence only). Each role explains itself in the picker, a change can be undone from its
  notice, and roles are read when the run reaches its subject stage, so the strip says which run
  they reached and that a change applies from the next. On the desktop, a run analyzed
  on that computer also hands each photo's faces to the project's people index, so people exist
  for the subject stage even when no face scan ran — only photos the index does not hold yet
  (`pending` items say `facesIndexed`), and only when this computer's Face processing setting
  says to describe photos here. Routes `GET /ai-culling/people` and
  `PATCH /ai-culling/people/:personId` (`{ role }`, null clears) under the same
  `IMAGE_SELECTION / Project Management` permission (`READ` sees roles, `READ_WRITE` sets
  them); migration `20261002180000_culling_subjects` (`image_selection_face_person.role`;
  `subject_score`, `people_count`, `subject_person_id`, `face_details` on the result).
  [subjects.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/analysis/subjects.js),
  [CullingPeopleStrip.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/culling/CullingPeopleStrip.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate`.
- **A culling run can be analyzed on the computer that holds the originals.** On the desktop app,
  Start AI Culling offers "Analyze on this computer" (on by default when the server has
  `DESKTOP_AI_ENABLED`): the desktop reads the originals where they live, computes the same
  sharpness, exposure and perceptual-hash numbers the server computes from previews — and face
  quality through its local face engine when that is ready — and posts only those numbers; the
  server fills any photo the desktop could not find or open from its preview, then groups and
  ranks exactly as before. Progress shows on the desktop ("120 of 154 photos analyzed · 3 with
  faces · 2 left to the server"), with Pause, Resume and "Let the server finish"; closing the app
  and coming back resumes from what is still pending. The web app shows such a run as waiting
  for the desktop and can let the server finish it. Three additive routes under
  `/ai-culling/sessions/:id` — `GET pending`, `POST signals` (behind `DESKTOP_AI_ENABLED` and the
  desktop ingest rate limit) and `POST run` — and migration `20261002150000_culling_analysis_source`
  (`analysis_source`, `engine_versions`). The numbers a workstation posts are trusted within the
  server's own ranges and reason-code vocabulary (a Project Management writer can already decide
  every photo by hand). A run waiting for its workstation counts as active, so it blocks an
  overlapping start until it is handed over or cancelled; asking "Let the server finish" again is
  the recovery if the server's job was ever lost. A desktop analyzes the full original while the
  server analyzes the ≤1600px preview, so a photo scored on one side can differ by a few points
  from the same photo scored on the other; each row says which side stamped it and the session
  records every engine, so a later calibration can tell them apart. The server's own InsightFace engine can now be the culling face provider
  (`AI_CULLING_PROVIDER=insightface`): face count and quality without AWS, eyes and smiles
  scored neutral rather than invented
  ([ai-culling/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/service.js),
  desktop repo `src/modules/image-selection/culling/localAnalysis.js` and `src-tauri/src/culling.rs`).
- **Clients can send several selection items at once with Submit All.** When two or more
  unsent items in a gallery - Retouches and Frames, say, under any shoot - hold saved picks, the
  footer adds a secondary Submit All beside the item's own Review & Submit. It opens Review All
  Selections, which sends nothing by itself: each ready item under its shoot heading with its
  count, status and its own Review & Submit - compact, no thumbnails - and its own Submit All, beside Close,
  to send the ready ones together. The server checks every item and stamps them in one transaction, so if any
  is refused nothing is sent and every pick stays; a double press is refused as already submitted.
  Items stay independent selection sets throughout. With one item picked, the footer is as before.
  The footer's button now reads plain "Review & Submit" (it still opens the item in the sidebar),
  and the review page's final button reads "Submit" instead of "Send <item>".
  Both footers keep their two actions on one row on phones too, wrapping only when a third
  (Deselect All) does not fit.
  No schema change and no permission change - the public route keeps its token and PIN session.
  [SubmitAllDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/SubmitAllDialog.js),
  [clientGalleryHome.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/clientGalleryHome.mjs),
  [publication/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/publication/service.js).

- **Employee Repository: an Incomplete Profiles tab.** After HR Onboarding Pending, it lists the working
  employees (serving notice included) whose Payslip Info is missing something Settings → Payroll rules
  → Edit Payslip asks for - an item listed and on, or a detail added there (the PF ones only while the
  payslip carries them) - so HR can find them and fill it in. Worked out on the page from the
  repository's own rows (`missingPayslipInfo`) and Edit Payslip's settings, on the permissions the
  repository and Payslip Info already read with. No migration, no permission changes.

- **Edit Payslip: an "Any character" input type.** An added Personal or PF detail can now take letters,
  numbers and symbols together ("TN/MAS-01", "A+ (ve)"). "Text and number" now means letters, numbers
  and spaces, and points to Any character for one with symbols. No migration, no permission changes.

- **Edit Payslip: a Dropdown input type.** Adding a Personal or PF detail now offers **Dropdown**
  beside Text, Number, Text and number and Date; choosing it asks for the options, one to a box (at
  least two, up to 30). Edit Employee → Payslip Details shows that detail as a dropdown of those
  options, and the server takes only one of them. `payslip_field.options` (JSON), migration
  `20261013120000_payslip_field_options`. No permission changes.

- **Payroll rules: Edit Payslip, in place of Extra columns.** A section with **Add** at its right,
  which asks what to add to - **Personal details**, **PF details**, **Earnings** or **Deductions** - its
  label, and for the first two what is typed into it (Text, Number or Date); Earnings and Deductions are
  numbers only. Personal and PF details become required fields in Edit Employee → Payslip Details (PF
  ones only, and only then, when Template Settings carries the PF details - disabled otherwise), are
  saved with the record (`payslipValues`, checked against each field's type) and print on the payslip
  after the built-in details. Earnings and Deductions are the Main Page's extra columns, as before. Each
  item - the payslip's own (Emp Name, PAN, Basic Salary, LOP Deduction...) and every added one - has an
  **on/off** (off leaves it off the payslip, its sample and its preview: `hrm_settings.payslip_built_in_items`,
  `payslip_field.shown_on_payslip`, `payroll_component.shown_on_payslip`, migration
  `20261012300000_payslip_item_visibility`) and a **Delete** (an own item kept off the payslip and no
  longer listed - deleted items are not shown; an added one removed with its answers; an Earnings or Deductions column a paid month holds turned off
  instead). An added detail turned off is not asked for in Payslip Details. New tables `payslip_field` and `employee_payslip_value` (migration
  `20261012290000_payslip_fields`), `/api/hrm/payslip-fields` - read on `HRM / Payroll Register` or
  `HRM / Employee Management` Read, changed on Payroll Register Read / Write by somebody reaching every
  branch. No new permission. [EditPayslipPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/EditPayslipPanel.js).

- **My Profile → Payslip.** A tab after My Details (Change Password moved last), shown to whoever
  holds `HRM / My Payslip`; the HRM sidebar entry is hidden, its route `/hrm/payslip` kept. The
  signed-in employee's own
  payslips, one a month whose pay cycle has ended, each with its pay cycle, Paid / Not paid yet, and a
  **Download** that prints it as a PDF laid out by Template Settings (the heading from Branding and the
  Head Office; the PF details only where it carries them). Built from their row on Payroll → Main
  Page through the register's own reading (`listEntries`, now narrowable to one employee): Basic
  Salary, Incentive and the extra earning columns beside LOP Deduction, Salary Advance, Recovery,
  Other Deductions and the extra deduction columns, a prior-month adjustment on whichever side it
  falls, Paid and LOP days under the month's day-rate rule, and Net Pay as paid (rounded).
  **Template Settings → Generate payslips on** sets how many days after the month's payable (payback
  due) date its payslip is generated - on it, or 1 to 30 days after (`hrm_settings.payslip_generate_days_after`,
  migrations `20261012270000_payslip_generate_day` and `20261012310000_payslip_generate_days_after`,
  which renames the column and clears what it held): before then the month is not on the employee's
  page, and with nothing set a payslip appears once its pay cycle ends. A month not paid yet prints as Provisional.
  `GET /api/hrm/my-payslips` and `GET /api/hrm/my-payslips/:year/:month/pdf` answer for the login's
  own employee record alone. The PDF download is now one shared helper
  (`services/api/downloadPdf.js`), which Template Settings' sample uses too. It answers to a new permission, **`HRM / My Payslip`**, added to the catalogue and by
  migration `20261012250000_hrm_my_payslip_permission`, granted to **SUPER_ADMIN only**: tick it in
  Administration → Roles for the employee roles whose people should see Payslip, and re-save them.
  [MyPayslipPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/MyPayslipPage.js).

- **Edit Employee Details: Payslip Details page.** A new page on the Edit rail, after Employee
  Preference and before Reviews, with two headings. **Personal Details** is what the payslip
  prints about the employee, **typed by HR** - empty until typed, nothing filled in from the rest of
  the record - Emp Code, Emp Name, Department, Designation, Location, Date Of Birth, Date of Joining,
  PAN and Bank A/c No., printed on the payslip as typed (`employee.payslip_personal_details`, one JSON
  object, migration `20261013110000_employee_payslip_personal_details`); and **Residential Status**
  (Resident / Non-Resident), saved with the record: `employee.residential_status`, migration
  `20261012230000_employee_residential_status`. **PF Details** is typed by HR: **PF No.** and **EPS
  No.** (letters, digits and /, e.g. TN/MAS/0012345/000/0000123, upper-cased), **UAN** (12 digits) and
  **ESI No.** (10 or 17 digits), each checked as typed and again by the server, none required -
  `employee.pf_number`, `uan_number`, `eps_number`, `esi_number`, migration
  `20261012240000_employee_pf_details`. **Every input on the page is required** when saving from it:
  Residential Status always, and the four PF details when Template Settings has the payslip carry
  them; with personal details only, PF Details is disabled and says why (read through
  `GET /api/hrm/employees/payslip-details`, on `HRM / Employee Management` Read). Edit only, like
  Reviews. No new permission.
  [EmployeeFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeFormPanel.js),
  [payslipEmployeeDetails.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/payslipEmployeeDetails.mjs).

- **Attendance Register: Irregularities and Request cards.** Two lists below Today's Attendance,
  side by side from a tablet up. **Irregularities** is whoever is Absent with no approved leave,
  comp-off or permission - no login after the shift started, or a login too short for a half day -
  with "Leave request pending" where one is still waiting on its approvers. Somebody allowed a
  flexible shift (often working at night) is only judged once their day is over: they are listed for
  yesterday, never for today. **Request** lists what waits on the viewer's answer - the same list as
  "Waiting for me" in Leave or Comp-Off Request - and Open goes there. `GET /api/hrm/attendance` now
  also answers `irregularities` (`registerIrregularities`), and each register row carries `flexible`.
  No new permission: the cards read what the register and the requests list already allow.
  [RegisterAttentionCards.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/RegisterAttentionCards.js).

- **Settings → Wishes.** A new section with two lists, **Birthday Wishes** and **Anniversary Wishes**
  (wedding anniversaries), each of ten ready-written messages the studio can reword in place and save.
  `{employee name}` stands for the employee's name; an anniversary wish may also use `{spouse name}`,
  the spouse's name on their record. Kept as message templates (`BIRTHDAY_WISH_01`..`10`,
  `WEDDING_ANNIVERSARY_WISH_01`..`10`) behind their own permission, `SETTINGS / Wishes` - Read shows
  them, Read / Write rewords them - added to the catalogue and by migration `20261012200000_wishes`,
  which also writes the twenty wishes (`INSERT IGNORE`, so a reworded one is never put back). Granted
  to **SUPER_ADMIN only**; tick it in Role Management for HR or any other role that should keep them.
  **They are sent by the Wishes Scheduler**, the first entry under Wishes: its own WhatsApp group name,
  send time (10:00 am unless set) and Priority 1, every other Allow-WhatsApp employee tried after -
  Attendance WhatsApp Report's panel, made configurable (`api`, `wording`) rather than copied, on
  `hrm_settings.wishes_group_name`, `wishes_send_at` and `wishes_sender_user_id` (a key to `user`,
  migration `20261012280000_wishes_scheduler`), read on `SETTINGS / Wishes` Read and set on Read /
  Write (`/api/settings/wishes/scheduler`). Senders connect their own WhatsApp once, from Attendance
  WhatsApp Report, for both. On each active employee's birthday and wedding anniversary, one wish of
  that kind is picked at random, filled in, and sent within the 135-minute window from that time,
  retried every five minutes while nobody can send; until a group is named, none is sent. A wish naming `{spouse name}` is only picked where the record has a spouse's name.
  At most five a try, a few seconds apart, so a day of many birthdays is not a burst from the studio's
  number; one that may have gone without WhatsApp confirming it is logged rather than sent again.
  Each one sent is logged in `employee_wish` (one a person, a kind and a day, with the wish picked), so
  nobody is wished twice; the claim and the last error sit on `hrm_settings` (migration
  `20261012210000_wish_sending`). The panel says which group and what time, and why the last try failed.
  `WISHES_AUTOSEND=false` turns the timer off; it is on by default, so the VPS needs no new setting. The report's try-each-sender loop is now
  `deliverToGroup(target)`, shared by both, each with its own group and Priority 1 (`sendOrder`). **Restart the backend** after `migrate deploy`.
  [sender.js](../backend/src/modules/settings/wishes/sender.js),
  [WishesPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/WishesPanel.js).

- **Payroll rules: round the net salary to the nearest ₹100 or ₹50.** Settings → Payroll rules →
  Round the net salary to now offers **Nearest ₹100** and **Nearest ₹50** above Nearest ₹10, Nearest ₹1
  and Down to the ₹1 - ₹30,546.15 rounds to ₹30,500 and ₹30,550; halfway goes up. Applied like the
  others: from the payroll month whose cycle is running when it is saved, and a paid or frozen row
  keeps the rule it was settled under. `NEAREST_100` / `NEAREST_50` in `ROUNDING_RULES`
  ([settingsVersions.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/settingsVersions.js)) and
  `roundedSalary` on both sides. No migration - the rule is stored as text.

- **Settings → Template Settings, with a payslip preview.** A new section, right after Templates,
  showing the **payslip template** laid out like the studio's own payslip - logo and company name and
  address, the employee's details (Emp Code, Department, Location, Date of Birth, Date of Joining, UAN,
  Emp Name, Cost Centre, Designation, Bank A/c No., Residential Status, PF No., ESI No., PAN, EPS No.),
  the month, Earnings beside Deductions with Amount and YTD, the totals, Net Pay in figures and in
  words (Indian lakh / crore wording, `amountInWords` in
  [payslipTemplate.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/payslipTemplate.mjs)), Paid and LOP days, and a note. The
  heading is set above the preview - **Logo** (uploaded like the Branding Logo), **Company Name** and
  **Address** (one line to a row) - saved on the HRM settings row (`payslip_company_name`,
  `payslip_address`, `payslip_logo_url`, migration `20261012120000_payslip_template`) through
  `GET` / `PUT /api/settings/template-settings/payslip`, and printed as the payslip's heading: the logo
  at the left; the name in bold, the address, and "PAYSLIP FOR THE MONTH OF ..." at the right. The
  employee and the figures are still a sample - no payroll is read yet; on a phone the payslip keeps
  its shape and scrolls sideways inside its frame. A logo link is kept only when it is the one already
  saved; anything new must be a picture uploaded from the form. **Download sample PDF** prints the
  saved template with the sample figures to an A4 PDF (`GET /api/settings/template-settings/payslip/sample.pdf`,
  Read): the HTML is written on the server ([payslipPdfService.js](../backend/src/services/payslipPdfService.js),
  every value escaped, no script run) and printed by the quotation PDF's headless browser; an edit not
  yet saved is said beside the button, since the PDF prints what is saved. **Financial year starts in**
  (a month, April by default; `payslip_financial_year_start_month`, migration
  `20261012140000_payslip_financial_year_start`) sets where a payslip's YTD counts from - the preview
  and the PDF say "Year to date (YTD): April 2026 to October 2026" above Earnings and Deductions
  (`ytdRange`; a year starting after the payslip's month began the calendar year before), with the
  months it covers - "(7 months)". In the sample each YTD amount is this month's amount for each of
  those months (`withSampleYtd`): April to October puts Basic Salary at 2,10,000.00, January to
  October at 3,00,000.00 - so moving the month visibly moves the YTD; a real payslip will add up the
  employee's own payroll months. Behind its own permission, `SETTINGS / Template Settings` (Read shows it), added to
  the catalogue and by migration `20261012100000_template_settings_permission` - granted to
  **SUPER_ADMIN only**; tick it in Role Management for any other role that should see it.
  [SettingsOverlay.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/SettingsOverlay.js).

- **Who used Casual Leave, permissions and comp-offs, on the administrator's Attendance Dashboard.**
  Three cards at the foot, in the page's own card style: **Casual Leave** (approved, in working days -
  a weekly off or holiday inside it is not counted, and Loss of Pay leave is left out),
  **Permissions** (how many and how long in all) and **Comp-offs** (approved days off taken). One row
  per person, the most first, with their branch and the days (three named, "+N more"); a long list
  scrolls inside its card. One to a row on a phone, two on a tablet, three on a wide screen. They follow
  the range, employee and branch filters, from the same `GET /api/hrm/attendance/overview` (`timeOff`)
  - no new endpoint or permission. [AdminTimeOffCards.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AdminTimeOffCards.js).

- **"Available to take" on the employee's Attendance Dashboard.** Under How the range went: the
  **Casual Leave** balance (and leave awaiting approval), the **permissions** left this month or pay
  cycle against Attendance Rules' limit, and the **comp-offs** still claimable, each with its Use by
  date, soonest first (three shown, "+N more" past that; one within a week says how close). On a phone
  and a tablet Casual Leave and Permissions sit side by side with comp-offs on the row below; on a
  laptop and up the three share one row. A tile that can't be read says so with its own Try again.
  The figures are drawn with a new shared `StatTile`, which How the range went now uses too. Read from the endpoints the Raise Request form
  already uses (`leave-balance`, `permission-usage`, `comp-off-options`), so no backend or permission
  change. [AttendanceBalancesCard.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceBalancesCard.js).

- **A frozen payroll month holds its employee until it is paid out.** While a row is frozen on the
  Payroll Main Page and its payable date has not passed: the employee can't raise an **Attendance
  Regularization** for a day in that row's pay cycle - the form says why as the date is picked, and
  the server refuses it on raise and edit - and no new **Salary Advance** or **Recovery** can be
  created for them, nor advances converted to a recovery (409; the forms say so as the employee is
  picked, marked "payroll frozen" in the list, with Create off). Correcting an existing advance or
  recovery, approving a regularization raised before the freeze, and other request types are unchanged. From the
  day after the payable date, both work again. One helper decides it
  ([freezeHold.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/freezeHold.js)). No migration, no
  permission change.

- **Comp-Off Taken on the Payroll Main Page.** A column right after Casual Leave Taken, in the table and
  its CSV export: the approved comp-off days off in the pay cycle (whatever else the day was). Shown
  only - a comp-off is never paid for and never taken off: the day worked was a weekly off or holiday,
  paid already, and the day off is paid like a working day, outside Attendance Leaves, so Total Leaves,
  LOP and Net Salary do not change. Counted by the attendance calculator (`tallyDays` `compOffTaken`)
  and stored on the row like Casual Leave Taken, so a settled month keeps its figure. The Payslip
  section is still empty; it is ready for it. Migration `20261010320000_payroll_entry_comp_off`
  (existing rows take their figure the next time their month updates). No permission change - the Main Page's `HRM / Payroll Register`.
  [calculator.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/calculator.js),
  [PayrollMainSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollMainSection.js).

- **Ledgers for Casual Leave, permissions and comp-offs.** Three new tables keep a stored record of
  each employee's: **`casual_leave_ledger`** - a row per month (or pay cycle) with the opening balance,
  credited, taken, Loss of Pay and closing balance; **`permission_ledger`** - a row per permission
  request with its day, the period it counts in, its minutes, its status and whether it counts toward
  the limit; **`comp_off_ledger`** - a row per weekly off or holiday worked a full day (or claimed), with
  the hours, its expiry and whether it is Available, Claimed, Used or Expired, and the claiming request.
  For history and audit; the rules stay the truth - an employee's rows are written again from them
  after any of their requests is raised, edited, decided, sent back, reverted or deleted, and after a
  logout, and everybody's after Attendance Rules or Settings → Holidays change. Written after the
  answer, so keeping a ledger never stops a request; who decided what stays on the request's history.
  A burst of changes - several holiday edits, a shift's logouts - comes to one rebuild plus at most one
  more, never several side by side. One rebuild of an employee runs at a time (their employee row is locked), and somebody archived or
  kept out of attendance has their rows cleared. Migration `20261010300000_attendance_ledgers`; then run
  `npm run ledgers:rebuild` once after the deploy (on the VPS: `cd /var/www/dbs-operations-os/current/backend`) to fill them for everybody - it writes these three
  tables only, and is safe on production. No permission change.
  [ledgers.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/ledgers.js).

- **A leave says whether it is Casual Leave or Loss of Pay.** The Leave form - the quick dialog and
  HRM → Request's Raise Request - asks **Leave Type**: **Casual Leave (CL)** or **Loss of Pay (LOP)**,
  with nothing chosen, and will not raise a leave without it. **CL** takes from the Casual Leave
  balance as before (a day beyond it is Loss of Pay) and shows the balance; **LOP** never touches the
  balance and every day of it is unpaid - the form says so in place of the balance. On Payroll's Main
  Page an LOP leave day counts in Attendance Leaves but not in Casual Leave Taken, so it lands in Total
  Leaves and the LOP deduction. Request lists say "Leave (CL)" or "Leave (LOP)". Every leave raised
  before this is marked CL by migration `20261010280000_attendance_request_leave_type` - what it
  already was - and a leave raised without a type (the assistant's, say) is CL. No permission change.
  [AttendanceRequestDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestDialog.js),
  [calculator.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/calculator.js).

- **Payroll's Main Page shows Casual Leave Taken, and Total Leaves takes it off.** **Attendance Leaves**
  is now every day away in the row's pay cycle - absences, half days as half, and approved leave -
  and a new **Casual Leave Taken** beside it is the leave the Casual Leave balance (Settings → Employee
