  → Attendance Rules) covered, which is paid. **Total Leaves = Attendance Leaves + Policy Breach Leaves
  − Casual Leave Taken** (never below 0), and the LOP deduction follows it - the same loss of pay as
  before, with the leave that was paid shown rather than left out. With no Casual Leave set, every
  approved leave day counts as covered, so leave stays paid. Casual Leave Taken is brought in from
  attendance with the rest of the row, never typed, and stored on it, so a month no longer updated
  keeps its figure. Migration `20261010260000_payroll_entry_casual_leave`; existing rows start at 0 and
  fill in the next time their month updates. No permission change.
  [calculator.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/calculator.js),
  [PayrollMainSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollMainSection.js).

- **Payroll's Main Page has a Cost Centre column.** In the Payment band, after Freeze, **Cost Centre**
  books each row to one of the organisation's branches - every active branch is offered, whatever the
  admin's own branch - picked in the cell or in the row's form, and cleared the same way. It is part of
  the payment, so a paid or frozen row can still be booked. Stored as a link to the branch
  (`payroll_entry.cost_centre_branch_id`, migration `20261010240000_payroll_entry_cost_centre`), so a
  renamed branch shows its new name; empty until chosen, and cleared if the branch is removed. No
  permission change: edited under HRM / Payroll Register.
  [PayrollMainSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollMainSection.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/service.js).

- **A limit on permissions, set in Settings → Employee → Attendance Rules → Permissions.** A new
  **Permissions** section holds **Longest permission (minutes)** - moved here from Working day - and
  **Permissions allowed per month**, with **Count permissions by** calendar month or **pay cycle** (the
  same choice Casual Leave has: on the pay cycle a permission counts in the payroll month whose cycle
  holds its date). Pending, sent back and approved permissions count; a request past the limit is
  refused, saying the period and how many were used ("You have already used the 2 permissions allowed
  in October 2026 (1 Oct 2026 to 31 Oct 2026)..."), and the Permission form shows "Permissions in
  October 2026: 1 of 2 used" before it is raised. **0 (the default) is no limit**, as before;
  permissions already raised are not re-checked. Migration `20261010200000_attendance_permission_limit`.
  No permission change: edited under HRM / Attendance Rules, read under the requests guard.
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js),
  [AttendanceRulesPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRulesPanel.js),
  [PermissionAllowance.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PermissionAllowance.js).

- **Comp-offs can expire, set in Settings → Employee → Attendance Rules → Comp-Off.** A new
  **Comp-Off** section asks **Comp-off expires after (days)**: the day off has to be taken within that
  many days of the weekly off or holiday worked - with 30, a Sunday worked on 6 Sep is used by 6 Oct.
  The comp-off picker shows each day's **Use by** date and leaves out one already expired, the Day off
  calendar stops at the expiry, and a later day off is refused saying by when it had to be taken.
  **0 (the default) never expires**, as before; comp-offs already raised are not re-checked. Migration
  `20261010180000_attendance_comp_off_expiry` adds `attendance_settings.comp_off_expiry_days`. No
  permission change: edited under HRM / Attendance Rules. The picker's heading now reads "Weekly Off /
  Holiday Worked".
  [attendanceRules.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/attendanceRules.js),
  [AttendanceRulesPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRulesPanel.js),
  [CompOffWorkedDayPicker.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/CompOffWorkedDayPicker.js).

- **Casual Leave, set in Settings → Employee → Attendance Rules.** A new **Casual Leave** section asks
  how many days each employee gets **per month** (whole or half days), whether **unused leave carries
  to the next month** (on: it builds up through the year; off: each month's lapses at its end, December's
  too), and - with carry on - how many **days carry into the next year** on 1 January (0: all lapse; the
  leave year is the calendar year). **Count Casual Leave by** chooses what a month is: the **calendar
  month** (1st to last day) or the **pay cycle** set in Payroll rules (25 Aug - 24 Sep for October's
  payroll with the cycle on the 25th) - each cycle credits the days, a leave counts in the payroll month
  that pays it, and the year turns with January's payroll (25 Nov); migration
  `20261010160000_attendance_casual_leave_period`, default the calendar month. A change to the policy
  is confirmed before it is saved. Every approved Leave is Casual Leave: each month's days are credited at its start, from the
  employee's joining month (or the month attendance starts being counted, if later), and leave on
  working days takes from the balance in date order (a leave day logged in on anyway takes nothing).
  Leave beyond the balance is still allowed but is
  **Loss of Pay**: the attendance calculator adds it to its loss-of-pay days, so the payroll register's
  Attendance Leaves deducts it on Generate or Refresh (paid and frozen rows are not touched). The Leave
  form - the quick dialog and HRM → Request - shows the balance, the leave waiting for approval, and
  "2 days of these 4 days are beyond your balance and will be Loss of Pay" before it is raised.
  **Off until set**: the default is 0 days a month, which keeps every approved leave paid, as before.
  Nothing is stored per employee - the balance is worked out from approved leave whenever it is read,
  so a policy change re-counts every balance from the start. Migration
  `20261010140000_attendance_casual_leave` adds three columns to `attendance_settings`. No permission
  change: edited under HRM / Attendance Rules, read under the requests guard.
  [attendanceRules.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/attendanceRules.js),
  [calculator.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/calculator.js),
  [AttendanceRulesPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRulesPanel.js),
  [CasualLeaveBalance.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/CasualLeaveBalance.js).

- **Attendance Login has a Flexible Shift work mode, for employees HR allows it.** A full-width
  **Flexible Shift** button sits under Office, Work from home, Client site and On-duty / Travel, and
  says what it means when chosen. Somebody on it logs in at any hour, and the day is counted from
  that login until the logout by the same attendance rule as everybody - under **Half day from** it
  is Absent, under the **Full day** a Half day, and a full day reads **Present** - but it is never
  Late or Early exit, because there is no shift start or end to measure against. Until they log in,
  today reads Yet to log in all day rather than Absent from the shift start; a past day with no login
  is still Absent. It is offered only to an employee ticked **Allow Flexible Shift** - Employees →
  Login Credentials, a section of its own beside Exclude From Attendance - and the server refuses a
  Flexible Shift login from anybody else, so hiding the button is not the only protection. Every
  existing employee starts unticked. A login again after a logout keeps the day's first work mode, as
  it always has, and the Login box now says so ("Flexible Shift, kept from your first login today")
  instead of offering mode buttons that would change nothing. The register, dashboard, overview, totals and payroll read the
  same status, so all of them agree. Migration `20261010100000_employee_allow_flexible_shift` adds
  `employee.allow_flexible_shift` (NOT NULL, default false). No permission change.
  [attendanceRules.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/attendanceRules.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js),
  [EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js),
  [useCredentialForm.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/useCredentialForm.js).

- **Payroll → Main Page can freeze a row.** A **Freeze** switch at the start of the Payment band, before Payment Status,
  settles a row before it is paid: from then on nothing changes its figures - typing in it is
  refused, **Refresh payroll** passes it by (and says how many it left), and an advance, a recovery,
  a Skip, Convert to Recovery or its undo, or removing an extra column is refused for its month, as
  for a paid one. It keeps the salary rules of the moment it was frozen, so a later rules change does
  not move it either. Its payment can still be recorded, and it can be marked Paid. Switching it off
  opens the row again. Migration `20261009240000_hrm_payroll_entry_freeze` adds `frozen`,
  `frozen_at` and `frozen_by_user_id` to `payroll_entry`; after pulling run `npx prisma migrate
  deploy` and `npx prisma generate` in `backend`. No new permission.
  [PayrollMainSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollMainSection.js)
- **Payroll → Main Page ticks rows, and pays them in one go.** Unpaid rows get tick boxes (as on
  every register, with `ADMIN / Table Select All`); the header then offers **Mark Paid** - one
  payment mode, date, paying account and remarks for every ticked row - beside Export and Delete.
  Each row is checked as one marked Paid by hand (a mode and a date, the studio's own account, the
  rules it is paid under); one already paid or refused is named with why and the rest still go.
  Delete removes unpaid rows through the single Remove. New `POST /api/hrm/payroll-register/mark-paid`
  and `DELETE /api/hrm/payroll-register/bulk`, under `HRM / Payroll Register` Read / Write and
  `ADMIN / Table Select All`; no migration and no new permission.
  [PayrollMainSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollMainSection.js)
- **Payroll → Advance Salary and Recovery show each record's payment history.** Below the info
  panel's details, and as a Payment History tab in the full-screen view: how much has been deducted
  so far and the balance (and, for a recovery, how many instalments), then every month of its run -
  **Deducted** once that month's payroll on the Main Page is Paid, with the payment date and mode;
  **Due** while it is Pending or not generated yet; **On Hold**; or **Skipped**. Read from the
  payroll as it stands, so it follows payments made on the Main Page. New
  `GET /api/hrm/payroll-advances/:id/history` and `GET /api/hrm/payroll-recoveries/:id/history`, under
  each register's own Read; no migration and no permission change. `DataTableInfoPanel` takes `after`
  for content below the fields. [PayrollPaymentHistory.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollPaymentHistory.js)
- **Payroll → Main Page can skip a month's Salary Advance or Recovery Deduction.** A **Skip**
  beside the amount leaves it out of that month: an advance then comes off the next month's salary
  instead (its From Month on Advance Salary moves on), and a recovery's instalment is left out with
  the run ending one month later - the same instalment, a later end date on Recovery. The cell then
  reads **Skipped** with **Undo**, and Advance Salary and Recovery gain a column listing the months
  skipped. Nothing is skipped on a paid month, or where it would change what a paid month took; the
  unpaid rows of every month touched update at once. Skip needs `HRM / Payroll Register` and
  `HRM / Payroll Advance` (or `HRM / Payroll Recovery`) Read / Write - no new permission. Migration
  `20261009220000_hrm_payroll_deduction_skips` adds `payroll_advance_skip` and
  `payroll_recovery_skip`; after pulling run `npx prisma migrate deploy` and `npx prisma generate` in
  `backend`. [skips.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/skips.js),
  [PayrollDeductionCell.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollDeductionCell.js)
- **Payroll → Advance Salary converts advances into a recovery.** Tick one employee's advances
  (once one is ticked, only that employee's can join it) and **Convert to Recovery** in the header
  asks the start month and the number of months, then makes one recovery for their total -
  `RECO-ID-...`, on Payroll → Recovery with the advances under its new From Advances column. The
  advances then live on Recovery: they leave the Advance Salary list (kept in the database for the
  audit) and no longer come off their own months' salary, so nothing is taken back twice; the unpaid
  Main Page rows of both the advances' months and the recovery's months follow at once. On Recovery
  such a recovery keeps its employee and total, moves its months only across unpaid ones (the Main
  Page following), and its ⋮ offers **Undo conversion** in place of Remove - removing it and bringing
  the advances back to Advance Salary. Nothing touches a month already Paid. Converting and undoing
  need `HRM / Payroll Advance` **and** `HRM / Payroll Recovery` Read / Write - no new permission; the
  studio may want to grant both to whoever runs payroll. Migration `20261009200000_hrm_payroll_advance_conversion` adds `converted_recovery_id` and
  `converted_at` to `payroll_advance`; after pulling run `npx prisma migrate deploy` and
  `npx prisma generate` in `backend`. Any table can now add its own buttons over a selection
  (`features.selection.actions`).
  [PayrollAdvanceSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollAdvanceSection.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-advance/service.js)
- **Payroll's Main Page says which days a month covers and when it is paid.** At the right of the
  All / Pending / Paid / On Hold tabs, on the same line (wrapping under them on a phone):
  "Pay cycle 25 Aug 2026 - 24 Sep 2026 · Payable on 10 Oct 2026" for October, from the Start and End
  date and the Payable Date (Following Month) in Settings → Payroll rules. Once a month is generated
  it shows the days its rows were actually worked out over, so changing the cycle day later never
  makes a generated month misstate itself; before that it shows what Generate would read, marked
  "(as set in Payroll rules)". The shared page header takes it through a new `tabsAside` slot,
  drawn beside the tabs; pages that do not pass one are unchanged.
  [PayrollMainSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollMainSection.js),
  [PageHeaderTabsRow.js](../frontend/src/components/layout/PageHeaderTabsRow.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/service.js).
- **Payroll rules can add extra columns under Earnings and Deductions on the Main Page.** Settings
  → Employee → Payroll rules has a new **Extra columns** block: name a column (a travel allowance,
  a late fine) and choose **Earnings** or **Deductions**. It appears on Payroll → Main Page in that
  band - an earning after Incentive, a deduction after Other Deductions - is typed per employee in
  its cell or the row's form, and counts in **Total Earned Salary** or **Total Deductions** (and so
  in the net and rounded salary). A paid month's amounts are settled like its other figures.
  Columns can be renamed, archived (no longer offered, but still shown on any month that holds an
  amount for it), restored and **removed** - removing clears the column's amounts from every month
  not yet paid (the confirmation says how many rows), and is refused for a column a paid month
  holds, offering Archive instead, since that pay is settled. Whether a column is an
  earning or a deduction is fixed once it is added. Only somebody who reaches every branch through
  `HRM / Payroll Register` may change them - no new permission. Migration
  `20261009140000_hrm_payroll_components` adds the `payroll_component` and `payroll_entry_component`
  tables; after pulling run `npx prisma migrate deploy` and `npx prisma generate` in `backend`.
  The shared table now places a column it has not seen before beside the column it follows, rather
  than at the far end of a layout somebody arranged, so a new column stays in its band.
  [PayrollComponentsPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/PayrollComponentsPanel.js),
  [components.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/components.js),
  [PayrollMainSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollMainSection.js),
  [tableLayout.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/tableLayout.js).
- **Payroll → Advance Salary records money paid ahead of salary, and the Main Page takes it back.**
  Laid out like Recovery: Create Advance asks for the **Date**, the **Employee Name** (the **Employee
  ID** fills in), the **Amount**, the month it is taken back from (**From Month** and year) and the
  **Reason**, and each advance gets an ID - `ADV-ID-0001`. The whole amount comes off that month's
  payroll as its **Salary Advance**: Generate and Refresh bring it in, and recording, correcting or
  removing an advance updates that month's row at once if it is there and not yet paid. Salary
  Advance is therefore no longer typed on the Main Page, which gains an **Advance ID** column beside
  it; a figure typed there before is replaced by the advances' total the next time that month is
  refreshed or one of its advances changes. Somebody holding only the advance permission therefore
  changes a register total indirectly - only the Salary Advance, only on unpaid rows. A month already Paid is settled, so an advance cannot be put into, moved out of or removed
  from it. Status reads Pending until the month begins and Deducted from then, with All / Pending /
  Deducted tabs; Edit and Remove (with a reason, the row kept for the audit) need write access.
  **New permission `HRM / Payroll Advance`**, granted to SUPER_ADMIN only by migration
  `20261009120000_hrm_payroll_advance` (which also adds the `payroll_advance` table); the studio may
  want to grant it to the roles that run payroll (HR, Branch Admin), in Role Management. After pulling, run
  `npx prisma migrate deploy` and `npx prisma generate` in `backend` (stop the dev server first).
  [PayrollAdvanceSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollAdvanceSection.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-advance/service.js),
  [payroll-register/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/service.js).
- **The administrator's Attendance Dashboard links each login and logout to the map.** The
  Employees table has two new columns, **Login location link** and **Logout location link**: "View on
  map" opens the position captured with the login or logout (its latitude and longitude) in Google
  Maps, in a new tab. Over one day it is that day's; over a longer range, the latest captured in it.
  A dash where no position was captured. The shared table link cell takes a `linkLabel` for links
  that are not files. [AdminAttendanceEmployees.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AdminAttendanceEmployees.js),
  [mapLink.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/mapLink.mjs).
- **Payroll → Main Page: the studio's payroll sheet, as a monthly register.** Pick a month and
  **Generate payroll**: every working employee gets a row with their base salary, their loss-of-pay
  days from attendance over the pay cycle (25 Apr - 24 May for June, with the cycle on the 25th),
  and any recovery due that month from Payroll → Recovery (with its Recovery ID). Type the incentive,
  policy breach leaves, salary advance, other deductions and remarks, then the payment - status,
  mode, the account it was paid from, date and remarks. Total Earned, Total Leaves, LOP Deduction,
  Total Deductions, Net Salary and Rounded Salary are worked out for you, previewed as you type, under
  the new **Settings → Employee → Payroll rules**: a day's pay is the base salary over the pay cycle's
  working days (default), calendar days or a fixed 30, and the salary rounds to the nearest ₹10
  (default), ₹1 or down to ₹1. All / Pending / Paid / On Hold tabs, the month's rounded total, CSV
  export, and Edit / Refresh from attendance / Remove from each row's ⋮. A paid row's figures are
  locked until it is set back to Pending, and it keeps the rules it was paid under - changing the
  rules (which only somebody reaching every branch may do) reprices only months not yet paid. A new permission, `HRM / Payroll Register` (catalogue and
  migration), granted to SUPER_ADMIN only - the studio may want it for HR or Accounts roles; without
  it the Main Page section and the Payroll rules are not offered, and a role limited to some branches
  sees only those branches' employees. Marking a row Paid records nothing in Accounts.
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate`.
  [PayrollMainSection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollMainSection.js),
  [payroll-register/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-register/service.js).
- **Payroll → Recovery: the studio's recovery sheet, as a register.** Create Recovery picks the
  employee by name - their Employee ID comes with them - and asks the total amount, the start month
  and year, the number of months and the reason, showing the monthly deduction and the start and
  end dates as they are typed. Each recovery gets its own ID (`RECO-ID-0001` onwards), and the
  register works out the Monthly Deduction (total ÷ months), Start Date (1st of the start month),
  End Date (start + months) and Status (Completed once the end date has come, Active until then),
  with All / Active / Completed tabs, CSV export, and Edit / Remove from each row's ⋮. A new
  permission, `HRM / Payroll Recovery` (catalogue and migration), granted to SUPER_ADMIN only - the
  studio may want it for HR or Accounts roles in Role Management; without it the Recovery section is
  not offered. A role limited to some branches sees and records recoveries only for employees in
  those branches. **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate`.
  [PayrollRecoverySection.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollRecoverySection.js),
  [payroll-recovery/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payroll-recovery/service.js).
- **Payroll has four sections: Main Page, Advance Salary, Recovery and Payslip.** A menu beside
  the Payroll heading switches between them, as Employee Attendance switches its Dashboard and
  Register, and the section open is kept in the address (`?section=`), so a refresh or a bookmark
  reopens it. Each section is empty for now, and all four are open to everybody who can open
  Payroll (`HRM / Payroll`). [PayrollPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollPage.js).

- **Speak-up Review can now Approve, Approve & Assign, or Reject each speak-up, and every speak-up
  shows its status.** Each pending row in Speak-up Review has a ⋮ with the three choices. **Approve**
  marks it Approved. **Approve & Assign** asks who (only people who can answer tasks are offered),
  the priority and an optional due date, and creates an HRM task for that person in the same save -
  the task carries the speak-up's ID, type, subject and description, but **never who raised it**,
  and the attachment stays in Speak-up Review. **Reject** needs a reason. A speak-up is decided once.
  Speak-up Review shows the status, who decided it and when, the remark and the task code; the
  employee's own "My Speak-ups" shows **only the status** (Pending, Approved, Approved & Assigned,
  Rejected). Deciding needs **HRM → Speak-up Review at Read & Write** - an existing permission, so
  nothing new to seed; roles that should decide need that level ticked in Role Management. Migration
  `20261009120000_speak_up_review_decisions` adds the columns; every existing speak-up starts as
  Pending. The "can answer tasks" check and its assignee list moved from Feedback into the tasks
  service, where both modules now read them. Double-clicking a pending speak-up opens it with the
  same three decisions as buttons at the foot, the way a task opens with its verbs; a decided one
  keeps the plain Close (`RecordViewPanel` gained a `footer` prop for it). **Duplicate Task** is now offered only on tasks written
  by hand: a task raised from a speak-up or a feedback issue no longer has it in its ⋮
  ([TasksPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/TasksPage.js)).
  [SpeakUpReviewPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/SpeakUpReviewPanel.js),
  [SpeakUpDecisionDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/SpeakUpDecisionDialog.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/speak-up/controller.js)

- **Offboarding an employee now reassigns their pending work.** When HR completes Offboarding for
  somebody who still holds work, a pop-up lists it - open tasks, CRM leads, projects where they are
  CRM, Project Manager, Pre Production Coordinator, Creative Manager, Post Production Coordinator or
  Production Manager, production shoots they coordinate or crew, interview candidates, the sheet
  rules that send them new leads or candidates, and colleagues they approve for - with "Reassign to"
  starting at their reporting manager. Confirming moves all of it to that person in the same save
  as the offboarding, writes "Reassigned from … to …" on each task, and notifies the receiver. Only
  pending work moves: completed tasks, converted leads, delivered projects, finished shoots and
  decided candidates keep the leaver's name. Changing someone's status to a non-working one from
  the employee form is refused while they still hold pending work, and points to Offboarding.
  Uses `HRM / Employee Management` - no new permission.
  [handover.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/separations/handover.js),
  [HandOverDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/HandOverDialog.js).

- **Speak-up Review can now Approve, Approve & Assign, or Reject each speak-up, and every speak-up
  shows its status.** Each pending row in Speak-up Review has a ⋮ with the three choices. **Approve**
  marks it Approved. **Approve & Assign** asks who (only people who can answer tasks are offered),
  the priority and an optional due date, and creates an HRM task for that person in the same save -
  the task carries the speak-up's ID, type, subject and description, but **never who raised it**,
  and the attachment stays in Speak-up Review. **Reject** needs a reason. A speak-up is decided once.
  Speak-up Review shows the status, who decided it and when, the remark and the task code; the
  employee's own "My Speak-ups" shows **only the status** (Pending, Approved, Approved & Assigned,
  Rejected). Deciding needs **HRM → Speak-up Review at Read & Write** - an existing permission, so
  nothing new to seed; roles that should decide need that level ticked in Role Management. Migration
  `20261009120000_speak_up_review_decisions` adds the columns; every existing speak-up starts as
  Pending. The "can answer tasks" check and its assignee list moved from Feedback into the tasks
  service, where both modules now read them. Double-clicking a pending speak-up opens it with the
  same three decisions as buttons at the foot, the way a task opens with its verbs; a decided one
  keeps the plain Close (`RecordViewPanel` gained a `footer` prop for it). **Duplicate Task** is now offered only on tasks written
  by hand: a task raised from a speak-up or a feedback issue no longer has it in its ⋮
  ([TasksPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/TasksPage.js)).
  [SpeakUpReviewPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/SpeakUpReviewPanel.js),
  [SpeakUpDecisionDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/SpeakUpDecisionDialog.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/speak-up/controller.js)

- **Offboarding an employee now reassigns their pending work.** When HR completes Offboarding for
  somebody who still holds work, a pop-up lists it - open tasks, CRM leads, projects where they are
  CRM, Project Manager, Pre Production Coordinator, Creative Manager, Post Production Coordinator or
  Production Manager, production shoots they coordinate or crew, interview candidates, the sheet
  rules that send them new leads or candidates, and colleagues they approve for - with "Reassign to"
  starting at their reporting manager. Confirming moves all of it to that person in the same save
  as the offboarding, writes "Reassigned from … to …" on each task, and notifies the receiver. Only
  pending work moves: completed tasks, converted leads, delivered projects, finished shoots and
  decided candidates keep the leaver's name. Changing someone's status to a non-working one from
  the employee form is refused while they still hold pending work, and points to Offboarding.
  Uses `HRM / Employee Management` - no new permission.
  [handover.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/separations/handover.js),
  [HandOverDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/HandOverDialog.js).

- **A Pre Production re-import can bring back what was deleted.** Pre Production → Import has a
  **Restore deleted projects and shoots** tick beside Replace, offered to the same people. A row
  naming a project or shoot that was deleted in the app was always refused - and still is, unticked,
  so an old file uploaded again never silently undoes a delete. Ticked, the deleted project or shoot
  is undeleted - the same row and IDs, so nothing is duplicated - and updated from the file, and the
  result says how many came back. Only what the import made is restored: a project that had an Image
  Selection gallery, a client login or client storage, or a shoot whose deliverables or post
  production were deleted with it, is skipped and named, to restore by hand. Restoring a project
  needs the right to delete it. No new permission.
  [import.service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/import.service.js),
  [ImportDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/ImportDialog.js).

- **Pre Production → Import can replace a project already in the app with the sheet's booking.**
  A tick box in the import dialog, "Replace projects that already exist", offered only to people
  who may delete any project (a branch administrator, or Show All Projects at Read / Write). Ticked,
  Import first shows a preview that changes nothing - the projects that would be deleted, and the
  rows that would be skipped - and "Delete and import" then does it: a project with the same client
  name in the same vertical is deleted with all its shoots and details, the way the Delete button
  deletes one, and the sheet's booking imported in its place. A project with payments recorded or
  an Image Selection gallery is skipped and listed rather than deleted; a match on the client number
  alone is never replaced, since one client can book twice; and two app projects with one client
  name are refused and named. Unticked, nothing changes: matching rows are refused as before. This
  is the one place an import deletes anything, and only when somebody ticks it.
  [import.service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/import.service.js),
  [ImportDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/ImportDialog.js). No new permission.
- **HRM → Payroll.** A new screen in the HRM sidebar, after Interview (`/hrm/payroll`), behind its
  own permission `HRM / Payroll` (catalogue; migration `20261008200000_hrm_payslip_permission`
  created it as Payslip, granted to SUPER_ADMIN only, and `20261008210000_hrm_payslip_renamed_payroll`
  renames it in place, so any role granted Payslip keeps it as Payroll). The page is empty for now - only its heading - and there is no
  backend yet, so no API to guard. The studio may want it granted to HR's roles in Role Management.
  [navigation.mjs](../frontend/src/constants/navigation.mjs),
  [PayrollPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PayrollPage.js).
- **Customer Issues and Feedback: a Shoot Completion Feedback for every shoot Production completes,
  then an Overall Feedback once they are all completed.**
  Once a shoot reads Completed on the Production board (plan submitted, last step done), it waits on
  Yet to be done - a row of its own, with its Shoot ID, beside its project's New Project Feedback -
  and a writer's Give Feedback takes its Review and Feedback the same way, an Average or Poor one
  assigned to somebody as a task. A shoot's form also asks **Appreciation** and **Not Satisfied** -
  multi-selects of the people who worked on that shoot (the CRM; the Pre Production Coordinator,
  Creative Manager and Project Manager; the Production Manager and the shoot's Production
  Coordinator, Production Team and service crew), never one in both - stored in
  `project_feedback_employee` as Production Completion Feedback's were, so they reach the employee's
  review timeline as Shine and Shadow. One per shoot; every other shoot of the Event ID waits for its own.
  Once every live shoot of the Event ID is Completed (a Rejected one set aside), the project waits
  once more, for its **Overall Feedback** - the same form, one per project.
  The table has a Shoot ID column, the form's project card adds the shoot, the info panel and View
  read a section per shoot, and a shoot's issue task names the shoot in its title and in Tasks. An
  issue task is filed under the department of the feedback it came from - **Sales** for a New Project
  Feedback, **Production** for a shoot's, **Post Production** for the Overall Feedback - rather than
  the assignee's own department. A feedback now names its shoot (`project_feedback.shoot_id`, migration
  `20261008180000_project_feedback_shoot`; the unique key is project, stage and shoot, and the save
  locks the project row so the project's one New Project Feedback still holds). `POST
  /api/project-management/feedback` takes `stage` (`NEW_PROJECT`, `SHOOT_COMPLETION` with its
  `shootId`, and for it `appreciatedEmployeeIds` and `notSatisfiedEmployeeIds`, or `OVERALL`);
  `GET /projects/:projectId/people?shootId=` lists the shoot's people by area; `GET /pending` lists the waiting shoots first, then the Overall
  Feedbacks, then the New Project Feedbacks. No permission change - still PROJECT / Feedback.
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/feedback/service.js),
  [feedbackRecord.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/feedbackRecord.mjs),
  [project-feedback.test.js](../backend/test/project-feedback.test.js).
- **Employee Preference → Exclude → Exclude From Attendance.** A new **Exclude** section, after
  WhatsApp, with the same tick box as Allow WhatsApp. An employee ticked is kept out of the Attendance
  module: not on the register, the admin Dashboard (its counts, its Employees table, its Employee
  filter) or the daily WhatsApp report, not counted in any total, and not named by the assistant's
  attendance answers. Their requests are in nobody's team or approver queue, nor approved or rejected
  by id (one raised before the tick stays as it was, and they may still withdraw it), and they cannot raise a
  new one (nobody would see it - they are told their attendance is not tracked); their day, its
  check-in photo and its edit are "not on file" to anybody but themselves. On their own Employee
  Attendance page a day they do not mark reads Not required rather than Absent - the treatment a
  Super Admin already had, through the same `attendanceOptionalEmployeeIds`, which now answers for
  both. Stored on the employee (`employee.exclude_from_attendance`, migration
  `20261008160000_employee_exclude_from_attendance`, default off - nobody is excluded until ticked),
  saved with Employee Preference's create and update (an update that does not send it leaves it as
  it was) and kept in its draft. `GET /api/hrm/employees/directory?for=attendance` is the Dashboard
  filter's list; every other picker is unchanged. The WhatsApp report's sender list is not filtered:
  an excluded employee can still be the one who sends it
  ([service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js),
  [useCredentialForm.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/useCredentialForm.js),
  [attendance-exclude.test.js](../backend/test/attendance-exclude.test.js)).

- **A quotation's shoot can be duplicated from the Shoot List.** The ⋮ on each shoot in the
  Quotation Generator now reads Edit, Duplicate, Delete. Duplicate adds a new shoot to the same
  quotation holding everything the original does - type, date, place, district, state, sessions and
  length, food, stay, travel and preference - with its own Shoot ID, and says so with an Undo. Its
  service and deliverable lines are not copied, as for any new shoot, and a copy is never the Main
  Event, so the mark stays on the original. Edit and Delete are unchanged. New Shoot IDs now
  continue from the highest already listed, so a shoot added after another was deleted can no
  longer be given an ID the quotation still holds. See
  [QuotationGeneratorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationGeneratorPanel.js) and
  [ProjectShootList.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectShootList.js).

- **An unassigned lead is given an owner by dragging it off the board's Unassigned column.** Those
  cards could not be dragged at all before - a lead with no CRM reads as Unassigned whatever its
  status, so a status dropped on one was stored and never shown. What such a lead is actually missing
  is an **owner**, and the lead popup has no Assign To field: the only control in the module that
  picks an employee is Add Lead's. So dropping one on a status opens **Add Lead on the lead it
  already is** - its own details, its own enquiry id, the name and enquiry id said at the top, the
  dropped status chosen, and Assign To waiting. Confirm **updates** that lead rather than adding
  another: no new enquiry id, and its Added Time and Enquiry Date stay its own. Name somebody and it
  moves to the status it was dropped on; leave Assign To empty and it stays in Unassigned, which
  needs no rule of its own - the board already reads any lead with no CRM that way. Every status is
  offered while assigning, CNA, Invalid and Rejected included, since the card could have been dropped
  on any column; and the lead is not warned about as a duplicate of itself.
  [CRMPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CRMPage.js),
  [CrmKanbanBoard.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CrmKanbanBoard.js). No migration.
  **Access:** no new permission - the same `CRM / Leads` the board and the form already answer to,
  and the Unassigned column is only drawn for somebody who hands work out.

- **Production can import the studio's old production sheet, linked to the pre production import.**
  The ⋮ in the Production board's header offers Import for Dum Dum, Qua Qua and Corp. Each row
  is a shoot, named by the sheet's own Shoot ID - the same one the Pre Production import stored -
  so the two files link without matching anything by hand; import pre production first, with a
  Production Manager, since that is what gives a shoot its production record. A row fills the
  Production Coordinator and team (by Employee Code), travel, plan remarks, whether the plan was
  submitted, the step the shoot reached, its status, and the photo copy. Uploading again fills only
  what is still empty and never moves a shoot back a step. Only somebody who may change the plan
  on the board - the project's Production Manager, a Super Admin, or Show All Projects at Read /
  Write - can import a shoot. The steps' own times and photos are not in the old sheet and are left
  empty. [importColumns.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/importColumns.js),
  [import.service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/import.service.js),
  [ProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionPage.js).
  Uses `PROJECT / Production` - no new permission, no migration.

- **Logging out now says what it does to the day - before and after.** The Logout box warns, before
  you confirm, when logging out now would mark the day **Absent** (under Half day from), a **Half
  day** (under the full day) or an **Early exit**, so you can cancel and stay. After logging out, a
  **You're logged out** box - like the login's - shows the time and either "Successfully logged out"
  or what the day will be marked as. An approved permission that covers every shortfall - the early
  departure, and the late arrival if there was one - now keeps a short day from being a Half day or
  Absent: the day reads **Permitted** and the logout is simply successful. A permitted late arrival
  does not excuse an unpermitted early departure. Both boxes read the day from the server, by the register's own rules
  (new `GET /api/hrm/attendance/logout-preview`, and the logout's answer now carries `day`), so they
  cannot disagree with it. No permission changed - the same `HRM / Employee Attendance`.
  [EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js),
  [logoutMessage.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/logoutMessage.mjs),
  [attendanceRules.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/attendanceRules.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js).
- **The Attendance Register has an Available card: who is working right now.** Beside Present, in
  the same design, it counts - and when pressed, narrows Today's Attendance to - everybody who has
  logged in today and not logged out, is not on a break, and is not inside an approved permission's
  time window at this moment. Somebody who steps out for a break or a permission leaves it and comes
  back when they return; the figure is as of when the register was opened or refreshed. The cards now
  sit five in a row on a laptop and three on a tablet; on a phone Present takes the whole row, then
  Available and Break, then Permissions and Leave. No permission changed - the
  same register behind `HRM / Attendance Approval`.
  [AttendanceRegisterPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRegisterPage.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js).
- **Your own late, absent and leave days now show on your Calendar, under "My Attendance".** The
  Calendar's category switch has a **My Attendance** entry (it replaces the empty "Employee
  Attendance" one) that draws the signed-in person's own days from the HRM register that were not
  simply on time - **Absent, On leave, Comp off, Late, Half day, Early exit** - one chip per day,
  each status in its own colour; the List view and the day's detail panel show the same days with
  login, logout and hours worked. It answers to **HRM / Employee Attendance** (Read) - the
  permission the person's own Attendance page already needs, so no role gains anything new - and it
  only ever shows the viewer's own days; a login with no linked employee sees none. Days appear once
  the register has judged them (up to today, at most 92 days at a time), and a comp-off is told
  apart from ordinary leave.
  Read through the same `attendanceDays` the Attendance page and the register use, so the calendar
  cannot disagree with them. [service.js](../backend/src/modules/schedule/calendar/service.js),
  [schedule.js](../frontend/src/lib/schedule.js), [meetingSources.js](../frontend/src/lib/meetingSources.js).
- **The Attendance Register has two more cards: Permissions and Break.** Beside Present and Leave, in
  the same design, Permissions counts everybody with an approved permission today and Break everybody
  who has taken a break (one still running included); pressing either narrows Today's Attendance to
  those people, and pressing it again lets go. The table gains Permission (each permission's time
  window) and Break (the day's break time, with "On break" while one runs) columns. The four cards sit
  two abreast on a phone and a tablet and in one row from a laptop up. No new permission.
  [AttendanceRegisterPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRegisterPage.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js).
- **An Average or Poor review is now assigned to someone as a task, and their answer moves the
  feedback.** On every Give Feedback form, a review rated Average or Poor shows **Assign to** beside
  it (required). Saving gives each one to its person as an HRM task (type Feedback, High priority), which
  they open from Tasks and answer **Issues sorted** or **Rejected** (with the reason) in place of Mark
  Complete; it can be reassigned but not cancelled or deleted. The feedback stays under Issues until
  every assigned issue is answered, then moves to Rejected if any was rejected, otherwise Issues
  sorted. The info panel and View list each issue, who has it and the answer. Feedback given earlier,
  with no tasks, is still moved from the Feedback page's ⋮ menu. Only people who can answer a task -
  an active login with HRM / Task Management (Read & Write) - are offered and accepted; the task is
  given on the feedback giver's behalf, so a Feedback writer raises it without needing Task
  Management themselves. Answering locks the feedback first, so two last answers at once still move
  it. No new permission.
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (adds `project_feedback_issue`), then `npx prisma generate`
  and restart the API.
  [FeedbackFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackFormPanel.js),
  [TaskDetailPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/TaskDetailPanel.js),
  [issues.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/feedback/issues.js),
  [tasks/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/tasks/service.js),
  [migration](../backend/prisma/migrations/20261008090000_project_feedback_issue/migration.sql).
- **Project Completed Feedback can now be given: Post Production's review and feedback, the
  Overall Experience, and a Suggestion.** Once a project's Production Completion Feedback is given,
  the project comes back to Feedback → Yet to be done for its Project Completed Feedback (Feedback
  Stage column). Give Feedback asks for a Review and Feedback for Post Production (required), the
  Overall Experience as a rating (required), and a Suggestion (optional); an Average or Poor on either
  rating files it under Issues. The View's Project Completed Feedback section unlocks and shows it.
  There is no Post Production module yet, so for now it opens after the Production Completion
  Feedback; it moves to Post Production's completion when that exists (`projectCompletedOpen`).
  No new permission - still PROJECT / Feedback.
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (adds `project_feedback.overall_experience` and
  `suggestion`), then `npx prisma generate` and restart the API.
  [FeedbackFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackFormPanel.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/feedback/service.js),
  [migration](../backend/prisma/migrations/20261007230000_project_feedback_project_completed/migration.sql).
- **A client's Appreciation now shows on the employee's review timeline as a Shine, and Not
  Satisfied as a Shadow.** Everyone named in a Production Completion Feedback gets a dashed "Client
  feedback" card on their Employee Repository review timeline - on the Shine side for an
  Appreciation, the Shadow side for Not Satisfied - in date order with the project and Feedback ID,
  and a count at the top. They are read from the feedback, so they never change the salary and are
  not edited or deleted with the salary reviews; deleting the project removes them. Each employee
  row from `GET /api/hrm/employees` carries them as `clientFeedback`; the project and Feedback ID
  come only to a reader who also holds PROJECT / Feedback (Read) - anyone else sees the Shine or
  Shadow and its date alone. No new permission and no database change.
  [EmployeeReviewTimeline.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeReviewTimeline.js),
  [employeeReviewTimeline.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/employeeReviewTimeline.mjs),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/employees/controller.js).
- **Production Completion Feedback now asks for a review of Sales, Pre Production and Production,
  the client's referral, and who they appreciate or were not satisfied with.** Give Feedback on a
  Production Completion row asks for a Review and Feedback for each of the three areas, optional
  Referral Details (name and mobile), and Appreciation and Not Satisfied - multi-selects of the people
  who worked on the project (Sales: the CRM; Pre Production: the Pre Production Coordinator, Creative
  Manager and Project Manager; Production: the Production Manager and each shoot's Production
  Coordinator, Production Team and service crew), never the same person in both. One Average or Poor
  among the three files it under Issues. Everything given shows in the View's Production Completion
  Feedback section. The shared form panel gains a `multiselect` field type
  ([SchemaFormFields.js](../frontend/src/components/schema-form/SchemaFormFields.js)). No new
  permission - still PROJECT / Feedback.
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (adds `project_feedback_area`, `project_feedback_employee`,
  `project_feedback.referral_name` / `referral_mobile`, and makes `project_feedback.feedback`
  optional), then `npx prisma generate` and restart the API.
  [FeedbackFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackFormPanel.js),
  [feedbackConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/feedbackConfig.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/feedback/service.js),
  [migration](../backend/prisma/migrations/20261007220000_project_feedback_production_completion/migration.sql).
- **Once Production completes a project's shoots, the project comes back to Feedback → Yet to be
  done for its Production Completion Feedback.** Each project's feedback is now taken in stages: its
  New Project Feedback as soon as it is created, and its Production Completion Feedback once every
  live shoot is Completed on the Production board (a Rejected shoot is set aside; at least one must
  be Completed). Each stage is a row of its own, named in the new **Feedback Stage** column, filed by
  its review as before, one per project per stage. While a project waits in Yet to be done for its
  next stage, its earlier Completed feedback is held off the Completed tab (and its count), and comes
  back once that next feedback is given; a feedback under Issues is never held back. The View and info panel show the project's every
  feedback - given, Yet to be done, or still locked; Production Completion Feedback unlocks when
  Production completes, and Project Completed Feedback stays locked for now. No new permission -
  still PROJECT / Feedback.
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (adds `project_feedback.stage`, every existing feedback
  being a New Project Feedback, and makes the unique key project + stage), then `npx prisma generate`
  and restart the API.
  [FeedbackPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackPage.js),
  [feedbackRecord.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/feedbackRecord.mjs),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/feedback/service.js),
  [migration](../backend/prisma/migrations/20261007200000_project_feedback_stage/migration.sql).
- **Services and Deliverables have a Duplicate action in Settings → Project.** More → Duplicate
  opens the Add Service or Add Deliverable dialog filled with everything the row holds - pricing
  lines and their deliverables, brands and variants, answers, remarks, shoot type, timings and
  duration - with the name left empty to type. Add creates a new record on Save; the original is
  not touched, and Edit and Delete work as before. A name already in use, ignoring case, spacing
  and punctuation, is refused in the dialog and by the server, which now answers two adds of one
  name at the same moment with its usual "already exists" rather than an error. See
  [definitionDuplicate.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/definitionDuplicate.mjs). No migration, no
  permission change: it is the same Add, behind the same `PROJECT / Projects` guard.

- **Moving a feedback out of Issues now asks for remarks: required to reject it, optional when
  marking it Issues sorted.** Project Management → Feedback → Issues → ⋮ → Issues sorted or Rejected
  opens the confirmation with a Remarks box; a rejection without a reason is stopped there, and the
  server refuses one too. The remark shows as a Remarks column on the Issues sorted and Rejected
  tabs, and in the info panel and View with who decided it and when (Decided By, Decided On). Feedback moved before this has
  no remark. No new permission - still PROJECT / Feedback at Read & Write.
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (adds `project_feedback.issue_remarks`,
  `issue_resolved_by_user_id` and `issue_resolved_at`), then `npx prisma generate` and restart the API.
  [FeedbackPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackPage.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/feedback/service.js),
  [migration](../backend/prisma/migrations/20261007160000_project_feedback_issue_remarks/migration.sql).
- **Attendance can be switched on from a chosen day: Settings → Employee → Attendance Rules →
  Attendance starts on.** Before that date nothing is counted for anybody - no day reads Absent or
  Late, no hours are owed, logins recorded then (rehearsals before go-live) are ignored, and those
  days cannot be regularized or claimed as comp-off. Each person is counted from that date or their
  joining date, whichever is later, on their own attendance page, the Attendance Register, the
  Admin Dashboard, the salary calculator, the missed-logout notices and Nebula's attendance answers.
  Blank means every day counts, as before. Changing the date asks for confirmation first, since it
  re-counts everybody's past days; nothing is deleted, so moving it earlier brings them back. Editable with `HRM / Attendance Rules` write, read-only otherwise; no new permission.
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (adds `attendance_settings.attendance_start_date`), then
  `npx prisma generate` and restart the API; then set the date in Attendance Rules.
  [AttendanceRulesPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRulesPanel.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js),
  [migration](../backend/prisma/migrations/20261007140000_attendance_start_date/migration.sql).
- **A volume button can take the attendance selfie, where the phone allows it.** While the camera is
  live in the Login, Logout and break circle, pressing a volume button takes the picture just as the
  camera button does. Browsers mostly keep the volume buttons for the volume - iPhone always, Android
  Chrome usually - so this is an extra, not the way in; a Bluetooth selfie remote (which presses
  volume up) is the case it reliably serves. The camera button is unchanged.
  [EmployeeAttendancePage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/EmployeeAttendancePage.js).
- **Attendance Regularization requests have an approver of their own.** Employee Repository →
  Administration → Edit → Employee Preference has a new **Attendance Regularization Approval** section
  with one Attendance Regularization Approver. A regularization goes to that person alone, and Raise
  Request names them before it is sent ("Goes to your Attendance Regularization Approver."). Left
  empty, a regularization goes to the Permission Approver, as every one did before, and the form says
  so - nobody is stopped from raising one while HR fills the new field in. Nobody may approve their own.
  The approver also gets the Waiting for me queue. No new permission.
  [approvals.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/approvals.js),
  [employeeCredentialConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/employeeCredentialConfig.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate` (adds
  `employee.regularization_approver_employee_id`).
- **Every feedback now has a Feedback ID.** Saving a feedback gives it the next `DBS-FB-00001`-style
  ID from the counter every business ID comes from; it is the Feedback table's first column, the
  first line of the info panel and the title of View. Feedback already given is numbered in the
  order it was given. The Yet to be done tab, which holds the shoots still waiting for feedback,
  leaves the column off.
  [FeedbackPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackPage.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/feedback/service.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate` (adds `project_feedback.feedback_code`
  and numbers the existing rows).
- **A feedback under Issues can be moved on to Issues sorted or Rejected.** In the Issues tab, the
  row's ⋮ menu offers both to anyone who can give feedback; each asks for a confirmation, then
  moves the feedback to that tab. It cannot be moved back, and two people answering the same
  feedback at once cannot both move it. No new permission and no migration.
  [FeedbackPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackPage.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/feedback/service.js).
- **Giving feedback now files it by its review and opens the message to send the client.**
  Excellent and Good feedback goes to Completed, Average and Poor to Issues, and the Feedback page
  moves to that tab. The client's message opens in the shared message box, to copy - there is no
  Send WhatsApp on the Feedback page, and every other message box keeps its own. A Completed one is
  thanked and asked for a Google review and a follow, using the branch's social media links
  (Settings → Organization → Branches); an Issues one is thanked for the prompt feedback, given its
  Feedback ID to quote, and told the team will sort it out. Both are new templates in Settings →
  Message Templates - Feedback Thank You and Feedback Issues, with a `{feedback id}` placeholder -
  and PROJECT → Feedback may now read message templates. No new permission.
  [FeedbackMessageDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackMessageDialog.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/feedback/service.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (adds the two templates; nothing to generate).
- **A branch now keeps its external and social media links.** Settings → Organization → Branches →
  Edit has an External URLs section - the Web URL, moved there from beside the Email, a new Location
  URL (the branch on a map) and the Google Review URL, each added with "+ Add external URL" (its
  Label a dropdown of the three not yet added, the button disabled once all three are) and each
  with a delete button - and below it a Social Media Links section
  with no fixed fields: "+ Add social media link" asks for a label (Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube, ...)
  and its link together and adds the row filled in - up to ten, each removable, the two sections one
  shared component - and the social media links are listed in the Feedback thank-you
  message under its label. Every new link is optional, checked
  loosely, refused if anything but http(s) comes before the address, and saved with https:// in
  front when typed without it. No new permission: the branch form is already behind SETTINGS →
  Organization. [BranchesPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/BranchesPanel.js),
  [validation.js](../backend/src/modules/admin/branches/validation.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate` (adds three columns to `branch`:
  `google_review_url`, `location_url` and `custom_social_links`).
- **Feedback is now given from the shoots waiting for it: Yet to be done lists every shoot
  Production has completed that nobody has reviewed yet.** Each sits at the top of the tab as the
  shoot and its project, with no review, and its ⋮ menu offers Give Feedback to a writer. The form
  states that shoot - its Shoot ID and Project Description - and asks only for the review and the
  feedback; the header's Add Feedback and its Shoot ID dropdown are gone, and `GET /feedback/options`
  now returns the reviews alone. Once saved, the feedback takes the shoot's place. No new permission
  and no migration: read under PROJECT → Feedback, and not narrowed to the reader's projects.
  [FeedbackPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackPage.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/feedback/service.js).
- **Feedback has a status bar: Yet to be done, Issues, Issues sorted, Completed and Rejected.**
  Project Management → Feedback now splits its table by status from tabs in the header, each with
  its count, and remembers the tab chosen. Feedback already given reads Yet to be done; new
  feedback is filed by its review (see the entry above). No new permission: the status is
  read under PROJECT → Feedback. [FeedbackPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackPage.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/feedback/service.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate` (adds `project_feedback.status`).
- **The client page now follows each shoot through production: plan pending, team on the way,
  team reached the shoot place, shoot started, shoot completed.** On the Production stage every
  shoot carries a timeline of those steps, each with when it happened, and its chip says where it
  stands now; a shoot the crew has paused or put on hold says Paused / On hold. The crew's other
  steps - the Pineapple meeting, Reached studio, Photo copy - and their remarks are not sent to the
  client, and a Rejected shoot status is not shown (it is still worked through). No new route or
  permission: it rides on the client's own `GET /api/client/project`, behind `requireClient`.
  [client/portal/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/controller.js),
  [projectTracking.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/projectTracking.mjs),
  [ShootTimeline.js](../frontend/src/components/client/ShootTimeline.js).
- **Signing in to the client page, and out of it, is a length of film drawn across the screen.**
  When a client signs in, dark film in the studio's colours - sprocket holes along its edges - slides
  down over the sign-in; the project page loads behind it, and once there is something to show the
  film runs on down and off it, uncovering the project as its strip winds in. Signing out goes the
  same way back, and the sign-in shown under it does not unroll its opening film again. The client
  never watches the project load. It lives in the client layout both pages share, which stays put
  between them; it never stays closed (it opens by itself after 8 seconds), and a device asking for
  less motion simply changes pages.
  [ClientCurtain.js](../frontend/src/components/client/ClientCurtain.js) (new),
  [app/client/layout.js](../frontend/src/app/client/layout.js),
  [ClientLoginForm.js](../frontend/src/components/client/ClientLoginForm.js),
  [ClientPortalPage.js](../frontend/src/components/client/ClientPortalPage.js).

- **The client sign-in opens on a roll of film unrolling into its place on the page.** Before the
  sign-in page, over a dark screen in the studio's colours, a roll of film - seen from above, a
  cylinder lying across the film with its sprocket holes turning as it goes - rests, rolled up,
  exactly where the sign-in page's own strip starts (nothing brings it in) and rolls along that
  strip's very track and tilt, laying the film
  out behind it, its frames developing as they are uncovered and the roll thinning as the film comes
  off. As it is spent past the strip's end the dark lifts off the page around the film, and the
  page's own strip, in exactly that place, drifts on from that frame. About two and a quarter
  seconds, with no words over it; a key ends it at once, a device asking for less motion goes
  straight to the page, and it never stays standing over the form even where the browser holds the
  animation back. The track is the page's strip as it is, read again if the page scrolls under it.
  [FilmSplash.js](../frontend/src/components/client/FilmSplash.js) (new),
  [ClientBackdrop.js](../frontend/src/components/client/ClientBackdrop.js) (new: the dark ground both share),
  [ClientAuthLayout.js](../frontend/src/components/client/ClientAuthLayout.js).

- **The client sign-in page's film strip carries the studio's own pictures, set in Settings →
  Project Management → Client page images.** A new **Project Management** group in Settings holds
  one screen, **Client page images**: up to 8 pictures, in order, picked or photographed the way
  Login Slide's are, and saved together. They are the client page's own - the staff sign-in keeps
  its Login Slide pictures, and the client strip no longer borrows them; with none set it shows
  plain frames in the studio's colours. Stored beside the login slides on the studio-wide settings
  row (new `client_login_slides` column), uploaded and compressed the same way, published on the
  public branding the sign-in page already reads, and edited through
  `GET`/`PUT /api/image-selection/settings/client-page-images`, which accepts that list and nothing
  else - and in it only pictures picked from a device (up to 5 MB each) or ones already saved, never
  a link to another site, since every client signing in loads them.
  [ClientAuthLayout.js](../frontend/src/components/client/ClientAuthLayout.js),
  [LoginSlidePanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/LoginSlidePanel.js) (`ClientPageImagesPanel`),
  [SettingsOverlay.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/SettingsOverlay.js),
  [client-page-images.routes.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/settings/client-page-images.routes.js).
  **Access:** a new permission, `SETTINGS / Client Page Images`, guards both the section and its
  endpoint, and the migration grants it to **SUPER_ADMIN only**. Whoever else keeps the client
  page's look - a Branch Admin, or a role that holds Login Slide - needs it ticked in Role
  Management and the role re-saved. **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then
  `npx prisma generate`.

- **Clients can follow their project on their portal.** The page opens on the studio's mark with
  **Sign out** beside it and goes straight to the project - no welcome card in between. The same
  five stages the studio's Edit Project → Status tab works out - read on the server with that tab's own rule
  (`sales/projects/stage.js`), so the client and the studio always see the same stage - with the
  current one marked and a card for it; on a phone the stages read down the screen as a timeline,
  from tablet width up they run across it. To the client the first stage is **Project**, whose
  card shows the status and the project's basic details (Event ID, name, branch, vertical, main
  event date, project manager). **Pre Production** shows the coordinator, creative manager, plans
  submitted, each shoot's plan (Plan submitted <day> / Awaiting plan), the **Welcome Gift** and the
  **Shoot Completed Gift** as Client Gifts tracks them (Yet To Sent / Sent / Received by Client,
  with the day); **Production** shows shoots finished; the Shoot Completed Gift stays on the cards
  after Pre Production. For a project whose CRD Document is Applicable, a **CRD Document** card:
  **Not started** until the studio sends it, then **Waiting for your details** (or **Started - not
  yet submitted** once a draft is saved) with a **Complete** button that opens the same form the
  WhatsApp link does, and **Form submitted** with the day. A client reads it from
  `GET /api/client/project`, for client accounts only (staff are refused): the project is found
  from the client's own account, never an id in the request, and only that is sent - no money,
  who converted or recorded the sale, update remarks, the crew's step names, phone numbers or
  quotation, the gifts' status and days but not who sends them, and the CRD form's link only while
  it is sent and not yet submitted. Rate-limited per account and never cached. No permission
  changed and no role needs re-saving.
  [ProjectTracker.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/ProjectTracker.js),
  [FilmStrip.js](../frontend/src/components/client/FilmStrip.js),
  [projectTracking.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/projectTracking.mjs),
  [ClientPortalPage.js](../frontend/src/components/client/ClientPortalPage.js),
  [client/portal/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/client/portal/controller.js),
  [authMiddleware.js](../backend/src/middleware/authMiddleware.js).
- **A client's own sign-in page, `/client/login`.** Where a client signs in with the username and
  password the studio sent on WhatsApp - the Client Login Credential message's `{login link}` now
  points here, and the client page's Sign out returns here. Built for the phone the message is
  opened on, from the shared `TextField` and `Button`: 16px, 48px-tall fields (smaller and iOS zooms
  in on focus), no autocapitalising or autocorrect on the username, `autocomplete` hints so a saved
  password fills in, Show password, safe-area padding for the notch and home bar, a smaller mark
  and no studio name on a short screen (a phone held sideways), and - from `lg` - the studio's login
  slides beside it through `AuthLayout`, as the studio's own sign-in has. Checked at 320, 360, 390,
  740×360, 768 and 1280 wide. It signs in client accounts only - a studio account is not kept and
  is pointed to the studio's page - says plainly when the details do not match or the login is
  switched off, and offers no reset or sign-up: "contact the studio". The client page now carries
  the studio's mark too
  ([ClientLoginForm.js](../frontend/src/components/client/ClientLoginForm.js),
  [page.js](../frontend/src/app/client/login/page.js)).
- **Create Project: a Project group, and Client Credentials - a client's own sign-in.** The rail
  now groups Project Details, Sales Remarks, Service Creation, Shedule Payment and Payment Received
  under **Project** (a scrolling grouped form now opens on its first section, with the group open -
  `SchemaFormPanel`). Below it, **Client Credentials**, modelled on Employee Preference →
  Credentials: a **Username** and a generated **Temporary Password** (Regenerate) - always made
  with the project, no switch, and **no email**: a client signs in by username. Saving the project
  makes the account in the project's own transaction - `role` CLIENT, no IAM roles, no email,
  linked by the new `user.client_project_id` (migration `20261001160000_user_client_project`: one
  nullable column, and `user.email` made nullable for logins without one), password bcrypt-hashed
  and only of the generated shape. **Client Login Ready** then opens - the shape of the Interview
  screen's Screening Form Ready and an employee's Login credentials created: the message in the
  shared `ShareableMessage` box with Copy message, and Close and **Send WhatsApp** in the footer,
  which sends from the sender's own WhatsApp to the project's client number
  (`POST /api/sales/projects/:id/client-login/whatsapp`). The wording is a new **Client Login
  Credentials** template in Settings → Message Templates (migration
  `20261001170000_client_login_message_template`, written only when absent; `{project name}`,
  `{username}`, `{password}`, `{login link}`), readable by User Management. **Edit Sale Details**
  has the same Project group and Client Credentials: a project with a client login shows its
  username and status (never the password); one booked without a login offers the same fields and
  **Create Client Login**, which makes it at once (`GET`/`POST /api/sales/projects/:id/client-login`,
  guarded like the edit, plus User Management) and opens Client Login Ready over the form. **A client keeps the
  password it is given**: `protect` lets a client token reach its own profile and nothing else -
  not the password change - the code-by-phone reset will not find a client, and the account is not
  marked to change it. The section and the server both require **`ADMIN / User Management`** at
  Read & Write - the permission an employee's credentials already need, so no new permission and no
  grant to change. A client signing in lands on `/client`: "your client portal is being set up" and
  Sign out - never the studio's shell. `protect` re-reads a client account on each request, and
  deleting the project sets the login INACTIVE. What a client sees of their project is to be built
  next. Username and email rules are now one set for employees and clients
  (`lib/loginCredentials.mjs`, `services/loginCredentials.js`). Editing a user in User Management
  now stores a blank email as none (NULL) rather than `""`
  ([CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js),
  [ClientCredentialsSection.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/ClientCredentialsSection.js),
  [ClientLoginReadyDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/ClientLoginReadyDialog.js),
  [ClientPortalPage.js](../frontend/src/components/client/ClientPortalPage.js),
  [authMiddleware.js](../backend/src/middleware/authMiddleware.js),
  [client-login.test.js](../backend/test/client-login.test.js)).
- **Project Management → Feedback: review a shoot.** A new **Feedback** entry sits at the end of
  Project Management in the sidebar, opening `/project-management/feedback`: a table of the feedback
  given on each shoot (Shoot ID, Project, Event ID, Event Date - the project's main event date,
  Shoot, Review, Feedback, Given By, Given On); clicking a row shows it in the info panel, and a
  double-click or the row's ⋮ **View** opens it in full (`RecordViewPanel`), both drawing
  `feedbackInfoSections` (the review, its shoot and its project),
  and an **Add Feedback** button in the header, styled as Raise Request is. The form asks for the
  **Shoot ID** (a searchable dropdown, newest shoot first), shows the **Project Description** of
  that shoot in the same card Cash Spent shows for one (`RecordSummaryCard`: Shoot, Shoot Date,
  Place, Event ID, Client Name, Project Status, Main Event Date, Branch, CRM - with a hint until a
  shoot is chosen), then a **Review** (Excellent, Good, Average, Poor) and the **Feedback** itself. A review is
  stored against the shoot's key in the new `project_feedback` table (migration
  `20261001140000_project_feedback`, a new empty table; the project is read through the shoot, not
  copied). Behind **PROJECT / Feedback** on both sides: `GET /api/project-management/feedback`,
  `GET …/feedback/options` and `POST …/feedback` mount `protect` and
  `requireModule("PROJECT", "Feedback")`. The Shoot ID dropdown offers **every** live shoot to
  everybody who can use the form, whoever's project it is (as Cash Spent's picker does). The table
  shows only the feedback the person gave, unless their role holds the new action permission
  **PROJECT / View All Feedback** (Role Management → Edit → Action permissions → Project
  Management), which shows everybody's feedback as far as that role's branches reach - all of it
  for a Super Admin. Added by migration `20261001150000_project_view_all_feedback_permission` and
  the catalogue; **only Super Admin holds it** - tick it for the roles that should see everybody's
  feedback, such as managers reviewing their team's. Read shows the list; Add Feedback is drawn only at Read & Write. The permission is
  added by migration `20261001130000_project_feedback_permission` as well as the catalogue, since
  the seed cannot run on production. **Only Super Admin reaches it**; tick it for the roles that
  should see Feedback in Administration → Roles and re-save them
  ([FeedbackPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackPage.js),
  [FeedbackFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/FeedbackFormPanel.js),
  [feedbackConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/feedbackConfig.js),
  [feedback/service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/feedback/service.js),
  [project-feedback.test.js](../backend/test/project-feedback.test.js)).

- **Create Project can be saved as a draft and finished later.** The form now has **Save Draft**
  beside Save Project, wherever it opens - a CRM conversion, New Project, or a quotation. It keeps
  the half-filled booking in this browser for five days from its last save, for the person who
  saved it. **Drafts** on Bookings & Converted - shown only while there is a draft - lists them with
  when each was saved and the day it will be gone, to open or delete. One draft per enquiry: the
  moment an enquiry with a draft is chosen on the form - picked, or arriving with a converted lead or
  a quotation - it asks **Use draft** or **Create new**; a new one deletes the old draft when the
  project is saved.
  Receipt files picked under Payment Received are not kept and are chosen again. Reopened service
  and deliverable rows are matched against today's master data, so a retired one is dropped and
  said so. Nothing is written to the server and no permission is new - it sits behind `SALES /
  Sales Manager` at Read / Write like the form itself.
  [lib/projectDrafts.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/projectDrafts.mjs),
  [ProjectDraftsDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/ProjectDraftsDialog.js),
  `test/project-drafts.test.mjs`.

- **Employee dropdowns show each person's face beside their name.** Every form picker that chooses
  an employee or user - CRM Assign To, meeting and interview guests, a project's coordinators,
  pre-production and production crew, asset assignees, task assignees, interviewers, Reports To and
  Referred By, credential approvers, Paid By, sheet assignment rules, a role's users, user linking
  and the attendance report sender - now draws their profile photo, or their initials on a fixed
  colour, in each row, on the chosen value and on multi-select chips. `Dropdown`,
  `MultiSelectField` and `EmailChipsField` take an optional `avatar` on an option, built by
  [lib/employeeAvatar.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/employeeAvatar.mjs). The employee list endpoints
  behind those pickers now return `profilePhotoUrl`, passed through `listPhotoUrl` in
  [employeeOptionLists.js](../backend/src/services/employeeOptionLists.js): only a stored URL is
  sent, never a photo held inline as a `data:` URI, so a list of every employee cannot balloon -
  such a person shows initials until object storage holds their photo. Table filters are unchanged.
  No permission or route guard changed.

- **A branch is paid into as many bank accounts as it holds.** Settings → Organization → Branches
  takes a list where it took one account: **+ Add Account** for the next, Remove for one that is
  gone, and each row asking for the holder, the bank and branch, the account number and the IFSC -
  all four, because an account missing one cannot be paid into. The order is the studio's: the first
  account is the one the branch leads with, and the client's quotation payment page prints a **Bank
  Transfer card per account** in that order, each with its own copy controls. A number another
  branch already holds is still refused, now against the row that holds it, and the same number
  twice in one list is refused as a pasted row. A branch's row in the register lists every account
  it holds rather than the first. UPI IDs and the Payment QR are unchanged, and stay on the branch.
  [BranchesPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/BranchesPanel.js),
  [branches/validation.js](../backend/src/modules/admin/branches/validation.js),
  [branches/service.js](../backend/src/modules/admin/branches/service.js),
  [PublicQuotationPaymentPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/PublicQuotationPaymentPage.js).
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate`. The migration creates
  `branch_bank_account`, copies each branch's existing account into the first row of its list, and
  **then drops the four `bank_*` columns from `branch`** - rehearse it on a copy of the database
