  first, since that last step cannot be undone. A branch that held only an account number arrives
  with the other three blank and the register will ask for them the next time it is saved.
  **Access:** no new permission - the same `ADMIN / Branch` endpoints.

- **CRM & Leads has a Board view: the same leads stood up in columns by status.** The switch beside
  My Leads chooses Table or Board and is remembered per person. Each column is one status - led by
  the leads nobody has rung yet, and, for somebody who hands work out, the leads nobody owns - with
  its count in the heading, the columns in the pipeline's own order, and each column paging itself as it is
  scrolled rather than asking to be pressed. It is the reader's own board: it obeys My Leads, the
  vertical, the tab, the filters and the date range exactly as the table does, so an individual sees
  the leads named to them and nothing else (the unowned column is not offered to them, since those
  are not theirs to work).

  Dragging a card to a column opens that lead with the target status already chosen, so the save
  that follows is the ordinary one - it still refuses without a remark, and the register still says
  why the lead moved. That holds for **Converted** and **Converted & Followup** too: the lead opens
  at that status, the required fields and the remark are asked for where they always are, and once
  Update has saved it the page asks whether to open Create Project on it now - *Not now* leaves a
  lead that is converted and not yet booked, which Bookings & Converted can pick up later. A lead
  with no owner is not dragged at all. **The board scrolls itself while a card is held near either edge**, faster the
  nearer the edge and at the same speed the data table's columns scroll at, so the statuses off the
  right of the screen can be reached - a browser scrolls nothing for a drag on its own, and both
  hands are busy holding the card. **Esc puts the card down**, as does letting go of it anywhere; a
  card carried out of the browser window stops the scroll and can be dropped into nothing, so it
  simply comes back.
  [CrmKanbanBoard.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CrmKanbanBoard.js),
  [CRMPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CRMPage.js).
  **Access:** no new permission - the board reads the same `CRM:Leads` endpoint the table does, so
  anybody who can see the list can see it in columns.

- **Pre Production can import the studio's old pre production sheet, one template per vertical.**
  The ⋮ in the board's header offers Import (Dum Dum, Qua Qua and Corp each on their own board,
  all three on the combined one). One row per shoot: each booking and shoot is created with the
  app's own Event ID and Shoot ID - which carry the vertical and branch the sheet's numbers lack -
  while the sheet's IDs are kept beside them, so uploading the file again fills in what was left
  blank instead of creating copies. People are given by Employee Code and shown by name; dates are
  DD-MM-YYYY and times HH:MM, both said in the dialog. The bookings carry no enquiry, as the old
  sheet has none. A second upload reaches only projects the importer could edit, names people only
  where nobody is named yet and never changes a status; a client already in the app - the same
  client number, or the same client name as written, ignoring capitals and spacing - is refused
  rather than duplicated.
  [importColumns.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/importColumns.js),
  [import.service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/import.service.js),
  [PreProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionPage.js),
  [ImportMenuButton.js](../frontend/src/components/data-table/ImportMenuButton.js).
  Needs both `PROJECT / Pre Production` and `SALES / Sales Manager` at Read / Write - no new
  permission. **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (migration `20261006120000_add_sheet_ids`:
  two nullable unique columns), then `npx prisma generate`.

- **Project Management → Shoot Board: a timeline of your shoots by project.** Projects run down the
  left, days across the top, and each project's shoots are bars in its colour; shoots on the same or
  consecutive days join into one bar, which lists its shoots when tapped. It scrolls sideways
  through the range and the project column follows the days on screen; ‹ › scroll a day, and an
  empty stretch offers a jump to the previous or next shoot. Filter by dates (next 30 days, next 3
  months, this week, this month, next month, or from–to up to 92 days) and by project, with Clear.
  A shoot is on it when you or anybody reporting to you is named on it in any role — Project Manager, Pre Production
  Coordinator, Creative Manager, Production Manager, Post Production Coordinator, Production
  Coordinator, the production team or crew. A Super Admin and Show All Projects see every shoot;
  shoots with no date are left off. Its colours (each project's chip, today, the empty stretch, the card outline) are defined for Light, Dark and Enhanced dark in `globals.css` (`.shoot-chip`, `.shoot-hue-*`), since the dark tiers do not repaint those hues. A shoot opens its production panel for anybody holding Production. New permission **`PROJECT / Shoot
  Board`**, in the catalogue and in **migration** `20261005130000_shoot_board_permission`, granted
  to `SUPER_ADMIN` only — the studio may want to grant it in Role Management to the roles of
  Project Managers, Pre Production Coordinators, Creative Managers, Production Managers and
  Coordinators, and Post Production Coordinators. `npx prisma migrate deploy` on the VPS.
  [ShootBoardPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/shoot-board/ShootBoardPage.js),
  [read.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/shoot-board/read.js).
- **The client's quotation says how long its link still opens.** A small gold status chip in the
  bottom-right corner of a quotation link - clear of Download, which keeps the top right - reads the
  time left to the minute on two short lines, "Expires in 3d" over a slightly bolder "22h 39m"
  ("Expires in" over "12h 45m" on the last day, "42m" in the last hour), a unit left out where it is
  nought, no seconds and no date, so it stays narrow on a phone. It floats (12px from the edges, or
  the device's safe area where that is larger), takes no room in the page, and turns over every
  minute without a refresh. It is read from the link's stored expiry, the date the server checks
  ([expiredLink.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/expiredLink.mjs) `linkTimeLeft`, which also hands the two
  lines over as `lead` and `rest`), and is information only: a lapsed link is still refused by the
  server and shows the existing expired page, unchanged, and a link with no expiry shows no chip.
  The proposal header is unchanged, and the chip is not printed in the PDF
  ([PublicQuotationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/PublicQuotationPage.js)).

- **A quotation shoot can carry Additional Text beside its name.** Add Shoot in the Quotation
  Generator has an optional **Additional Text** section just above Mark as Main Event, with one box
  per selected shoot ("e.g. Bride Varatham") - so Bride Haldi, Bride Making and Reception chosen
  together each get their own, kept while shoots are added to or removed from the selection; the rest
  of the popup is unchanged. Each shoot is then shown as "Rituals (Bride Varatham)" on its card in the generator, on the client's quotation and in
  its PDF, through one helper ([shootDisplay.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/shootDisplay.mjs)). It is saved
  on the shoot as `customText`, apart from the shoot's own name, so the Event Type header, packages
  and pricing still read "Rituals"; it is trimmed, empty is saved as null (clearing it on an edit
  removes it), and the same shoot can be added twice with different text. It goes with the quotation
  through edit, new versions and duplicate. A quotation without it reads as before, and the project
  screens' Add Shoot is unchanged - a project's shoots have no such field, so booking a quotation into
  a project keeps the shoot's name without the text
  ([AddShootDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/AddShootDialog.js)).

- **Attendance logins now last 24 hours, a login never logged out of becomes an Incorrect Login,
  and any day's status can be corrected through a request.** A login stays open for exactly 24 hours from the
  latest login - 9:30 can be logged out of until 9:29 the next morning, across midnight, where a
  logout after midnight used to be refused. Past that with no logout, the day reads as **Incorrect
  login** (it replaces Missed checkout, which was decided at midnight): it is not attended and not
  paid as present, it has its own **Incorrect Login** card on the attendance dashboard, and it never
  blocks the next login. Raise Request gains a fourth type, **Correction**: pick a date, see that
  day's current status as the server reads it (Present, Absent, Half day, Early exit, Late, On leave
  or Incorrect Login - not editable), choose what it should be from a searchable list (Present,
  Absent, Half day, Early exit, Late, On leave - never Incorrect Login, and never the status it
  already is), give a reason; it goes to the same approvers as a permission. A holiday, a weekly off
  or a day still logged in cannot be corrected, and the form says why. Only once the request is
  approved does the day change - an absence corrected to Present needs no login behind it and none
  is invented - and the dashboard, register and payroll then read the new status; a day that has
  changed since the request was raised is refused rather than overwritten. Rejected or still
  pending, the day is unchanged. The "needs attention" banner now opens this request. Leave, Permission and Comp-off are
  unchanged, and so is every day already logged out
  ([attendanceRules.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/attendanceRules.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/controller.js),
  [AttendanceRequestFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestFormPanel.js)).
  **Pay effect:** a day left logged in past 24 hours in an open pay period now counts as absent in
  the attendance calculator until a request corrects it; before, it counted as present.
  **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy` (migration `20260930120000_attendance_incorrect_login`
  adds three nullable columns and the `attendance_status_override` table, rewrites no row), then
  `npx prisma generate`. No new permission: the
  request rides the existing attendance request routes and approvers.
- **The Attendance Register greets the day's birthdays and wedding anniversaries.** Above the
  filters, a line for each - "Birthday today: Asha", "Wedding anniversaries on 28 Sep: Ravi, Meena" -
  among the people working here (active and not archived, on the roster that day, in the chosen
  branch), matched on month and day. Names only: no year of birth or marriage leaves the server, and
  a 29 February birthday is marked on the 28th in other years. The box is always there: a day with
  neither reads "No birthdays or wedding anniversaries today". The register now also answers
  `celebrations: { birthdays, anniversaries }`
  ([service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js),
  [AttendanceRegisterPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRegisterPage.js)).
- **Settings → Employee → Attendance calculator is now the pay period and its payback day, in one
  row, and nothing else.** **Start date**, **End date** and **Payback date** sit side by side (one
  above the other on a phone); the employee picker, the Current / Previous cycle buttons and every
  result (the day tiles, payable days, salary and the rules list) are gone. The payback day is the
  day of **every** month salary is paid out - "10th of every month" by default, any day 1st-31st, a
  day past a short month's end meaning its last day - so it is not set again each month. It is a
  **date picker like Start date and End date**, labelled Payback date, showing the next payback
  date (e.g. 2026-10-10) with "Repeats on the 10th of every month" beneath; picking a date keeps
  only its day, which repeats monthly, and clearing it goes back to the 10th. All three
  are saved on the studio's HR settings the moment they change: nullable `pay_period_start` and
  `pay_period_end`, and `payback_day` (default 10) on `hrm_settings` (migrations
  `20260928140000_hrm_pay_period` and `20260928160000_hrm_payback_day`, the second replacing a
  single payback date with the day). Until a period is saved the dates offer the 25th to the next
  month's 25th. Refused: an end before the start, a period over 45 days, a payback day outside 1-31.
  `GET` / `PUT /api/hrm/attendance/calculator/period` (`{ from, to, paybackDay }`) - Read on `HRM /
  Attendance Calculator` to see, Read / Write to change; the fields are read-only without Write. The
  separate, empty **Payback Date** page under Settings → Employee is removed. The per-employee
  calculation described in the next entry stays on the server (`/calculator`,
  `/calculator/employees`) but no screen reads it now. **Deploy:** `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then
  `npx prisma generate`.

- **Settings → Employee → Attendance calculator works out a pay period's payable days and salary.**
  An administrator picks an employee (searchable) and a **start and end date** - set to the studio's
  pay cycle, the **25th of one month to the 25th of the next**, with **Current** and **Previous**
  cycle buttons, and either date can be changed - and sees the period's working days, present,
  absent, on leave, half days, late marks and holidays and weekly offs, then the **payable days**
  and, from the salary on the Employee Repository record, the **payable salary**. Read-only -
  nothing is saved. The rules are fixed and printed on the page: salary per day is the monthly
  salary over the days in the period (both dates counted), so a full period with nothing missed
  pays the salary; each absence is a day's loss of pay and each half day half of one; approved
  leave, comp-offs, **approved on-duty days**, holidays and weekly offs are paid; **late marks take
  nothing off**; a day logged in but not logged out counts as present; and working a holiday or
  weekly off does not cancel an absence (a comp-off gives the day back). Each day is classified
  once, from its kind and status (`tallyDays`), so the counts always add up to the days counted -
  not from the range totals, which work absences out as working days less logins less leave and so
  let a worked Sunday cancel a weekday absence and counted a login on a leave day twice. The salary
  lines add up on the page: for a period still running or joined part-way, a "For N days counted"
  line shows what the deduction comes off, and earned less deduction is always the payable to the
  paisa. Every line follows from the per-day rate as shown, rounded to the paisa - the deduction is
  that rate times the days lost, so a rate of ₹967.74 never sits above a deduction of ₹967.75 - and
  a whole period with nothing lost is the monthly salary exactly. Counting
  starts at the date of joining where that falls inside the period, and a period still running is
  counted up to yesterday ("Payable so far"). A period is at most 45 days - one pay cycle. With no
  salary on record the days are still worked out. New `GET
  /api/hrm/attendance/calculator/employees` and `GET
  /api/hrm/attendance/calculator?employeeId=&from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD`, both refused to
  anybody but an administrator (they read salaries)
  ([calculator.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/calculator.js),
  [AttendanceCalculatorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/AttendanceCalculatorPanel.js),
  [SettingsOverlay.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/SettingsOverlay.js)). No migration.

- **Settings has an Employee group, and Employee Referral sits inside it.** The Settings rail's
  **Employee Referral** moved into a new **Employee** group, under the same permissions as before
  (`HRM / Employee Referral` with `SETTINGS / Employee Referral`), so everybody who could reach it
  still can - through the group. Beside it, for an administrator alone, are **Attendance
  calculator** and **Payback Date**, empty for now ("Nothing to set here yet"): the places those
  settings will go. Somebody with neither the referral's permissions nor the administrator does not
  see the group at all. Who is an administrator - a
  Super Admin, or a role with the Administrator tick - is the server's answer: `GET /api/user/permissions` now also answers
  `isAdministrator` (the same `services/administrator.js` check the attendance rules use), and
  `usePermissions()` exposes it to any screen that belongs to administrators alone
  ([SettingsOverlay.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/SettingsOverlay.js),
  [PermissionsProvider.js](../frontend/src/components/auth/PermissionsProvider.js)). No new
  permission, no migration.
- **Raise Request is in the account menu too.** The menu under your name has a **Raise Request**
  item, below My Profile, opening the same form as the Request screen's Raise Request - leave,
  permission or comp-off - over whatever page you are on, with the same checks and the same
  refusals on the form. The Request screen keeps its own button. Shown to anybody holding
  `HRM / Requests` or `HRM / Employee Attendance`, the two permissions the request routes accept
  ([RaiseRequestLauncher.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/RaiseRequestLauncher.js)); no backend
  change.
- **A new post on HRM → Events rings the bell.** Posting an event writes a stored notification -
  "New event: *title*", with the event's day and who posted it, opening HRM → Events - to every
  active login holding `HRM / Events` at Read or above, bar the poster
  ([eventNotifications.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/events/eventNotifications.js)). It is the
  existing bell's stored half (new type `EVENT_POSTED`, gated in `TYPE_PERMISSIONS` on
  `HRM / Events`), so it keeps its read state across devices and nobody who cannot open Events is
  told about a post. Written after the reply, so posting is no slower; removing an event deletes
  its notifications. No migration and no new permission: the roles that already reach Events are
  the ones told.

- **Every project has a Status tab showing which stage it is at** — in Start / Edit Project and in
  the record a double-click opens on the Projects page. Beside Details and
  Payments, a track walks Project started → Pre Production → Production → Post Production →
  Delivered, each marked done, in progress or not started yet. Clicking a stage shows its details:
  who converted the project, when and for how much; who runs each later stage; and each shoot's
  plan and production step. A stopped
  project (On Hold, Rejected, Cancelled…) shows a banner above it. Read under `PROJECT /
  Projects`. **In Edit Project a stage can be updated from here:** Update opens that stage's own
  editor on top, each with a ← back arrow — the project's details (as a panel of their own, not the
  Details tab), the Pre Production shoot cards and forms, or a shoot's Production — so a save is the same save those screens make and shows everywhere; Back returns to
  Status. When something was changed, a required remark is asked on the way back and listed under
  the stage as its Updates history. Update shows only to holders of `PROJECT / Pre Production` or
  `PROJECT / Production` at Read / Write; the remark is written behind the started-project editor
  guards. Post Production and Delivered have no editor yet. The double-click record stays
  read-only. **Migration** `20261001120000_project_stage_update` adds `project_stage_update`; run
  `npx prisma migrate deploy` on the VPS — no permission or seed change.
  [ProjectStageView.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectStageView.js),
  [PreProductionProjectEditor.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionProjectEditor.js),
  [StageUpdateRemarkDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/StageUpdateRemarkDialog.js),
  [stage.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/stage.js).

- **Production is a working board: a per-shoot plan for the Production Manager and a step-by-step
  day for the Production Coordinator, with WhatsApp updates to the project's group.** Each shoot of a
  started project that has a Production Manager gets a production record. The manager saves or
  submits the plan; the coordinator named in it works through Started from studio → Reached shoot
  place → Pineapple meeting → Shoot started → Shoot status → Reached studio → Photo copy, strictly in
  order, from the phone; Started from studio and Reached shoot place each need a photo. The
  Production Manager or a Super Admin may complete the current step on the coordinator's behalf,
  with the same photo and remark checks, logged under their own name. Whoever holds `PROJECT /
  Show All Projects` at Read / Write works every shoot as a Super Admin does (plan and steps), and
  every project on the Pre Production board too; at Read it shows every shoot on the Production
  board. A shoot's **Activity** tab is shown only to the Production Manager and above (Super Admin,
  Show All Projects at Read / Write), like the WhatsApp status; the coordinator does not see it, and
  `GET /shoots/:shootId/activity` refuses them (403). They still need `PROJECT / Pre Production` and `PROJECT / Production` to reach those
  screens. Started
  from studio, Reached shoot place and setting the shoot status to
  Completed each ask first, then post to the project's WhatsApp group, which is linked on Pre
  Production → General and sent from the linker's WhatsApp; a failed send never blocks the step, is
  said to the coordinator at once, and the step stays open showing "Not sent · Retry". A plan keeps
  a camera, vendor, team member or coordinator retired since it was planned, and still saves. Each
  service booked on the shoot gets its own person and camera on the plan, and a candid service two
  assistants as well. The three message
  wordings are in Settings → Templates. Built for the phone first: the
  shoot full-screen, the step's action in a bar at the bottom, and photos that fail to upload stay
  on the phone with Retry. **The Production Coordinator moved from pre production to the production plan:** the pre
  production shoot form no longer asks for it, and a shoot's existing answer is carried over once,
  as the plan's starting coordinator, when its production record is raised (the old columns stay
  until a later migration drops them). **Travel moved the same way:** the plan asks Travel Mode —
  Bus, Train, Flight, Own, **Car** (new), Office Vehicle or Other — and only the detail that mode
  uses: tickets for Bus / Train / Flight, a vehicle number plate (upper-cased) for Own / Car, an
  Asset Management vehicle for Office Vehicle, a line for Other. A draft may leave it empty;
  submitting needs it. Changing the mode clears the detail that no longer applies; tickets already
  added are kept under "From the earlier travel mode", and new ones are accepted only while the
  mode is Bus, Train or Flight — picking it is enough, the ticket upload itself sets it on the
  plan. Pre production's shoot form no longer asks it, and a shoot's earlier
  answer is carried over once to the plan; its `travel_*` columns stay, deprecated, and go with the
  coordinator columns in the same follow-up migration. `StepRail` moved to `components/shared`.
  [production/](../backend/src/modules/project-management/production/),
  [ProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/production/ProductionPage.js),
  [ProjectWhatsappGroupField.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectWhatsappGroupField.js).
  **Roles:** `PROJECT / Production` already exists and no permission row is added. Grant it
  **Read / Write** to the roles held by Production Managers and Production Coordinators in Admin →
  Role Management and **re-save those roles**; linking the group needs `PROJECT / Pre Production`
  Read / Write, which pre production roles already hold.
  **Deploy:** three migrations (`20260930120000_production_stage`,
  `20260930130000_production_message_reason`, `20260930140000_production_travel`); rehearse on a
  copy of production, then `npx prisma migrate deploy` and `npx prisma generate`. Production
  records appear for a project the next time it is saved or gets a shoot.

- **Company Given Number - an optional company-issued phone, distinct from an employee's own
  Contact Number.** On the public onboarding form (most candidates do not have one yet, so it is the
  one phone field there that is not required) and on Employee Details' Personal Details, right
  beside Contact Number; shown back on My Profile like every other onboarding answer. Validated the
  same way every other phone number on the record is when one is given.
  [schema.prisma](../backend/prisma/schema.prisma),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/employees/controller.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/onboarding-invites/controller.js),
  [onboardingFormConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/onboardingFormConfig.js),
  [EmployeeFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeFormPanel.js). **Deploy:**
  `npx prisma migrate deploy`, then `npx prisma generate`.

- **A departing employee's direct reports move up to that employee's own manager**, rather than
  being left pointing at somebody no longer working here. This happens the moment they stop working
  here - offboarded through Separations, deleted/archived from the Employee Repository, or Employment
  Status edited on their record to anything outside Active/in Training/PIP - and it refuses the
  whole change, naming how many reports, when the employee had nobody above them to move those
  reports up to: HR reassigns them to another manager first, rather than the reports being left
  rootless automatically. [reportingLine.js](../backend/src/services/reportingLine.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/separations/controller.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/employees/controller.js). No migration.

- **A module with a long list of sub-modules now carries its own search once it is open**, in Role
  Management's Add/Edit Role and Admin Permissions panels — CRM Leads, Asset Management and the
  like, where scrolling to find one sub-module was slower than the page-wide search that opens the
  module in the first place. The two are independent: the page-wide search still decides which
  modules are worth opening, and a module's own search only narrows its own rows once it is. Closes
  itself when the module is put away.
  [RoleDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/admin/RoleDialog.js)
- **Speak-up: a confidential line to HR**, inside Employee Attendance's own section dropdown. An
  employee picks a type (Team / Manager Issue, HR / People, Work Environment, Suggestion, App /
  System Issue, Other), writes a subject and what happened, and may attach one file — sent only to
  HR, never to their manager or coworkers, and they can see their own past ones from the same
  section. `HRM / Speak-up` (submit + your own history) reaches every role that already holds
  `HRM / Employee Attendance` at any level — in effect, every employee role, since that's how anyone
  raises their own leave/permission request — and the Branch Admin permission set, so a branch admin
  can submit their own too. `HRM / Speak-up Review` (read everyone's, studio-wide) is granted only to
  roles that hold `HRM / Employee Management` at Read/Write — HR — and to SUPER_ADMIN; Branch Admin
  does not get it, because the inbox is confidential to HR. Re-save any role in Role Management
  whose grants should change. An attachment is at most 5MB and must be a PDF, PNG/JPEG/WebP image,
  Word document or text file.
  [SpeakUpPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/SpeakUpPanel.js),
  [SpeakUpReviewPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/SpeakUpReviewPanel.js),
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/speak-up/controller.js)

  anybody but an administrator (they read salaries)
  ([calculator.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/calculator.js),
  [AttendanceCalculatorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/AttendanceCalculatorPanel.js),
  [SettingsOverlay.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/SettingsOverlay.js)). No migration.

- **Settings has an Employee group, and Employee Referral sits inside it.** The Settings rail's
  **Employee Referral** moved into a new **Employee** group, under the same permissions as before
  (`HRM / Employee Referral` with `SETTINGS / Employee Referral`), so everybody who could reach it
  still can - through the group. Beside it, for an administrator alone, are **Attendance
  calculator** and **Payback Date**, empty for now ("Nothing to set here yet"): the places those
  settings will go. Somebody with neither the referral's permissions nor the administrator does not
  see the group at all. Who is an administrator - a
  Super Admin, or a role with the Administrator tick - is the server's answer: `GET /api/user/permissions` now also answers
  `isAdministrator` (the same `services/administrator.js` check the attendance rules use), and
  `usePermissions()` exposes it to any screen that belongs to administrators alone
  ([SettingsOverlay.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/SettingsOverlay.js),
  [PermissionsProvider.js](../frontend/src/components/auth/PermissionsProvider.js)). No new
  permission, no migration.
- **Raise Request is in the account menu too.** The menu under your name has a **Raise Request**
  item, below My Profile, opening the same form as the Request screen's Raise Request - leave,
  permission or comp-off - over whatever page you are on, with the same checks and the same
  refusals on the form. The Request screen keeps its own button. Shown to anybody holding
  `HRM / Requests` or `HRM / Employee Attendance`, the two permissions the request routes accept
  ([RaiseRequestLauncher.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/RaiseRequestLauncher.js)); no backend
  change.
- **A new post on HRM → Events rings the bell.** Posting an event writes a stored notification -
  "New event: *title*", with the event's day and who posted it, opening HRM → Events - to every
  active login holding `HRM / Events` at Read or above, bar the poster
  ([eventNotifications.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/events/eventNotifications.js)). It is the
  existing bell's stored half (new type `EVENT_POSTED`, gated in `TYPE_PERMISSIONS` on
  `HRM / Events`), so it keeps its read state across devices and nobody who cannot open Events is
  told about a post. Written after the reply, so posting is no slower; removing an event deletes
  its notifications. No migration and no new permission: the roles that already reach Events are
  the ones told.

- **Lost thumbnails and previews can be put back without re-running the pipeline.**
  `npm run recover:derivatives -- --project <id>` (`--all`, `--apply`, `--force`, `--list`;
  [scripts/recoverImageSelectionDerivatives.js](../backend/scripts/recoverImageSelectionDerivatives.js))
  is a dry run by default. With `--apply` it rebuilds, for each READY photo whose object is gone
  from R2 and whose original this server can read, only the missing thumbnail or preview - rendered
  by the same `renderDerivatives` the processing worker now shares - and writes it under the key
  already on the row, so no database row changes and no selection, link, folder, album version or
  face record is touched; the face scan is not told and nothing is queued, which a test pins by
  checking the recovery module loads neither the hook nor the pipeline. Each rebuilt object is
  fetched back from its public URL and counts only on 200 image bytes. Photos registered from the
  desktop or uploaded by the browser drop zone have no original on the server and are counted as
  skipped-unavailable. An apply first reads the bucket's lifecycle rules: an enabled expiry rule over
  the photo-selection root - what emptied it - blocks the run, as do rules the token cannot read,
  unless `--force` is passed after checking the Cloudflare dashboard. Counts printed: missing,
  rebuildable, rebuilt, skipped-unavailable, failed.

- **A read-only audit of which Image Selection photos still have their thumbnail and preview in
  the bucket.** `node backend/scripts/auditImageSelectionDerivatives.js` (`--project <id>`,
  `--list`) lists the photo-selection root of R2 once, checks every READY photo's two keys against
  it, and prints per project how many are whole, how many have lost an object, and whether this
  server could rebuild each lost one from an original it can reach or the photo has to come back
  through the desktop app or the browser. It also prints the oldest object still under the root.
  Written while tracing broken previews: the gallery API composes a correct public URL from the key
  on every row and never exposes an original path, and the same code serves the photos processed on
  2026-09-29 - the objects behind every older key were simply gone from the bucket, with nothing
  older than 2026-09-21 left under the photo-selection and album-proof roots and no code path that
  deletes by prefix. The script writes nothing, deletes nothing and queues nothing; `r2.listKeys`
  is the one addition to [storage/r2.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/storage/r2.js).

- **Album Proofing has a dashboard, on the web and the desktop, in the Image Selection dashboard's
  family.** Album Proofing → Dashboard (the sidebar entry now lands there, with Projects one switch
  away in the header) shows every album proof as it stands: ten cards — Total Albums, Draft, Ready
  for QC, QC Review, Corrections Open, Ready for Revised Version, Ready for Client, Client Review,
  Link Expiring Soon, Completed — each a filter on the Recent Albums table beneath (album and
  project, client, version, status, open corrections, a workflow progress bar, the client link's
  state and last activity, with the standard filter row and sorting); then QC & Correction Progress
  (the albums in a correction round, resolved over raised, and whether the revised upload is
  unlocked) beside Proofing & Link Status (active, expiring, expired and revoked links, who is in
  client review and on which version, client approved, open corrections by state, processing,
  archived). The range picker scopes the caption's period figures — albums created, sent to QC, sent
  to clients, completed — and the arrows on the two cards whose past the rows still hold. A row
  opens the album; New Project goes to the Projects page. One request feeds both clients
  (`GET /api/image-selection/album-proofs/dashboard?range=`), so the web and the desktop can never
  show different figures, and nothing on either decides a state: the counts read the album's status,
  the gate is `revisionGate.js`'s own answer and the link state the publication card's. Reads with
  `IMAGE_SELECTION / Album Proofing` or `Album Proofing QC` at READ, as the album list does — no new
  permission, nothing to re-grant; the web page keeps the Album Proofing route permission the
  Projects page beside it has. The QC flow, versions, corrections, publication and expiry rules are
  untouched ([AlbumProofingDashboardPage.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/album-proofing/dashboard/AlbumProofingDashboardPage.js),
  [dashboard.service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/album-proofs/dashboard.service.js)).
- **The desktop app's Automatic face-processing mode can now tell whether this server's own
  engine is answering.** `GET /api/desktop/capabilities` carries `serverEngineReady`, read off the
  engine's own health in the process that runs the AI worker (no spawn, no wait); the desktop reads
  it to leave the work to the server when it is online and to describe photos itself when it is
  not. Before, the key was never sent and Automatic behaved like Local Only
  ([service.js](../backend/src/modules/desktop/service.js)).
- **`npm run prisma:generate` now works while the backend is running on Windows.** A plain
  `npx prisma generate` fails with `EPERM: operation not permitted, rename ...query_engine-windows.dll.node`
  whenever `npm run dev` is up, because the running server holds the query engine DLL, and every
  failed attempt left a 21 MB `.tmp<pid>` copy of the engine in `node_modules/.prisma/client` (63 of
  them, 1.3 GB, on one machine). The script behind the command
  ([scripts/prismaGenerate.js](../backend/scripts/prismaGenerate.js)) stops only this backend's dev
  tree first - nodemon, `src/server.js`, the dev Redis and their wrappers, never the frontend or the
  desktop app - runs generate, sweeps the leftover copies, and says to start the server again with
  `npm run dev`. It never touches the database. On Linux and macOS nothing is stopped.

- **AI Feature → Media uploads straight from the workspace, and photos are optimized before they
  leave the computer.** Open a folder and its upload area is right there - the same "Drop your
  photo folders here" with Choose Photos and Choose Folder that Photo Selection has - with no
  dialog at any step. Each photo is compressed in a background worker to the event's preview recipe
  (2048 px JPEG by default, the frame the face engine reads; originals never leave the machine),
  then sent four at a time with retries. The progress sits under the drop zone: photos, optimized
  size, Preparing / Compressing / Uploading / Completed / Failed, with Pause, Resume, Retry failed
  uploads and Cancel remaining, and every file's line (8.5 MB → 620 KB · Complete) behind Show files,
  windowed so ten thousand rows stay light. Leaving the tab or the page changes nothing about the
  upload: a small card bottom-left follows you around the app and brings you back - on the same
  event's other tabs too, since the event page keeps its tab out of the address. A failed send
  waits its second or three before the photo goes again rather than trying at once, and Retry
  failed uploads never touches a photo you cancelled. One failed photo
  never stops the rest; a photo already in the event says "Already uploaded" instead of becoming a
  second row; subfolder paths and each photo's capture time are kept. The grid fills in as photos
  land, without a reload; face recognition queues as before, once the optimized file is stored
  ([AiMediaUploadWorkspace.js](../frontend/src/components/ai-feature/media-upload/components/AiMediaUploadWorkspace.js),
  [uploadEngine.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/aiMediaUpload/uploadEngine.mjs); the server side is
  exercised on real bytes in
  [ai-feature-media-upload-service.test.js](../backend/test/ai-feature-media-upload-service.test.js)).
  Image Selection's uploader is untouched. Reached by the roles that already reach AI Feature uploads.
- **Event Default Settings has a Media Upload section, and every event carries its own copy of it:
  how a photo is compressed before it is stored.** Image compression on or off, preview quality
  (84) and max dimension (2048 px), thumbnail size (480 px) and format (WebP or JPEG), how many
  photos are uploaded (4) and compressed (3) at once, and whether the camera's metadata is kept on
  the preview (camera make, model, lens and capture times only - location and everything else
  embedded are never written to a preview, because previews are public; off, only the capture time
  is kept, as its own field), with Restore recommended defaults. The recommended values are the recipe the AI Feature has
  always derived, so nothing looks different until somebody changes it. The browser's worker, the
  desktop and the server all read the same keys: the server derives a photo uploaded whole with the
  event's recipe, and keeps a client-optimized preview byte for byte only when it fits that recipe
  ([MediaUploadSettings.js](../frontend/src/components/ai-feature/settings/MediaUploadSettings.js),
  [settingsDefaults.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/shared/settingsDefaults.js),
  [derivatives.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/media/derivatives.js)). The eight keys live in
  the existing `media` settings group, so no table changes and an event saved before them reads the
  defaults. A change applies to future uploads only: nothing stored is recompressed, and no link,
  face, index or id changes. The same event's Settings dialog and the Create Event wizard draw the
  same fields. Reached by the roles that already reach AI Event Default Settings and Event Settings.

- **AI Feature photos can arrive already optimized, and the server treats them as the same photo
  it would have made itself.** The media upload route accepts an optional description of the source
  photo from a client that ran the preview recipe on its own machine - the original's SHA-256
  (kept as the row's `contentHash`, so old whole-file uploads, the web and the desktop all agree on
  "already uploaded"), its size, name and relative path, and a flag that the bytes already are the
  preview, in which case they are stored byte for byte and only the thumbnail is made
  ([uploadIntake.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/media/uploadIntake.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/media/service.js)). Two nullable columns,
  `source_size_bytes` and `relative_path`, were added to `ai_event_media`. Face processing queues
  exactly as before, once the preview is stored. An optional `sourceCapturedAt` carries the capture
  time the client read off the original's EXIF, used only when the file that arrived has none of
  its own, so a folder still orders by when each photo was taken. Nothing changes for a client that
  sends the file alone - except that a member of staff must now name a folder (below). Reached by
  the roles that already reach AI Feature uploads.

- **The Virtual Curation desktop app can now install and repair its Local AI runtime from the
  server itself, and tell the server which uploads it will describe on its own.** Three more
  desktop routes, every one a 404 unless `DESKTOP_VIRTUAL_CURATION_ENABLED=true` and open to any
  signed-in user because they hold no studio data - only the face engine the server already runs:
  `GET /api/desktop/runtime/manifest` says which engine version, script digest, model and model
  files (name, size, sha256) a workstation must match, with each digest computed once and cached
  ([runtime.js](../backend/src/modules/desktop/runtime.js)); `GET /api/desktop/runtime/models/:file`
  streams one of the two model files, resumable by `Range` (206 / 416), with its digest as `ETag`,
  the name checked against a fixed allowlist so nothing else on the disk can be asked for, and
  120 requests per person per quarter hour; `GET /api/desktop/runtime/face-engine.py` serves the
  engine script ([controller.js](../backend/src/modules/desktop/controller.js),
  [routes.js](../backend/src/modules/desktop/routes.js)). All three answer 503 while the server's
  own model files are not downloaded yet. `GET /api/desktop/capabilities` now also says
  `deferral: true` and `runtime: { engineVersion, modelVersion }`, so an older server is told apart
  by their absence. Deferral rides on the existing upload routes and their permissions - Image
  Selection `POST …/uploads/derivatives` reads an optional `deferFaceScan` field and the AI Feature
  `POST /events/:eventId/media/upload` an optional `deferAi` field - and only when both desktop
  switches are on and the field says `"true"`: the photo is recorded as waiting but not handed to
  the server's worker, so the desktop's own hand-off does not race it
  ([derivativeController.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/uploads/derivativeController.js),
  [faces/hook.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/faces/hook.js),
  [media/service.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/media/service.js)). With the switches off
  both fields are ignored and every upload is queued exactly as before. So that a deferred photo is
  never lost to a desktop that closed before describing it, each worker now sweeps every ten
  minutes and queues any photo still waiting, never attempted, and untouched for fifteen minutes
  ([faces/worker.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/faces/worker.js),
  [processing/queue.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/processing/queue.js)). A restart does
  not undo a deferral either: the recovery that puts waiting rows back on the queue at boot leaves
  a never-attempted photo inside that grace to its desktop, and with the switches off recovers
  every waiting row exactly as before. Tests:
  [desktop-runtime.test.js](../backend/test/desktop-runtime.test.js),
  [desktop-deferral.test.js](../backend/test/desktop-deferral.test.js).
- **The Virtual Curation desktop app can now run the studio's own face engine on the original files
  and hand the faces it finds to the server, so the gallery's People filter and the AI Feature use
  them without a second AI system.** Three additive backend routes, every one off by default and a
  plain 404 while off, so a server that has not opted in is exactly the web application it was - no
  existing route, response, table, permission or screen moves. `GET /api/desktop/capabilities`
  ([modules/desktop/](../backend/src/modules/desktop/)) tells a signed-in desktop which extras are
  on, which face model it must load (`buffalo_l`, 512 dimensions) and the People filter's
  thresholds; `POST /api/image-selection/projects/:projectId/faces/ingest`
  ([faces/ingest.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/faces/ingest.js)) writes one photo's
  faces exactly as the People filter's worker does - cleared, quality-gated, clustered into the
  project's people - and `POST /api/ai-feature/events/:eventId/media/:mediaId/faces`
  ([processing/ingest.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/processing/ingest.js)) writes them as
  the AI Feature's worker does - face and embedding rows, clustering and guest matching by the
  event's settings, the timeline told when the event finishes - taking the desktop's own 160×160
  crop when it sends one and cutting it from the preview when not. Descriptors from any other model
  or width are refused (409 / 400) and never stored
  ([descriptors.js](../backend/src/modules/desktop/descriptors.js)). Switched on with
  `DESKTOP_VIRTUAL_CURATION_ENABLED=true` and, for the two hand-offs, `DESKTOP_AI_ENABLED=true`
  ([.env.example](../backend/.env.example)). No new permission: capabilities is open to any signed-in
  user (it holds no data), the Image Selection hand-off asks `IMAGE_SELECTION / Project Management`
  Read / Write like the faces router it joins, and the AI Feature hand-off asks `AI Face Management`
  Read / Write like retry-failed - so the roles that already run those pipelines reach it, and no
  role needs re-saving. Tests: [desktop-capabilities.test.js](../backend/test/desktop-capabilities.test.js),
  [desktop-image-selection-ingest.test.js](../backend/test/desktop-image-selection-ingest.test.js),
  [desktop-ai-feature-ingest.test.js](../backend/test/desktop-ai-feature-ingest.test.js).
- **A project can now be given a Production Manager, assigned from Pre Production's General panel.**
  It is the fifth seat on a project, beside the Project Manager, the two coordinators and the
  Creative Manager - but unlike those four it is not asked for on the Start Project form, because it
  is settled once pre-production is under way rather than needed to open the project at all. The
  General bar above the shoot cards shows who it is without opening anything, and the register
  carries a **Production Manager** column beside the other seats - on all four tabs, since they are
  views over one column list - which sorts, filters and exports to CSV like any other, with the name
  also under People in the record panel. Whoever may edit a
  project may assign it; everybody else sees the name filled in and read-only, the same way the
  panel already treats the gifts and the hard disk. The person named has to be an employee who still
  works here, and the name is resolved through the link on every read, so somebody renamed in the
  employee register is renamed here too. **Being the Production Manager does not by itself let
  somebody edit or delete the project** - the other four seats do carry that, and extending it to
  this one is a deliberate permission change rather than part of adding the field. Ships with a
  migration (`20260928170000_sales_project_production_manager`)
  ([PreProductionGeneral](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionGeneral.js),
  [projects/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js)).

- **A role's row menu now has Manage Users, for giving it to several accounts at once.** Handing a
  new role to the ten or fifteen people it is meant for used to mean opening each one in turn through
  User Management → Manage Roles; this is the identical picker, read from the role's own side — the
  same `RolePicker` control, now generalised to take either direction, with Select all/Clear built in
  through its `MultiSelectField`, pre-ticked with whoever already carries the role. Adding or
  removing an account takes effect immediately, exactly as Manage Roles already behaves, including
  the Undo offered on a removal; it calls the same `assignRoleToUser`/`removeRoleFromUser` endpoints
  Manage Roles already does, so nothing new was added on the server. Offered wherever
  `Role Management` is `READ_WRITE`, locked roles included — deciding who carries Super Admin is a
  different question from editing what it grants. See
  [RoleManagement.js](../frontend/src/components/admin/RoleManagement.js),
  [RoleUsersDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/admin/RoleUsersDialog.js) and
  [RolePicker.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/RolePicker.js).

- **The Employee Repository has a Review Pending tab, next to HR Onboarding Pending.** It shows every
  working employee (Active, in Training, PIP) whose Next Review Date has gone by — the same overdue
  check the employee's own Reviews section already colours "Upcoming" with — without moving the row
  out of its own tab: somebody Active with an overdue review still shows under Active as well. The
  row's ⋮ menu gains **Start Review** wherever it is shown, opening the employee's Add Review dialog
  directly, prefilled with the overdue date, instead of sending the reader to find Reviews and press
  Add Review themselves. See [EmployeeVerificationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeVerificationPage.js),
  [EmployeeTable.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeTable.js) and
  [employmentStatus.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/employmentStatus.mjs).

- **Pre Production is a working board, not a read-only list.** The four Pre Production screens now
  list one row per **project**, each summarising its shoots (a Completion Status rolled up from them — On Hold if any shoot is, Completed only when all are, In Progress once anything has started, so a shoot added to a finished project sends it back to In Progress on its own — plus the completed count, a Shoots Pending column naming the shoots not yet completed so the column filter can find every project still owing a given shoot, the follow-up and WRC), while the record underneath stays one per **shoot** — opened as cards from the row, carrying the studio's own pre production sheet
  end to end: the 18 columns already known are inherited read-only from the sale and the shoot, and
  the coordinator fills in the rest — Event Start and End Time, Reporting Time, Studio Start Date and
  Time, Location Address and Link, Travel & Accommodation Needed with the accommodation address, link
  and remarks, Last and Next Followup Date, Completion Status, WRC (waiting for client reply) and
  Production Coordinator. A row is raised automatically the moment a started project has a Pre
  Production Coordinator, and for every shoot added afterwards, so the work reaches whoever was named
  without anybody creating it; **My Shoots** matches the signed-in account's employee record against
  that assignment, and **All Shoots** is the same board unfiltered. **Edit Pre Production** opens the
  project's shoots as cards. A card carries only what is needed to pick a shoot to work on — status,
  date, place, event and reporting times, and a bar saying how much is still blank, as a percentage and a pending count rather than a fraction, since a shoot needing accommodation is asked more questions than one that does not — rather
  than every answer it holds; clicking a card opens that
  shoot's form; saving returns to the cards, which is the loop a coordinator works in. A General tile leads the grid ahead of every shoot, stating Welcome Kit, Storage Needed, CRD Document and Storage ID once for the project instead of repeating down every tile
  ([PreProductionProjectPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionProjectPanel.js)).
  Overdue follow-ups are called out above the table and coloured in it. Each vertical carries its
  own checklist on top of the shared fields — Dum Dum's couple addresses, per-side intro calls,
  meeting and invitation chasing, site visit and production readiness; Qua Qua's single intro call,
  dresses images, production statuses and Google Review — described once in
  [preProductionVerticalFields.js](../frontend/src/constants/preProductionVerticalFields.js) and
  read by the board columns, shoot cards, info panel and form alike, stored as one superset row per
  shoot. Received The Storage / Storage ID are read from the project's Client Storage record rather
  than typed twice, and the CRD document reads itself: alongside the sale's hand-set note, the board
  and the General tile show what the CRD Documents page knows — the document's state, its completion
  percentage, and which side has actually been received, worked out from the answers rather than
  remembered. Each shoot now records whether it is being shot to a
  concept — a plain Yes/No that asks for the Reference and concept Remarks only when the answer is
  yes, and clears both if it turns back to no. Travel gained a mode — Bus, Train, Flight, Own, Office Vehicle, Other — where
  "Other" asks to be spelled out and "Office Vehicle" is picked from Asset Management's vehicles,
  the vehicle's name resolved server-side and kept beside the link; changing the mode clears the
  detail that belonged to the old one. Reading the board needs `PROJECT / Pre Production` at READ,
  saving a row needs READ_WRITE, and nothing here can reach the sale
  ([PreProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionPage.js),
  [PreProductionFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionFormPanel.js),
  [pre-production/service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/service.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **Long pickers can be searched.** Typing narrows the list instead of scrolling it, in the three
  places the list grows with the studio: the branches a role covers, and the roles an account
  carries — both where an employee's login is created and in Manage Roles on the Users page, which
  share one `RolePicker`. Search is an opt-in `searchable` prop on the shared multi-select, so no
  other picker changed, and an option already ticked stays ticked while the search hides it
  ([MultiSelectField.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/MultiSelectField.js),
  [RoleDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/admin/RoleDialog.js),
  [RolePicker.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/RolePicker.js)).

- **An extra quotation can name a service the studio's list does not hold.** The Service picker ends
  with **Others**, and choosing it opens a box to type the service in. Work agreed on top of a
  project is often the thing nobody had a name for yet, and until now it had to be forced into the
  nearest listed service or written in Remarks, where the approving manager would not see it as what
  was being charged for.

  What is stored is the typed name, never the word "Others" — a row reading "Others" tells a manager
  approving it nothing. Reopening such an extra puts the picker back on **Others** with the name
  filled in, which has to wait for the service list to arrive from the server: until it does there is
  no way to tell a typed name from one that simply has not loaded. No server change was needed —
  `service` was already free text up to 150 characters. See
  [ExtraQuotationFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ExtraQuotationFormPanel.js).

- **A payment request can be corrected while it is still pending.** All four kinds — Salary Advance,
  Advance Expense, Expense Submission and Vendor Payment — now offer **Edit** in the row menu, which
  reopens the request in the form it was raised on with every answer, expense line and attachment
  already filled in. Until now a typo meant withdrawing the request and raising it again.

  **The option disappears the moment it is decided.** Approving writes a Cash Spent entry from the
  request's amount, so an edit afterwards would leave the books saying something the request no
  longer does; a rejected request is a closed record for the same reason. `PATCH
  /api/hrm/payment-requests/:id` refuses anything but `PENDING`, and refuses a change of kind at
  all — `requestCode` carries a prefix per kind, so a salary advance turning into a vendor payment
  would leave the code describing something it is not. Who may edit is the answer withdrawing
  already gives: the person who raised it, or somebody who could have decided it — and an approver
  editing somebody else's request does not become the person who raised it. See
  [payment-requests/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payment-requests/controller.js) and
  [PaymentRequestFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PaymentRequestFormPanel.js).

- **An employee's reporting chart, on the Emp Chart tab of their record.** Double-click anybody in
  the Employee Repository and the record opens as it always has, now with a second tab beside
  **Details**. It draws the chain from that person up to whoever reports to nobody, and everybody
  reporting directly to them; each node says how many reports it has of its own, and clicking any
  other node re-centres the chart on that person, so the whole studio is walked one screen at a
  time rather than loaded as one tree. Who somebody reports to is set from **Reports To** in the
  employee form, beside Department — the form offers everyone but the person themselves, and the
  server refuses a longer ring that the list cannot show, so the chart always has a top to arrive
  at. Read at `READ` of `HRM / Employee Management`, the permission that already governs the
  repository it is shown inside, through a router of its own rather than the master-data one next
  door, which deliberately lets any signed-in session read the lists that fill pickers app-wide. A
  node carries the name, designation, department and employee id and nothing else: an employee row
  also holds salary, Aadhaar and PAN, and none of that belongs in a response drawn as a diagram.
  Adds the migration `20260829090000_add_employee_reports_to`. No new permission, so there is
  nothing to reseed or re-save. See
  [EmployeeOrgChart.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeOrgChart.js) and
  [hrm/org-chart/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/org-chart/service.js).

- **The screening form, the onboarding invite and a new joiner's login can now be sent on WhatsApp,
  from the sender's own paired account.** All three screens already showed the finished wording in an editable box with a
  Copy button, and the studio then left the application, opened WhatsApp and pasted it. **Send
  WhatsApp** sits in the dialog's footer beside Close and Send Invite, in WhatsApp's own green with
  its mark, and sends what is on screen — including a line somebody added before
  pressing it, which is why the box is editable and why the message travels from the browser rather
  than being rebuilt on the server. The **recipient's number never does**: it is read off the
  invite or the employee record, so neither screen can reach anybody but the person it is about,
  and there is deliberately no "send WhatsApp to this number" endpoint anywhere. The interview register's **Send Onboarding
  Invite** needed nothing of its own: it opens the employee onboarding dialog, which carries the
  button already. Sending the
  credentials asks for `ADMIN / User Management` Read / Write — the same permission that creates
  them, and a stronger one than the rest of that screen, because the message carries the temporary
  password; the onboarding invite rides the `HRM / Employee Management` Read / Write the router
  already applies, and the screening form the `HRM / Interview` its own router does. No new
  permission and no migration. All three go through the WhatsApp module's own
  send path, so they keep every habit that makes the studio's paired number look like a person
  writing to one person — the pacing between messages, the check that the number is on WhatsApp at
  all, the typing indicator — and both the studio-wide and per-user kill switches stop them. They
  are behind the **same per-user rate limit** as every other send, deliberately sharing one budget
  with the CRM rather than being given a second one: it is one account, and WhatsApp watches the
  account. Somebody who has not linked their own WhatsApp sees the button greyed with the reason,
  rather than not at all — the three reasons it can be greyed (the studio's switch, their own
  switch, no phone linked) are told apart, because only the last is one they can fix. Nothing is
  recorded, which is what the invite's email does too: there is no sent stamp on an invite and no
  screen that shows one.
### Added
- **The Interview candidate popup now carries the call recordings and their transcripts, as the CRM
  lead popup does.** Its Call Logs tab already answered *has anybody rung this person* — when, how
  long, and which of the studio's people was on it — but deliberately stripped the rest, on the
  reading that `HRM / Interview` is not a grant of `SALES / CRM Leads`. **The studio's decision is
  the other one: each module answers for its own permission.** So the tab now also carries the note
  whoever took the call typed, the CRM status at the time, and a player for the recording itself;
  and a new **Transcripts** tab beside it shows what was actually said, with the AI summary, call
  outcome, next action, and the spoken text behind *View Full Transcript*. Worth knowing, because it
  is a real widening: the call log is one studio-wide table keyed by the number dialled, so somebody
  who may edit a candidate can point a record at any number and read what the log holds against it.
  Narrowing it again is a permission decision rather than a code change. What is still **not** passed
  on is the CRM's own filing of that person — the name it chose, the enquiry it opened — and the
  integration's raw webhook payload; none of it says anything about the call. A transcript hangs off
  a *call* rather than a lead, which is the only reason this is reachable at all: a candidate has
  never had an enquiry id, so the number finds the calls and the calls find their transcripts. Asking
  for one in full goes through the candidate, never by transcript id alone, so the tab cannot be used
  to read a call belonging to somebody else. The Transcripts tab itself is now **one shared
  component** ([CallTranscriptsTab](../frontend/src/components/shared/CallTranscriptsTab.js)), lifted
  out of `CRMPage` where it lived: it carries careful statements about machine translation and
  inferred speakers that a second copy would not have kept, and only *where a transcript is fetched
  from* differs between the two screens.

### Changed

- **Permission and Attendance regularization requests go to the Permission Approver only.** They
  no longer fall back to the Leave Approvers when an employee has no Permission Approver: such an
  employee cannot raise either until HR sets one - the form says so before anything is filled in,
  and the server refuses it. The Permission Approver box on Employee Preference now reads "Not set
  - permissions and regularizations cannot be raised" while empty. Leave, comp-off, on-duty and
  outside-location requests are unchanged, and requests already raised keep the approvers they were
  sent to. [approvals.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/approvals.js),
  [AttendanceRequestFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestFormPanel.js).
- **"Correction" is now called "Attendance regularization".** The request type in Raise Request,
  its form section, the request lists, the approver's bell notification, the employee's banner
  ("Raise attendance regularization") and the logout messages all use the new name. Nothing else
  about the request changed. [attendanceRequestConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/attendanceRequestConfig.js),
  [requestNotifications.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/requestNotifications.js).
- **A login nobody logs out of within 24 hours now reads Absent.** It used to read "Incorrect
  login"; it is an Absent day now on the dashboard, the register and in the salary calculator, and
  the employee's screen says "<day> is marked Absent: you logged in at … and did not log out within
  24 hours. Raise a correction". The correction changes it from Absent to Present, Half day and the
  rest, as before. On a holiday, a weekly off or a day of approved leave it reads as that day, not
  Absent. Corrections already pending from the old status can still be approved.
  [attendanceRules.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/attendanceRules.js),
  [service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/service.js).
- **The attendance rules moved into Settings, for administrators only.** They are Settings →
  Employee → Attendance Rules now, beside the Attendance calculator, and offered to administrators
  alone; the account menu's Rules - which anybody with Employee Attendance saw - is gone. Saving
  them still needs `HRM / Attendance Rules` Read / Write, and every employee is still judged by
  the same rules. [AttendanceRulesSettingsPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/AttendanceRulesSettingsPanel.js),
  [SettingsOverlay.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/SettingsOverlay.js).
- **The next step on a shoot's timeline pulses.** On the client page, the gold dot of the step a
  shoot is waiting on now sends a ring out around it, over and over - still for anybody whose
  device asks for less motion. [ShootTimeline.js](../frontend/src/components/client/ShootTimeline.js).
- **The shoot cards on the client page are tidier.** A submitted plan is now a "Plan submitted"
  pill with its day under it, and "Plan ready" on Production is a pill too, rather than loose grey
  text; the shoot's date stays on one line, and on a narrow card the pill moves under the name
  instead of squeezing it. [ProjectTracker.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/ProjectTracker.js),
  [projectTracking.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/projectTracking.mjs).
- **An administrator no longer sees the Raise Request button on HRM → Request.** It used to be
  shown greyed out to them; it is now left out, as the account menu already left it out. Everybody
  else keeps the button. [AttendanceRequestsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/AttendanceRequestsPage.js).
- **The administrator's Employee Attendance dashboard opens on today's figures.** It used to open
  on the last thirty days; From and To, the branch and the employee filters still reach any other
  range, and Reset comes back to today. The arrows on the cards then compare with yesterday.
  [attendanceOverviewRange.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/attendanceOverviewRange.mjs).
- **Signing in to the client page is quicker.** The film drawn across the screen between the
  sign-in and the project page now takes about 0.75s instead of 1.4s - 0.3s to close, 0.4s to
  open. [globals.css](../frontend/src/app/globals.css).
- **The client page's status pills have a look of their own.** Every status on it - the stage,
  the gifts, each shoot - is a bordered pill with a mark before the words: a tick when done, a
  half-filled circle while under way, a pause when paused or on hold, a dashed circle when not
  started - so a status reads by its shape as well as its colour. The studio's screens keep
  the plain chip. [ProgressChip.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/ProgressChip.js),
  [ProjectTracker.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/ProjectTracker.js).
- **Settings → User Settings → WhatsApp now also lists anybody Allow WhatsApp is ticked for, not
  only the Sales team.** Allow WhatsApp (Login Credentials → WhatsApp) holds somebody to the
  application-wide link gate regardless of department, but until now the only place that showed
  whether they had actually linked was the gate itself, on their own screen the next time they
  opened the application — an administrator switching the tick on had no way to check back. A row
  reached either way now carries **Required** next to their name, so Sales and Required read as the
  two different reasons they can be, rather than one list. An administrator is never shown as
  Required, since the gate never holds one regardless of the tick, even where they also carry it.
  See [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/whatsapp-chat/controller.js) and
  [WhatsAppUsersTable.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/WhatsAppUsersTable.js).

- **CRD Documents has a My Documents switch, the one the CRM board already has.** The data scope widens
  "mine" to "mine and my team's" — it follows the reporting chain the whole way down, so a manager four
  levels above a coordinator sees their documents. That is the right default, and it is also why a
  coordinator with a team of their own could not find their own work: eleven rows, one of them theirs. On,
  the list is the documents that reader is the **pre-production coordinator** for, which is the owner the
  Assigned To column names. Remembered per person, and drawn **only** for somebody who has a team under
  them — for everybody else the two states are the same list, and a switch that changes nothing invites a
  reader to flip it, see no difference and conclude the screen is broken. A document with **nobody staffed
  on it** surfaces while the switch is on for a reader who sees everything, since they are the ones who
  staff projects; a coordinator reading their own work is not shown other people's unstaffed documents
  ([crd-documents/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crd-documents/controller.js),
  [CrdDocumentsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CrdDocumentsPage.js)).

- **CRD Documents says who each document is on.** The owner is the project's **pre-production
  coordinator**, and it is not a new field: that person is already named on the project and is already one
  of the five columns the data scope narrows the register by, which is why the row reaches that reader at
  all. So the screen was already showing each person their own work and looked exactly like a list of
  everybody's, because no column said whose it was. A **standalone** document — one raised by hand against
  an enquiry that answers to no project — has no coordinator to name and reads as a dash rather than
  borrowing somebody
  ([crd-documents/service.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crd-documents/service.js),
  [CrdDocumentsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CrdDocumentsPage.js)).
  The name comes back **through the employee relation**, with the project's stored text only as a fallback,
  so a coordinator who has since been renamed reads correctly.

- **CRD Documents is one list instead of one list per vertical.** The page opened on Dum Dum with a
  picker beside the heading, so Qua Qua's documents sat behind a control and a reader who did not notice
  it saw a list that was simply missing rows — with the status tabs counting confidently over the half
  they could see. Both verticals are on the page now and the tabs count all of it. Nothing is lost in
  telling them apart: **Vertical is a column** on the row and always was, sortable and filterable like
  every other, so somebody who wants one narrows that column and somebody who wants the whole of what
  the studio is owed does nothing
  ([CrdDocumentsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CrdDocumentsPage.js)).

- **Every dropdown in a form field can be typed into to find an option.** It was opt-in, so whether a list
  could be searched depended on whether whoever wrote that form had thought to pass the prop — ninety-odd
  call sites had, and identical lists of branches, designations, employees and master data elsewhere could
  only be scrolled. It is decided once in `Dropdown` now, which is also the only way the forms nobody has
  looked at get it. Safe as a default because of what the box does with what is typed: it is a combobox
  with `aria-autocomplete="list"`, so typing is the **search** and the value moves only when an option is
  chosen — a half-typed word in a branch field cannot be stored as a branch. The section picker beside a
  module heading (`mode="switch"`) is unchanged, and a picker that genuinely should not be typed into can
  still pass `searchable={false}`
  ([Dropdown.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/Dropdown.js)).
  **Reaching a dropdown no longer opens its list.** A searchable field opened its menu on focus, which was
  fine while search was something a form asked for and is not as the default: tabbing through a form would
  pop a menu at every dropdown, ten of them on some screens. A click opens it, typing opens it and the
  arrow keys open it — what is gone is the one that fired without anybody asking for anything.

- **Schedule Payment takes an amount as well as a percentage, and the percentage takes decimals.** A row
  could only be entered as a share of the signed quotation, with the Amount beside it a figure to read —
  so a client who agreed to ₹50,000 at slot booking meant somebody working out what percentage of
  ₹4,20,000 that is. Both boxes are typed into now and each works out the other. The **percentage stays
  what is stored**, so a schedule entered in rupees still follows a corrected quotation. The decimals are
  what make that possible: ₹50,000 of ₹4,20,000 is 11.904762%, and a whole number would be ₹210 out — the
  box was a `type="number"` with no `step`, which is a step of one, so a browser marked 11.9 invalid and
  its arrows walked in whole numbers. It is digits and a single decimal point now, sanitised as typed, the
  same rule the Signed Quotation box above it already used. The Amount box is disabled while there is no
  signed quotation, since a share of nothing cannot be expressed, and shows what is being typed rather
  than re-deriving itself under the cursor
  ([paymentSchedule.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/paymentSchedule.mjs),
  [SchedulePaymentSection.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/SchedulePaymentSection.js)).

- **Production is in the sidebar, under Project Management.** The board was only reachable by
  typing its address; it now sits after Pre Production and shows only to roles holding
  `PROJECT / Production` at `READ` or above — no new permission, and no role needs re-saving. A
  saved Sidebar Layout gets the entry appended to Project Management. Post Production stays off the
  menu ([navigation.mjs](../frontend/src/constants/navigation.mjs),
  [sidebarStructure.js](../backend/src/modules/user/preferences/sidebarStructure.js)).

- **The production frontend build now runs on webpack, not Turbopack.** Turbopack's build pipeline
  has a known, currently open bug fetching `next/font/google` at build time
  ([vercel/next.js#99114](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/99114)): when Google's font CSS
  happens to return a URL containing `&` in its query, Turbopack's resolver mis-splits it and the
  build fails with "next/font/google queries have exactly one entry" — intermittent, since it
  depends on exactly what Google returns for that request, and it hit both a CI run and, once, the
  nightly deploy itself on the client-facing quotation page (`/q/[token]`, which sets five Google
  Fonts for the PDF-styled sheet). `next build` is now pinned to `--webpack`
  ([package.json](../frontend/package.json)) so the production build never depends on Turbopack's
  font-fetch code path; `next dev` is untouched and still runs on Turbopack
  ([next.config.mjs](../frontend/next.config.mjs)).

- **The client's quotation shows its discounts.** Between the events (and their storage note) and
  the price, the client's copy - and the PDF printed from it - now has a card listing the discounts
  the quotation was saved with: **Discount (10%) - ₹1,000** under a gold tag icon, then **Extra
  Discount** under a second icon with each one by its reason ("Referral concession - ₹500"; one
  saved without a reason reads "Extra Discount"), never numbered
  ([PublicQuotationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/PublicQuotationPage.js)). Nothing at
  zero is listed, and a quotation with no discount has no card and prints exactly as before. The
  figures are read from the saved quotation, not worked out again
  ([quotationBrand.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/quotationBrand.mjs) `quotationDiscountBreakdown`,
  `extraDiscountsOf` - the same reading the generator reopens a quotation's extra discounts with),
  and the price below is the saved total as ever, so nothing is taken off twice. The Performance
  Cost is not listed. Frontend only.

- **The Quotation Summary adds a Performance Cost and takes up to three extra discounts.** Under
  Service Cost, **Performance Cost +** opens a rupee amount that is added to the quotation before
  any discount, so Discount in % is now worked out on service cost plus performance cost. Extra
  Discount is now a list: **Extra Discount +** opens the first (a reason and a rupee amount, never a
  percentage), the **+** beside the Extra Discount heading adds the next, up to three, and goes away
  at three. The rows sit under one heading with Reason and Amount (₹) named once above them, and
  each row - like the Performance Cost - has a small × beside its amount that takes only that one
  away (undoable); the amounts line up in one column with the discount's. Total Cost is service cost + performance cost − the
  percentage − every extra discount; extra discounts that together pass what is left after the
  percentage are shown as an error and the quotation cannot be generated with them
  ([QuotationGeneratorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationGeneratorPanel.js),
  [quotationBrand.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/quotationBrand.mjs) `quotationTotals`). Saved in the
  version's payload as `performanceCost` and `extraDiscounts` and checked by the server (no
  negative amount, at most three, together no more than the cost); a quotation saved with the
  earlier single extra discount opens with it as the first of the list, and one with none reads
  exactly as before. The client's copy and its PDF still print only the final amount. No
  migration.

- **Add Shoot in the Quotation Generator takes several shoots at once.** Its Shoot field is now a
  searchable multi-select (chips, one line high) - Bride Haldi, Engagement and Groom Haldi can be
  ticked together - and the rest of the form is their common details: Shoot Type, place, district,
