  state, Session Timing, duration, date, food, accommodation, travel and preference. Add Shoot List
  (or Save) makes one ordinary shoot row per chosen shoot with those details, so each is its own
  shoot with its own services and the saved quotation holds individual shoots exactly as before
  ([AddShootDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/AddShootDialog.js),
  `multipleShoots`). The checks run once for the batch, and a batch that fails adds nothing. Only
  one shoot can be the Main Event, so with several chosen and Main Event on the form asks which one;
  a shoot already in the list is never added twice - Add Shoot List adds the others and names it,
  Save stops and names it. The field says its details apply to every shoot chosen. One shoot chosen
  behaves as it always did; editing a shoot, and Add Shoot on the project screens, still take one.
  Frontend only.

- **The Quotation Summary shows what the discount comes to, and takes an extra discount in rupees.**
  In the Quotation Generator, Discount in % now has the amount it takes off shown beside it,
  read-only, and a new quotation starts at 0% rather than at the Default Discount set in Settings →
  Quotation Settings (or the brand's) - that setting is kept but no longer pre-fills; a saved,
  edited, versioned or duplicated quotation keeps its own, and a calculator draft the one chosen
  there. Below it, **Extra Discount +** opens a Reason and an Amount (₹, never a percentage) taken
  off after the percentage - Service Cost − percentage − extra = Total Cost - with Remove to clear
  both. An amount larger than what is left is shown as an error and the quotation cannot be
  generated with it, so the total never goes below nothing
  ([QuotationGeneratorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationGeneratorPanel.js),
  [quotationBrand.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/quotationBrand.mjs) `quotationTotals`). The reason and
  amount are saved in the version's payload beside the discount and checked by the server (a reason
  of at most 191 characters, an amount from 0 up to the subtotal); an older quotation has neither
  and reads exactly as before. The client's copy and its PDF print only the final amount, as they
  always have. No migration, and no permission changed.

- **The Quotation Generator offers every active service on every shoot, and a new service starts on
  the shoot's Session Timing.** Choose Services on a quotation's shoot no longer hides the services
  ticked for the other shoot type - a Studio / In-House shoot lists the Outdoor services too, and
  the other way round ([ProjectServiceCreationSection.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ProjectServiceCreationSection.js),
  `servicesFollowShootType`, off only in the generator). Shoot Type stays on the shoot, in Settings
  → Services and in pricing; the project screens keep narrowing by it, and Choose Deliverables is
  unchanged. A service added to a shoot now starts its Session Timing on the shoot's own session
  where the service offers exactly that one - Half Session for a half-session shoot - matched by the
  session's code, and stays blank where the service does not offer it; an hourly shoot has no
  session to pick, so its services keep their Hours / Minutes box as before
  ([servicePricing.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/servicePricing.mjs) `defaultSessionOptionId`). It is set
  once, when the line is added, and then follows the same path a chosen timing always has - the
  booking's deliverables follow it - so changing it by hand is never undone, and a saved
  quotation's lines load with the timing they were saved with. Prices are worked out exactly as
  before. Frontend only.

- **The client Signature Album's download is an icon, and the album Gallery's delete button is
  cleaner.** The client album's top-right Download Album is now a round download icon beside Share
  ([SignatureAlbumView.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/client/SignatureAlbumView.js)),
  named "Download album" for screen readers and on hover; while the PDF is prepared it shows a
  spinner and its name reads "Preparing album...". It starts the same whole-album PDF as before. In
  the studio's Signature Album Gallery the delete button on each photo is a white circle with a thin
  border and the project's Material UI trash icon, named "Delete photo"
  ([AlbumGallery.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/AlbumGallery.js));
  it opens the same confirmation and deletes the same way. Frontend only.

- **The client gallery's People tab is marked as still being tested.** The tab row now reads
  **All Photos · People β (this feature is under testing) · Selected (n)**, so a client meeting face
  grouping for the first time knows what it is before they judge it. The label is the whole of the
  change: the tab still answers to the same `people` value and the same handler, and face
  recognition, the grouping, the multi-select and its AND filtering, the photo counts, All Photos,
  Selected and the client's own selection all behave exactly as before. No backend, API or database
  change. The note is on the label's own line, so the three underlines stay on one baseline and
  nothing reaches into the cards below; on a phone it shortens to **(testing)** and the row's gap
  narrows, which is what keeps all three tabs on one line at 360px with no sideways scroll. Screen
  readers hear the tab once, as "People (beta, under testing)", and the note is dark enough that
  11px text clears the 4.5:1 contrast WCAG AA asks of it
  ([FolderCards.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/FolderCards.js)).
- **The client's Signature Album downloads as one designed PDF, and its photos no longer open.**
  Download Album used to save a ZIP of the photos; it now saves the whole album as one PDF -
  `<title>-signature-album.pdf` - with the cover and its crop, the title, subtitle and date, the
  highlights and every chapter in the saved order and layout, the theme, fonts and spacing, and the
  ending. It is printed on the server by the headless browser the quotation PDF already uses, from
  the client's own page drawn whole at `/a/<code>/print`
  ([SignatureAlbumPrint.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/client/SignatureAlbumPrint.js),
  [signatureAlbum.pdf.service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/signature-album/signatureAlbum.pdf.service.js)),
  so the PDF is the album by construction; every photo is the web preview the album shows, never an
  original. A large album takes a while, so it is built in the background: the button reads
  *Preparing album...* and cannot be pressed again, then the browser saves the one file. One album
  is printed once however often it is asked for, two print at once in all, and files are deleted
  after 30 minutes. The API is now `POST /download` (start), `GET /download/status` (preparing /
  failed / ready with the ticket) and `GET /download?ticket=` (the PDF); the ZIP builder is removed.
  Clicking a photo in the album now does nothing - the full-screen photo viewer with its arrows,
  full screen and share is removed from the Signature Album only, and a photo no longer looks
  clickable. The client gallery's own viewer is a different component and is unchanged. Allow
  Download works exactly as before. No migration, and no permission changed.

- **A Signature Album's cover is chosen from the album's own uploads, and every photo is dragged
  into place in the Design preview.** Choose Cover in the cover dialog now lists only the photos uploaded in Album →
  Upload - no project folders, no Photo Selection photos - in one searchable grid, and says *No
  Signature Album photos uploaded yet* when there are none
  ([AlbumCoverPicker.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/AlbumCoverPicker.js)).
  The cover is a reference to that stored photo, never a copy: a new nullable
  `signature_album.cover_album_photo_id` (foreign key, `ON DELETE SET NULL`, migration
  `20260928110000_signature_album_cover_photo`) sits beside `cover_image_id`, choosing an album photo
  clears the project-photo cover, and publishing accepts either. An album whose cover is a project
  photo keeps showing it until an album photo replaces it. On the Design tab the preview is now
  **Edit Album Preview**: with write access any photo can be dragged inside its frame - the cover in
  every cover style, a chapter's cover band, and each photo in the highlights and the chapters, in
  every layout, on the Desktop and Phone previews
  ([usePhotoDrag.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/client/usePhotoDrag.js)).
  It moves the same focal point Adjust Cover / Adjust Photo set, clamped so no edge shows, and is
  saved on release through the update that already owns it (album, chapter or item); a drag never
  opens the photo, and a failed save puts the photo back and says why. A photo shown whole, or in a
  frame of its own shape and not zoomed, has nothing to drag. The client's page draws the same
  positions and cannot be dragged. Run `npx prisma migrate deploy` - this
  migration and `20260928100000_signature_album_photos` are both needed. No permission changed:
  choosing and dragging are `IMAGE_SELECTION / Signature Album` at `READ_WRITE`, as editing was.

- **On a phone, the client gallery's open photo is swiped to move and double-tapped to pick.** Below
  640px the two arrows over the picture are gone; swipe left for the next photo, right for the
  previous, and **double tap** the picture to pick it
  ([ImageViewer.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/ImageViewer.js)). A
  single tap does nothing, and a double tap on a photo already picked does nothing too: unpicking is
  the bottom tick's alone, and the tick still picks and unpicks as before. All of it calls the
  handlers the bottom bar already uses, with its stops at the first and last photo, so the tick and
  the selected count follow at once. A gesture is one action, never both: at least 50px of clearly
  horizontal movement is a swipe, under 10px and half a second is a tap, two taps within 300ms and
  30px are a double tap, and a swipe ends any double tap in progress
  ([viewerGesture.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/viewerGesture.mjs)). One pick is in flight at a time, so a
  triple tap sends one request, and a photo still loading cannot be picked. The browser's own
  double-tap zoom is held off on the photo only, on a phone only (`touch-action: manipulation`), so
  pinch-zoom still works. A pick answers with a check that swells in over the photo with one soft ring
  (about 0.55s) while the photo dips by a hair - played only once the selection has really changed, so
  a refused pick (a submitted item, a PIN still to enter) shows nothing; the bottom tick gives the same
  feedback on a phone, a contracting check when it unpicks. Transform and opacity only, CSS keyframes
  in `globals.css`, and a short fade under reduced motion. The bottom Previous / tick / Next, tablets,
  desktops and the keyboard are unchanged. Frontend only.

- **The Signature Album's cover is edited in a dialog, opened by Add Cover / Edit Cover.** The cover
  form no longer sits on the Album tab; a button on the upload's header opens it - **Add Cover** while
  the album has no cover photo saved (the rule publishing already reads), **Edit Cover** after, and
  View Cover for somebody who may only read. The dialog is the same cover editor
  ([AlbumCover.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/AlbumCover.js)) - photo,
  Change Cover, Adjust Cover, title, subtitle, event date, alignment, ending message - but everything
  in it is now a draft until **Save Cover**, which writes it all in the one album update it always
  used; choosing a photo and applying Adjust Cover no longer save on their own, so Cancel keeps
  nothing, and Escape or the close button ask before dropping unsaved changes. A failed save leaves the
  dialog open with what was typed. No backend or data change.

- **Duplicate on a quotation now opens the Quotation Generator on an editable copy that saves as a
  new quotation.** The row menu's Duplicate used to ask only for a target enquiry and copy the version
  there unseen. It now opens the generator in duplicate mode
  ([QuotationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationPage.js),
  [QuotationGeneratorPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/QuotationGeneratorPanel.js)): every
  field copied from the source version, all of it editable, the header reading *Duplicating
  DBS-QO-…-03 — saving raises a new quotation, version 01*, no version picker, the brand free to
  change as on any new quotation, and the button **Save as Duplication**. Saving goes through the
  same `POST /api/sales/quotations` as a new quotation, so the copy gets the next number in the
  sequence and starts at version 01 whatever version it was copied from, and nothing is written to
  the source. The copy keeps the source's rates, GST and discount rather than today's while it stays
  on the source's brand. The open duplicate is named in the address (`?duplicate=<version id>`) so a
  reload reopens it. The generator's save button is now the shared `Button` held shut while a save is
  in flight (`useSubmitOnce`), so a double-click raises one quotation, and the form cannot be closed
  under a running save — for Edit and new quotations too. Edit and **Save as new version** are unchanged. `QuotationDuplicateDialog` and
  `duplicateSalesQuotation` are removed; the server's `POST /quotations/:id/duplicate` stays. No
  schema change, no permission change — Duplicate is still offered only with `SALES / Quotation
  Management` Read / Write.

- **Anybody who sends from this application can now link their own WhatsApp, not just the CRM.** The
  session is per **user** — credentials are stored per user id and every message goes out from the phone
  that person paired, which is already how the screening form, the onboarding invite and a new joiner's
  login are sent. But the route that shows the pairing QR sat behind `SALES / CRM Leads`, so an HR user
  was told they were not linked and had nowhere to link it. Pairing and unpairing your **own** account now
  sit above that guard, beside `GET /my-session` which was lifted for the same reason, and answer to
  whichever of the three jobs actually messages anybody — CRM Leads, HRM / Interview, or
  HRM / Employee Management. A lead's conversation stays behind the CRM's permission. The candidate
  popup's WhatsApp tab shows the code when the viewer is not linked, instead of a compose box that was
  refused on send
  ([routes.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/whatsapp-chat/routes.js),
  [WhatsAppLinkCard.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/WhatsAppLinkCard.js),
  [InterviewWhatsAppTab.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewWhatsAppTab.js)).
  The pairing card is **one component** now rather than markup inside the lead panel, and it asks for a
  code only when a person presses the button: pairing is deliberately not rate limited on the server, and
  each attempt is a real registration against a number WhatsApp can ban for registering repeatedly.

- **Client Storage asks its yes/no questions with Yes / No radio buttons instead of switches.** All seven
  checks — Labeled?, Footage Backup, Final Files Copy, Harddisk Footages Back up, Folder Structure
  Checked, Final Renders, Other Files in Harddisk — on the storage form and at every step of the flow
  that asks them (Hand In, Footage Backup Done, HDD Out), plus Shoot Status Pending, which is a reading
  rather than a question and would have been the one switch left among seven pairs. The same change the
  pre production shoot form already had, through the same field helper, which now lives on its own
  ([yesNoField.js](../frontend/src/constants/yesNoField.js)) rather than in the pre production field list
  ([formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js)).

- **Switching Storage Needed to Yes no longer explains itself.** Pre-Production's General bar drew a
  dashed box reading "No hard disk record yet — saving Storage Needed as Yes raises one" the moment the
  answer was turned on, which told somebody the mechanism they had just used: they chose Yes, they are
  about to save, and the disk appears when they do. Nothing was being asked and nothing had gone wrong.
  The Hard Disk field now waits until there is a disk to show — the whole field rather than an empty
  renderer, which would have left a gap in the grid where the box was
  ([PreProductionGeneral.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionGeneral.js)).

- **In the lead popup, the remarks box now sits at the top and the remarks read newest first.** The box
  and its toolbar used to be under the whole list, so on a lead with many remarks the next note meant
  scrolling past every earlier one, and the latest remark was at the bottom. The box is now first and stays
  in view while the remarks scroll beneath it, with the most recent remark directly under it. Nothing
  about what is saved changed: the remarks are stored in the order they were written, and editing one
  still rewrites that entry. The same composer serves the candidate popup and the Add Lead and info
  panels, which get the new order too; the lead popup and the candidate popup's Remarks tab both pin the box
  ([NotesComposer.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/NotesComposer.js),
  [CRMPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CRMPage.js),
  [InterviewRemarksTab.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewRemarksTab.js)).
- **The candidate popup's Next Follow-up date no longer stretches across the whole card.** It takes one
  column of the same grid the lead popup's Follow-up Details uses: full width on a phone, half the card
  from tablet width and a third on wide screens
  ([InterviewCandidatePopup.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewCandidatePopup.js)).
- **The candidate popup now has a Call Logs tab, and Remarks reads like a lead's.** Call Logs answers
  the question the **Follow Up** stage exists to ask and the register could not: has anybody actually
  rung this candidate, when, for how long, and which of the studio's people was on it. The studio's call
  log is one table fed by the handset integration and keyed by the number dialled, so a recruiter's call
  lands in it exactly as a salesperson's does — it had only ever been read from the CRM's lead popup.
  **A recruiter is shown the call and nothing about the CRM's client**: a number that is a candidate here
  can be a client there, so the client's name, enquiry, CRM status, recording, note and raw payload are
  all stripped — `HRM / Interview` is not a grant of `CRM / Leads`. **Remarks is now the lead's
  remarks composer itself** — the collapsible entry bubbles, the bullet and numbered lists, Enter to
  post, the send button in the toolbar — not a box that resembles it. `NotesComposer` had been sitting
  unexported in the middle of `CRMPage.js`, which is how the register came to have a second, poorer
  answer to "how do I write down what was said"; it now lives in `components/shared/` and nothing about
  it changed for the lead — and it imports no service of its own, the upload and fetch behind its
  paperclip arriving from whichever module owns the bucket the files are in. Two of its controls are switched off for a candidate: the **pencil**, because
  `statusNotes` is append-only with no per-entry id and no endpoint that rewrites one, and the
  **paperclip**, because a candidate's remark has nowhere to put a file. Each bubble also carries the
  **stage** the remark was written at, which a lead's has no equivalent of — "they asked to be called
  back" means one thing at Follow Up and another at Selected. **Activity Logs** is the same log read as *what
  happened* — the stage, when it moved and who moved it — so the card no longer holds one list twice. The
  two panes also share the width better: the record was taking two thirds of the screen for a form that
  draws only the fields the candidate answered
  ([InterviewCallLogsTab.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewCallLogsTab.js),
  [InterviewRemarksTab.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewRemarksTab.js),
  [interviewInfoFormatters.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/interviewInfoFormatters.js),
  [callLogService.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/callLogService.js)).

- **Position Applied For is no longer required when the studio writes a candidate down.** Add
  Application and the candidate record still ask for it and the register still files by it, but a
  blank one is accepted: the job somebody is after is regularly unknown at the moment the application
  arrives — a walk-in, a number passed on by a friend of the studio, a CV with no covering note — and
  refusing the row for it bought either a guess typed into the field or the candidate not being
  written down at all. The server already took it as optional, so this removes a refusal the frontend
  was making on its own
  ([InterviewAddApplicationDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewAddApplicationDialog.js),
  [interviewConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/interviewConfig.js),
  [candidateRecordForm.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/candidateRecordForm.js)).
  The **candidate's own screening form still requires it**, which is where the real answer comes from.

- **Double-clicking a candidate on HRM → Interview now opens the screen where they are worked, not
  a read-only card.** One popup holds the whole errand: the fields the candidate actually filled in
  (with the empty ones one press away), a remark composer, the activity log, a WhatsApp message, and
  a Follow-up Details card where the stage is chosen. Choosing **Follow Up** asks when, directly
  under the pills; choosing **Selected**, **On Hold** or **Rejected** is answered by the remark, which
  Update requires — so the register can always say why a candidate moved. The three stages that are
  consequences of an act — Form Submission Pending, Interview Scheduled, Onboarded — offer that act
  instead, and confirming it saves the record and opens the act's own form **over** the popup, which
  stays open underneath — cancelling that form puts you back on the candidate, and only the act
  succeeding writes the stage and closes both;
  **Form Submitted** is refused outright, because that stage is the candidate answering. **Choosing a
  stage asks for its remark first**: the pill records the choice, the card says a remark is needed to
  move that candidate, the Remarks tab comes forward, and Update writes the stage and the reason
  together or neither. Pressing Update with no remark is refused in the **snackbar** rather than as a
  banner above the form — it is not a fault in a field, and a banner pushed the record down the screen
  and stayed there to be re-read. **Schedule Interview and Send Screening Form draw their form over the popup**
  rather than closing it — closing that form leaves the popup exactly as it was, and only a round
  actually booked or a form actually sent closes both. Posting a remark or sending a WhatsApp message
  no longer closes the popup either. A viewer with
  **read-only** HRM access gets the record, the log and no editable field — the guard is
  `ReadOnlyFieldset`'s own `canWrite`, and the press that opens the empty fields sits outside it, since
  reading the whole record is exactly what that viewer is there to do. The side
  drawer this replaces is gone, and the ⋮'s **Edit** / **Review** opens the same popup, so there is
  one editor for a candidate rather than two
  Answering the stage question no longer raises a second one: `Dialog` draws inside the popup rather
  than portalling out of it, so a press on **Leave the stage as it is** used to bubble to the popup's
  dimmed backdrop and put "Close without saving?" on top of its own answer — in any tab and at any
  stage. A press on the backdrop is now a press whose target *is* the backdrop
  ([InterviewCandidatePopup.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewCandidatePopup.js),
  [candidateRecordForm.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/candidateRecordForm.js),
  [InterviewPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewPage.js)).
  The **Onboarded** pill is only offered to somebody holding `HRM / Employee Management`
  READ_WRITE — the same permission the row menu's Send Onboarding Invite is gated on — and a
  read-only viewer gets the record, the log and no way to move anybody.

- **Branch reach now follows the role that granted the permission, not the person.** Somebody who
  holds CRM Leads across every branch through one role and Asset Management in one branch through
  another now sees every branch's leads and one branch's assets, where before the wider role
  silently widened the narrower one. Every call into the branch API names the `{ module, feature }`
  it is asking about; a role naming no branches contributes none, and a person's own
  `user.branch_id` no longer widens anything — work they or their team are named on still reaches
  them through `dataScope`
  ([iam.service.js](../backend/src/services/iam.service.js),
  [dataScope.service.js](../backend/src/services/dataScope.service.js)).
  **A read-only role's branches no longer scope writes**: `dataScope.resolve` takes the access level,
  so an employee write is measured against the roles that grant READ_WRITE.

- **Start Project's radio buttons now sit in a bordered box with the same title style as the
  fields around them.** Welcome Gift, Shoot Completed Gift, Storage Needed and CRD Document match
  the pre production form's Yes / No radios, through a new `variant="field"` on the shared
  `RadioGroupField`; an unanswered required group now reddens its box too
  ([RadioGroupField.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/RadioGroupField.js),
  [StartProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/StartProjectFormPanel.js)).

- **The pre production shoot form asks its yes/no questions with Yes / No radio buttons instead
  of switches.** Travel & Accommodation Needed, WRC and every checklist yes/no (Event Schedule
  Meeting, Invitation Soft Copy, Site Visit, Team Reached Message, Shoot Completion Message, Google
  Review) now show both answers side by side; what is saved is unchanged
  ([preProductionVerticalFields.js](../frontend/src/constants/preProductionVerticalFields.js),
  [formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js)).

- **A shoot's pre production status now works itself out; nobody sets it by hand.** Completion
  Status is gone from the shoot form. A shoot with no details filled is Not Started, one with every
  counted detail filled (checklist included) is Completed, and anything between is In Progress, so
  the tabs, card dots and completed counts move as details are saved. **On Hold is gone** - it
  cannot be worked out from the details - so its tab is removed. The API no longer accepts or
  returns `completionStatus`; the `completion_status` column is left in place, unread
  ([preProductionProgress.js](../frontend/src/lib/preProductionProgress.js),
  [PreProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionPage.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **A shoot card's "details pending" now counts the Dum Dum or Qua Qua checklist too.** A
  checklist question counts as done once it is Completed, an action toggle once it is on, and the
  meeting and invitation fields only when their switch is on; remarks are not counted. A shoot no
  longer reads "All details filled" while its checklist is untouched
  ([PreProductionProjectPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionProjectPanel.js)).

- **The pre production shoot form now leads with the creative work and ends with the logistics.**
  The Dum Dum or Qua Qua checklist sits straight under Concepts, and Location and Event Timing
  come after Travel & Accommodation; Status stays last
  ([formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js)).

- **Switching a gift, the hard disk or the CRD document on or off now asks why, and keeps the
  answer.** In Pre Production's General panel, changing Welcome Kit, Shoot Completed Gift, Storage
  Needed or CRD Document between applicable and not asks for a reason before it saves; each switch
  is kept in the new `project_applicability_change` table with who made it and when, and while an
  item stays not applicable its section shows the reason it was switched off. The project save records a switch from any screen, so one
  made on Edit Project appears too, without a reason. Migration
  `20260926140000_add_project_applicability_changes`; run `prisma migrate deploy`
  ([PreProductionGeneral.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionGeneral.js),
  [projects/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js)).

- **Pre Production's General is a bar above the shoot cards that opens into an editable panel.**
  It was the first tile among the shoots. It now spans the panel above them, showing Welcome Kit,
  Shoot Completed Gift, Hard Disk and CRD Document as filled-in values; clicking it opens a panel —
  back to the shoots, follow-ups beside it — with a section for each. Every part saves through the
  screen that owns it, under that screen's permission: the gifts' Applicable and Assigned To,
  Storage Needed and CRD Document through Edit Project's save (`PROJECT / Projects` or `Show All
  Projects` at READ_WRITE — saving Storage Needed or CRD as applicable raises their records as it
  does there); a gift's Status through Client Gifts (`PROJECT / Client Gifts`), its sent and
  received dates stamping themselves; and the hard disk moves along the Client Storage flow —
  assign, hand in, backup, HDD out, in transit, delivered — with the same dialogs as the Client
  Storage screen (`ASSET / Client Storage`), now shared from `useClientStorageMoves`. A part the
  viewer may not change is shown filled in and read-only. No new permission; no role needs re-saving
  ([PreProductionGeneral.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionGeneral.js),
  [useClientStorageMoves.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/useClientStorageMoves.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **A Pre Production shoot can hold several concepts, and Location now comes before Event Timing.**
  Concepts were a yes/no toggle over one Reference and one Remarks box; the toggle is gone and the
  shoot form now shows a list added one by one with **+ Add Concept** — each with its own Reference
  and Remarks, removable — the same way an employee's qualifications are entered. The list keeps a
  fixed height and scrolls inside it once it grows past that. The read-back lists them one per line.
  Location moves above Event Timing on the form and the read-back. Existing concepts are carried
  over as the first of each shoot's list by migration
  `20260926130000_add_pre_production_concepts_list`; run `prisma migrate deploy`
  ([PreProductionFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionFormPanel.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **Pre Production follow-ups are a list beside the shoot cards, and only ask for the next date.**
  A project's follow-ups now sit in a column on the right of its Pre Production panel (under the
  cards on a phone) instead of a single form below them, and the same column stays beside a shoot
  when one is opened — its form, or its details for a reader. The board's refresh icon is gone. **Add Follow-up** asks for the Next
  Followup Date and Remarks — no Last Followup Date — and the follow-up joins the project's
  **Pending** list; **Mark done** moves it to a **Completed** list below, and a list with nothing in
  it is not shown. The earliest pending date is the project's Next
  Followup Date and the last one marked done its Last Followup Date, so the board's columns and
  overdue colouring work as before; the overdue banner above the table is gone. Follow-ups stay the project's, never a single shoot's. Existing
  follow-ups are carried over by migration `20260926120000_add_pre_production_followup_entries`
  (a next date becomes a pending follow-up, a last date one already done); run `prisma migrate
  deploy`. Guarded by the existing `PROJECT / Pre Production` — READ sees the list, READ_WRITE adds
  and marks done; no role needs re-saving
  ([PreProductionFollowups.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionFollowups.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **Pre Production is in the sidebar, under Project Management.** The board was only reachable by
  typing its address; it now sits after Projects, stays lit on the Corp, Dum Dum and Qua Qua boards
  beneath it, and shows only to roles holding `PROJECT / Pre Production` at `READ` or above — no
  new permission, and no role needs re-saving. A saved Sidebar Layout gets the entry appended to
  Project Management. Production and Post Production stay off the menu
  ([navigation.mjs](../frontend/src/constants/navigation.mjs),
  [sidebarStructure.js](../backend/src/modules/user/preferences/sidebarStructure.js)).

- **Create Project's Enquiry ID now lists CRM leads, and brings their vertical with it.** It
  searched existing projects, which is circular — only an enquiry that already had a project could
  be found, so a genuine new lead could never be picked and the field was really a free-text box. It
  now searches `sales_crm_lead` by enquiry id, name or number, leaves out any lead that already has
  a live project, and fills in the client, the number they are messaged on, the branch it is worked
  from and the **Product** from the lead's own vertical — the answer the studio gave when the lead
  was taken, so nobody is asked for it twice
  ([projects/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js),
  [CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js)).

- **Pre production's follow-up is now the project's, not each shoot's.** A coordinator rings the
  couple about the wedding, not about the Haldi and then again about the Reception, so Last Followup
  Date, Next Followup Date and Followup Remarks moved out of the per-shoot form into a Follow-up
  panel below the shoot cards, stored once per project. Existing per-shoot entries were carried
  across by the migration — the most recent contact and the soonest date owed — so no chasing was
  lost, and the old columns are kept but deprecated
  ([PreProductionProjectPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionProjectPanel.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **A manual WhatsApp group name now asks which product the sale is.** A reserved group name has
  always carried its vertical (Dum Dum → WED, Qua Qua → QQ, Corp → CORP), but typing a group name
  cleared it silently — and a project with no vertical reaches no branch board and gets no vertical
  checklist in Pre Production. Create Project and Edit Sale Details now show a required Product
  (Group Type) selector whenever no reserved name is attached, the server derives the vertical from
  it with the generator's own mapping, and editing a legacy project is how it gets backfilled
  ([CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js),
  [projects/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js)).

- **An extra quotation's files are called Attachments, not Proof.** The label on the form, the
  section heading where the record is read back, and the links on Project Payments all said
  "Proof" — a narrower word than what the field is actually used for. The stored keys are unchanged
  (`proof`, `proofUrls`), so this is what the reader sees and nothing else.

- **The role menu lists every role, ticks the ones already held, and unticking one gives it up.** It
  used to drop held roles from the list, which said the wrong thing — a role missing from a list of
  roles reads as one that does not exist or cannot be granted, not as one this account already
  carries. The menu is now the whole picture and a real toggle: tick to stage a role for Add, untick
  to remove one the account holds. Removing this way is the same call the row's Remove button makes,
  immediate and undoable, so the menu is not a quieter way to do something the row would have asked
  about first. Branch selection on a role already behaved this way and is unchanged.

- **Every new account starts on one known password instead of a generated one.** Creating login
  credentials for an employee used to mint a random 12-character password per person, which had to
  be read off the screen and passed on individually. It is now the same starting password for
  everyone, `123qweasdzxc`, and the Regenerate control is gone. The server's
  uppercase-and-symbol requirement went with it — it refused the chosen password — leaving a
  minimum length, since whatever arrives is hashed and becomes a real password.

  **This leans on a guard that is not built yet.** Accounts are created with
  `mustChangePassword: true` and the login response carries the flag, but nothing reads it: there is
  no forced change-password screen on either side. Until there is, this password stays valid on
  every account whose owner has not changed it by choice, and it is written in the repository. The
  flag is already in place, so the screen is the only piece missing.

- **The spinner is drawn as an SVG, so the moving part cannot go missing.** It was a bordered box
  whose blue arc existed only as `border-t-blue-600` overriding a full grey `border-color`, with its
  width from an arbitrary `border-[3px]` and its style resolved through a `@property` variable. Any
  one of those not landing left a plain grey ring — and a *uniform* ring that rotates looks
  completely still, because the arc is the only thing that shows movement. It is now a grey circle
  and a blue quarter-turn as two explicit strokes, which no cascade can flatten into one colour. The
  Public Gallery's own hand-rolled copy of the old markup now uses the shared component too.

- **Every full-page wait shows the same spinner in the same place.** Moving between modules drew a
  large spinner centred in the content area, and the permission check that follows drew a smaller
  one centred in a 16rem box — so the loader visibly jumped upward and shrank between two halves of
  the same wait. `Checking access…`, `Loading workspace…` and the route-change loader now all render
  through `PageLoader`, which fills whatever surface it is given, and the refusal that can follow a
  failed permission fetch sits in that same box rather than higher up. Only the words change between
  them. See [RouteGuard.js](../frontend/src/components/auth/RouteGuard.js) and
  [RequireAuth.js](../frontend/src/components/auth/RequireAuth.js).

- **The Accounts footers carry Last updated and Total rows, and no running totals.** Accounts
  Manager showed Received, Spent and Net; Payment Requests showed Pending and Approved. Both put a
  second, differently-scoped set of figures under a table that was already listing the amounts they
  summed. The reduces that fed them went with them rather than being left to recompute on every
  filter change for a value nobody shows. The CRM and Meetings footers keep their own counts and
  guidance, which read as that page's own commentary rather than a total.

- **An edit panel's button says Update; only creating still says Save.** Every form that opens for
  both adding and editing offered the same **Save**, so the control gave no clue which of the two
  the panel was doing — the heading read *Edit Vendor* while the button under it read *Save Vendor*.
  Each panel now reuses the condition its own title is already built from, so heading and button
  cannot disagree: Update Vendor, Update Storage, Update Asset, Update Account, Update Entry, Update
  Offboarding, Update Project, and a plain **Update** on the employee, shoot, role and extra
  quotation panels. Creating is untouched, and so are the settings panels — Image Selection
  Settings, Table Settings, Project Settings and Quotation Pricing have nothing to create, so
  **Save** is still the right word there.

- **A WhatsApp group name says the branch as a short code.** `Erode` → **ERD**, `Tiruppur` → **TPR**,
  `Coimbatore` → **CBE**, `Bangalore` → **BLR**, `Hyderabad` → **HYD**, `Vizag` → **VSKP**. The name
  is read in WhatsApp's own chat list, where it is truncated to a phone's width, so five characters
  spent on "Erode" are five the couple and the date lose off the end. All three shapes use it —
  `WED Premium VSKP Arun & Meena`, `QQTPR Asha`, `CORP CBE Acme`. The register spells a branch with
  its state after it and the sheets do not, so "Erode TN", "Visakhapatnam AP", "Bengaluru" and
  "Tirupur" all reach the right code; a branch with no code is left exactly as typed rather than
  dropped. **The list is held in the code, not read from the branch table**, and is deliberately
  separate from the one in `backend/src/services/identifiers.js`: that one mints enquiry ids and
  writes Tiruppur as `TUP` and Vizag as `VIZAG`, so changing it would rename the branch segment of
  every id minted afterwards and split one studio's records across two spellings.
  [whatsappGroupNameUtils.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/whatsappGroupNameUtils.js),
  [group-name-branch-code.test.mjs](../frontend/test/group-name-branch-code.test.mjs).

- **A linked sheet no longer loses a whole lead over one unreadable cell — it blanks the cell and
  keeps the row.** A row was refused outright when any single field failed to parse, and the fields
  that fail are the ones a person answers in their own words: `feb 10 th and 11 th 2027` in *When is
  the Event Planned*, `Immediate` in *When Can You Join*, a state name where a date was expected.
  Each of those took a whole enquiry with it — the name, the number, the campaign that paid for it —
  so a studio could sync ten new leads and import none of them. Now the unreadable cell is stored as
  **null** and every readable column on the row is kept as it is. It applies to both linked
  integrations and to every field that can fail: name, email, lead status, all six date columns and
  all six phone columns. **A row with no name imports too**, with the name blank — a lead is a lead,
  and a wholly empty spreadsheet row never reaches the importer anyway. Cells are blanked *before*
  the row is matched, so a phone the importer could not read is not a phone it tries to find an
  existing lead by. Deduplication is untouched: a readable phone that already belongs to a lead is
  still recognised and the row still skipped. The summary reports **"6 fields left blank"** on a line
  of its own rather than as rows skipped — nothing was skipped — and names each one by column and
  row (`row 12 — eventPlannedDate: Invalid date value`) so the sheet can be corrected. The import
  preview counts them under **Fields Left Blank** in place of *Invalid Rows*, which is now always 0.
  [googleSheetsService.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/googleSheetsService.js),
  [sheetImport.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/interview/sheetImport.js),
  `hrm_interview_candidate.name` had to be widened to nullable to honour this — it was the one
  column that could not, so a nameless row was being stored as `''`, which on this schema is exactly
  what a blank must never be
  ([20260926090000_interview_candidate_name_nullable](../backend/prisma/migrations/20260926090000_interview_candidate_name_nullable/migration.sql);
  `sales_crm_lead.name` has always been nullable). One trade-off worth stating: a **phone** that
  cannot be read is blanked like anything else, and the phone is the deduplication key. A re-sync of
  the same sheet row still matches on its source id or position, but a first sync against a lead
  somebody typed in by hand that shares only that malformed phone will now import beside it rather
  than being refused — losing the row was the previous answer, and this is the one that keeps it.
  [sheet-import-blank-bad-fields.test.js](../backend/test/sheet-import-blank-bad-fields.test.js).

### Added
- **The Signature Album's Album tab is now an upload and a Gallery, with no folder sidebar.** On the
  Signature Album tab the project's folder tree and folder toolbar are no longer drawn and the album
  takes their width; Photo Selection and Photo Culling keep them, and no folder changes
  ([ImageSelectionProjectWorkspace.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/ImageSelectionProjectWorkspace.js)).
  The Album tab opens on Photo Selection's own drop zone - drop a folder, **Choose Photos**, **Choose
  Folder** - now one shared component
  ([PhotoDropZone.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/PhotoDropZone.js), drawn by
  `UploadManager` exactly as before), with the same progress panel (Pause, Retry failed, Cancel),
  then a **Gallery** of what was uploaded (processed count, search, sort, Delete - no All photos /
  Selected, since every upload is in the album), then the Cover. Uploading is the album's own: each photo is prepared in the browser by the
  project upload's encoder (a 480px WebP thumbnail and a ≤1600px JPEG preview of about 200 KB; the
  original never leaves the computer) and sent by the album's queue
  ([useAlbumUploadQueue.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/useAlbumUploadQueue.js))
  to a new `signature_album_photo` table and R2 under `image-selection/signature-album/` - never as a
  project photo, so Photo Selection, the client gallery, People, face recognition and every count are
  untouched. An upload is in the client's album as it lands: the server files it into the album's
  first chapter ("Gallery", created by the first upload of an album with none), so the client page,
  the ZIP download and publishing work unchanged. Live preview, chapters, highlights and + Add Photos
  are no longer on the Album tab, and neither is the album's ⋮ menu with Delete Signature Album (the
  server's delete endpoint is unchanged); nothing is deleted - an album built before keeps its chapters,
  highlights and photos, and the client page draws them as ever. Publishing now asks for "at least
  one photo" rather than a chapter. **Needs migration `20260928100000_signature_album_photos`** (new
  table; new nullable `signature_album_item.album_photo_id`; `image_id` relaxed to NULL - no row is
  rewritten). No permission change: uploading is `IMAGE_SELECTION / Signature Album` Read / Write.

- **A role's row menu now has Manage Users, for giving it to several accounts at once.** Handing a
  new role to the ten or fifteen people it is meant for used to mean opening each one in turn through
  User Management → Manage Roles; this is the identical picker, read from the role's own side — the
  same `RolePicker` control, now generalised to take either direction, with Select all/Clear built in
  through its `MultiSelectField`, pre-ticked with whoever already carries the role. Adding or
  removing an account takes effect immediately, exactly as Manage Roles already behaves, including
  the Undo offered on a removal; it calls the same `assignRoleToUser`/`removeRoleFromUser` endpoints
  Manage Roles already does, so nothing new was added on the server. Offered wherever
  `Role Management` is `READ_WRITE`, locked roles included — deciding who carries Super Admin is a
  different question from editing what it grants. See
  [RoleManagement.js](../frontend/src/components/admin/RoleManagement.js),
  [RoleUsersDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/admin/RoleUsersDialog.js) and
  [RolePicker.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/RolePicker.js).

- **The Employee Repository has a Review Pending tab, next to HR Onboarding Pending.** It shows every
  working employee (Active, in Training, PIP) whose Next Review Date has gone by — the same overdue
  check the employee's own Reviews section already colours "Upcoming" with — without moving the row
  out of its own tab: somebody Active with an overdue review still shows under Active as well. The
  row's ⋮ menu gains **Start Review** wherever it is shown, opening the employee's Add Review dialog
  directly, prefilled with the overdue date, instead of sending the reader to find Reviews and press
  Add Review themselves. See [EmployeeVerificationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeVerificationPage.js),
  [EmployeeTable.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeTable.js) and
  [employmentStatus.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/employmentStatus.mjs).

- **Pre Production is a working board, not a read-only list.** The four Pre Production screens now
  list one row per **project**, each summarising its shoots (a Completion Status rolled up from them — On Hold if any shoot is, Completed only when all are, In Progress once anything has started, so a shoot added to a finished project sends it back to In Progress on its own — plus the completed count, a Shoots Pending column naming the shoots not yet completed so the column filter can find every project still owing a given shoot, the follow-up and WRC), while the record underneath stays one per **shoot** — opened as cards from the row, carrying the studio's own pre production sheet
  end to end: the 18 columns already known are inherited read-only from the sale and the shoot, and
  the coordinator fills in the rest — Event Start and End Time, Reporting Time, Studio Start Date and
  Time, Location Address and Link, Travel & Accommodation Needed with the accommodation address, link
  and remarks, Last and Next Followup Date, Completion Status, WRC (waiting for client reply) and
  Production Coordinator. A row is raised automatically the moment a started project has a Pre
  Production Coordinator, and for every shoot added afterwards, so the work reaches whoever was named
  without anybody creating it; **My Shoots** matches the signed-in account's employee record against
  that assignment, and **All Shoots** is the same board unfiltered. **Edit Pre Production** opens the
  project's shoots as cards. A card carries only what is needed to pick a shoot to work on — status,
  date, place, event and reporting times, and a bar saying how much is still blank, as a percentage and a pending count rather than a fraction, since a shoot needing accommodation is asked more questions than one that does not — rather
  than every answer it holds; clicking a card opens that
  shoot's form; saving returns to the cards, which is the loop a coordinator works in. A General tile leads the grid ahead of every shoot, stating Welcome Kit, Storage Needed, CRD Document and Storage ID once for the project instead of repeating down every tile
  ([PreProductionProjectPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionProjectPanel.js)).
  Overdue follow-ups are called out above the table and coloured in it. Each vertical carries its
  own checklist on top of the shared fields — Dum Dum's couple addresses, per-side intro calls,
  meeting and invitation chasing, site visit and production readiness; Qua Qua's single intro call,
  dresses images, production statuses and Google Review — described once in
  [preProductionVerticalFields.js](../frontend/src/constants/preProductionVerticalFields.js) and
  read by the board columns, shoot cards, info panel and form alike, stored as one superset row per
  shoot. Received The Storage / Storage ID are read from the project's Client Storage record rather
  than typed twice, and the CRD document reads itself: alongside the sale's hand-set note, the board
  and the General tile show what the CRD Documents page knows — the document's state, its completion
  percentage, and which side has actually been received, worked out from the answers rather than
  remembered. Each shoot now records whether it is being shot to a
  concept — a plain Yes/No that asks for the Reference and concept Remarks only when the answer is
  yes, and clears both if it turns back to no. Travel gained a mode — Bus, Train, Flight, Own, Office Vehicle, Other — where
  "Other" asks to be spelled out and "Office Vehicle" is picked from Asset Management's vehicles,
  the vehicle's name resolved server-side and kept beside the link; changing the mode clears the
  detail that belonged to the old one. Reading the board needs `PROJECT / Pre Production` at READ,
  saving a row needs READ_WRITE, and nothing here can reach the sale
  ([PreProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionPage.js),
  [PreProductionFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionFormPanel.js),
  [pre-production/service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/service.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **Long pickers can be searched.** Typing narrows the list instead of scrolling it, in the three
  places the list grows with the studio: the branches a role covers, and the roles an account
  carries — both where an employee's login is created and in Manage Roles on the Users page, which
  share one `RolePicker`. Search is an opt-in `searchable` prop on the shared multi-select, so no
  other picker changed, and an option already ticked stays ticked while the search hides it
  ([MultiSelectField.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/MultiSelectField.js),
  [RoleDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/admin/RoleDialog.js),
  [RolePicker.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/RolePicker.js)).

- **An extra quotation can name a service the studio's list does not hold.** The Service picker ends
  with **Others**, and choosing it opens a box to type the service in. Work agreed on top of a
  project is often the thing nobody had a name for yet, and until now it had to be forced into the
  nearest listed service or written in Remarks, where the approving manager would not see it as what
  was being charged for.

  What is stored is the typed name, never the word "Others" — a row reading "Others" tells a manager
  approving it nothing. Reopening such an extra puts the picker back on **Others** with the name
  filled in, which has to wait for the service list to arrive from the server: until it does there is
  no way to tell a typed name from one that simply has not loaded. No server change was needed —
  `service` was already free text up to 150 characters. See
  [ExtraQuotationFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ExtraQuotationFormPanel.js).

- **A payment request can be corrected while it is still pending.** All four kinds — Salary Advance,
  Advance Expense, Expense Submission and Vendor Payment — now offer **Edit** in the row menu, which
  reopens the request in the form it was raised on with every answer, expense line and attachment
  already filled in. Until now a typo meant withdrawing the request and raising it again.

  **The option disappears the moment it is decided.** Approving writes a Cash Spent entry from the
  request's amount, so an edit afterwards would leave the books saying something the request no
  longer does; a rejected request is a closed record for the same reason. `PATCH
  /api/hrm/payment-requests/:id` refuses anything but `PENDING`, and refuses a change of kind at
  all — `requestCode` carries a prefix per kind, so a salary advance turning into a vendor payment
  would leave the code describing something it is not. Who may edit is the answer withdrawing
  already gives: the person who raised it, or somebody who could have decided it — and an approver
  editing somebody else's request does not become the person who raised it. See
  [payment-requests/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payment-requests/controller.js) and
  [PaymentRequestFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PaymentRequestFormPanel.js).

- **An employee's reporting chart, on the Emp Chart tab of their record.** Double-click anybody in
  the Employee Repository and the record opens as it always has, now with a second tab beside
  **Details**. It draws the chain from that person up to whoever reports to nobody, and everybody
  reporting directly to them; each node says how many reports it has of its own, and clicking any
  other node re-centres the chart on that person, so the whole studio is walked one screen at a
  time rather than loaded as one tree. Who somebody reports to is set from **Reports To** in the
  employee form, beside Department — the form offers everyone but the person themselves, and the
  server refuses a longer ring that the list cannot show, so the chart always has a top to arrive
  at. Read at `READ` of `HRM / Employee Management`, the permission that already governs the
  repository it is shown inside, through a router of its own rather than the master-data one next
  door, which deliberately lets any signed-in session read the lists that fill pickers app-wide. A
  node carries the name, designation, department and employee id and nothing else: an employee row
  also holds salary, Aadhaar and PAN, and none of that belongs in a response drawn as a diagram.
  Adds the migration `20260829090000_add_employee_reports_to`. No new permission, so there is
  nothing to reseed or re-save. See
  [EmployeeOrgChart.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeOrgChart.js) and
  [hrm/org-chart/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/org-chart/service.js).

- **The screening form, the onboarding invite and a new joiner's login can now be sent on WhatsApp,
  from the sender's own paired account.** All three screens already showed the finished wording in an editable box with a
  Copy button, and the studio then left the application, opened WhatsApp and pasted it. **Send
  WhatsApp** sits in the dialog's footer beside Close and Send Invite, in WhatsApp's own green with
  its mark, and sends what is on screen — including a line somebody added before
  pressing it, which is why the box is editable and why the message travels from the browser rather
  than being rebuilt on the server. The **recipient's number never does**: it is read off the
  invite or the employee record, so neither screen can reach anybody but the person it is about,
  and there is deliberately no "send WhatsApp to this number" endpoint anywhere. The interview register's **Send Onboarding
  Invite** needed nothing of its own: it opens the employee onboarding dialog, which carries the
  button already. Sending the
  credentials asks for `ADMIN / User Management` Read / Write — the same permission that creates
  them, and a stronger one than the rest of that screen, because the message carries the temporary
  password; the onboarding invite rides the `HRM / Employee Management` Read / Write the router
  already applies, and the screening form the `HRM / Interview` its own router does. No new
  permission and no migration. All three go through the WhatsApp module's own
  send path, so they keep every habit that makes the studio's paired number look like a person
  writing to one person — the pacing between messages, the check that the number is on WhatsApp at
  all, the typing indicator — and both the studio-wide and per-user kill switches stop them. They
  are behind the **same per-user rate limit** as every other send, deliberately sharing one budget
  with the CRM rather than being given a second one: it is one account, and WhatsApp watches the
  account. Somebody who has not linked their own WhatsApp sees the button greyed with the reason,
  rather than not at all — the three reasons it can be greyed (the studio's switch, their own
  switch, no phone linked) are told apart, because only the last is one they can fix. Nothing is
  recorded, which is what the invite's email does too: there is no sent stamp on an invite and no
  screen that shows one.
### Added
- **The Interview candidate popup now carries the call recordings and their transcripts, as the CRM
  lead popup does.** Its Call Logs tab already answered *has anybody rung this person* — when, how
  long, and which of the studio's people was on it — but deliberately stripped the rest, on the
  reading that `HRM / Interview` is not a grant of `SALES / CRM Leads`. **The studio's decision is
  the other one: each module answers for its own permission.** So the tab now also carries the note
  whoever took the call typed, the CRM status at the time, and a player for the recording itself;
  and a new **Transcripts** tab beside it shows what was actually said, with the AI summary, call
  outcome, next action, and the spoken text behind *View Full Transcript*. Worth knowing, because it
  is a real widening: the call log is one studio-wide table keyed by the number dialled, so somebody
  who may edit a candidate can point a record at any number and read what the log holds against it.
  Narrowing it again is a permission decision rather than a code change. What is still **not** passed
  on is the CRM's own filing of that person — the name it chose, the enquiry it opened — and the
  integration's raw webhook payload; none of it says anything about the call. A transcript hangs off
  a *call* rather than a lead, which is the only reason this is reachable at all: a candidate has
  never had an enquiry id, so the number finds the calls and the calls find their transcripts. Asking
  for one in full goes through the candidate, never by transcript id alone, so the tab cannot be used
  to read a call belonging to somebody else. The Transcripts tab itself is now **one shared
  component** ([CallTranscriptsTab](../frontend/src/components/shared/CallTranscriptsTab.js)), lifted
  out of `CRMPage` where it lived: it carries careful statements about machine translation and
  inferred speakers that a second copy would not have kept, and only *where a transcript is fetched
  from* differs between the two screens.

### Changed

- **Settings → User Settings → WhatsApp now also lists anybody Allow WhatsApp is ticked for, not
  only the Sales team.** Allow WhatsApp (Login Credentials → WhatsApp) holds somebody to the
  application-wide link gate regardless of department, but until now the only place that showed
  whether they had actually linked was the gate itself, on their own screen the next time they
  opened the application — an administrator switching the tick on had no way to check back. A row
  reached either way now carries **Required** next to their name, so Sales and Required read as the
  two different reasons they can be, rather than one list. An administrator is never shown as
  Required, since the gate never holds one regardless of the tick, even where they also carry it.
  See [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/whatsapp-chat/controller.js) and
  [WhatsAppUsersTable.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/WhatsAppUsersTable.js).

- **CRD Documents has a My Documents switch, the one the CRM board already has.** The data scope widens
  "mine" to "mine and my team's" — it follows the reporting chain the whole way down, so a manager four
  levels above a coordinator sees their documents. That is the right default, and it is also why a
  coordinator with a team of their own could not find their own work: eleven rows, one of them theirs. On,
  the list is the documents that reader is the **pre-production coordinator** for, which is the owner the
  Assigned To column names. Remembered per person, and drawn **only** for somebody who has a team under
  them — for everybody else the two states are the same list, and a switch that changes nothing invites a
  reader to flip it, see no difference and conclude the screen is broken. A document with **nobody staffed
  on it** surfaces while the switch is on for a reader who sees everything, since they are the ones who
  staff projects; a coordinator reading their own work is not shown other people's unstaffed documents
  ([crd-documents/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crd-documents/controller.js),
  [CrdDocumentsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CrdDocumentsPage.js)).

- **CRD Documents says who each document is on.** The owner is the project's **pre-production
  coordinator**, and it is not a new field: that person is already named on the project and is already one
  of the five columns the data scope narrows the register by, which is why the row reaches that reader at
  all. So the screen was already showing each person their own work and looked exactly like a list of
  everybody's, because no column said whose it was. A **standalone** document — one raised by hand against
  an enquiry that answers to no project — has no coordinator to name and reads as a dash rather than
  borrowing somebody
  ([crd-documents/service.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crd-documents/service.js),
  [CrdDocumentsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CrdDocumentsPage.js)).
  The name comes back **through the employee relation**, with the project's stored text only as a fallback,
  so a coordinator who has since been renamed reads correctly.

- **CRD Documents is one list instead of one list per vertical.** The page opened on Dum Dum with a
  picker beside the heading, so Qua Qua's documents sat behind a control and a reader who did not notice
  it saw a list that was simply missing rows — with the status tabs counting confidently over the half
  they could see. Both verticals are on the page now and the tabs count all of it. Nothing is lost in
  telling them apart: **Vertical is a column** on the row and always was, sortable and filterable like
  every other, so somebody who wants one narrows that column and somebody who wants the whole of what
  the studio is owed does nothing
  ([CrdDocumentsPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CrdDocumentsPage.js)).

- **Every dropdown in a form field can be typed into to find an option.** It was opt-in, so whether a list
  could be searched depended on whether whoever wrote that form had thought to pass the prop — ninety-odd
  call sites had, and identical lists of branches, designations, employees and master data elsewhere could
  only be scrolled. It is decided once in `Dropdown` now, which is also the only way the forms nobody has
  looked at get it. Safe as a default because of what the box does with what is typed: it is a combobox
  with `aria-autocomplete="list"`, so typing is the **search** and the value moves only when an option is
  chosen — a half-typed word in a branch field cannot be stored as a branch. The section picker beside a
  module heading (`mode="switch"`) is unchanged, and a picker that genuinely should not be typed into can
  still pass `searchable={false}`
  ([Dropdown.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/Dropdown.js)).
  **Reaching a dropdown no longer opens its list.** A searchable field opened its menu on focus, which was
  fine while search was something a form asked for and is not as the default: tabbing through a form would
  pop a menu at every dropdown, ten of them on some screens. A click opens it, typing opens it and the
  arrow keys open it — what is gone is the one that fired without anybody asking for anything.

- **Schedule Payment takes an amount as well as a percentage, and the percentage takes decimals.** A row
  could only be entered as a share of the signed quotation, with the Amount beside it a figure to read —
  so a client who agreed to ₹50,000 at slot booking meant somebody working out what percentage of
  ₹4,20,000 that is. Both boxes are typed into now and each works out the other. The **percentage stays
  what is stored**, so a schedule entered in rupees still follows a corrected quotation. The decimals are
  what make that possible: ₹50,000 of ₹4,20,000 is 11.904762%, and a whole number would be ₹210 out — the
  box was a `type="number"` with no `step`, which is a step of one, so a browser marked 11.9 invalid and
  its arrows walked in whole numbers. It is digits and a single decimal point now, sanitised as typed, the
  same rule the Signed Quotation box above it already used. The Amount box is disabled while there is no
  signed quotation, since a share of nothing cannot be expressed, and shows what is being typed rather
  than re-deriving itself under the cursor
  ([paymentSchedule.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/paymentSchedule.mjs),
  [SchedulePaymentSection.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/SchedulePaymentSection.js)).

- **Production is in the sidebar, under Project Management.** The board was only reachable by
  typing its address; it now sits after Pre Production and shows only to roles holding
  `PROJECT / Production` at `READ` or above — no new permission, and no role needs re-saving. A
  saved Sidebar Layout gets the entry appended to Project Management. Post Production stays off the
  menu ([navigation.mjs](../frontend/src/constants/navigation.mjs),
  [sidebarStructure.js](../backend/src/modules/user/preferences/sidebarStructure.js)).

- **The production frontend build now runs on webpack, not Turbopack.** Turbopack's build pipeline
  has a known, currently open bug fetching `next/font/google` at build time
  ([vercel/next.js#99114](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/99114)): when Google's font CSS
  happens to return a URL containing `&` in its query, Turbopack's resolver mis-splits it and the
  build fails with "next/font/google queries have exactly one entry" — intermittent, since it
  depends on exactly what Google returns for that request, and it hit both a CI run and, once, the
  nightly deploy itself on the client-facing quotation page (`/q/[token]`, which sets five Google
  Fonts for the PDF-styled sheet). `next build` is now pinned to `--webpack`
  ([package.json](../frontend/package.json)) so the production build never depends on Turbopack's
  font-fetch code path; `next dev` is untouched and still runs on Turbopack
  ([next.config.mjs](../frontend/next.config.mjs)).

- **Anybody who sends from this application can now link their own WhatsApp, not just the CRM.** The
  session is per **user** — credentials are stored per user id and every message goes out from the phone
  that person paired, which is already how the screening form, the onboarding invite and a new joiner's
  login are sent. But the route that shows the pairing QR sat behind `SALES / CRM Leads`, so an HR user
  was told they were not linked and had nowhere to link it. Pairing and unpairing your **own** account now
  sit above that guard, beside `GET /my-session` which was lifted for the same reason, and answer to
  whichever of the three jobs actually messages anybody — CRM Leads, HRM / Interview, or
  HRM / Employee Management. A lead's conversation stays behind the CRM's permission. The candidate
  popup's WhatsApp tab shows the code when the viewer is not linked, instead of a compose box that was
  refused on send
  ([routes.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/whatsapp-chat/routes.js),
  [WhatsAppLinkCard.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/WhatsAppLinkCard.js),
  [InterviewWhatsAppTab.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewWhatsAppTab.js)).
  The pairing card is **one component** now rather than markup inside the lead panel, and it asks for a
  code only when a person presses the button: pairing is deliberately not rate limited on the server, and
  each attempt is a real registration against a number WhatsApp can ban for registering repeatedly.

- **Client Storage asks its yes/no questions with Yes / No radio buttons instead of switches.** All seven
  checks — Labeled?, Footage Backup, Final Files Copy, Harddisk Footages Back up, Folder Structure
  Checked, Final Renders, Other Files in Harddisk — on the storage form and at every step of the flow
  that asks them (Hand In, Footage Backup Done, HDD Out), plus Shoot Status Pending, which is a reading
  rather than a question and would have been the one switch left among seven pairs. The same change the
  pre production shoot form already had, through the same field helper, which now lives on its own
  ([yesNoField.js](../frontend/src/constants/yesNoField.js)) rather than in the pre production field list
  ([formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js)).

- **Switching Storage Needed to Yes no longer explains itself.** Pre-Production's General bar drew a
  dashed box reading "No hard disk record yet — saving Storage Needed as Yes raises one" the moment the
  answer was turned on, which told somebody the mechanism they had just used: they chose Yes, they are
  about to save, and the disk appears when they do. Nothing was being asked and nothing had gone wrong.
  The Hard Disk field now waits until there is a disk to show — the whole field rather than an empty
  renderer, which would have left a gap in the grid where the box was
  ([PreProductionGeneral.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionGeneral.js)).

- **In the lead popup, the remarks box now sits at the top and the remarks read newest first.** The box
  and its toolbar used to be under the whole list, so on a lead with many remarks the next note meant
  scrolling past every earlier one, and the latest remark was at the bottom. The box is now first and stays
  in view while the remarks scroll beneath it, with the most recent remark directly under it. Nothing
  about what is saved changed: the remarks are stored in the order they were written, and editing one
  still rewrites that entry. The same composer serves the candidate popup and the Add Lead and info
  panels, which get the new order too; the lead popup and the candidate popup's Remarks tab both pin the box
  ([NotesComposer.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/NotesComposer.js),
  [CRMPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CRMPage.js),
  [InterviewRemarksTab.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewRemarksTab.js)).
- **The candidate popup's Next Follow-up date no longer stretches across the whole card.** It takes one
  column of the same grid the lead popup's Follow-up Details uses: full width on a phone, half the card
  from tablet width and a third on wide screens
  ([InterviewCandidatePopup.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewCandidatePopup.js)).
- **The candidate popup now has a Call Logs tab, and Remarks reads like a lead's.** Call Logs answers
  the question the **Follow Up** stage exists to ask and the register could not: has anybody actually
  rung this candidate, when, for how long, and which of the studio's people was on it. The studio's call
  log is one table fed by the handset integration and keyed by the number dialled, so a recruiter's call
  lands in it exactly as a salesperson's does — it had only ever been read from the CRM's lead popup.
  **A recruiter is shown the call and nothing about the CRM's client**: a number that is a candidate here
  can be a client there, so the client's name, enquiry, CRM status, recording, note and raw payload are
  all stripped — `HRM / Interview` is not a grant of `CRM / Leads`. **Remarks is now the lead's
  remarks composer itself** — the collapsible entry bubbles, the bullet and numbered lists, Enter to
  post, the send button in the toolbar — not a box that resembles it. `NotesComposer` had been sitting
  unexported in the middle of `CRMPage.js`, which is how the register came to have a second, poorer
  answer to "how do I write down what was said"; it now lives in `components/shared/` and nothing about
  it changed for the lead — and it imports no service of its own, the upload and fetch behind its
  paperclip arriving from whichever module owns the bucket the files are in. Two of its controls are switched off for a candidate: the **pencil**, because
  `statusNotes` is append-only with no per-entry id and no endpoint that rewrites one, and the
  **paperclip**, because a candidate's remark has nowhere to put a file. Each bubble also carries the
  **stage** the remark was written at, which a lead's has no equivalent of — "they asked to be called
  back" means one thing at Follow Up and another at Selected. **Activity Logs** is the same log read as *what
  happened* — the stage, when it moved and who moved it — so the card no longer holds one list twice. The
  two panes also share the width better: the record was taking two thirds of the screen for a form that
  draws only the fields the candidate answered
  ([InterviewCallLogsTab.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewCallLogsTab.js),
  [InterviewRemarksTab.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewRemarksTab.js),
  [interviewInfoFormatters.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/interviewInfoFormatters.js),
  [callLogService.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/callLogService.js)).

- **Position Applied For is no longer required when the studio writes a candidate down.** Add
  Application and the candidate record still ask for it and the register still files by it, but a
  blank one is accepted: the job somebody is after is regularly unknown at the moment the application
  arrives — a walk-in, a number passed on by a friend of the studio, a CV with no covering note — and
  refusing the row for it bought either a guess typed into the field or the candidate not being
  written down at all. The server already took it as optional, so this removes a refusal the frontend
  was making on its own
  ([InterviewAddApplicationDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewAddApplicationDialog.js),
  [interviewConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/interviewConfig.js),
  [candidateRecordForm.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/candidateRecordForm.js)).
  The **candidate's own screening form still requires it**, which is where the real answer comes from.

- **Double-clicking a candidate on HRM → Interview now opens the screen where they are worked, not
  a read-only card.** One popup holds the whole errand: the fields the candidate actually filled in
  (with the empty ones one press away), a remark composer, the activity log, a WhatsApp message, and
  a Follow-up Details card where the stage is chosen. Choosing **Follow Up** asks when, directly
  under the pills; choosing **Selected**, **On Hold** or **Rejected** is answered by the remark, which
  Update requires — so the register can always say why a candidate moved. The three stages that are
  consequences of an act — Form Submission Pending, Interview Scheduled, Onboarded — offer that act
  instead, and confirming it saves the record and opens the act's own form **over** the popup, which
  stays open underneath — cancelling that form puts you back on the candidate, and only the act
  succeeding writes the stage and closes both;
  **Form Submitted** is refused outright, because that stage is the candidate answering. **Choosing a
  stage asks for its remark first**: the pill records the choice, the card says a remark is needed to
  move that candidate, the Remarks tab comes forward, and Update writes the stage and the reason
  together or neither. Pressing Update with no remark is refused in the **snackbar** rather than as a
  banner above the form — it is not a fault in a field, and a banner pushed the record down the screen
  and stayed there to be re-read. **Schedule Interview and Send Screening Form draw their form over the popup**
  rather than closing it — closing that form leaves the popup exactly as it was, and only a round
  actually booked or a form actually sent closes both. Posting a remark or sending a WhatsApp message
  no longer closes the popup either. A viewer with
