  **read-only** HRM access gets the record, the log and no editable field — the guard is
  `ReadOnlyFieldset`'s own `canWrite`, and the press that opens the empty fields sits outside it, since
  reading the whole record is exactly what that viewer is there to do. The side
  drawer this replaces is gone, and the ⋮'s **Edit** / **Review** opens the same popup, so there is
  one editor for a candidate rather than two
  Answering the stage question no longer raises a second one: `Dialog` draws inside the popup rather
  than portalling out of it, so a press on **Leave the stage as it is** used to bubble to the popup's
  dimmed backdrop and put "Close without saving?" on top of its own answer — in any tab and at any
  stage. A press on the backdrop is now a press whose target *is* the backdrop
  ([InterviewCandidatePopup.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewCandidatePopup.js),
  [candidateRecordForm.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/candidateRecordForm.js),
  [InterviewPage.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/InterviewPage.js)).
  The **Onboarded** pill is only offered to somebody holding `HRM / Employee Management`
  READ_WRITE — the same permission the row menu's Send Onboarding Invite is gated on — and a
  read-only viewer gets the record, the log and no way to move anybody.

- **Branch reach now follows the role that granted the permission, not the person.** Somebody who
  holds CRM Leads across every branch through one role and Asset Management in one branch through
  another now sees every branch's leads and one branch's assets, where before the wider role
  silently widened the narrower one. Every call into the branch API names the `{ module, feature }`
  it is asking about; a role naming no branches contributes none, and a person's own
  `user.branch_id` no longer widens anything — work they or their team are named on still reaches
  them through `dataScope`
  ([iam.service.js](../backend/src/services/iam.service.js),
  [dataScope.service.js](../backend/src/services/dataScope.service.js)).
  **A read-only role's branches no longer scope writes**: `dataScope.resolve` takes the access level,
  so an employee write is measured against the roles that grant READ_WRITE.

- **Start Project's radio buttons now sit in a bordered box with the same title style as the
  fields around them.** Welcome Gift, Shoot Completed Gift, Storage Needed and CRD Document match
  the pre production form's Yes / No radios, through a new `variant="field"` on the shared
  `RadioGroupField`; an unanswered required group now reddens its box too
  ([RadioGroupField.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/RadioGroupField.js),
  [StartProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/StartProjectFormPanel.js)).

- **The pre production shoot form asks its yes/no questions with Yes / No radio buttons instead
  of switches.** Travel & Accommodation Needed, WRC and every checklist yes/no (Event Schedule
  Meeting, Invitation Soft Copy, Site Visit, Team Reached Message, Shoot Completion Message, Google
  Review) now show both answers side by side; what is saved is unchanged
  ([preProductionVerticalFields.js](../frontend/src/constants/preProductionVerticalFields.js),
  [formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js)).

- **A shoot's pre production status now works itself out; nobody sets it by hand.** Completion
  Status is gone from the shoot form. A shoot with no details filled is Not Started, one with every
  counted detail filled (checklist included) is Completed, and anything between is In Progress, so
  the tabs, card dots and completed counts move as details are saved. **On Hold is gone** - it
  cannot be worked out from the details - so its tab is removed. The API no longer accepts or
  returns `completionStatus`; the `completion_status` column is left in place, unread
  ([preProductionProgress.js](../frontend/src/lib/preProductionProgress.js),
  [PreProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionPage.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **A shoot card's "details pending" now counts the Dum Dum or Qua Qua checklist too.** A
  checklist question counts as done once it is Completed, an action toggle once it is on, and the
  meeting and invitation fields only when their switch is on; remarks are not counted. A shoot no
  longer reads "All details filled" while its checklist is untouched
  ([PreProductionProjectPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionProjectPanel.js)).

- **The pre production shoot form now leads with the creative work and ends with the logistics.**
  The Dum Dum or Qua Qua checklist sits straight under Concepts, and Location and Event Timing
  come after Travel & Accommodation; Status stays last
  ([formPanelConfig.js](../frontend/src/constants/formPanelConfig.js)).

- **Switching a gift, the hard disk or the CRD document on or off now asks why, and keeps the
  answer.** In Pre Production's General panel, changing Welcome Kit, Shoot Completed Gift, Storage
  Needed or CRD Document between applicable and not asks for a reason before it saves; each switch
  is kept in the new `project_applicability_change` table with who made it and when, and while an
  item stays not applicable its section shows the reason it was switched off. The project save records a switch from any screen, so one
  made on Edit Project appears too, without a reason. Migration
  `20260926140000_add_project_applicability_changes`; run `prisma migrate deploy`
  ([PreProductionGeneral.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionGeneral.js),
  [projects/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js)).

- **Pre Production's General is a bar above the shoot cards that opens into an editable panel.**
  It was the first tile among the shoots. It now spans the panel above them, showing Welcome Kit,
  Shoot Completed Gift, Hard Disk and CRD Document as filled-in values; clicking it opens a panel —
  back to the shoots, follow-ups beside it — with a section for each. Every part saves through the
  screen that owns it, under that screen's permission: the gifts' Applicable and Assigned To,
  Storage Needed and CRD Document through Edit Project's save (`PROJECT / Projects` or `Show All
  Projects` at READ_WRITE — saving Storage Needed or CRD as applicable raises their records as it
  does there); a gift's Status through Client Gifts (`PROJECT / Client Gifts`), its sent and
  received dates stamping themselves; and the hard disk moves along the Client Storage flow —
  assign, hand in, backup, HDD out, in transit, delivered — with the same dialogs as the Client
  Storage screen (`ASSET / Client Storage`), now shared from `useClientStorageMoves`. A part the
  viewer may not change is shown filled in and read-only. No new permission; no role needs re-saving
  ([PreProductionGeneral.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionGeneral.js),
  [useClientStorageMoves.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/useClientStorageMoves.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **A Pre Production shoot can hold several concepts, and Location now comes before Event Timing.**
  Concepts were a yes/no toggle over one Reference and one Remarks box; the toggle is gone and the
  shoot form now shows a list added one by one with **+ Add Concept** — each with its own Reference
  and Remarks, removable — the same way an employee's qualifications are entered. The list keeps a
  fixed height and scrolls inside it once it grows past that. The read-back lists them one per line.
  Location moves above Event Timing on the form and the read-back. Existing concepts are carried
  over as the first of each shoot's list by migration
  `20260926130000_add_pre_production_concepts_list`; run `prisma migrate deploy`
  ([PreProductionFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionFormPanel.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **Pre Production follow-ups are a list beside the shoot cards, and only ask for the next date.**
  A project's follow-ups now sit in a column on the right of its Pre Production panel (under the
  cards on a phone) instead of a single form below them, and the same column stays beside a shoot
  when one is opened — its form, or its details for a reader. The board's refresh icon is gone. **Add Follow-up** asks for the Next
  Followup Date and Remarks — no Last Followup Date — and the follow-up joins the project's
  **Pending** list; **Mark done** moves it to a **Completed** list below, and a list with nothing in
  it is not shown. The earliest pending date is the project's Next
  Followup Date and the last one marked done its Last Followup Date, so the board's columns and
  overdue colouring work as before; the overdue banner above the table is gone. Follow-ups stay the project's, never a single shoot's. Existing
  follow-ups are carried over by migration `20260926120000_add_pre_production_followup_entries`
  (a next date becomes a pending follow-up, a last date one already done); run `prisma migrate
  deploy`. Guarded by the existing `PROJECT / Pre Production` — READ sees the list, READ_WRITE adds
  and marks done; no role needs re-saving
  ([PreProductionFollowups.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionFollowups.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **Pre Production is in the sidebar, under Project Management.** The board was only reachable by
  typing its address; it now sits after Projects, stays lit on the Corp, Dum Dum and Qua Qua boards
  beneath it, and shows only to roles holding `PROJECT / Pre Production` at `READ` or above — no
  new permission, and no role needs re-saving. A saved Sidebar Layout gets the entry appended to
  Project Management. Production and Post Production stay off the menu
  ([navigation.mjs](../frontend/src/constants/navigation.mjs),
  [sidebarStructure.js](../backend/src/modules/user/preferences/sidebarStructure.js)).

- **Create Project's Enquiry ID now lists CRM leads, and brings their vertical with it.** It
  searched existing projects, which is circular — only an enquiry that already had a project could
  be found, so a genuine new lead could never be picked and the field was really a free-text box. It
  now searches `sales_crm_lead` by enquiry id, name or number, leaves out any lead that already has
  a live project, and fills in the client, the number they are messaged on, the branch it is worked
  from and the **Product** from the lead's own vertical — the answer the studio gave when the lead
  was taken, so nobody is asked for it twice
  ([projects/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js),
  [CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js)).

- **Pre production's follow-up is now the project's, not each shoot's.** A coordinator rings the
  couple about the wedding, not about the Haldi and then again about the Reception, so Last Followup
  Date, Next Followup Date and Followup Remarks moved out of the per-shoot form into a Follow-up
  panel below the shoot cards, stored once per project. Existing per-shoot entries were carried
  across by the migration — the most recent contact and the soonest date owed — so no chasing was
  lost, and the old columns are kept but deprecated
  ([PreProductionProjectPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionProjectPanel.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **A manual WhatsApp group name now asks which product the sale is.** A reserved group name has
  always carried its vertical (Dum Dum → WED, Qua Qua → QQ, Corp → CORP), but typing a group name
  cleared it silently — and a project with no vertical reaches no branch board and gets no vertical
  checklist in Pre Production. Create Project and Edit Sale Details now show a required Product
  (Group Type) selector whenever no reserved name is attached, the server derives the vertical from
  it with the generator's own mapping, and editing a legacy project is how it gets backfilled
  ([CreateProjectFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/CreateProjectFormPanel.js),
  [projects/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js)).

- **An extra quotation's files are called Attachments, not Proof.** The label on the form, the
  section heading where the record is read back, and the links on Project Payments all said
  "Proof" — a narrower word than what the field is actually used for. The stored keys are unchanged
  (`proof`, `proofUrls`), so this is what the reader sees and nothing else.

- **The role menu lists every role, ticks the ones already held, and unticking one gives it up.** It
  used to drop held roles from the list, which said the wrong thing — a role missing from a list of
  roles reads as one that does not exist or cannot be granted, not as one this account already
  carries. The menu is now the whole picture and a real toggle: tick to stage a role for Add, untick
  to remove one the account holds. Removing this way is the same call the row's Remove button makes,
  immediate and undoable, so the menu is not a quieter way to do something the row would have asked
  about first. Branch selection on a role already behaved this way and is unchanged.

- **Every new account starts on one known password instead of a generated one.** Creating login
  credentials for an employee used to mint a random 12-character password per person, which had to
  be read off the screen and passed on individually. It is now the same starting password for
  everyone, `123qweasdzxc`, and the Regenerate control is gone. The server's
  uppercase-and-symbol requirement went with it — it refused the chosen password — leaving a
  minimum length, since whatever arrives is hashed and becomes a real password.

  **This leans on a guard that is not built yet.** Accounts are created with
  `mustChangePassword: true` and the login response carries the flag, but nothing reads it: there is
  no forced change-password screen on either side. Until there is, this password stays valid on
  every account whose owner has not changed it by choice, and it is written in the repository. The
  flag is already in place, so the screen is the only piece missing.

- **The spinner is drawn as an SVG, so the moving part cannot go missing.** It was a bordered box
  whose blue arc existed only as `border-t-blue-600` overriding a full grey `border-color`, with its
  width from an arbitrary `border-[3px]` and its style resolved through a `@property` variable. Any
  one of those not landing left a plain grey ring — and a *uniform* ring that rotates looks
  completely still, because the arc is the only thing that shows movement. It is now a grey circle
  and a blue quarter-turn as two explicit strokes, which no cascade can flatten into one colour. The
  Public Gallery's own hand-rolled copy of the old markup now uses the shared component too.

- **Every full-page wait shows the same spinner in the same place.** Moving between modules drew a
  large spinner centred in the content area, and the permission check that follows drew a smaller
  one centred in a 16rem box — so the loader visibly jumped upward and shrank between two halves of
  the same wait. `Checking access…`, `Loading workspace…` and the route-change loader now all render
  through `PageLoader`, which fills whatever surface it is given, and the refusal that can follow a
  failed permission fetch sits in that same box rather than higher up. Only the words change between
  them. See [RouteGuard.js](../frontend/src/components/auth/RouteGuard.js) and
  [RequireAuth.js](../frontend/src/components/auth/RequireAuth.js).

- **The Accounts footers carry Last updated and Total rows, and no running totals.** Accounts
  Manager showed Received, Spent and Net; Payment Requests showed Pending and Approved. Both put a
  second, differently-scoped set of figures under a table that was already listing the amounts they
  summed. The reduces that fed them went with them rather than being left to recompute on every
  filter change for a value nobody shows. The CRM and Meetings footers keep their own counts and
  guidance, which read as that page's own commentary rather than a total.

- **An edit panel's button says Update; only creating still says Save.** Every form that opens for
  both adding and editing offered the same **Save**, so the control gave no clue which of the two
  the panel was doing — the heading read *Edit Vendor* while the button under it read *Save Vendor*.
  Each panel now reuses the condition its own title is already built from, so heading and button
  cannot disagree: Update Vendor, Update Storage, Update Asset, Update Account, Update Entry, Update
  Offboarding, Update Project, and a plain **Update** on the employee, shoot, role and extra
  quotation panels. Creating is untouched, and so are the settings panels — Image Selection
  Settings, Table Settings, Project Settings and Quotation Pricing have nothing to create, so
  **Save** is still the right word there.

- **A WhatsApp group name says the branch as a short code.** `Erode` → **ERD**, `Tiruppur` → **TPR**,
  `Coimbatore` → **CBE**, `Bangalore` → **BLR**, `Hyderabad` → **HYD**, `Vizag` → **VSKP**. The name
  is read in WhatsApp's own chat list, where it is truncated to a phone's width, so five characters
  spent on "Erode" are five the couple and the date lose off the end. All three shapes use it —
  `WED Premium VSKP Arun & Meena`, `QQTPR Asha`, `CORP CBE Acme`. The register spells a branch with
  its state after it and the sheets do not, so "Erode TN", "Visakhapatnam AP", "Bengaluru" and
  "Tirupur" all reach the right code; a branch with no code is left exactly as typed rather than
  dropped. **The list is held in the code, not read from the branch table**, and is deliberately
  separate from the one in `backend/src/services/identifiers.js`: that one mints enquiry ids and
  writes Tiruppur as `TUP` and Vizag as `VIZAG`, so changing it would rename the branch segment of
  every id minted afterwards and split one studio's records across two spellings.
  [whatsappGroupNameUtils.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/whatsappGroupNameUtils.js),
  [group-name-branch-code.test.mjs](../frontend/test/group-name-branch-code.test.mjs).

- **A linked sheet no longer loses a whole lead over one unreadable cell — it blanks the cell and
  keeps the row.** A row was refused outright when any single field failed to parse, and the fields
  that fail are the ones a person answers in their own words: `feb 10 th and 11 th 2027` in *When is
  the Event Planned*, `Immediate` in *When Can You Join*, a state name where a date was expected.
  Each of those took a whole enquiry with it — the name, the number, the campaign that paid for it —
  so a studio could sync ten new leads and import none of them. Now the unreadable cell is stored as
  **null** and every readable column on the row is kept as it is. It applies to both linked
  integrations and to every field that can fail: name, email, lead status, all six date columns and
  all six phone columns. **A row with no name imports too**, with the name blank — a lead is a lead,
  and a wholly empty spreadsheet row never reaches the importer anyway. Cells are blanked *before*
  the row is matched, so a phone the importer could not read is not a phone it tries to find an
  existing lead by. Deduplication is untouched: a readable phone that already belongs to a lead is
  still recognised and the row still skipped. The summary reports **"6 fields left blank"** on a line
  of its own rather than as rows skipped — nothing was skipped — and names each one by column and
  row (`row 12 — eventPlannedDate: Invalid date value`) so the sheet can be corrected. The import
  preview counts them under **Fields Left Blank** in place of *Invalid Rows*, which is now always 0.
  [googleSheetsService.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/googleSheetsService.js),
  [sheetImport.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/interview/sheetImport.js),
  `hrm_interview_candidate.name` had to be widened to nullable to honour this — it was the one
  column that could not, so a nameless row was being stored as `''`, which on this schema is exactly
  what a blank must never be
  ([20260926090000_interview_candidate_name_nullable](../backend/prisma/migrations/20260926090000_interview_candidate_name_nullable/migration.sql);
  `sales_crm_lead.name` has always been nullable). One trade-off worth stating: a **phone** that
  cannot be read is blanked like anything else, and the phone is the deduplication key. A re-sync of
  the same sheet row still matches on its source id or position, but a first sync against a lead
  somebody typed in by hand that shares only that malformed phone will now import beside it rather
  than being refused — losing the row was the previous answer, and this is the one that keeps it.
  [sheet-import-blank-bad-fields.test.js](../backend/test/sheet-import-blank-bad-fields.test.js).

### Added
- **A role's row menu now has Manage Users, for giving it to several accounts at once.** Handing a
  new role to the ten or fifteen people it is meant for used to mean opening each one in turn through
  User Management → Manage Roles; this is the identical picker, read from the role's own side — the
  same `RolePicker` control, now generalised to take either direction, with Select all/Clear built in
  through its `MultiSelectField`, pre-ticked with whoever already carries the role. Adding or
  removing an account takes effect immediately, exactly as Manage Roles already behaves, including
  the Undo offered on a removal; it calls the same `assignRoleToUser`/`removeRoleFromUser` endpoints
  Manage Roles already does, so nothing new was added on the server. Offered wherever
  `Role Management` is `READ_WRITE`, locked roles included — deciding who carries Super Admin is a
  different question from editing what it grants. See
  [RoleManagement.js](../frontend/src/components/admin/RoleManagement.js),
  [RoleUsersDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/admin/RoleUsersDialog.js) and
  [RolePicker.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/RolePicker.js).

- **The Employee Repository has a Review Pending tab, next to HR Onboarding Pending.** It shows every
  working employee (Active, in Training, PIP) whose Next Review Date has gone by — the same overdue
  check the employee's own Reviews section already colours "Upcoming" with — without moving the row
  out of its own tab: somebody Active with an overdue review still shows under Active as well. The
  row's ⋮ menu gains **Start Review** wherever it is shown, opening the employee's Add Review dialog
  directly, prefilled with the overdue date, instead of sending the reader to find Reviews and press
  Add Review themselves. See [EmployeeVerificationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeVerificationPage.js),
  [EmployeeTable.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeTable.js) and
  [employmentStatus.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/employmentStatus.mjs).

- **Pre Production is a working board, not a read-only list.** The four Pre Production screens now
  list one row per **project**, each summarising its shoots (a Completion Status rolled up from them — On Hold if any shoot is, Completed only when all are, In Progress once anything has started, so a shoot added to a finished project sends it back to In Progress on its own — plus the completed count, a Shoots Pending column naming the shoots not yet completed so the column filter can find every project still owing a given shoot, the follow-up and WRC), while the record underneath stays one per **shoot** — opened as cards from the row, carrying the studio's own pre production sheet
  end to end: the 18 columns already known are inherited read-only from the sale and the shoot, and
  the coordinator fills in the rest — Event Start and End Time, Reporting Time, Studio Start Date and
  Time, Location Address and Link, Travel & Accommodation Needed with the accommodation address, link
  and remarks, Last and Next Followup Date, Completion Status, WRC (waiting for client reply) and
  Production Coordinator. A row is raised automatically the moment a started project has a Pre
  Production Coordinator, and for every shoot added afterwards, so the work reaches whoever was named
  without anybody creating it; **My Shoots** matches the signed-in account's employee record against
  that assignment, and **All Shoots** is the same board unfiltered. **Edit Pre Production** opens the
  project's shoots as cards. A card carries only what is needed to pick a shoot to work on — status,
  date, place, event and reporting times, and a bar saying how much is still blank, as a percentage and a pending count rather than a fraction, since a shoot needing accommodation is asked more questions than one that does not — rather
  than every answer it holds; clicking a card opens that
  shoot's form; saving returns to the cards, which is the loop a coordinator works in. A General tile leads the grid ahead of every shoot, stating Welcome Kit, Storage Needed, CRD Document and Storage ID once for the project instead of repeating down every tile
  ([PreProductionProjectPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionProjectPanel.js)).
  Overdue follow-ups are called out above the table and coloured in it. Each vertical carries its
  own checklist on top of the shared fields — Dum Dum's couple addresses, per-side intro calls,
  meeting and invitation chasing, site visit and production readiness; Qua Qua's single intro call,
  dresses images, production statuses and Google Review — described once in
  [preProductionVerticalFields.js](../frontend/src/constants/preProductionVerticalFields.js) and
  read by the board columns, shoot cards, info panel and form alike, stored as one superset row per
  shoot. Received The Storage / Storage ID are read from the project's Client Storage record rather
  than typed twice, and the CRD document reads itself: alongside the sale's hand-set note, the board
  and the General tile show what the CRD Documents page knows — the document's state, its completion
  percentage, and which side has actually been received, worked out from the answers rather than
  remembered. Each shoot now records whether it is being shot to a
  concept — a plain Yes/No that asks for the Reference and concept Remarks only when the answer is
  yes, and clears both if it turns back to no. Travel gained a mode — Bus, Train, Flight, Own, Office Vehicle, Other — where
  "Other" asks to be spelled out and "Office Vehicle" is picked from Asset Management's vehicles,
  the vehicle's name resolved server-side and kept beside the link; changing the mode clears the
  detail that belonged to the old one. Reading the board needs `PROJECT / Pre Production` at READ,
  saving a row needs READ_WRITE, and nothing here can reach the sale
  ([PreProductionPage.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionPage.js),
  [PreProductionFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/PreProductionFormPanel.js),
  [pre-production/service.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/service.js),
  [pre-production/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/project-management/pre-production/controller.js)).

- **Long pickers can be searched.** Typing narrows the list instead of scrolling it, in the three
  places the list grows with the studio: the branches a role covers, and the roles an account
  carries — both where an employee's login is created and in Manage Roles on the Users page, which
  share one `RolePicker`. Search is an opt-in `searchable` prop on the shared multi-select, so no
  other picker changed, and an option already ticked stays ticked while the search hides it
  ([MultiSelectField.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/MultiSelectField.js),
  [RoleDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/admin/RoleDialog.js),
  [RolePicker.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/RolePicker.js)).

- **An extra quotation can name a service the studio's list does not hold.** The Service picker ends
  with **Others**, and choosing it opens a box to type the service in. Work agreed on top of a
  project is often the thing nobody had a name for yet, and until now it had to be forced into the
  nearest listed service or written in Remarks, where the approving manager would not see it as what
  was being charged for.

  What is stored is the typed name, never the word "Others" — a row reading "Others" tells a manager
  approving it nothing. Reopening such an extra puts the picker back on **Others** with the name
  filled in, which has to wait for the service list to arrive from the server: until it does there is
  no way to tell a typed name from one that simply has not loaded. No server change was needed —
  `service` was already free text up to 150 characters. See
  [ExtraQuotationFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/project-management/ExtraQuotationFormPanel.js).

- **A payment request can be corrected while it is still pending.** All four kinds — Salary Advance,
  Advance Expense, Expense Submission and Vendor Payment — now offer **Edit** in the row menu, which
  reopens the request in the form it was raised on with every answer, expense line and attachment
  already filled in. Until now a typo meant withdrawing the request and raising it again.

  **The option disappears the moment it is decided.** Approving writes a Cash Spent entry from the
  request's amount, so an edit afterwards would leave the books saying something the request no
  longer does; a rejected request is a closed record for the same reason. `PATCH
  /api/hrm/payment-requests/:id` refuses anything but `PENDING`, and refuses a change of kind at
  all — `requestCode` carries a prefix per kind, so a salary advance turning into a vendor payment
  would leave the code describing something it is not. Who may edit is the answer withdrawing
  already gives: the person who raised it, or somebody who could have decided it — and an approver
  editing somebody else's request does not become the person who raised it. See
  [payment-requests/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/payment-requests/controller.js) and
  [PaymentRequestFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/hrm/PaymentRequestFormPanel.js).

- **An employee's reporting chart, on the Emp Chart tab of their record.** Double-click anybody in
  the Employee Repository and the record opens as it always has, now with a second tab beside
  **Details**. It draws the chain from that person up to whoever reports to nobody, and everybody
  reporting directly to them; each node says how many reports it has of its own, and clicking any
  other node re-centres the chart on that person, so the whole studio is walked one screen at a
  time rather than loaded as one tree. Who somebody reports to is set from **Reports To** in the
  employee form, beside Department — the form offers everyone but the person themselves, and the
  server refuses a longer ring that the list cannot show, so the chart always has a top to arrive
  at. Read at `READ` of `HRM / Employee Management`, the permission that already governs the
  repository it is shown inside, through a router of its own rather than the master-data one next
  door, which deliberately lets any signed-in session read the lists that fill pickers app-wide. A
  node carries the name, designation, department and employee id and nothing else: an employee row
  also holds salary, Aadhaar and PAN, and none of that belongs in a response drawn as a diagram.
  Adds the migration `20260829090000_add_employee_reports_to`. No new permission, so there is
  nothing to reseed or re-save. See
  [EmployeeOrgChart.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeOrgChart.js) and
  [hrm/org-chart/service.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/org-chart/service.js).

- **The screening form, the onboarding invite and a new joiner's login can now be sent on WhatsApp,
  from the sender's own paired account.** All three screens already showed the finished wording in an editable box with a
  Copy button, and the studio then left the application, opened WhatsApp and pasted it. **Send
  WhatsApp** sits in the dialog's footer beside Close and Send Invite, in WhatsApp's own green with
  its mark, and sends what is on screen — including a line somebody added before
  pressing it, which is why the box is editable and why the message travels from the browser rather
  than being rebuilt on the server. The **recipient's number never does**: it is read off the
  invite or the employee record, so neither screen can reach anybody but the person it is about,
  and there is deliberately no "send WhatsApp to this number" endpoint anywhere. The interview register's **Send Onboarding
  Invite** needed nothing of its own: it opens the employee onboarding dialog, which carries the
  button already. Sending the
  credentials asks for `ADMIN / User Management` Read / Write — the same permission that creates
  them, and a stronger one than the rest of that screen, because the message carries the temporary
  password; the onboarding invite rides the `HRM / Employee Management` Read / Write the router
  already applies, and the screening form the `HRM / Interview` its own router does. No new
  permission and no migration. All three go through the WhatsApp module's own
  send path, so they keep every habit that makes the studio's paired number look like a person
  writing to one person — the pacing between messages, the check that the number is on WhatsApp at
  all, the typing indicator — and both the studio-wide and per-user kill switches stop them. They
  are behind the **same per-user rate limit** as every other send, deliberately sharing one budget
  with the CRM rather than being given a second one: it is one account, and WhatsApp watches the
  account. Somebody who has not linked their own WhatsApp sees the button greyed with the reason,
  rather than not at all — the three reasons it can be greyed (the studio's switch, their own
  switch, no phone linked) are told apart, because only the last is one they can fix. Nothing is
  recorded, which is what the invite's email does too: there is no sent stamp on an invite and no
  screen that shows one.
### Added
- **The client gallery's People tab now shows one combined grid of a person's photos instead of a
  card to open at a time, and More opens a searchable People panel.** Choosing anybody in the
  People rail gathers their photos from **every card of the shoot in view** into a single grid,
  headed with the names and the number of frames and grown by scrolling — the client was being
  asked which memory card to look in, which is something only the studio knows. Each photo is still
  the card's own: nothing is copied or moved, a photo appears once however many cards the search
  crossed, and ticking one files it against the same selection item the cards would have, so a
  photo picked here is picked in All Photos and Selected and one picked there is already ticked
  here. Several people still mean the photos **all** of them are in together, never either alone.
  With **All** — nobody chosen — the tab keeps the folder cards exactly as before. **More** now
  opens a panel rather than pouring the rest of the people into the rail: a search box matching the
  number a person is shown under (`40` finds Person 40 and Person 400), the faces listed with their
  photo counts and a tick box each, scrolling inside the panel a page at a time so a gallery
  holding thousands of faces is never handed to the browser at once, and **Apply** filtering the
  gallery once for the whole choice rather than on every tick. Whoever is chosen is lit in the rail
  afterwards, however far down the list they came from. The rail itself leads with at most eight
  people, equal in width and aligned, and never grows the section. Nothing else changes: face data,
  clustering, the folder view, All Photos, the PIN, submission and download are untouched, and no
  photo selection is ever cleared by changing who is being looked for. Drawing the People list is
  also **one grouped count** now instead of a counting query per person. See
  [PeoplePickerDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/PeoplePickerDialog.js),
  [PeoplePanel.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/PeoplePanel.js) and
  [faces/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/faces/service.js).

- **A branch can now hold several UPI IDs, added one at a time.** Settings → Organization →
  Branches opens on a single **UPI ID** box, as before. **+ Add UPI ID** beneath it adds another,
  and again for as many as the branch is paid into — a branch is commonly paid into more than one
  handle, and the Payment QR beside them encodes only one. The first box is always there and has no
  delete; every box added after it has one, and removing a box only edits the form until **Add
  Branch** or **Update Branch** is pressed. Opening an existing branch shows exactly the UPI IDs it
  already holds — three saved is three boxes, one saved is one, none saved is one empty box — never
  a spare box underneath. A box left empty stores nothing, each is trimmed, and one handle typed
  twice is said under the second box rather than stored twice. `e.g. beamcraft@upi` is only the
  example in an empty box and is never saved as a value. The client's quotation payment page prints
  every UPI ID the branch holds, in the studio's order and each with its own copy icon. Nothing
  about the Payment QR, the bank account, GSTIN, PAN or the rest of the branch form changes, and
  one branch still has one QR. **Migration** `20260927100000_branch_upi_ids` replaces `branch.upi_id`
  with a JSON `branch.upi_ids` and copies each branch's existing UPI ID in as the first entry of its
  list, so nothing typed into the old single box is lost — `prisma migrate deploy`. See
  [BranchesPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/settings/BranchesPanel.js),
  [RepeatableTextField.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/RepeatableTextField.js) and
  [validation.js](../backend/src/modules/admin/branches/validation.js).

### Changed
- **Every table's column filters can now be searched and worked from the keyboard.** A column whose
  values are a closed set — Services, Shoot Type, Session Timing, Size, Status, Branch, Deliverable
  Added, Complimentary and their like, in every module drawing through the shared table — has
  offered a tick-list for a while, but the search box inside it only appeared past nine values, so
  the lists people actually open were searched by eye. It appears from five values up now, takes
  focus as the menu opens, and matches without regard to case or stray spaces, so opening a filter
  and typing is one gesture. All of it is worked without a mouse: Down and Up walk the list and wrap
  at either end, Home and End reach the ends, the highlighted row is scrolled into view, Enter ticks
  it, and Escape closes the menu and puts focus back on the filter. The single-answer version of the
  same control, used where one value is the question, takes the same keys and closes on Enter; a
  long value no longer stretches its menu past the edge of the window.

  Two other things came out of it. A menu whose column was scrolled half off the side of the screen
  used to open partly outside the window, with no way to scroll to the rest — worst on a phone,
  where a single column can be wider than the screen; it is now held inside on both edges. And
  closing a menu now always forgets where the keyboard had got to, so reopening one starts at the
  top rather than on a row nobody chose.

  Nothing was added to any module: the two controls in
  [components/shared/](../frontend/src/components/shared/FilterMultiSelect.js) are what every table
  already drew, so every table has this at once. Which columns are dropdowns and which stay text
  boxes is unchanged and still decided by the rows — a column past 40 distinct values, and any date,
  day, link or picture, keeps the box it had. Filtering, sorting, pagination, column order, saved
  table preferences, selected rows and the query each table sends its server are all untouched.

- **The client gallery's People tab is now one grid of the shoot's photographs, and people are
  numbered by how many photographs they are in.** Pressing **All** used to hand the client a row of
  memory cards to open one at a time — *Card 1, Total: 52, See Photos* — which asked them to know
  something only the studio knows. All now shows every photograph of the shoot in view, gathered
  from all of its cards, in the same grid a chosen person already used; a card is never a step in
  between. Choosing a person, or several, narrows that same grid to the photographs all of them are
  in together, still from every card of the shoot. Nothing crosses a shoot: the counts, the
  ranking, the filter and the grid are all scoped to the shoot being browsed, so a face in 35
  Wedding photographs and 40 Engagement ones reads as 35 inside Wedding.
  **Person 1 is now whoever is in the most photographs**, Person 2 the next, and so on, instead of
  the order the worker happened to find them in — which put a guest who walked past one frame first
  and the bride eleventh. A tie is settled by which was found first so two reads never disagree,
  and the picker is ranked the same way, so its numbers always agree with the rail's. The number is
  a label for the shoot being looked at: everything that means a particular person carries the face
  cluster's own id, so nothing depends on the words on screen. Counts are of photographs, not
  faces — a frame somebody appears in twice counts once, which the database already guaranteed.
  Nothing else changed: the AND rule still means all the chosen people in the same frame, photos
  keep their card, a photo appears once however many cards were searched, picking still writes to
  the one selection record the photo has always had, paging is still by scrolling with no page
  numbers, and the scroll position still survives opening and closing a photograph. The picker's
  order control is gone with this, since a second ordering could only disagree with the numbers.
  See [PeoplePanel.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/PeoplePanel.js)
  and [faces/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/faces/service.js).
- **The client gallery's People picker is now a Select People panel.** The same choosing, in a
  panel that reads like the rest of the gallery. A header with the title and *Choose one or more
  people to filter photos*; on the left the search box across the whole width, then a row saying
  how many people the gallery holds and how many of the ten are chosen, then the faces as a grid —
  two across on a phone, three on a tablet, four where the column is widest; on the right the
  people chosen so far as removable cards that scroll on their own, over the line that states the
  rule — *photos will be shown where all selected people appear together in the same photo* — with
  a quiet illustration where that column is still empty. **A card carries nothing until it is
  chosen**: an empty tick box on every face turned a set of people to recognise into a form to fill
  in, so an unchosen card is a face, a name and a count, and a chosen one tints pale blue, takes a
  blue edge and a blue ring, and grows a tick in its corner. The whole card is the target, so there
  is no small box to hit and the keyboard works where a press does. Two columns on a tablet and a
  desktop; on a phone a near full-height sheet with a sticky header and footer, only the grid
  scrolling, the right column folded into a row of faces carrying its own **Clear all**, and 44px
  targets throughout. The gallery behind is locked while the panel is open, the scrollbar is a
  hairline, and the panel fades and lifts in and out rather than appearing. There are **no page
  numbers**: the grid is read as it is scrolled, and a search starts it at the top without
  disturbing who has been chosen. There is deliberately **no select-all** — the filter takes ten
  people at most, so such a control could only refuse the eleventh, and the ceiling is stated
  beside the count instead. The footer is **Cancel** and **Apply** alone; emptying the choice lives
  beside the people it empties. **None of the behaviour changed**: ticking still edits a draft and
  filters nothing until **Apply**, Cancel and Escape still drop it, **Clear all** still empties the
  people filter and never a picked photo, and several people still mean the photos all of them are
  in together. See
  [PeoplePickerDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/PeoplePickerDialog.js).

- **The copy controls on the client's quotation payment page are the icon alone.** The account
  number, the IFSC and each UPI ID carried a button reading **Copy** — and **Copy UPI ID** beside
  the UPI row — which named the row it sat on a second time, twice over on a card holding two of
  them. Each is now a plain copy icon in the sheet's gold, and a copy turns it to a tick for a
  moment in place of the word "Copied". Nothing is printed beside it: the control is named for a
  screen reader and in the tooltip a mouse sees. What is copied, and everything else on the page,
  is unchanged. See
  [PublicQuotationPaymentPage.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/PublicQuotationPaymentPage.js).

### Fixed

- **A backend restart no longer fails photos the desktop app is still uploading.** Boot recovery
  re-queued every photo still marked Processing, including the ones a workstation had registered
  and was posting previews for; the server holds no bytes for those, so the worker failed each
  one three times and marked it Processing failed. Recovery now skips workstation-registered
  photos, and the worker leaves any photo alone whose original is a relative trail it cannot
  open ([processing/queue.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/processing/queue.js),
  [processing/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/processing/service.js)).
- **Photo Culling: a photo hidden by a finalized cull no longer resolves on the client gallery's
  image routes by id**, a bulk decision that lists the same photo twice applies once instead of
  being refused, a session of a soft-deleted project is out of reach, a preview that never loads
  from storage fails that one photo within 30 seconds instead of stalling the run, and a failed
  run tells the photographer what to do next rather than showing the raw server error
  ([ai-culling/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/ai-culling/service.js),
  [gallery/service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/gallery/service.js)). Typing a
  target count no longer sends Keep / Maybe / Reject to the active card, and Enter on a button
  activates the button instead of opening the preview
  ([imageSelectionCulling.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/imageSelectionCulling.mjs)).
- **A project-wide bug sweep: client links can no longer be guessed or outlive a PIN change, and
  several screens stop losing or leaking data.**
  - **Client links.** A Photo Selection gallery's PIN is now limited on failures (ten per link per
    address, thirty per link anywhere) and the preview session shares the link lookup's budget
    ([public-gallery/routes.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/public-gallery/routes.js)).
    Regenerating a gallery PIN, resetting an album proof's PIN, or turning on or resetting a
    Signature Album's PIN now ends the sessions the old PIN opened; sessions issued before this
    release carry no PIN mark and stay valid until they expire. Album Proofing and the Signature
    Album count wrong PINs per client address (`clientIp`) instead of the proxy's, so one person's
    typos no longer lock out every client, and the Signature Album's public routes are rate limited.
  - **Photo Selection.** A gallery with no selection items can untick a photo again (the tick
    survived a reload only in the count); two quick picks can no longer pass a selection item's
    limit (the pick locks the item's row,
    [gallery/repository.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/gallery/repository.js)); a pick
    with no item is refused when the project offers items; Deselect All ignores a retired item.
  - **Signature Album.** A returning client of an album with no PIN gets a new session instead of a
    PIN screen they cannot pass; a chapter cover chosen from older project photos loads, and so does
    the cover on the PIN screen; the edit preview's dragging is offered only with Signature Album
    write access ([AdminAlbumPreview.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/signature-album/AdminAlbumPreview.js)).
  - **AI Feature.** Unlinking a person from a guest, or linking them to another, takes the person's
    photos away from the old guest; a new selfie drops the matches the old one found that nobody
    confirmed or rejected; deleting a photo, or a folder of them, recounts their guests; face crops
    and a photo's faces and matches need AI Face Management; a group edit that leaves out its
    sub-events keeps them; a guest upload with no file and an unreadable activity date are a 400,
    not a 500.
  - **CRM Leads.** Delete and the bulk actions read branch reach from CRM Leads itself, not from
    CRM Lead Deletion or Select All, and a change is held to the branches granted at Read & Write;
    a call transcript opens only through a lead the reader can see
    ([crm-leads/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/controller.js)).
  - **HRM Interview.** A reopened application form keeps the candidate's portfolio links; the
    schedule dialog can clear the interviewer, follow-up date and remarks; deleting or restoring a
    sheet link is held to its owner like editing it; a transcript on a missing candidate is a 404.
  - **Sales.** An invalid deliverable size on an allocation edit says why instead of a 500.
- **A Windows machine with the Store's `python3` alias no longer loses its backend at boot.** The
  call transcriber and the face engine each look for a Python by trying `python3` first. On Windows
  that name can be a Store app alias, and once Node has spawned one, its next spawn of anything
  aborts the whole process with "AssignProcessToJobObject: (87)" - which is what the transcription
  check at startup, and the transcriber's own tests, ran into. Both searches now skip an alias, found
  from PATH without spawning it ([windowsAppAlias.js](../backend/src/services/windowsAppAlias.js)),
  and pick the real install instead. Linux and macOS are untouched: there the check always says no.
- **The backend tests pass on a Windows development machine.** Eleven tests failed there whatever
  the change: they read POSIX permission bits Windows does not have, handed `import()` a bare
  Windows path, treated a backslash as an ordinary character, or needed the database to hold a user
  with id 1. Each now asks only what it can answer: the permission and execute-bit checks run on
  Linux, which is what the server is; the import goes through `pathToFileURL`; a backslash refused
  on Windows counts as contained; and the Show All Projects tests describe their own login
  ([project-show-all-branches.test.js](../backend/test/project-show-all-branches.test.js)). Test
  files only - no application code changed.
- **Web uploads work again: the thumbnail check no longer refuses the colour profile Chrome puts
  in every WebP.** Every photo chosen in the browser failed with "The thumbnail must be a WebP image
  and the preview a JPEG image" while the counters showed 0 failed. The derivative route's new
  byte walk admitted only the frame, alpha and animation chunks of a WebP, but Chrome's canvas writes
  each thumbnail as an extended WebP carrying its sRGB profile (`ICCP`), so every web thumbnail was
  turned away; the JPEG walk already admitted the matching APP2 profile, and the desktop's encoder
  writes a bare frame, which is why only the web was hit. The profile chunk is now accepted
  ([imageBytes.js](../backend/src/services/imageBytes.js)); EXIF and XMP chunks stay refused, and
  nothing about keys, compression or the desktop changed. The progress panel's Failed and Queue
  figures now count the photos this browser could not send and those still waiting in it, folded into
  the batch the Photo Selection store publishes, so they agree with the "Retry N failed" button
  ([imageSelectionUploadStore.js](../frontend/src/lib/imageSelectionUploadStore.js)); the Signature
  Album's own queue, which already counts locally, is untouched.

- **Naming a storage root after a retired one now says so instead of failing.** The database keeps
  every root's name unique, retired ones included, while the duplicate check only looked at living
  roots; a name still held by a retired root slipped past the check and came back as "Unable to
  create the storage root". It is now refused as a 409 that explains the retired root still holds
  the name and that its photos keep pointing at it
  ([service.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/storage-roots/service.js)).
- **Deleting an AI event folder now deletes its photos, and All Photos never shows a photo whose
  folder is gone.** Deleting a folder used to keep every photo in it live with no folder, so
  "card 1" vanished from the panel while its photos stayed in All Photos and in the event's count.
  All Photos is not a place of its own: it is every folder's photos seen together (plus a guest's
  uploads from the event page, which name no folder by design). Now `DELETE …/folders/:id` marks
  the folder's photos deleted and removes the folder in one transaction - never a deleted folder
  with live photos, however the request fails after - and then discards each photo exactly as a
  single delete does: the faces found in it and their crops, the people they counted towards
  recounted, a guest's matches, the preview and thumbnail in storage, the row
  ([media/service.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/media/service.js)). The All Photos listing,
  the event's All Photos count and the guest gallery all read one predicate - live, in a folder or
  a guest's, where "a guest's" is read as "not a staff upload", so removing a guest never hides or
  retires the photos they sent - so a photo left in no folder by an earlier deletion is listed nowhere even before it
  is cleaned up; `node backend/scripts/cleanupOrphanAiMedia.js` counts those per event, along with
  any row marked deleted whose cleanup failed part way, and with `--apply` retires both through the
  same discard (it changes rows and storage wherever it is run, so read the dry run first). A face
  job still running on a photo as it is deleted writes nothing into it. On the web and the desktop
  the confirmation now says "Delete folder and photos" with the count and that it cannot be
  undone, and after the delete - or a failure part way - the gallery, the folder counts and the
  event's total are read again from the server rather than subtracted on screen. Uploads, compression, face processing for the remaining photos, folder
  creation and rename, Image Selection, Album Proofing and the Signature Album are untouched.
- **The server's face engine finds its own environment on Windows too.** The interpreter search
  looked only for the Linux layout of `backend/.venv-face` (`bin/python3`), so a Windows development
  machine had to name an interpreter in `.env` by hand. It now looks for `Scripts\python.exe` in the
  same folders, so every machine mirrors the server - create `backend/.venv-face` with the face
  engine's requirements and leave `AI_FACE_PYTHON_BIN` empty
  ([engine.js](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/face-engine/engine.js)).
- **The face engine loads its models from the folder it was told to use.** `face_engine.py` checked
  `INSIGHTFACE_HOME` for the model files but then let InsightFace look in its own default folder,
  so a machine whose models live elsewhere - the Virtual Curation desktop's managed runtime - would
  have ignored the verified files and tried a download of its own. The engine now hands InsightFace
  the same root; a server without the variable set behaves exactly as before
  ([face_engine.py](../backend/src/modules/ai-feature/face-engine/face_engine.py)).
- **Editing an employee whose Employee ID predates the current `DBS-<n>` format no longer fails
  with "Validation failed".** The field is read-only everywhere it is shown and the server already
  ignores it on an update, but the edit form still sent it back unchanged, and a stored id the
  current pattern rejects (seed rows like `DEMO-EMP-001`, or any id minted under an older scheme)
  failed that check before the save reached anything the person actually changed. The form now
  never sends Employee ID on an edit, matching how Add already omits it.
  [EmployeeFormPanel.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeFormPanel.js)
- **Saving Employee Details now says which field was rejected**, instead of the bare "Validation
  failed" every refused save showed regardless of cause. The backend already returns the Zod
  `fieldErrors` behind that message; the Employee page now reads them and shows the offending
  field's own name and reason (e.g. "Contact Number: Enter a valid phone number with its country
  code"), joining more than one if several fields failed at once — the detail that led to finding
  the Employee ID bug above.
  [apiValidationError.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/apiValidationError.mjs),
  [EmployeeVerificationPage.js](../frontend/src/components/employees/EmployeeVerificationPage.js)
- **The notification bell always opens.** With nothing to list, the bell was drawn as a plain icon
  with nothing behind it, so pressing it did nothing at all - and since a notice now leaves the bell
  once it is read, that was the ordinary state: after reading everything, and in the moment before
  the first check answers. It now always opens its panel, which says "You're all caught up -
  nothing waiting on you." when there is nothing
  ([AppNotifications.js](../frontend/src/components/app-shell/AppNotifications.js)).

- **Attendance fixes from the pre-release review.**
  - **An approved Request correction now actually closes the day.** The proposed checkout was only
    stored for a permission, so a correction was saved without its time: approving it changed
    nothing, the day stayed open at nought hours, and the approver never saw the time asked for.
  - **Correction and HR-edit times are the studio's time, not UTC.** "18:00" was stored as 23:30 IST,
    and "09:00" passed the "after the login" check for a 09:30 login. Both now go through one helper,
    `wallClockInstant` in
    [attendanceRules.js](../backend/src/modules/hrm/attendance/attendanceRules.js).
  - **Deciding a request is one decision at a time.** Two approvers pressing together could leave a
    fully approved leave stuck as Pending, or have an approval overwrite a rejection; the request
    row is now locked for the decision and everything re-checked inside it, and an answer already
    given is never overwritten.
  - **A permission, on-duty, correction or outside-attendance request is settled by the first
    approval** when it falls back to several leave approvers (no Permission Approver set); it used to
    wait for all of them like a leave. A rejection still settles any request.
  - **Break In / Break Off lock the day**, so two quick presses cannot open two breaks and a break
    cannot start after the logout that closed the day.
  - **A day closed by an approved correction or an HR edit ends any break still running**, instead
    of leaving it running and its length - and the dashboard's break totals - growing.
  - **The person whose request was rejected is not told who rejected it** - their own request data
    still carried the refuser's name.
  - **HRM → Events accepts only photos sent with the post** (JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF, up to ~3 MB
    encoded each), never an outside link every employee's browser would fetch, and refuses an
    impossible date such as 31 February instead of rolling it over.
  - **Request outside attendance** moved from the Login dialog, where it could never succeed (it is
    about a day already logged in), to the check-in card and a dashboard notice - both only when the
    login was measured outside the office - and asks for one date, as the server requires. Checkout
    correction and Outside attendance now read by name in the request lists, and a rejected
    correction no longer offers "Apply again", which could only be refused.
  - **Employee Attendance:** Login waits for today to load rather than offering Login to somebody
    already logged in; an account with no employee record no longer gets an error on every visit;
    the capture dialog cannot be closed while it is sending; a browser with no camera access says so
    instead of "Opening camera..." for ever; a retry after an outside-location refusal reads the
    position again; ticking Login Summary rows no longer hides Login, Logout and Break.
  - **The time picker takes keyboard focus** when it opens and gives it back when it closes.
  - **The server's sidebar list includes HRM → Events**, which it was missing, so a saved sidebar
    layout no longer disagrees with the menu.

- **A date picker no longer opens with its month and year row cut off the top of the screen.** A
  date field low in a dialog on a short screen opened its calendar above itself, anchored by its
  bottom edge against a guessed height, so the top of the calendar - the month and year steppers -
  landed above the viewport. Every calendar in the app (each `DateField`, and the column date
  filters' `FilterDateInput`) is now placed by one rule in
  [calendarPlacement.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/calendarPlacement.js), against the
  calendar's measured height: below the field if it fits, above it if it fits there, and otherwise
  as low as it can sit with every edge on screen, over the field.

- **Navigating between screens no longer crashes the page with "Cannot read properties of null
  (reading 'removeChild')".** The studio's mark in the browser tab is kept right without a reload by
  a component that rewrites the `<link rel="icon">` in the head, and it cleared the way by *removing*
  every icon tag it had not written itself. Those tags are the ones the server wrote from
  `metadata.icons`, and React hoists each of them into the head as a resource it deletes itself — so
  taking one out of the document left React removing a node whose parent was already gone, and it
  threw the next time that part of the tree unmounted. Because the throw came out of React's own
  commit phase, the stack named nothing in this application and pointed at no screen. A competing tag
  is now disarmed instead — its `rel` is dropped, which is all the browser needs to ignore it, and
  put back when the component stops drawing its own mark — so the tab still changes the moment
  Settings saves a favicon, and nothing React owns is detached.
  [StudioFavicon.js](../frontend/src/components/shared/StudioFavicon.js)
- **The one-table tripwire passes on Windows.** The test that keeps a hand-drawn `<table>` out of
  every component but `DataTable` and `SimpleTable` compared paths spelled with `/` against the `\`
  that `path.relative` hands back on Windows, so it never recognised the two components it allows and
  reported both as offences — `npm test` was red on a Windows checkout and green on macOS. Paths are
  now compared with one spelling.
  [one-table-component.test.mjs](../frontend/test/one-table-component.test.mjs)
- **A lead a Callyzer call touches is now owned by the employee whose handset took it.** The CRM
  against the lead was written from the handset's label, and `crm` is a name copy of
  `owner_employee_id` with the id resolved back out of that text — so a phone named anything but its
  owner resolved to **nobody**, and the lead was created owned by no one: absent from that person's
  My Leads, and carrying no id for `dataScope` to narrow it by. The name is now taken from the match
  the webhook already makes — Callyzer's Employee Code against the repository's own code, then the
  label — so the text is the repository's spelling and the id resolves to the right person. The
  **Calls board** reads the same way, which is what pre-fills the CRM when a call is triaged into a
  lead. Callyzer's label remains the fallback for a handset the repository cannot place.
  Its CRM **filter** also worked again as a side effect: that query named no table alias while its
  SQL was written with one, so it failed on every column and the error was swallowed into an empty
  dropdown ([controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/controller.js),
  [callBoardService.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/callBoardService.js)).
- **Call History names the studio's own people, and its Employee filter finds them.** The employee
  column read the handset's label straight from Callyzer, so a phone named `saranita` while the
  repository says `Saranita` read as somebody who is not in the repository — and the Employee filter
  offers the repository's spelling, so choosing that person returned **no calls at all** however many
  they had made. Both halves now go through the match the webhook already writes: the column shows
  the repository's name, falling back to Callyzer's label only where the handset could not be placed,
  and the filter tests `matched_employee_id` before the label. Never Attended and Not Picked Up are
  named the same way. No row appears or disappears — only the name on it, and whether the filter can
  find it ([crm-reports/service.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-reports/service.js),
  [crm-reports/filters.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-reports/filters.js)).
- **The mandatory "Link your WhatsApp to continue" gate silently never held anybody outside
  `SALES / CRM Leads`.** It read its answer from `/session`, which that permission guards — so
  Allow WhatsApp ticked on an employee without it came back 403 on every poll, and the gate treats
  a failed read exactly like a network hiccup and holds nobody for it, by design. An administrator
  could tick the switch and see nothing happen, with no error anywhere to explain why. It now reads
  `/my-session` instead — the identical `status` handler, sitting above that guard on purpose for
  exactly this — so "everybody except an administrator" is what actually happens, matching what the
  code already said it did. See
  [WhatsappRequiredGate.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/WhatsappRequiredGate.js).

- **The browser tab shows the favicon uploaded in Settings → Branding, not the bundled "BC" mark.**
  The page's `<head>` only ever declared the bundled mark; the uploaded favicon was swapped in by
  script after the branding had been fetched, which a browser may ignore and Next's own metadata
  could undo - so the BC mark won. The root layout now writes the uploaded favicons into the page on
  the server ([layout.js](../frontend/src/app/layout.js) `generateMetadata`,
  [favicon.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/favicon.mjs) `faviconIcons`,
  [serverStudioBranding.js](../frontend/src/lib/serverStudioBranding.js)): Favicon — Light Mode for a
  light tab strip and Favicon — Dark Mode for a dark one, the other upload standing in when one is
  missing, and the bundled mark only when neither is uploaded or the branding cannot be read. The
  branding is read from the same public endpoint, cached for a minute and given two seconds at most,
  so a slow API never holds a page up. `StudioFavicon` no longer puts the bundled mark up while the
  branding is still loading, and still follows a newly saved favicon without a reload. It also no
  longer deletes Next's own icon tags - React owns them, and removing one crashed the next page
  change with "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'removeChild')" - but switches them off with
  `media="not all"` instead. Each upload
  already has its own file name, so a replaced favicon is a new URL and is not served from cache.
  No backend or database change.

- **A quotation link shared on WhatsApp now previews as BeamCraft.** The client pages at `/q/<token>`
  (and its Payment and Terms pages) set no preview of their own, so a chat app showed the tab title
  "Quotation | DBS", the root layout's leftover description "HRM Foundation" and, for want of a
  picture, the app icon. Each now sets its own title ("Quotation | BeamCraft", "Payment Details |
  BeamCraft", "Terms & Conditions | BeamCraft"), the description "View your quotation securely.",
  and Open Graph and Twitter cards whose image is a new 1200×630 BeamCraft card
  ([public/brand/beamcraft-og.png](../frontend/public/brand/beamcraft-og.png)), named by an absolute
  URL built from the configured public URL or the host the link was opened on
  ([shareMetadata.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/shareMetadata.mjs), [requestOrigin.js](../frontend/src/lib/requestOrigin.js)).
  Nothing about the quotation goes into the preview, the pages are still never indexed, and what
  the client sees on the page is unchanged. WhatsApp caches a link's preview, so a link already
  shared may keep the old card for a while; a newly shared one shows the new one.

- **The client gallery's People row shows everybody who fits before it shows More, and Select People
  has no search box.** The row led with at most eight people and always kept a slot for More, so a
  wide screen showed eight and a More while room was left over. It now leads with as many as its
  measured width holds and shows More only when some genuinely do not fit, taking one slot for it
  (`railSlotsForRest` in [clientGalleryPeople.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/clientGalleryPeople.mjs),
  [PeopleFilterRow.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/PeopleFilterRow.js));
  it re-measures as the window is resized, and More's count is the people behind it, never All. The
  gallery now hands the row the first 40 people rather than 12
  ([PublicGallery.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/PublicGallery.js)), so a wide
  screen is not limited by what was fetched. The search box, its state, its debounced reload and the
  `search` pass-through are gone from Select People
  ([PeoplePickerDialog.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/PeoplePickerDialog.js));
  the grid is everybody in the gallery's order, and the panel now takes the shared focus trap
  (`useFocusTrap`), so Tab stays inside it and closing returns focus to More. Order,
  counts, the ten-person ceiling, Clear all, Apply, Cancel and the photos-together (AND) filter are
  unchanged. Frontend only.

- **Opening a project from the Image Selection dashboard's Yet to Download view now lands on the shoot
  waiting to be downloaded.** It used to open the project at its root, where Download Selected is
  never offered, leaving the studio to find the shoot. Each dashboard row now carries
  `readyToDownloadFolderId`, worked out on the server from the same rule the Yet to Download card counts
  with, asked item by item (`readyToDownloadConfigs` in
  [classify.js](../backend/src/modules/image-selection/dashboard/classify.js)): the items submitted with
  picks since the last download. The folder is the first root folder, in the project tree's own order,
  that stands for one of those shoots — by shoot id, or by name for a folder with no shoot behind it —
  which is the rule the project page already uses to scope Download Selected. A row under Yet to Download
  opens `?projectId=…&folderId=…`, the link the upload dock already uses, so a reload reopens the same
  shoot ([imageSelectionDashboard.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/imageSelectionDashboard.mjs)). Every other
  view, the Selection Progress panel, the Projects sidebar and a project whose shoot has no folder open
  exactly as before; a folder deleted since the dashboard loaded opens the project at its root. Nothing
  is written: no download starts and no status changes. No permission change.

- **Select All then Delete on the Quotations register now removes every ticked quotation.** A register
  row is a quotation chain, and its id is the chain's latest version; the bulk delete used the row
  menu's delete, which removes only that version, so any chain with earlier versions came straight back
  as its previous one and All never reached 0. `DELETE /api/sales/quotations/bulk` now deletes every
  version of each ticked chain through `deleteQuotationChainRecord` in
  [controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js), refusing a chain whose id is no
  longer its current version (a version raised since the register was read) or that has a version the
  caller may not change. The row menu's **Delete** is unchanged and still removes one version. Earlier
  versions opened under a chain no longer show a tick box, which never sent anything, and the
  confirmation says every version goes (a new optional `deleteMessage` on
  [useTableSelection](../frontend/src/components/data-table/useTableSelection.js); every other table
  keeps its wording). Same permissions as before — `SALES / Quotation Management` plus
  `ADMIN / Table Select All`; no role changes.

  against the lead was written from the handset's label, and `crm` is a name copy of
  `owner_employee_id` with the id resolved back out of that text — so a phone named anything but its

  My Leads, and carrying no id for `dataScope` to narrow it by. The name is now taken from the match
  the webhook already makes — Callyzer's Employee Code against the repository's own code, then the
  label — so the text is the repository's spelling and the id resolves to the right person. The
  **Calls board** reads the same way, which is what pre-fills the CRM when a call is triaged into a
  lead. Callyzer's label remains the fallback for a handset the repository cannot place.
  Its CRM **filter** also worked again as a side effect: that query named no table alias while its
  SQL was written with one, so it failed on every column and the error was swallowed into an empty
  dropdown ([controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/controller.js),
  [callBoardService.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-leads/callBoardService.js)).
- **Call History names the studio's own people, and its Employee filter finds them.** The employee
  column read the handset's label straight from Callyzer, so a phone named `saranita` while the

  find it ([crm-reports/service.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-reports/service.js),
