  the repository's name, falling back to Callyzer's label only where the handset could not be placed,
  and the filter tests `matched_employee_id` before the label. Never Attended and Not Picked Up are
  named the same way. No row appears or disappears — only the name on it, and whether the filter can
  find it ([crm-reports/service.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-reports/service.js),
  [crm-reports/filters.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/crm-reports/filters.js)).
- **The mandatory "Link your WhatsApp to continue" gate silently never held anybody outside
  `SALES / CRM Leads`.** It read its answer from `/session`, which that permission guards — so
  Allow WhatsApp ticked on an employee without it came back 403 on every poll, and the gate treats
  a failed read exactly like a network hiccup and holds nobody for it, by design. An administrator
  could tick the switch and see nothing happen, with no error anywhere to explain why. It now reads
  `/my-session` instead — the identical `status` handler, sitting above that guard on purpose for
  exactly this — so "everybody except an administrator" is what actually happens, matching what the
  code already said it did. See
  [WhatsappRequiredGate.js](../frontend/src/components/sales/WhatsappRequiredGate.js).

- **No page reached by a client link can be picked up by a search engine any more.** These pages
  carry no login - the unguessable token in the URL is the whole of the secrecy - so a link that
  reaches a crawler once, forwarded or pasted into a chat that previews it, makes the page findable
  by anybody. Eight of the fourteen already refused indexing and six did not: the client's
  quotation, its Terms and its **Payment Details** (which prints the studio's account number, IFSC
  and UPI IDs, and whose address now travels as a clickable link inside the PDF clients receive and
  forward), the album proof, and the candidate's and new employee's application forms. All six now
  carry the same `robots: { index: false, follow: false }` line the other eight always had, and
  [public-pages-noindex.test.mjs](../frontend/test/public-pages-noindex.test.mjs) fails if a
  token-addressed page is ever added without it. Nothing else changes: the pages render, load and
  behave exactly as before, and no token, route, permission or query is touched - a search engine
  is simply told not to keep them.
- **Every active service in Settings is offered on every brand's quotation again.** Choose Services
  on a Corp quotation listed five services against the ten the studio had created in Settings →
  Project → Services, and nothing the studio could do would add the other five. A brand's own
  service and deliverable masters were *replacing* the catalogue rather than sitting on top of it,
  which was a safe reading only while Quotation Settings still had the Services, Deliverables,
  Packages and Pricing tabs to manage them with. Those tabs were removed at the studio's request
  and the rows behind them stayed, so a brand that had been configured before went on answering
  with the handful it was given, every service added afterwards was invisible on it, and no screen
  was left that could change it. The catalogue is now always the list, on every brand: a brand
  master renames and prices its entry in it, and a master naming no entry is offered beside it as
  before. Nothing that could be picked yesterday cannot be picked today, no price already stamped
  on a line moves, and the services that were missing are simply there
  ([quotationBrand.mjs](../frontend/src/lib/quotationBrand.mjs)). The same applied to deliverables,
  which lost the same screen, and reads the same way now.

- **A quotation refused over its Enquire ID now says so, instead of failing with no reason.** The
  Enquire ID box is a suggestion box rather than a closed list, because a quotation is often raised
  for an enquiry the CRM has not been given yet — so an id can be typed straight in. The column is
  a real key onto the CRM lead, so an id that names no lead was refused by the database, and the
  refusal reached the studio as "Unable to save quotation." and nothing else. The one answer that
  had to change was the one thing nobody was told, on a required field at the top of a long form,
  scrolled out of view by the time Generate Quotation is pressed. It is now named, and the server
  log carries the constraint that refused it rather than only the words
  ([projects/controller.js](../backend/src/modules/sales/projects/controller.js)).

- **A quotation now names a deliverable the way Settings does, brand and size and all, instead of
  printing its bare name.** A line the studio configured as `Album Printing - Canvera - 12x18 -
  1.5 inch` and chose by that name in the generator reached the client's copy at
  [`/q/<token>`](../frontend/src/components/sales/PublicQuotationPage.js) — and therefore the PDF,
  which is printed from that page — reading only `Album Printing`. Two variants of one deliverable
  on the same event arrived as two identical lines, and the client was sent less than was picked.
  The full label was already on the row: the generator stamps it when the variant is chosen, which
  is why the generator's own table and the deliverables picker have always read correctly. The
  client sheet now prints that label. Nothing about pricing, quantity, the deliverable's own name,
  service mapping or a project raised off the quotation changes: the quantity beside the line is
  the same figure it was, and a line added without a variant — as is every quotation saved before
  variants existed — still reads by its stored name.

- **Opening a photo no longer sends the client back to the first one.** A client who had scrolled
  a long way into a gallery, opened a photograph and closed it again was returned to the top and
  had to scroll all the way down once more — the single loudest complaint about the client gallery.
  The photo viewer was being drawn **instead of** the gallery rather than over it, so the grid
  unmounted while a picture was open and the pane that actually scrolls went with it; closing built
  a fresh pane, and a fresh pane starts at the top. The gallery now stays in the tree underneath,
  so the pane, its scroll position and every page already loaded are exactly where they were left.
  Closing reveals them instantly, with nothing to restore, nothing to fetch again and no jump. It
  holds for the folder view and the People grid alike, for the window and the inner pane (both are
  scroll containers here), on a phone as on a desktop, and whether the photo is closed with the
  back arrow, with Escape or with the **browser's Back button** — opening a photo now adds a
  history entry of its own, so Back and a phone's back gesture close the picture and land on the
  gallery where it was rather than leaving the page. The gallery is held still while a photo is
  open so it cannot scroll away behind it, and a photo picked or released inside the viewer shows
  as picked the moment the client is back. Nothing about the photos, the filters, the selections or
  the People filter changed: the data was never lost, only the scrolled box holding it. See
  [PublicGallery.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/PublicGallery.js) and
  [ImageViewer.js](../frontend/src/components/image-selection/client-gallery/ImageViewer.js).
